henceforth eat no fish of fortune's buttering.
Prithee, allow the wind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, you need not to stop your nose, sir; I spake
but by a metaphor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, sir, if your metaphor stink, I will stop my
nose; or against any man's metaphor. Prithee, get
thee further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, sir, deliver me this paper.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Foh! prithee, stand away: a paper from fortune's
close-stool to give to a nobleman! Look, here he
comes himself.
Here is a purr of fortune's, sir, or of fortune's
cat,--but not a musk-cat,--that has fallen into the
unclean fishpond of her displeasure, and, as he
says, is muddied withal: pray you, sir, use the
carp as you may; for he looks like a poor, decayed,
ingenious, foolish, rascally knave. I do pity his
distress in my similes of comfort and leave him to
your lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I am a man whom fortune hath cruelly
scratched.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: And what would you have me to do? 'Tis too late to
pare her nails now. Wherein have you played the
knave with fortune, that she should scratch you, who
of herself is a good lady and would not have knaves
thrive long under her? There's a quart d'ecu for
you: let the justices make you and fortune friends:
I am for other business.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech your honour to hear me one single word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: You beg a single penny more: come, you shall ha't;
save your word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: My name, my good lord, is Parolles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: You beg more than 'word,' then. Cox my passion!
give me your hand. How does your drum?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: O my good lord, you were the first that found me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: Was I, in sooth? and I was the first that lost thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: It lies in you, my lord, to bring me in some grace,
for you did bring me out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: Out upon thee, knave! dost thou put upon me at once
both the office of God and the devil? One brings
thee in grace and the other brings thee out.
The king's coming; I know by his trumpets. Sirrah,
inquire further after me; I had talk of you last
night: though you are a fool and a knave, you shall
eat; go to, follow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: I praise God for you.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Rousillon. The COUNT's palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING, COUNTESS, LAFEU, the two French Lords, with Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: We lost a jewel of her; and our esteem
Was made much poorer by it: but your son,
As mad in folly, lack'd the sense to know
Her estimation home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COUNTESS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis past, my liege;
And I beseech your majesty to make it
Natural rebellion, done i' the blaze of youth;
When oil and fire, too strong for reason's force,
O'erbears it and burns on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: My honour'd lady,
I have forgiven and forgotten all;
Though my revenges were high bent upon him,
And watch'd the time to shoot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: This I must say,
But first I beg my pardon, the young lord
Did to his majesty, his mother and his lady
Offence of mighty note; but to himself
The greatest wrong of all. He lost a wife
Whose beauty did astonish the survey
Of richest eyes, whose words all ears took captive,
Whose dear perfection hearts that scorn'd to serve
Humbly call'd mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Praising what is lost
Makes the remembrance dear. Well, call him hither;
We are reconciled, and the first view shall kill
All repetition: let him not ask our pardon;
The nature of his great offence is dead,
And deeper than oblivion we do bury
The incensing relics of it: let him approach,
A stranger, no offender; and inform him
So 'tis our will he should.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I shall, my liege.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: What says he to your daughter? have you spoke?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: All that he is hath reference to your highness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Then shall we have a match. I have letters sent me
That set him high in fame.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: He looks well on't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: I am not a day of season,
For thou mayst see a sunshine and a hail
In me at once: but to the brightest beams
Distracted clouds give way; so stand thou forth;
The time is fair again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: My high-repented blames,
Dear sovereign, pardon to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: All is whole;
Not one word more of the consumed time.
Let's take the instant by the forward top;
For we are old, and on our quick'st decrees
The inaudible and noiseless foot of Time
Steals ere we can effect them. You remember
The daughter of this lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: Admiringly, my liege, at first
I stuck my choice upon her, ere my heart
Durst make too bold a herald of my tongue
Where the impression of mine eye infixing,
Contempt his scornful perspective did lend me,
Which warp'd the line of every other favour;
Scorn'd a fair colour, or express'd it stolen;
Extended or contracted all proportions
To a most hideous object: thence it came
That she whom all men praised and whom myself,
Since I have lost, have loved, was in mine eye
The dust that did offend it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Well excused:
That thou didst love her, strikes some scores away
From the great compt: but love that comes too late,
Like a remorseful pardon slowly carried,
To the great sender turns a sour offence,
Crying, 'That's good that's gone.' Our rash faults
Make trivial price of serious things we have,
Not knowing them until we know their grave:
Oft our displeasures, to ourselves unjust,
Destroy our friends and after weep their dust
Our own love waking cries to see what's done,
While shame full late sleeps out the afternoon.
Be this sweet Helen's knell, and now forget her.
Send forth your amorous token for fair Maudlin:
The main consents are had; and here we'll stay
To see our widower's second marriage-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COUNTESS
SPEECH.LINE: Which better than the first, O dear heaven, bless!
Or, ere they meet, in me, O nature, cesse!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, my son, in whom my house's name
Must be digested, give a favour from you
To sparkle in the spirits of my daughter,
That she may quickly come.
By my old beard,
And every hair that's on't, Helen, that's dead,
Was a sweet creature: such a ring as this,
The last that e'er I took her at court,
I saw upon her finger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: Hers it was not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Now, pray you, let me see it; for mine eye,
While I was speaking, oft was fasten'd to't.
This ring was mine; and, when I gave it Helen,
I bade her, if her fortunes ever stood
Necessitied to help, that by this token
I would relieve her. Had you that craft, to reave
her
Of what should stead her most?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious sovereign,
Howe'er it pleases you to take it so,
The ring was never hers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COUNTESS
SPEECH.LINE: Son, on my life,
I have seen her wear it; and she reckon'd it
At her life's rate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: I am sure I saw her wear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: You are deceived, my lord; she never saw it:
In Florence was it from a casement thrown me,
Wrapp'd in a paper, which contain'd the name
Of her that threw it: noble she was, and thought
I stood engaged: but when I had subscribed
To mine own fortune and inform'd her fully
I could not answer in that course of honour
As she had made the overture, she ceased
In heavy satisfaction and would never
Receive the ring again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Plutus himself,
That knows the tinct and multiplying medicine,
Hath not in nature's mystery more science
Than I have in this ring: 'twas mine, 'twas Helen's,
Whoever gave it you. Then, if you know
That you are well acquainted with yourself,
Confess 'twas hers, and by what rough enforcement
You got it from her: she call'd the saints to surety
That she would never put it from her finger,
Unless she gave it to yourself in bed,
Where you have never come, or sent it us
Upon her great disaster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: She never saw it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Thou speak'st it falsely, as I love mine honour;
And makest conjectural fears to come into me
Which I would fain shut out. If it should prove
That thou art so inhuman,--'twill not prove so;--
And yet I know not: thou didst hate her deadly,
And she is dead; which nothing, but to close
Her eyes myself, could win me to believe,
More than to see this ring. Take him away.
My fore-past proofs, howe'er the matter fall,
Shall tax my fears of little vanity,
Having vainly fear'd too little. Away with him!
We'll sift this matter further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: If you shall prove
This ring was ever hers, you shall as easy
Prove that I husbanded her bed in Florence,
Where yet she never was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: I am wrapp'd in dismal thinkings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Gracious sovereign,
Whether I have been to blame or no, I know not:
Here's a petition from a Florentine,
Who hath for four or five removes come short
To tender it herself. I undertook it,
Vanquish'd thereto by the fair grace and speech
Of the poor suppliant, who by this I know
Is here attending: her business looks in her
With an importing visage; and she told me,
In a sweet verbal brief, it did concern
Your highness with herself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Reads Upon his many protestations to marry me
when his wife was dead, I blush to say it, he won
me. Now is the Count Rousillon a widower: his vows
are forfeited to me, and my honour's paid to him. He
stole from Florence, taking no leave, and I follow
him to his country for justice: grant it me, O
king! in you it best lies; otherwise a seducer
flourishes, and a poor maid is undone.
DIANA CAPILET.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: I will buy me a son-in-law in a fair, and toll for
this: I'll none of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: The heavens have thought well on thee Lafeu,
To bring forth this discovery. Seek these suitors:
Go speedily and bring again the count.
I am afeard the life of Helen, lady,
Was foully snatch'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COUNTESS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, justice on the doers!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder, sir, sith wives are monsters to you,
And that you fly them as you swear them lordship,
Yet you desire to marry.
What woman's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I am, my lord, a wretched Florentine,
Derived from the ancient Capilet:
My suit, as I do understand, you know,
And therefore know how far I may be pitied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: I am her mother, sir, whose age and honour
Both suffer under this complaint we bring,
And both shall cease, without your remedy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, count; do you know these women?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I neither can nor will deny
But that I know them: do they charge me further?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Why do you look so strange upon your wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: She's none of mine, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: If you shall marry,
You give away this hand, and that is mine;
You give away heaven's vows, and those are mine;
You give away myself, which is known mine;
For I by vow am so embodied yours,
That she which marries you must marry me,
Either both or none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: Your reputation comes too short for my daughter; you
are no husband for her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, this is a fond and desperate creature,
Whom sometime I have laugh'd with: let your highness
Lay a more noble thought upon mine honour
Than for to think that I would sink it here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, for my thoughts, you have them ill to friend
Till your deeds gain them: fairer prove your honour
Than in my thought it lies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Good my lord,
Ask him upon his oath, if he does think
He had not my virginity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: What say'st thou to her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: She's impudent, my lord,
And was a common gamester to the camp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: He does me wrong, my lord; if I were so,
He might have bought me at a common price:
Do not believe him. O, behold this ring,
Whose high respect and rich validity
Did lack a parallel; yet for all that
He gave it to a commoner o' the camp,
If I be one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COUNTESS
SPEECH.LINE: He blushes, and 'tis it:
Of six preceding ancestors, that gem,
Conferr'd by testament to the sequent issue,
Hath it been owed and worn. This is his wife;
That ring's a thousand proofs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Methought you said
You saw one here in court could witness it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I did, my lord, but loath am to produce
So bad an instrument: his name's Parolles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: I saw the man to-day, if man he be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Find him, and bring him hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: What of him?
He's quoted for a most perfidious slave,
With all the spots o' the world tax'd and debosh'd;
Whose nature sickens but to speak a truth.
Am I or that or this for what he'll utter,
That will speak any thing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: She hath that ring of yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: I think she has: certain it is I liked her,
And boarded her i' the wanton way of youth:
She knew her distance and did angle for me,
Madding my eagerness with her restraint,
As all impediments in fancy's course
Are motives of more fancy; and, in fine,
Her infinite cunning, with her modern grace,
Subdued me to her rate: she got the ring;
And I had that which any inferior might
At market-price have bought.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I must be patient:
You, that have turn'd off a first so noble wife,
May justly diet me. I pray you yet;
Since you lack virtue, I will lose a husband;
Send for your ring, I will return it home,
And give me mine again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: I have it not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: What ring was yours, I pray you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, much like
The same upon your finger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Know you this ring? this ring was his of late.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: And this was it I gave him, being abed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: The story then goes false, you threw it him
Out of a casement.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I have spoke the truth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I do confess the ring was hers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: You boggle shrewdly, every feather stars you.
Is this the man you speak of?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me, sirrah, but tell me true, I charge you,
Not fearing the displeasure of your master,
Which on your just proceeding I'll keep off,
By him and by this woman here what know you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: So please your majesty, my master hath been an
honourable gentleman: tricks he hath had in him,
which gentlemen have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, to the purpose: did he love this woman?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, sir, he did love her; but how?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: How, I pray you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: He did love her, sir, as a gentleman loves a woman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: How is that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: He loved her, sir, and loved her not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: As thou art a knave, and no knave. What an
equivocal companion is this!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: I am a poor man, and at your majesty's command.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: He's a good drum, my lord, but a naughty orator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Do you know he promised me marriage?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, I know more than I'll speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: But wilt thou not speak all thou knowest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAROLLES
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, so please your majesty. I did go between them,
as I said; but more than that, he loved her: for
indeed he was mad for her, and talked of Satan and
of Limbo and of Furies and I know not what: yet I
was in that credit with them at that time that I
knew of their going to bed, and of other motions,
as promising her marriage, and things which would
derive me ill will to speak of; therefore I will not
speak what I know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast spoken all already, unless thou canst say
they are married: but thou art too fine in thy
evidence; therefore stand aside.
This ring, you say, was yours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Where did you buy it? or who gave it you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: It was not given me, nor I did not buy it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Who lent it you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: It was not lent me neither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Where did you find it, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I found it not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: If it were yours by none of all these ways,
How could you give it him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I never gave it him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: This woman's an easy glove, my lord; she goes off
and on at pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: This ring was mine; I gave it his first wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: It might be yours or hers, for aught I know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Take her away; I do not like her now;
To prison with her: and away with him.
Unless thou tell'st me where thou hadst this ring,
Thou diest within this hour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll never tell you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Take her away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll put in bail, my liege.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: I think thee now some common customer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: By Jove, if ever I knew man, 'twas you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore hast thou accused him all this while?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Because he's guilty, and he is not guilty:
He knows I am no maid, and he'll swear to't;
I'll swear I am a maid, and he knows not.
Great king, I am no strumpet, by my life;
I am either maid, or else this old man's wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: She does abuse our ears: to prison with her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: Good mother, fetch my bail. Stay, royal sir:
The jeweller that owes the ring is sent for,
And he shall surety me. But for this lord,
Who hath abused me, as he knows himself,
Though yet he never harm'd me, here I quit him:
He knows himself my bed he hath defiled;
And at that time he got his wife with child:
Dead though she be, she feels her young one kick:
So there's my riddle: one that's dead is quick:
And now behold the meaning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Is there no exorcist
Beguiles the truer office of mine eyes?
Is't real that I see?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELENA
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord;
'Tis but the shadow of a wife you see,
The name and not the thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: Both, both. O, pardon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELENA
SPEECH.LINE: O my good lord, when I was like this maid,
I found you wondrous kind. There is your ring;
And, look you, here's your letter; this it says:
'When from my finger you can get this ring
And are by me with child,' &c. This is done:
Will you be mine, now you are doubly won?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BERTRAM
SPEECH.LINE: If she, my liege, can make me know this clearly,
I'll love her dearly, ever, ever dearly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELENA
SPEECH.LINE: If it appear not plain and prove untrue,
Deadly divorce step between me and you!
O my dear mother, do I see you living?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAFEU
SPEECH.LINE: Mine eyes smell onions; I shall weep anon:
Good Tom Drum, lend me a handkercher: so,
I thank thee: wait on me home, I'll make sport with thee:
Let thy courtesies alone, they are scurvy ones.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: Let us from point to point this story know,
To make the even truth in pleasure flow.
If thou be'st yet a fresh uncropped flower,
Choose thou thy husband, and I'll pay thy dower;
For I can guess that by thy honest aid
Thou keep'st a wife herself, thyself a maid.
Of that and all the progress, more or less,
Resolvedly more leisure shall express:
All yet seems well; and if it end so meet,
The bitter past, more welcome is the sweet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING
SPEECH.LINE: The king's a beggar, now the play is done:
All is well ended, if this suit be won,
That you express content; which we will pay,
With strife to please you, day exceeding day:
Ours be your patience then, and yours our parts;
Your gentle hands lend us, and take our hearts.

PLAY.TITLE: As You Like It

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: DUKE FREDERICK, his brother, an usurper of his dominions.

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: lords attending on the banished duke.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: LE BEAU, a courtier attending upon Frederick.

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: sons of Sir Rowland de Boys.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: WILLIAM, a country fellow in love with Audrey.
ROSALIND, daughter to the banished duke.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE Oliver's house; Duke Frederick's court; and the Forest of Arden.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Orchard of Oliver's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: As I remember, Adam, it was upon this fashion
bequeathed me by will but poor a thousand crowns,
and, as thou sayest, charged my brother, on his
blessing, to breed me well: and there begins my
sadness. My brother Jaques he keeps at school, and
report speaks goldenly of his profit: for my part,
he keeps me rustically at home, or, to speak more
properly, stays me here at home unkept; for call you
that keeping for a gentleman of my birth, that
differs not from the stalling of an ox? His horses
are bred better; for, besides that they are fair
with their feeding, they are taught their manage,
and to that end riders dearly hired: but I, his
brother, gain nothing under him but growth; for the
which his animals on his dunghills are as much
bound to him as I. Besides this nothing that he so
plentifully gives me, the something that nature gave
me his countenance seems to take from me: he lets
me feed with his hinds, bars me the place of a
brother, and, as much as in him lies, mines my
gentility with my education. This is it, Adam, that
grieves me; and the spirit of my father, which I
think is within me, begins to mutiny against this
servitude: I will no longer endure it, though yet I
know no wise remedy how to avoid it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: Yonder comes my master, your brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Go apart, Adam, and thou shalt hear how he will
shake me up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Now, sir! what make you here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing: I am not taught to make any thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: What mar you then, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, I am helping you to mar that which God
made, a poor unworthy brother of yours, with idleness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, be better employed, and be naught awhile.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I keep your hogs and eat husks with them?
What prodigal portion have I spent, that I should
come to such penury?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Know you where your are, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, very well; here in your orchard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Know you before whom, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, better than him I am before knows me. I know
you are my eldest brother; and, in the gentle
condition of blood, you should so know me. The
courtesy of nations allows you my better, in that
you are the first-born; but the same tradition
takes not away my blood, were there twenty brothers
betwixt us: I have as much of my father in me as
you; albeit, I confess, your coming before me is
nearer to his reverence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: What, boy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, elder brother, you are too young in this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Wilt thou lay hands on me, villain?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I am no villain; I am the youngest son of Sir
Rowland de Boys; he was my father, and he is thrice
a villain that says such a father begot villains.
Wert thou not my brother, I would not take this hand
from thy throat till this other had pulled out thy
tongue for saying so: thou hast railed on thyself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet masters, be patient: for your father's
remembrance, be at accord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Let me go, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I will not, till I please: you shall hear me. My
father charged you in his will to give me good
education: you have trained me like a peasant,
obscuring and hiding from me all gentleman-like
qualities. The spirit of my father grows strong in
me, and I will no longer endure it: therefore allow
me such exercises as may become a gentleman, or
give me the poor allottery my father left me by
testament; with that I will go buy my fortunes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: And what wilt thou do? beg, when that is spent?
Well, sir, get you in: I will not long be troubled
with you; you shall have some part of your will: I
pray you, leave me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I will no further offend you than becomes me for my good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Get you with him, you old dog.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: Is 'old dog' my reward? Most true, I have lost my
teeth in your service. God be with my old master!
he would not have spoke such a word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Is it even so? begin you to grow upon me? I will
physic your rankness, and yet give no thousand
crowns neither. Holla, Dennis!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DENNIS
SPEECH.LINE: Calls your worship?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Was not Charles, the duke's wrestler, here to speak with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DENNIS
SPEECH.LINE: So please you, he is here at the door and importunes
access to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Call him in.
'Twill be a good way; and to-morrow the wrestling is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow to your worship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Good Monsieur Charles, what's the new news at the
new court?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: There's no news at the court, sir, but the old news:
that is, the old duke is banished by his younger
brother the new duke; and three or four loving lords
have put themselves into voluntary exile with him,
whose lands and revenues enrich the new duke;
therefore he gives them good leave to wander.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Can you tell if Rosalind, the duke's daughter, be
banished with her father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: O, no; for the duke's daughter, her cousin, so loves
her, being ever from their cradles bred together,
that she would have followed her exile, or have died
to stay behind her. She is at the court, and no
less beloved of her uncle than his own daughter; and
never two ladies loved as they do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Where will the old duke live?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: They say he is already in the forest of Arden, and
a many merry men with him; and there they live like
the old Robin Hood of England: they say many young
gentlemen flock to him every day, and fleet the time
carelessly, as they did in the golden world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: What, you wrestle to-morrow before the new duke?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, do I, sir; and I came to acquaint you with a
matter. I am given, sir, secretly to understand
that your younger brother Orlando hath a disposition
to come in disguised against me to try a fall.
To-morrow, sir, I wrestle for my credit; and he that
escapes me without some broken limb shall acquit him
well. Your brother is but young and tender; and,
for your love, I would be loath to foil him, as I
must, for my own honour, if he come in: therefore,
out of my love to you, I came hither to acquaint you
withal, that either you might stay him from his
intendment or brook such disgrace well as he shall
run into, in that it is a thing of his own search
and altogether against my will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Charles, I thank thee for thy love to me, which
thou shalt find I will most kindly requite. I had
myself notice of my brother's purpose herein and
have by underhand means laboured to dissuade him from
it, but he is resolute. I'll tell thee, Charles:
it is the stubbornest young fellow of France, full
of ambition, an envious emulator of every man's
good parts, a secret and villanous contriver against
me his natural brother: therefore use thy
discretion; I had as lief thou didst break his neck
as his finger. And thou wert best look to't; for if
thou dost him any slight disgrace or if he do not
mightily grace himself on thee, he will practise
against thee by poison, entrap thee by some
treacherous device and never leave thee till he
hath ta'en thy life by some indirect means or other;
for, I assure thee, and almost with tears I speak
it, there is not one so young and so villanous this
day living. I speak but brotherly of him; but
should I anatomize him to thee as he is, I must
blush and weep and thou must look pale and wonder.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: I am heartily glad I came hither to you. If he come
to-morrow, I'll give him his payment: if ever he go
alone again, I'll never wrestle for prize more: and
so God keep your worship!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVER
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, good Charles.
Now will I stir this gamester: I hope I shall see
an end of him; for my soul, yet I know not why,
hates nothing more than he. Yet he's gentle, never
schooled and yet learned, full of noble device, of
all sorts enchantingly beloved, and indeed so much
in the heart of the world, and especially of my own
people, who best know him, that I am altogether
misprised: but it shall not be so long; this
wrestler shall clear all: nothing remains but that
I kindle the boy thither; which now I'll go about.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Lawn before the Duke's palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, Rosalind, sweet my coz, be merry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Dear Celia, I show more mirth than I am mistress of;
and would you yet I were merrier? Unless you could
teach me to forget a banished father, you must not
learn me how to remember any extraordinary pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Herein I see thou lovest me not with the full weight
that I love thee. If my uncle, thy banished father,
had banished thy uncle, the duke my father, so thou
hadst been still with me, I could have taught my
love to take thy father for mine: so wouldst thou,
if the truth of thy love to me were so righteously
tempered as mine is to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will forget the condition of my estate, to
rejoice in yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: You know my father hath no child but I, nor none is
like to have: and, truly, when he dies, thou shalt
be his heir, for what he hath taken away from thy
father perforce, I will render thee again in
affection; by mine honour, I will; and when I break
that oath, let me turn monster: therefore, my
sweet Rose, my dear Rose, be merry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: From henceforth I will, coz, and devise sports. Let
me see; what think you of falling in love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, I prithee, do, to make sport withal: but
love no man in good earnest; nor no further in sport
neither than with safety of a pure blush thou mayst
in honour come off again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: What shall be our sport, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Let us sit and mock the good housewife Fortune from
her wheel, that her gifts may henceforth be bestowed equally.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I would we could do so, for her benefits are
mightily misplaced, and the bountiful blind woman
doth most mistake in her gifts to women.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true; for those that she makes fair she scarce
makes honest, and those that she makes honest she
makes very ill-favouredly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, now thou goest from Fortune's office to
Nature's: Fortune reigns in gifts of the world,
not in the lineaments of Nature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: No? when Nature hath made a fair creature, may she
not by Fortune fall into the fire? Though Nature
hath given us wit to flout at Fortune, hath not
Fortune sent in this fool to cut off the argument?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, there is Fortune too hard for Nature, when
Fortune makes Nature's natural the cutter-off of
Nature's wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Peradventure this is not Fortune's work neither, but
Nature's; who perceiveth our natural wits too dull
to reason of such goddesses and hath sent this
natural for our whetstone; for always the dulness of
the fool is the whetstone of the wits. How now,
wit! whither wander you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress, you must come away to your father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Were you made the messenger?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: No, by mine honour, but I was bid to come for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Where learned you that oath, fool?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Of a certain knight that swore by his honour they
were good pancakes and swore by his honour the
mustard was naught: now I'll stand to it, the
pancakes were naught and the mustard was good, and
yet was not the knight forsworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: How prove you that, in the great heap of your
knowledge?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry, now unmuzzle your wisdom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Stand you both forth now: stroke your chins, and
swear by your beards that I am a knave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: By our beards, if we had them, thou art.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: By my knavery, if I had it, then I were; but if you
swear by that that is not, you are not forsworn: no
more was this knight swearing by his honour, for he
never had any; or if he had, he had sworn it away
before ever he saw those pancakes or that mustard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, who is't that thou meanest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: One that old Frederick, your father, loves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: My father's love is enough to honour him: enough!
speak no more of him; you'll be whipped for taxation
one of these days.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: The more pity, that fools may not speak wisely what
wise men do foolishly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, thou sayest true; for since the little
wit that fools have was silenced, the little foolery
that wise men have makes a great show. Here comes
Monsieur Le Beau.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: With his mouth full of news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Which he will put on us, as pigeons feed their young.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Then shall we be news-crammed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: All the better; we shall be the more marketable.
Bon jour, Monsieur Le Beau: what's the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Fair princess, you have lost much good sport.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sport! of what colour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: What colour, madam! how shall I answer you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: As wit and fortune will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Or as the Destinies decree.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Well said: that was laid on with a trowel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, if I keep not my rank,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Thou losest thy old smell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: You amaze me, ladies: I would have told you of good
wrestling, which you have lost the sight of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: You tell us the manner of the wrestling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: I will tell you the beginning; and, if it please
your ladyships, you may see the end; for the best is
yet to do; and here, where you are, they are coming
to perform it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, the beginning, that is dead and buried.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: There comes an old man and his three sons,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I could match this beginning with an old tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Three proper young men, of excellent growth and presence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: With bills on their necks, 'Be it known unto all men
by these presents.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: The eldest of the three wrestled with Charles, the
duke's wrestler; which Charles in a moment threw him
and broke three of his ribs, that there is little
hope of life in him: so he served the second, and
so the third. Yonder they lie; the poor old man,
their father, making such pitiful dole over them
that all the beholders take his part with weeping.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Alas!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: But what is the sport, monsieur, that the ladies
have lost?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this that I speak of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Thus men may grow wiser every day: it is the first
time that ever I heard breaking of ribs was sport
for ladies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Or I, I promise thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: But is there any else longs to see this broken music
in his sides? is there yet another dotes upon
rib-breaking? Shall we see this wrestling, cousin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: You must, if you stay here; for here is the place
appointed for the wrestling, and they are ready to
perform it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Yonder, sure, they are coming: let us now stay and see it.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter DUKE FREDERICK, Lords, ORLANDO, CHARLES, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Come on: since the youth will not be entreated, his
own peril on his forwardness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Is yonder the man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Even he, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, he is too young! yet he looks successfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: How now, daughter and cousin! are you crept hither
to see the wrestling?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my liege, so please you give us leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: You will take little delight in it, I can tell you;
there is such odds in the man. In pity of the
challenger's youth I would fain dissuade him, but he
will not be entreated. Speak to him, ladies; see if
you can move him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Call him hither, good Monsieur Le Beau.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Do so: I'll not be by.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Monsieur the challenger, the princesses call for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I attend them with all respect and duty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Young man, have you challenged Charles the wrestler?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: No, fair princess; he is the general challenger: I
come but in, as others do, to try with him the
strength of my youth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Young gentleman, your spirits are too bold for your
years. You have seen cruel proof of this man's
strength: if you saw yourself with your eyes or
knew yourself with your judgment, the fear of your
adventure would counsel you to a more equal
enterprise. We pray you, for your own sake, to
embrace your own safety and give over this attempt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Do, young sir; your reputation shall not therefore
be misprised: we will make it our suit to the duke
that the wrestling might not go forward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you, punish me not with your hard
thoughts; wherein I confess me much guilty, to deny
so fair and excellent ladies any thing. But let
your fair eyes and gentle wishes go with me to my
trial: wherein if I be foiled, there is but one
shamed that was never gracious; if killed, but one
dead that was willing to be so: I shall do my
friends no wrong, for I have none to lament me, the
world no injury, for in it I have nothing; only in
the world I fill up a place, which may be better
supplied when I have made it empty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: The little strength that I have, I would it were with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: And mine, to eke out hers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well: pray heaven I be deceived in you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Your heart's desires be with you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, where is this young gallant that is so
desirous to lie with his mother earth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Ready, sir; but his will hath in it a more modest working.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: You shall try but one fall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHARLES
SPEECH.LINE: No, I warrant your grace, you shall not entreat him
to a second, that have so mightily persuaded him
from a first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: An you mean to mock me after, you should not have
mocked me before: but come your ways.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Now Hercules be thy speed, young man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I would I were invisible, to catch the strong
fellow by the leg.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: O excellent young man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: If I had a thunderbolt in mine eye, I can tell who
should down.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: No more, no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, I beseech your grace: I am not yet well breathed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: How dost thou, Charles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: He cannot speak, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Bear him away. What is thy name, young man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Orlando, my liege; the youngest son of Sir Rowland de Boys.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: I would thou hadst been son to some man else:
The world esteem'd thy father honourable,
But I did find him still mine enemy:
Thou shouldst have better pleased me with this deed,
Hadst thou descended from another house.
But fare thee well; thou art a gallant youth:
I would thou hadst told me of another father.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt DUKE FREDERICK, train, and LE BEAU

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Were I my father, coz, would I do this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I am more proud to be Sir Rowland's son,
His youngest son; and would not change that calling,
To be adopted heir to Frederick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: My father loved Sir Rowland as his soul,
And all the world was of my father's mind:
Had I before known this young man his son,
I should have given him tears unto entreaties,
Ere he should thus have ventured.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Gentle cousin,
Let us go thank him and encourage him:
My father's rough and envious disposition
Sticks me at heart. Sir, you have well deserved:
If you do keep your promises in love
But justly, as you have exceeded all promise,
Your mistress shall be happy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Gentleman,
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Giving him a chain from her neck
SPEECH.LINE: Wear this for me, one out of suits with fortune,
That could give more, but that her hand lacks means.
Shall we go, coz?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay. Fare you well, fair gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Can I not say, I thank you? My better parts
Are all thrown down, and that which here stands up
Is but a quintain, a mere lifeless block.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: He calls us back: my pride fell with my fortunes;
I'll ask him what he would. Did you call, sir?
Sir, you have wrestled well and overthrown
More than your enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Will you go, coz?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Have with you. Fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: What passion hangs these weights upon my tongue?
I cannot speak to her, yet she urged conference.
O poor Orlando, thou art overthrown!
Or Charles or something weaker masters thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Good sir, I do in friendship counsel you
To leave this place. Albeit you have deserved
High commendation, true applause and love,
Yet such is now the duke's condition
That he misconstrues all that you have done.
The duke is humorous; what he is indeed,
More suits you to conceive than I to speak of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, sir: and, pray you, tell me this:
Which of the two was daughter of the duke
That here was at the wrestling?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LE BEAU
SPEECH.LINE: Neither his daughter, if we judge by manners;
But yet indeed the lesser is his daughter
The other is daughter to the banish'd duke,
And here detain'd by her usurping uncle,
To keep his daughter company; whose loves
Are dearer than the natural bond of sisters.
But I can tell you that of late this duke
Hath ta'en displeasure 'gainst his gentle niece,
Grounded upon no other argument
But that the people praise her for her virtues
And pity her for her good father's sake;
And, on my life, his malice 'gainst the lady
Will suddenly break forth. Sir, fare you well:
Hereafter, in a better world than this,
I shall desire more love and knowledge of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I rest much bounden to you: fare you well.
Thus must I from the smoke into the smother;
From tyrant duke unto a tyrant brother:
But heavenly Rosalind!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A room in the palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, cousin! why, Rosalind! Cupid have mercy! not a word?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Not one to throw at a dog.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: No, thy words are too precious to be cast away upon
curs; throw some of them at me; come, lame me with reasons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Then there were two cousins laid up; when the one
should be lamed with reasons and the other mad
without any.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: But is all this for your father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: No, some of it is for my child's father. O, how
full of briers is this working-day world!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: They are but burs, cousin, thrown upon thee in
holiday foolery: if we walk not in the trodden
paths our very petticoats will catch them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I could shake them off my coat: these burs are in my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Hem them away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I would try, if I could cry 'hem' and have him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, wrestle with thy affections.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: O, they take the part of a better wrestler than myself!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, a good wish upon you! you will try in time, in
despite of a fall. But, turning these jests out of
service, let us talk in good earnest: is it
possible, on such a sudden, you should fall into so
strong a liking with old Sir Rowland's youngest son?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: The duke my father loved his father dearly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Doth it therefore ensue that you should love his son
dearly? By this kind of chase, I should hate him,
for my father hated his father dearly; yet I hate
not Orlando.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: No, faith, hate him not, for my sake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why should I not? doth he not deserve well?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Let me love him for that, and do you love him
because I do. Look, here comes the duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: With his eyes full of anger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress, dispatch you with your safest haste
And get you from our court.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Me, uncle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: You, cousin
Within these ten days if that thou be'st found
So near our public court as twenty miles,
Thou diest for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I do beseech your grace,
Let me the knowledge of my fault bear with me:
If with myself I hold intelligence
Or have acquaintance with mine own desires,
If that I do not dream or be not frantic,--
As I do trust I am not--then, dear uncle,
Never so much as in a thought unborn
Did I offend your highness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thus do all traitors:
If their purgation did consist in words,
They are as innocent as grace itself:
Let it suffice thee that I trust thee not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Yet your mistrust cannot make me a traitor:
Tell me whereon the likelihood depends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art thy father's daughter; there's enough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: So was I when your highness took his dukedom;
So was I when your highness banish'd him:
Treason is not inherited, my lord;
Or, if we did derive it from our friends,
What's that to me? my father was no traitor:
Then, good my liege, mistake me not so much
To think my poverty is treacherous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Dear sovereign, hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Celia; we stay'd her for your sake,
Else had she with her father ranged along.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I did not then entreat to have her stay;
It was your pleasure and your own remorse:
I was too young that time to value her;
But now I know her: if she be a traitor,
Why so am I; we still have slept together,
Rose at an instant, learn'd, play'd, eat together,
And wheresoever we went, like Juno's swans,
Still we went coupled and inseparable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: She is too subtle for thee; and her smoothness,
Her very silence and her patience
Speak to the people, and they pity her.
Thou art a fool: she robs thee of thy name;
And thou wilt show more bright and seem more virtuous
When she is gone. Then open not thy lips:
Firm and irrevocable is my doom
Which I have pass'd upon her; she is banish'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Pronounce that sentence then on me, my liege:
I cannot live out of her company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: You are a fool. You, niece, provide yourself:
If you outstay the time, upon mine honour,
And in the greatness of my word, you die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: O my poor Rosalind, whither wilt thou go?
Wilt thou change fathers? I will give thee mine.
I charge thee, be not thou more grieved than I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I have more cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast not, cousin;
Prithee be cheerful: know'st thou not, the duke
Hath banish'd me, his daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: That he hath not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: No, hath not? Rosalind lacks then the love
Which teacheth thee that thou and I am one:
Shall we be sunder'd? shall we part, sweet girl?
No: let my father seek another heir.
Therefore devise with me how we may fly,
Whither to go and what to bear with us;
And do not seek to take your change upon you,
To bear your griefs yourself and leave me out;
For, by this heaven, now at our sorrows pale,
Say what thou canst, I'll go along with thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Why, whither shall we go?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: To seek my uncle in the forest of Arden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, what danger will it be to us,
Maids as we are, to travel forth so far!
Beauty provoketh thieves sooner than gold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll put myself in poor and mean attire
And with a kind of umber smirch my face;
The like do you: so shall we pass along
And never stir assailants.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Were it not better,
Because that I am more than common tall,
That I did suit me all points like a man?
A gallant curtle-axe upon my thigh,
A boar-spear in my hand; and--in my heart
Lie there what hidden woman's fear there will--
We'll have a swashing and a martial outside,
As many other mannish cowards have
That do outface it with their semblances.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: What shall I call thee when thou art a man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have no worse a name than Jove's own page;
And therefore look you call me Ganymede.
But what will you be call'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: Something that hath a reference to my state
No longer Celia, but Aliena.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: But, cousin, what if we assay'd to steal
The clownish fool out of your father's court?
Would he not be a comfort to our travel?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: He'll go along o'er the wide world with me;
Leave me alone to woo him. Let's away,
And get our jewels and our wealth together,
Devise the fittest time and safest way
To hide us from pursuit that will be made
After my flight. Now go we in content
To liberty and not to banishment.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The Forest of Arden.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DUKE SENIOR, AMIENS, and two or three Lords, like foresters

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Now, my co-mates and brothers in exile,
Hath not old custom made this life more sweet
Than that of painted pomp? Are not these woods
More free from peril than the envious court?
Here feel we but the penalty of Adam,
The seasons' difference, as the icy fang
And churlish chiding of the winter's wind,
Which, when it bites and blows upon my body,
Even till I shrink with cold, I smile and say
'This is no flattery: these are counsellors
That feelingly persuade me what I am.'
Sweet are the uses of adversity,
Which, like the toad, ugly and venomous,
Wears yet a precious jewel in his head;
And this our life exempt from public haunt
Finds tongues in trees, books in the running brooks,
Sermons in stones and good in every thing.
I would not change it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: Happy is your grace,
That can translate the stubbornness of fortune
Into so quiet and so sweet a style.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Come, shall we go and kill us venison?
And yet it irks me the poor dappled fools,
Being native burghers of this desert city,
Should in their own confines with forked heads
Have their round haunches gored.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, my lord,
The melancholy Jaques grieves at that,
And, in that kind, swears you do more usurp
Than doth your brother that hath banish'd you.
To-day my Lord of Amiens and myself
Did steal behind him as he lay along
Under an oak whose antique root peeps out
Upon the brook that brawls along this wood:
To the which place a poor sequester'd stag,
That from the hunter's aim had ta'en a hurt,
Did come to languish, and indeed, my lord,
The wretched animal heaved forth such groans
That their discharge did stretch his leathern coat
Almost to bursting, and the big round tears
Coursed one another down his innocent nose
In piteous chase; and thus the hairy fool
Much marked of the melancholy Jaques,
Stood on the extremest verge of the swift brook,
Augmenting it with tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: But what said Jaques?
Did he not moralize this spectacle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: O, yes, into a thousand similes.
First, for his weeping into the needless stream;
'Poor deer,' quoth he, 'thou makest a testament
As worldlings do, giving thy sum of more
To that which had too much:' then, being there alone,
Left and abandon'd of his velvet friends,
''Tis right:' quoth he; 'thus misery doth part
The flux of company:' anon a careless herd,
Full of the pasture, jumps along by him
And never stays to greet him; 'Ay' quoth Jaques,
'Sweep on, you fat and greasy citizens;
'Tis just the fashion: wherefore do you look
Upon that poor and broken bankrupt there?'
Thus most invectively he pierceth through
The body of the country, city, court,
Yea, and of this our life, swearing that we
Are mere usurpers, tyrants and what's worse,
To fright the animals and to kill them up
In their assign'd and native dwelling-place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: And did you leave him in this contemplation?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: We did, my lord, weeping and commenting
Upon the sobbing deer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Show me the place:
I love to cope him in these sullen fits,
For then he's full of matter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I'll bring you to him straight.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A room in the palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Can it be possible that no man saw them?
It cannot be: some villains of my court
Are of consent and sufferance in this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot hear of any that did see her.
The ladies, her attendants of her chamber,
Saw her abed, and in the morning early
They found the bed untreasured of their mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, the roynish clown, at whom so oft
Your grace was wont to laugh, is also missing.
Hisperia, the princess' gentlewoman,
Confesses that she secretly o'erheard
Your daughter and her cousin much commend
The parts and graces of the wrestler
That did but lately foil the sinewy Charles;
And she believes, wherever they are gone,
That youth is surely in their company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE FREDERICK
SPEECH.LINE: Send to his brother; fetch that gallant hither;
If he be absent, bring his brother to me;
I'll make him find him: do this suddenly,
And let not search and inquisition quail
To bring again these foolish runaways.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Before OLIVER'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Who's there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: What, my young master? O, my gentle master!
O my sweet master! O you memory
Of old Sir Rowland! why, what make you here?
Why are you virtuous? why do people love you?
And wherefore are you gentle, strong and valiant?
Why would you be so fond to overcome
The bonny priser of the humorous duke?
Your praise is come too swiftly home before you.
Know you not, master, to some kind of men
Their graces serve them but as enemies?
No more do yours: your virtues, gentle master,
Are sanctified and holy traitors to you.
O, what a world is this, when what is comely
Envenoms him that bears it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: O unhappy youth!
Come not within these doors; within this roof
The enemy of all your graces lives:
Your brother--no, no brother; yet the son--
Yet not the son, I will not call him son
Of him I was about to call his father--
Hath heard your praises, and this night he means
To burn the lodging where you use to lie
And you within it: if he fail of that,
He will have other means to cut you off.
I overheard him and his practises.
This is no place; this house is but a butchery:
Abhor it, fear it, do not enter it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, whither, Adam, wouldst thou have me go?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: No matter whither, so you come not here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: What, wouldst thou have me go and beg my food?
Or with a base and boisterous sword enforce
A thievish living on the common road?
This I must do, or know not what to do:
Yet this I will not do, do how I can;
I rather will subject me to the malice
Of a diverted blood and bloody brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: But do not so. I have five hundred crowns,
The thrifty hire I saved under your father,
Which I did store to be my foster-nurse
When service should in my old limbs lie lame
And unregarded age in corners thrown:
Take that, and He that doth the ravens feed,
Yea, providently caters for the sparrow,
Be comfort to my age! Here is the gold;
And all this I give you. Let me be your servant:
Though I look old, yet I am strong and lusty;
For in my youth I never did apply
Hot and rebellious liquors in my blood,
Nor did not with unbashful forehead woo
The means of weakness and debility;
Therefore my age is as a lusty winter,
Frosty, but kindly: let me go with you;
I'll do the service of a younger man
In all your business and necessities.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: O good old man, how well in thee appears
The constant service of the antique world,
When service sweat for duty, not for meed!
Thou art not for the fashion of these times,
Where none will sweat but for promotion,
And having that, do choke their service up
Even with the having: it is not so with thee.
But, poor old man, thou prunest a rotten tree,
That cannot so much as a blossom yield
In lieu of all thy pains and husbandry
But come thy ways; well go along together,
And ere we have thy youthful wages spent,
We'll light upon some settled low content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: Master, go on, and I will follow thee,
To the last gasp, with truth and loyalty.
From seventeen years till now almost fourscore
Here lived I, but now live here no more.
At seventeen years many their fortunes seek;
But at fourscore it is too late a week:
Yet fortune cannot recompense me better
Than to die well and not my master's debtor.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. The Forest of Arden.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter ROSALIND for Ganymede, CELIA for Aliena, and TOUCHSTONE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: O Jupiter, how weary are my spirits!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: I care not for my spirits, if my legs were not weary.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I could find in my heart to disgrace my man's
apparel and to cry like a woman; but I must comfort
the weaker vessel, as doublet and hose ought to show
itself courageous to petticoat: therefore courage,
good Aliena!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, bear with me; I cannot go no further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: For my part, I had rather bear with you than bear
you; yet I should bear no cross if I did bear you,
for I think you have no money in your purse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Well, this is the forest of Arden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, now am I in Arden; the more fool I; when I was
at home, I was in a better place: but travellers
must be content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, be so, good Touchstone.
Look you, who comes here; a young man and an old in
solemn talk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: That is the way to make her scorn you still.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Corin, that thou knew'st how I do love her!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: I partly guess; for I have loved ere now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, Corin, being old, thou canst not guess,
Though in thy youth thou wast as true a lover
As ever sigh'd upon a midnight pillow:
But if thy love were ever like to mine--
As sure I think did never man love so--
How many actions most ridiculous
Hast thou been drawn to by thy fantasy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: Into a thousand that I have forgotten.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, thou didst then ne'er love so heartily!
If thou remember'st not the slightest folly
That ever love did make thee run into,
Thou hast not loved:
Or if thou hast not sat as I do now,
Wearying thy hearer in thy mistress' praise,
Thou hast not loved:
Or if thou hast not broke from company
Abruptly, as my passion now makes me,
Thou hast not loved.
O Phebe, Phebe, Phebe!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, poor shepherd! searching of thy wound,
I have by hard adventure found mine own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: And I mine. I remember, when I was in love I broke
my sword upon a stone and bid him take that for
coming a-night to Jane Smile; and I remember the
kissing of her batlet and the cow's dugs that her
pretty chopt hands had milked; and I remember the
wooing of a peascod instead of her, from whom I took
two cods and, giving her them again, said with
weeping tears 'Wear these for my sake.' We that are
true lovers run into strange capers; but as all is
mortal in nature, so is all nature in love mortal in folly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Thou speakest wiser than thou art ware of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I shall ne'er be ware of mine own wit till I
break my shins against it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Jove, Jove! this shepherd's passion
Is much upon my fashion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: And mine; but it grows something stale with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, one of you question yond man
If he for gold will give us any food:
I faint almost to death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Holla, you clown!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, fool: he's not thy kinsman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: Who calls?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TOUCHSTONE
SPEECH.LINE: Your betters, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: Else are they very wretched.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, I say. Good even to you, friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: And to you, gentle sir, and to you all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee, shepherd, if that love or gold
Can in this desert place buy entertainment,
Bring us where we may rest ourselves and feed:
Here's a young maid with travel much oppress'd
And faints for succor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: Fair sir, I pity her
And wish, for her sake more than for mine own,
My fortunes were more able to relieve her;
But I am shepherd to another man
And do not shear the fleeces that I graze:
My master is of churlish disposition
And little recks to find the way to heaven
By doing deeds of hospitality:
Besides, his cote, his flocks and bounds of feed
Are now on sale, and at our sheepcote now,
By reason of his absence, there is nothing
That you will feed on; but what is, come see.
And in my voice most welcome shall you be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: What is he that shall buy his flock and pasture?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: That young swain that you saw here but erewhile,
That little cares for buying any thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALIND
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, if it stand with honesty,
Buy thou the cottage, pasture and the flock,
And thou shalt have to pay for it of us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CELIA
SPEECH.LINE: And we will mend thy wages. I like this place.
And willingly could waste my time in it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIN
SPEECH.LINE: Assuredly the thing is to be sold:
Go with me: if you like upon report
The soil, the profit and this kind of life,
I will your very faithful feeder be
And buy it with your gold right suddenly.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The Forest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: Under the greenwood tree
Who loves to lie with me,
And turn his merry note
Unto the sweet bird's throat,
Come hither, come hither, come hither:
Here shall he see No enemy
But winter and rough weather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: More, more, I prithee, more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: It will make you melancholy, Monsieur Jaques.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: I thank it. More, I prithee, more. I can suck
melancholy out of a song, as a weasel sucks eggs.
More, I prithee, more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: My voice is ragged: I know I cannot please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: I do not desire you to please me; I do desire you to
sing. Come, more; another stanzo: call you 'em stanzos?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: What you will, Monsieur Jaques.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I care not for their names; they owe me
nothing. Will you sing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: More at your request than to please myself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Well then, if ever I thank any man, I'll thank you;
but that they call compliment is like the encounter
of two dog-apes, and when a man thanks me heartily,
methinks I have given him a penny and he renders me
the beggarly thanks. Come, sing; and you that will
not, hold your tongues.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I'll end the song. Sirs, cover the while; the
duke will drink under this tree. He hath been all
this day to look you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: And I have been all this day to avoid him. He is
too disputable for my company: I think of as many
matters as he, but I give heaven thanks and make no
boast of them. Come, warble, come.
Who doth ambition shun
And loves to live i' the sun,
Seeking the food he eats
And pleased with what he gets,
Come hither, come hither, come hither:
Here shall he see No enemy
But winter and rough weather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: I'll give you a verse to this note that I made
yesterday in despite of my invention.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: And I'll sing it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Thus it goes:--
If it do come to pass
That any man turn ass,
Leaving his wealth and ease,
A stubborn will to please,
Ducdame, ducdame, ducdame:
Here shall he see
Gross fools as he,
An if he will come to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: What's that 'ducdame'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a Greek invocation, to call fools into a
circle. I'll go sleep, if I can; if I cannot, I'll
rail against all the first-born of Egypt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AMIENS
SPEECH.LINE: And I'll go seek the duke: his banquet is prepared.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. The forest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: Dear master, I can go no further. O, I die for food!
Here lie I down, and measure out my grave. Farewell,
kind master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, Adam! no greater heart in thee? Live
a little; comfort a little; cheer thyself a little.
If this uncouth forest yield any thing savage, I
will either be food for it or bring it for food to
thee. Thy conceit is nearer death than thy powers.
For my sake be comfortable; hold death awhile at
the arm's end: I will here be with thee presently;
and if I bring thee not something to eat, I will
give thee leave to die: but if thou diest before I
come, thou art a mocker of my labour. Well said!
thou lookest cheerly, and I'll be with thee quickly.
Yet thou liest in the bleak air: come, I will bear
thee to some shelter; and thou shalt not die for
lack of a dinner, if there live any thing in this
desert. Cheerly, good Adam!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VII. The forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: A table set out. Enter DUKE SENIOR, AMIENS, and Lords like outlaws

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: I think he be transform'd into a beast;
For I can no where find him like a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, he is but even now gone hence:
Here was he merry, hearing of a song.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: If he, compact of jars, grow musical,
We shall have shortly discord in the spheres.
Go, seek him: tell him I would speak with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: He saves my labour by his own approach.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, monsieur! what a life is this,
That your poor friends must woo your company?
What, you look merrily!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: A fool, a fool! I met a fool i' the forest,
A motley fool; a miserable world!
As I do live by food, I met a fool
Who laid him down and bask'd him in the sun,
And rail'd on Lady Fortune in good terms,
In good set terms and yet a motley fool.
'Good morrow, fool,' quoth I. 'No, sir,' quoth he,
'Call me not fool till heaven hath sent me fortune:'
And then he drew a dial from his poke,
And, looking on it with lack-lustre eye,
Says very wisely, 'It is ten o'clock:
Thus we may see,' quoth he, 'how the world wags:
'Tis but an hour ago since it was nine,
And after one hour more 'twill be eleven;
And so, from hour to hour, we ripe and ripe,
And then, from hour to hour, we rot and rot;
And thereby hangs a tale.' When I did hear
The motley fool thus moral on the time,
My lungs began to crow like chanticleer,
That fools should be so deep-contemplative,
And I did laugh sans intermission
An hour by his dial. O noble fool!
A worthy fool! Motley's the only wear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: What fool is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: O worthy fool! One that hath been a courtier,
And says, if ladies be but young and fair,
They have the gift to know it: and in his brain,
Which is as dry as the remainder biscuit
After a voyage, he hath strange places cramm'd
With observation, the which he vents
In mangled forms. O that I were a fool!
I am ambitious for a motley coat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt have one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: It is my only suit;
Provided that you weed your better judgments
Of all opinion that grows rank in them
That I am wise. I must have liberty
Withal, as large a charter as the wind,
To blow on whom I please; for so fools have;
And they that are most galled with my folly,
They most must laugh. And why, sir, must they so?
The 'why' is plain as way to parish church:
He that a fool doth very wisely hit
Doth very foolishly, although he smart,
Not to seem senseless of the bob: if not,
The wise man's folly is anatomized
Even by the squandering glances of the fool.
Invest me in my motley; give me leave
To speak my mind, and I will through and through
Cleanse the foul body of the infected world,
If they will patiently receive my medicine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Fie on thee! I can tell what thou wouldst do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: What, for a counter, would I do but good?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Most mischievous foul sin, in chiding sin:
For thou thyself hast been a libertine,
As sensual as the brutish sting itself;
And all the embossed sores and headed evils,
That thou with licence of free foot hast caught,
Wouldst thou disgorge into the general world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, who cries out on pride,
That can therein tax any private party?
Doth it not flow as hugely as the sea,
Till that the weary very means do ebb?
What woman in the city do I name,
When that I say the city-woman bears
The cost of princes on unworthy shoulders?
Who can come in and say that I mean her,
When such a one as she such is her neighbour?
Or what is he of basest function
That says his bravery is not of my cost,
Thinking that I mean him, but therein suits
His folly to the mettle of my speech?
There then; how then? what then? Let me see wherein
My tongue hath wrong'd him: if it do him right,
Then he hath wrong'd himself; if he be free,
Why then my taxing like a wild-goose flies,
Unclaim'd of any man. But who comes here?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter ORLANDO, with his sword drawn

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Forbear, and eat no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I have eat none yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Nor shalt not, till necessity be served.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: Of what kind should this cock come of?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou thus bolden'd, man, by thy distress,
Or else a rude despiser of good manners,
That in civility thou seem'st so empty?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: You touch'd my vein at first: the thorny point
Of bare distress hath ta'en from me the show
Of smooth civility: yet am I inland bred
And know some nurture. But forbear, I say:
He dies that touches any of this fruit
Till I and my affairs are answered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: An you will not be answered with reason, I must die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: What would you have? Your gentleness shall force
More than your force move us to gentleness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I almost die for food; and let me have it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Sit down and feed, and welcome to our table.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Speak you so gently? Pardon me, I pray you:
I thought that all things had been savage here;
And therefore put I on the countenance
Of stern commandment. But whate'er you are
That in this desert inaccessible,
Under the shade of melancholy boughs,
Lose and neglect the creeping hours of time
If ever you have look'd on better days,
If ever been where bells have knoll'd to church,
If ever sat at any good man's feast,
If ever from your eyelids wiped a tear
And know what 'tis to pity and be pitied,
Let gentleness my strong enforcement be:
In the which hope I blush, and hide my sword.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: True is it that we have seen better days,
And have with holy bell been knoll'd to church
And sat at good men's feasts and wiped our eyes
Of drops that sacred pity hath engender'd:
And therefore sit you down in gentleness
And take upon command what help we have
That to your wanting may be minister'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: Then but forbear your food a little while,
Whiles, like a doe, I go to find my fawn
And give it food. There is an old poor man,
Who after me hath many a weary step
Limp'd in pure love: till he be first sufficed,
Oppress'd with two weak evils, age and hunger,
I will not touch a bit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Go find him out,
And we will nothing waste till you return.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank ye; and be blest for your good comfort!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Thou seest we are not all alone unhappy:
This wide and universal theatre
Presents more woeful pageants than the scene
Wherein we play in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUES
SPEECH.LINE: All the world's a stage,
And all the men and women merely players:
They have their exits and their entrances;
And one man in his time plays many parts,
His acts being seven ages. At first the infant,
Mewling and puking in the nurse's arms.
And then the whining school-boy, with his satchel
And shining morning face, creeping like snail
Unwillingly to school. And then the lover,
Sighing like furnace, with a woeful ballad
Made to his mistress' eyebrow. Then a soldier,
Full of strange oaths and bearded like the pard,
Jealous in honour, sudden and quick in quarrel,
Seeking the bubble reputation
Even in the cannon's mouth. And then the justice,
In fair round belly with good capon lined,
With eyes severe and beard of formal cut,
Full of wise saws and modern instances;
And so he plays his part. The sixth age shifts
Into the lean and slipper'd pantaloon,
With spectacles on nose and pouch on side,
His youthful hose, well saved, a world too wide
For his shrunk shank; and his big manly voice,
Turning again toward childish treble, pipes
And whistles in his sound. Last scene of all,
That ends this strange eventful history,
Is second childishness and mere oblivion,
Sans teeth, sans eyes, sans taste, sans everything.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE SENIOR
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome. Set down your venerable burthen,
And let him feed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ORLANDO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you most for him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ADAM
SPEECH.LINE: So had you need:
