when she's fallen out with her husband. Your noble
Tullus Aufidius will appear well in these wars, his
great opposer, Coriolanus, being now in no request
of his country.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Volsce
SPEECH.LINE: He cannot choose. I am most fortunate, thus
accidentally to encounter you: you have ended my
business, and I will merrily accompany you home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Roman
SPEECH.LINE: I shall, between this and supper, tell you most
strange things from Rome; all tending to the good of
their adversaries. Have you an army ready, say you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Volsce
SPEECH.LINE: A most royal one; the centurions and their charges,
distinctly billeted, already in the entertainment,
and to be on foot at an hour's warning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Roman
SPEECH.LINE: I am joyful to hear of their readiness, and am the
man, I think, that shall set them in present action.
So, sir, heartily well met, and most glad of your company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Volsce
SPEECH.LINE: You take my part from me, sir; I have the most cause
to be glad of yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Roman
SPEECH.LINE: Well, let us go together.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Antium. Before Aufidius's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CORIOLANUS in mean apparel, disguised and muffled

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: A goodly city is this Antium. City,
'Tis I that made thy widows: many an heir
Of these fair edifices 'fore my wars
Have I heard groan and drop: then know me not,
Lest that thy wives with spits and boys with stones
In puny battle slay me.
Save you, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: And you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Direct me, if it be your will,
Where great Aufidius lies: is he in Antium?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: He is, and feasts the nobles of the state
At his house this night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Which is his house, beseech you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: This, here before you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thank you, sir: farewell.
O world, thy slippery turns! Friends now fast sworn,
Whose double bosoms seem to wear one heart,
Whose house, whose bed, whose meal, and exercise,
Are still together, who twin, as 'twere, in love
Unseparable, shall within this hour,
On a dissension of a doit, break out
To bitterest enmity: so, fellest foes,
Whose passions and whose plots have broke their sleep,
To take the one the other, by some chance,
Some trick not worth an egg, shall grow dear friends
And interjoin their issues. So with me:
My birth-place hate I, and my love's upon
This enemy town. I'll enter: if he slay me,
He does fair justice; if he give me way,
I'll do his country service.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The same. A hall in Aufidius's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Wine, wine, wine! What service
is here! I think our fellows are asleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Where's Cotus? my master calls
for him. Cotus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: A goodly house: the feast smells well; but I
Appear not like a guest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What would you have, friend? whence are you?
Here's no place for you: pray, go to the door.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have deserved no better entertainment,
In being Coriolanus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Whence are you, sir? Has the porter his eyes in his
head; that he gives entrance to such companions?
Pray, get you out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Away! get you away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now thou'rt troublesome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Are you so brave? I'll have you talked with anon.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter a third Servingman. The first meets him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What fellow's this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: A strange one as ever I looked on: I cannot get him
out of the house: prithee, call my master to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What have you to do here, fellow? Pray you, avoid
the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let me but stand; I will not hurt your hearth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: A gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: A marvellous poor one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: True, so I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, poor gentleman, take up some other
station; here's no place for you; pray you, avoid: come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Follow your function, go, and batten on cold bits.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What, you will not? Prithee, tell my master what a
strange guest he has here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: And I shall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Where dwellest thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Under the canopy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Under the canopy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Where's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: I' the city of kites and crows.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: I' the city of kites and crows! What an ass it is!
Then thou dwellest with daws too?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, I serve not thy master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: How, sir! do you meddle with my master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; 'tis an honester service than to meddle with thy
mistress. Thou pratest, and pratest; serve with thy
trencher, hence!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Beats him away. Exit third Servingman
Enter AUFIDIUS with the second Servingman

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where is this fellow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir: I'ld have beaten him like a dog, but for
disturbing the lords within.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Whence comest thou? what wouldst thou? thy name?
Why speak'st not? speak, man: what's thy name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: If, Tullus,
Not yet thou knowest me, and, seeing me, dost not
Think me for the man I am, necessity
Commands me name myself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What is thy name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: A name unmusical to the Volscians' ears,
And harsh in sound to thine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Say, what's thy name?
Thou hast a grim appearance, and thy face
Bears a command in't; though thy tackle's torn.
Thou show'st a noble vessel: what's thy name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prepare thy brow to frown: know'st
thou me yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know thee not: thy name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: My name is Caius Marcius, who hath done
To thee particularly and to all the Volsces
Great hurt and mischief; thereto witness may
My surname, Coriolanus: the painful service,
The extreme dangers and the drops of blood
Shed for my thankless country are requited
But with that surname; a good memory,
And witness of the malice and displeasure
Which thou shouldst bear me: only that name remains;
The cruelty and envy of the people,
Permitted by our dastard nobles, who
Have all forsook me, hath devour'd the rest;
And suffer'd me by the voice of slaves to be
Whoop'd out of Rome. Now this extremity
Hath brought me to thy hearth; not out of hope--
Mistake me not--to save my life, for if
I had fear'd death, of all the men i' the world
I would have 'voided thee, but in mere spite,
To be full quit of those my banishers,
Stand I before thee here. Then if thou hast
A heart of wreak in thee, that wilt revenge
Thine own particular wrongs and stop those maims
Of shame seen through thy country, speed
thee straight,
And make my misery serve thy turn: so use it
That my revengeful services may prove
As benefits to thee, for I will fight
Against my canker'd country with the spleen
Of all the under fiends. But if so be
Thou darest not this and that to prove more fortunes
Thou'rt tired, then, in a word, I also am
Longer to live most weary, and present
My throat to thee and to thy ancient malice;
Which not to cut would show thee but a fool,
Since I have ever follow'd thee with hate,
Drawn tuns of blood out of thy country's breast,
And cannot live but to thy shame, unless
It be to do thee service.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Marcius, Marcius!
Each word thou hast spoke hath weeded from my heart
A root of ancient envy. If Jupiter
Should from yond cloud speak divine things,
And say 'Tis true,' I'ld not believe them more
Than thee, all noble Marcius. Let me twine
Mine arms about that body, where against
My grained ash an hundred times hath broke
And scarr'd the moon with splinters: here I clip
The anvil of my sword, and do contest
As hotly and as nobly with thy love
As ever in ambitious strength I did
Contend against thy valour. Know thou first,
I loved the maid I married; never man
Sigh'd truer breath; but that I see thee here,
Thou noble thing! more dances my rapt heart
Than when I first my wedded mistress saw
Bestride my threshold. Why, thou Mars! I tell thee,
We have a power on foot; and I had purpose
Once more to hew thy target from thy brawn,
Or lose mine arm fort: thou hast beat me out
Twelve several times, and I have nightly since
Dreamt of encounters 'twixt thyself and me;
We have been down together in my sleep,
Unbuckling helms, fisting each other's throat,
And waked half dead with nothing. Worthy Marcius,
Had we no quarrel else to Rome, but that
Thou art thence banish'd, we would muster all
From twelve to seventy, and pouring war
Into the bowels of ungrateful Rome,
Like a bold flood o'er-bear. O, come, go in,
And take our friendly senators by the hands;
Who now are here, taking their leaves of me,
Who am prepared against your territories,
Though not for Rome itself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: You bless me, gods!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore, most absolute sir, if thou wilt have
The leading of thine own revenges, take
The one half of my commission; and set down--
As best thou art experienced, since thou know'st
Thy country's strength and weakness,--thine own ways;
Whether to knock against the gates of Rome,
Or rudely visit them in parts remote,
To fright them, ere destroy. But come in:
Let me commend thee first to those that shall
Say yea to thy desires. A thousand welcomes!
And more a friend than e'er an enemy;
Yet, Marcius, that was much. Your hand: most welcome!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt CORIOLANUS and AUFIDIUS. The two Servingmen come forward

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Here's a strange alteration!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: By my hand, I had thought to have strucken him with
a cudgel; and yet my mind gave me his clothes made a
false report of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What an arm he has! he turned me about with his
finger and his thumb, as one would set up a top.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I knew by his face that there was something in
him: he had, sir, a kind of face, methought,--I
cannot tell how to term it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: He had so; looking as it were--would I were hanged,
but I thought there was more in him than I could think.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: So did I, I'll be sworn: he is simply the rarest
man i' the world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: I think he is: but a greater soldier than he you wot on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Who, my master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, it's no matter for that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Worth six on him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, not so neither: but I take him to be the
greater soldier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, look you, one cannot tell how to say that:
for the defence of a town, our general is excellent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and for an assault too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: O slaves, I can tell you news,-- news, you rascals!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: What, what, what? let's partake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: I would not be a Roman, of all nations; I had as
lieve be a condemned man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore? wherefore?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Why, here's he that was wont to thwack our general,
Caius Marcius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Why do you say 'thwack our general '?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: I do not say 'thwack our general;' but he was always
good enough for him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Come, we are fellows and friends: he was ever too
hard for him; I have heard him say so himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: He was too hard for him directly, to say the troth
on't: before Corioli he scotched him and notched
him like a carbon ado.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: An he had been cannibally given, he might have
broiled and eaten him too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: But, more of thy news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Why, he is so made on here within, as if he were son
and heir to Mars; set at upper end o' the table; no
question asked him by any of the senators, but they
stand bald before him: our general himself makes a
mistress of him: sanctifies himself with's hand and
turns up the white o' the eye to his discourse. But
the bottom of the news is that our general is cut i'
the middle and but one half of what he was
yesterday; for the other has half, by the entreaty
and grant of the whole table. He'll go, he says,
and sowl the porter of Rome gates by the ears: he
will mow all down before him, and leave his passage polled.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: And he's as like to do't as any man I can imagine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Do't! he will do't; for, look you, sir, he has as
many friends as enemies; which friends, sir, as it
were, durst not, look you, sir, show themselves, as
we term it, his friends whilst he's in directitude.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Directitude! what's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: But when they shall see, sir, his crest up again,
and the man in blood, they will out of their
burrows, like conies after rain, and revel all with
him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: But when goes this forward?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: To-morrow; to-day; presently; you shall have the
drum struck up this afternoon: 'tis, as it were, a
parcel of their feast, and to be executed ere they
wipe their lips.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then we shall have a stirring world again.
This peace is nothing, but to rust iron, increase
tailors, and breed ballad-makers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Let me have war, say I; it exceeds peace as far as
day does night; it's spritely, waking, audible, and
full of vent. Peace is a very apoplexy, lethargy;
mulled, deaf, sleepy, insensible; a getter of more
bastard children than war's a destroyer of men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis so: and as war, in some sort, may be said to
be a ravisher, so it cannot be denied but peace is a
great maker of cuckolds.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and it makes men hate one another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servingman
SPEECH.LINE: Reason; because they then less need one another.
The wars for my money. I hope to see Romans as cheap
as Volscians. They are rising, they are rising.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: In, in, in, in!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. Rome. A public place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We hear not of him, neither need we fear him;
His remedies are tame i' the present peace
And quietness of the people, which before
Were in wild hurry. Here do we make his friends
Blush that the world goes well, who rather had,
Though they themselves did suffer by't, behold
Dissentious numbers pestering streets than see
Our tradesmen with in their shops and going
About their functions friendly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: We stood to't in good time.
Is this Menenius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis he,'tis he: O, he is grown most kind of late.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both Tribunes
SPEECH.LINE: Hail sir!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail to you both!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your Coriolanus
Is not much miss'd, but with his friends:
The commonwealth doth stand, and so would do,
Were he more angry at it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: All's well; and might have been much better, if
He could have temporized.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where is he, hear you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I hear nothing: his mother and his wife
Hear nothing from him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: The gods preserve you both!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: God-den, our neighbours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: God-den to you all, god-den to you all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ourselves, our wives, and children, on our knees,
Are bound to pray for you both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Live, and thrive!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, kind neighbours: we wish'd Coriolanus
Had loved you as we did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: Now the gods keep you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both Tribunes
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This is a happier and more comely time
Than when these fellows ran about the streets,
Crying confusion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caius Marcius was
A worthy officer i' the war; but insolent,
O'ercome with pride, ambitious past all thinking,
Self-loving,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And affecting one sole throne,
Without assistance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I think not so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We should by this, to all our lamentation,
If he had gone forth consul, found it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: The gods have well prevented it, and Rome
Sits safe and still without him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AEdile
SPEECH.LINE: Worthy tribunes,
There is a slave, whom we have put in prison,
Reports, the Volsces with two several powers
Are enter'd in the Roman territories,
And with the deepest malice of the war
Destroy what lies before 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis Aufidius,
Who, hearing of our Marcius' banishment,
Thrusts forth his horns again into the world;
Which were inshell'd when Marcius stood for Rome,
And durst not once peep out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, what talk you
Of Marcius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go see this rumourer whipp'd. It cannot be
The Volsces dare break with us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cannot be!
We have record that very well it can,
And three examples of the like have been
Within my age. But reason with the fellow,
Before you punish him, where he heard this,
Lest you shall chance to whip your information
And beat the messenger who bids beware
Of what is to be dreaded.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Tell not me:
I know this cannot be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not possible.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: The nobles in great earnestness are going
All to the senate-house: some news is come
That turns their countenances.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis this slave;--
Go whip him, 'fore the people's eyes:--his raising;
Nothing but his report.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, worthy sir,
The slave's report is seconded; and more,
More fearful, is deliver'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What more fearful?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: It is spoke freely out of many mouths--
How probable I do not know--that Marcius,
Join'd with Aufidius, leads a power 'gainst Rome,
And vows revenge as spacious as between
The young'st and oldest thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This is most likely!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Raised only, that the weaker sort may wish
Good Marcius home again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: The very trick on't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This is unlikely:
He and Aufidius can no more atone
Than violentest contrariety.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: You are sent for to the senate:
A fearful army, led by Caius Marcius
Associated with Aufidius, rages
Upon our territories; and have already
O'erborne their way, consumed with fire, and took
What lay before them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, you have made good work!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What news? what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have holp to ravish your own daughters and
To melt the city leads upon your pates,
To see your wives dishonour'd to your noses,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What's the news? what's the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your temples burned in their cement, and
Your franchises, whereon you stood, confined
Into an auger's bore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray now, your news?
You have made fair work, I fear me.--Pray, your news?--
If Marcius should be join'd with Volscians,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If!
He is their god: he leads them like a thing
Made by some other deity than nature,
That shapes man better; and they follow him,
Against us brats, with no less confidence
Than boys pursuing summer butterflies,
Or butchers killing flies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have made good work,
You and your apron-men; you that stood so up much
on the voice of occupation and
The breath of garlic-eaters!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He will shake
Your Rome about your ears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: As Hercules
Did shake down mellow fruit.
You have made fair work!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: But is this true, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; and you'll look pale
Before you find it other. All the regions
Do smilingly revolt; and who resist
Are mock'd for valiant ignorance,
And perish constant fools. Who is't can blame him?
Your enemies and his find something in him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We are all undone, unless
The noble man have mercy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who shall ask it?
The tribunes cannot do't for shame; the people
Deserve such pity of him as the wolf
Does of the shepherds: for his best friends, if they
Should say 'Be good to Rome,' they charged him even
As those should do that had deserved his hate,
And therein show'd like enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true:
If he were putting to my house the brand
That should consume it, I have not the face
To say 'Beseech you, cease.' You have made fair hands,
You and your crafts! you have crafted fair!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have brought
A trembling upon Rome, such as was never
So incapable of help.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both Tribunes
SPEECH.LINE: Say not we brought it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How! Was it we? we loved him but, like beasts
And cowardly nobles, gave way unto your clusters,
Who did hoot him out o' the city.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: But I fear
They'll roar him in again. Tullus Aufidius,
The second name of men, obeys his points
As if he were his officer: desperation
Is all the policy, strength and defence,
That Rome can make against them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here come the clusters.
And is Aufidius with him? You are they
That made the air unwholesome, when you cast
Your stinking greasy caps in hooting at
Coriolanus' exile. Now he's coming;
And not a hair upon a soldier's head
Which will not prove a whip: as many coxcombs
As you threw caps up will he tumble down,
And pay you for your voices. 'Tis no matter;
if he could burn us all into one coal,
We have deserved it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, we hear fearful news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: For mine own part,
When I said, banish him, I said 'twas pity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: And so did I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: And so did I; and, to say the truth, so did very
many of us: that we did, we did for the best; and
though we willingly consented to his banishment, yet
it was against our will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ye re goodly things, you voices!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have made
Good work, you and your cry! Shall's to the Capitol?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, ay, what else?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go, masters, get you home; be not dismay'd:
These are a side that would be glad to have
This true which they so seem to fear. Go home,
And show no sign of fear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: The gods be good to us! Come, masters, let's home.
I ever said we were i' the wrong when we banished
him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: So did we all. But, come, let's home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not like this news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let's to the Capitol. Would half my wealth
Would buy this for a lie!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, let us go.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VII. A camp, at a small distance from Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do they still fly to the Roman?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lieutenant
SPEECH.LINE: I do not know what witchcraft's in him, but
Your soldiers use him as the grace 'fore meat,
Their talk at table, and their thanks at end;
And you are darken'd in this action, sir,
Even by your own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot help it now,
Unless, by using means, I lame the foot
Of our design. He bears himself more proudlier,
Even to my person, than I thought he would
When first I did embrace him: yet his nature
In that's no changeling; and I must excuse
What cannot be amended.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lieutenant
SPEECH.LINE: Yet I wish, sir,--
I mean for your particular,--you had not
Join'd in commission with him; but either
Had borne the action of yourself, or else
To him had left it solely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I understand thee well; and be thou sure,
when he shall come to his account, he knows not
What I can urge against him. Although it seems,
And so he thinks, and is no less apparent
To the vulgar eye, that he bears all things fairly.
And shows good husbandry for the Volscian state,
Fights dragon-like, and does achieve as soon
As draw his sword; yet he hath left undone
That which shall break his neck or hazard mine,
Whene'er we come to our account.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lieutenant
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I beseech you, think you he'll carry Rome?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: All places yield to him ere he sits down;
And the nobility of Rome are his:
The senators and patricians love him too:
The tribunes are no soldiers; and their people
Will be as rash in the repeal, as hasty
To expel him thence. I think he'll be to Rome
As is the osprey to the fish, who takes it
By sovereignty of nature. First he was
A noble servant to them; but he could not
Carry his honours even: whether 'twas pride,
Which out of daily fortune ever taints
The happy man; whether defect of judgment,
To fail in the disposing of those chances
Which he was lord of; or whether nature,
Not to be other than one thing, not moving
From the casque to the cushion, but commanding peace
Even with the same austerity and garb
As he controll'd the war; but one of these--
As he hath spices of them all, not all,
For I dare so far free him--made him fear'd,
So hated, and so banish'd: but he has a merit,
To choke it in the utterance. So our virtues
Lie in the interpretation of the time:
And power, unto itself most commendable,
Hath not a tomb so evident as a chair
To extol what it hath done.
One fire drives out one fire; one nail, one nail;
Rights by rights falter, strengths by strengths do fail.
Come, let's away. When, Caius, Rome is thine,
Thou art poor'st of all; then shortly art thou mine.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Rome. A public place.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MENENIUS, COMINIUS, SICINIUS, BRUTUS, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, I'll not go: you hear what he hath said
Which was sometime his general; who loved him
In a most dear particular. He call'd me father:
But what o' that? Go, you that banish'd him;
A mile before his tent fall down, and knee
The way into his mercy: nay, if he coy'd
To hear Cominius speak, I'll keep at home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He would not seem to know me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yet one time he did call me by my name:
I urged our old acquaintance, and the drops
That we have bled together. Coriolanus
He would not answer to: forbad all names;
He was a kind of nothing, titleless,
Till he had forged himself a name o' the fire
Of burning Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so: you have made good work!
A pair of tribunes that have rack'd for Rome,
To make coals cheap,--a noble memory!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I minded him how royal 'twas to pardon
When it was less expected: he replied,
It was a bare petition of a state
To one whom they had punish'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Very well:
Could he say less?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I offer'd to awaken his regard
For's private friends: his answer to me was,
He could not stay to pick them in a pile
Of noisome musty chaff: he said 'twas folly,
For one poor grain or two, to leave unburnt,
And still to nose the offence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: For one poor grain or two!
I am one of those; his mother, wife, his child,
And this brave fellow too, we are the grains:
You are the musty chaff; and you are smelt
Above the moon: we must be burnt for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, pray, be patient: if you refuse your aid
In this so never-needed help, yet do not
Upbraid's with our distress. But, sure, if you
Would be your country's pleader, your good tongue,
More than the instant army we can make,
Might stop our countryman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, I'll not meddle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, go to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What should I do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Only make trial what your love can do
For Rome, towards Marcius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, and say that Marcius
Return me, as Cominius is return'd,
Unheard; what then?
But as a discontented friend, grief-shot
With his unkindness? say't be so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yet your good will
must have that thanks from Rome, after the measure
As you intended well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll undertake 't:
I think he'll hear me. Yet, to bite his lip
And hum at good Cominius, much unhearts me.
He was not taken well; he had not dined:
The veins unfill'd, our blood is cold, and then
We pout upon the morning, are unapt
To give or to forgive; but when we have stuff'd
These and these conveyances of our blood
With wine and feeding, we have suppler souls
Than in our priest-like fasts: therefore I'll watch him
Till he be dieted to my request,
And then I'll set upon him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You know the very road into his kindness,
And cannot lose your way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good faith, I'll prove him,
Speed how it will. I shall ere long have knowledge
Of my success.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He'll never hear him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I tell you, he does sit in gold, his eye
Red as 'twould burn Rome; and his injury
The gaoler to his pity. I kneel'd before him;
'Twas very faintly he said 'Rise;' dismiss'd me
Thus, with his speechless hand: what he would do,
He sent in writing after me; what he would not,
Bound with an oath to yield to his conditions:
So that all hope is vain.
Unless his noble mother, and his wife;
Who, as I hear, mean to solicit him
For mercy to his country. Therefore, let's hence,
And with our fair entreaties haste them on.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Entrance of the Volscian camp before Rome. Two Sentinels on guard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Stay: whence are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, and go back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You guard like men; 'tis well: but, by your leave,
I am an officer of state, and come
To speak with Coriolanus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: From whence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: From Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You may not pass, you must return: our general
Will no more hear from thence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You'll see your Rome embraced with fire before
You'll speak with Coriolanus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good my friends,
If you have heard your general talk of Rome,
And of his friends there, it is lots to blanks,
My name hath touch'd your ears it is Menenius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so; go back: the virtue of your name
Is not here passable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I tell thee, fellow,
The general is my lover: I have been
The book of his good acts, whence men have read
His name unparallel'd, haply amplified;
For I have ever verified my friends,
Of whom he's chief, with all the size that verity
Would without lapsing suffer: nay, sometimes,
Like to a bowl upon a subtle ground,
I have tumbled past the throw; and in his praise
Have almost stamp'd the leasing: therefore, fellow,
I must have leave to pass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, sir, if you had told as many lies in his
behalf as you have uttered words in your own, you
should not pass here; no, though it were as virtuous
to lie as to live chastely. Therefore, go back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, fellow, remember my name is Menenius,
always factionary on the party of your general.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Howsoever you have been his liar, as you say you
have, I am one that, telling true under him, must
say, you cannot pass. Therefore, go back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Has he dined, canst thou tell? for I would not
speak with him till after dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You are a Roman, are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am, as thy general is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Then you should hate Rome, as he does. Can you,
when you have pushed out your gates the very
defender of them, and, in a violent popular
ignorance, given your enemy your shield, think to
front his revenges with the easy groans of old
women, the virginal palms of your daughters, or with
the palsied intercession of such a decayed dotant as
you seem to be? Can you think to blow out the
intended fire your city is ready to flame in, with
such weak breath as this? No, you are deceived;
therefore, back to Rome, and prepare for your
execution: you are condemned, our general has sworn
you out of reprieve and pardon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah, if thy captain knew I were here, he would
use me with estimation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Come, my captain knows you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I mean, thy general.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: My general cares not for you. Back, I say, go; lest
I let forth your half-pint of blood; back,--that's
the utmost of your having: back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but, fellow, fellow,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: What's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, you companion, I'll say an errand for you:
You shall know now that I am in estimation; you shall
perceive that a Jack guardant cannot office me from
my son Coriolanus: guess, but by my entertainment
with him, if thou standest not i' the state of
hanging, or of some death more long in
spectatorship, and crueller in suffering; behold now
presently, and swoon for what's to come upon thee.
The glorious gods sit in hourly synod about thy
particular prosperity, and love thee no worse than
thy old father Menenius does! O my son, my son!
thou art preparing fire for us; look thee, here's
water to quench it. I was hardly moved to come to
thee; but being assured none but myself could move
thee, I have been blown out of your gates with
sighs; and conjure thee to pardon Rome, and thy
petitionary countrymen. The good gods assuage thy
wrath, and turn the dregs of it upon this varlet
here,--this, who, like a block, hath denied my
access to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How! away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Wife, mother, child, I know not. My affairs
Are servanted to others: though I owe
My revenge properly, my remission lies
In Volscian breasts. That we have been familiar,
Ingrate forgetfulness shall poison, rather
Than pity note how much. Therefore, be gone.
Mine ears against your suits are stronger than
Your gates against my force. Yet, for I loved thee,
Take this along; I writ it for thy sake
And would have rent it. Another word, Menenius,
I will not hear thee speak. This man, Aufidius,
Was my beloved in Rome: yet thou behold'st!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You keep a constant temper.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Now, sir, is your name Menenius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a spell, you see, of much power: you know the
way home again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear how we are shent for keeping your
greatness back?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: What cause, do you think, I have to swoon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I neither care for the world nor your general: for
such things as you, I can scarce think there's any,
ye're so slight. He that hath a will to die by
himself fears it not from another: let your general
do his worst. For you, be that you are, long; and
your misery increase with your age! I say to you,
as I was said to, Away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: A noble fellow, I warrant him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: The worthy fellow is our general: he's the rock, the
oak not to be wind-shaken.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The tent of Coriolanus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: We will before the walls of Rome tomorrow
Set down our host. My partner in this action,
You must report to the Volscian lords, how plainly
I have borne this business.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Only their ends
You have respected; stopp'd your ears against
The general suit of Rome; never admitted
A private whisper, no, not with such friends
That thought them sure of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: This last old man,
Whom with a crack'd heart I have sent to Rome,
Loved me above the measure of a father;
Nay, godded me, indeed. Their latest refuge
Was to send him; for whose old love I have,
Though I show'd sourly to him, once more offer'd
The first conditions, which they did refuse
And cannot now accept; to grace him only
That thought he could do more, a very little
I have yielded to: fresh embassies and suits,
Nor from the state nor private friends, hereafter
Will I lend ear to. Ha! what shout is this?
Shall I be tempted to infringe my vow
In the same time 'tis made? I will not.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter in mourning habits, VIRGILIA, VOLUMNIA, leading young MARCIUS, VALERIA, and Attendants
SPEECH.LINE: My wife comes foremost; then the honour'd mould
Wherein this trunk was framed, and in her hand
The grandchild to her blood. But, out, affection!
All bond and privilege of nature, break!
Let it be virtuous to be obstinate.
What is that curt'sy worth? or those doves' eyes,
Which can make gods forsworn? I melt, and am not
Of stronger earth than others. My mother bows;
As if Olympus to a molehill should
In supplication nod: and my young boy
Hath an aspect of intercession, which
Great nature cries 'Deny not.' let the Volsces
Plough Rome and harrow Italy: I'll never
Be such a gosling to obey instinct, but stand,
As if a man were author of himself
And knew no other kin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIRGILIA
SPEECH.LINE: My lord and husband!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: These eyes are not the same I wore in Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIRGILIA
SPEECH.LINE: The sorrow that delivers us thus changed
Makes you think so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Like a dull actor now,
I have forgot my part, and I am out,
Even to a full disgrace. Best of my flesh,
Forgive my tyranny; but do not say
For that 'Forgive our Romans.' O, a kiss
Long as my exile, sweet as my revenge!
Now, by the jealous queen of heaven, that kiss
I carried from thee, dear; and my true lip
Hath virgin'd it e'er since. You gods! I prate,
And the most noble mother of the world
Leave unsaluted: sink, my knee, i' the earth;
Of thy deep duty more impression show
Than that of common sons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, stand up blest!
Whilst, with no softer cushion than the flint,
I kneel before thee; and unproperly
Show duty, as mistaken all this while
Between the child and parent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: What is this?
Your knees to me? to your corrected son?
Then let the pebbles on the hungry beach
Fillip the stars; then let the mutinous winds
Strike the proud cedars 'gainst the fiery sun;
Murdering impossibility, to make
What cannot be, slight work.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art my warrior;
I holp to frame thee. Do you know this lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: The noble sister of Publicola,
The moon of Rome, chaste as the icicle
That's curdied by the frost from purest snow
And hangs on Dian's temple: dear Valeria!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: This is a poor epitome of yours,
Which by the interpretation of full time
May show like all yourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: The god of soldiers,
With the consent of supreme Jove, inform
Thy thoughts with nobleness; that thou mayst prove
To shame unvulnerable, and stick i' the wars
Like a great sea-mark, standing every flaw,
And saving those that eye thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Your knee, sirrah.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: That's my brave boy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Even he, your wife, this lady, and myself,
Are suitors to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you, peace:
Or, if you'ld ask, remember this before:
The thing I have forsworn to grant may never
Be held by you denials. Do not bid me
Dismiss my soldiers, or capitulate
Again with Rome's mechanics: tell me not
Wherein I seem unnatural: desire not
To ally my rages and revenges with
Your colder reasons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, no more, no more!
You have said you will not grant us any thing;
For we have nothing else to ask, but that
Which you deny already: yet we will ask;
That, if you fail in our request, the blame
May hang upon your hardness: therefore hear us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aufidius, and you Volsces, mark; for we'll
Hear nought from Rome in private. Your request?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Should we be silent and not speak, our raiment
And state of bodies would bewray what life
We have led since thy exile. Think with thyself
How more unfortunate than all living women
Are we come hither: since that thy sight,
which should
Make our eyes flow with joy, hearts dance
with comforts,
Constrains them weep and shake with fear and sorrow;
Making the mother, wife and child to see
The son, the husband and the father tearing
His country's bowels out. And to poor we
Thine enmity's most capital: thou barr'st us
Our prayers to the gods, which is a comfort
That all but we enjoy; for how can we,
Alas, how can we for our country pray.
Whereto we are bound, together with thy victory,
Whereto we are bound? alack, or we must lose
The country, our dear nurse, or else thy person,
Our comfort in the country. We must find
An evident calamity, though we had
Our wish, which side should win: for either thou
Must, as a foreign recreant, be led
With manacles thorough our streets, or else
triumphantly tread on thy country's ruin,
And bear the palm for having bravely shed
Thy wife and children's blood. For myself, son,
I purpose not to wait on fortune till
These wars determine: if I cannot persuade thee
Rather to show a noble grace to both parts
Than seek the end of one, thou shalt no sooner
March to assault thy country than to tread--
Trust to't, thou shalt not--on thy mother's womb,
That brought thee to this world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIRGILIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and mine,
That brought you forth this boy, to keep your name
Living to time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young MARCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: A' shall not tread on me;
I'll run away till I am bigger, but then I'll fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not of a woman's tenderness to be,
Requires nor child nor woman's face to see.
I have sat too long.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VOLUMNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, go not from us thus.
If it were so that our request did tend
To save the Romans, thereby to destroy
The Volsces whom you serve, you might condemn us,
As poisonous of your honour: no; our suit
Is that you reconcile them: while the Volsces
May say 'This mercy we have show'd;' the Romans,
'This we received;' and each in either side
Give the all-hail to thee and cry 'Be blest
For making up this peace!' Thou know'st, great son,
The end of war's uncertain, but this certain,
That, if thou conquer Rome, the benefit
Which thou shalt thereby reap is such a name,
Whose repetition will be dogg'd with curses;
Whose chronicle thus writ: 'The man was noble,
But with his last attempt he wiped it out;
Destroy'd his country, and his name remains
To the ensuing age abhorr'd.' Speak to me, son:
Thou hast affected the fine strains of honour,
To imitate the graces of the gods;
To tear with thunder the wide cheeks o' the air,
And yet to charge thy sulphur with a bolt
That should but rive an oak. Why dost not speak?
Think'st thou it honourable for a noble man
Still to remember wrongs? Daughter, speak you:
He cares not for your weeping. Speak thou, boy:
Perhaps thy childishness will move him more
Than can our reasons. There's no man in the world
More bound to 's mother; yet here he lets me prate
Like one i' the stocks. Thou hast never in thy life
Show'd thy dear mother any courtesy,
When she, poor hen, fond of no second brood,
Has cluck'd thee to the wars and safely home,
Loaden with honour. Say my request's unjust,
And spurn me back: but if it be not so,
Thou art not honest; and the gods will plague thee,
That thou restrain'st from me the duty which
To a mother's part belongs. He turns away:
Down, ladies; let us shame him with our knees.
To his surname Coriolanus 'longs more pride
Than pity to our prayers. Down: an end;
This is the last: so we will home to Rome,
And die among our neighbours. Nay, behold 's:
This boy, that cannot tell what he would have
But kneels and holds up bands for fellowship,
Does reason our petition with more strength
Than thou hast to deny 't. Come, let us go:
This fellow had a Volscian to his mother;
His wife is in Corioli and his child
Like him by chance. Yet give us our dispatch:
I am hush'd until our city be a-fire,
And then I'll speak a little.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: He holds her by the hand, silent

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: O mother, mother!
What have you done? Behold, the heavens do ope,
The gods look down, and this unnatural scene
They laugh at. O my mother, mother! O!
You have won a happy victory to Rome;
But, for your son,--believe it, O, believe it,
Most dangerously you have with him prevail'd,
If not most mortal to him. But, let it come.
Aufidius, though I cannot make true wars,
I'll frame convenient peace. Now, good Aufidius,
Were you in my stead, would you have heard
A mother less? or granted less, Aufidius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I was moved withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: I dare be sworn you were:
And, sir, it is no little thing to make
Mine eyes to sweat compassion. But, good sir,
What peace you'll make, advise me: for my part,
I'll not to Rome, I'll back with you; and pray you,
Stand to me in this cause. O mother! wife!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I am glad thou hast set thy mercy and
thy honour
At difference in thee: out of that I'll work
Myself a former fortune.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: The Ladies make signs to CORIOLANUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, by and by;
But we will drink together; and you shall bear
A better witness back than words, which we,
On like conditions, will have counter-seal'd.
Come, enter with us. Ladies, you deserve
To have a temple built you: all the swords
In Italy, and her confederate arms,
Could not have made this peace.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Rome. A public place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: See you yond coign o' the Capitol, yond
corner-stone?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what of that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If it be possible for you to displace it with your
little finger, there is some hope the ladies of
Rome, especially his mother, may prevail with him.
But I say there is no hope in't: our throats are
sentenced and stay upon execution.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible that so short a time can alter the
condition of a man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: There is differency between a grub and a butterfly;
yet your butterfly was a grub. This Marcius is grown
from man to dragon: he has wings; he's more than a
creeping thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He loved his mother dearly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: So did he me: and he no more remembers his mother
now than an eight-year-old horse. The tartness
of his face sours ripe grapes: when he walks, he
moves like an engine, and the ground shrinks before
his treading: he is able to pierce a corslet with
his eye; talks like a knell, and his hum is a
battery. He sits in his state, as a thing made for
Alexander. What he bids be done is finished with
his bidding. He wants nothing of a god but eternity
and a heaven to throne in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, mercy, if you report him truly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I paint him in the character. Mark what mercy his
mother shall bring from him: there is no more mercy
in him than there is milk in a male tiger; that
shall our poor city find: and all this is long of
you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: The gods be good unto us!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, in such a case the gods will not be good unto
us. When we banished him, we respected not them;
and, he returning to break our necks, they respect not us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, if you'ld save your life, fly to your house:
The plebeians have got your fellow-tribune
And hale him up and down, all swearing, if
The Roman ladies bring not comfort home,
They'll give him death by inches.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What's the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Good news, good news; the ladies have prevail'd,
The Volscians are dislodged, and Marcius gone:
A merrier day did never yet greet Rome,
No, not the expulsion of the Tarquins.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Friend,
Art thou certain this is true? is it most certain?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: As certain as I know the sun is fire:
Where have you lurk'd, that you make doubt of it?
Ne'er through an arch so hurried the blown tide,
As the recomforted through the gates. Why, hark you!
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Trumpets; hautboys; drums beat; all together
SPEECH.LINE: The trumpets, sackbuts, psalteries and fifes,
Tabours and cymbals and the shouting Romans,
Make the sun dance. Hark you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENENIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This is good news:
I will go meet the ladies. This Volumnia
Is worth of consuls, senators, patricians,
A city full; of tribunes, such as you,
A sea and land full. You have pray'd well to-day:
This morning for ten thousand of your throats
I'd not have given a doit. Hark, how they joy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: First, the gods bless you for your tidings; next,
Accept my thankfulness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, we have all
Great cause to give great thanks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: They are near the city?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Almost at point to enter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SICINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We will meet them,
And help the joy.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The same. A street near the gate.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter two Senators with VOLUMNIA, VIRGILIA, VALERIA, &c. passing over the stage, followed by Patricians and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Behold our patroness, the life of Rome!
Call all your tribes together, praise the gods,
And make triumphant fires; strew flowers before them:
Unshout the noise that banish'd Marcius,
Repeal him with the welcome of his mother;
Cry 'Welcome, ladies, welcome!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, ladies, Welcome!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: A flourish with drums and trumpets. Exeunt

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. Antium. A public place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go tell the lords o' the city I am here:
Deliver them this paper: having read it,
Bid them repair to the market place; where I,
Even in theirs and in the commons' ears,
Will vouch the truth of it. Him I accuse
The city ports by this hath enter'd and
Intends to appear before the people, hoping
To purge herself with words: dispatch.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter three or four Conspirators of AUFIDIUS' faction
SPEECH.LINE: Most welcome!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: How is it with our general?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Even so
As with a man by his own alms empoison'd,
And with his charity slain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: Most noble sir,
If you do hold the same intent wherein
You wish'd us parties, we'll deliver you
Of your great danger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I cannot tell:
We must proceed as we do find the people.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: The people will remain uncertain whilst
'Twixt you there's difference; but the fall of either
Makes the survivor heir of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know it;
And my pretext to strike at him admits
A good construction. I raised him, and I pawn'd
Mine honour for his truth: who being so heighten'd,
He water'd his new plants with dews of flattery,
Seducing so my friends; and, to this end,
He bow'd his nature, never known before
But to be rough, unswayable and free.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, his stoutness
When he did stand for consul, which he lost
By lack of stooping,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: That I would have spoke of:
Being banish'd for't, he came unto my hearth;
Presented to my knife his throat: I took him;
Made him joint-servant with me; gave him way
In all his own desires; nay, let him choose
Out of my files, his projects to accomplish,
My best and freshest men; served his designments
In mine own person; holp to reap the fame
Which he did end all his; and took some pride
To do myself this wrong: till, at the last,
I seem'd his follower, not partner, and
He waged me with his countenance, as if
I had been mercenary.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: So he did, my lord:
The army marvell'd at it, and, in the last,
When he had carried Rome and that we look'd
For no less spoil than glory,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: There was it:
For which my sinews shall be stretch'd upon him.
At a few drops of women's rheum, which are
As cheap as lies, he sold the blood and labour
Of our great action: therefore shall he die,
And I'll renew me in his fall. But, hark!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Drums and trumpets sound, with great shouts of the People

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: Your native town you enter'd like a post,
And had no welcomes home: but he returns,
Splitting the air with noise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: And patient fools,
Whose children he hath slain, their base throats tear
With giving him glory.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Conspirator
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore, at your vantage,
Ere he express himself, or move the people
With what he would say, let him feel your sword,
Which we will second. When he lies along,
After your way his tale pronounced shall bury
His reasons with his body.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Say no more:
Here come the lords.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the Lords of the city

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All The Lords
SPEECH.LINE: You are most welcome home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have not deserved it.
But, worthy lords, have you with heed perused
What I have written to you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lords
SPEECH.LINE: We have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: And grieve to hear't.
What faults he made before the last, I think
Might have found easy fines: but there to end
Where he was to begin and give away
The benefit of our levies, answering us
With our own charge, making a treaty where
There was a yielding,--this admits no excuse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He approaches: you shall hear him.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CORIOLANUS, marching with drum and colours; commoners being with him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, lords! I am return'd your soldier,
No more infected with my country's love
Than when I parted hence, but still subsisting
Under your great command. You are to know
That prosperously I have attempted and
With bloody passage led your wars even to
The gates of Rome. Our spoils we have brought home
Do more than counterpoise a full third part
The charges of the action. We have made peace
With no less honour to the Antiates
Than shame to the Romans: and we here deliver,
Subscribed by the consuls and patricians,
Together with the seal o' the senate, what
We have compounded on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Read it not, noble lords;
But tell the traitor, in the high'st degree
He hath abused your powers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Traitor! how now!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, traitor, Marcius!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Marcius!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Marcius, Caius Marcius: dost thou think
I'll grace thee with that robbery, thy stol'n name
Coriolanus in Corioli?
You lords and heads o' the state, perfidiously
He has betray'd your business, and given up,
For certain drops of salt, your city Rome,
I say 'your city,' to his wife and mother;
Breaking his oath and resolution like
A twist of rotten silk, never admitting
Counsel o' the war, but at his nurse's tears
He whined and roar'd away your victory,
That pages blush'd at him and men of heart
Look'd wondering each at other.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear'st thou, Mars?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Name not the god, thou boy of tears!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Measureless liar, thou hast made my heart
Too great for what contains it. Boy! O slave!
Pardon me, lords, 'tis the first time that ever
I was forced to scold. Your judgments, my grave lords,
Must give this cur the lie: and his own notion--
Who wears my stripes impress'd upon him; that
Must bear my beating to his grave--shall join
To thrust the lie unto him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, both, and hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cut me to pieces, Volsces; men and lads,
Stain all your edges on me. Boy! false hound!
If you have writ your annals true, 'tis there,
That, like an eagle in a dove-cote, I
Flutter'd your Volscians in Corioli:
Alone I did it. Boy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, noble lords,
Will you be put in mind of his blind fortune,
Which was your shame, by this unholy braggart,
'Fore your own eyes and ears?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Conspirators
SPEECH.LINE: Let him die for't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All The People
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tear him to pieces.' 'Do it presently.' 'He kill'd
my son.' 'My daughter.' 'He killed my cousin
Marcus.' 'He killed my father.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, ho! no outrage: peace!
The man is noble and his fame folds-in
This orb o' the earth. His last offences to us
Shall have judicious hearing. Stand, Aufidius,
And trouble not the peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CORIOLANUS
SPEECH.LINE: O that I had him,
With six Aufidiuses, or more, his tribe,
To use my lawful sword!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Insolent villain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Conspirators
SPEECH.LINE: Kill, kill, kill, kill, kill him!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: The Conspirators draw, and kill CORIOLANUS: AUFIDIUS stands on his body

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lords
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, hold, hold, hold!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My noble masters, hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: O Tullus,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast done a deed whereat valour will weep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Tread not upon him. Masters all, be quiet;
Put up your swords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lords, when you shall know--as in this rage,
Provoked by him, you cannot--the great danger
Which this man's life did owe you, you'll rejoice
That he is thus cut off. Please it your honours
To call me to your senate, I'll deliver
Myself your loyal servant, or endure
Your heaviest censure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Bear from hence his body;
And mourn you for him: let him be regarded
As the most noble corse that ever herald
Did follow to his urn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: His own impatience
Takes from Aufidius a great part of blame.
Let's make the best of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AUFIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My rage is gone;
And I am struck with sorrow. Take him up.
Help, three o' the chiefest soldiers; I'll be one.
Beat thou the drum, that it speak mournfully:
Trail your steel pikes. Though in this city he
Hath widow'd and unchilded many a one,
Which to this hour bewail the injury,
Yet he shall have a noble memory. Assist.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt, bearing the body of CORIOLANUS. A dead march sounded

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: CLOTEN, son to the Queen by a former husband.
POSTHUMUS LEONATUS, a gentleman, husband to Imogen.
BELARIUS, a banished lord, disguised under the name of Morgan.

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: sons to Cymbeline, disguised under the names of Polydote and Cadwal, supposed sons to Morgan.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: CAIUS LUCIUS, general of the Roman forces.
IMOGEN, daughter to Cymbeline by a former queen.
HELEN, a lady attending on Imogen.
Lords, Ladies, Roman Senators, Tribunes, a Soothsayer, a Dutchman, a Spaniard, Musicians, Officers, Captains, Soldiers, Messengers, and other Attendants.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Britain. The garden of Cymbeline's palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: You do not meet a man but frowns: our bloods
No more obey the heavens than our courtiers
Still seem as does the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: But what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: His daughter, and the heir of's kingdom, whom
He purposed to his wife's sole son--a widow
That late he married--hath referr'd herself
Unto a poor but worthy gentleman: she's wedded;
Her husband banish'd; she imprison'd: all
Is outward sorrow; though I think the king
Be touch'd at very heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: None but the king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: He that hath lost her too; so is the queen,
That most desired the match; but not a courtier,
Although they wear their faces to the bent
Of the king's look's, hath a heart that is not
Glad at the thing they scowl at.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: And why so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: He that hath miss'd the princess is a thing
Too bad for bad report: and he that hath her--
I mean, that married her, alack, good man!
And therefore banish'd--is a creature such
As, to seek through the regions of the earth
For one his like, there would be something failing
In him that should compare. I do not think
So fair an outward and such stuff within
Endows a man but he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: You speak him far.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I do extend him, sir, within himself,
Crush him together rather than unfold
His measure duly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: What's his name and birth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot delve him to the root: his father
Was call'd Sicilius, who did join his honour
Against the Romans with Cassibelan,
But had his titles by Tenantius whom
He served with glory and admired success,
So gain'd the sur-addition Leonatus;
And had, besides this gentleman in question,
Two other sons, who in the wars o' the time
Died with their swords in hand; for which
their father,
Then old and fond of issue, took such sorrow
That he quit being, and his gentle lady,
Big of this gentleman our theme, deceased
As he was born. The king he takes the babe
To his protection, calls him Posthumus Leonatus,
Breeds him and makes him of his bed-chamber,
Puts to him all the learnings that his time
Could make him the receiver of; which he took,
As we do air, fast as 'twas minister'd,
And in's spring became a harvest, lived in court--
Which rare it is to do--most praised, most loved,
A sample to the youngest, to the more mature
A glass that feated them, and to the graver
A child that guided dotards; to his mistress,
For whom he now is banish'd, her own price
Proclaims how she esteem'd him and his virtue;
By her election may be truly read
What kind of man he is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I honour him
Even out of your report. But, pray you, tell me,
Is she sole child to the king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: His only child.
He had two sons: if this be worth your hearing,
Mark it: the eldest of them at three years old,
I' the swathing-clothes the other, from their nursery
Were stol'n, and to this hour no guess in knowledge
Which way they went.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: How long is this ago?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Some twenty years.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: That a king's children should be so convey'd,
So slackly guarded, and the search so slow,
That could not trace them!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Howsoe'er 'tis strange,
Or that the negligence may well be laugh'd at,
Yet is it true, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I do well believe you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: We must forbear: here comes the gentleman,
The queen, and princess.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the QUEEN, POSTHUMUS LEONATUS, and IMOGEN

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: No, be assured you shall not find me, daughter,
After the slander of most stepmothers,
Evil-eyed unto you: you're my prisoner, but
Your gaoler shall deliver you the keys
That lock up your restraint. For you, Posthumus,
So soon as I can win the offended king,
I will be known your advocate: marry, yet
The fire of rage is in him, and 'twere good
You lean'd unto his sentence with what patience
Your wisdom may inform you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: Please your highness,
I will from hence to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: You know the peril.
I'll fetch a turn about the garden, pitying
The pangs of barr'd affections, though the king
Hath charged you should not speak together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: O
Dissembling courtesy! How fine this tyrant
Can tickle where she wounds! My dearest husband,
I something fear my father's wrath; but nothing--
Always reserved my holy duty--what
His rage can do on me: you must be gone;
And I shall here abide the hourly shot
Of angry eyes, not comforted to live,
But that there is this jewel in the world
That I may see again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: My queen! my mistress!
O lady, weep no more, lest I give cause
To be suspected of more tenderness
Than doth become a man. I will remain
The loyal'st husband that did e'er plight troth:
My residence in Rome at one Philario's,
Who to my father was a friend, to me
Known but by letter: thither write, my queen,
And with mine eyes I'll drink the words you send,
Though ink be made of gall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: Be brief, I pray you:
If the king come, I shall incur I know not
How much of his displeasure.
Yet I'll move him
To walk this way: I never do him wrong,
But he does buy my injuries, to be friends;
Pays dear for my offences.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: Should we be taking leave
As long a term as yet we have to live,
The loathness to depart would grow. Adieu!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, stay a little:
Were you but riding forth to air yourself,
Such parting were too petty. Look here, love;
This diamond was my mother's: take it, heart;
But keep it till you woo another wife,
When Imogen is dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: How, how! another?
You gentle gods, give me but this I have,
And sear up my embracements from a next
With bonds of death!
Remain, remain thou here
While sense can keep it on. And, sweetest, fairest,
As I my poor self did exchange for you,
To your so infinite loss, so in our trifles
I still win of you: for my sake wear this;
It is a manacle of love; I'll place it
Upon this fairest prisoner.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Putting a bracelet upon her arm

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: O the gods!
When shall we see again?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: Alack, the king!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou basest thing, avoid! hence, from my sight!
If after this command thou fraught the court
With thy unworthiness, thou diest: away!
Thou'rt poison to my blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POSTHUMUS LEONATUS
SPEECH.LINE: The gods protect you!
And bless the good remainders of the court! I am gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: There cannot be a pinch in death
More sharp than this is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: O disloyal thing,
That shouldst repair my youth, thou heap'st
A year's age on me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you, sir,
Harm not yourself with your vexation
I am senseless of your wrath; a touch more rare
Subdues all pangs, all fears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: Past grace? obedience?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Past hope, and in despair; that way, past grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: That mightst have had the sole son of my queen!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: O blest, that I might not! I chose an eagle,
And did avoid a puttock.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou took'st a beggar; wouldst have made my throne
A seat for baseness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: No; I rather added
A lustre to it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: O thou vile one!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
It is your fault that I have loved Posthumus:
You bred him as my playfellow, and he is
A man worth any woman, overbuys me
Almost the sum he pays.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: What, art thou mad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Almost, sir: heaven restore me! Would I were
A neat-herd's daughter, and my Leonatus
Our neighbour shepherd's son!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou foolish thing!
They were again together: you have done
Not after our command. Away with her,
And pen her up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: Beseech your patience. Peace,
Dear lady daughter, peace! Sweet sovereign,
Leave us to ourselves; and make yourself some comfort
Out of your best advice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CYMBELINE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, let her languish
A drop of blood a day; and, being aged,
Die of this folly!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: Fie! you must give way.
Here is your servant. How now, sir! What news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord your son drew on my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!
No harm, I trust, is done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: There might have been,
But that my master rather play'd than fought
And had no help of anger: they were parted
By gentlemen at hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: I am very glad on't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Your son's my father's friend; he takes his part.
To draw upon an exile! O brave sir!
I would they were in Afric both together;
Myself by with a needle, that I might prick
The goer-back. Why came you from your master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: On his command: he would not suffer me
To bring him to the haven; left these notes
Of what commands I should be subject to,
When 't pleased you to employ me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: This hath been
Your faithful servant: I dare lay mine honour
He will remain so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I humbly thank your highness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, walk awhile.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: About some half-hour hence,
I pray you, speak with me: you shall at least
Go see my lord aboard: for this time leave me.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. A public place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I would advise you to shift a shirt; the
violence of action hath made you reek as a
sacrifice: where air comes out, air comes in:
there's none abroad so wholesome as that you vent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: If my shirt were bloody, then to shift it. Have I hurt him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside No, 'faith; not so much as his patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Hurt him! his body's a passable carcass, if he be
not hurt: it is a thoroughfare for steel, if it be not hurt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside His steel was in debt; it went o' the
backside the town.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: The villain would not stand me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside No; but he fled forward still, toward your face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Stand you! You have land enough of your own: but
he added to your having; gave you some ground.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside As many inches as you have oceans. Puppies!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: I would they had not come between us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside So would I, till you had measured how long
a fool you were upon the ground.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: And that she should love this fellow and refuse me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside If it be a sin to make a true election, she
is damned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, as I told you always, her beauty and her brain
go not together: she's a good sign, but I have seen
small reflection of her wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside She shines not upon fools, lest the
reflection should hurt her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: Come, I'll to my chamber. Would there had been some
hurt done!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I wish not so; unless it had been the fall
of an ass, which is no great hurt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: You'll go with us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I'll attend your lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLOTEN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, come, let's go together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Well, my lord.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A room in Cymbeline's palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: I would thou grew'st unto the shores o' the haven,
And question'dst every sail: if he should write
And not have it, 'twere a paper lost,
As offer'd mercy is. What was the last
That he spake to thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: It was his queen, his queen!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Then waved his handkerchief?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: And kiss'd it, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Senseless Linen! happier therein than I!
And that was all?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: No, madam; for so long
As he could make me with this eye or ear
Distinguish him from others, he did keep
The deck, with glove, or hat, or handkerchief,
Still waving, as the fits and stirs of 's mind
Could best express how slow his soul sail'd on,
How swift his ship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shouldst have made him
As little as a crow, or less, ere left
To after-eye him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, so I did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: I would have broke mine eye-strings; crack'd them, but
To look upon him, till the diminution
Of space had pointed him sharp as my needle,
Nay, follow'd him, till he had melted from
The smallness of a gnat to air, and then
Have turn'd mine eye and wept. But, good Pisanio,
When shall we hear from him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Be assured, madam,
With his next vantage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: I did not take my leave of him, but had
Most pretty things to say: ere I could tell him
How I would think on him at certain hours
Such thoughts and such, or I could make him swear
The shes of Italy should not betray
Mine interest and his honour, or have charged him,
At the sixth hour of morn, at noon, at midnight,
To encounter me with orisons, for then
I am in heaven for him; or ere I could
Give him that parting kiss which I had set
Betwixt two charming words, comes in my father
And like the tyrannous breathing of the north
Shakes all our buds from growing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lady
SPEECH.LINE: The queen, madam,
Desires your highness' company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IMOGEN
SPEECH.LINE: Those things I bid you do, get them dispatch'd.
I will attend the queen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, I shall.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Rome. Philario's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PHILARIO, IACHIMO, a Frenchman, a Dutchman, and a Spaniard

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IACHIMO
SPEECH.LINE: Believe it, sir, I have seen him in Britain: he was
then of a crescent note, expected to prove so worthy
as since he hath been allowed the name of; but I
could then have looked on him without the help of
admiration, though the catalogue of his endowments
had been tabled by his side and I to peruse him by items.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILARIO
SPEECH.LINE: You speak of him when he was less furnished than now
he is with that which makes him both without and within.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Frenchman
SPEECH.LINE: I have seen him in France: we had very many there
could behold the sun with as firm eyes as he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IACHIMO
SPEECH.LINE: This matter of marrying his king's daughter, wherein
he must be weighed rather by her value than his own,
words him, I doubt not, a great deal from the matter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Frenchman
SPEECH.LINE: And then his banishment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IACHIMO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and the approbation of those that weep this
lamentable divorce under her colours are wonderfully
to extend him; be it but to fortify her judgment,
which else an easy battery might lay flat, for
taking a beggar without less quality. But how comes
it he is to sojourn with you? How creeps
acquaintance?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILARIO
