well, sweet Jack, have a care of thyself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Well, fare thee well: I have known thee these
twenty-nine years, come peascod-time; but an
honester and truer-hearted man,--well, fare thee well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Within Mistress Tearsheet!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: What's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Within Good Mistress Tearsheet, come to my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: O, run, Doll, run; run, good Doll: come.
Yea, will you come, Doll?

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Westminster. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter KING HENRY IV in his nightgown, with a Page

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Go call the Earls of Surrey and of Warwick;
But, ere they come, bid them o'er-read these letters,
And well consider of them; make good speed.
How many thousand of my poorest subjects
Are at this hour asleep! O sleep, O gentle sleep,
Nature's soft nurse, how have I frighted thee,
That thou no more wilt weigh my eyelids down
And steep my senses in forgetfulness?
Why rather, sleep, liest thou in smoky cribs,
Upon uneasy pallets stretching thee
And hush'd with buzzing night-flies to thy slumber,
Than in the perfumed chambers of the great,
Under the canopies of costly state,
And lull'd with sound of sweetest melody?
O thou dull god, why liest thou with the vile
In loathsome beds, and leavest the kingly couch
A watch-case or a common 'larum-bell?
Wilt thou upon the high and giddy mast
Seal up the ship-boy's eyes, and rock his brains
In cradle of the rude imperious surge
And in the visitation of the winds,
Who take the ruffian billows by the top,
Curling their monstrous heads and hanging them
With deafening clamour in the slippery clouds,
That, with the hurly, death itself awakes?
Canst thou, O partial sleep, give thy repose
To the wet sea-boy in an hour so rude,
And in the calmest and most stillest night,
With all appliances and means to boot,
Deny it to a king? Then happy low, lie down!
Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Many good morrows to your majesty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Is it good morrow, lords?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis one o'clock, and past.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, good morrow to you all, my lords.
Have you read o'er the letters that I sent you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: We have, my liege.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Then you perceive the body of our kingdom
How foul it is; what rank diseases grow
And with what danger, near the heart of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: It is but as a body yet distemper'd;
Which to his former strength may be restored
With good advice and little medicine:
My Lord Northumberland will soon be cool'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: O God! that one might read the book of fate,
And see the revolution of the times
Make mountains level, and the continent,
Weary of solid firmness, melt itself
Into the sea! and, other times, to see
The beachy girdle of the ocean
Too wide for Neptune's hips; how chances mock,
And changes fill the cup of alteration
With divers liquors! O, if this were seen,
The happiest youth, viewing his progress through,
What perils past, what crosses to ensue,
Would shut the book, and sit him down and die.
'Tis not 'ten years gone
Since Richard and Northumberland, great friends,
Did feast together, and in two years after
Were they at wars: it is but eight years since
This Percy was the man nearest my soul,
Who like a brother toil'd in my affairs
And laid his love and life under my foot,
Yea, for my sake, even to the eyes of Richard
Gave him defiance. But which of you was by--
You, cousin Nevil, as I may remember--
When Richard, with his eye brimful of tears,
Then cheque'd and rated by Northumberland,
Did speak these words, now proved a prophecy?
'Northumberland, thou ladder by the which
My cousin Bolingbroke ascends my throne;'
Though then, God knows, I had no such intent,
But that necessity so bow'd the state
That I and greatness were compell'd to kiss:
'The time shall come,' thus did he follow it,
'The time will come, that foul sin, gathering head,
Shall break into corruption:' so went on,
Foretelling this same time's condition
And the division of our amity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: There is a history in all men's lives,
Figuring the nature of the times deceased;
The which observed, a man may prophesy,
With a near aim, of the main chance of things
As yet not come to life, which in their seeds
And weak beginnings lie intreasured.
Such things become the hatch and brood of time;
And by the necessary form of this
King Richard might create a perfect guess
That great Northumberland, then false to him,
Would of that seed grow to a greater falseness;
Which should not find a ground to root upon,
Unless on you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Are these things then necessities?
Then let us meet them like necessities:
And that same word even now cries out on us:
They say the bishop and Northumberland
Are fifty thousand strong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: It cannot be, my lord;
Rumour doth double, like the voice and echo,
The numbers of the fear'd. Please it your grace
To go to bed. Upon my soul, my lord,
The powers that you already have sent forth
Shall bring this prize in very easily.
To comfort you the more, I have received
A certain instance that Glendower is dead.
Your majesty hath been this fortnight ill,
And these unseason'd hours perforce must add
Unto your sickness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: I will take your counsel:
And were these inward wars once out of hand,
We would, dear lords, unto the Holy Land.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Gloucestershire. Before SHALLOW'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SHALLOW and SILENCE, meeting; MOULDY, SHADOW, WART, FEEBLE, BULLCALF, a Servant or two with them

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, come on, come on, sir; give me your hand,
sir, give me your hand, sir: an early stirrer, by
the rood! And how doth my good cousin Silence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, good cousin Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: And how doth my cousin, your bedfellow? and your
fairest daughter and mine, my god-daughter Ellen?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, a black ousel, cousin Shallow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: By yea and nay, sir, I dare say my cousin William is
become a good scholar: he is at Oxford still, is he not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, sir, to my cost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: A' must, then, to the inns o' court shortly. I was
once of Clement's Inn, where I think they will
talk of mad Shallow yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: You were called 'lusty Shallow' then, cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: By the mass, I was called any thing; and I would
have done any thing indeed too, and roundly too.
There was I, and little John Doit of Staffordshire,
and black George Barnes, and Francis Pickbone, and
Will Squele, a Cotswold man; you had not four such
swinge-bucklers in all the inns o' court again: and
I may say to you, we knew where the bona-robas were
and had the best of them all at commandment. Then
was Jack Falstaff, now Sir John, a boy, and page to
Thomas Mowbray, Duke of Norfolk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: This Sir John, cousin, that comes hither anon about soldiers?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: The same Sir John, the very same. I see him break
Skogan's head at the court-gate, when a' was a
crack not thus high: and the very same day did I
fight with one Sampson Stockfish, a fruiterer,
behind Gray's Inn. Jesu, Jesu, the mad days that I
have spent! and to see how many of my old
acquaintance are dead!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: We shall all follow, cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHADOW
SPEECH.LINE: Certain, 'tis certain; very sure, very sure: death,
as the Psalmist saith, is certain to all; all shall
die. How a good yoke of bullocks at Stamford fair?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, I was not there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Death is certain. Is old Double of your town living
yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Dead, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Jesu, Jesu, dead! a' drew a good bow; and dead! a'
shot a fine shoot: John a Gaunt loved him well, and
betted much money on his head. Dead! a' would have
clapped i' the clout at twelve score; and carried
you a forehand shaft a fourteen and fourteen and a
half, that it would have done a man's heart good to
see. How a score of ewes now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Thereafter as they be: a score of good ewes may be
worth ten pounds.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: And is old Double dead?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Here come two of Sir John Falstaff's men, as I think.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BARDOLPH and one with him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, honest gentlemen: I beseech you, which
is Justice Shallow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: I am Robert Shallow, sir; a poor esquire of this
county, and one of the king's justices of the peace:
What is your good pleasure with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: My captain, sir, commends him to you; my captain,
Sir John Falstaff, a tall gentleman, by heaven, and
a most gallant leader.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: He greets me well, sir. I knew him a good backsword
man. How doth the good knight? may I ask how my
lady his wife doth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, pardon; a soldier is better accommodated than
with a wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: It is well said, in faith, sir; and it is well said
indeed too. Better accommodated! it is good; yea,
indeed, is it: good phrases are surely, and ever
were, very commendable. Accommodated! it comes of
'accommodo' very good; a good phrase.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, sir; I have heard the word. Phrase call
you it? by this good day, I know not the phrase;
but I will maintain the word with my sword to be a
soldier-like word, and a word of exceeding good
command, by heaven. Accommodated; that is, when a
man is, as they say, accommodated; or when a man is,
being, whereby a' may be thought to be accommodated;
which is an excellent thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: It is very just.
Look, here comes good Sir John. Give me your good
hand, give me your worship's good hand: by my
troth, you like well and bear your years very well:
welcome, good Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad to see you well, good Master Robert
Shallow: Master Surecard, as I think?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: No, Sir John; it is my cousin Silence, in commission with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Good Master Silence, it well befits you should be of
the peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Your good-worship is welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Fie! this is hot weather, gentlemen. Have you
provided me here half a dozen sufficient men?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, have we, sir. Will you sit?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Let me see them, I beseech you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Where's the roll? where's the roll? where's the
roll? Let me see, let me see, let me see. So, so:
yea, marry, sir: Ralph Mouldy! Let them appear as
I call; let them do so, let them do so. Let me
see; where is Mouldy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOULDY
SPEECH.LINE: Here, an't please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: What think you, Sir John? a good-limbed fellow;
young, strong, and of good friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Is thy name Mouldy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOULDY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, an't please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis the more time thou wert used.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha, ha! most excellent, i' faith! Things that
are mouldy lack use: very singular good! in faith,
well said, Sir John, very well said.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Prick him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOULDY
SPEECH.LINE: I was pricked well enough before, an you could have
let me alone: my old dame will be undone now for
one to do her husbandry and her drudgery: you need
not to have pricked me; there are other men fitter
to go out than I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Go to: peace, Mouldy; you shall go. Mouldy, it is
time you were spent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOULDY
SPEECH.LINE: Spent!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, fellow, peace; stand aside: know you where
you are? For the other, Sir John: let me see:
Simon Shadow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, marry, let me have him to sit under: he's like
to be a cold soldier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Where's Shadow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHADOW
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Shadow, whose son art thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHADOW
SPEECH.LINE: My mother's son, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Thy mother's son! like enough, and thy father's
shadow: so the son of the female is the shadow of
the male: it is often so, indeed; but much of the
father's substance!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Do you like him, Sir John?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Shadow will serve for summer; prick him, for we have
a number of shadows to fill up the muster-book.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Thomas Wart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Where's he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WART
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Is thy name Wart?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WART
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art a very ragged wart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I prick him down, Sir John?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: It were superfluous; for his apparel is built upon
his back and the whole frame stands upon pins:
prick him no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha, ha! you can do it, sir; you can do it: I
commend you well. Francis Feeble!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What trade art thou, Feeble?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: A woman's tailor, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I prick him, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: You may: but if he had been a man's tailor, he'ld
ha' pricked you. Wilt thou make as many holes in
an enemy's battle as thou hast done in a woman's petticoat?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: I will do my good will, sir; you can have no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, good woman's tailor! well said,
courageous Feeble! thou wilt be as valiant as the
wrathful dove or most magnanimous mouse. Prick the
woman's tailor: well, Master Shallow; deep, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: I would Wart might have gone, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I would thou wert a man's tailor, that thou mightst
mend him and make him fit to go. I cannot put him
to a private soldier that is the leader of so many
thousands: let that suffice, most forcible Feeble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: It shall suffice, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I am bound to thee, reverend Feeble. Who is next?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Peter Bullcalf o' the green!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, marry, let's see Bullcalf.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BULLCALF
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: 'Fore God, a likely fellow! Come, prick me Bullcalf
till he roar again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BULLCALF
SPEECH.LINE: O Lord! good my lord captain,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What, dost thou roar before thou art pricked?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BULLCALF
SPEECH.LINE: O Lord, sir! I am a diseased man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What disease hast thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BULLCALF
SPEECH.LINE: A whoreson cold, sir, a cough, sir, which I caught
with ringing in the king's affairs upon his
coronation-day, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come, thou shalt go to the wars in a gown; we wilt
have away thy cold; and I will take such order that
my friends shall ring for thee. Is here all?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Here is two more called than your number, you must
have but four here, sir: and so, I pray you, go in
with me to dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come, I will go drink with you, but I cannot tarry
dinner. I am glad to see you, by my troth, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: O, Sir John, do you remember since we lay all night
in the windmill in Saint George's field?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: No more of that, good Master Shallow, no more of that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! 'twas a merry night. And is Jane Nightwork alive?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: She lives, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: She never could away with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Never, never; she would always say she could not
abide Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: By the mass, I could anger her to the heart. She
was then a bona-roba. Doth she hold her own well?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Old, old, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, she must be old; she cannot choose but be old;
certain she's old; and had Robin Nightwork by old
Nightwork before I came to Clement's Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SILENCE
SPEECH.LINE: That's fifty-five year ago.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, cousin Silence, that thou hadst seen that that
this knight and I have seen! Ha, Sir John, said I well?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: We have heard the chimes at midnight, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: That we have, that we have, that we have; in faith,
Sir John, we have: our watch-word was 'Hem boys!'
Come, let's to dinner; come, let's to dinner:
Jesus, the days that we have seen! Come, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BULLCALF
SPEECH.LINE: Good Master Corporate Bardolph, stand my friend;
and here's four Harry ten shillings in French crowns
for you. In very truth, sir, I had as lief be
hanged, sir, as go: and yet, for mine own part, sir,
I do not care; but rather, because I am unwilling,
and, for mine own part, have a desire to stay with
my friends; else, sir, I did not care, for mine own
part, so much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; stand aside.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOULDY
SPEECH.LINE: And, good master corporal captain, for my old
dame's sake, stand my friend: she has nobody to do
any thing about her when I am gone; and she is old,
and cannot help herself: You shall have forty, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; stand aside.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, I care not; a man can die but once: we
owe God a death: I'll ne'er bear a base mind:
an't be my destiny, so; an't be not, so: no man is
too good to serve's prince; and let it go which way
it will, he that dies this year is quit for the next.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Well said; thou'rt a good fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FEEBLE
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, I'll bear no base mind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come, sir, which men shall I have?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Four of which you please.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, a word with you: I have three pound to free
Mouldy and Bullcalf.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Sir John, which four will you have?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Do you choose for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, then, Mouldy, Bullcalf, Feeble and Shadow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Mouldy and Bullcalf: for you, Mouldy, stay at home
till you are past service: and for your part,
Bullcalf, grow till you come unto it: I will none of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John, Sir John, do not yourself wrong: they are
your likeliest men, and I would have you served with the best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Will you tell me, Master Shallow, how to choose a
man? Care I for the limb, the thewes, the stature,
bulk, and big assemblance of a man! Give me the
spirit, Master Shallow. Here's Wart; you see what a
ragged appearance it is; a' shall charge you and
discharge you with the motion of a pewterer's
hammer, come off and on swifter than he that gibbets
on the brewer's bucket. And this same half-faced
fellow, Shadow; give me this man: he presents no
mark to the enemy; the foeman may with as great aim
level at the edge of a penknife. And for a retreat;
how swiftly will this Feeble the woman's tailor run
off! O, give me the spare men, and spare me the
great ones. Put me a caliver into Wart's hand, Bardolph.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, Wart, traverse; thus, thus, thus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come, manage me your caliver. So: very well: go
to: very good, exceeding good. O, give me always a
little, lean, old, chapt, bald shot. Well said, i'
faith, Wart; thou'rt a good scab: hold, there's a
tester for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: He is not his craft's master; he doth not do it
right. I remember at Mile-end Green, when I lay at
Clement's Inn--I was then Sir Dagonet in Arthur's
show,--there was a little quiver fellow, and a'
would manage you his piece thus; and a' would about
and about, and come you in and come you in: 'rah,
tah, tah,' would a' say; 'bounce' would a' say; and
away again would a' go, and again would a' come: I
shall ne'er see such a fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: These fellows will do well, Master Shallow. God
keep you, Master Silence: I will not use many words
with you. Fare you well, gentlemen both: I thank
you: I must a dozen mile to-night. Bardolph, give
the soldiers coats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John, the Lord bless you! God prosper your
affairs! God send us peace! At your return visit
our house; let our old acquaintance be renewed;
peradventure I will with ye to the court.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: 'Fore God, I would you would, Master Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; I have spoke at a word. God keep you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, gentle gentlemen.
On, Bardolph; lead the men away.
As I return, I will fetch off these justices: I do
see the bottom of Justice Shallow. Lord, Lord, how
subject we old men are to this vice of lying! This
same starved justice hath done nothing but prate to
me of the wildness of his youth, and the feats he
hath done about Turnbull Street: and every third
word a lie, duer paid to the hearer than the Turk's
tribute. I do remember him at Clement's Inn like a
man made after supper of a cheese-paring: when a'
was naked, he was, for all the world, like a forked
radish, with a head fantastically carved upon it
with a knife: a' was so forlorn, that his
dimensions to any thick sight were invincible: a'
was the very genius of famine; yet lecherous as a
monkey, and the whores called him mandrake: a' came
ever in the rearward of the fashion, and sung those
tunes to the overscutched huswives that he heard the
carmen whistle, and swear they were his fancies or
his good-nights. And now is this Vice's dagger
become a squire, and talks as familiarly of John a
Gaunt as if he had been sworn brother to him; and
I'll be sworn a' ne'er saw him but once in the
Tilt-yard; and then he burst his head for crowding
among the marshal's men. I saw it, and told John a
Gaunt he beat his own name; for you might have
thrust him and all his apparel into an eel-skin; the
case of a treble hautboy was a mansion for him, a
court: and now has he land and beefs. Well, I'll
be acquainted with him, if I return; and it shall
go hard but I will make him a philosopher's two
stones to me: if the young dace be a bait for the
old pike, I see no reason in the law of nature but I
may snap at him. Let time shape, and there an end.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Yorkshire. Gaultree Forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the ARCHBISHOP OF YORK, MOWBRAY, LORD HASTINGS, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What is this forest call'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis Gaultree Forest, an't shall please your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Here stand, my lords; and send discoverers forth
To know the numbers of our enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: We have sent forth already.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well done.
My friends and brethren in these great affairs,
I must acquaint you that I have received
New-dated letters from Northumberland;
Their cold intent, tenor and substance, thus:
Here doth he wish his person, with such powers
As might hold sortance with his quality,
The which he could not levy; whereupon
He is retired, to ripe his growing fortunes,
To Scotland: and concludes in hearty prayers
That your attempts may overlive the hazard
And fearful melting of their opposite.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Thus do the hopes we have in him touch ground
And dash themselves to pieces.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: West of this forest, scarcely off a mile,
In goodly form comes on the enemy;
And, by the ground they hide, I judge their number
Upon or near the rate of thirty thousand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: The just proportion that we gave them out
Let us sway on and face them in the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What well-appointed leader fronts us here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: I think it is my Lord of Westmoreland.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Health and fair greeting from our general,
The prince, Lord John and Duke of Lancaster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Say on, my Lord of Westmoreland, in peace:
What doth concern your coming?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Then, my lord,
Unto your grace do I in chief address
The substance of my speech. If that rebellion
Came like itself, in base and abject routs,
Led on by bloody youth, guarded with rags,
And countenanced by boys and beggary,
I say, if damn'd commotion so appear'd,
In his true, native and most proper shape,
You, reverend father, and these noble lords
Had not been here, to dress the ugly form
Of base and bloody insurrection
With your fair honours. You, lord archbishop,
Whose see is by a civil peace maintained,
Whose beard the silver hand of peace hath touch'd,
Whose learning and good letters peace hath tutor'd,
Whose white investments figure innocence,
The dove and very blessed spirit of peace,
Wherefore do you so ill translate ourself
Out of the speech of peace that bears such grace,
Into the harsh and boisterous tongue of war;
Turning your books to graves, your ink to blood,
Your pens to lances and your tongue divine
To a trumpet and a point of war?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore do I this? so the question stands.
Briefly to this end: we are all diseased,
And with our surfeiting and wanton hours
Have brought ourselves into a burning fever,
And we must bleed for it; of which disease
Our late king, Richard, being infected, died.
But, my most noble Lord of Westmoreland,
I take not on me here as a physician,
Nor do I as an enemy to peace
Troop in the throngs of military men;
But rather show awhile like fearful war,
To diet rank minds sick of happiness
And purge the obstructions which begin to stop
Our very veins of life. Hear me more plainly.
I have in equal balance justly weigh'd
What wrongs our arms may do, what wrongs we suffer,
And find our griefs heavier than our offences.
We see which way the stream of time doth run,
And are enforced from our most quiet there
By the rough torrent of occasion;
And have the summary of all our griefs,
When time shall serve, to show in articles;
Which long ere this we offer'd to the king,
And might by no suit gain our audience:
When we are wrong'd and would unfold our griefs,
We are denied access unto his person
Even by those men that most have done us wrong.
The dangers of the days but newly gone,
Whose memory is written on the earth
With yet appearing blood, and the examples
Of every minute's instance, present now,
Hath put us in these ill-beseeming arms,
Not to break peace or any branch of it,
But to establish here a peace indeed,
Concurring both in name and quality.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: When ever yet was your appeal denied?
Wherein have you been galled by the king?
What peer hath been suborn'd to grate on you,
That you should seal this lawless bloody book
Of forged rebellion with a seal divine
And consecrate commotion's bitter edge?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: My brother general, the commonwealth,
To brother born an household cruelty,
I make my quarrel in particular.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: There is no need of any such redress;
Or if there were, it not belongs to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Why not to him in part, and to us all
That feel the bruises of the days before,
And suffer the condition of these times
To lay a heavy and unequal hand
Upon our honours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: O, my good Lord Mowbray,
Construe the times to their necessities,
And you shall say indeed, it is the time,
And not the king, that doth you injuries.
Yet for your part, it not appears to me
Either from the king or in the present time
That you should have an inch of any ground
To build a grief on: were you not restored
To all the Duke of Norfolk's signories,
Your noble and right well remember'd father's?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: What thing, in honour, had my father lost,
That need to be revived and breathed in me?
The king that loved him, as the state stood then,
Was force perforce compell'd to banish him:
And then that Harry Bolingbroke and he,
Being mounted and both roused in their seats,
Their neighing coursers daring of the spur,
Their armed staves in charge, their beavers down,
Their eyes of fire sparking through sights of steel
And the loud trumpet blowing them together,
Then, then, when there was nothing could have stay'd
My father from the breast of Bolingbroke,
O when the king did throw his warder down,
His own life hung upon the staff he threw;
Then threw he down himself and all their lives
That by indictment and by dint of sword
Have since miscarried under Bolingbroke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: You speak, Lord Mowbray, now you know not what.
The Earl of Hereford was reputed then
In England the most valiant gentlemen:
Who knows on whom fortune would then have smiled?
But if your father had been victor there,
He ne'er had borne it out of Coventry:
For all the country in a general voice
Cried hate upon him; and all their prayers and love
Were set on Hereford, whom they doted on
And bless'd and graced indeed, more than the king.
But this is mere digression from my purpose.
Here come I from our princely general
To know your griefs; to tell you from his grace
That he will give you audience; and wherein
It shall appear that your demands are just,
You shall enjoy them, every thing set off
That might so much as think you enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: But he hath forced us to compel this offer;
And it proceeds from policy, not love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Mowbray, you overween to take it so;
This offer comes from mercy, not from fear:
For, lo! within a ken our army lies,
Upon mine honour, all too confident
To give admittance to a thought of fear.
Our battle is more full of names than yours,
Our men more perfect in the use of arms,
Our armour all as strong, our cause the best;
Then reason will our heart should be as good
Say you not then our offer is compell'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Well, by my will we shall admit no parley.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: That argues but the shame of your offence:
A rotten case abides no handling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Hath the Prince John a full commission,
In very ample virtue of his father,
To hear and absolutely to determine
Of what conditions we shall stand upon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: That is intended in the general's name:
I muse you make so slight a question.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Then take, my Lord of Westmoreland, this schedule,
For this contains our general grievances:
Each several article herein redress'd,
All members of our cause, both here and hence,
That are insinew'd to this action,
Acquitted by a true substantial form
And present execution of our wills
To us and to our purposes confined,
We come within our awful banks again
And knit our powers to the arm of peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: This will I show the general. Please you, lords,
In sight of both our battles we may meet;
And either end in peace, which God so frame!
Or to the place of difference call the swords
Which must decide it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, we will do so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: There is a thing within my bosom tells me
That no conditions of our peace can stand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Fear you not that: if we can make our peace
Upon such large terms and so absolute
As our conditions shall consist upon,
Our peace shall stand as firm as rocky mountains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, but our valuation shall be such
That every slight and false-derived cause,
Yea, every idle, nice and wanton reason
Shall to the king taste of this action;
That, were our royal faiths martyrs in love,
We shall be winnow'd with so rough a wind
That even our corn shall seem as light as chaff
And good from bad find no partition.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, my lord. Note this; the king is weary
Of dainty and such picking grievances:
For he hath found to end one doubt by death
Revives two greater in the heirs of life,
And therefore will he wipe his tables clean
And keep no tell-tale to his memory
That may repeat and history his loss
To new remembrance; for full well he knows
He cannot so precisely weed this land
As his misdoubts present occasion:
His foes are so enrooted with his friends
That, plucking to unfix an enemy,
He doth unfasten so and shake a friend:
So that this land, like an offensive wife
That hath enraged him on to offer strokes,
As he is striking, holds his infant up
And hangs resolved correction in the arm
That was uprear'd to execution.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Besides, the king hath wasted all his rods
On late offenders, that he now doth lack
The very instruments of chastisement:
So that his power, like to a fangless lion,
May offer, but not hold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis very true:
And therefore be assured, my good lord marshal,
If we do now make our atonement well,
Our peace will, like a broken limb united,
Grow stronger for the breaking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so.
Here is return'd my Lord of Westmoreland.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: The prince is here at hand: pleaseth your lordship
To meet his grace just distance 'tween our armies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace of York, in God's name then, set forward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Before, and greet his grace: my lord, we come.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Another part of the forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter, from one side, MOWBRAY, attended; afterwards the ARCHBISHOP OF YORK, HASTINGS, and others: from the other side, Prince John of LANCASTER, and WESTMORELAND; Officers, and others with them

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: You are well encounter'd here, my cousin Mowbray:
Good day to you, gentle lord archbishop;
And so to you, Lord Hastings, and to all.
My Lord of York, it better show'd with you
When that your flock, assembled by the bell,
Encircled you to hear with reverence
Your exposition on the holy text
Than now to see you here an iron man,
Cheering a rout of rebels with your drum,
Turning the word to sword and life to death.
That man that sits within a monarch's heart,
And ripens in the sunshine of his favour,
Would he abuse the countenance of the king,
Alack, what mischiefs might he set abrooch
In shadow of such greatness! With you, lord bishop,
It is even so. Who hath not heard it spoken
How deep you were within the books of God?
To us the speaker in his parliament;
To us the imagined voice of God himself;
The very opener and intelligencer
Between the grace, the sanctities of heaven
And our dull workings. O, who shall believe
But you misuse the reverence of your place,
Employ the countenance and grace of heaven,
As a false favourite doth his prince's name,
In deeds dishonourable? You have ta'en up,
Under the counterfeited zeal of God,
The subjects of his substitute, my father,
And both against the peace of heaven and him
Have here up-swarm'd them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Good my Lord of Lancaster,
I am not here against your father's peace;
But, as I told my lord of Westmoreland,
The time misorder'd doth, in common sense,
Crowd us and crush us to this monstrous form,
To hold our safety up. I sent your grace
The parcels and particulars of our grief,
The which hath been with scorn shoved from the court,
Whereon this Hydra son of war is born;
Whose dangerous eyes may well be charm'd asleep
With grant of our most just and right desires,
And true obedience, of this madness cured,
Stoop tamely to the foot of majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: If not, we ready are to try our fortunes
To the last man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: And though we here fall down,
We have supplies to second our attempt:
If they miscarry, theirs shall second them;
And so success of mischief shall be born
And heir from heir shall hold this quarrel up
Whiles England shall have generation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: You are too shallow, Hastings, much too shallow,
To sound the bottom of the after-times.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Pleaseth your grace to answer them directly
How far forth you do like their articles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: I like them all, and do allow them well,
And swear here, by the honour of my blood,
My father's purposes have been mistook,
And some about him have too lavishly
Wrested his meaning and authority.
My lord, these griefs shall be with speed redress'd;
Upon my soul, they shall. If this may please you,
Discharge your powers unto their several counties,
As we will ours: and here between the armies
Let's drink together friendly and embrace,
That all their eyes may bear those tokens home
Of our restored love and amity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I take your princely word for these redresses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: I give it you, and will maintain my word:
And thereupon I drink unto your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Go, captain, and deliver to the army
This news of peace: let them have pay, and part:
I know it will well please them. Hie thee, captain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: To you, my noble Lord of Westmoreland.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: I pledge your grace; and, if you knew what pains
I have bestow'd to breed this present peace,
You would drink freely: but my love to ye
Shall show itself more openly hereafter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I do not doubt you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad of it.
Health to my lord and gentle cousin, Mowbray.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: You wish me health in very happy season;
For I am, on the sudden, something ill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Against ill chances men are ever merry;
But heaviness foreruns the good event.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore be merry, coz; since sudden sorrow
Serves to say thus, 'some good thing comes
to-morrow.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Believe me, I am passing light in spirit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: So much the worse, if your own rule be true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: The word of peace is render'd: hark, how they shout!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: This had been cheerful after victory.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: A peace is of the nature of a conquest;
For then both parties nobly are subdued,
And neither party loser.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Go, my lord,
And let our army be discharged too.
And, good my lord, so please you, let our trains
March, by us, that we may peruse the men
We should have coped withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Go, good Lord Hastings,
And, ere they be dismissed, let them march by.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: I trust, lords, we shall lie to-night together.
Now, cousin, wherefore stands our army still?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: The leaders, having charge from you to stand,
Will not go off until they hear you speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: They know their duties.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, our army is dispersed already;
Like youthful steers unyoked, they take their courses
East, west, north, south; or, like a school broke up,
Each hurries toward his home and sporting-place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Good tidings, my Lord Hastings; for the which
I do arrest thee, traitor, of high treason:
And you, lord archbishop, and you, Lord Mowbray,
Of capitol treason I attach you both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOWBRAY
SPEECH.LINE: Is this proceeding just and honourable?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Is your assembly so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Will you thus break your faith?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: I pawn'd thee none:
I promised you redress of these same grievances
Whereof you did complain; which, by mine honour,
I will perform with a most Christian care.
But for you, rebels, look to taste the due
Meet for rebellion and such acts as yours.
Most shallowly did you these arms commence,
Fondly brought here and foolishly sent hence.
Strike up our drums, pursue the scatter'd stray:
God, and not we, hath safely fought to-day.
Some guard these traitors to the block of death,
Treason's true bed and yielder up of breath.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Another part of the forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum. Excursions. Enter FALSTAFF and COLEVILE, meeting

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What's your name, sir? of what condition are you,
and of what place, I pray?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: I am a knight, sir, and my name is Colevile of the dale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Well, then, Colevile is your name, a knight is your
degree, and your place the dale: Colevile shall be
still your name, a traitor your degree, and the
dungeon your place, a place deep enough; so shall
you be still Colevile of the dale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: Are not you Sir John Falstaff?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: As good a man as he, sir, whoe'er I am. Do ye
yield, sir? or shall I sweat for you? if I do
sweat, they are the drops of thy lovers, and they
weep for thy death: therefore rouse up fear and
trembling, and do observance to my mercy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: I think you are Sir John Falstaff, and in that
thought yield me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I have a whole school of tongues in this belly of
mine, and not a tongue of them all speaks any other
word but my name. An I had but a belly of any
indifference, I were simply the most active fellow
in Europe: my womb, my womb, my womb, undoes me.
Here comes our general.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PRINCE JOHN OF LANCASTER, WESTMORELAND, BLUNT, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: The heat is past; follow no further now:
Call in the powers, good cousin Westmoreland.
Now, Falstaff, where have you been all this while?
When every thing is ended, then you come:
These tardy tricks of yours will, on my life,
One time or other break some gallows' back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I would be sorry, my lord, but it should be thus: I
never knew yet but rebuke and cheque was the reward
of valour. Do you think me a swallow, an arrow, or a
bullet? have I, in my poor and old motion, the
expedition of thought? I have speeded hither with
the very extremest inch of possibility; I have
foundered nine score and odd posts: and here,
travel-tainted as I am, have in my pure and
immaculate valour, taken Sir John Colevile of the
dale, a most furious knight and valorous enemy.
But what of that? he saw me, and yielded; that I
may justly say, with the hook-nosed fellow of Rome,
'I came, saw, and overcame.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: It was more of his courtesy than your deserving.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I know not: here he is, and here I yield him: and
I beseech your grace, let it be booked with the
rest of this day's deeds; or, by the Lord, I will
have it in a particular ballad else, with mine own
picture on the top on't, Colevile kissing my foot:
to the which course if I be enforced, if you do not
all show like gilt twopences to me, and I in the
clear sky of fame o'ershine you as much as the full
moon doth the cinders of the element, which show
like pins' heads to her, believe not the word of
the noble: therefore let me have right, and let
desert mount.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Thine's too heavy to mount.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Let it shine, then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Thine's too thick to shine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Let it do something, my good lord, that may do me
good, and call it what you will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Is thy name Colevile?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: It is, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: A famous rebel art thou, Colevile.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: And a famous true subject took him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: I am, my lord, but as my betters are
That led me hither: had they been ruled by me,
You should have won them dearer than you have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I know not how they sold themselves: but thou, like
a kind fellow, gavest thyself away gratis; and I
thank thee for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Now, have you left pursuit?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Retreat is made and execution stay'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Send Colevile with his confederates
To York, to present execution:
Blunt, lead him hence; and see you guard him sure.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Exeunt BLUNT and others with COLEVILE
SPEECH.LINE: And now dispatch we toward the court, my lords:
I hear the king my father is sore sick:
Our news shall go before us to his majesty,
Which, cousin, you shall bear to comfort him,
And we with sober speed will follow you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I beseech you, give me leave to go
Through Gloucestershire: and, when you come to court,
Stand my good lord, pray, in your good report.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, Falstaff: I, in my condition,
Shall better speak of you than you deserve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I would you had but the wit: 'twere better than
your dukedom. Good faith, this same young sober-
blooded boy doth not love me; nor a man cannot make
him laugh; but that's no marvel, he drinks no wine.
There's never none of these demure boys come to any
proof; for thin drink doth so over-cool their blood,
and making many fish-meals, that they fall into a
kind of male green-sickness; and then when they
marry, they get wenches: they are generally fools
and cowards; which some of us should be too, but for
inflammation. A good sherris sack hath a two-fold
operation in it. It ascends me into the brain;
dries me there all the foolish and dull and curdy
vapours which environ it; makes it apprehensive,
quick, forgetive, full of nimble fiery and
delectable shapes, which, delivered o'er to the
voice, the tongue, which is the birth, becomes
excellent wit. The second property of your
excellent sherris is, the warming of the blood;
which, before cold and settled, left the liver
white and pale, which is the badge of pusillanimity
and cowardice; but the sherris warms it and makes
it course from the inwards to the parts extreme:
it illumineth the face, which as a beacon gives
warning to all the rest of this little kingdom,
man, to arm; and then the vital commoners and
inland petty spirits muster me all to their captain,
the heart, who, great and puffed up with this
retinue, doth any deed of courage; and this valour
comes of sherris. So that skill in the weapon is
nothing without sack, for that sets it a-work; and
learning a mere hoard of gold kept by a devil, till
sack commences it and sets it in act and use.
Hereof comes it that Prince Harry is valiant; for
the cold blood he did naturally inherit of his
father, he hath, like lean, sterile and bare land,
manured, husbanded and tilled with excellent
endeavour of drinking good and good store of fertile
sherris, that he is become very hot and valiant. If
I had a thousand sons, the first humane principle I
would teach them should be, to forswear thin
potations and to addict themselves to sack.
How now Bardolph?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: The army is discharged all and gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Let them go. I'll through Gloucestershire; and
there will I visit Master Robert Shallow, esquire:
I have him already tempering between my finger and
my thumb, and shortly will I seal with him. Come away.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Westminster. The Jerusalem Chamber.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter KING HENRY IV, the Princes Thomas of CLARENCE and Humphrey of GLOUCESTER, WARWICK, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now, lords, if God doth give successful end
To this debate that bleedeth at our doors,
We will our youth lead on to higher fields
And draw no swords but what are sanctified.
Our navy is address'd, our power collected,
Our substitutes in absence well invested,
And every thing lies level to our wish:
Only, we want a little personal strength;
And pause us, till these rebels, now afoot,
Come underneath the yoke of government.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Both which we doubt not but your majesty
Shall soon enjoy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Humphrey, my son of Gloucester,
Where is the prince your brother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I think he's gone to hunt, my lord, at Windsor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: And how accompanied?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I do not know, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Is not his brother, Thomas of Clarence, with him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord; he is in presence here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: What would my lord and father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing but well to thee, Thomas of Clarence.
How chance thou art not with the prince thy brother?
He loves thee, and thou dost neglect him, Thomas;
Thou hast a better place in his affection
Than all thy brothers: cherish it, my boy,
And noble offices thou mayst effect
Of mediation, after I am dead,
Between his greatness and thy other brethren:
Therefore omit him not; blunt not his love,
Nor lose the good advantage of his grace
By seeming cold or careless of his will;
For he is gracious, if he be observed:
He hath a tear for pity and a hand
Open as day for melting charity:
Yet notwithstanding, being incensed, he's flint,
As humorous as winter and as sudden
As flaws congealed in the spring of day.
His temper, therefore, must be well observed:
Chide him for faults, and do it reverently,
When thou perceive his blood inclined to mirth;
But, being moody, give him line and scope,
Till that his passions, like a whale on ground,
Confound themselves with working. Learn this, Thomas,
And thou shalt prove a shelter to thy friends,
A hoop of gold to bind thy brothers in,
That the united vessel of their blood,
Mingled with venom of suggestion--
As, force perforce, the age will pour it in--
Shall never leak, though it do work as strong
As aconitum or rash gunpowder.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: I shall observe him with all care and love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Why art thou not at Windsor with him, Thomas?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: He is not there to-day; he dines in London.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: And how accompanied? canst thou tell that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: With Poins, and other his continual followers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Most subject is the fattest soil to weeds;
And he, the noble image of my youth,
Is overspread with them: therefore my grief
Stretches itself beyond the hour of death:
The blood weeps from my heart when I do shape
In forms imaginary the unguided days
And rotten times that you shall look upon
When I am sleeping with my ancestors.
For when his headstrong riot hath no curb,
When rage and hot blood are his counsellors,
When means and lavish manners meet together,
O, with what wings shall his affections fly
Towards fronting peril and opposed decay!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious lord, you look beyond him quite:
The prince but studies his companions
Like a strange tongue, wherein, to gain the language,
'Tis needful that the most immodest word
Be look'd upon and learn'd; which once attain'd,
Your highness knows, comes to no further use
But to be known and hated. So, like gross terms,
The prince will in the perfectness of time
Cast off his followers; and their memory
Shall as a pattern or a measure live,
By which his grace must mete the lives of others,
Turning past evils to advantages.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis seldom when the bee doth leave her comb
In the dead carrion.
Who's here? Westmoreland?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Health to my sovereign, and new happiness
Added to that that I am to deliver!
Prince John your son doth kiss your grace's hand:
Mowbray, the Bishop Scroop, Hastings and all
Are brought to the correction of your law;
There is not now a rebel's sword unsheath'd
But peace puts forth her olive every where.
The manner how this action hath been borne
Here at more leisure may your highness read,
With every course in his particular.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: O Westmoreland, thou art a summer bird,
Which ever in the haunch of winter sings
The lifting up of day.
Look, here's more news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HARCOURT
SPEECH.LINE: From enemies heaven keep your majesty;
And, when they stand against you, may they fall
As those that I am come to tell you of!
The Earl Northumberland and the Lord Bardolph,
With a great power of English and of Scots
Are by the sheriff of Yorkshire overthrown:
The manner and true order of the fight
This packet, please it you, contains at large.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: And wherefore should these good news make me sick?
Will fortune never come with both hands full,
But write her fair words still in foulest letters?
She either gives a stomach and no food;
Such are the poor, in health; or else a feast
And takes away the stomach; such are the rich,
That have abundance and enjoy it not.
I should rejoice now at this happy news;
And now my sight fails, and my brain is giddy:
O me! come near me; now I am much ill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Comfort, your majesty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O my royal father!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: My sovereign lord, cheer up yourself, look up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Be patient, princes; you do know, these fits
Are with his highness very ordinary.
Stand from him. Give him air; he'll straight be well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, he cannot long hold out these pangs:
The incessant care and labour of his mind
Hath wrought the mure that should confine it in
So thin that life looks through and will break out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: The people fear me; for they do observe
Unfather'd heirs and loathly births of nature:
The seasons change their manners, as the year
Had found some months asleep and leap'd them over.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: The river hath thrice flow'd, no ebb between;
And the old folk, time's doting chronicles,
Say it did so a little time before
That our great-grandsire, Edward, sick'd and died.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Speak lower, princes, for the king recovers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: This apoplexy will certain be his end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, take me up, and bear me hence
Into some other chamber: softly, pray.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another chamber.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: KING HENRY IV lying on a bed: CLARENCE, GLOUCESTER, WARWICK, and others in attendance

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Let there be no noise made, my gentle friends;
Unless some dull and favourable hand
Will whisper music to my weary spirit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Call for the music in the other room.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Set me the crown upon my pillow here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: His eye is hollow, and he changes much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Less noise, less noise!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: Who saw the Duke of Clarence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: I am here, brother, full of heaviness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: How now! rain within doors, and none abroad!
How doth the king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Exceeding ill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: Heard he the good news yet?
Tell it him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: He alter'd much upon the hearing it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: If he be sick with joy, he'll recover without physic.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Not so much noise, my lords: sweet prince,
speak low;
The king your father is disposed to sleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Let us withdraw into the other room.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Will't please your grace to go along with us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: No; I will sit and watch here by the king.
Why doth the crown lie there upon his pillow,
Being so troublesome a bedfellow?
O polish'd perturbation! golden care!
That keep'st the ports of slumber open wide
To many a watchful night! sleep with it now!
Yet not so sound and half so deeply sweet
As he whose brow with homely biggen bound
Snores out the watch of night. O majesty!
When thou dost pinch thy bearer, thou dost sit
Like a rich armour worn in heat of day,
That scalds with safety. By his gates of breath
There lies a downy feather which stirs not:
Did he suspire, that light and weightless down
Perforce must move. My gracious lord! my father!
This sleep is sound indeed, this is a sleep
That from this golden rigol hath divorced
So many English kings. Thy due from me
Is tears and heavy sorrows of the blood,
Which nature, love, and filial tenderness,
Shall, O dear father, pay thee plenteously:
My due from thee is this imperial crown,
Which, as immediate as thy place and blood,
Derives itself to me. Lo, here it sits,
Which God shall guard: and put the world's whole strength
Into one giant arm, it shall not force
This lineal honour from me: this from thee
Will I to mine leave, as 'tis left to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Warwick! Gloucester! Clarence!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter WARWICK, GLOUCESTER, CLARENCE, and the rest

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Doth the king call?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: What would your majesty? How fares your grace?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Why did you leave me here alone, my lords?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: We left the prince my brother here, my liege,
Who undertook to sit and watch by you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: The Prince of Wales! Where is he? let me see him:
He is not here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: This door is open; he is gone this way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: He came not through the chamber where we stay'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Where is the crown? who took it from my pillow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: When we withdrew, my liege, we left it here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: The prince hath ta'en it hence: go, seek him out.
Is he so hasty that he doth suppose
My sleep my death?
Find him, my Lord of Warwick; chide him hither.
This part of his conjoins with my disease,
And helps to end me. See, sons, what things you are!
How quickly nature falls into revolt
When gold becomes her object!
For this the foolish over-careful fathers
Have broke their sleep with thoughts, their brains with care,
Their bones with industry;
For this they have engrossed and piled up
The canker'd heaps of strange-achieved gold;
For this they have been thoughtful to invest
Their sons with arts and martial exercises:
When, like the bee, culling from every flower
The virtuous sweets,
Our thighs pack'd with wax, our mouths with honey,
We bring it to the hive, and, like the bees,
Are murdered for our pains. This bitter taste
Yield his engrossments to the ending father.
Now, where is he that will not stay so long
Till his friend sickness hath determined me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I found the prince in the next room,
Washing with kindly tears his gentle cheeks,
With such a deep demeanor in great sorrow
That tyranny, which never quaff'd but blood,
Would, by beholding him, have wash'd his knife
With gentle eye-drops. He is coming hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: But wherefore did he take away the crown?
Lo, where he comes. Come hither to me, Harry.
Depart the chamber, leave us here alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: I never thought to hear you speak again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Thy wish was father, Harry, to that thought:
I stay too long by thee, I weary thee.
Dost thou so hunger for mine empty chair
That thou wilt needs invest thee with my honours
Before thy hour be ripe? O foolish youth!
Thou seek'st the greatness that will o'erwhelm thee.
Stay but a little; for my cloud of dignity
Is held from falling with so weak a wind
That it will quickly drop: my day is dim.
Thou hast stolen that which after some few hours
Were thine without offence; and at my death
Thou hast seal'd up my expectation:
Thy life did manifest thou lovedst me not,
And thou wilt have me die assured of it.
Thou hidest a thousand daggers in thy thoughts,
Which thou hast whetted on thy stony heart,
To stab at half an hour of my life.
What! canst thou not forbear me half an hour?
Then get thee gone and dig my grave thyself,
And bid the merry bells ring to thine ear
That thou art crowned, not that I am dead.
Let all the tears that should bedew my hearse
Be drops of balm to sanctify thy head:
Only compound me with forgotten dust
Give that which gave thee life unto the worms.
Pluck down my officers, break my decrees;
For now a time is come to mock at form:
Harry the Fifth is crown'd: up, vanity!
Down, royal state! all you sage counsellors, hence!
And to the English court assemble now,
From every region, apes of idleness!
Now, neighbour confines, purge you of your scum:
Have you a ruffian that will swear, drink, dance,
Revel the night, rob, murder, and commit
The oldest sins the newest kind of ways?
Be happy, he will trouble you no more;
England shall double gild his treble guilt,
England shall give him office, honour, might;
For the fifth Harry from curb'd licence plucks
The muzzle of restraint, and the wild dog
Shall flesh his tooth on every innocent.
O my poor kingdom, sick with civil blows!
When that my care could not withhold thy riots,
What wilt thou do when riot is thy care?
O, thou wilt be a wilderness again,
Peopled with wolves, thy old inhabitants!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: O, pardon me, my liege! but for my tears,
The moist impediments unto my speech,
I had forestall'd this dear and deep rebuke
Ere you with grief had spoke and I had heard
The course of it so far. There is your crown;
And He that wears the crown immortally
Long guard it yours! If I affect it more
Than as your honour and as your renown,
Let me no more from this obedience rise,
Which my most inward true and duteous spirit
Teacheth, this prostrate and exterior bending.
God witness with me, when I here came in,
And found no course of breath within your majesty,
How cold it struck my heart! If I do feign,
O, let me in my present wildness die
And never live to show the incredulous world
The noble change that I have purposed!
Coming to look on you, thinking you dead,
And dead almost, my liege, to think you were,
I spake unto this crown as having sense,
And thus upbraided it: 'The care on thee depending
Hath fed upon the body of my father;
Therefore, thou best of gold art worst of gold:
Other, less fine in carat, is more precious,
Preserving life in medicine potable;
But thou, most fine, most honour'd: most renown'd,
Hast eat thy bearer up.' Thus, my most royal liege,
Accusing it, I put it on my head,
To try with it, as with an enemy
That had before my face murder'd my father,
The quarrel of a true inheritor.
But if it did infect my blood with joy,
Or swell my thoughts to any strain of pride;
If any rebel or vain spirit of mine
Did with the least affection of a welcome
Give entertainment to the might of it,
Let God for ever keep it from my head
And make me as the poorest vassal is
That doth with awe and terror kneel to it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: O my son,
God put it in thy mind to take it hence,
That thou mightst win the more thy father's love,
Pleading so wisely in excuse of it!
Come hither, Harry, sit thou by my bed;
And hear, I think, the very latest counsel
That ever I shall breathe. God knows, my son,
By what by-paths and indirect crook'd ways
I met this crown; and I myself know well
How troublesome it sat upon my head.
To thee it shall descend with bitter quiet,
Better opinion, better confirmation;
For all the soil of the achievement goes
With me into the earth. It seem'd in me
But as an honour snatch'd with boisterous hand,
And I had many living to upbraid
My gain of it by their assistances;
Which daily grew to quarrel and to bloodshed,
Wounding supposed peace: all these bold fears
Thou see'st with peril I have answered;
For all my reign hath been but as a scene
Acting that argument: and now my death
Changes the mode; for what in me was purchased,
Falls upon thee in a more fairer sort;
So thou the garland wear'st successively.
Yet, though thou stand'st more sure than I could do,
Thou art not firm enough, since griefs are green;
And all my friends, which thou must make thy friends,
Have but their stings and teeth newly ta'en out;
By whose fell working I was first advanced
And by whose power I well might lodge a fear
To be again displaced: which to avoid,
I cut them off; and had a purpose now
To lead out many to the Holy Land,
Lest rest and lying still might make them look
Too near unto my state. Therefore, my Harry,
Be it thy course to busy giddy minds
With foreign quarrels; that action, hence borne out,
May waste the memory of the former days.
More would I, but my lungs are wasted so
That strength of speech is utterly denied me.
How I came by the crown, O God forgive;
And grant it may with thee in true peace live!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious liege,
You won it, wore it, kept it, gave it me;
Then plain and right must my possession be:
Which I with more than with a common pain
'Gainst all the world will rightfully maintain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Look, look, here comes my John of Lancaster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Health, peace, and happiness to my royal father!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Thou bring'st me happiness and peace, son John;
But health, alack, with youthful wings is flown
From this bare wither'd trunk: upon thy sight
My worldly business makes a period.
Where is my Lord of Warwick?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE HENRY
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord of Warwick!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Doth any name particular belong
Unto the lodging where I first did swoon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis call'd Jerusalem, my noble lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY IV
SPEECH.LINE: Laud be to God! even there my life must end.
It hath been prophesied to me many years,
I should not die but in Jerusalem;
Which vainly I supposed the Holy Land:
But bear me to that chamber; there I'll lie;
In that Jerusalem shall Harry die.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Gloucestershire. SHALLOW'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SHALLOW, FALSTAFF, BARDOLPH, and Page

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: By cock and pie, sir, you shall not away to-night.
What, Davy, I say!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: You must excuse me, Master Robert Shallow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: I will not excuse you; you shall not be excused;
excuses shall not be admitted; there is no excuse
shall serve; you shall not be excused. Why, Davy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Davy, Davy, Davy, Davy, let me see, Davy; let me
see, Davy; let me see: yea, marry, William cook,
bid him come hither. Sir John, you shall not be excused.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, thus; those precepts cannot be served:
and, again, sir, shall we sow the headland with wheat?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: With red wheat, Davy. But for William cook: are
there no young pigeons?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, sir. Here is now the smith's note for shoeing
and plough-irons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Let it be cast and paid. Sir John, you shall not be excused.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: Now, sir, a new link to the bucket must need be
had: and, sir, do you mean to stop any of William's
wages, about the sack he lost the other day at
Hinckley fair?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: A' shall answer it. Some pigeons, Davy, a couple
of short-legged hens, a joint of mutton, and any
pretty little tiny kickshaws, tell William cook.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: Doth the man of war stay all night, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, Davy. I will use him well: a friend i' the
court is better than a penny in purse. Use his men
well, Davy; for they are arrant knaves, and will backbite.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: No worse than they are backbitten, sir; for they
have marvellous foul linen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Well conceited, Davy: about thy business, Davy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you, sir, to countenance William Visor of
Woncot against Clement Perkes of the hill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: There is many complaints, Davy, against that Visor:
that Visor is an arrant knave, on my knowledge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DAVY
SPEECH.LINE: I grant your worship that he is a knave, sir; but
yet, God forbid, sir, but a knave should have some
countenance at his friend's request. An honest
man, sir, is able to speak for himself, when a knave
is not. I have served your worship truly, sir,
this eight years; and if I cannot once or twice in
a quarter bear out a knave against an honest man, I
have but a very little credit with your worship. The
knave is mine honest friend, sir; therefore, I
beseech your worship, let him be countenanced.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; I say he shall have no wrong. Look about, Davy.
Where are you, Sir John? Come, come, come, off
with your boots. Give me your hand, Master Bardolph.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad to see your worship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee with all my heart, kind
Master Bardolph: and welcome, my tall fellow.
Come, Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I'll follow you, good Master Robert Shallow.
Bardolph, look to our horses.
If I were sawed into quantities, I should make four
dozen of such bearded hermits' staves as Master
Shallow. It is a wonderful thing to see the
semblable coherence of his men's spirits and his:
they, by observing of him, do bear themselves like
foolish justices; he, by conversing with them, is
turned into a justice-like serving-man: their
spirits are so married in conjunction with the
participation of society that they flock together in
consent, like so many wild-geese. If I had a suit
to Master Shallow, I would humour his men with the
imputation of being near their master: if to his
men, I would curry with Master Shallow that no man
could better command his servants. It is certain
that either wise bearing or ignorant carriage is
caught, as men take diseases, one of another:
therefore let men take heed of their company. I
will devise matter enough out of this Shallow to
keep Prince Harry in continual laughter the wearing
out of six fashions, which is four terms, or two
actions, and a' shall laugh without intervallums. O,
it is much that a lie with a slight oath and a jest
with a sad brow will do with a fellow that never
had the ache in his shoulders! O, you shall see him
laugh till his face be like a wet cloak ill laid up!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Within Sir John!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I come, Master Shallow; I come, Master Shallow.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Westminster. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter WARWICK and the Lord Chief-Justice, meeting

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: How now, my lord chief-justice! whither away?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: How doth the king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Exceeding well; his cares are now all ended.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: I hope, not dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: He's walk'd the way of nature;
And to our purposes he lives no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: I would his majesty had call'd me with him:
The service that I truly did his life
Hath left me open to all injuries.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed I think the young king loves you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: I know he doth not, and do arm myself
To welcome the condition of the time,
Which cannot look more hideously upon me
Than I have drawn it in my fantasy.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter LANCASTER, CLARENCE, GLOUCESTER, WESTMORELAND, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Here come the heavy issue of dead Harry:
O that the living Harry had the temper
Of him, the worst of these three gentlemen!
How many nobles then should hold their places
That must strike sail to spirits of vile sort!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: O God, I fear all will be overturn'd!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, cousin Warwick, good morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: We meet like men that had forgot to speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: We do remember; but our argument
Is all too heavy to admit much talk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Well, peace be with him that hath made us heavy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: Peace be with us, lest we be heavier!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: O, good my lord, you have lost a friend indeed;
And I dare swear you borrow not that face
Of seeming sorrow, it is sure your own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LANCASTER
SPEECH.LINE: Though no man be assured what grace to find,
You stand in coldest expectation:
I am the sorrier; would 'twere otherwise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Well, you must now speak Sir John Falstaff fair;
Which swims against your stream of quality.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet princes, what I did, I did in honour,
Led by the impartial conduct of my soul:
And never shall you see that I will beg
A ragged and forestall'd remission.
If truth and upright innocency fail me,
I'll to the king my master that is dead,
And tell him who hath sent me after him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the prince.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow; and God save your majesty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY V
SPEECH.LINE: This new and gorgeous garment, majesty,
Sits not so easy on me as you think.
Brothers, you mix your sadness with some fear:
This is the English, not the Turkish court;
Not Amurath an Amurath succeeds,
But Harry Harry. Yet be sad, good brothers,
For, by my faith, it very well becomes you:
Sorrow so royally in you appears
That I will deeply put the fashion on
And wear it in my heart: why then, be sad;
But entertain no more of it, good brothers,
Than a joint burden laid upon us all.
For me, by heaven, I bid you be assured,
I'll be your father and your brother too;
Let me but bear your love, I 'll bear your cares:
Yet weep that Harry's dead; and so will I;
But Harry lives, that shall convert those tears
By number into hours of happiness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Princes
SPEECH.LINE: We hope no other from your majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY V
SPEECH.LINE: You all look strangely on me: and you most;
You are, I think, assured I love you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: I am assured, if I be measured rightly,
Your majesty hath no just cause to hate me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY V
SPEECH.LINE: No!
How might a prince of my great hopes forget
So great indignities you laid upon me?
What! rate, rebuke, and roughly send to prison
The immediate heir of England! Was this easy?
May this be wash'd in Lethe, and forgotten?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Chief-Justice
SPEECH.LINE: I then did use the person of your father;
The image of his power lay then in me:
And, in the administration of his law,
Whiles I was busy for the commonwealth,
Your highness pleased to forget my place,
The majesty and power of law and justice,
The image of the king whom I presented,
And struck me in my very seat of judgment;
Whereon, as an offender to your father,
I gave bold way to my authority
And did commit you. If the deed were ill,
Be you contented, wearing now the garland,
To have a son set your decrees at nought,
To pluck down justice from your awful bench,
To trip the course of law and blunt the sword
That guards the peace and safety of your person;
Nay, more, to spurn at your most royal image
And mock your workings in a second body.
Question your royal thoughts, make the case yours;
Be now the father and propose a son,
Hear your own dignity so much profaned,
See your most dreadful laws so loosely slighted,
Behold yourself so by a son disdain'd;
And then imagine me taking your part
And in your power soft silencing your son:
After this cold considerance, sentence me;
And, as you are a king, speak in your state
What I have done that misbecame my place,
My person, or my liege's sovereignty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY V
SPEECH.LINE: You are right, justice, and you weigh this well;
Therefore still bear the balance and the sword:
And I do wish your honours may increase,
Till you do live to see a son of mine
Offend you and obey you, as I did.
So shall I live to speak my father's words:
'Happy am I, that have a man so bold,
That dares do justice on my proper son;
