SPEECH.LINE: God save the king! God save the king!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: What, Buckingham and Clifford, are ye so brave? And
you, base peasants, do ye believe him? will you
needs be hanged with your pardons about your necks?
Hath my sword therefore broke through London gates,
that you should leave me at the White Hart in
Southwark? I thought ye would never have given out
these arms till you had recovered your ancient
freedom: but you are all recreants and dastards,
and delight to live in slavery to the nobility. Let
them break your backs with burthens, take your
houses over your heads, ravish your wives and
daughters before your faces: for me, I will make
shift for one; and so, God's curse light upon you
all!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: We'll follow Cade, we'll follow Cade!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Is Cade the son of Henry the Fifth,
That thus you do exclaim you'll go with him?
Will he conduct you through the heart of France,
And make the meanest of you earls and dukes?
Alas, he hath no home, no place to fly to;
Nor knows he how to live but by the spoil,
Unless by robbing of your friends and us.
Were't not a shame, that whilst you live at jar,
The fearful French, whom you late vanquished,
Should make a start o'er seas and vanquish you?
Methinks already in this civil broil
I see them lording it in London streets,
Crying 'Villiago!' unto all they meet.
Better ten thousand base-born Cades miscarry
Than you should stoop unto a Frenchman's mercy.
To France, to France, and get what you have lost;
Spare England, for it is your native coast;
Henry hath money, you are strong and manly;
God on our side, doubt not of victory.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: A Clifford! a Clifford! we'll follow the king and Clifford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: Was ever feather so lightly blown to and fro as this
multitude? The name of Henry the Fifth hales them
to an hundred mischiefs, and makes them leave me
desolate. I see them lay their heads together to
surprise me. My sword make way for me, for here is
no staying. In despite of the devils and hell, have
through the very middest of you? and heavens and
honour be witness, that no want of resolution in me.
but only my followers' base and ignominious
treasons, makes me betake me to my heels.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: What, is he fled? Go some, and follow him;
And he that brings his head unto the king
Shall have a thousand crowns for his reward.
Follow me, soldiers: we'll devise a mean
To reconcile you all unto the king.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IX. Kenilworth Castle.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Sound Trumpets. Enter KING HENRY VI, QUEEN MARGARET, and SOMERSET, on the terrace

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Was ever king that joy'd an earthly throne,
And could command no more content than I?
No sooner was I crept out of my cradle
But I was made a king, at nine months old.
Was never subject long'd to be a king
As I do long and wish to be a subject.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Health and glad tidings to your majesty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Why, Buckingham, is the traitor Cade surprised?
Or is he but retired to make him strong?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter below, multitudes, with halters about their necks

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: He is fled, my lord, and all his powers do yield;
And humbly thus, with halters on their necks,
Expect your highness' doom of life or death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Then, heaven, set ope thy everlasting gates,
To entertain my vows of thanks and praise!
Soldiers, this day have you redeemed your lives,
And show'd how well you love your prince and country:
Continue still in this so good a mind,
And Henry, though he be infortunate,
Assure yourselves, will never be unkind:
And so, with thanks and pardon to you all,
I do dismiss you to your several countries.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: God save the king! God save the king!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Please it your grace to be advertised
The Duke of York is newly come from Ireland,
And with a puissant and a mighty power
Of gallowglasses and stout kerns
Is marching hitherward in proud array,
And still proclaimeth, as he comes along,
His arms are only to remove from thee
The Duke of Somerset, whom he terms traitor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Thus stands my state, 'twixt Cade and York distress'd.
Like to a ship that, having 'scaped a tempest,
Is straightway calm'd and boarded with a pirate:
But now is Cade driven back, his men dispersed;
And now is York in arms to second him.
I pray thee, Buckingham, go and meet him,
And ask him what's the reason of these arms.
Tell him I'll send Duke Edmund to the Tower;
And, Somerset, we'll commit thee thither,
Until his army be dismiss'd from him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,
I'll yield myself to prison willingly,
Or unto death, to do my country good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: In any case, be not too rough in terms;
For he is fierce and cannot brook hard language.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I will, my lord; and doubt not so to deal
As all things shall redound unto your good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Come, wife, let's in, and learn to govern better;
For yet may England curse my wretched reign.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE X. Kent. IDEN's garden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: Fie on ambition! fie on myself, that have a sword,
and yet am ready to famish! These five days have I
hid me in these woods and durst not peep out, for
all the country is laid for me; but now am I so
hungry that if I might have a lease of my life for a
thousand years I could stay no longer. Wherefore,
on a brick wall have I climbed into this garden, to
see if I can eat grass, or pick a sallet another
while, which is not amiss to cool a man's stomach
this hot weather. And I think this word 'sallet'
was born to do me good: for many a time, but for a
sallet, my brainpan had been cleft with a brown
bill; and many a time, when I have been dry and
bravely marching, it hath served me instead of a
quart pot to drink in; and now the word 'sallet'
must serve me to feed on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: Lord, who would live turmoiled in the court,
And may enjoy such quiet walks as these?
This small inheritance my father left me
Contenteth me, and worth a monarchy.
I seek not to wax great by others' waning,
Or gather wealth, I care not, with what envy:
Sufficeth that I have maintains my state
And sends the poor well pleased from my gate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: Here's the lord of the soil come to seize me for a
stray, for entering his fee-simple without leave.
Ah, villain, thou wilt betray me, and get a thousand
crowns of the king carrying my head to him: but
I'll make thee eat iron like an ostrich, and swallow
my sword like a great pin, ere thou and I part.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: Why, rude companion, whatsoe'er thou be,
I know thee not; why, then, should I betray thee?
Is't not enough to break into my garden,
And, like a thief, to come to rob my grounds,
Climbing my walls in spite of me the owner,
But thou wilt brave me with these saucy terms?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: Brave thee! ay, by the best blood that ever was
broached, and beard thee too. Look on me well: I
have eat no meat these five days; yet, come thou and
thy five men, and if I do not leave you all as dead
as a doornail, I pray God I may never eat grass more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, it shall ne'er be said, while England stands,
That Alexander Iden, an esquire of Kent,
Took odds to combat a poor famish'd man.
Oppose thy steadfast-gazing eyes to mine,
See if thou canst outface me with thy looks:
Set limb to limb, and thou art far the lesser;
Thy hand is but a finger to my fist,
Thy leg a stick compared with this truncheon;
My foot shall fight with all the strength thou hast;
And if mine arm be heaved in the air,
Thy grave is digg'd already in the earth.
As for words, whose greatness answers words,
Let this my sword report what speech forbears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: By my valour, the most complete champion that ever I
heard! Steel, if thou turn the edge, or cut not out
the burly-boned clown in chines of beef ere thou
sleep in thy sheath, I beseech God on my knees thou
mayst be turned to hobnails.
O, I am slain! famine and no other hath slain me:
let ten thousand devils come against me, and give me
but the ten meals I have lost, and I'll defy them
all. Wither, garden; and be henceforth a
burying-place to all that do dwell in this house,
because the unconquered soul of Cade is fled.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: Is't Cade that I have slain, that monstrous traitor?
Sword, I will hollow thee for this thy deed,
And hang thee o'er my tomb when I am dead:
Ne'er shall this blood be wiped from thy point;
But thou shalt wear it as a herald's coat,
To emblaze the honour that thy master got.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CADE
SPEECH.LINE: Iden, farewell, and be proud of thy victory. Tell
Kent from me, she hath lost her best man, and exhort
all the world to be cowards; for I, that never
feared any, am vanquished by famine, not by valour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: How much thou wrong'st me, heaven be my judge.
Die, damned wretch, the curse of her that bare thee;
And as I thrust thy body in with my sword,
So wish I, I might thrust thy soul to hell.
Hence will I drag thee headlong by the heels
Unto a dunghill which shall be thy grave,
And there cut off thy most ungracious head;
Which I will bear in triumph to the king,
Leaving thy trunk for crows to feed upon.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Fields between Dartford and Blackheath.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter YORK, and his army of Irish, with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: From Ireland thus comes York to claim his right,
And pluck the crown from feeble Henry's head:
Ring, bells, aloud; burn, bonfires, clear and bright,
To entertain great England's lawful king.
Ah! sancta majestas, who would not buy thee dear?
Let them obey that know not how to rule;
This hand was made to handle naught but gold.
I cannot give due action to my words,
Except a sword or sceptre balance it:
A sceptre shall it have, have I a soul,
On which I'll toss the flower-de-luce of France.
Whom have we here? Buckingham, to disturb me?
The king hath sent him, sure: I must dissemble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: York, if thou meanest well, I greet thee well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Humphrey of Buckingham, I accept thy greeting.
Art thou a messenger, or come of pleasure?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: A messenger from Henry, our dread liege,
To know the reason of these arms in peace;
Or why thou, being a subject as I am,
Against thy oath and true allegiance sworn,
Should raise so great a power without his leave,
Or dare to bring thy force so near the court.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Scarce can I speak, my choler is so great:
O, I could hew up rocks and fight with flint,
I am so angry at these abject terms;
And now, like Ajax Telamonius,
On sheep or oxen could I spend my fury.
I am far better born than is the king,
More like a king, more kingly in my thoughts:
But I must make fair weather yet a while,
Till Henry be more weak and I more strong,--
Buckingham, I prithee, pardon me,
That I have given no answer all this while;
My mind was troubled with deep melancholy.
The cause why I have brought this army hither
Is to remove proud Somerset from the king,
Seditious to his grace and to the state.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: That is too much presumption on thy part:
But if thy arms be to no other end,
The king hath yielded unto thy demand:
The Duke of Somerset is in the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Upon thine honour, is he prisoner?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Upon mine honour, he is prisoner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Then, Buckingham, I do dismiss my powers.
Soldiers, I thank you all; disperse yourselves;
Meet me to-morrow in St. George's field,
You shall have pay and every thing you wish.
And let my sovereign, virtuous Henry,
Command my eldest son, nay, all my sons,
As pledges of my fealty and love;
I'll send them all as willing as I live:
Lands, goods, horse, armour, any thing I have,
Is his to use, so Somerset may die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: York, I commend this kind submission:
We twain will go into his highness' tent.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter KING HENRY VI and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Buckingham, doth York intend no harm to us,
That thus he marcheth with thee arm in arm?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: In all submission and humility
York doth present himself unto your highness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Then what intends these forces thou dost bring?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: To heave the traitor Somerset from hence,
And fight against that monstrous rebel Cade,
Who since I heard to be discomfited.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: If one so rude and of so mean condition
May pass into the presence of a king,
Lo, I present your grace a traitor's head,
The head of Cade, whom I in combat slew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: The head of Cade! Great God, how just art Thou!
O, let me view his visage, being dead,
That living wrought me such exceeding trouble.
Tell me, my friend, art thou the man that slew him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: I was, an't like your majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: How art thou call'd? and what is thy degree?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: Alexander Iden, that's my name;
A poor esquire of Kent, that loves his king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: So please it you, my lord, 'twere not amiss
He were created knight for his good service.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Iden, kneel down.
Rise up a knight.
We give thee for reward a thousand marks,
And will that thou henceforth attend on us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IDEN
SPEECH.LINE: May Iden live to merit such a bounty.
And never live but true unto his liege!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: See, Buckingham, Somerset comes with the queen:
Go, bid her hide him quickly from the duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: For thousand Yorks he shall not hide his head,
But boldly stand and front him to his face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: How now! is Somerset at liberty?
Then, York, unloose thy long-imprison'd thoughts,
And let thy tongue be equal with thy heart.
Shall I endure the sight of Somerset?
False king! why hast thou broken faith with me,
Knowing how hardly I can brook abuse?
King did I call thee? no, thou art not king,
Not fit to govern and rule multitudes,
Which darest not, no, nor canst not rule a traitor.
That head of thine doth not become a crown;
Thy hand is made to grasp a palmer's staff,
And not to grace an awful princely sceptre.
That gold must round engirt these brows of mine,
Whose smile and frown, like to Achilles' spear,
Is able with the change to kill and cure.
Here is a hand to hold a sceptre up
And with the same to act controlling laws.
Give place: by heaven, thou shalt rule no more
O'er him whom heaven created for thy ruler.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: O monstrous traitor! I arrest thee, York,
Of capital treason 'gainst the king and crown;
Obey, audacious traitor; kneel for grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Wouldst have me kneel? first let me ask of these,
If they can brook I bow a knee to man.
Sirrah, call in my sons to be my bail;
I know, ere they will have me go to ward,
They'll pawn their swords for my enfranchisement.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Call hither Clifford! bid him come amain,
To say if that the bastard boys of York
Shall be the surety for their traitor father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: O blood-besotted Neapolitan,
Outcast of Naples, England's bloody scourge!
The sons of York, thy betters in their birth,
Shall be their father's bail; and bane to those
That for my surety will refuse the boys!
See where they come: I'll warrant they'll
make it good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: And here comes Clifford to deny their bail.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Health and all happiness to my lord the king!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, Clifford: say, what news with thee?
Nay, do not fright us with an angry look;
We are thy sovereign, Clifford, kneel again;
For thy mistaking so, we pardon thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: This is my king, York, I do not mistake;
But thou mistakest me much to think I do:
To Bedlam with him! is the man grown mad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Clifford; a bedlam and ambitious humour
Makes him oppose himself against his king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: He is a traitor; let him to the Tower,
And chop away that factious pate of his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: He is arrested, but will not obey;
His sons, he says, shall give their words for him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Will you not, sons?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, noble father, if our words will serve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: And if words will not, then our weapons shall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what a brood of traitors have we here!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Look in a glass, and call thy image so:
I am thy king, and thou a false-heart traitor.
Call hither to the stake my two brave bears,
That with the very shaking of their chains
They may astonish these fell-lurking curs:
Bid Salisbury and Warwick come to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Are these thy bears? we'll bait thy bears to death.
And manacle the bear-ward in their chains,
If thou darest bring them to the baiting place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Oft have I seen a hot o'erweening cur
Run back and bite, because he was withheld;
Who, being suffer'd with the bear's fell paw,
Hath clapp'd his tail between his legs and cried:
And such a piece of service will you do,
If you oppose yourselves to match Lord Warwick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Hence, heap of wrath, foul indigested lump,
As crooked in thy manners as thy shape!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, we shall heat you thoroughly anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Take heed, lest by your heat you burn yourselves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Why, Warwick, hath thy knee forgot to bow?
Old Salisbury, shame to thy silver hair,
Thou mad misleader of thy brain-sick son!
What, wilt thou on thy death-bed play the ruffian,
And seek for sorrow with thy spectacles?
O, where is faith? O, where is loyalty?
If it be banish'd from the frosty head,
Where shall it find a harbour in the earth?
Wilt thou go dig a grave to find out war,
And shame thine honourable age with blood?
Why art thou old, and want'st experience?
Or wherefore dost abuse it, if thou hast it?
For shame! in duty bend thy knee to me
That bows unto the grave with mickle age.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALISBURY
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I have consider'd with myself
The title of this most renowned duke;
And in my conscience do repute his grace
The rightful heir to England's royal seat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Hast thou not sworn allegiance unto me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALISBURY
SPEECH.LINE: I have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Canst thou dispense with heaven for such an oath?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALISBURY
SPEECH.LINE: It is great sin to swear unto a sin,
But greater sin to keep a sinful oath.
Who can be bound by any solemn vow
To do a murderous deed, to rob a man,
To force a spotless virgin's chastity,
To reave the orphan of his patrimony,
To wring the widow from her custom'd right,
And have no other reason for this wrong
But that he was bound by a solemn oath?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: A subtle traitor needs no sophister.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Call Buckingham, and bid him arm himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Call Buckingham, and all the friends thou hast,
I am resolved for death or dignity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: The first I warrant thee, if dreams prove true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: You were best to go to bed and dream again,
To keep thee from the tempest of the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: I am resolved to bear a greater storm
Than any thou canst conjure up to-day;
And that I'll write upon thy burgonet,
Might I but know thee by thy household badge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my father's badge, old Nevil's crest,
The rampant bear chain'd to the ragged staff,
This day I'll wear aloft my burgonet,
As on a mountain top the cedar shows
That keeps his leaves in spite of any storm,
Even to affright thee with the view thereof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: And from thy burgonet I'll rend thy bear
And tread it under foot with all contempt,
Despite the bear-ward that protects the bear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YOUNG CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: And so to arms, victorious father,
To quell the rebels and their complices.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Fie! charity, for shame! speak not in spite,
For you shall sup with Jesu Christ to-night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YOUNG CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Foul stigmatic, that's more than thou canst tell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: If not in heaven, you'll surely sup in hell.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Saint Alban's.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarums to the battle. Enter WARWICK

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Clifford of Cumberland, 'tis Warwick calls:
And if thou dost not hide thee from the bear,
Now, when the angry trumpet sounds alarum
And dead men's cries do fill the empty air,
Clifford, I say, come forth and fight with me:
Proud northern lord, Clifford of Cumberland,
Warwick is hoarse with calling thee to arms.
How now, my noble lord? what, all afoot?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: The deadly-handed Clifford slew my steed,
But match to match I have encounter'd him
And made a prey for carrion kites and crows
Even of the bonny beast he loved so well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Of one or both of us the time is come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, Warwick, seek thee out some other chase,
For I myself must hunt this deer to death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Then, nobly, York; 'tis for a crown thou fight'st.
As I intend, Clifford, to thrive to-day,
It grieves my soul to leave thee unassail'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: What seest thou in me, York? why dost thou pause?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: With thy brave bearing should I be in love,
But that thou art so fast mine enemy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nor should thy prowess want praise and esteem,
But that 'tis shown ignobly and in treason.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: So let it help me now against thy sword
As I in justice and true right express it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: My soul and body on the action both!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: A dreadful lay! Address thee instantly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: La fin couronne les oeuvres.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Thus war hath given thee peace, for thou art still.
Peace with his soul, heaven, if it be thy will!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YOUNG CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Shame and confusion! all is on the rout;
Fear frames disorder, and disorder wounds
Where it should guard. O war, thou son of hell,
Whom angry heavens do make their minister
Throw in the frozen bosoms of our part
Hot coals of vengeance! Let no soldier fly.
He that is truly dedicate to war
Hath no self-love, nor he that loves himself
Hath not essentially but by circumstance
The name of valour.
O, let the vile world end,
And the premised flames of the last day
Knit earth and heaven together!
Now let the general trumpet blow his blast,
Particularities and petty sounds
To cease! Wast thou ordain'd, dear father,
To lose thy youth in peace, and to achieve
The silver livery of advised age,
And, in thy reverence and thy chair-days, thus
To die in ruffian battle? Even at this sight
My heart is turn'd to stone: and while 'tis mine,
It shall be stony. York not our old men spares;
No more will I their babes: tears virginal
Shall be to me even as the dew to fire,
And beauty that the tyrant oft reclaims
Shall to my flaming wrath be oil and flax.
Henceforth I will not have to do with pity:
Meet I an infant of the house of York,
Into as many gobbets will I cut it
As wild Medea young Absyrtus did:
In cruelty will I seek out my fame.
Come, thou new ruin of old Clifford's house:
As did AEneas old Anchises bear,
So bear I thee upon my manly shoulders;
But then AEneas bare a living load,
Nothing so heavy as these woes of mine.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter RICHARD and SOMERSET to fight. SOMERSET is killed

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: So, lie thou there;
For underneath an alehouse' paltry sign,
The Castle in Saint Alban's, Somerset
Hath made the wizard famous in his death.
Sword, hold thy temper; heart, be wrathful still:
Priests pray for enemies, but princes kill.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Fight: excursions. Enter KING HENRY VI, QUEEN MARGARET, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Away, my lord! you are slow; for shame, away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Can we outrun the heavens? good Margaret, stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: What are you made of? you'll nor fight nor fly:
Now is it manhood, wisdom and defence,
To give the enemy way, and to secure us
By what we can, which can no more but fly.
If you be ta'en, we then should see the bottom
Of all our fortunes: but if we haply scape,
As well we may, if not through your neglect,
We shall to London get, where you are loved
And where this breach now in our fortunes made
May readily be stopp'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YOUNG CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: But that my heart's on future mischief set,
I would speak blasphemy ere bid you fly:
But fly you must; uncurable discomfit
Reigns in the hearts of all our present parts.
Away, for your relief! and we will live
To see their day and them our fortune give:
Away, my lord, away!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Fields near St. Alban's.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum. Retreat. Enter YORK, RICHARD, WARWICK, and Soldiers, with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Of Salisbury, who can report of him,
That winter lion, who in rage forgets
Aged contusions and all brush of time,
And, like a gallant in the brow of youth,
Repairs him with occasion? This happy day
Is not itself, nor have we won one foot,
If Salisbury be lost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: My noble father,
Three times to-day I holp him to his horse,
Three times bestrid him; thrice I led him off,
Persuaded him from any further act:
But still, where danger was, still there I met him;
And like rich hangings in a homely house,
So was his will in his old feeble body.
But, noble as he is, look where he comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALISBURY
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my sword, well hast thou fought to-day;
By the mass, so did we all. I thank you, Richard:
God knows how long it is I have to live;
And it hath pleased him that three times to-day
You have defended me from imminent death.
Well, lords, we have not got that which we have:
'Tis not enough our foes are this time fled,
Being opposites of such repairing nature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I know our safety is to follow them;
For, as I hear, the king is fled to London,
To call a present court of parliament.
Let us pursue him ere the writs go forth.
What says Lord Warwick? shall we after them?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: After them! nay, before them, if we can.
Now, by my faith, lords, 'twas a glorious day:
Saint Alban's battle won by famous York
Shall be eternized in all age to come.
Sound drums and trumpets, and to London all:
And more such days as these to us befall!

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: EDWARD, PRINCE OF WALES, his son.
KING LEWIS XI, King of France.

PGROUP.PERSONA: EDWARD, Earl of March, afterwards King Edward IV.

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: uncles to the Duke of York.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: HENRY, Earl of Richmond, a youth.
LORD RIVERS, brother to Lady Grey.
A Son that has killed his father.
A Father that has killed his son.
LADY GREY, afterwards Queen to Edward IV.
BONA, sister to the French Queen.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. London. The Parliament-house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum. Enter YORK, EDWARD, RICHARD, NORFOLK, MONTAGUE, WARWICK, and Soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder how the king escaped our hands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: While we pursued the horsemen of the north,
He slily stole away and left his men:
Whereat the great Lord of Northumberland,
Whose warlike ears could never brook retreat,
Cheer'd up the drooping army; and himself,
Lord Clifford and Lord Stafford, all abreast,
Charged our main battle's front, and breaking in
Were by the swords of common soldiers slain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Stafford's father, Duke of Buckingham,
Is either slain or wounded dangerously;
I cleft his beaver with a downright blow:
That this is true, father, behold his blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: And, brother, here's the Earl of Wiltshire's blood,
Whom I encounter'd as the battles join'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Speak thou for me and tell them what I did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Richard hath best deserved of all my sons.
But is your grace dead, my Lord of Somerset?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Such hope have all the line of John of Gaunt!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Thus do I hope to shake King Henry's head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: And so do I. Victorious Prince of York,
Before I see thee seated in that throne
Which now the house of Lancaster usurps,
I vow by heaven these eyes shall never close.
This is the palace of the fearful king,
And this the regal seat: possess it, York;
For this is thine and not King Henry's heirs'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Assist me, then, sweet Warwick, and I will;
For hither we have broken in by force.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: We'll all assist you; he that flies shall die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Thanks, gentle Norfolk: stay by me, my lords;
And, soldiers, stay and lodge by me this night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: And when the king comes, offer no violence,
Unless he seek to thrust you out perforce.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: The queen this day here holds her parliament,
But little thinks we shall be of her council:
By words or blows here let us win our right.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Arm'd as we are, let's stay within this house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: The bloody parliament shall this be call'd,
Unless Plantagenet, Duke of York, be king,
And bashful Henry deposed, whose cowardice
Hath made us by-words to our enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Then leave me not, my lords; be resolute;
I mean to take possession of my right.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Neither the king, nor he that loves him best,
The proudest he that holds up Lancaster,
Dares stir a wing, if Warwick shake his bells.
I'll plant Plantagenet, root him up who dares:
Resolve thee, Richard; claim the English crown.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING HENRY VI, CLIFFORD, NORTHUMBERLAND, WESTMORELAND, EXETER, and the rest

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: My lords, look where the sturdy rebel sits,
Even in the chair of state: belike he means,
Back'd by the power of Warwick, that false peer,
To aspire unto the crown and reign as king.
Earl of Northumberland, he slew thy father.
And thine, Lord Clifford; and you both have vow'd revenge
On him, his sons, his favourites and his friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: If I be not, heavens be revenged on me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: The hope thereof makes Clifford mourn in steel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall we suffer this? let's pluck him down:
My heart for anger burns; I cannot brook it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Be patient, gentle Earl of Westmoreland.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Patience is for poltroons, such as he:
He durst not sit there, had your father lived.
My gracious lord, here in the parliament
Let us assail the family of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Well hast thou spoken, cousin: be it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, know you not the city favours them,
And they have troops of soldiers at their beck?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: But when the duke is slain, they'll quickly fly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Far be the thought of this from Henry's heart,
To make a shambles of the parliament-house!
Cousin of Exeter, frowns, words and threats
Shall be the war that Henry means to use.
Thou factious Duke of York, descend my throne,
and kneel for grace and mercy at my feet;
I am thy sovereign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I am thine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: For shame, come down: he made thee Duke of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas my inheritance, as the earldom was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: Thy father was a traitor to the crown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Exeter, thou art a traitor to the crown
In following this usurping Henry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Whom should he follow but his natural king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: True, Clifford; and that's Richard Duke of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: And shall I stand, and thou sit in my throne?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: It must and shall be so: content thyself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Be Duke of Lancaster; let him be king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: He is both king and Duke of Lancaster;
And that the Lord of Westmoreland shall maintain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: And Warwick shall disprove it. You forget
That we are those which chased you from the field
And slew your fathers, and with colours spread
March'd through the city to the palace gates.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, Warwick, I remember it to my grief;
And, by his soul, thou and thy house shall rue it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Plantagenet, of thee and these thy sons,
Thy kinsman and thy friends, I'll have more lives
Than drops of blood were in my father's veins.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Urge it no more; lest that, instead of words,
I send thee, Warwick, such a messenger
As shall revenge his death before I stir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Poor Clifford! how I scorn his worthless threats!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Will you we show our title to the crown?
If not, our swords shall plead it in the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: What title hast thou, traitor, to the crown?
Thy father was, as thou art, Duke of York;
Thy grandfather, Roger Mortimer, Earl of March:
I am the son of Henry the Fifth,
Who made the Dauphin and the French to stoop
And seized upon their towns and provinces.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Talk not of France, sith thou hast lost it all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: The lord protector lost it, and not I:
When I was crown'd I was but nine months old.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: You are old enough now, and yet, methinks, you lose.
Father, tear the crown from the usurper's head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet father, do so; set it on your head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Good brother, as thou lovest and honourest arms,
Let's fight it out and not stand cavilling thus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Sound drums and trumpets, and the king will fly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Sons, peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, thou! and give King Henry leave to speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Plantagenet shall speak first: hear him, lords;
And be you silent and attentive too,
For he that interrupts him shall not live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Think'st thou that I will leave my kingly throne,
Wherein my grandsire and my father sat?
No: first shall war unpeople this my realm;
Ay, and their colours, often borne in France,
And now in England to our heart's great sorrow,
Shall be my winding-sheet. Why faint you, lords?
My title's good, and better far than his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Prove it, Henry, and thou shalt be king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Henry the Fourth by conquest got the crown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas by rebellion against his king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I know not what to say; my title's weak.--
Tell me, may not a king adopt an heir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: An if he may, then am I lawful king;
For Richard, in the view of many lords,
Resign'd the crown to Henry the Fourth,
Whose heir my father was, and I am his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: He rose against him, being his sovereign,
And made him to resign his crown perforce.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Suppose, my lords, he did it unconstrain'd,
Think you 'twere prejudicial to his crown?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: No; for he could not so resign his crown
But that the next heir should succeed and reign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou against us, Duke of Exeter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: His is the right, and therefore pardon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Why whisper you, my lords, and answer not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: My conscience tells me he is lawful king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Aside All will revolt from me, and turn to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Plantagenet, for all the claim thou lay'st,
Think not that Henry shall be so deposed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Deposed he shall be, in despite of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art deceived: 'tis not thy southern power,
Of Essex, Norfolk, Suffolk, nor of Kent,
Which makes thee thus presumptuous and proud,
Can set the duke up in despite of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: King Henry, be thy title right or wrong,
Lord Clifford vows to fight in thy defence:
May that ground gape and swallow me alive,
Where I shall kneel to him that slew my father!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: O Clifford, how thy words revive my heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Henry of Lancaster, resign thy crown.
What mutter you, or what conspire you, lords?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Do right unto this princely Duke of York,
Or I will fill the house with armed men,
And over the chair of state, where now he sits,
Write up his title with usurping blood.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: He stamps with his foot and the soldiers show themselves

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord of Warwick, hear me but one word:
Let me for this my life-time reign as king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Confirm the crown to me and to mine heirs,
And thou shalt reign in quiet while thou livest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: I am content: Richard Plantagenet,
Enjoy the kingdom after my decease.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: What wrong is this unto the prince your son!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: What good is this to England and himself!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Base, fearful and despairing Henry!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: How hast thou injured both thyself and us!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot stay to hear these articles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Come, cousin, let us tell the queen these news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WESTMORELAND
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, faint-hearted and degenerate king,
In whose cold blood no spark of honour bides.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Be thou a prey unto the house of York,
And die in bands for this unmanly deed!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: In dreadful war mayst thou be overcome,
Or live in peace abandon'd and despised!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Turn this way, Henry, and regard them not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: They seek revenge and therefore will not yield.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Exeter!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Why should you sigh, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Not for myself, Lord Warwick, but my son,
Whom I unnaturally shall disinherit.
But be it as it may: I here entail
The crown to thee and to thine heirs for ever;
Conditionally, that here thou take an oath
To cease this civil war, and, whilst I live,
To honour me as thy king and sovereign,
And neither by treason nor hostility
To seek to put me down and reign thyself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: This oath I willingly take and will perform.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Long live King Henry! Plantagenet embrace him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: And long live thou and these thy forward sons!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Now York and Lancaster are reconciled.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: Accursed be he that seeks to make them foes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, my gracious lord; I'll to my castle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: And I'll keep London with my soldiers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: And I to Norfolk with my followers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: And I unto the sea from whence I came.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt YORK, EDWARD, EDMUND, GEORGE, RICHARD, WARWICK, NORFOLK, MONTAGUE, their Soldiers, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: And I, with grief and sorrow, to the court.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter QUEEN MARGARET and PRINCE EDWARD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the queen, whose looks bewray her anger:
I'll steal away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Exeter, so will I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, go not from me; I will follow thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Be patient, gentle queen, and I will stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Who can be patient in such extremes?
Ah, wretched man! would I had died a maid
And never seen thee, never borne thee son,
Seeing thou hast proved so unnatural a father
Hath he deserved to lose his birthright thus?
Hadst thou but loved him half so well as I,
Or felt that pain which I did for him once,
Or nourish'd him as I did with my blood,
Thou wouldst have left thy dearest heart-blood there,
Rather than have that savage duke thine heir
And disinherited thine only son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Father, you cannot disinherit me:
If you be king, why should not I succeed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, Margaret; pardon me, sweet son:
The Earl of Warwick and the duke enforced me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Enforced thee! art thou king, and wilt be forced?
I shame to hear thee speak. Ah, timorous wretch!
Thou hast undone thyself, thy son and me;
And given unto the house of York such head
As thou shalt reign but by their sufferance.
To entail him and his heirs unto the crown,
What is it, but to make thy sepulchre
And creep into it far before thy time?
Warwick is chancellor and the lord of Calais;
Stern Falconbridge commands the narrow seas;
The duke is made protector of the realm;
And yet shalt thou be safe? such safety finds
The trembling lamb environed with wolves.
Had I been there, which am a silly woman,
The soldiers should have toss'd me on their pikes
Before I would have granted to that act.
But thou preferr'st thy life before thine honour:
And seeing thou dost, I here divorce myself
Both from thy table, Henry, and thy bed,
Until that act of parliament be repeal'd
Whereby my son is disinherited.
The northern lords that have forsworn thy colours
Will follow mine, if once they see them spread;
And spread they shall be, to thy foul disgrace
And utter ruin of the house of York.
Thus do I leave thee. Come, son, let's away;
Our army is ready; come, we'll after them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, gentle Margaret, and hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast spoke too much already: get thee gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Gentle son Edward, thou wilt stay with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, to be murder'd by his enemies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: When I return with victory from the field
I'll see your grace: till then I'll follow her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Come, son, away; we may not linger thus.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt QUEEN MARGARET and PRINCE EDWARD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Poor queen! how love to me and to her son
Hath made her break out into terms of rage!
Revenged may she be on that hateful duke,
Whose haughty spirit, winged with desire,
Will cost my crown, and like an empty eagle
Tire on the flesh of me and of my son!
The loss of those three lords torments my heart:
I'll write unto them and entreat them fair.
Come, cousin you shall be the messenger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: And I, I hope, shall reconcile them all.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Sandal Castle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Brother, though I be youngest, give me leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: No, I can better play the orator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: But I have reasons strong and forcible.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, sons and brother! at a strife?
What is your quarrel? how began it first?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: No quarrel, but a slight contention.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: About what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: About that which concerns your grace and us;
The crown of England, father, which is yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Mine boy? not till King Henry be dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Your right depends not on his life or death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Now you are heir, therefore enjoy it now:
By giving the house of Lancaster leave to breathe,
It will outrun you, father, in the end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I took an oath that he should quietly reign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: But for a kingdom any oath may be broken:
I would break a thousand oaths to reign one year.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: No; God forbid your grace should be forsworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I shall be, if I claim by open war.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: I'll prove the contrary, if you'll hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou canst not, son; it is impossible.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: An oath is of no moment, being not took
Before a true and lawful magistrate,
That hath authority over him that swears:
Henry had none, but did usurp the place;
Then, seeing 'twas he that made you to depose,
Your oath, my lord, is vain and frivolous.
Therefore, to arms! And, father, do but think
How sweet a thing it is to wear a crown;
Within whose circuit is Elysium
And all that poets feign of bliss and joy.
Why do we finger thus? I cannot rest
Until the white rose that I wear be dyed
Even in the lukewarm blood of Henry's heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Richard, enough; I will be king, or die.
Brother, thou shalt to London presently,
And whet on Warwick to this enterprise.
Thou, Richard, shalt to the Duke of Norfolk,
And tell him privily of our intent.
You Edward, shall unto my Lord Cobham,
With whom the Kentishmen will willingly rise:
In them I trust; for they are soldiers,
Witty, courteous, liberal, full of spirit.
While you are thus employ'd, what resteth more,
But that I seek occasion how to rise,
And yet the king not privy to my drift,
Nor any of the house of Lancaster?
But, stay: what news? Why comest thou in such post?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: The queen with all the northern earls and lords
Intend here to besiege you in your castle:
She is hard by with twenty thousand men;
And therefore fortify your hold, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, with my sword. What! think'st thou that we fear them?
Edward and Richard, you shall stay with me;
My brother Montague shall post to London:
Let noble Warwick, Cobham, and the rest,
Whom we have left protectors of the king,
With powerful policy strengthen themselves,
And trust not simple Henry nor his oaths.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Brother, I go; I'll win them, fear it not:
And thus most humbly I do take my leave.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter JOHN MORTIMER and HUGH MORTIMER
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John and Sir Hugh Mortimer, mine uncles,
You are come to Sandal in a happy hour;
The army of the queen mean to besiege us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JOHN MORTIMER
SPEECH.LINE: She shall not need; we'll meet her in the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What, with five thousand men?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, with five hundred, father, for a need:
A woman's general; what should we fear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I hear their drums: let's set our men in order,
And issue forth and bid them battle straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Five men to twenty! though the odds be great,
I doubt not, uncle, of our victory.
Many a battle have I won in France,
When as the enemy hath been ten to one:
Why should I not now have the like success?
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Field of battle betwixt Sandal Castle and Wakefield.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarums. Enter RUTLAND and his Tutor

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, whither shall I fly to 'scape their hands?
Ah, tutor, look where bloody Clifford comes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Chaplain, away! thy priesthood saves thy life.
As for the brat of this accursed duke,
Whose father slew my father, he shall die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tutor
SPEECH.LINE: And I, my lord, will bear him company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Soldiers, away with him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tutor
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Clifford, murder not this innocent child,
Lest thou be hated both of God and man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: How now! is he dead already? or is it fear
That makes him close his eyes? I'll open them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: So looks the pent-up lion o'er the wretch
That trembles under his devouring paws;
And so he walks, insulting o'er his prey,
And so he comes, to rend his limbs asunder.
Ah, gentle Clifford, kill me with thy sword,
And not with such a cruel threatening look.
Sweet Clifford, hear me speak before I die.
I am too mean a subject for thy wrath:
Be thou revenged on men, and let me live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: In vain thou speak'st, poor boy; my father's blood
Hath stopp'd the passage where thy words should enter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Then let my father's blood open it again:
He is a man, and, Clifford, cope with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Had thy brethren here, their lives and thine
Were not revenge sufficient for me;
No, if I digg'd up thy forefathers' graves
And hung their rotten coffins up in chains,
It could not slake mine ire, nor ease my heart.
The sight of any of the house of York
Is as a fury to torment my soul;
And till I root out their accursed line
And leave not one alive, I live in hell.
Therefore--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: O, let me pray before I take my death!
To thee I pray; sweet Clifford, pity me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Such pity as my rapier's point affords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: I never did thee harm: why wilt thou slay me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Thy father hath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: But 'twas ere I was born.
Thou hast one son; for his sake pity me,
Lest in revenge thereof, sith God is just,
He be as miserably slain as I.
Ah, let me live in prison all my days;
And when I give occasion of offence,
Then let me die, for now thou hast no cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: No cause!
Thy father slew my father; therefore, die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RUTLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Di faciant laudis summa sit ista tuae!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Plantagenet! I come, Plantagenet!
And this thy son's blood cleaving to my blade
Shall rust upon my weapon, till thy blood,
Congeal'd with this, do make me wipe off both.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Another part of the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: The army of the queen hath got the field:
My uncles both are slain in rescuing me;
And all my followers to the eager foe
Turn back and fly, like ships before the wind
Or lambs pursued by hunger-starved wolves.
My sons, God knows what hath bechanced them:
But this I know, they have demean'd themselves
Like men born to renown by life or death.
Three times did Richard make a lane to me.
And thrice cried 'Courage, father! fight it out!'
And full as oft came Edward to my side,
With purple falchion, painted to the hilt
In blood of those that had encounter'd him:
And when the hardiest warriors did retire,
Richard cried 'Charge! and give no foot of ground!'
And cried 'A crown, or else a glorious tomb!
A sceptre, or an earthly sepulchre!'
With this, we charged again: but, out, alas!
We bodged again; as I have seen a swan
With bootless labour swim against the tide
And spend her strength with over-matching waves.
Ah, hark! the fatal followers do pursue;
And I am faint and cannot fly their fury:
And were I strong, I would not shun their fury:
The sands are number'd that make up my life;
Here must I stay, and here my life must end.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter QUEEN MARGARET, CLIFFORD, NORTHUMBERLAND, PRINCE EDWARD, and Soldiers
SPEECH.LINE: Come, bloody Clifford, rough Northumberland,
I dare your quenchless fury to more rage:
I am your butt, and I abide your shot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Yield to our mercy, proud Plantagenet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, to such mercy as his ruthless arm,
With downright payment, show'd unto my father.
Now Phaethon hath tumbled from his car,
And made an evening at the noontide prick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: My ashes, as the phoenix, may bring forth
A bird that will revenge upon you all:
And in that hope I throw mine eyes to heaven,
Scorning whate'er you can afflict me with.
Why come you not? what! multitudes, and fear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: So cowards fight when they can fly no further;
So doves do peck the falcon's piercing talons;
So desperate thieves, all hopeless of their lives,
Breathe out invectives 'gainst the officers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: O Clifford, but bethink thee once again,
And in thy thought o'er-run my former time;
And, if though canst for blushing, view this face,
And bite thy tongue, that slanders him with cowardice
Whose frown hath made thee faint and fly ere this!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: I will not bandy with thee word for word,
But buckle with thee blows, twice two for one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, valiant Clifford! for a thousand causes
I would prolong awhile the traitor's life.
Wrath makes him deaf: speak thou, Northumberland.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, Clifford! do not honour him so much
To prick thy finger, though to wound his heart:
What valour were it, when a cur doth grin,
For one to thrust his hand between his teeth,
When he might spurn him with his foot away?
It is war's prize to take all vantages;
And ten to one is no impeach of valour.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: They lay hands on YORK, who struggles

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay, so strives the woodcock with the gin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: So doth the cony struggle in the net.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: So triumph thieves upon their conquer'd booty;
So true men yield, with robbers so o'ermatch'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: What would your grace have done unto him now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Brave warriors, Clifford and Northumberland,
Come, make him stand upon this molehill here,
That raught at mountains with outstretched arms,
Yet parted but the shadow with his hand.
What! was it you that would be England's king?
Was't you that revell'd in our parliament,
And made a preachment of your high descent?
Where are your mess of sons to back you now?
The wanton Edward, and the lusty George?
And where's that valiant crook-back prodigy,
Dicky your boy, that with his grumbling voice
Was wont to cheer his dad in mutinies?
Or, with the rest, where is your darling Rutland?
Look, York: I stain'd this napkin with the blood
That valiant Clifford, with his rapier's point,
Made issue from the bosom of the boy;
And if thine eyes can water for his death,
I give thee this to dry thy cheeks withal.
Alas poor York! but that I hate thee deadly,
I should lament thy miserable state.
I prithee, grieve, to make me merry, York.
What, hath thy fiery heart so parch'd thine entrails
That not a tear can fall for Rutland's death?
Why art thou patient, man? thou shouldst be mad;
And I, to make thee mad, do mock thee thus.
Stamp, rave, and fret, that I may sing and dance.
Thou wouldst be fee'd, I see, to make me sport:
York cannot speak, unless he wear a crown.
A crown for York! and, lords, bow low to him:
Hold you his hands, whilst I do set it on.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Putting a paper crown on his head
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry, sir, now looks he like a king!
Ay, this is he that took King Henry's chair,
And this is he was his adopted heir.
But how is it that great Plantagenet
Is crown'd so soon, and broke his solemn oath?
As I bethink me, you should not be king
Till our King Henry had shook hands with death.
And will you pale your head in Henry's glory,
And rob his temples of the diadem,
Now in his life, against your holy oath?
O, 'tis a fault too too unpardonable!
Off with the crown, and with the crown his head;
And, whilst we breathe, take time to do him dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: That is my office, for my father's sake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, stay; lets hear the orisons he makes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: She-wolf of France, but worse than wolves of France,
Whose tongue more poisons than the adder's tooth!
How ill-beseeming is it in thy sex
To triumph, like an Amazonian trull,
Upon their woes whom fortune captivates!
But that thy face is, vizard-like, unchanging,
Made impudent with use of evil deeds,
I would assay, proud queen, to make thee blush.
To tell thee whence thou camest, of whom derived,
Were shame enough to shame thee, wert thou not shameless.
Thy father bears the type of King of Naples,
Of both the Sicils and Jerusalem,
Yet not so wealthy as an English yeoman.
Hath that poor monarch taught thee to insult?
It needs not, nor it boots thee not, proud queen,
Unless the adage must be verified,
That beggars mounted run their horse to death.
'Tis beauty that doth oft make women proud;
But, God he knows, thy share thereof is small:
'Tis virtue that doth make them most admired;
The contrary doth make thee wonder'd at:
'Tis government that makes them seem divine;
The want thereof makes thee abominable:
Thou art as opposite to every good
As the Antipodes are unto us,
Or as the south to the septentrion.
O tiger's heart wrapt in a woman's hide!
How couldst thou drain the life-blood of the child,
To bid the father wipe his eyes withal,
And yet be seen to bear a woman's face?
Women are soft, mild, pitiful and flexible;
Thou stern, obdurate, flinty, rough, remorseless.
Bids't thou me rage? why, now thou hast thy wish:
Wouldst have me weep? why, now thou hast thy will:
For raging wind blows up incessant showers,
And when the rage allays, the rain begins.
These tears are my sweet Rutland's obsequies:
And every drop cries vengeance for his death,
'Gainst thee, fell Clifford, and thee, false
Frenchwoman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Beshrew me, but his passion moves me so
That hardly can I cheque my eyes from tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: That face of his the hungry cannibals
Would not have touch'd, would not have stain'd with blood:
But you are more inhuman, more inexorable,
O, ten times more, than tigers of Hyrcania.
See, ruthless queen, a hapless father's tears:
This cloth thou dip'dst in blood of my sweet boy,
And I with tears do wash the blood away.
Keep thou the napkin, and go boast of this:
And if thou tell'st the heavy story right,
Upon my soul, the hearers will shed tears;
Yea even my foes will shed fast-falling tears,
And say 'Alas, it was a piteous deed!'
There, take the crown, and, with the crown, my curse;
And in thy need such comfort come to thee
As now I reap at thy too cruel hand!
Hard-hearted Clifford, take me from the world:
My soul to heaven, my blood upon your heads!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Had he been slaughter-man to all my kin,
I should not for my life but weep with him.
To see how inly sorrow gripes his soul.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: What, weeping-ripe, my Lord Northumberland?
Think but upon the wrong he did us all,
And that will quickly dry thy melting tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Here's for my oath, here's for my father's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: And here's to right our gentle-hearted king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Open Thy gate of mercy, gracious God!
My soul flies through these wounds to seek out Thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Off with his head, and set it on York gates;
So York may overlook the town of York.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A plain near Mortimer's Cross in Herefordshire.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: A march. Enter EDWARD, RICHARD, and their power

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder how our princely father 'scaped,
Or whether he be 'scaped away or no
From Clifford's and Northumberland's pursuit:
Had he been ta'en, we should have heard the news;
Had he been slain, we should have heard the news;
Or had he 'scaped, methinks we should have heard
The happy tidings of his good escape.
How fares my brother? why is he so sad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot joy, until I be resolved
Where our right valiant father is become.
I saw him in the battle range about;
And watch'd him how he singled Clifford forth.
Methought he bore him in the thickest troop
As doth a lion in a herd of neat;
Or as a bear, encompass'd round with dogs,
Who having pinch'd a few and made them cry,
The rest stand all aloof, and bark at him.
So fared our father with his enemies;
So fled his enemies my warlike father:
Methinks, 'tis prize enough to be his son.
See how the morning opes her golden gates,
And takes her farewell of the glorious sun!
How well resembles it the prime of youth,
Trimm'd like a younker prancing to his love!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Dazzle mine eyes, or do I see three suns?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Three glorious suns, each one a perfect sun;
Not separated with the racking clouds,
But sever'd in a pale clear-shining sky.
See, see! they join, embrace, and seem to kiss,
As if they vow'd some league inviolable:
Now are they but one lamp, one light, one sun.
In this the heaven figures some event.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis wondrous strange, the like yet never heard of.
I think it cites us, brother, to the field,
That we, the sons of brave Plantagenet,
Each one already blazing by our meeds,
Should notwithstanding join our lights together
And over-shine the earth as this the world.
Whate'er it bodes, henceforward will I bear
Upon my target three fair-shining suns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, bear three daughters: by your leave I speak it,
You love the breeder better than the male.
But what art thou, whose heavy looks foretell
Some dreadful story hanging on thy tongue?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, one that was a woful looker-on
When as the noble Duke of York was slain,
Your princely father and my loving lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: O, speak no more, for I have heard too much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Say how he died, for I will hear it all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Environed he was with many foes,
And stood against them, as the hope of Troy
Against the Greeks that would have enter'd Troy.
But Hercules himself must yield to odds;
And many strokes, though with a little axe,
Hew down and fell the hardest-timber'd oak.
By many hands your father was subdued;
But only slaughter'd by the ireful arm
Of unrelenting Clifford and the queen,
Who crown'd the gracious duke in high despite,
Laugh'd in his face; and when with grief he wept,
The ruthless queen gave him to dry his cheeks
A napkin steeped in the harmless blood
Of sweet young Rutland, by rough Clifford slain:
And after many scorns, many foul taunts,
They took his head, and on the gates of York
They set the same; and there it doth remain,
The saddest spectacle that e'er I view'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Duke of York, our prop to lean upon,
Now thou art gone, we have no staff, no stay.
O Clifford, boisterous Clifford! thou hast slain
The flower of Europe for his chivalry;
And treacherously hast thou vanquish'd him,
For hand to hand he would have vanquish'd thee.
Now my soul's palace is become a prison:
Ah, would she break from hence, that this my body
Might in the ground be closed up in rest!
For never henceforth shall I joy again,
Never, O never shall I see more joy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot weep; for all my body's moisture
Scarce serves to quench my furnace-burning heart:
Nor can my tongue unload my heart's great burthen;
For selfsame wind that I should speak withal
Is kindling coals that fires all my breast,
And burns me up with flames that tears would quench.
To weep is to make less the depth of grief:
Tears then for babes; blows and revenge for me
Richard, I bear thy name; I'll venge thy death,
Or die renowned by attempting it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: His name that valiant duke hath left with thee;
His dukedom and his chair with me is left.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, if thou be that princely eagle's bird,
Show thy descent by gazing 'gainst the sun:
For chair and dukedom, throne and kingdom say;
Either that is thine, or else thou wert not his.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: March. Enter WARWICK, MONTAGUE, and their army

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: How now, fair lords! What fare? what news abroad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Great Lord of Warwick, if we should recount
Our baleful news, and at each word's deliverance
Stab poniards in our flesh till all were told,
The words would add more anguish than the wounds.
O valiant lord, the Duke of York is slain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: O Warwick, Warwick! that Plantagenet,
Which held three dearly as his soul's redemption,
Is by the stern Lord Clifford done to death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Ten days ago I drown'd these news in tears;
And now, to add more measure to your woes,
I come to tell you things sith then befall'n.
After the bloody fray at Wakefield fought,
Where your brave father breathed his latest gasp,
Tidings, as swiftly as the posts could run,
Were brought me of your loss and his depart.
I, then in London keeper of the king,
Muster'd my soldiers, gather'd flocks of friends,
And very well appointed, as I thought,
March'd toward Saint Alban's to intercept the queen,
Bearing the king in my behalf along;
For by my scouts I was advertised
That she was coming with a full intent
To dash our late decree in parliament
Touching King Henry's oath and your succession.
Short tale to make, we at Saint Alban's met
Our battles join'd, and both sides fiercely fought:
But whether 'twas the coldness of the king,
Who look'd full gently on his warlike queen,
That robb'd my soldiers of their heated spleen;
Or whether 'twas report of her success;
Or more than common fear of Clifford's rigour,
Who thunders to his captives blood and death,
I cannot judge: but to conclude with truth,
Their weapons like to lightning came and went;
Our soldiers', like the night-owl's lazy flight,
Or like an idle thresher with a flail,
Fell gently down, as if they struck their friends.
I cheer'd them up with justice of our cause,
With promise of high pay and great rewards:
But all in vain; they had no heart to fight,
And we in them no hope to win the day;
So that we fled; the king unto the queen;
Lord George your brother, Norfolk and myself,
In haste, post-haste, are come to join with you:
For in the marches here we heard you were,
Making another head to fight again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Where is the Duke of Norfolk, gentle Warwick?
And when came George from Burgundy to England?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Some six miles off the duke is with the soldiers;
And for your brother, he was lately sent
From your kind aunt, Duchess of Burgundy,
With aid of soldiers to this needful war.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas odds, belike, when valiant Warwick fled:
Oft have I heard his praises in pursuit,
But ne'er till now his scandal of retire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Nor now my scandal, Richard, dost thou hear;
For thou shalt know this strong right hand of mine
Can pluck the diadem from faint Henry's head,
And wring the awful sceptre from his fist,
Were he as famous and as bold in war
As he is famed for mildness, peace, and prayer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: I know it well, Lord Warwick; blame me not:
'Tis love I bear thy glories makes me speak.
But in this troublous time what's to be done?
Shall we go throw away our coats of steel,
And wrap our bodies in black mourning gowns,
Numbering our Ave-Maries with our beads?
Or shall we on the helmets of our foes
Tell our devotion with revengeful arms?
If for the last, say ay, and to it, lords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, therefore Warwick came to seek you out;
And therefore comes my brother Montague.
Attend me, lords. The proud insulting queen,
With Clifford and the haught Northumberland,
And of their feather many more proud birds,
Have wrought the easy-melting king like wax.
He swore consent to your succession,
His oath enrolled in the parliament;
And now to London all the crew are gone,
To frustrate both his oath and what beside
May make against the house of Lancaster.
Their power, I think, is thirty thousand strong:
Now, if the help of Norfolk and myself,
With all the friends that thou, brave Earl of March,
Amongst the loving Welshmen canst procure,
Will but amount to five and twenty thousand,
Why, Via! to London will we march amain,
And once again bestride our foaming steeds,
And once again cry 'Charge upon our foes!'
But never once again turn back and fly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, now methinks I hear great Warwick speak:
Ne'er may he live to see a sunshine day,
That cries 'Retire,' if Warwick bid him stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Warwick, on thy shoulder will I lean;
And when thou fail'st--as God forbid the hour!--
Must Edward fall, which peril heaven forfend!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: No longer Earl of March, but Duke of York:
The next degree is England's royal throne;
For King of England shalt thou be proclaim'd
In every borough as we pass along;
And he that throws not up his cap for joy
Shall for the fault make forfeit of his head.
King Edward, valiant Richard, Montague,
Stay we no longer, dreaming of renown,
But sound the trumpets, and about our task.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Then, Clifford, were thy heart as hard as steel,
As thou hast shown it flinty by thy deeds,
I come to pierce it, or to give thee mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Then strike up drums: God and Saint George for us!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: The Duke of Norfolk sends you word by me,
The queen is coming with a puissant host;
And craves your company for speedy counsel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Why then it sorts, brave warriors, let's away.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Before York.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING HENRY VI, QUEEN MARGARET, PRINCE EDWARD, CLIFFORD, and NORTHUMBERLAND, with drum and trumpets

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, my lord, to this brave town of York.
Yonder's the head of that arch-enemy
That sought to be encompass'd with your crown:
Doth not the object cheer your heart, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, as the rocks cheer them that fear their wreck:
To see this sight, it irks my very soul.
Withhold revenge, dear God! 'tis not my fault,
Nor wittingly have I infringed my vow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious liege, this too much lenity
And harmful pity must be laid aside.
To whom do lions cast their gentle looks?
Not to the beast that would usurp their den.
Whose hand is that the forest bear doth lick?
Not his that spoils her young before her face.
Who 'scapes the lurking serpent's mortal sting?
Not he that sets his foot upon her back.
The smallest worm will turn being trodden on,
And doves will peck in safeguard of their brood.
Ambitious York doth level at thy crown,
Thou smiling while he knit his angry brows:
He, but a duke, would have his son a king,
And raise his issue, like a loving sire;
Thou, being a king, blest with a goodly son,
Didst yield consent to disinherit him,
Which argued thee a most unloving father.
Unreasonable creatures feed their young;
And though man's face be fearful to their eyes,
Yet, in protection of their tender ones,
Who hath not seen them, even with those wings
Which sometime they have used with fearful flight,
Make war with him that climb'd unto their nest,
Offer their own lives in their young's defence?
For shame, my liege, make them your precedent!
Were it not pity that this goodly boy
Should lose his birthright by his father's fault,
And long hereafter say unto his child,
'What my great-grandfather and his grandsire got
My careless father fondly gave away'?
Ah, what a shame were this! Look on the boy;
And let his manly face, which promiseth
Successful fortune, steel thy melting heart
To hold thine own and leave thine own with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Full well hath Clifford play'd the orator,
Inferring arguments of mighty force.
But, Clifford, tell me, didst thou never hear
That things ill-got had ever bad success?
And happy always was it for that son
Whose father for his hoarding went to hell?
I'll leave my son my virtuous deeds behind;
And would my father had left me no more!
For all the rest is held at such a rate
As brings a thousand-fold more care to keep
Than in possession and jot of pleasure.
Ah, cousin York! would thy best friends did know
How it doth grieve me that thy head is here!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, cheer up your spirits: our foes are nigh,
And this soft courage makes your followers faint.
You promised knighthood to our forward son:
Unsheathe your sword, and dub him presently.
Edward, kneel down.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Edward Plantagenet, arise a knight;
And learn this lesson, draw thy sword in right.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious father, by your kingly leave,
I'll draw it as apparent to the crown,
And in that quarrel use it to the death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, that is spoken like a toward prince.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Royal commanders, be in readiness:
For with a band of thirty thousand men
Comes Warwick, backing of the Duke of York;
And in the towns, as they do march along,
Proclaims him king, and many fly to him:
Darraign your battle, for they are at hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: I would your highness would depart the field:
The queen hath best success when you are absent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, good my lord, and leave us to our fortune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Why, that's my fortune too; therefore I'll stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: Be it with resolution then to fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: My royal father, cheer these noble lords
And hearten those that fight in your defence:
Unsheathe your sword, good father; cry 'Saint George!'

SCENE.STAGEDIR: March. Enter EDWARD, GEORGE, RICHARD, WARWICK, NORFOLK, MONTAGUE, and Soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Now, perjured Henry! wilt thou kneel for grace,
And set thy diadem upon my head;
Or bide the mortal fortune of the field?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Go, rate thy minions, proud insulting boy!
Becomes it thee to be thus bold in terms
Before thy sovereign and thy lawful king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I am his king, and he should bow his knee;
I was adopted heir by his consent:
Since when, his oath is broke; for, as I hear,
You, that are king, though he do wear the crown,
Have caused him, by new act of parliament,
To blot out me, and put his own son in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: And reason too:
Who should succeed the father but the son?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Are you there, butcher? O, I cannot speak!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, crook-back, here I stand to answer thee,
Or any he the proudest of thy sort.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas you that kill'd young Rutland, was it not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and old York, and yet not satisfied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: For God's sake, lords, give signal to the fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: What say'st thou, Henry, wilt thou yield the crown?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, long-tongued Warwick! dare you speak?
When you and I met at Saint Alban's last,
Your legs did better service than your hands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Then 'twas my turn to fly, and now 'tis thine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: You said so much before, and yet you fled.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas not your valour, Clifford, drove me thence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORTHUMBERLAND
SPEECH.LINE: No, nor your manhood that durst make you stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Northumberland, I hold thee reverently.
Break off the parley; for scarce I can refrain
The execution of my big-swoln heart
Upon that Clifford, that cruel child-killer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: I slew thy father, call'st thou him a child?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, like a dastard and a treacherous coward,
As thou didst kill our tender brother Rutland;
But ere sunset I'll make thee curse the deed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Have done with words, my lords, and hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Defy them then, or else hold close thy lips.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee, give no limits to my tongue:
I am a king, and privileged to speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLIFFORD
SPEECH.LINE: My liege, the wound that bred this meeting here
Cannot be cured by words; therefore be still.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHARD
SPEECH.LINE: Then, executioner, unsheathe thy sword:
By him that made us all, I am resolved
that Clifford's manhood lies upon his tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Say, Henry, shall I have my right, or no?
A thousand men have broke their fasts to-day,
