Till then, 'tis wisdom to conceal our meaning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Away with scrupulous wit! now arms must rule.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: And fearless minds climb soonest unto crowns.
Brother, we will proclaim you out of hand:
The bruit thereof will bring you many friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Then be it as you will; for 'tis my right,
And Henry but usurps the diadem.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, now my sovereign speaketh like himself;
And now will I be Edward's champion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Sound trumpet; Edward shall be here proclaim'd:
Come, fellow-soldier, make thou proclamation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soldier
SPEECH.LINE: Edward the Fourth, by the grace of God, king of
England and France, and lord of Ireland, &c.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: And whosoe'er gainsays King Edward's right,
By this I challenge him to single fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Long live Edward the Fourth!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Thanks, brave Montgomery; and thanks unto you all:
If fortune serve me, I'll requite this kindness.
Now, for this night, let's harbour here in York;
And when the morning sun shall raise his car
Above the border of this horizon,
We'll forward towards Warwick and his mates;
For well I wot that Henry is no soldier.
Ah, froward Clarence! how evil it beseems thee
To flatter Henry and forsake thy brother!
Yet, as we may, we'll meet both thee and Warwick.
Come on, brave soldiers: doubt not of the day,
And, that once gotten, doubt not of large pay.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VIII. London. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING HENRY VI, WARWICK, MONTAGUE, CLARENCE, EXETER, and OXFORD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: What counsel, lords? Edward from Belgia,
With hasty Germans and blunt Hollanders,
Hath pass'd in safety through the narrow seas,
And with his troops doth march amain to London;
And many giddy people flock to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Let's levy men, and beat him back again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: A little fire is quickly trodden out;
Which, being suffer'd, rivers cannot quench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: In Warwickshire I have true-hearted friends,
Not mutinous in peace, yet bold in war;
Those will I muster up: and thou, son Clarence,
Shalt stir up in Suffolk, Norfolk, and in Kent,
The knights and gentlemen to come with thee:
Thou, brother Montague, in Buckingham,
Northampton and in Leicestershire, shalt find
Men well inclined to hear what thou command'st:
And thou, brave Oxford, wondrous well beloved,
In Oxfordshire shalt muster up thy friends.
My sovereign, with the loving citizens,
Like to his island girt in with the ocean,
Or modest Dian circled with her nymphs,
Shall rest in London till we come to him.
Fair lords, take leave and stand not to reply.
Farewell, my sovereign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, my Hector, and my Troy's true hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: In sign of truth, I kiss your highness' hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Well-minded Clarence, be thou fortunate!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Comfort, my lord; and so I take my leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: And thus I seal my truth, and bid adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Oxford, and my loving Montague,
And all at once, once more a happy farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, sweet lords: let's meet at Coventry.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but KING HENRY VI and EXETER

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Here at the palace I will rest awhile.
Cousin of Exeter, what thinks your lordship?
Methinks the power that Edward hath in field
Should not be able to encounter mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: The doubt is that he will seduce the rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: That's not my fear; my meed hath got me fame:
I have not stopp'd mine ears to their demands,
Nor posted off their suits with slow delays;
My pity hath been balm to heal their wounds,
My mildness hath allay'd their swelling griefs,
My mercy dried their water-flowing tears;
I have not been desirous of their wealth,
Nor much oppress'd them with great subsidies.
Nor forward of revenge, though they much err'd:
Then why should they love Edward more than me?
No, Exeter, these graces challenge grace:
And when the lion fawns upon the lamb,
The lamb will never cease to follow him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EXETER
SPEECH.LINE: Hark, hark, my lord! what shouts are these?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter KING EDWARD IV, GLOUCESTER, and soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Seize on the shame-faced Henry, bear him hence;
And once again proclaim us King of England.
You are the fount that makes small brooks to flow:
Now stops thy spring; my sea sha$l suck them dry,
And swell so much the higher by their ebb.
Hence with him to the Tower; let him not speak.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Exeunt some with KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: And, lords, towards Coventry bend we our course
Where peremptory Warwick now remains:
The sun shines hot; and, if we use delay,
Cold biting winter mars our hoped-for hay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Away betimes, before his forces join,
And take the great-grown traitor unawares:
Brave warriors, march amain towards Coventry.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Coventry.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter WARWICK, the Mayor of Coventry, two Messengers, and others upon the walls

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Where is the post that came from valiant Oxford?
How far hence is thy lord, mine honest fellow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: By this at Dunsmore, marching hitherward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: How far off is our brother Montague?
Where is the post that came from Montague?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: By this at Daintry, with a puissant troop.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Say, Somerville, what says my loving son?
And, by thy guess, how nigh is Clarence now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: At Southam I did leave him with his forces,
And do expect him here some two hours hence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Then Clarence is at hand, I hear his drum.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: It is not his, my lord; here Southam lies:
The drum your honour hears marcheth from Warwick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Who should that be? belike, unlook'd-for friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: They are at hand, and you shall quickly know.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: March: flourish. Enter KING EDWARD IV, GLOUCESTER, and soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Go, trumpet, to the walls, and sound a parle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: See how the surly Warwick mans the wall!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: O unbid spite! is sportful Edward come?
Where slept our scouts, or how are they seduced,
That we could hear no news of his repair?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Warwick, wilt thou ope the city gates,
Speak gentle words and humbly bend thy knee,
Call Edward king and at his hands beg mercy?
And he shall pardon thee these outrages.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, rather, wilt thou draw thy forces hence,
Confess who set thee up and pluck'd thee own,
Call Warwick patron and be penitent?
And thou shalt still remain the Duke of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I thought, at least, he would have said the king;
Or did he make the jest against his will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Is not a dukedom, sir, a goodly gift?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, by my faith, for a poor earl to give:
I'll do thee service for so good a gift.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas I that gave the kingdom to thy brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Why then 'tis mine, if but by Warwick's gift.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art no Atlas for so great a weight:
And weakling, Warwick takes his gift again;
And Henry is my king, Warwick his subject.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: But Warwick's king is Edward's prisoner:
And, gallant Warwick, do but answer this:
What is the body when the head is off?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, that Warwick had no more forecast,
But, whiles he thought to steal the single ten,
The king was slily finger'd from the deck!
You left poor Henry at the Bishop's palace,
And, ten to one, you'll meet him in the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis even so; yet you are Warwick still.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Warwick, take the time; kneel down, kneel down:
Nay, when? strike now, or else the iron cools.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: I had rather chop this hand off at a blow,
And with the other fling it at thy face,
Than bear so low a sail, to strike to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Sail how thou canst, have wind and tide thy friend,
This hand, fast wound about thy coal-black hair
Shall, whiles thy head is warm and new cut off,
Write in the dust this sentence with thy blood,
'Wind-changing Warwick now can change no more.'

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter OXFORD, with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: O cheerful colours! see where Oxford comes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Oxford, Oxford, for Lancaster!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: He and his forces enter the city

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: The gates are open, let us enter too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: So other foes may set upon our backs.
Stand we in good array; for they no doubt
Will issue out again and bid us battle:
If not, the city being but of small defence,
We'll quickly rouse the traitors in the same.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: O, welcome, Oxford! for we want thy help.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MONTAGUE with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Montague, Montague, for Lancaster!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: He and his forces enter the city

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Thou and thy brother both shall buy this treason
Even with the dearest blood your bodies bear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: The harder match'd, the greater victory:
My mind presageth happy gain and conquest.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SOMERSET, with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: Somerset, Somerset, for Lancaster!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: He and his forces enter the city

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Two of thy name, both Dukes of Somerset,
Have sold their lives unto the house of York;
And thou shalt be the third if this sword hold.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CLARENCE, with drum and colours

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: And lo, where George of Clarence sweeps along,
Of force enough to bid his brother battle;
With whom an upright zeal to right prevails
More than the nature of a brother's love!
Come, Clarence, come; thou wilt, if Warwick call.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Father of Warwick, know you what this means?
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Taking his red rose out of his hat
SPEECH.LINE: Look here, I throw my infamy at thee
I will not ruinate my father's house,
Who gave his blood to lime the stones together,
And set up Lancaster. Why, trow'st thou, Warwick,
That Clarence is so harsh, so blunt, unnatural,
To bend the fatal instruments of war
Against his brother and his lawful king?
Perhaps thou wilt object my holy oath:
To keep that oath were more impiety
Than Jephthah's, when he sacrificed his daughter.
I am so sorry for my trespass made
That, to deserve well at my brother's hands,
I here proclaim myself thy mortal foe,
With resolution, wheresoe'er I meet thee--
As I will meet thee, if thou stir abroad--
To plague thee for thy foul misleading me.
And so, proud-hearted Warwick, I defy thee,
And to my brother turn my blushing cheeks.
Pardon me, Edward, I will make amends:
And, Richard, do not frown upon my faults,
For I will henceforth be no more unconstant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now welcome more, and ten times more beloved,
Than if thou never hadst deserved our hate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, good Clarence; this is brotherlike.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: O passing traitor, perjured and unjust!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: What, Warwick, wilt thou leave the town and fight?
Or shall we beat the stones about thine ears?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, I am not coop'd here for defence!
I will away towards Barnet presently,
And bid thee battle, Edward, if thou darest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, Warwick, Edward dares, and leads the way.
Lords, to the field; Saint George and victory!
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Exeunt King Edward and his company. March. Warwick and his company follow
SPEECH.LINE: 3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A field of battle near Barnet.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum and excursions. Enter KING EDWARD IV, bringing forth WARWICK wounded

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: So, lie thou there: die thou, and die our fear;
For Warwick was a bug that fear'd us all.
Now, Montague, sit fast; I seek for thee,
That Warwick's bones may keep thine company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, who is nigh? come to me, friend or foe,
And tell me who is victor, York or Warwick?
Why ask I that? my mangled body shows,
My blood, my want of strength, my sick heart shows.
That I must yield my body to the earth
And, by my fall, the conquest to my foe.
Thus yields the cedar to the axe's edge,
Whose arms gave shelter to the princely eagle,
Under whose shade the ramping lion slept,
Whose top-branch overpeer'd Jove's spreading tree
And kept low shrubs from winter's powerful wind.
These eyes, that now are dimm'd with death's black veil,
Have been as piercing as the mid-day sun,
To search the secret treasons of the world:
The wrinkles in my brows, now filled with blood,
Were liken'd oft to kingly sepulchres;
For who lived king, but I could dig his grave?
And who durst mine when Warwick bent his brow?
Lo, now my glory smear'd in dust and blood!
My parks, my walks, my manors that I had.
Even now forsake me, and of all my lands
Is nothing left me but my body's length.
Why, what is pomp, rule, reign, but earth and dust?
And, live we how we can, yet die we must.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Warwick, Warwick! wert thou as we are.
We might recover all our loss again;
The queen from France hath brought a puissant power:
Even now we heard the news: ah, could'st thou fly!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then I would not fly. Ah, Montague,
If thou be there, sweet brother, take my hand.
And with thy lips keep in my soul awhile!
Thou lovest me not; for, brother, if thou didst,
Thy tears would wash this cold congealed blood
That glues my lips and will not let me speak.
Come quickly, Montague, or I am dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Warwick! Montague hath breathed his last;
And to the latest gasp cried out for Warwick,
And said 'Commend me to my valiant brother.'
And more he would have said, and more he spoke,
Which sounded like a clamour in a vault,
That mought not be distinguished; but at last
I well might hear, delivered with a groan,
'O, farewell, Warwick!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WARWICK
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet rest his soul! Fly, lords, and save yourselves;
For Warwick bids you all farewell to meet in heaven.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Away, away, to meet the queen's great power!
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Here they bear away his body. Exeunt
SPEECH.LINE: 3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Another part of the field.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING EDWARD IV in triumph; with GLOUCESTER, CLARENCE, and the rest

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Thus far our fortune keeps an upward course,
And we are graced with wreaths of victory.
But, in the midst of this bright-shining day,
I spy a black, suspicious, threatening cloud,
That will encounter with our glorious sun,
Ere he attain his easeful western bed:
I mean, my lords, those powers that the queen
Hath raised in Gallia have arrived our coast
And, as we hear, march on to fight with us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: A little gale will soon disperse that cloud
And blow it to the source from whence it came:
The very beams will dry those vapours up,
For every cloud engenders not a storm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: The queen is valued thirty thousand strong,
And Somerset, with Oxford fled to her:
If she have time to breathe be well assured
Her faction will be full as strong as ours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: We are advertised by our loving friends
That they do hold their course toward Tewksbury:
We, having now the best at Barnet field,
Will thither straight, for willingness rids way;
And, as we march, our strength will be augmented
In every county as we go along.
Strike up the drum; cry 'Courage!' and away.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Plains near Tewksbury.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: March. Enter QUEEN MARGARET, PRINCE EDWARD, SOMERSET, OXFORD, and soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Great lords, wise men ne'er sit and wail their loss,
But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.
What though the mast be now blown overboard,
The cable broke, the holding-anchor lost,
And half our sailors swallow'd in the flood?
Yet lives our pilot still. Is't meet that he
Should leave the helm and like a fearful lad
With tearful eyes add water to the sea
And give more strength to that which hath too much,
Whiles, in his moan, the ship splits on the rock,
Which industry and courage might have saved?
Ah, what a shame! ah, what a fault were this!
Say Warwick was our anchor; what of that?
And Montague our topmost; what of him?
Our slaughter'd friends the tackles; what of these?
Why, is not Oxford here another anchor?
And Somerset another goodly mast?
The friends of France our shrouds and tacklings?
And, though unskilful, why not Ned and I
For once allow'd the skilful pilot's charge?
We will not from the helm to sit and weep,
But keep our course, though the rough wind say no,
From shelves and rocks that threaten us with wreck.
As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.
And what is Edward but ruthless sea?
What Clarence but a quicksand of deceit?
And Richard but a ragged fatal rock?
All these the enemies to our poor bark.
Say you can swim; alas, 'tis but a while!
Tread on the sand; why, there you quickly sink:
Bestride the rock; the tide will wash you off,
Or else you famish; that's a threefold death.
This speak I, lords, to let you understand,
If case some one of you would fly from us,
That there's no hoped-for mercy with the brothers
More than with ruthless waves, with sands and rocks.
Why, courage then! what cannot be avoided
'Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Methinks a woman of this valiant spirit
Should, if a coward heard her speak these words,
Infuse his breast with magnanimity
And make him, naked, foil a man at arms.
I speak not this as doubting any here
For did I but suspect a fearful man
He should have leave to go away betimes,
Lest in our need he might infect another
And make him of like spirit to himself.
If any such be here--as God forbid!--
Let him depart before we need his help.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Women and children of so high a courage,
And warriors faint! why, 'twere perpetual shame.
O brave young prince! thy famous grandfather
Doth live again in thee: long mayst thou live
To bear his image and renew his glories!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: And he that will not fight for such a hope.
Go home to bed, and like the owl by day,
If he arise, be mock'd and wonder'd at.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Thanks, gentle Somerset; sweet Oxford, thanks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: And take his thanks that yet hath nothing else.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Prepare you, lords, for Edward is at hand.
Ready to fight; therefore be resolute.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: I thought no less: it is his policy
To haste thus fast, to find us unprovided.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: But he's deceived; we are in readiness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: This cheers my heart, to see your forwardness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Here pitch our battle; hence we will not budge.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish and march. Enter KING EDWARD IV, GLOUCESTER, CLARENCE, and soldiers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Brave followers, yonder stands the thorny wood,
Which, by the heavens' assistance and your strength,
Must by the roots be hewn up yet ere night.
I need not add more fuel to your fire,
For well I wot ye blaze to burn them out
Give signal to the fight, and to it, lords!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Lords, knights, and gentlemen, what I should say
My tears gainsay; for every word I speak,
Ye see, I drink the water of mine eyes.
Therefore, no more but this: Henry, your sovereign,
Is prisoner to the foe; his state usurp'd,
His realm a slaughter-house, his subjects slain,
His statutes cancell'd and his treasure spent;
And yonder is the wolf that makes this spoil.
You fight in justice: then, in God's name, lords,
Be valiant and give signal to the fight.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another part of the field.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING EDWARD IV, GLOUCESTER, CLARENCE, and soldiers; with QUEEN MARGARET, OXFORD, and SOMERSET, prisoners

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now here a period of tumultuous broils.
Away with Oxford to Hames Castle straight:
For Somerset, off with his guilty head.
Go, bear them hence; I will not hear them speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OXFORD
SPEECH.LINE: For my part, I'll not trouble thee with words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SOMERSET
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I, but stoop with patience to my fortune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: So part we sadly in this troublous world,
To meet with joy in sweet Jerusalem.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Is proclamation made, that who finds Edward
Shall have a high reward, and he his life?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: It is: and lo, where youthful Edward comes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Bring forth the gallant, let us hear him speak.
What! can so young a thorn begin to prick?
Edward, what satisfaction canst thou make
For bearing arms, for stirring up my subjects,
And all the trouble thou hast turn'd me to?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Speak like a subject, proud ambitious York!
Suppose that I am now my father's mouth;
Resign thy chair, and where I stand kneel thou,
Whilst I propose the selfsame words to thee,
Which traitor, thou wouldst have me answer to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, that thy father had been so resolved!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: That you might still have worn the petticoat,
And ne'er have stol'n the breech from Lancaster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Let AEsop fable in a winter's night;
His currish riddles sort not with this place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, brat, I'll plague ye for that word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, thou wast born to be a plague to men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: For God's sake, take away this captive scold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, take away this scolding crookback rather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, wilful boy, or I will charm your tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Untutor'd lad, thou art too malapert.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I know my duty; you are all undutiful:
Lascivious Edward, and thou perjured George,
And thou mis-shapen Dick, I tell ye all
I am your better, traitors as ye are:
And thou usurp'st my father's right and mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Take that, thou likeness of this railer here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Sprawl'st thou? take that, to end thy agony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: And there's for twitting me with perjury.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: O, kill me too!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, and shall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, Richard, hold; for we have done too much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Why should she live, to fill the world with words?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: What, doth she swoon? use means for her recovery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Clarence, excuse me to the king my brother;
I'll hence to London on a serious matter:
Ere ye come there, be sure to hear some news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: What? what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: The Tower, the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: O Ned, sweet Ned! speak to thy mother, boy!
Canst thou not speak? O traitors! murderers!
They that stabb'd Caesar shed no blood at all,
Did not offend, nor were not worthy blame,
If this foul deed were by to equal it:
He was a man; this, in respect, a child:
And men ne'er spend their fury on a child.
What's worse than murderer, that I may name it?
No, no, my heart will burst, and if I speak:
And I will speak, that so my heart may burst.
Butchers and villains! bloody cannibals!
How sweet a plant have you untimely cropp'd!
You have no children, butchers! if you had,
The thought of them would have stirr'd up remorse:
But if you ever chance to have a child,
Look in his youth to have him so cut off
As, deathmen, you have rid this sweet young prince!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Away with her; go, bear her hence perforce.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, never bear me hence, dispatch me here,
Here sheathe thy sword, I'll pardon thee my death:
What, wilt thou not? then, Clarence, do it thou.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, I will not do thee so much ease.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Good Clarence, do; sweet Clarence, do thou do it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Didst thou not hear me swear I would not do it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but thou usest to forswear thyself:
'Twas sin before, but now 'tis charity.
What, wilt thou not? Where is that devil's butcher,
Hard-favour'd Richard? Richard, where art thou?
Thou art not here: murder is thy alms-deed;
Petitioners for blood thou ne'er put'st back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Away, I say; I charge ye, bear her hence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: So come to you and yours, as to this Prince!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Where's Richard gone?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: To London, all in post; and, as I guess,
To make a bloody supper in the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: He's sudden, if a thing comes in his head.
Now march we hence: discharge the common sort
With pay and thanks, and let's away to London
And see our gentle queen how well she fares:
By this, I hope, she hath a son for me.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. London. The Tower.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter KING HENRY VI and GLOUCESTER, with the Lieutenant, on the walls

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Good day, my lord. What, at your book so hard?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord:--my lord, I should say rather;
'Tis sin to flatter; 'good' was little better:
'Good Gloucester' and 'good devil' were alike,
And both preposterous; therefore, not 'good lord.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah, leave us to ourselves: we must confer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: So flies the reckless shepherd from the wolf;
So first the harmless sheep doth yield his fleece
And next his throat unto the butcher's knife.
What scene of death hath Roscius now to act?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Suspicion always haunts the guilty mind;
The thief doth fear each bush an officer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: The bird that hath been limed in a bush,
With trembling wings misdoubteth every bush;
And I, the hapless male to one sweet bird,
Have now the fatal object in my eye
Where my poor young was limed, was caught and kill'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what a peevish fool was that of Crete,
That taught his son the office of a fowl!
An yet, for all his wings, the fool was drown'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: I, Daedalus; my poor boy, Icarus;
Thy father, Minos, that denied our course;
The sun that sear'd the wings of my sweet boy
Thy brother Edward, and thyself the sea
Whose envious gulf did swallow up his life.
Ah, kill me with thy weapon, not with words!
My breast can better brook thy dagger's point
Than can my ears that tragic history.
But wherefore dost thou come? is't for my life?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Think'st thou I am an executioner?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: A persecutor, I am sure, thou art:
If murdering innocents be executing,
Why, then thou art an executioner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Thy son I kill'd for his presumption.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Hadst thou been kill'd when first thou didst presume,
Thou hadst not lived to kill a son of mine.
And thus I prophesy, that many a thousand,
Which now mistrust no parcel of my fear,
And many an old man's sigh and many a widow's,
And many an orphan's water-standing eye--
Men for their sons, wives for their husbands,
And orphans for their parents timeless death--
Shall rue the hour that ever thou wast born.
The owl shriek'd at thy birth,--an evil sign;
The night-crow cried, aboding luckless time;
Dogs howl'd, and hideous tempest shook down trees;
The raven rook'd her on the chimney's top,
And chattering pies in dismal discords sung.
Thy mother felt more than a mother's pain,
And, yet brought forth less than a mother's hope,
To wit, an indigested and deformed lump,
Not like the fruit of such a goodly tree.
Teeth hadst thou in thy head when thou wast born,
To signify thou camest to bite the world:
And, if the rest be true which I have heard,
Thou camest--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I'll hear no more: die, prophet in thy speech:
For this amongst the rest, was I ordain'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VI
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and for much more slaughter after this.
God forgive my sins, and pardon thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: What, will the aspiring blood of Lancaster
Sink in the ground? I thought it would have mounted.
See how my sword weeps for the poor king's death!
O, may such purple tears be alway shed
From those that wish the downfall of our house!
If any spark of life be yet remaining,
Down, down to hell; and say I sent thee thither:
I, that have neither pity, love, nor fear.
Indeed, 'tis true that Henry told me of;
For I have often heard my mother say
I came into the world with my legs forward:
Had I not reason, think ye, to make haste,
And seek their ruin that usurp'd our right?
The midwife wonder'd and the women cried
'O, Jesus bless us, he is born with teeth!'
And so I was; which plainly signified
That I should snarl and bite and play the dog.
Then, since the heavens have shaped my body so,
Let hell make crook'd my mind to answer it.
I have no brother, I am like no brother;
And this word 'love,' which graybeards call divine,
Be resident in men like one another
And not in me: I am myself alone.
Clarence, beware; thou keep'st me from the light:
But I will sort a pitchy day for thee;
For I will buz abroad such prophecies
That Edward shall be fearful of his life,
And then, to purge his fear, I'll be thy death.
King Henry and the prince his son are gone:
Clarence, thy turn is next, and then the rest,
Counting myself but bad till I be best.
I'll throw thy body in another room
And triumph, Henry, in thy day of doom.
3 KING HENRY VI

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VII. London. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING EDWARD IV, QUEEN ELIZABETH, CLARENCE, GLOUCESTER, HASTINGS, a Nurse with the young Prince, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Once more we sit in England's royal throne,
Re-purchased with the blood of enemies.
What valiant foemen, like to autumn's corn,
Have we mow'd down, in tops of all their pride!
Three Dukes of Somerset, threefold renown'd
For hardy and undoubted champions;
Two Cliffords, as the father and the son,
And two Northumberlands; two braver men
Ne'er spurr'd their coursers at the trumpet's sound;
With them, the two brave bears, Warwick and Montague,
That in their chains fetter'd the kingly lion
And made the forest tremble when they roar'd.
Thus have we swept suspicion from our seat
And made our footstool of security.
Come hither, Bess, and let me kiss my boy.
Young Ned, for thee, thine uncles and myself
Have in our armours watch'd the winter's night,
Went all afoot in summer's scalding heat,
That thou mightst repossess the crown in peace;
And of our labours thou shalt reap the gain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I'll blast his harvest, if your head were laid;
For yet I am not look'd on in the world.
This shoulder was ordain'd so thick to heave;
And heave it shall some weight, or break my back:
Work thou the way,--and thou shalt execute.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Clarence and Gloucester, love my lovely queen;
And kiss your princely nephew, brothers both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: The duty that I owe unto your majesty
I seal upon the lips of this sweet babe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Thanks, noble Clarence; worthy brother, thanks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: And, that I love the tree from whence thou sprang'st,
Witness the loving kiss I give the fruit.
Aside To say the truth, so Judas kiss'd his master,
And cried 'all hail!' when as he meant all harm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now am I seated as my soul delights,
Having my country's peace and brothers' loves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: What will your grace have done with Margaret?
Reignier, her father, to the king of France
Hath pawn'd the Sicils and Jerusalem,
And hither have they sent it for her ransom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Away with her, and waft her hence to France.
And now what rests but that we spend the time
With stately triumphs, mirthful comic shows,
Such as befits the pleasure of the court?
Sound drums and trumpets! farewell sour annoy!
For here, I hope, begins our lasting joy.

PLAY.TITLE: The Famous History of the Life of Henry the Eighth

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: CAPUCIUS, Ambassador from the Emperor Charles V.
DOCTOR BUTTS, Physician to the King.
Surveyor to the Duke of Buckingham.
Door-keeper of the Council-chamber. Porter, and his Man.
QUEEN KATHARINE Wife to King Henry, afterwards
ANNE BULLEN, her Maid of Honour, afterwards Queen.
An old Lady, friend to Anne Bullen.
Several Lords and Ladies in the Dumb Shows; Women attending upon the Queen; Scribes, Officers, Guards, and other Attendants.

SPEECH.LINE: I come no more to make you laugh: things now,
That bear a weighty and a serious brow,
Sad, high, and working, full of state and woe,
Such noble scenes as draw the eye to flow,
We now present. Those that can pity, here
May, if they think it well, let fall a tear;
The subject will deserve it. Such as give
Their money out of hope they may believe,
May here find truth too. Those that come to see
Only a show or two, and so agree
The play may pass, if they be still and willing,
I'll undertake may see away their shilling
Richly in two short hours. Only they
That come to hear a merry bawdy play,
A noise of targets, or to see a fellow
In a long motley coat guarded with yellow,
Will be deceived; for, gentle hearers, know,
To rank our chosen truth with such a show
As fool and fight is, beside forfeiting
Our own brains, and the opinion that we bring,
To make that only true we now intend,
Will leave us never an understanding friend.
Therefore, for goodness' sake, and as you are known
The first and happiest hearers of the town,
Be sad, as we would make ye: think ye see
The very persons of our noble story
As they were living; think you see them great,
And follow'd with the general throng and sweat
Of thousand friends; then in a moment, see
How soon this mightiness meets misery:
And, if you can be merry then, I'll say
A man may weep upon his wedding-day.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. London. An ante-chamber in the palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter NORFOLK at one door; at the other, BUCKINGHAM and ABERGAVENNY

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, and well met. How have ye done
Since last we saw in France?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your grace,
Healthful; and ever since a fresh admirer
Of what I saw there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: An untimely ague
Stay'd me a prisoner in my chamber when
Those suns of glory, those two lights of men,
Met in the vale of Andren.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twixt Guynes and Arde:
I was then present, saw them salute on horseback;
Beheld them, when they lighted, how they clung
In their embracement, as they grew together;
Which had they, what four throned ones could have weigh'd
Such a compounded one?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: All the whole time
I was my chamber's prisoner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Then you lost
The view of earthly glory: men might say,
Till this time pomp was single, but now married
To one above itself. Each following day
Became the next day's master, till the last
Made former wonders its. To-day the French,
All clinquant, all in gold, like heathen gods,
Shone down the English; and, to-morrow, they
Made Britain India: every man that stood
Show'd like a mine. Their dwarfish pages were
As cherubins, all guilt: the madams too,
Not used to toil, did almost sweat to bear
The pride upon them, that their very labour
Was to them as a painting: now this masque
Was cried incomparable; and the ensuing night
Made it a fool and beggar. The two kings,
Equal in lustre, were now best, now worst,
As presence did present them; him in eye,
Still him in praise: and, being present both
'Twas said they saw but one; and no discerner
Durst wag his tongue in censure. When these suns--
For so they phrase 'em--by their heralds challenged
The noble spirits to arms, they did perform
Beyond thought's compass; that former fabulous story,
Being now seen possible enough, got credit,
That Bevis was believed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: O, you go far.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: As I belong to worship and affect
In honour honesty, the tract of every thing
Would by a good discourser lose some life,
Which action's self was tongue to. All was royal;
To the disposing of it nought rebell'd.
Order gave each thing view; the office did
Distinctly his full function.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Who did guide,
I mean, who set the body and the limbs
Of this great sport together, as you guess?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: One, certes, that promises no element
In such a business.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, who, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: All this was order'd by the good discretion
Of the right reverend Cardinal of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: The devil speed him! no man's pie is freed
From his ambitious finger. What had he
To do in these fierce vanities? I wonder
That such a keech can with his very bulk
Take up the rays o' the beneficial sun
And keep it from the earth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Surely, sir,
There's in him stuff that puts him to these ends;
For, being not propp'd by ancestry, whose grace
Chalks successors their way, nor call'd upon
For high feats done to the crown; neither allied
For eminent assistants; but, spider-like,
Out of his self-drawing web, he gives us note,
The force of his own merit makes his way
A gift that heaven gives for him, which buys
A place next to the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABERGAVENNY
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot tell
What heaven hath given him,--let some graver eye
Pierce into that; but I can see his pride
Peep through each part of him: whence has he that,
If not from hell? the devil is a niggard,
Or has given all before, and he begins
A new hell in himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Why the devil,
Upon this French going out, took he upon him,
Without the privity o' the king, to appoint
Who should attend on him? He makes up the file
Of all the gentry; for the most part such
To whom as great a charge as little honour
He meant to lay upon: and his own letter,
The honourable board of council out,
Must fetch him in the papers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABERGAVENNY
SPEECH.LINE: I do know
Kinsmen of mine, three at the least, that have
By this so sickened their estates, that never
They shall abound as formerly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: O, many
Have broke their backs with laying manors on 'em
For this great journey. What did this vanity
But minister communication of
A most poor issue?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Grievingly I think,
The peace between the French and us not values
The cost that did conclude it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Every man,
After the hideous storm that follow'd, was
A thing inspired; and, not consulting, broke
Into a general prophecy; That this tempest,
Dashing the garment of this peace, aboded
The sudden breach on't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Which is budded out;
For France hath flaw'd the league, and hath attach'd
Our merchants' goods at Bourdeaux.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABERGAVENNY
SPEECH.LINE: Is it therefore
The ambassador is silenced?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, is't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABERGAVENNY
SPEECH.LINE: A proper title of a peace; and purchased
At a superfluous rate!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Why, all this business
Our reverend cardinal carried.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Like it your grace,
The state takes notice of the private difference
Betwixt you and the cardinal. I advise you--
And take it from a heart that wishes towards you
Honour and plenteous safety--that you read
The cardinal's malice and his potency
Together; to consider further that
What his high hatred would effect wants not
A minister in his power. You know his nature,
That he's revengeful, and I know his sword
Hath a sharp edge: it's long and, 't may be said,
It reaches far, and where 'twill not extend,
Thither he darts it. Bosom up my counsel,
You'll find it wholesome. Lo, where comes that rock
That I advise your shunning.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CARDINAL WOLSEY, the purse borne before him, certain of the Guard, and two Secretaries with papers. CARDINAL WOLSEY in his passage fixeth his eye on BUCKINGHAM, and BUCKINGHAM on him, both full of disdain

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: The Duke of Buckingham's surveyor, ha?
Where's his examination?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Secretary
SPEECH.LINE: Here, so please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Is he in person ready?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Secretary
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, please your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Well, we shall then know more; and Buckingham
Shall lessen this big look.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt CARDINAL WOLSEY and his Train

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: This butcher's cur is venom-mouth'd, and I
Have not the power to muzzle him; therefore best
Not wake him in his slumber. A beggar's book
Outworths a noble's blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: What, are you chafed?
Ask God for temperance; that's the appliance only
Which your disease requires.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I read in's looks
Matter against me; and his eye reviled
Me, as his abject object: at this instant
He bores me with some trick: he's gone to the king;
I'll follow and outstare him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, my lord,
And let your reason with your choler question
What 'tis you go about: to climb steep hills
Requires slow pace at first: anger is like
A full-hot horse, who being allow'd his way,
Self-mettle tires him. Not a man in England
Can advise me like you: be to yourself
As you would to your friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I'll to the king;
And from a mouth of honour quite cry down
This Ipswich fellow's insolence; or proclaim
There's difference in no persons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Be advised;
Heat not a furnace for your foe so hot
That it do singe yourself: we may outrun,
By violent swiftness, that which we run at,
And lose by over-running. Know you not,
The fire that mounts the liquor til run o'er,
In seeming to augment it wastes it? Be advised:
I say again, there is no English soul
More stronger to direct you than yourself,
If with the sap of reason you would quench,
Or but allay, the fire of passion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
I am thankful to you; and I'll go along
By your prescription: but this top-proud fellow,
Whom from the flow of gall I name not but
From sincere motions, by intelligence,
And proofs as clear as founts in July when
We see each grain of gravel, I do know
To be corrupt and treasonous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Say not 'treasonous.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: To the king I'll say't; and make my vouch as strong
As shore of rock. Attend. This holy fox,
Or wolf, or both,--for he is equal ravenous
As he is subtle, and as prone to mischief
As able to perform't; his mind and place
Infecting one another, yea, reciprocally--
Only to show his pomp as well in France
As here at home, suggests the king our master
To this last costly treaty, the interview,
That swallow'd so much treasure, and like a glass
Did break i' the rinsing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, and so it did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, give me favour, sir. This cunning cardinal
The articles o' the combination drew
As himself pleased; and they were ratified
As he cried 'Thus let be': to as much end
As give a crutch to the dead: but our count-cardinal
Has done this, and 'tis well; for worthy Wolsey,
Who cannot err, he did it. Now this follows,--
Which, as I take it, is a kind of puppy
To the old dam, treason,--Charles the emperor,
Under pretence to see the queen his aunt--
For 'twas indeed his colour, but he came
To whisper Wolsey,--here makes visitation:
His fears were, that the interview betwixt
England and France might, through their amity,
Breed him some prejudice; for from this league
Peep'd harms that menaced him: he privily
Deals with our cardinal; and, as I trow,--
Which I do well; for I am sure the emperor
Paid ere he promised; whereby his suit was granted
Ere it was ask'd; but when the way was made,
And paved with gold, the emperor thus desired,
That he would please to alter the king's course,
And break the foresaid peace. Let the king know,
As soon he shall by me, that thus the cardinal
Does buy and sell his honour as he pleases,
And for his own advantage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry
To hear this of him; and could wish he were
Something mistaken in't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: No, not a syllable:
I do pronounce him in that very shape
He shall appear in proof.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BRANDON, a Sergeant-at-arms before him, and two or three of the Guard

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: Your office, sergeant; execute it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sergeant
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
My lord the Duke of Buckingham, and Earl
Of Hereford, Stafford, and Northampton, I
Arrest thee of high treason, in the name
Of our most sovereign king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Lo, you, my lord,
The net has fall'n upon me! I shall perish
Under device and practise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry
To see you ta'en from liberty, to look on
The business present: 'tis his highness' pleasure
You shall to the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: It will help me nothing
To plead mine innocence; for that dye is on me
Which makes my whitest part black. The will of heaven
Be done in this and all things! I obey.
O my Lord Abergavenny, fare you well!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, he must bear you company. The king
Is pleased you shall to the Tower, till you know
How he determines further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABERGAVENNY
SPEECH.LINE: As the duke said,
The will of heaven be done, and the king's pleasure
By me obey'd!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: Here is a warrant from
The king to attach Lord Montacute; and the bodies
Of the duke's confessor, John de la Car,
One Gilbert Peck, his chancellor--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: So, so;
These are the limbs o' the plot: no more, I hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: A monk o' the Chartreux.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: O, Nicholas Hopkins?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRANDON
SPEECH.LINE: He.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: My surveyor is false; the o'er-great cardinal
Hath show'd him gold; my life is spann'd already:
I am the shadow of poor Buckingham,
Whose figure even this instant cloud puts on,
By darkening my clear sun. My lord, farewell.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. The council-chamber.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Cornets. Enter KING HENRY VIII, leaning on CARDINAL WOLSEY's shoulder, the Nobles, and LOVELL; CARDINAL WOLSEY places himself under KING HENRY VIII's feet on his right side

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: My life itself, and the best heart of it,
Thanks you for this great care: I stood i' the level
Of a full-charged confederacy, and give thanks
To you that choked it. Let be call'd before us
That gentleman of Buckingham's; in person
I'll hear him his confessions justify;
And point by point the treasons of his master
He shall again relate.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: A noise within, crying 'Room for the Queen!' Enter QUEEN KATHARINE, ushered by NORFOLK, and SUFFOLK: she kneels. KING HENRY VIII riseth from his state, takes her up, kisses and placeth her by him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, we must longer kneel: I am a suitor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Arise, and take place by us: half your suit
Never name to us; you have half our power:
The other moiety, ere you ask, is given;
Repeat your will and take it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thank your majesty.
That you would love yourself, and in that love
Not unconsider'd leave your honour, nor
The dignity of your office, is the point
Of my petition.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Lady mine, proceed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: I am solicited, not by a few,
And those of true condition, that your subjects
Are in great grievance: there have been commissions
Sent down among 'em, which hath flaw'd the heart
Of all their loyalties: wherein, although,
My good lord cardinal, they vent reproaches
Most bitterly on you, as putter on
Of these exactions, yet the king our master--
Whose honour heaven shield from soil!--even he
escapes not
Language unmannerly, yea, such which breaks
The sides of loyalty, and almost appears
In loud rebellion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Not almost appears,
It doth appear; for, upon these taxations,
The clothiers all, not able to maintain
The many to them longing, have put off
The spinsters, carders, fullers, weavers, who,
Unfit for other life, compell'd by hunger
And lack of other means, in desperate manner
Daring the event to the teeth, are all in uproar,
And danger serves among then!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Taxation!
Wherein? and what taxation? My lord cardinal,
You that are blamed for it alike with us,
Know you of this taxation?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Please you, sir,
I know but of a single part, in aught
Pertains to the state; and front but in that file
Where others tell steps with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: No, my lord,
You know no more than others; but you frame
Things that are known alike; which are not wholesome
To those which would not know them, and yet must
Perforce be their acquaintance. These exactions,
Whereof my sovereign would have note, they are
Most pestilent to the bearing; and, to bear 'em,
The back is sacrifice to the load. They say
They are devised by you; or else you suffer
Too hard an exclamation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Still exaction!
The nature of it? in what kind, let's know,
Is this exaction?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: I am much too venturous
In tempting of your patience; but am bolden'd
Under your promised pardon. The subjects' grief
Comes through commissions, which compel from each
The sixth part of his substance, to be levied
Without delay; and the pretence for this
Is named, your wars in France: this makes bold mouths:
Tongues spit their duties out, and cold hearts freeze
Allegiance in them; their curses now
Live where their prayers did: and it's come to pass,
This tractable obedience is a slave
To each incensed will. I would your highness
Would give it quick consideration, for
There is no primer business.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: By my life,
This is against our pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: And for me,
I have no further gone in this than by
A single voice; and that not pass'd me but
By learned approbation of the judges. If I am
Traduced by ignorant tongues, which neither know
My faculties nor person, yet will be
The chronicles of my doing, let me say
'Tis but the fate of place, and the rough brake
That virtue must go through. We must not stint
Our necessary actions, in the fear
To cope malicious censurers; which ever,
As ravenous fishes, do a vessel follow
That is new-trimm'd, but benefit no further
Than vainly longing. What we oft do best,
By sick interpreters, once weak ones, is
Not ours, or not allow'd; what worst, as oft,
Hitting a grosser quality, is cried up
For our best act. If we shall stand still,
In fear our motion will be mock'd or carp'd at,
We should take root here where we sit, or sit
State-statues only.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Things done well,
And with a care, exempt themselves from fear;
Things done without example, in their issue
Are to be fear'd. Have you a precedent
Of this commission? I believe, not any.
We must not rend our subjects from our laws,
And stick them in our will. Sixth part of each?
A trembling contribution! Why, we take
From every tree lop, bark, and part o' the timber;
And, though we leave it with a root, thus hack'd,
The air will drink the sap. To every county
Where this is question'd send our letters, with
Free pardon to each man that has denied
The force of this commission: pray, look to't;
I put it to your care.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: A word with you.
Let there be letters writ to every shire,
Of the king's grace and pardon. The grieved commons
Hardly conceive of me; let it be noised
That through our intercession this revokement
And pardon comes: I shall anon advise you
Further in the proceeding.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry that the Duke of Buckingham
Is run in your displeasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: It grieves many:
The gentleman is learn'd, and a most rare speaker;
To nature none more bound; his training such,
That he may furnish and instruct great teachers,
And never seek for aid out of himself. Yet see,
When these so noble benefits shall prove
Not well disposed, the mind growing once corrupt,
They turn to vicious forms, ten times more ugly
Than ever they were fair. This man so complete,
Who was enroll'd 'mongst wonders, and when we,
Almost with ravish'd listening, could not find
His hour of speech a minute; he, my lady,
Hath into monstrous habits put the graces
That once were his, and is become as black
As if besmear'd in hell. Sit by us; you shall hear--
This was his gentleman in trust--of him
Things to strike honour sad. Bid him recount
The fore-recited practises; whereof
We cannot feel too little, hear too much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Stand forth, and with bold spirit relate what you,
Most like a careful subject, have collected
Out of the Duke of Buckingham.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Speak freely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: First, it was usual with him, every day
It would infect his speech, that if the king
Should without issue die, he'll carry it so
To make the sceptre his: these very words
I've heard him utter to his son-in-law,
Lord Abergavenny; to whom by oath he menaced
Revenge upon the cardinal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Please your highness, note
This dangerous conception in this point.
Not friended by by his wish, to your high person
His will is most malignant; and it stretches
Beyond you, to your friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: My learn'd lord cardinal,
Deliver all with charity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Speak on:
How grounded he his title to the crown,
Upon our fail? to this point hast thou heard him
At any time speak aught?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: He was brought to this
By a vain prophecy of Nicholas Hopkins.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: What was that Hopkins?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, a Chartreux friar,
His confessor, who fed him every minute
With words of sovereignty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: How know'st thou this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: Not long before your highness sped to France,
The duke being at the Rose, within the parish
Saint Lawrence Poultney, did of me demand
What was the speech among the Londoners
Concerning the French journey: I replied,
Men fear'd the French would prove perfidious,
To the king's danger. Presently the duke
Said, 'twas the fear, indeed; and that he doubted
'Twould prove the verity of certain words
Spoke by a holy monk; 'that oft,' says he,
'Hath sent to me, wishing me to permit
John de la Car, my chaplain, a choice hour
To hear from him a matter of some moment:
Whom after under the confession's seal
He solemnly had sworn, that what he spoke
My chaplain to no creature living, but
To me, should utter, with demure confidence
This pausingly ensued: neither the king nor's heirs,
Tell you the duke, shall prosper: bid him strive
To gain the love o' the commonalty: the duke
Shall govern England.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: If I know you well,
You were the duke's surveyor, and lost your office
On the complaint o' the tenants: take good heed
You charge not in your spleen a noble person
And spoil your nobler soul: I say, take heed;
Yes, heartily beseech you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Let him on.
Go forward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: On my soul, I'll speak but truth.
I told my lord the duke, by the devil's illusions
The monk might be deceived; and that 'twas dangerous for him
To ruminate on this so far, until
It forged him some design, which, being believed,
It was much like to do: he answer'd, 'Tush,
It can do me no damage;' adding further,
That, had the king in his last sickness fail'd,
The cardinal's and Sir Thomas Lovell's heads
Should have gone off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! what, so rank? Ah ha!
There's mischief in this man: canst thou say further?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: I can, my liege.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Proceed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: Being at Greenwich,
After your highness had reproved the duke
About Sir William Blomer,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: I remember
Of such a time: being my sworn servant,
The duke retain'd him his. But on; what hence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: 'If,' quoth he, 'I for this had been committed,
As, to the Tower, I thought, I would have play'd
The part my father meant to act upon
The usurper Richard; who, being at Salisbury,
Made suit to come in's presence; which if granted,
As he made semblance of his duty, would
Have put his knife to him.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: A giant traitor!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Now, madam, may his highness live in freedom,
and this man out of prison?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: God mend all!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: There's something more would out of thee; what say'st?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Surveyor
SPEECH.LINE: After 'the duke his father,' with 'the knife,'
He stretch'd him, and, with one hand on his dagger,
Another spread on's breast, mounting his eyes
He did discharge a horrible oath; whose tenor
Was,--were he evil used, he would outgo
His father by as much as a performance
Does an irresolute purpose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: There's his period,
To sheathe his knife in us. He is attach'd;
Call him to present trial: if he may
Find mercy in the law, 'tis his: if none,
Let him not seek 't of us: by day and night,
He's traitor to the height.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. An ante-chamber in the palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible the spells of France should juggle
Men into such strange mysteries?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: New customs,
Though they be never so ridiculous,
Nay, let 'em be unmanly, yet are follow'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: As far as I see, all the good our English
Have got by the late voyage is but merely
A fit or two o' the face; but they are shrewd ones;
For when they hold 'em, you would swear directly
Their very noses had been counsellors
To Pepin or Clotharius, they keep state so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: They have all new legs, and lame ones: one would take it,
That never saw 'em pace before, the spavin
Or springhalt reign'd among 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Death! my lord,
Their clothes are after such a pagan cut too,
That, sure, they've worn out Christendom.
How now!
What news, Sir Thomas Lovell?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, my lord,
I hear of none, but the new proclamation
That's clapp'd upon the court-gate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: What is't for?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: The reformation of our travell'd gallants,
That fill the court with quarrels, talk, and tailors.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: I'm glad 'tis there: now I would pray our monsieurs
To think an English courtier may be wise,
And never see the Louvre.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: They must either,
For so run the conditions, leave those remnants
Of fool and feather that they got in France,
With all their honourable point of ignorance
Pertaining thereunto, as fights and fireworks,
Abusing better men than they can be,
Out of a foreign wisdom, renouncing clean
The faith they have in tennis, and tall stockings,
Short blister'd breeches, and those types of travel,
And understand again like honest men;
Or pack to their old playfellows: there, I take it,
They may, 'cum privilegio,' wear away
The lag end of their lewdness and be laugh'd at.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis time to give 'em physic, their diseases
Are grown so catching.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: What a loss our ladies
Will have of these trim vanities!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry,
There will be woe indeed, lords: the sly whoresons
Have got a speeding trick to lay down ladies;
A French song and a fiddle has no fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: The devil fiddle 'em! I am glad they are going,
For, sure, there's no converting of 'em: now
An honest country lord, as I am, beaten
A long time out of play, may bring his plainsong
And have an hour of hearing; and, by'r lady,
Held current music too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, Lord Sands;
Your colt's tooth is not cast yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: No, my lord;
Nor shall not, while I have a stump.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Thomas,
Whither were you a-going?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: To the cardinal's:
Your lordship is a guest too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'tis true:
This night he makes a supper, and a great one,
To many lords and ladies; there will be
The beauty of this kingdom, I'll assure you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: That churchman bears a bounteous mind indeed,
A hand as fruitful as the land that feeds us;
His dews fall every where.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: No doubt he's noble;
He had a black mouth that said other of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: He may, my lord; has wherewithal: in him
Sparing would show a worse sin than ill doctrine:
Men of his way should be most liberal;
They are set here for examples.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: True, they are so:
But few now give so great ones. My barge stays;
Your lordship shall along. Come, good Sir Thomas,
We shall be late else; which I would not be,
For I was spoke to, with Sir Henry Guildford
This night to be comptrollers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: I am your lordship's.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. A Hall in York Place.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Hautboys. A small table under a state for CARDINAL WOLSEY, a longer table for the guests. Then enter ANNE and divers other Ladies and Gentlemen as guests, at one door; at another door, enter GUILDFORD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GUILDFORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ladies, a general welcome from his grace
Salutes ye all; this night he dedicates
To fair content and you: none here, he hopes,
In all this noble bevy, has brought with her
One care abroad; he would have all as merry
As, first, good company, good wine, good welcome,
Can make good people. O, my lord, you're tardy:
The very thought of this fair company
Clapp'd wings to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: You are young, Sir Harry Guildford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Thomas Lovell, had the cardinal
But half my lay thoughts in him, some of these
Should find a running banquet ere they rested,
I think would better please 'em: by my life,
They are a sweet society of fair ones.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: O, that your lordship were but now confessor
To one or two of these!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: I would I were;
They should find easy penance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, how easy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: As easy as a down-bed would afford it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet ladies, will it please you sit? Sir Harry,
Place you that side; I'll take the charge of this:
His grace is entering. Nay, you must not freeze;
Two women placed together makes cold weather:
My Lord Sands, you are one will keep 'em waking;
Pray, sit between these ladies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: By my faith,
And thank your lordship. By your leave, sweet ladies:
If I chance to talk a little wild, forgive me;
I had it from my father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE
SPEECH.LINE: Was he mad, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: O, very mad, exceeding mad, in love too:
But he would bite none; just as I do now,
He would kiss you twenty with a breath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, my lord.
So, now you're fairly seated. Gentlemen,
The penance lies on you, if these fair ladies
Pass away frowning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: For my little cure,
Let me alone.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Hautboys. Enter CARDINAL WOLSEY, and takes his state

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: You're welcome, my fair guests: that noble lady,
Or gentleman, that is not freely merry,
Is not my friend: this, to confirm my welcome;
And to you all, good health.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace is noble:
Let me have such a bowl may hold my thanks,
And save me so much talking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Sands,
I am beholding to you: cheer your neighbours.
Ladies, you are not merry: gentlemen,
Whose fault is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: The red wine first must rise
In their fair cheeks, my lord; then we shall have 'em
Talk us to silence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE
SPEECH.LINE: You are a merry gamester,
My Lord Sands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, if I make my play.
Here's to your ladyship: and pledge it, madam,
For 'tis to such a thing,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE
SPEECH.LINE: You cannot show me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SANDS
SPEECH.LINE: I told your grace they would talk anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: What's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Look out there, some of ye.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: What warlike voice,
And to what end is this? Nay, ladies, fear not;
By all the laws of war you're privileged.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what is't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: A noble troop of strangers;
For so they seem: they've left their barge and landed;
And hither make, as great ambassadors
From foreign princes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Good lord chamberlain,
Go, give 'em welcome; you can speak the French tongue;
And, pray, receive 'em nobly, and conduct 'em
Into our presence, where this heaven of beauty
Shall shine at full upon them. Some attend him.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Exit Chamberlain, attended. All rise, and tables removed
SPEECH.LINE: You have now a broken banquet; but we'll mend it.
A good digestion to you all: and once more
I shower a welcome on ye; welcome all.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Hautboys. Enter KING HENRY VIII and others, as masquers, habited like shepherds, ushered by the Chamberlain. They pass directly before CARDINAL WOLSEY, and gracefully salute him
SPEECH.LINE: A noble company! what are their pleasures?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Because they speak no English, thus they pray'd
To tell your grace, that, having heard by fame
Of this so noble and so fair assembly
This night to meet here, they could do no less
Out of the great respect they bear to beauty,
But leave their flocks; and, under your fair conduct,
Crave leave to view these ladies and entreat
An hour of revels with 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Say, lord chamberlain,
They have done my poor house grace; for which I pay 'em
A thousand thanks, and pray 'em take their pleasures.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: They choose Ladies for the dance. KING HENRY VIII chooses ANNE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: The fairest hand I ever touch'd! O beauty,
Till now I never knew thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: My lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, tell 'em thus much from me:
There should be one amongst 'em, by his person,
More worthy this place than myself; to whom,
If I but knew him, with my love and duty
I would surrender it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: I will, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: What say they?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: Such a one, they all confess,
There is indeed; which they would have your grace
Find out, and he will take it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Let me see, then.
By all your good leaves, gentlemen; here I'll make
My royal choice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Ye have found him, cardinal:
You hold a fair assembly; you do well, lord:
You are a churchman, or, I'll tell you, cardinal,
I should judge now unhappily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad
Your grace is grown so pleasant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: My lord chamberlain,
Prithee, come hither: what fair lady's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Chamberlain
SPEECH.LINE: An't please your grace, Sir Thomas Bullen's daughter--
The Viscount Rochford,--one of her highness' women.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, she is a dainty one. Sweetheart,
I were unmannerly, to take you out,
And not to kiss you. A health, gentlemen!
Let it go round.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Thomas Lovell, is the banquet ready
I' the privy chamber?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace,
I fear, with dancing is a little heated.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: I fear, too much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL WOLSEY
SPEECH.LINE: There's fresher air, my lord,
In the next chamber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING HENRY VIII
SPEECH.LINE: Lead in your ladies, every one: sweet partner,
I must not yet forsake you: let's be merry:
Good my lord cardinal, I have half a dozen healths
To drink to these fair ladies, and a measure
To lead 'em once again; and then let's dream
Who's best in favour. Let the music knock it.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Westminster. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Whither away so fast?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: O, God save ye!
Even to the hall, to hear what shall become
Of the great Duke of Buckingham.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I'll save you
That labour, sir. All's now done, but the ceremony
Of bringing back the prisoner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Were you there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, indeed, was I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, speak what has happen'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: You may guess quickly what.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Is he found guilty?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, truly is he, and condemn'd upon't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry for't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: So are a number more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: But, pray, how pass'd it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I'll tell you in a little. The great duke
Came to the bar; where to his accusations
He pleaded still not guilty and alleged
Many sharp reasons to defeat the law.
The king's attorney on the contrary
Urged on the examinations, proofs, confessions
Of divers witnesses; which the duke desired
To have brought viva voce to his face:
At which appear'd against him his surveyor;
Sir Gilbert Peck his chancellor; and John Car,
Confessor to him; with that devil-monk,
Hopkins, that made this mischief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: That was he
That fed him with his prophecies?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: The same.
All these accused him strongly; which he fain
Would have flung from him, but, indeed, he could not:
And so his peers, upon this evidence,
Have found him guilty of high treason. Much
He spoke, and learnedly, for life; but all
Was either pitied in him or forgotten.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: After all this, how did he bear himself?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: When he was brought again to the bar, to hear
His knell rung out, his judgment, he was stirr'd
With such an agony, he sweat extremely,
And something spoke in choler, ill, and hasty:
But he fell to himself again, and sweetly
In all the rest show'd a most noble patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I do not think he fears death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Sure, he does not:
He never was so womanish; the cause
He may a little grieve at.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Certainly
The cardinal is the end of this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis likely,
By all conjectures: first, Kildare's attainder,
Then deputy of Ireland; who removed,
Earl Surrey was sent thither, and in haste too,
Lest he should help his father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: That trick of state
Was a deep envious one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: At his return
No doubt he will requite it. This is noted,
And generally, whoever the king favours,
The cardinal instantly will find employment,
And far enough from court too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: All the commons
Hate him perniciously, and, o' my conscience,
Wish him ten fathom deep: this duke as much
They love and dote on; call him bounteous Buckingham,
The mirror of all courtesy;--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Stay there, sir,
And see the noble ruin'd man you speak of.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BUCKINGHAM from his arraignment; tip-staves before him; the axe with the edge towards him; halberds on each side: accompanied with LOVELL, VAUX, SANDS, and common people

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Let's stand close, and behold him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: All good people,
You that thus far have come to pity me,
Hear what I say, and then go home and lose me.
I have this day received a traitor's judgment,
And by that name must die: yet, heaven bear witness,
And if I have a conscience, let it sink me,
Even as the axe falls, if I be not faithful!
The law I bear no malice for my death;
'T has done, upon the premises, but justice:
But those that sought it I could wish more Christians:
Be what they will, I heartily forgive 'em:
Yet let 'em look they glory not in mischief,
Nor build their evils on the graves of great men;
For then my guiltless blood must cry against 'em.
For further life in this world I ne'er hope,
Nor will I sue, although the king have mercies
More than I dare make faults. You few that loved me,
And dare be bold to weep for Buckingham,
His noble friends and fellows, whom to leave
Is only bitter to him, only dying,
Go with me, like good angels, to my end;
And, as the long divorce of steel falls on me,
Make of your prayers one sweet sacrifice,
And lift my soul to heaven. Lead on, o' God's name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: I do beseech your grace, for charity,
If ever any malice in your heart
Were hid against me, now to forgive me frankly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Thomas Lovell, I as free forgive you
As I would be forgiven: I forgive all;
There cannot be those numberless offences
'Gainst me, that I cannot take peace with:
no black envy
Shall mark my grave. Commend me to his grace;
And if he speak of Buckingham, pray, tell him
You met him half in heaven: my vows and prayers
Yet are the king's; and, till my soul forsake,
Shall cry for blessings on him: may he live
Longer than I have time to tell his years!
Ever beloved and loving may his rule be!
And when old time shall lead him to his end,
Goodness and he fill up one monument!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVELL
SPEECH.LINE: To the water side I must conduct your grace;
Then give my charge up to Sir Nicholas Vaux,
Who undertakes you to your end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VAUX
SPEECH.LINE: Prepare there,
The duke is coming: see the barge be ready;
And fit it with such furniture as suits
The greatness of his person.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, Sir Nicholas,
Let it alone; my state now will but mock me.
When I came hither, I was lord high constable
And Duke of Buckingham; now, poor Edward Bohun:
Yet I am richer than my base accusers,
That never knew what truth meant: I now seal it;
And with that blood will make 'em one day groan for't.
My noble father, Henry of Buckingham,
Who first raised head against usurping Richard,
Flying for succor to his servant Banister,
Being distress'd, was by that wretch betray'd,
And without trial fell; God's peace be with him!
Henry the Seventh succeeding, truly pitying
My father's loss, like a most royal prince,
Restored me to my honours, and, out of ruins,
Made my name once more noble. Now his son,
Henry the Eighth, life, honour, name and all
That made me happy at one stroke has taken
For ever from the world. I had my trial,
And, must needs say, a noble one; which makes me,
A little happier than my wretched father:
