SPEECH.LINE: I am not well in health, and that is all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Brutus is wise, and, were he not in health,
He would embrace the means to come by it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so I do. Good Portia, go to bed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is Brutus sick? and is it physical
To walk unbraced and suck up the humours
Of the dank morning? What, is Brutus sick,
And will he steal out of his wholesome bed,
To dare the vile contagion of the night
And tempt the rheumy and unpurged air
To add unto his sickness? No, my Brutus;
You have some sick offence within your mind,
Which, by the right and virtue of my place,
I ought to know of: and, upon my knees,
I charm you, by my once-commended beauty,
By all your vows of love and that great vow
Which did incorporate and make us one,
That you unfold to me, yourself, your half,
Why you are heavy, and what men to-night
Have had to resort to you: for here have been
Some six or seven, who did hide their faces
Even from darkness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Kneel not, gentle Portia.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I should not need, if you were gentle Brutus.
Within the bond of marriage, tell me, Brutus,
Is it excepted I should know no secrets
That appertain to you? Am I yourself
But, as it were, in sort or limitation,
To keep with you at meals, comfort your bed,
And talk to you sometimes? Dwell I but in the suburbs
Of your good pleasure? If it be no more,
Portia is Brutus' harlot, not his wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You are my true and honourable wife,
As dear to me as are the ruddy drops
That visit my sad heart

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: If this were true, then should I know this secret.
I grant I am a woman; but withal
A woman that Lord Brutus took to wife:
I grant I am a woman; but withal
A woman well-reputed, Cato's daughter.
Think you I am no stronger than my sex,
Being so father'd and so husbanded?
Tell me your counsels, I will not disclose 'em:
I have made strong proof of my constancy,
Giving myself a voluntary wound
Here, in the thigh: can I bear that with patience.
And not my husband's secrets?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O ye gods,
Render me worthy of this noble wife!
Hark, hark! one knocks: Portia, go in awhile;
And by and by thy bosom shall partake
The secrets of my heart.
All my engagements I will construe to thee,
All the charactery of my sad brows:
Leave me with haste.
Lucius, who's that knocks?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He is a sick man that would speak with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caius Ligarius, that Metellus spake of.
Boy, stand aside. Caius Ligarius! how?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LIGARIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Vouchsafe good morrow from a feeble tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, what a time have you chose out, brave Caius,
To wear a kerchief! Would you were not sick!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LIGARIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am not sick, if Brutus have in hand
Any exploit worthy the name of honour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Such an exploit have I in hand, Ligarius,
Had you a healthful ear to hear of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LIGARIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By all the gods that Romans bow before,
I here discard my sickness! Soul of Rome!
Brave son, derived from honourable loins!
Thou, like an exorcist, hast conjured up
My mortified spirit. Now bid me run,
And I will strive with things impossible;
Yea, get the better of them. What's to do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: A piece of work that will make sick men whole.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LIGARIUS
SPEECH.LINE: But are not some whole that we must make sick?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: That must we also. What it is, my Caius,
I shall unfold to thee, as we are going
To whom it must be done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LIGARIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Set on your foot,
And with a heart new-fired I follow you,
To do I know not what: but it sufficeth
That Brutus leads me on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Follow me, then.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. CAESAR's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Thunder and lightning. Enter CAESAR, in his night-gown

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Nor heaven nor earth have been at peace to-night:
Thrice hath Calpurnia in her sleep cried out,
'Help, ho! they murder Caesar!' Who's within?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Go bid the priests do present sacrifice
And bring me their opinions of success.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I will, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALPURNIA
SPEECH.LINE: What mean you, Caesar? think you to walk forth?
You shall not stir out of your house to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar shall forth: the things that threaten'd me
Ne'er look'd but on my back; when they shall see
The face of Caesar, they are vanished.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALPURNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar, I never stood on ceremonies,
Yet now they fright me. There is one within,
Besides the things that we have heard and seen,
Recounts most horrid sights seen by the watch.
A lioness hath whelped in the streets;
And graves have yawn'd, and yielded up their dead;
Fierce fiery warriors fought upon the clouds,
In ranks and squadrons and right form of war,
Which drizzled blood upon the Capitol;
The noise of battle hurtled in the air,
Horses did neigh, and dying men did groan,
And ghosts did shriek and squeal about the streets.
O Caesar! these things are beyond all use,
And I do fear them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: What can be avoided
Whose end is purposed by the mighty gods?
Yet Caesar shall go forth; for these predictions
Are to the world in general as to Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALPURNIA
SPEECH.LINE: When beggars die, there are no comets seen;
The heavens themselves blaze forth the death of princes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Cowards die many times before their deaths;
The valiant never taste of death but once.
Of all the wonders that I yet have heard.
It seems to me most strange that men should fear;
Seeing that death, a necessary end,
Will come when it will come.
What say the augurers?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: They would not have you to stir forth to-day.
Plucking the entrails of an offering forth,
They could not find a heart within the beast.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: The gods do this in shame of cowardice:
Caesar should be a beast without a heart,
If he should stay at home to-day for fear.
No, Caesar shall not: danger knows full well
That Caesar is more dangerous than he:
We are two lions litter'd in one day,
And I the elder and more terrible:
And Caesar shall go forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALPURNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, my lord,
Your wisdom is consumed in confidence.
Do not go forth to-day: call it my fear
That keeps you in the house, and not your own.
We'll send Mark Antony to the senate-house:
And he shall say you are not well to-day:
Let me, upon my knee, prevail in this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Mark Antony shall say I am not well,
And, for thy humour, I will stay at home.
Here's Decius Brutus, he shall tell them so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar, all hail! good morrow, worthy Caesar:
I come to fetch you to the senate-house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: And you are come in very happy time,
To bear my greeting to the senators
And tell them that I will not come to-day:
Cannot, is false, and that I dare not, falser:
I will not come to-day: tell them so, Decius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALPURNIA
SPEECH.LINE: Say he is sick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Shall Caesar send a lie?
Have I in conquest stretch'd mine arm so far,
To be afraid to tell graybeards the truth?
Decius, go tell them Caesar will not come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Most mighty Caesar, let me know some cause,
Lest I be laugh'd at when I tell them so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: The cause is in my will: I will not come;
That is enough to satisfy the senate.
But for your private satisfaction,
Because I love you, I will let you know:
Calpurnia here, my wife, stays me at home:
She dreamt to-night she saw my statua,
Which, like a fountain with an hundred spouts,
Did run pure blood: and many lusty Romans
Came smiling, and did bathe their hands in it:
And these does she apply for warnings, and portents,
And evils imminent; and on her knee
Hath begg'd that I will stay at home to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: This dream is all amiss interpreted;
It was a vision fair and fortunate:
Your statue spouting blood in many pipes,
In which so many smiling Romans bathed,
Signifies that from you great Rome shall suck
Reviving blood, and that great men shall press
For tinctures, stains, relics and cognizance.
This by Calpurnia's dream is signified.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: And this way have you well expounded it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have, when you have heard what I can say:
And know it now: the senate have concluded
To give this day a crown to mighty Caesar.
If you shall send them word you will not come,
Their minds may change. Besides, it were a mock
Apt to be render'd, for some one to say
'Break up the senate till another time,
When Caesar's wife shall meet with better dreams.'
If Caesar hide himself, shall they not whisper
'Lo, Caesar is afraid'?
Pardon me, Caesar; for my dear dear love
To our proceeding bids me tell you this;
And reason to my love is liable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: How foolish do your fears seem now, Calpurnia!
I am ashamed I did yield to them.
Give me my robe, for I will go.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter PUBLIUS, BRUTUS, LIGARIUS, METELLUS, CASCA, TREBONIUS, and CINNA
SPEECH.LINE: And look where Publius is come to fetch me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PUBLIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, Publius.
What, Brutus, are you stirr'd so early too?
Good morrow, Casca. Caius Ligarius,
Caesar was ne'er so much your enemy
As that same ague which hath made you lean.
What is 't o'clock?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar, 'tis strucken eight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you for your pains and courtesy.
See! Antony, that revels long o' nights,
Is notwithstanding up. Good morrow, Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: So to most noble Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Bid them prepare within:
I am to blame to be thus waited for.
Now, Cinna: now, Metellus: what, Trebonius!
I have an hour's talk in store for you;
Remember that you call on me to-day:
Be near me, that I may remember you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TREBONIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar, I will:
and so near will I be,
That your best friends shall wish I had been further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Good friends, go in, and taste some wine with me;
And we, like friends, will straightway go together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside That every like is not the same, O Caesar,
The heart of Brutus yearns to think upon!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A street near the Capitol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARTEMIDORUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Caesar, beware of Brutus; take heed of Cassius;
come not near Casca; have an eye to Cinna, trust not
Trebonius: mark well Metellus Cimber: Decius Brutus
loves thee not: thou hast wronged Caius Ligarius.
There is but one mind in all these men, and it is
bent against Caesar. If thou beest not immortal,
look about you: security gives way to conspiracy.
The mighty gods defend thee! Thy lover,
'ARTEMIDORUS.'
Here will I stand till Caesar pass along,
And as a suitor will I give him this.
My heart laments that virtue cannot live
Out of the teeth of emulation.
If thou read this, O Caesar, thou mayst live;
If not, the Fates with traitors do contrive.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Another part of the same street, before the house of BRUTUS.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee, boy, run to the senate-house;
Stay not to answer me, but get thee gone:
Why dost thou stay?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: To know my errand, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I would have had thee there, and here again,
Ere I can tell thee what thou shouldst do there.
O constancy, be strong upon my side,
Set a huge mountain 'tween my heart and tongue!
I have a man's mind, but a woman's might.
How hard it is for women to keep counsel!
Art thou here yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, what should I do?
Run to the Capitol, and nothing else?
And so return to you, and nothing else?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, bring me word, boy, if thy lord look well,
For he went sickly forth: and take good note
What Caesar doth, what suitors press to him.
Hark, boy! what noise is that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I hear none, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, listen well;
I heard a bustling rumour, like a fray,
And the wind brings it from the Capitol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sooth, madam, I hear nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, fellow: which way hast thou been?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: At mine own house, good lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: What is't o'clock?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: About the ninth hour, lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is Caesar yet gone to the Capitol?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, not yet: I go to take my stand,
To see him pass on to the Capitol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast some suit to Caesar, hast thou not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: That I have, lady: if it will please Caesar
To be so good to Caesar as to hear me,
I shall beseech him to befriend himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, know'st thou any harm's intended towards him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: None that I know will be, much that I fear may chance.
Good morrow to you. Here the street is narrow:
The throng that follows Caesar at the heels,
Of senators, of praetors, common suitors,
Will crowd a feeble man almost to death:
I'll get me to a place more void, and there
Speak to great Caesar as he comes along.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I must go in. Ay me, how weak a thing
The heart of woman is! O Brutus,
The heavens speed thee in thine enterprise!
Sure, the boy heard me: Brutus hath a suit
That Caesar will not grant. O, I grow faint.
Run, Lucius, and commend me to my lord;
Say I am merry: come to me again,
And bring me word what he doth say to thee.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Rome. Before the Capitol; the Senate sitting above.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: A crowd of people; among them ARTEMIDORUS and the Soothsayer. Flourish. Enter CAESAR, BRUTUS, CASSIUS, CASCA, DECIUS BRUTUS, METELLUS CIMBER, TREBONIUS, CINNA, ANTONY, LEPIDUS, POPILIUS, PUBLIUS, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: To the Soothsayer The ides of March are come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Soothsayer
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Caesar; but not gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARTEMIDORUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, Caesar! read this schedule.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Trebonius doth desire you to o'erread,
At your best leisure, this his humble suit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARTEMIDORUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Caesar, read mine first; for mine's a suit
That touches Caesar nearer: read it, great Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: What touches us ourself shall be last served.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARTEMIDORUS
SPEECH.LINE: Delay not, Caesar; read it instantly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: What, is the fellow mad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PUBLIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah, give place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, urge you your petitions in the street?
Come to the Capitol.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: CAESAR goes up to the Senate-House, the rest following

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POPILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I wish your enterprise to-day may thrive.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What enterprise, Popilius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: POPILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What said Popilius Lena?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He wish'd to-day our enterprise might thrive.
I fear our purpose is discovered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Look, how he makes to Caesar; mark him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Casca, be sudden, for we fear prevention.
Brutus, what shall be done? If this be known,
Cassius or Caesar never shall turn back,
For I will slay myself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cassius, be constant:
Popilius Lena speaks not of our purposes;
For, look, he smiles, and Caesar doth not change.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Trebonius knows his time; for, look you, Brutus.
He draws Mark Antony out of the way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where is Metellus Cimber? Let him go,
And presently prefer his suit to Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He is address'd: press near and second him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA
SPEECH.LINE: Casca, you are the first that rears your hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Are we all ready? What is now amiss
That Caesar and his senate must redress?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: METELLUS CIMBER
SPEECH.LINE: Most high, most mighty, and most puissant Caesar,
Metellus Cimber throws before thy seat
An humble heart,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: I must prevent thee, Cimber.
These couchings and these lowly courtesies
Might fire the blood of ordinary men,
And turn pre-ordinance and first decree
Into the law of children. Be not fond,
To think that Caesar bears such rebel blood
That will be thaw'd from the true quality
With that which melteth fools; I mean, sweet words,
Low-crooked court'sies and base spaniel-fawning.
Thy brother by decree is banished:
If thou dost bend and pray and fawn for him,
I spurn thee like a cur out of my way.
Know, Caesar doth not wrong, nor without cause
Will he be satisfied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: METELLUS CIMBER
SPEECH.LINE: Is there no voice more worthy than my own
To sound more sweetly in great Caesar's ear
For the repealing of my banish'd brother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I kiss thy hand, but not in flattery, Caesar;
Desiring thee that Publius Cimber may
Have an immediate freedom of repeal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: What, Brutus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, Caesar; Caesar, pardon:
As low as to thy foot doth Cassius fall,
To beg enfranchisement for Publius Cimber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I could be well moved, if I were as you:
If I could pray to move, prayers would move me:
But I am constant as the northern star,
Of whose true-fix'd and resting quality
There is no fellow in the firmament.
The skies are painted with unnumber'd sparks,
They are all fire and every one doth shine,
But there's but one in all doth hold his place:
So in the world; 'tis furnish'd well with men,
And men are flesh and blood, and apprehensive;
Yet in the number I do know but one
That unassailable holds on his rank,
Unshaked of motion: and that I am he,
Let me a little show it, even in this;
That I was constant Cimber should be banish'd,
And constant do remain to keep him so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA
SPEECH.LINE: O Caesar,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Hence! wilt thou lift up Olympus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Great Caesar,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Doth not Brutus bootless kneel?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASCA
SPEECH.LINE: Speak, hands for me!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: CASCA first, then the other Conspirators and BRUTUS stab CAESAR

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAESAR
SPEECH.LINE: Et tu, Brute! Then fall, Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA
SPEECH.LINE: Liberty! Freedom! Tyranny is dead!
Run hence, proclaim, cry it about the streets.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Some to the common pulpits, and cry out
'Liberty, freedom, and enfranchisement!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: People and senators, be not affrighted;
Fly not; stand stiff: ambition's debt is paid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASCA
SPEECH.LINE: Go to the pulpit, Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: And Cassius too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where's Publius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA
SPEECH.LINE: Here, quite confounded with this mutiny.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: METELLUS CIMBER
SPEECH.LINE: Stand fast together, lest some friend of Caesar's
Should chance--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Talk not of standing. Publius, good cheer;
There is no harm intended to your person,
Nor to no Roman else: so tell them, Publius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And leave us, Publius; lest that the people,
Rushing on us, should do your age some mischief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do so: and let no man abide this deed,
But we the doers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where is Antony?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TREBONIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fled to his house amazed:
Men, wives and children stare, cry out and run
As it were doomsday.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fates, we will know your pleasures:
That we shall die, we know; 'tis but the time
And drawing days out, that men stand upon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, he that cuts off twenty years of life
Cuts off so many years of fearing death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Grant that, and then is death a benefit:
So are we Caesar's friends, that have abridged
His time of fearing death. Stoop, Romans, stoop,
And let us bathe our hands in Caesar's blood
Up to the elbows, and besmear our swords:
Then walk we forth, even to the market-place,
And, waving our red weapons o'er our heads,
Let's all cry 'Peace, freedom and liberty!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stoop, then, and wash. How many ages hence
Shall this our lofty scene be acted over
In states unborn and accents yet unknown!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: How many times shall Caesar bleed in sport,
That now on Pompey's basis lies along
No worthier than the dust!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: So oft as that shall be,
So often shall the knot of us be call'd
The men that gave their country liberty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DECIUS BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall we forth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, every man away:
Brutus shall lead; and we will grace his heels
With the most boldest and best hearts of Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Soft! who comes here? A friend of Antony's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Thus, Brutus, did my master bid me kneel:
Thus did Mark Antony bid me fall down;
And, being prostrate, thus he bade me say:
Brutus is noble, wise, valiant, and honest;
Caesar was mighty, bold, royal, and loving:
Say I love Brutus, and I honour him;
Say I fear'd Caesar, honour'd him and loved him.
If Brutus will vouchsafe that Antony
May safely come to him, and be resolved
How Caesar hath deserved to lie in death,
Mark Antony shall not love Caesar dead
So well as Brutus living; but will follow
The fortunes and affairs of noble Brutus
Thorough the hazards of this untrod state
With all true faith. So says my master Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thy master is a wise and valiant Roman;
I never thought him worse.
Tell him, so please him come unto this place,
He shall be satisfied; and, by my honour,
Depart untouch'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I'll fetch him presently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know that we shall have him well to friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I wish we may: but yet have I a mind
That fears him much; and my misgiving still
Falls shrewdly to the purpose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: But here comes Antony.
Welcome, Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: O mighty Caesar! dost thou lie so low?
Are all thy conquests, glories, triumphs, spoils,
Shrunk to this little measure? Fare thee well.
I know not, gentlemen, what you intend,
Who else must be let blood, who else is rank:
If I myself, there is no hour so fit
As Caesar's death hour, nor no instrument
Of half that worth as those your swords, made rich
With the most noble blood of all this world.
I do beseech ye, if you bear me hard,
Now, whilst your purpled hands do reek and smoke,
Fulfil your pleasure. Live a thousand years,
I shall not find myself so apt to die:
No place will please me so, no mean of death,
As here by Caesar, and by you cut off,
The choice and master spirits of this age.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Antony, beg not your death of us.
Though now we must appear bloody and cruel,
As, by our hands and this our present act,
You see we do, yet see you but our hands
And this the bleeding business they have done:
Our hearts you see not; they are pitiful;
And pity to the general wrong of Rome--
As fire drives out fire, so pity pity--
Hath done this deed on Caesar. For your part,
To you our swords have leaden points, Mark Antony:
Our arms, in strength of malice, and our hearts
Of brothers' temper, do receive you in
With all kind love, good thoughts, and reverence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your voice shall be as strong as any man's
In the disposing of new dignities.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Only be patient till we have appeased
The multitude, beside themselves with fear,
And then we will deliver you the cause,
Why I, that did love Caesar when I struck him,
Have thus proceeded.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: I doubt not of your wisdom.
Let each man render me his bloody hand:
First, Marcus Brutus, will I shake with you;
Next, Caius Cassius, do I take your hand;
Now, Decius Brutus, yours: now yours, Metellus;
Yours, Cinna; and, my valiant Casca, yours;
Though last, not last in love, yours, good Trebonius.
Gentlemen all,--alas, what shall I say?
My credit now stands on such slippery ground,
That one of two bad ways you must conceit me,
Either a coward or a flatterer.
That I did love thee, Caesar, O, 'tis true:
If then thy spirit look upon us now,
Shall it not grieve thee dearer than thy death,
To see thy thy Anthony making his peace,
Shaking the bloody fingers of thy foes,
Most noble! in the presence of thy corse?
Had I as many eyes as thou hast wounds,
Weeping as fast as they stream forth thy blood,
It would become me better than to close
In terms of friendship with thine enemies.
Pardon me, Julius! Here wast thou bay'd, brave hart;
Here didst thou fall; and here thy hunters stand,
Sign'd in thy spoil, and crimson'd in thy lethe.
O world, thou wast the forest to this hart;
And this, indeed, O world, the heart of thee.
How like a deer, strucken by many princes,
Dost thou here lie!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mark Antony,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, Caius Cassius:
The enemies of Caesar shall say this;
Then, in a friend, it is cold modesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I blame you not for praising Caesar so;
But what compact mean you to have with us?
Will you be prick'd in number of our friends;
Or shall we on, and not depend on you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore I took your hands, but was, indeed,
Sway'd from the point, by looking down on Caesar.
Friends am I with you all and love you all,
Upon this hope, that you shall give me reasons
Why and wherein Caesar was dangerous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Or else were this a savage spectacle:
Our reasons are so full of good regard
That were you, Antony, the son of Caesar,
You should be satisfied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: That's all I seek:
And am moreover suitor that I may
Produce his body to the market-place;
And in the pulpit, as becomes a friend,
Speak in the order of his funeral.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You shall, Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Brutus, a word with you.
You know not what you do: do not consent
That Antony speak in his funeral:
Know you how much the people may be moved
By that which he will utter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: By your pardon;
I will myself into the pulpit first,
And show the reason of our Caesar's death:
What Antony shall speak, I will protest
He speaks by leave and by permission,
And that we are contented Caesar shall
Have all true rites and lawful ceremonies.
It shall advantage more than do us wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know not what may fall; I like it not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mark Antony, here, take you Caesar's body.
You shall not in your funeral speech blame us,
But speak all good you can devise of Caesar,
And say you do't by our permission;
Else shall you not have any hand at all
About his funeral: and you shall speak
In the same pulpit whereto I am going,
After my speech is ended.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so.
I do desire no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prepare the body then, and follow us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: O, pardon me, thou bleeding piece of earth,
That I am meek and gentle with these butchers!
Thou art the ruins of the noblest man
That ever lived in the tide of times.
Woe to the hand that shed this costly blood!
Over thy wounds now do I prophesy,--
Which, like dumb mouths, do ope their ruby lips,
To beg the voice and utterance of my tongue--
A curse shall light upon the limbs of men;
Domestic fury and fierce civil strife
Shall cumber all the parts of Italy;
Blood and destruction shall be so in use
And dreadful objects so familiar
That mothers shall but smile when they behold
Their infants quarter'd with the hands of war;
All pity choked with custom of fell deeds:
And Caesar's spirit, ranging for revenge,
With Ate by his side come hot from hell,
Shall in these confines with a monarch's voice
Cry 'Havoc,' and let slip the dogs of war;
That this foul deed shall smell above the earth
With carrion men, groaning for burial.
You serve Octavius Caesar, do you not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I do, Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar did write for him to come to Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: He did receive his letters, and is coming;
And bid me say to you by word of mouth--
O Caesar!--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Thy heart is big, get thee apart and weep.
Passion, I see, is catching; for mine eyes,
Seeing those beads of sorrow stand in thine,
Began to water. Is thy master coming?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: He lies to-night within seven leagues of Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Post back with speed, and tell him what hath chanced:
Here is a mourning Rome, a dangerous Rome,
No Rome of safety for Octavius yet;
Hie hence, and tell him so. Yet, stay awhile;
Thou shalt not back till I have borne this corse
Into the market-place: there shall I try
In my oration, how the people take
The cruel issue of these bloody men;
According to the which, thou shalt discourse
To young Octavius of the state of things.
Lend me your hand.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The Forum.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BRUTUS and CASSIUS, and a throng of Citizens

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: We will be satisfied; let us be satisfied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then follow me, and give me audience, friends.
Cassius, go you into the other street,
And part the numbers.
Those that will hear me speak, let 'em stay here;
Those that will follow Cassius, go with him;
And public reasons shall be rendered
Of Caesar's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: I will hear Brutus speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: I will hear Cassius; and compare their reasons,
When severally we hear them rendered.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exit CASSIUS, with some of the Citizens. BRUTUS goes into the pulpit

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: The noble Brutus is ascended: silence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Be patient till the last.
Romans, countrymen, and lovers! hear me for my
cause, and be silent, that you may hear: believe me
for mine honour, and have respect to mine honour, that
you may believe: censure me in your wisdom, and
awake your senses, that you may the better judge.
If there be any in this assembly, any dear friend of
Caesar's, to him I say, that Brutus' love to Caesar
was no less than his. If then that friend demand
why Brutus rose against Caesar, this is my answer:
--Not that I loved Caesar less, but that I loved
Rome more. Had you rather Caesar were living and
die all slaves, than that Caesar were dead, to live
all free men? As Caesar loved me, I weep for him;
as he was fortunate, I rejoice at it; as he was
valiant, I honour him: but, as he was ambitious, I
slew him. There is tears for his love; joy for his
fortune; honour for his valour; and death for his
ambition. Who is here so base that would be a
bondman? If any, speak; for him have I offended.
Who is here so rude that would not be a Roman? If
any, speak; for him have I offended. Who is here so
vile that will not love his country? If any, speak;
for him have I offended. I pause for a reply.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: None, Brutus, none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then none have I offended. I have done no more to
Caesar than you shall do to Brutus. The question of
his death is enrolled in the Capitol; his glory not
extenuated, wherein he was worthy, nor his offences
enforced, for which he suffered death.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter ANTONY and others, with CAESAR's body
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes his body, mourned by Mark Antony: who,
though he had no hand in his death, shall receive
the benefit of his dying, a place in the
commonwealth; as which of you shall not? With this
I depart,--that, as I slew my best lover for the
good of Rome, I have the same dagger for myself,
when it shall please my country to need my death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Live, Brutus! live, live!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Bring him with triumph home unto his house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Give him a statue with his ancestors.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Let him be Caesar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar's better parts
Shall be crown'd in Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: We'll bring him to his house
With shouts and clamours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: My countrymen,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, silence! Brutus speaks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good countrymen, let me depart alone,
And, for my sake, stay here with Antony:
Do grace to Caesar's corpse, and grace his speech
Tending to Caesar's glories; which Mark Antony,
By our permission, is allow'd to make.
I do entreat you, not a man depart,
Save I alone, till Antony have spoke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, ho! and let us hear Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Let him go up into the public chair;
We'll hear him. Noble Antony, go up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: For Brutus' sake, I am beholding to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: What does he say of Brutus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: He says, for Brutus' sake,
He finds himself beholding to us all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twere best he speak no harm of Brutus here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: This Caesar was a tyrant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that's certain:
We are blest that Rome is rid of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Peace! let us hear what Antony can say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: You gentle Romans,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, ho! let us hear him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears;
I come to bury Caesar, not to praise him.
The evil that men do lives after them;
The good is oft interred with their bones;
So let it be with Caesar. The noble Brutus
Hath told you Caesar was ambitious:
If it were so, it was a grievous fault,
And grievously hath Caesar answer'd it.
Here, under leave of Brutus and the rest--
For Brutus is an honourable man;
So are they all, all honourable men--
Come I to speak in Caesar's funeral.
He was my friend, faithful and just to me:
But Brutus says he was ambitious;
And Brutus is an honourable man.
He hath brought many captives home to Rome
Whose ransoms did the general coffers fill:
Did this in Caesar seem ambitious?
When that the poor have cried, Caesar hath wept:
Ambition should be made of sterner stuff:
Yet Brutus says he was ambitious;
And Brutus is an honourable man.
You all did see that on the Lupercal
I thrice presented him a kingly crown,
Which he did thrice refuse: was this ambition?
Yet Brutus says he was ambitious;
And, sure, he is an honourable man.
I speak not to disprove what Brutus spoke,
But here I am to speak what I do know.
You all did love him once, not without cause:
What cause withholds you then, to mourn for him?
O judgment! thou art fled to brutish beasts,
And men have lost their reason. Bear with me;
My heart is in the coffin there with Caesar,
And I must pause till it come back to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Methinks there is much reason in his sayings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: If thou consider rightly of the matter,
Caesar has had great wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Has he, masters?
I fear there will a worse come in his place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Mark'd ye his words? He would not take the crown;
Therefore 'tis certain he was not ambitious.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: If it be found so, some will dear abide it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Poor soul! his eyes are red as fire with weeping.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: There's not a nobler man in Rome than Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Now mark him, he begins again to speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: But yesterday the word of Caesar might
Have stood against the world; now lies he there.
And none so poor to do him reverence.
O masters, if I were disposed to stir
Your hearts and minds to mutiny and rage,
I should do Brutus wrong, and Cassius wrong,
Who, you all know, are honourable men:
I will not do them wrong; I rather choose
To wrong the dead, to wrong myself and you,
Than I will wrong such honourable men.
But here's a parchment with the seal of Caesar;
I found it in his closet, 'tis his will:
Let but the commons hear this testament--
Which, pardon me, I do not mean to read--
And they would go and kiss dead Caesar's wounds
And dip their napkins in his sacred blood,
Yea, beg a hair of him for memory,
And, dying, mention it within their wills,
Bequeathing it as a rich legacy
Unto their issue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: We'll hear the will: read it, Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: The will, the will! we will hear Caesar's will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Have patience, gentle friends, I must not read it;
It is not meet you know how Caesar loved you.
You are not wood, you are not stones, but men;
And, being men, bearing the will of Caesar,
It will inflame you, it will make you mad:
'Tis good you know not that you are his heirs;
For, if you should, O, what would come of it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Read the will; we'll hear it, Antony;
You shall read us the will, Caesar's will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Will you be patient? will you stay awhile?
I have o'ershot myself to tell you of it:
I fear I wrong the honourable men
Whose daggers have stabb'd Caesar; I do fear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: They were traitors: honourable men!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: The will! the testament!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: They were villains, murderers: the will! read the will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: You will compel me, then, to read the will?
Then make a ring about the corpse of Caesar,
And let me show you him that made the will.
Shall I descend? and will you give me leave?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Several Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: Come down.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Descend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: You shall have leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: A ring; stand round.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Stand from the hearse, stand from the body.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Room for Antony, most noble Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, press not so upon me; stand far off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Several Citizens
SPEECH.LINE: Stand back; room; bear back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: If you have tears, prepare to shed them now.
You all do know this mantle: I remember
The first time ever Caesar put it on;
'Twas on a summer's evening, in his tent,
That day he overcame the Nervii:
Look, in this place ran Cassius' dagger through:
See what a rent the envious Casca made:
Through this the well-beloved Brutus stabb'd;
And as he pluck'd his cursed steel away,
Mark how the blood of Caesar follow'd it,
As rushing out of doors, to be resolved
If Brutus so unkindly knock'd, or no;
For Brutus, as you know, was Caesar's angel:
Judge, O you gods, how dearly Caesar loved him!
This was the most unkindest cut of all;
For when the noble Caesar saw him stab,
Ingratitude, more strong than traitors' arms,
Quite vanquish'd him: then burst his mighty heart;
And, in his mantle muffling up his face,
Even at the base of Pompey's statua,
Which all the while ran blood, great Caesar fell.
O, what a fall was there, my countrymen!
Then I, and you, and all of us fell down,
Whilst bloody treason flourish'd over us.
O, now you weep; and, I perceive, you feel
The dint of pity: these are gracious drops.
Kind souls, what, weep you when you but behold
Our Caesar's vesture wounded? Look you here,
Here is himself, marr'd, as you see, with traitors.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O piteous spectacle!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O noble Caesar!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O woful day!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O traitors, villains!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O most bloody sight!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: We will be revenged.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Revenge! About! Seek! Burn! Fire! Kill! Slay!
Let not a traitor live!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, countrymen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Peace there! hear the noble Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: We'll hear him, we'll follow him, we'll die with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Good friends, sweet friends, let me not stir you up
To such a sudden flood of mutiny.
They that have done this deed are honourable:
What private griefs they have, alas, I know not,
That made them do it: they are wise and honourable,
And will, no doubt, with reasons answer you.
I come not, friends, to steal away your hearts:
I am no orator, as Brutus is;
But, as you know me all, a plain blunt man,
That love my friend; and that they know full well
That gave me public leave to speak of him:
For I have neither wit, nor words, nor worth,
Action, nor utterance, nor the power of speech,
To stir men's blood: I only speak right on;
I tell you that which you yourselves do know;
Show you sweet Caesar's wounds, poor poor dumb mouths,
And bid them speak for me: but were I Brutus,
And Brutus Antony, there were an Antony
Would ruffle up your spirits and put a tongue
In every wound of Caesar that should move
The stones of Rome to rise and mutiny.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: We'll mutiny.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: We'll burn the house of Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Away, then! come, seek the conspirators.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Yet hear me, countrymen; yet hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, ho! Hear Antony. Most noble Antony!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Why, friends, you go to do you know not what:
Wherein hath Caesar thus deserved your loves?
Alas, you know not: I must tell you then:
You have forgot the will I told you of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Most true. The will! Let's stay and hear the will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Here is the will, and under Caesar's seal.
To every Roman citizen he gives,
To every several man, seventy-five drachmas.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Most noble Caesar! We'll revenge his death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: O royal Caesar!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me with patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Moreover, he hath left you all his walks,
His private arbours and new-planted orchards,
On this side Tiber; he hath left them you,
And to your heirs for ever, common pleasures,
To walk abroad, and recreate yourselves.
Here was a Caesar! when comes such another?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Never, never. Come, away, away!
We'll burn his body in the holy place,
And with the brands fire the traitors' houses.
Take up the body.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Go fetch fire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Pluck down benches.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Pluck down forms, windows, any thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Now let it work. Mischief, thou art afoot,
Take thou what course thou wilt!
How now, fellow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, Octavius is already come to Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Where is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: He and Lepidus are at Caesar's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: And thither will I straight to visit him:
He comes upon a wish. Fortune is merry,
And in this mood will give us any thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I heard him say, Brutus and Cassius
Are rid like madmen through the gates of Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Belike they had some notice of the people,
How I had moved them. Bring me to Octavius.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: I dreamt to-night that I did feast with Caesar,
And things unlucky charge my fantasy:
I have no will to wander forth of doors,
Yet something leads me forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: What is your name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Whither are you going?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Where do you dwell?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Are you a married man or a bachelor?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Answer every man directly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and briefly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and wisely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and truly, you were best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: What is my name? Whither am I going? Where do I
dwell? Am I a married man or a bachelor? Then, to
answer every man directly and briefly, wisely and
truly: wisely I say, I am a bachelor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: That's as much as to say, they are fools that marry:
you'll bear me a bang for that, I fear. Proceed; directly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: Directly, I am going to Caesar's funeral.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: As a friend or an enemy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: As a friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: That matter is answered directly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: For your dwelling,--briefly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: Briefly, I dwell by the Capitol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Your name, sir, truly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, my name is Cinna.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Tear him to pieces; he's a conspirator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: I am Cinna the poet, I am Cinna the poet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Tear him for his bad verses, tear him for his bad verses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CINNA THE POET
SPEECH.LINE: I am not Cinna the conspirator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fourth Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: It is no matter, his name's Cinna; pluck but his
name out of his heart, and turn him going.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Tear him, tear him! Come, brands ho! fire-brands:
to Brutus', to Cassius'; burn all: some to Decius'
house, and some to Casca's; some to Ligarius': away, go!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A house in Rome.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: ANTONY, OCTAVIUS, and LEPIDUS, seated at a table

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: These many, then, shall die; their names are prick'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your brother too must die; consent you, Lepidus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEPIDUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do consent--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prick him down, Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEPIDUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon condition Publius shall not live,
Who is your sister's son, Mark Antony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: He shall not live; look, with a spot I damn him.
But, Lepidus, go you to Caesar's house;
Fetch the will hither, and we shall determine
How to cut off some charge in legacies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEPIDUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall I find you here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Or here, or at the Capitol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: This is a slight unmeritable man,
Meet to be sent on errands: is it fit,
The three-fold world divided, he should stand
One of the three to share it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: So you thought him;
And took his voice who should be prick'd to die,
In our black sentence and proscription.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Octavius, I have seen more days than you:
And though we lay these honours on this man,
To ease ourselves of divers slanderous loads,
He shall but bear them as the ass bears gold,
To groan and sweat under the business,
Either led or driven, as we point the way;
And having brought our treasure where we will,
Then take we down his load, and turn him off,
Like to the empty ass, to shake his ears,
And graze in commons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You may do your will;
But he's a tried and valiant soldier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: So is my horse, Octavius; and for that
I do appoint him store of provender:
It is a creature that I teach to fight,
To wind, to stop, to run directly on,
His corporal motion govern'd by my spirit.
And, in some taste, is Lepidus but so;
He must be taught and train'd and bid go forth;
A barren-spirited fellow; one that feeds
On abjects, orts and imitations,
Which, out of use and staled by other men,
Begin his fashion: do not talk of him,
But as a property. And now, Octavius,
Listen great things:--Brutus and Cassius
Are levying powers: we must straight make head:
Therefore let our alliance be combined,
Our best friends made, our means stretch'd
And let us presently go sit in council,
How covert matters may be best disclosed,
And open perils surest answered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let us do so: for we are at the stake,
And bay'd about with many enemies;
And some that smile have in their hearts, I fear,
Millions of mischiefs.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Camp near Sardis. Before BRUTUS's tent.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Drum. Enter BRUTUS, LUCILIUS, LUCIUS, and Soldiers; TITINIUS and PINDARUS meeting them

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Give the word, ho! and stand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What now, Lucilius! is Cassius near?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He is at hand; and Pindarus is come
To do you salutation from his master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He greets me well. Your master, Pindarus,
In his own change, or by ill officers,
Hath given me some worthy cause to wish
Things done, undone: but, if he be at hand,
I shall be satisfied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PINDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not doubt
But that my noble master will appear
Such as he is, full of regard and honour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He is not doubted. A word, Lucilius;
How he received you, let me be resolved.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: With courtesy and with respect enough;
But not with such familiar instances,
Nor with such free and friendly conference,
As he hath used of old.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast described
A hot friend cooling: ever note, Lucilius,
When love begins to sicken and decay,
It useth an enforced ceremony.
There are no tricks in plain and simple faith;
But hollow men, like horses hot at hand,
Make gallant show and promise of their mettle;
But when they should endure the bloody spur,
They fall their crests, and, like deceitful jades,
Sink in the trial. Comes his army on?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: They mean this night in Sardis to be quarter'd;
The greater part, the horse in general,
Are come with Cassius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hark! he is arrived.
March gently on to meet him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, ho! Speak the word along.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Soldier
SPEECH.LINE: Stand!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Soldier
SPEECH.LINE: Stand!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Soldier
SPEECH.LINE: Stand!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Most noble brother, you have done me wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Judge me, you gods! wrong I mine enemies?
And, if not so, how should I wrong a brother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Brutus, this sober form of yours hides wrongs;
And when you do them--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cassius, be content.
Speak your griefs softly: I do know you well.
Before the eyes of both our armies here,
Which should perceive nothing but love from us,
Let us not wrangle: bid them move away;
Then in my tent, Cassius, enlarge your griefs,
And I will give you audience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pindarus,
Bid our commanders lead their charges off
A little from this ground.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucilius, do you the like; and let no man
Come to our tent till we have done our conference.
Let Lucius and Titinius guard our door.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Brutus's tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: That you have wrong'd me doth appear in this:
You have condemn'd and noted Lucius Pella
For taking bribes here of the Sardians;
Wherein my letters, praying on his side,
Because I knew the man, were slighted off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You wronged yourself to write in such a case.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: In such a time as this it is not meet
That every nice offence should bear his comment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let me tell you, Cassius, you yourself
Are much condemn'd to have an itching palm;
To sell and mart your offices for gold
To undeservers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I an itching palm!
You know that you are Brutus that speak this,
Or, by the gods, this speech were else your last.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: The name of Cassius honours this corruption,
And chastisement doth therefore hide his head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Chastisement!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Remember March, the ides of March remember:
Did not great Julius bleed for justice' sake?
What villain touch'd his body, that did stab,
And not for justice? What, shall one of us
That struck the foremost man of all this world
But for supporting robbers, shall we now
Contaminate our fingers with base bribes,
And sell the mighty space of our large honours
For so much trash as may be grasped thus?
I had rather be a dog, and bay the moon,
Than such a Roman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Brutus, bay not me;
I'll not endure it: you forget yourself,
To hedge me in; I am a soldier, I,
Older in practise, abler than yourself
To make conditions.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; you are not, Cassius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I say you are not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Urge me no more, I shall forget myself;
Have mind upon your health, tempt me no further.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away, slight man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, for I will speak.
Must I give way and room to your rash choler?
Shall I be frighted when a madman stares?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O ye gods, ye gods! must I endure all this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: All this! ay, more: fret till your proud heart break;
Go show your slaves how choleric you are,
And make your bondmen tremble. Must I budge?
Must I observe you? must I stand and crouch
Under your testy humour? By the gods
You shall digest the venom of your spleen,
Though it do split you; for, from this day forth,
I'll use you for my mirth, yea, for my laughter,
When you are waspish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is it come to this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You say you are a better soldier:
Let it appear so; make your vaunting true,
And it shall please me well: for mine own part,
I shall be glad to learn of noble men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You wrong me every way; you wrong me, Brutus;
I said, an elder soldier, not a better:
Did I say 'better'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: If you did, I care not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: When Caesar lived, he durst not thus have moved me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, peace! you durst not so have tempted him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I durst not!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, durst not tempt him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: For your life you durst not!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do not presume too much upon my love;
I may do that I shall be sorry for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have done that you should be sorry for.
There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats,
For I am arm'd so strong in honesty
That they pass by me as the idle wind,
Which I respect not. I did send to you
For certain sums of gold, which you denied me:
For I can raise no money by vile means:
By heaven, I had rather coin my heart,
And drop my blood for drachmas, than to wring
From the hard hands of peasants their vile trash
By any indirection: I did send
To you for gold to pay my legions,
Which you denied me: was that done like Cassius?
Should I have answer'd Caius Cassius so?
When Marcus Brutus grows so covetous,
To lock such rascal counters from his friends,
Be ready, gods, with all your thunderbolts;
Dash him to pieces!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I denied you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: You did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I did not: he was but a fool that brought
My answer back. Brutus hath rived my heart:
A friend should bear his friend's infirmities,
But Brutus makes mine greater than they are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not, till you practise them on me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You love me not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not like your faults.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: A friendly eye could never see such faults.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: A flatterer's would not, though they do appear
As huge as high Olympus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Antony, and young Octavius, come,
Revenge yourselves alone on Cassius,
For Cassius is aweary of the world;
Hated by one he loves; braved by his brother;
Cheque'd like a bondman; all his faults observed,
Set in a note-book, learn'd, and conn'd by rote,
To cast into my teeth. O, I could weep
My spirit from mine eyes! There is my dagger,
And here my naked breast; within, a heart
Dearer than Plutus' mine, richer than gold:
If that thou be'st a Roman, take it forth;
I, that denied thee gold, will give my heart:
Strike, as thou didst at Caesar; for, I know,
When thou didst hate him worst, thou lovedst him better
Than ever thou lovedst Cassius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sheathe your dagger:
Be angry when you will, it shall have scope;
Do what you will, dishonour shall be humour.
O Cassius, you are yoked with a lamb
That carries anger as the flint bears fire;
Who, much enforced, shows a hasty spark,
And straight is cold again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hath Cassius lived
To be but mirth and laughter to his Brutus,
When grief, and blood ill-temper'd, vexeth him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: When I spoke that, I was ill-temper'd too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do you confess so much? Give me your hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: And my heart too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Brutus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Have not you love enough to bear with me,
When that rash humour which my mother gave me
Makes me forgetful?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, Cassius; and, from henceforth,
When you are over-earnest with your Brutus,
He'll think your mother chides, and leave you so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Within Let me go in to see the generals;
There is some grudge between 'em, 'tis not meet
They be alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Within You shall not come to them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Within Nothing but death shall stay me.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter Poet, followed by LUCILIUS, TITINIUS, and LUCIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: For shame, you generals! what do you mean?
Love, and be friends, as two such men should be;
For I have seen more years, I'm sure, than ye.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha! how vilely doth this cynic rhyme!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Get you hence, sirrah; saucy fellow, hence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Bear with him, Brutus; 'tis his fashion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll know his humour, when he knows his time:
What should the wars do with these jigging fools?
Companion, hence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away, away, be gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucilius and Titinius, bid the commanders
Prepare to lodge their companies to-night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And come yourselves, and bring Messala with you
Immediately to us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucius, a bowl of wine!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I did not think you could have been so angry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Cassius, I am sick of many griefs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Of your philosophy you make no use,
If you give place to accidental evils.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No man bears sorrow better. Portia is dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! Portia!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: She is dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How 'scaped I killing when I cross'd you so?
O insupportable and touching loss!
Upon what sickness?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Impatient of my absence,
And grief that young Octavius with Mark Antony
Have made themselves so strong:--for with her death
That tidings came;--with this she fell distract,
And, her attendants absent, swallow'd fire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And died so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Even so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O ye immortal gods!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter LUCIUS, with wine and taper

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Speak no more of her. Give me a bowl of wine.
In this I bury all unkindness, Cassius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My heart is thirsty for that noble pledge.
Fill, Lucius, till the wine o'erswell the cup;
I cannot drink too much of Brutus' love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come in, Titinius!
Welcome, good Messala.
Now sit we close about this taper here,
And call in question our necessities.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Portia, art thou gone?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No more, I pray you.
Messala, I have here received letters,
That young Octavius and Mark Antony
Come down upon us with a mighty power,
Bending their expedition toward Philippi.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Myself have letters of the selfsame tenor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: With what addition?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: That by proscription and bills of outlawry,
Octavius, Antony, and Lepidus,
Have put to death an hundred senators.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Therein our letters do not well agree;
Mine speak of seventy senators that died
By their proscriptions, Cicero being one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cicero one!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Cicero is dead,
And by that order of proscription.
Had you your letters from your wife, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, Messala.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Nor nothing in your letters writ of her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing, Messala.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: That, methinks, is strange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why ask you? hear you aught of her in yours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: No, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, as you are a Roman, tell me true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Then like a Roman bear the truth I tell:
For certain she is dead, and by strange manner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, farewell, Portia. We must die, Messala:
With meditating that she must die once,
I have the patience to endure it now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Even so great men great losses should endure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have as much of this in art as you,
But yet my nature could not bear it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, to our work alive. What do you think
Of marching to Philippi presently?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not think it good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your reason?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This it is:
'Tis better that the enemy seek us:
So shall he waste his means, weary his soldiers,
Doing himself offence; whilst we, lying still,
Are full of rest, defense, and nimbleness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good reasons must, of force, give place to better.
The people 'twixt Philippi and this ground
Do stand but in a forced affection;
For they have grudged us contribution:
The enemy, marching along by them,
By them shall make a fuller number up,
Come on refresh'd, new-added, and encouraged;
From which advantage shall we cut him off,
If at Philippi we do face him there,
These people at our back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, good brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Under your pardon. You must note beside,
That we have tried the utmost of our friends,
Our legions are brim-full, our cause is ripe:
The enemy increaseth every day;
We, at the height, are ready to decline.
There is a tide in the affairs of men,
Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune;
Omitted, all the voyage of their life
Is bound in shallows and in miseries.
On such a full sea are we now afloat;
And we must take the current when it serves,
Or lose our ventures.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then, with your will, go on;
We'll along ourselves, and meet them at Philippi.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: The deep of night is crept upon our talk,
And nature must obey necessity;
Which we will niggard with a little rest.
There is no more to say?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No more. Good night:
Early to-morrow will we rise, and hence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucius!
My gown.
Farewell, good Messala:
Good night, Titinius. Noble, noble Cassius,
Good night, and good repose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O my dear brother!
This was an ill beginning of the night:
Never come such division 'tween our souls!
Let it not, Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Every thing is well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, good brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITINIUS
MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, Lord Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, every one.
Give me the gown. Where is thy instrument?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here in the tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, thou speak'st drowsily?
Poor knave, I blame thee not; thou art o'er-watch'd.
Call Claudius and some other of my men:
I'll have them sleep on cushions in my tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Varro and Claudius!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
SPEECH.LINE: Calls my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, sirs, lie in my tent and sleep;
It may be I shall raise you by and by
On business to my brother Cassius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
SPEECH.LINE: So please you, we will stand and watch your pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I will not have it so: lie down, good sirs;
It may be I shall otherwise bethink me.
Look, Lucius, here's the book I sought for so;
I put it in the pocket of my gown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I was sure your lordship did not give it me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Bear with me, good boy, I am much forgetful.
Canst thou hold up thy heavy eyes awhile,
And touch thy instrument a strain or two?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my lord, an't please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: It does, my boy:
I trouble thee too much, but thou art willing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is my duty, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I should not urge thy duty past thy might;
I know young bloods look for a time of rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have slept, my lord, already.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: It was well done; and thou shalt sleep again;
I will not hold thee long: if I do live,
I will be good to thee.
This is a sleepy tune. O murderous slumber,
Lay'st thou thy leaden mace upon my boy,
That plays thee music? Gentle knave, good night;
I will not do thee so much wrong to wake thee:
If thou dost nod, thou break'st thy instrument;
I'll take it from thee; and, good boy, good night.
Let me see, let me see; is not the leaf turn'd down
Where I left reading? Here it is, I think.
How ill this taper burns! Ha! who comes here?
I think it is the weakness of mine eyes
That shapes this monstrous apparition.
It comes upon me. Art thou any thing?
Art thou some god, some angel, or some devil,
That makest my blood cold and my hair to stare?
Speak to me what thou art.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GHOST
SPEECH.LINE: Thy evil spirit, Brutus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why comest thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GHOST
SPEECH.LINE: To tell thee thou shalt see me at Philippi.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well; then I shall see thee again?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GHOST
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, at Philippi.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I will see thee at Philippi, then.
Now I have taken heart thou vanishest:
Ill spirit, I would hold more talk with thee.
Boy, Lucius! Varro! Claudius! Sirs, awake! Claudius!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: The strings, my lord, are false.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He thinks he still is at his instrument.
Lucius, awake!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Didst thou dream, Lucius, that thou so criedst out?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I do not know that I did cry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, that thou didst: didst thou see any thing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sleep again, Lucius. Sirrah Claudius!
Fellow thou, awake!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why did you so cry out, sirs, in your sleep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
CLAUDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Did we, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay: saw you any thing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
SPEECH.LINE: No, my lord, I saw nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go and commend me to my brother Cassius;
Bid him set on his powers betimes before,
And we will follow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VARRO
CLAUDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: It shall be done, my lord.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The plains of Philippi.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter OCTAVIUS, ANTONY, and their army

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Antony, our hopes are answered:
You said the enemy would not come down,
But keep the hills and upper regions;
It proves not so: their battles are at hand;
They mean to warn us at Philippi here,
Answering before we do demand of them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Tut, I am in their bosoms, and I know
Wherefore they do it: they could be content
To visit other places; and come down
With fearful bravery, thinking by this face
To fasten in our thoughts that they have courage;
But 'tis not so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Prepare you, generals:
The enemy comes on in gallant show;
Their bloody sign of battle is hung out,
And something to be done immediately.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Octavius, lead your battle softly on,
Upon the left hand of the even field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the right hand I; keep thou the left.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Why do you cross me in this exigent?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do not cross you; but I will do so.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Drum. Enter BRUTUS, CASSIUS, and their Army; LUCILIUS, TITINIUS, MESSALA, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: They stand, and would have parley.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand fast, Titinius: we must out and talk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mark Antony, shall we give sign of battle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: No, Caesar, we will answer on their charge.
Make forth; the generals would have some words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stir not until the signal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Words before blows: is it so, countrymen?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not that we love words better, as you do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good words are better than bad strokes, Octavius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: In your bad strokes, Brutus, you give good words:
Witness the hole you made in Caesar's heart,
Crying 'Long live! hail, Caesar!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Antony,
The posture of your blows are yet unknown;
But for your words, they rob the Hybla bees,
And leave them honeyless.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Not stingless too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, yes, and soundless too;
For you have stol'n their buzzing, Antony,
And very wisely threat before you sting.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Villains, you did not so, when your vile daggers
Hack'd one another in the sides of Caesar:
You show'd your teeth like apes, and fawn'd like hounds,
And bow'd like bondmen, kissing Caesar's feet;
Whilst damned Casca, like a cur, behind
Struck Caesar on the neck. O you flatterers!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Flatterers! Now, Brutus, thank yourself:
This tongue had not offended so to-day,
If Cassius might have ruled.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, the cause: if arguing make us sweat,
The proof of it will turn to redder drops. Look;
I draw a sword against conspirators;
When think you that the sword goes up again?
Never, till Caesar's three and thirty wounds
Be well avenged; or till another Caesar
Have added slaughter to the sword of traitors.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Caesar, thou canst not die by traitors' hands,
Unless thou bring'st them with thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: So I hope;
I was not born to die on Brutus' sword.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, if thou wert the noblest of thy strain,
Young man, thou couldst not die more honourable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: A peevish schoolboy, worthless of such honour,
Join'd with a masker and a reveller!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONY
SPEECH.LINE: Old Cassius still!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OCTAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Antony, away!
Defiance, traitors, hurl we in your teeth:
If you dare fight to-day, come to the field;
If not, when you have stomachs.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt OCTAVIUS, ANTONY, and their army

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, now, blow wind, swell billow and swim bark!
The storm is up, and all is on the hazard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ho, Lucilius! hark, a word with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Standing forth My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Messala!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Standing forth What says my general?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Messala,
This is my birth-day; as this very day
Was Cassius born. Give me thy hand, Messala:
Be thou my witness that against my will,
As Pompey was, am I compell'd to set
Upon one battle all our liberties.
You know that I held Epicurus strong
And his opinion: now I change my mind,
And partly credit things that do presage.
Coming from Sardis, on our former ensign
Two mighty eagles fell, and there they perch'd,
Gorging and feeding from our soldiers' hands;
Who to Philippi here consorted us:
This morning are they fled away and gone;
And in their steads do ravens, crows and kites,
Fly o'er our heads and downward look on us,
As we were sickly prey: their shadows seem
A canopy most fatal, under which
Our army lies, ready to give up the ghost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MESSALA
SPEECH.LINE: Believe not so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I but believe it partly;
For I am fresh of spirit and resolved
To meet all perils very constantly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Even so, Lucilius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, most noble Brutus,
The gods to-day stand friendly, that we may,
Lovers in peace, lead on our days to age!
But since the affairs of men rest still incertain,
Let's reason with the worst that may befall.
If we do lose this battle, then is this
The very last time we shall speak together:
What are you then determined to do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Even by the rule of that philosophy
By which I did blame Cato for the death
Which he did give himself, I know not how,
But I do find it cowardly and vile,
For fear of what might fall, so to prevent
The time of life: arming myself with patience
To stay the providence of some high powers
That govern us below.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then, if we lose this battle,
You are contented to be led in triumph
Thorough the streets of Rome?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, Cassius, no: think not, thou noble Roman,
That ever Brutus will go bound to Rome;
He bears too great a mind. But this same day
Must end that work the ides of March begun;
And whether we shall meet again I know not.
Therefore our everlasting farewell take:
For ever, and for ever, farewell, Cassius!
If we do meet again, why, we shall smile;
If not, why then, this parting was well made.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: For ever, and for ever, farewell, Brutus!
If we do meet again, we'll smile indeed;
If not, 'tis true this parting was well made.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, lead on. O, that a man might know
The end of this day's business ere it come!
But it sufficeth that the day will end,
And then the end is known. Come, ho! away!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. The field of battle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRUTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ride, ride, Messala, ride, and give these bills
Unto the legions on the other side.
Let them set on at once; for I perceive
But cold demeanor in Octavius' wing,
And sudden push gives them the overthrow.
Ride, ride, Messala: let them all come down.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Another part of the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, look, Titinius, look, the villains fly!
Myself have to mine own turn'd enemy:
This ensign here of mine was turning back;
I slew the coward, and did take it from him.
