Whilst I was big in clamour came there in a man,
Who, having seen me in my worst estate,
Shunn'd my abhorr'd society; but then, finding
Who 'twas that so endured, with his strong arms
He fastened on my neck, and bellow'd out
As he'ld burst heaven; threw him on my father;
Told the most piteous tale of Lear and him
That ever ear received: which in recounting
His grief grew puissant and the strings of life
Began to crack: twice then the trumpets sounded,
And there I left him tranced.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: But who was this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: Kent, sir, the banish'd Kent; who in disguise
Follow'd his enemy king, and did him service
Improper for a slave.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter a Gentleman, with a bloody knife

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Help, help, O, help!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: What kind of help?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Speak, man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: What means that bloody knife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis hot, it smokes;
It came even from the heart of--O, she's dead!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Who dead? speak, man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Your lady, sir, your lady: and her sister
By her is poisoned; she hath confess'd it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDMUND
SPEECH.LINE: I was contracted to them both: all three
Now marry in an instant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes Kent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Produce their bodies, be they alive or dead:
This judgment of the heavens, that makes us tremble,
Touches us not with pity.
O, is this he?
The time will not allow the compliment
Which very manners urges.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: I am come
To bid my king and master aye good night:
Is he not here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Great thing of us forgot!
Speak, Edmund, where's the king? and where's Cordelia?
See'st thou this object, Kent?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: The bodies of GONERIL and REGAN are brought in

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Alack, why thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDMUND
SPEECH.LINE: Yet Edmund was beloved:
The one the other poison'd for my sake,
And after slew herself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Even so. Cover their faces.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDMUND
SPEECH.LINE: I pant for life: some good I mean to do,
Despite of mine own nature. Quickly send,
Be brief in it, to the castle; for my writ
Is on the life of Lear and on Cordelia:
Nay, send in time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Run, run, O, run!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: To who, my lord? Who hath the office? send
Thy token of reprieve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDMUND
SPEECH.LINE: Well thought on: take my sword,
Give it the captain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Haste thee, for thy life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDMUND
SPEECH.LINE: He hath commission from thy wife and me
To hang Cordelia in the prison, and
To lay the blame upon her own despair,
That she fordid herself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: The gods defend her! Bear him hence awhile.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter KING LEAR, with CORDELIA dead in his arms; EDGAR, Captain, and others following

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: Howl, howl, howl, howl! O, you are men of stones:
Had I your tongues and eyes, I'ld use them so
That heaven's vault should crack. She's gone for ever!
I know when one is dead, and when one lives;
She's dead as earth. Lend me a looking-glass;
If that her breath will mist or stain the stone,
Why, then she lives.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Is this the promised end

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: Or image of that horror?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Fall, and cease!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: This feather stirs; she lives! if it be so,
It is a chance which does redeem all sorrows
That ever I have felt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Kneeling O my good master!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis noble Kent, your friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: A plague upon you, murderers, traitors all!
I might have saved her; now she's gone for ever!
Cordelia, Cordelia! stay a little. Ha!
What is't thou say'st? Her voice was ever soft,
Gentle, and low, an excellent thing in woman.
I kill'd the slave that was a-hanging thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true, my lords, he did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: Did I not, fellow?
I have seen the day, with my good biting falchion
I would have made them skip: I am old now,
And these same crosses spoil me. Who are you?
Mine eyes are not o' the best: I'll tell you straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: If fortune brag of two she loved and hated,
One of them we behold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: This is a dull sight. Are you not Kent?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: The same,
Your servant Kent: Where is your servant Caius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: He's a good fellow, I can tell you that;
He'll strike, and quickly too: he's dead and rotten.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord; I am the very man,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: I'll see that straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: That, from your first of difference and decay,
Have follow'd your sad steps.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: You are welcome hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Nor no man else: all's cheerless, dark, and deadly.
Your eldest daughters have fordone them selves,
And desperately are dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, so I think.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: He knows not what he says: and vain it is
That we present us to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: Very bootless.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: Edmund is dead, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: That's but a trifle here.
You lords and noble friends, know our intent.
What comfort to this great decay may come
Shall be applied: for us we will resign,
During the life of this old majesty,
To him our absolute power:
you, to your rights:
With boot, and such addition as your honours
Have more than merited. All friends shall taste
The wages of their virtue, and all foes
The cup of their deservings. O, see, see!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING LEAR
SPEECH.LINE: And my poor fool is hang'd! No, no, no life!
Why should a dog, a horse, a rat, have life,
And thou no breath at all? Thou'lt come no more,
Never, never, never, never, never!
Pray you, undo this button: thank you, sir.
Do you see this? Look on her, look, her lips,
Look there, look there!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: He faints! My lord, my lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Break, heart; I prithee, break!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: Look up, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: Vex not his ghost: O, let him pass! he hates him much
That would upon the rack of this tough world
Stretch him out longer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: EDGAR
SPEECH.LINE: He is gone, indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: The wonder is, he hath endured so long:
He but usurp'd his life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: Bear them from hence. Our present business
Is general woe.
Friends of my soul, you twain
Rule in this realm, and the gored state sustain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KENT
SPEECH.LINE: I have a journey, sir, shortly to go;
My master calls me, I must not say no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALBANY
SPEECH.LINE: The weight of this sad time we must obey;
Speak what we feel, not what we ought to say.
The oldest hath borne most: we that are young
Shall never see so much, nor live so long.

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: lords attending on the Princess of France.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO, a fantastical Spaniard.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The king of Navarre's park.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FERDINAND king of Navarre, BIRON, LONGAVILLE and DUMAIN

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Let fame, that all hunt after in their lives,
Live register'd upon our brazen tombs
And then grace us in the disgrace of death;
When, spite of cormorant devouring Time,
The endeavor of this present breath may buy
That honour which shall bate his scythe's keen edge
And make us heirs of all eternity.
Therefore, brave conquerors,--for so you are,
That war against your own affections
And the huge army of the world's desires,--
Our late edict shall strongly stand in force:
Navarre shall be the wonder of the world;
Our court shall be a little Academe,
Still and contemplative in living art.
You three, Biron, Dumain, and Longaville,
Have sworn for three years' term to live with me
My fellow-scholars, and to keep those statutes
That are recorded in this schedule here:
Your oaths are pass'd; and now subscribe your names,
That his own hand may strike his honour down
That violates the smallest branch herein:
If you are arm'd to do as sworn to do,
Subscribe to your deep oaths, and keep it too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: I am resolved; 'tis but a three years' fast:
The mind shall banquet, though the body pine:
Fat paunches have lean pates, and dainty bits
Make rich the ribs, but bankrupt quite the wits.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: My loving lord, Dumain is mortified:
The grosser manner of these world's delights
He throws upon the gross world's baser slaves:
To love, to wealth, to pomp, I pine and die;
With all these living in philosophy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I can but say their protestation over;
So much, dear liege, I have already sworn,
That is, to live and study here three years.
But there are other strict observances;
As, not to see a woman in that term,
Which I hope well is not enrolled there;
And one day in a week to touch no food
And but one meal on every day beside,
The which I hope is not enrolled there;
And then, to sleep but three hours in the night,
And not be seen to wink of all the day--
When I was wont to think no harm all night
And make a dark night too of half the day--
Which I hope well is not enrolled there:
O, these are barren tasks, too hard to keep,
Not to see ladies, study, fast, not sleep!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Your oath is pass'd to pass away from these.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Let me say no, my liege, an if you please:
I only swore to study with your grace
And stay here in your court for three years' space.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: You swore to that, Biron, and to the rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: By yea and nay, sir, then I swore in jest.
What is the end of study? let me know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Why, that to know, which else we should not know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Things hid and barr'd, you mean, from common sense?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that is study's godlike recompense.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, then; I will swear to study so,
To know the thing I am forbid to know:
As thus,--to study where I well may dine,
When I to feast expressly am forbid;
Or study where to meet some mistress fine,
When mistresses from common sense are hid;
Or, having sworn too hard a keeping oath,
Study to break it and not break my troth.
If study's gain be thus and this be so,
Study knows that which yet it doth not know:
Swear me to this, and I will ne'er say no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: These be the stops that hinder study quite
And train our intellects to vain delight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, all delights are vain; but that most vain,
Which with pain purchased doth inherit pain:
As, painfully to pore upon a book
To seek the light of truth; while truth the while
Doth falsely blind the eyesight of his look:
Light seeking light doth light of light beguile:
So, ere you find where light in darkness lies,
Your light grows dark by losing of your eyes.
Study me how to please the eye indeed
By fixing it upon a fairer eye,
Who dazzling so, that eye shall be his heed
And give him light that it was blinded by.
Study is like the heaven's glorious sun
That will not be deep-search'd with saucy looks:
Small have continual plodders ever won
Save base authority from others' books
These earthly godfathers of heaven's lights
That give a name to every fixed star
Have no more profit of their shining nights
Than those that walk and wot not what they are.
Too much to know is to know nought but fame;
And every godfather can give a name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: How well he's read, to reason against reading!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: Proceeded well, to stop all good proceeding!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: He weeds the corn and still lets grow the weeding.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: The spring is near when green geese are a-breeding.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: How follows that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Fit in his place and time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: In reason nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Something then in rhyme.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Biron is like an envious sneaping frost,
That bites the first-born infants of the spring.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Well, say I am; why should proud summer boast
Before the birds have any cause to sing?
Why should I joy in any abortive birth?
At Christmas I no more desire a rose
Than wish a snow in May's new-fangled mirth;
But like of each thing that in season grows.
So you, to study now it is too late,
Climb o'er the house to unlock the little gate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sit you out: go home, Biron: adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord; I have sworn to stay with you:
And though I have for barbarism spoke more
Than for that angel knowledge you can say,
Yet confident I'll keep what I have swore
And bide the penance of each three years' day.
Give me the paper; let me read the same;
And to the strict'st decrees I'll write my name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: How well this yielding rescues thee from shame!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'Item, That no woman shall come within a
mile of my court:' Hath this been proclaimed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Four days ago.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Let's see the penalty.
'On pain of losing her tongue.' Who devised this penalty?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, that did I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet lord, and why?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: To fright them hence with that dread penalty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: A dangerous law against gentility!
'Item, If any man be seen to talk with a woman
within the term of three years, he shall endure such
public shame as the rest of the court can possibly devise.'
This article, my liege, yourself must break;
For well you know here comes in embassy
The French king's daughter with yourself to speak--
A maid of grace and complete majesty--
About surrender up of Aquitaine
To her decrepit, sick and bedrid father:
Therefore this article is made in vain,
Or vainly comes the admired princess hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: What say you, lords? Why, this was quite forgot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: So study evermore is overshot:
While it doth study to have what it would
It doth forget to do the thing it should,
And when it hath the thing it hunteth most,
'Tis won as towns with fire, so won, so lost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: We must of force dispense with this decree;
She must lie here on mere necessity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Necessity will make us all forsworn
Three thousand times within this three years' space;
For every man with his affects is born,
Not by might master'd but by special grace:
If I break faith, this word shall speak for me;
I am forsworn on 'mere necessity.'
So to the laws at large I write my name:
And he that breaks them in the least degree
Stands in attainder of eternal shame:
Suggestions are to other as to me;
But I believe, although I seem so loath,
I am the last that will last keep his oath.
But is there no quick recreation granted?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that there is. Our court, you know, is haunted
With a refined traveller of Spain;
A man in all the world's new fashion planted,
That hath a mint of phrases in his brain;
One whom the music of his own vain tongue
Doth ravish like enchanting harmony;
A man of complements, whom right and wrong
Have chose as umpire of their mutiny:
This child of fancy, that Armado hight,
For interim to our studies shall relate
In high-born words the worth of many a knight
From tawny Spain lost in the world's debate.
How you delight, my lords, I know not, I;
But, I protest, I love to hear him lie
And I will use him for my minstrelsy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Armado is a most illustrious wight,
A man of fire-new words, fashion's own knight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Costard the swain and he shall be our sport;
And so to study, three years is but short.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DULL with a letter, and COSTARD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: Which is the duke's own person?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: This, fellow: what wouldst?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: I myself reprehend his own person, for I am his
grace's tharborough: but I would see his own person
in flesh and blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: This is he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: Signior Arme--Arme--commends you. There's villany
abroad: this letter will tell you more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, the contempts thereof are as touching me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: A letter from the magnificent Armado.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: How low soever the matter, I hope in God for high words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: A high hope for a low heaven: God grant us patience!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: To hear? or forbear laughing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: To hear meekly, sir, and to laugh moderately; or to
forbear both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, be it as the style shall give us cause to
climb in the merriness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: The matter is to me, sir, as concerning Jaquenetta.
The manner of it is, I was taken with the manner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: In what manner?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: In manner and form following, sir; all those three:
I was seen with her in the manor-house, sitting with
her upon the form, and taken following her into the
park; which, put together, is in manner and form
following. Now, sir, for the manner,--it is the
manner of a man to speak to a woman: for the form,--
in some form.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: For the following, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: As it shall follow in my correction: and God defend
the right!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Will you hear this letter with attention?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: As we would hear an oracle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Such is the simplicity of man to hearken after the flesh.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'Great deputy, the welkin's vicegerent and
sole dominator of Navarre, my soul's earth's god,
and body's fostering patron.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Not a word of Costard yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'So it is,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: It may be so: but if he say it is so, he is, in
telling true, but so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Be to me and every man that dares not fight!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: No words!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Of other men's secrets, I beseech you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'So it is, besieged with sable-coloured
melancholy, I did commend the black-oppressing humour
to the most wholesome physic of thy health-giving
air; and, as I am a gentleman, betook myself to
walk. The time when. About the sixth hour; when
beasts most graze, birds best peck, and men sit down
to that nourishment which is called supper: so much
for the time when. Now for the ground which; which,
I mean, I walked upon: it is y-cleped thy park. Then
for the place where; where, I mean, I did encounter
that obscene and preposterous event, that draweth
from my snow-white pen the ebon-coloured ink, which
here thou viewest, beholdest, surveyest, or seest;
but to the place where; it standeth north-north-east
and by east from the west corner of thy curious-
knotted garden: there did I see that low-spirited
swain, that base minnow of thy mirth,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'that unlettered small-knowing soul,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'that shallow vassal,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Still me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'which, as I remember, hight Costard,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: O, me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'sorted and consorted, contrary to thy
established proclaimed edict and continent canon,
which with,--O, with--but with this I passion to say
wherewith,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: With a wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'with a child of our grandmother Eve, a
female; or, for thy more sweet understanding, a
woman. Him I, as my ever-esteemed duty pricks me on,
have sent to thee, to receive the meed of
punishment, by thy sweet grace's officer, Anthony
Dull; a man of good repute, carriage, bearing, and
estimation.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: 'Me, an't shall please you; I am Anthony Dull.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'For Jaquenetta,--so is the weaker vessel
called which I apprehended with the aforesaid
swain,--I keep her as a vessel of the law's fury;
and shall, at the least of thy sweet notice, bring
her to trial. Thine, in all compliments of devoted
and heart-burning heat of duty.
DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: This is not so well as I looked for, but the best
that ever I heard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, the best for the worst. But, sirrah, what say
you to this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I confess the wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Did you hear the proclamation?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I do confess much of the hearing it but little of
the marking of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: It was proclaimed a year's imprisonment, to be taken
with a wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I was taken with none, sir: I was taken with a damsel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Well, it was proclaimed 'damsel.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: This was no damsel, neither, sir; she was a virgin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: It is so varied, too; for it was proclaimed 'virgin.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: If it were, I deny her virginity: I was taken with a maid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: This maid will not serve your turn, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: This maid will serve my turn, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I will pronounce your sentence: you shall fast
a week with bran and water.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I had rather pray a month with mutton and porridge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: And Don Armado shall be your keeper.
My Lord Biron, see him deliver'd o'er:
And go we, lords, to put in practise that
Which each to other hath so strongly sworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I'll lay my head to any good man's hat,
These oaths and laws will prove an idle scorn.
Sirrah, come on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I suffer for the truth, sir; for true it is, I was
taken with Jaquenetta, and Jaquenetta is a true
girl; and therefore welcome the sour cup of
prosperity! Affliction may one day smile again; and
till then, sit thee down, sorrow!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO and MOTH

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Boy, what sign is it when a man of great spirit
grows melancholy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A great sign, sir, that he will look sad.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, sadness is one and the self-same thing, dear imp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: No, no; O Lord, sir, no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: How canst thou part sadness and melancholy, my
tender juvenal?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: By a familiar demonstration of the working, my tough senior.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Why tough senior? why tough senior?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Why tender juvenal? why tender juvenal?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I spoke it, tender juvenal, as a congruent epitheton
appertaining to thy young days, which we may
nominate tender.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: And I, tough senior, as an appertinent title to your
old time, which we may name tough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Pretty and apt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: How mean you, sir? I pretty, and my saying apt? or
I apt, and my saying pretty?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou pretty, because little.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Little pretty, because little. Wherefore apt?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: And therefore apt, because quick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Speak you this in my praise, master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: In thy condign praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: I will praise an eel with the same praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: What, that an eel is ingenious?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: That an eel is quick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I do say thou art quick in answers: thou heatest my blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: I am answered, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I love not to be crossed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Aside He speaks the mere contrary; crosses love not him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I have promised to study three years with the duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: You may do it in an hour, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Impossible.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: How many is one thrice told?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I am ill at reckoning; it fitteth the spirit of a tapster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: You are a gentleman and a gamester, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I confess both: they are both the varnish of a
complete man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Then, I am sure, you know how much the gross sum of
deuce-ace amounts to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: It doth amount to one more than two.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Which the base vulgar do call three.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: True.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Why, sir, is this such a piece of study? Now here
is three studied, ere ye'll thrice wink: and how
easy it is to put 'years' to the word 'three,' and
study three years in two words, the dancing horse
will tell you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: A most fine figure!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: To prove you a cipher.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I will hereupon confess I am in love: and as it is
base for a soldier to love, so am I in love with a
base wench. If drawing my sword against the humour
of affection would deliver me from the reprobate
thought of it, I would take Desire prisoner, and
ransom him to any French courtier for a new-devised
courtesy. I think scorn to sigh: methinks I should
outswear Cupid. Comfort, me, boy: what great men
have been in love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Hercules, master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Most sweet Hercules! More authority, dear boy, name
more; and, sweet my child, let them be men of good
repute and carriage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Samson, master: he was a man of good carriage, great
carriage, for he carried the town-gates on his back
like a porter: and he was in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: O well-knit Samson! strong-jointed Samson! I do
excel thee in my rapier as much as thou didst me in
carrying gates. I am in love too. Who was Samson's
love, my dear Moth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A woman, master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Of what complexion?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Of all the four, or the three, or the two, or one of the four.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me precisely of what complexion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Of the sea-water green, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Is that one of the four complexions?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: As I have read, sir; and the best of them too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Green indeed is the colour of lovers; but to have a
love of that colour, methinks Samson had small reason
for it. He surely affected her for her wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: It was so, sir; for she had a green wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: My love is most immaculate white and red.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Most maculate thoughts, master, are masked under
such colours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Define, define, well-educated infant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: My father's wit and my mother's tongue, assist me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet invocation of a child; most pretty and
pathetical!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: If she be made of white and red,
Her faults will ne'er be known,
For blushing cheeks by faults are bred
And fears by pale white shown:
Then if she fear, or be to blame,
By this you shall not know,
For still her cheeks possess the same
Which native she doth owe.
A dangerous rhyme, master, against the reason of
white and red.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Is there not a ballad, boy, of the King and the Beggar?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: The world was very guilty of such a ballad some
three ages since: but I think now 'tis not to be
found; or, if it were, it would neither serve for
the writing nor the tune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I will have that subject newly writ o'er, that I may
example my digression by some mighty precedent.
Boy, I do love that country girl that I took in the
park with the rational hind Costard: she deserves well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Aside To be whipped; and yet a better love than
my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Sing, boy; my spirit grows heavy in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: And that's great marvel, loving a light wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I say, sing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Forbear till this company be past.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, the duke's pleasure is, that you keep Costard
safe: and you must suffer him to take no delight
nor no penance; but a' must fast three days a week.
For this damsel, I must keep her at the park: she
is allowed for the day-woman. Fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I do betray myself with blushing. Maid!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I will visit thee at the lodge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: That's hereby.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I know where it is situate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Lord, how wise you are!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I will tell thee wonders.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: With that face?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I love thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: So I heard you say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: And so, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Fair weather after you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Jaquenetta, away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Villain, thou shalt fast for thy offences ere thou
be pardoned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, I hope, when I do it, I shall do it on a
full stomach.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt be heavily punished.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I am more bound to you than your fellows, for they
are but lightly rewarded.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Take away this villain; shut him up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Come, you transgressing slave; away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Let me not be pent up, sir: I will fast, being loose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir; that were fast and loose: thou shalt to prison.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Well, if ever I do see the merry days of desolation
that I have seen, some shall see.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: What shall some see?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, nothing, Master Moth, but what they look upon.
It is not for prisoners to be too silent in their
words; and therefore I will say nothing: I thank
God I have as little patience as another man; and
therefore I can be quiet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I do affect the very ground, which is base, where
her shoe, which is baser, guided by her foot, which
is basest, doth tread. I shall be forsworn, which
is a great argument of falsehood, if I love. And
how can that be true love which is falsely
attempted? Love is a familiar; Love is a devil:
there is no evil angel but Love. Yet was Samson so
tempted, and he had an excellent strength; yet was
Solomon so seduced, and he had a very good wit.
Cupid's butt-shaft is too hard for Hercules' club;
and therefore too much odds for a Spaniard's rapier.
The first and second cause will not serve my turn;
the passado he respects not, the duello he regards
not: his disgrace is to be called boy; but his
glory is to subdue men. Adieu, valour! rust rapier!
be still, drum! for your manager is in love; yea,
he loveth. Assist me, some extemporal god of rhyme,
for I am sure I shall turn sonnet. Devise, wit;
write, pen; for I am for whole volumes in folio.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The same.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the PRINCESS of France, ROSALINE, MARIA, KATHARINE, BOYET, Lords, and other Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Now, madam, summon up your dearest spirits:
Consider who the king your father sends,
To whom he sends, and what's his embassy:
Yourself, held precious in the world's esteem,
To parley with the sole inheritor
Of all perfections that a man may owe,
Matchless Navarre; the plea of no less weight
Than Aquitaine, a dowry for a queen.
Be now as prodigal of all dear grace
As Nature was in making graces dear
When she did starve the general world beside
And prodigally gave them all to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Good Lord Boyet, my beauty, though but mean,
Needs not the painted flourish of your praise:
Beauty is bought by judgement of the eye,
Not utter'd by base sale of chapmen's tongues:
I am less proud to hear you tell my worth
Than you much willing to be counted wise
In spending your wit in the praise of mine.
But now to task the tasker: good Boyet,
You are not ignorant, all-telling fame
Doth noise abroad, Navarre hath made a vow,
Till painful study shall outwear three years,
No woman may approach his silent court:
Therefore to's seemeth it a needful course,
Before we enter his forbidden gates,
To know his pleasure; and in that behalf,
Bold of your worthiness, we single you
As our best-moving fair solicitor.
Tell him, the daughter of the King of France,
On serious business, craving quick dispatch,
Importunes personal conference with his grace:
Haste, signify so much; while we attend,
Like humble-visaged suitors, his high will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Proud of employment, willingly I go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: All pride is willing pride, and yours is so.
Who are the votaries, my loving lords,
That are vow-fellows with this virtuous duke?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Longaville is one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Know you the man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: I know him, madam: at a marriage-feast,
Between Lord Perigort and the beauteous heir
Of Jaques Falconbridge, solemnized
In Normandy, saw I this Longaville:
A man of sovereign parts he is esteem'd;
Well fitted in arts, glorious in arms:
Nothing becomes him ill that he would well.
The only soil of his fair virtue's gloss,
If virtue's gloss will stain with any soil,
Is a sharp wit matched with too blunt a will;
Whose edge hath power to cut, whose will still wills
It should none spare that come within his power.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Some merry mocking lord, belike; is't so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: They say so most that most his humours know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Such short-lived wits do wither as they grow.
Who are the rest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINE
SPEECH.LINE: The young Dumain, a well-accomplished youth,
Of all that virtue love for virtue loved:
Most power to do most harm, least knowing ill;
For he hath wit to make an ill shape good,
And shape to win grace though he had no wit.
I saw him at the Duke Alencon's once;
And much too little of that good I saw
Is my report to his great worthiness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Another of these students at that time
Was there with him, if I have heard a truth.
Biron they call him; but a merrier man,
Within the limit of becoming mirth,
I never spent an hour's talk withal:
His eye begets occasion for his wit;
For every object that the one doth catch
The other turns to a mirth-moving jest,
Which his fair tongue, conceit's expositor,
Delivers in such apt and gracious words
That aged ears play truant at his tales
And younger hearings are quite ravished;
So sweet and voluble is his discourse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: God bless my ladies! are they all in love,
That every one her own hath garnished
With such bedecking ornaments of praise?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes Boyet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, what admittance, lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Navarre had notice of your fair approach;
And he and his competitors in oath
Were all address'd to meet you, gentle lady,
Before I came. Marry, thus much I have learnt:
He rather means to lodge you in the field,
Like one that comes here to besiege his court,
Than seek a dispensation for his oath,
To let you enter his unpeopled house.
Here comes Navarre.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FERDINAND, LONGAVILLE, DUMAIN, BIRON, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Fair princess, welcome to the court of Navarre.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Fair' I give you back again; and 'welcome' I have
not yet: the roof of this court is too high to be
yours; and welcome to the wide fields too base to be mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: You shall be welcome, madam, to my court.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: I will be welcome, then: conduct me thither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, dear lady; I have sworn an oath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Our Lady help my lord! he'll be forsworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Not for the world, fair madam, by my will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, will shall break it; will and nothing else.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Your ladyship is ignorant what it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Were my lord so, his ignorance were wise,
Where now his knowledge must prove ignorance.
I hear your grace hath sworn out house-keeping:
Tis deadly sin to keep that oath, my lord,
And sin to break it.
But pardon me. I am too sudden-bold:
To teach a teacher ill beseemeth me.
Vouchsafe to read the purpose of my coming,
And suddenly resolve me in my suit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, I will, if suddenly I may.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: You will the sooner, that I were away;
For you'll prove perjured if you make me stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I know you did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: How needless was it then to ask the question!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: You must not be so quick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis 'long of you that spur me with such questions.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Your wit's too hot, it speeds too fast, 'twill tire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Not till it leave the rider in the mire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: What time o' day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: The hour that fools should ask.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Now fair befall your mask!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Fair fall the face it covers!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: And send you many lovers!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Amen, so you be none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, then will I be gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, your father here doth intimate
The payment of a hundred thousand crowns;
Being but the one half of an entire sum
Disbursed by my father in his wars.
But say that he or we, as neither have,
Received that sum, yet there remains unpaid
A hundred thousand more; in surety of the which,
One part of Aquitaine is bound to us,
Although not valued to the money's worth.
If then the king your father will restore
But that one half which is unsatisfied,
We will give up our right in Aquitaine,
And hold fair friendship with his majesty.
But that, it seems, he little purposeth,
For here he doth demand to have repaid
A hundred thousand crowns; and not demands,
On payment of a hundred thousand crowns,
To have his title live in Aquitaine;
Which we much rather had depart withal
And have the money by our father lent
Than Aquitaine so gelded as it is.
Dear Princess, were not his requests so far
From reason's yielding, your fair self should make
A yielding 'gainst some reason in my breast
And go well satisfied to France again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: You do the king my father too much wrong
And wrong the reputation of your name,
In so unseeming to confess receipt
Of that which hath so faithfully been paid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: I do protest I never heard of it;
And if you prove it, I'll repay it back
Or yield up Aquitaine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: We arrest your word.
Boyet, you can produce acquittances
For such a sum from special officers
Of Charles his father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Satisfy me so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: So please your grace, the packet is not come
Where that and other specialties are bound:
To-morrow you shall have a sight of them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: It shall suffice me: at which interview
All liberal reason I will yield unto.
Meantime receive such welcome at my hand
As honour without breach of honour may
Make tender of to thy true worthiness:
You may not come, fair princess, in my gates;
But here without you shall be so received
As you shall deem yourself lodged in my heart,
Though so denied fair harbour in my house.
Your own good thoughts excuse me, and farewell:
To-morrow shall we visit you again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet health and fair desires consort your grace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Thy own wish wish I thee in every place!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Lady, I will commend you to mine own heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, do my commendations; I would be glad to see it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I would you heard it groan.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Is the fool sick?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Sick at the heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Alack, let it blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Would that do it good?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: My physic says 'ay.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Will you prick't with your eye?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: No point, with my knife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Now, God save thy life!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: And yours from long living!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot stay thanksgiving.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I pray you, a word: what lady is that same?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: The heir of Alencon, Katharine her name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUMAIN
SPEECH.LINE: A gallant lady. Monsieur, fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you a word: what is she in the white?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: A woman sometimes, an you saw her in the light.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Perchance light in the light. I desire her name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: She hath but one for herself; to desire that were a shame.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, sir, whose daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Her mother's, I have heard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: God's blessing on your beard!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Good sir, be not offended.
She is an heir of Falconbridge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LONGAVILLE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, my choler is ended.
She is a most sweet lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Not unlike, sir, that may be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: What's her name in the cap?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Rosaline, by good hap.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Is she wedded or no?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: To her will, sir, or so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: You are welcome, sir: adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell to me, sir, and welcome to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: That last is Biron, the merry madcap lord:
Not a word with him but a jest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: And every jest but a word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: It was well done of you to take him at his word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: I was as willing to grapple as he was to board.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Two hot sheeps, marry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: And wherefore not ships?
No sheep, sweet lamb, unless we feed on your lips.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: You sheep, and I pasture: shall that finish the jest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: So you grant pasture for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Not so, gentle beast:
My lips are no common, though several they be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Belonging to whom?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: To my fortunes and me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Good wits will be jangling; but, gentles, agree:
This civil war of wits were much better used
On Navarre and his book-men; for here 'tis abused.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: If my observation, which very seldom lies,
By the heart's still rhetoric disclosed with eyes,
Deceive me not now, Navarre is infected.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: With what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: With that which we lovers entitle affected.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Your reason?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Why, all his behaviors did make their retire
To the court of his eye, peeping thorough desire:
His heart, like an agate, with your print impress'd,
Proud with his form, in his eye pride express'd:
His tongue, all impatient to speak and not see,
Did stumble with haste in his eyesight to be;
All senses to that sense did make their repair,
To feel only looking on fairest of fair:
Methought all his senses were lock'd in his eye,
As jewels in crystal for some prince to buy;
Who, tendering their own worth from where they were glass'd,
Did point you to buy them, along as you pass'd:
His face's own margent did quote such amazes
That all eyes saw his eyes enchanted with gazes.
I'll give you Aquitaine and all that is his,
An you give him for my sake but one loving kiss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Come to our pavilion: Boyet is disposed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: But to speak that in words which his eye hath
disclosed.
I only have made a mouth of his eye,
By adding a tongue which I know will not lie.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art an old love-monger and speakest skilfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: He is Cupid's grandfather and learns news of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Then was Venus like her mother, for her father is but grim.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear, my mad wenches?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: What then, do you see?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, our way to be gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: You are too hard for me.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The same.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO and MOTH

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Warble, child; make passionate my sense of hearing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Concolinel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet air! Go, tenderness of years; take this key,
give enlargement to the swain, bring him festinately
hither: I must employ him in a letter to my love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Master, will you win your love with a French brawl?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: How meanest thou? brawling in French?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: No, my complete master: but to jig off a tune at
the tongue's end, canary to it with your feet, humour
it with turning up your eyelids, sigh a note and
sing a note, sometime through the throat, as if you
swallowed love with singing love, sometime through
the nose, as if you snuffed up love by smelling
love; with your hat penthouse-like o'er the shop of
your eyes; with your arms crossed on your thin-belly
doublet like a rabbit on a spit; or your hands in
your pocket like a man after the old painting; and
keep not too long in one tune, but a snip and away.
These are complements, these are humours; these
betray nice wenches, that would be betrayed without
these; and make them men of note--do you note
me?--that most are affected to these.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: How hast thou purchased this experience?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: By my penny of observation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: But O,--but O,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: 'The hobby-horse is forgot.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Callest thou my love 'hobby-horse'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: No, master; the hobby-horse is but a colt, and your
love perhaps a hackney. But have you forgot your love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Almost I had.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Negligent student! learn her by heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: By heart and in heart, boy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: And out of heart, master: all those three I will prove.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: What wilt thou prove?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A man, if I live; and this, by, in, and without, upon
the instant: by heart you love her, because your
heart cannot come by her; in heart you love her,
because your heart is in love with her; and out of
heart you love her, being out of heart that you
cannot enjoy her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I am all these three.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: And three times as much more, and yet nothing at
all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Fetch hither the swain: he must carry me a letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A message well sympathized; a horse to be ambassador
for an ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha! what sayest thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, you must send the ass upon the horse,
for he is very slow-gaited. But I go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: The way is but short: away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: As swift as lead, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: The meaning, pretty ingenious?
Is not lead a metal heavy, dull, and slow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Minime, honest master; or rather, master, no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I say lead is slow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: You are too swift, sir, to say so:
Is that lead slow which is fired from a gun?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet smoke of rhetoric!
He reputes me a cannon; and the bullet, that's he:
I shoot thee at the swain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Thump then and I flee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: A most acute juvenal; voluble and free of grace!
By thy favour, sweet welkin, I must sigh in thy face:
Most rude melancholy, valour gives thee place.
My herald is return'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A wonder, master! here's a costard broken in a shin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Some enigma, some riddle: come, thy l'envoy; begin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: No enigma, no riddle, no l'envoy; no salve in the
mail, sir: O, sir, plantain, a plain plantain! no
l'envoy, no l'envoy; no salve, sir, but a plantain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: By virtue, thou enforcest laughter; thy silly
thought my spleen; the heaving of my lungs provokes
me to ridiculous smiling. O, pardon me, my stars!
Doth the inconsiderate take salve for l'envoy, and
the word l'envoy for a salve?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Do the wise think them other? is not l'envoy a salve?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: No, page: it is an epilogue or discourse, to make plain
Some obscure precedence that hath tofore been sain.
I will example it:
The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee,
Were still at odds, being but three.
There's the moral. Now the l'envoy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: I will add the l'envoy. Say the moral again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee,
Were still at odds, being but three.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Until the goose came out of door,
And stay'd the odds by adding four.
Now will I begin your moral, and do you follow with
my l'envoy.
The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee,
Were still at odds, being but three.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Until the goose came out of door,
Staying the odds by adding four.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: A good l'envoy, ending in the goose: would you
desire more?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: The boy hath sold him a bargain, a goose, that's flat.
Sir, your pennyworth is good, an your goose be fat.
To sell a bargain well is as cunning as fast and loose:
Let me see; a fat l'envoy; ay, that's a fat goose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, come hither. How did this argument begin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: By saying that a costard was broken in a shin.
Then call'd you for the l'envoy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: True, and I for a plantain: thus came your
argument in;
Then the boy's fat l'envoy, the goose that you bought;
And he ended the market.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: But tell me; how was there a costard broken in a shin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: I will tell you sensibly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast no feeling of it, Moth: I will speak that l'envoy:
I Costard, running out, that was safely within,
Fell over the threshold and broke my shin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: We will talk no more of this matter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Till there be more matter in the shin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah Costard, I will enfranchise thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: O, marry me to one Frances: I smell some l'envoy,
some goose, in this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: By my sweet soul, I mean setting thee at liberty,
enfreedoming thy person; thou wert immured,
restrained, captivated, bound.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: True, true; and now you will be my purgation and let me loose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO
SPEECH.LINE: I give thee thy liberty, set thee from durance; and,
in lieu thereof, impose on thee nothing but this:
bear this significant
to the country maid Jaquenetta:
there is remuneration; for the best ward of mine
honour is rewarding my dependents. Moth, follow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOTH
SPEECH.LINE: Like the sequel, I. Signior Costard, adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: My sweet ounce of man's flesh! my incony Jew!
Now will I look to his remuneration. Remuneration!
O, that's the Latin word for three farthings: three
farthings--remuneration.--'What's the price of this
inkle?'--'One penny.'--'No, I'll give you a
remuneration:' why, it carries it. Remuneration!
why, it is a fairer name than French crown. I will
never buy and sell out of this word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: O, my good knave Costard! exceedingly well met.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, sir, how much carnation ribbon may a man
buy for a remuneration?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: What is a remuneration?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, halfpenny farthing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, three-farthing worth of silk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your worship: God be wi' you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, slave; I must employ thee:
As thou wilt win my favour, good my knave,
Do one thing for me that I shall entreat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: When would you have it done, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: This afternoon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will do it, sir: fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Thou knowest not what it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I shall know, sir, when I have done it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, villain, thou must know first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I will come to your worship to-morrow morning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: It must be done this afternoon.
Hark, slave, it is but this:
The princess comes to hunt here in the park,
And in her train there is a gentle lady;
When tongues speak sweetly, then they name her name,
And Rosaline they call her: ask for her;
And to her white hand see thou do commend
This seal'd-up counsel. There's thy guerdon; go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Gardon, O sweet gardon! better than remuneration,
a'leven-pence farthing better: most sweet gardon! I
will do it sir, in print. Gardon! Remuneration!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: And I, forsooth, in love! I, that have been love's whip;
A very beadle to a humorous sigh;
A critic, nay, a night-watch constable;
A domineering pedant o'er the boy;
Than whom no mortal so magnificent!
This whimpled, whining, purblind, wayward boy;
This senior-junior, giant-dwarf, Dan Cupid;
Regent of love-rhymes, lord of folded arms,
The anointed sovereign of sighs and groans,
Liege of all loiterers and malcontents,
Dread prince of plackets, king of codpieces,
Sole imperator and great general
Of trotting 'paritors:--O my little heart:--
And I to be a corporal of his field,
And wear his colours like a tumbler's hoop!
What, I! I love! I sue! I seek a wife!
A woman, that is like a German clock,
Still a-repairing, ever out of frame,
And never going aright, being a watch,
But being watch'd that it may still go right!
Nay, to be perjured, which is worst of all;
And, among three, to love the worst of all;
A wightly wanton with a velvet brow,
With two pitch-balls stuck in her face for eyes;
Ay, and by heaven, one that will do the deed
Though Argus were her eunuch and her guard:
And I to sigh for her! to watch for her!
To pray for her! Go to; it is a plague
That Cupid will impose for my neglect
Of his almighty dreadful little might.
Well, I will love, write, sigh, pray, sue and groan:
Some men must love my lady and some Joan.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The same.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the PRINCESS, and her train, a Forester, BOYET, ROSALINE, MARIA, and KATHARINE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Was that the king, that spurred his horse so hard
Against the steep uprising of the hill?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: I know not; but I think it was not he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Whoe'er a' was, a' show'd a mounting mind.
Well, lords, to-day we shall have our dispatch:
On Saturday we will return to France.
Then, forester, my friend, where is the bush
That we must stand and play the murderer in?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Forester
SPEECH.LINE: Hereby, upon the edge of yonder coppice;
A stand where you may make the fairest shoot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank my beauty, I am fair that shoot,
And thereupon thou speak'st the fairest shoot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Forester
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, madam, for I meant not so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: What, what? first praise me and again say no?
O short-lived pride! Not fair? alack for woe!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Forester
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, madam, fair.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, never paint me now:
Where fair is not, praise cannot mend the brow.
Here, good my glass, take this for telling true:
Fair payment for foul words is more than due.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Forester
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing but fair is that which you inherit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: See see, my beauty will be saved by merit!
O heresy in fair, fit for these days!
A giving hand, though foul, shall have fair praise.
But come, the bow: now mercy goes to kill,
And shooting well is then accounted ill.
Thus will I save my credit in the shoot:
Not wounding, pity would not let me do't;
If wounding, then it was to show my skill,
That more for praise than purpose meant to kill.
And out of question so it is sometimes,
Glory grows guilty of detested crimes,
When, for fame's sake, for praise, an outward part,
We bend to that the working of the heart;
As I for praise alone now seek to spill
The poor deer's blood, that my heart means no ill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Do not curst wives hold that self-sovereignty
Only for praise sake, when they strive to be
Lords o'er their lords?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Only for praise: and praise we may afford
To any lady that subdues a lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes a member of the commonwealth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: God dig-you-den all! Pray you, which is the head lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt know her, fellow, by the rest that have no heads.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Which is the greatest lady, the highest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: The thickest and the tallest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: The thickest and the tallest! it is so; truth is truth.
An your waist, mistress, were as slender as my wit,
One o' these maids' girdles for your waist should be fit.
Are not you the chief woman? you are the thickest here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: What's your will, sir? what's your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I have a letter from Monsieur Biron to one Lady Rosaline.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: O, thy letter, thy letter! he's a good friend of mine:
Stand aside, good bearer. Boyet, you can carve;
Break up this capon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: I am bound to serve.
This letter is mistook, it importeth none here;
It is writ to Jaquenetta.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: We will read it, I swear.
Break the neck of the wax, and every one give ear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: 'By heaven, that thou art fair, is most infallible;
true, that thou art beauteous; truth itself, that
thou art lovely. More fairer than fair, beautiful
than beauteous, truer than truth itself, have
commiseration on thy heroical vassal! The
magnanimous and most illustrate king Cophetua set
eye upon the pernicious and indubitate beggar
Zenelophon; and he it was that might rightly say,
Veni, vidi, vici; which to annothanize in the
vulgar,--O base and obscure vulgar!--videlicet, He
came, saw, and overcame: he came, one; saw two;
overcame, three. Who came? the king: why did he
come? to see: why did he see? to overcome: to
whom came he? to the beggar: what saw he? the
beggar: who overcame he? the beggar. The
conclusion is victory: on whose side? the king's.
The captive is enriched: on whose side? the
beggar's. The catastrophe is a nuptial: on whose
side? the king's: no, on both in one, or one in
both. I am the king; for so stands the comparison:
thou the beggar; for so witnesseth thy lowliness.
Shall I command thy love? I may: shall I enforce
thy love? I could: shall I entreat thy love? I
will. What shalt thou exchange for rags? robes;
for tittles? titles; for thyself? me. Thus,
expecting thy reply, I profane my lips on thy foot,
my eyes on thy picture. and my heart on thy every
part. Thine, in the dearest design of industry,
DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO.'
Thus dost thou hear the Nemean lion roar
'Gainst thee, thou lamb, that standest as his prey.
Submissive fall his princely feet before,
And he from forage will incline to play:
But if thou strive, poor soul, what art thou then?
Food for his rage, repasture for his den.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: What plume of feathers is he that indited this letter?
What vane? what weathercock? did you ever hear better?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: I am much deceived but I remember the style.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Else your memory is bad, going o'er it erewhile.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: This Armado is a Spaniard, that keeps here in court;
A phantasime, a Monarcho, and one that makes sport
To the prince and his bookmates.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou fellow, a word:
Who gave thee this letter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: I told you; my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: To whom shouldst thou give it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: From my lord to my lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: From which lord to which lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: From my lord Biron, a good master of mine,
To a lady of France that he call'd Rosaline.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCESS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast mistaken his letter. Come, lords, away.
Here, sweet, put up this: 'twill be thine another day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Who is the suitor? who is the suitor?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I teach you to know?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my continent of beauty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, she that bears the bow.
Finely put off!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: My lady goes to kill horns; but, if thou marry,
Hang me by the neck, if horns that year miscarry.
Finely put on!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Well, then, I am the shooter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: And who is your deer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: If we choose by the horns, yourself come not near.
Finely put on, indeed!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: You still wrangle with her, Boyet, and she strikes
at the brow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: But she herself is hit lower: have I hit her now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I come upon thee with an old saying, that was
a man when King Pepin of France was a little boy, as
touching the hit it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: So I may answer thee with one as old, that was a
woman when Queen Guinover of Britain was a little
wench, as touching the hit it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSALINE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou canst not hit it, hit it, hit it,
Thou canst not hit it, my good man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: An I cannot, cannot, cannot,
An I cannot, another can.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, most pleasant: how both did fit it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: A mark marvellous well shot, for they both did hit it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: A mark! O, mark but that mark! A mark, says my lady!
Let the mark have a prick in't, to mete at, if it may be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Wide o' the bow hand! i' faith, your hand is out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, a' must shoot nearer, or he'll ne'er hit the clout.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: An if my hand be out, then belike your hand is in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Then will she get the upshoot by cleaving the pin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, you talk greasily; your lips grow foul.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: She's too hard for you at pricks, sir: challenge her to bowl.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOYET
SPEECH.LINE: I fear too much rubbing. Good night, my good owl.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: By my soul, a swain! a most simple clown!
Lord, Lord, how the ladies and I have put him down!
O' my troth, most sweet jests! most incony
vulgar wit!
When it comes so smoothly off, so obscenely, as it
were, so fit.
Armado o' th' one side,--O, a most dainty man!
To see him walk before a lady and to bear her fan!
To see him kiss his hand! and how most sweetly a'
will swear!
And his page o' t' other side, that handful of wit!
Ah, heavens, it is a most pathetical nit!
Sola, sola!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter HOLOFERNES, SIR NATHANIEL, and DULL

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Very reverend sport, truly; and done in the testimony
of a good conscience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: The deer was, as you know, sanguis, in blood; ripe
as the pomewater, who now hangeth like a jewel in
the ear of caelo, the sky, the welkin, the heaven;
and anon falleth like a crab on the face of terra,
the soil, the land, the earth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, Master Holofernes, the epithets are sweetly
varied, like a scholar at the least: but, sir, I
assure ye, it was a buck of the first head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Nathaniel, haud credo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas not a haud credo; 'twas a pricket.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Most barbarous intimation! yet a kind of
insinuation, as it were, in via, in way, of
explication; facere, as it were, replication, or
rather, ostentare, to show, as it were, his
inclination, after his undressed, unpolished,
uneducated, unpruned, untrained, or rather,
unlettered, or ratherest, unconfirmed fashion, to
insert again my haud credo for a deer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: I said the deer was not a haud credo; twas a pricket.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Twice-sod simplicity, his coctus!
O thou monster Ignorance, how deformed dost thou look!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, he hath never fed of the dainties that are bred
in a book; he hath not eat paper, as it were; he
hath not drunk ink: his intellect is not
replenished; he is only an animal, only sensible in
the duller parts:
And such barren plants are set before us, that we
thankful should be,
Which we of taste and feeling are, for those parts that
do fructify in us more than he.
For as it would ill become me to be vain, indiscreet, or a fool,
So were there a patch set on learning, to see him in a school:
But omne bene, say I; being of an old father's mind,
Many can brook the weather that love not the wind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: You two are book-men: can you tell me by your wit
What was a month old at Cain's birth, that's not five
weeks old as yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Dictynna, goodman Dull; Dictynna, goodman Dull.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: What is Dictynna?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: A title to Phoebe, to Luna, to the moon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: The moon was a month old when Adam was no more,
And raught not to five weeks when he came to
five-score.
The allusion holds in the exchange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true indeed; the collusion holds in the exchange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: God comfort thy capacity! I say, the allusion holds
in the exchange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: And I say, the pollusion holds in the exchange; for
the moon is never but a month old: and I say beside
that, 'twas a pricket that the princess killed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Nathaniel, will you hear an extemporal epitaph
on the death of the deer? And, to humour the
ignorant, call I the deer the princess killed a pricket.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Perge, good Master Holofernes, perge; so it shall
please you to abrogate scurrility.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: I will something affect the letter, for it argues facility.
The preyful princess pierced and prick'd a pretty
pleasing pricket;
Some say a sore; but not a sore, till now made
sore with shooting.
The dogs did yell: put L to sore, then sorel jumps
from thicket;
Or pricket sore, or else sorel; the people fall a-hooting.
If sore be sore, then L to sore makes fifty sores
one sorel.
Of one sore I an hundred make by adding but one more L.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: A rare talent!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DULL
SPEECH.LINE: Aside If a talent be a claw, look how he claws
him with a talent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: This is a gift that I have, simple, simple; a
foolish extravagant spirit, full of forms, figures,
shapes, objects, ideas, apprehensions, motions,
revolutions: these are begot in the ventricle of
memory, nourished in the womb of pia mater, and
delivered upon the mellowing of occasion. But the
gift is good in those in whom it is acute, and I am
thankful for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I praise the Lord for you; and so may my
parishioners; for their sons are well tutored by
you, and their daughters profit very greatly under
you: you are a good member of the commonwealth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Mehercle, if their sons be ingenuous, they shall
want no instruction; if their daughters be capable,
I will put it to them: but vir sapit qui pauca
loquitur; a soul feminine saluteth us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: God give you good morrow, master Parson.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Master Parson, quasi pers-on. An if one should be
pierced, which is the one?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, master schoolmaster, he that is likest to a hogshead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Piercing a hogshead! a good lustre of conceit in a
tuft of earth; fire enough for a flint, pearl enough
for a swine: 'tis pretty; it is well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Good master Parson, be so good as read me this
letter: it was given me by Costard, and sent me
from Don Armado: I beseech you, read it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Fauste, precor gelida quando pecus omne sub umbra
Ruminat,--and so forth. Ah, good old Mantuan! I
may speak of thee as the traveller doth of Venice;
Venetia, Venetia,
Chi non ti vede non ti pretia.
Old Mantuan, old Mantuan! who understandeth thee
not, loves thee not. Ut, re, sol, la, mi, fa.
Under pardon, sir, what are the contents? or rather,
as Horace says in his--What, my soul, verses?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, and very learned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Let me hear a staff, a stanze, a verse; lege, domine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: If love make me forsworn, how shall I swear to love?
Ah, never faith could hold, if not to beauty vow'd!
Though to myself forsworn, to thee I'll faithful prove:
Those thoughts to me were oaks, to thee like
osiers bow'd.
Study his bias leaves and makes his book thine eyes,
Where all those pleasures live that art would
comprehend:
If knowledge be the mark, to know thee shall suffice;
Well learned is that tongue that well can thee commend,
All ignorant that soul that sees thee without wonder;
Which is to me some praise that I thy parts admire:
Thy eye Jove's lightning bears, thy voice his dreadful thunder,
Which not to anger bent, is music and sweet fire.
Celestial as thou art, O, pardon, love, this wrong,
That sings heaven's praise with such an earthly tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: You find not the apostraphas, and so miss the
accent: let me supervise the canzonet. Here are
only numbers ratified; but, for the elegancy,
facility, and golden cadence of poesy, caret.
Ovidius Naso was the man: and why, indeed, Naso,
but for smelling out the odouriferous flowers of
fancy, the jerks of invention? Imitari is nothing:
so doth the hound his master, the ape his keeper,
the tired horse his rider. But, damosella virgin,
was this directed to you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, from one Monsieur Biron, one of the strange
queen's lords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: I will overglance the superscript: 'To the
snow-white hand of the most beauteous Lady
Rosaline.' I will look again on the intellect of
the letter, for the nomination of the party writing
to the person written unto: 'Your ladyship's in all
desired employment, BIRON.' Sir Nathaniel, this
Biron is one of the votaries with the king; and here
he hath framed a letter to a sequent of the stranger
queen's, which accidentally, or by the way of
progression, hath miscarried. Trip and go, my
sweet; deliver this paper into the royal hand of the
king: it may concern much. Stay not thy
compliment; I forgive thy duty; adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JAQUENETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Good Costard, go with me. Sir, God save your life!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: COSTARD
SPEECH.LINE: Have with thee, my girl.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, you have done this in the fear of God, very
religiously; and, as a certain father saith,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: Sir tell me not of the father; I do fear colourable
colours. But to return to the verses: did they
please you, Sir Nathaniel?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Marvellous well for the pen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: I do dine to-day at the father's of a certain pupil
of mine; where, if, before repast, it shall please
you to gratify the table with a grace, I will, on my
privilege I have with the parents of the foresaid
child or pupil, undertake your ben venuto; where I
will prove those verses to be very unlearned,
neither savouring of poetry, wit, nor invention: I
beseech your society.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: And thank you too; for society, saith the text, is
the happiness of life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HOLOFERNES
SPEECH.LINE: And, certes, the text most infallibly concludes it.
Sir, I do invite you too; you shall not
say me nay: pauca verba. Away! the gentles are at
their game, and we will to our recreation.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The same.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIRON
SPEECH.LINE: The king he is hunting the deer; I am coursing
myself: they have pitched a toil; I am toiling in
a pitch,--pitch that defiles: defile! a foul
word. Well, set thee down, sorrow! for so they say
