SPEECH.LINE: Help to cover your master, boy. Call your men,
Mistress Ford. You dissembling knight!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: What, John! Robert! John!
Go take up these clothes here quickly. Where's the
cowl-staff? look, how you drumble! Carry them to
the laundress in Datchet-meat; quickly, come.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FORD, PAGE, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, come near: if I suspect without cause,
why then make sport at me; then let me be your jest;
I deserve it. How now! whither bear you this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: To the laundress, forsooth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what have you to do whither they bear it? You
were best meddle with buck-washing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Buck! I would I could wash myself of the buck!
Buck, buck, buck! Ay, buck; I warrant you, buck;
and of the season too, it shall appear.
Gentlemen, I have dreamed to-night; I'll tell you my
dream. Here, here, here be my keys: ascend my
chambers; search, seek, find out: I'll warrant
we'll unkennel the fox. Let me stop this way first.
So, now uncape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Good Master Ford, be contented: you wrong yourself too much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: True, Master Page. Up, gentlemen: you shall see
sport anon: follow me, gentlemen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: This is fery fantastical humours and jealousies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By gar, 'tis no the fashion of France; it is not
jealous in France.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, follow him, gentlemen; see the issue of his search.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt PAGE, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Is there not a double excellency in this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I know not which pleases me better, that my husband
is deceived, or Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: What a taking was he in when your husband asked who
was in the basket!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I am half afraid he will have need of washing; so
throwing him into the water will do him a benefit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Hang him, dishonest rascal! I would all of the same
strain were in the same distress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I think my husband hath some special suspicion of
Falstaff's being here; for I never saw him so gross
in his jealousy till now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I will lay a plot to try that; and we will yet have
more tricks with Falstaff: his dissolute disease will
scarce obey this medicine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Shall we send that foolish carrion, Mistress
Quickly, to him, and excuse his throwing into the
water; and give him another hope, to betray him to
another punishment?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: We will do it: let him be sent for to-morrow,
eight o'clock, to have amends.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter FORD, PAGE, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot find him: may be the knave bragged of that
he could not compass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to MISTRESS FORD Heard you that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: You use me well, Master Ford, do you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, I do so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Heaven make you better than your thoughts!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Amen!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: You do yourself mighty wrong, Master Ford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay; I must bear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: If there be any pody in the house, and in the
chambers, and in the coffers, and in the presses,
heaven forgive my sins at the day of judgment!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By gar, nor I too: there is no bodies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie, Master Ford! are you not ashamed? What
spirit, what devil suggests this imagination? I
would not ha' your distemper in this kind for the
wealth of Windsor Castle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis my fault, Master Page: I suffer for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: You suffer for a pad conscience: your wife is as
honest a 'omans as I will desires among five
thousand, and five hundred too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By gar, I see 'tis an honest woman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I promised you a dinner. Come, come, walk in
the Park: I pray you, pardon me; I will hereafter
make known to you why I have done this. Come,
wife; come, Mistress Page. I pray you, pardon me;
pray heartily, pardon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Let's go in, gentlemen; but, trust me, we'll mock
him. I do invite you to-morrow morning to my house
to breakfast: after, we'll a-birding together; I
have a fine hawk for the bush. Shall it be so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Any thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: If there is one, I shall make two in the company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If dere be one or two, I shall make-a the turd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, go, Master Page.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you now, remembrance tomorrow on the lousy
knave, mine host.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Dat is good; by gar, with all my heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: A lousy knave, to have his gibes and his mockeries!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. A room in PAGE'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: I see I cannot get thy father's love;
Therefore no more turn me to him, sweet Nan.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, how then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, thou must be thyself.
He doth object I am too great of birth--,
And that, my state being gall'd with my expense,
I seek to heal it only by his wealth:
Besides these, other bars he lays before me,
My riots past, my wild societies;
And tells me 'tis a thing impossible
I should love thee but as a property.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: May be he tells you true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: No, heaven so speed me in my time to come!
Albeit I will confess thy father's wealth
Was the first motive that I woo'd thee, Anne:
Yet, wooing thee, I found thee of more value
Than stamps in gold or sums in sealed bags;
And 'tis the very riches of thyself
That now I aim at.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Gentle Master Fenton,
Yet seek my father's love; still seek it, sir:
If opportunity and humblest suit
Cannot attain it, why, then,--hark you hither!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SHALLOW, SLENDER, and MISTRESS QUICKLY

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Break their talk, Mistress Quickly: my kinsman shall
speak for himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: I'll make a shaft or a bolt on't: 'slid, 'tis but
venturing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Be not dismayed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: No, she shall not dismay me: I care not for that,
but that I am afeard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Hark ye; Master Slender would speak a word with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I come to him.
This is my father's choice.
O, what a world of vile ill-favor'd faults
Looks handsome in three hundred pounds a-year!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: And how does good Master Fenton? Pray you, a word with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: She's coming; to her, coz. O boy, thou hadst a father!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: I had a father, Mistress Anne; my uncle can tell you
good jests of him. Pray you, uncle, tell Mistress
Anne the jest, how my father stole two geese out of
a pen, good uncle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Anne, my cousin loves you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that I do; as well as I love any woman in
Gloucestershire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: He will maintain you like a gentlewoman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that I will, come cut and long-tail, under the
degree of a squire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: He will make you a hundred and fifty pounds jointure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Good Master Shallow, let him woo for himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, I thank you for it; I thank you for that good
comfort. She calls you, coz: I'll leave you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Master Slender,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Now, good Mistress Anne,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: What is your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: My will! 'od's heartlings, that's a pretty jest
indeed! I ne'er made my will yet, I thank heaven; I
am not such a sickly creature, I give heaven praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I mean, Master Slender, what would you with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, for mine own part, I would little or nothing
with you. Your father and my uncle hath made
motions: if it be my luck, so; if not, happy man be
his dole! They can tell you how things go better
than I can: you may ask your father; here he comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Master Slender: love him, daughter Anne.
Why, how now! what does Master Fenton here?
You wrong me, sir, thus still to haunt my house:
I told you, sir, my daughter is disposed of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, Master Page, be not impatient.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Good Master Fenton, come not to my child.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: She is no match for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, will you hear me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: No, good Master Fenton.
Come, Master Shallow; come, son Slender, in.
Knowing my mind, you wrong me, Master Fenton.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Speak to Mistress Page.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Good Mistress Page, for that I love your daughter
In such a righteous fashion as I do,
Perforce, against all cheques, rebukes and manners,
I must advance the colours of my love
And not retire: let me have your good will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Good mother, do not marry me to yond fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I mean it not; I seek you a better husband.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: That's my master, master doctor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, I had rather be set quick i' the earth
And bowl'd to death with turnips!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Come, trouble not yourself. Good Master Fenton,
I will not be your friend nor enemy:
My daughter will I question how she loves you,
And as I find her, so am I affected.
Till then farewell, sir: she must needs go in;
Her father will be angry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, gentle mistress: farewell, Nan.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt MISTRESS PAGE and ANNE PAGE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: This is my doing, now: 'Nay,' said I, 'will you cast
away your child on a fool, and a physician? Look on
Master Fenton:' this is my doing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee; and I pray thee, once to-night
Give my sweet Nan this ring: there's for thy pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Now heaven send thee good fortune!
A kind heart he hath: a woman would run through
fire and water for such a kind heart. But yet I
would my master had Mistress Anne; or I would
Master Slender had her; or, in sooth, I would Master
Fenton had her; I will do what I can for them all
three; for so I have promised, and I'll be as good
as my word; but speciously for Master Fenton. Well,
I must of another errand to Sir John Falstaff from
my two mistresses: what a beast am I to slack it!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Bardolph, I say,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Go fetch me a quart of sack; put a toast in't.
Have I lived to be carried in a basket, like a
barrow of butcher's offal, and to be thrown in the
Thames? Well, if I be served such another trick,
I'll have my brains ta'en out and buttered, and give
them to a dog for a new-year's gift. The rogues
slighted me into the river with as little remorse as
they would have drowned a blind bitch's puppies,
fifteen i' the litter: and you may know by my size
that I have a kind of alacrity in sinking; if the
bottom were as deep as hell, I should down. I had
been drowned, but that the shore was shelvy and
shallow,--a death that I abhor; for the water swells
a man; and what a thing should I have been when I
had been swelled! I should have been a mountain of mummy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Here's Mistress Quickly, sir, to speak with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Let me pour in some sack to the Thames water; for my
belly's as cold as if I had swallowed snowballs for
pills to cool the reins. Call her in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Come in, woman!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: By your leave; I cry you mercy: give your worship
good morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Take away these chalices. Go brew me a pottle of
sack finely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: With eggs, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Simple of itself; I'll no pullet-sperm in my brewage.
How now!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, I come to your worship from Mistress Ford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Ford! I have had ford enough; I was thrown
into the ford; I have my belly full of ford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Alas the day! good heart, that was not her fault:
she does so take on with her men; they mistook their erection.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: So did I mine, to build upon a foolish woman's promise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Well, she laments, sir, for it, that it would yearn
your heart to see it. Her husband goes this morning
a-birding; she desires you once more to come to her
between eight and nine: I must carry her word
quickly: she'll make you amends, I warrant you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will visit her: tell her so; and bid her
think what a man is: let her consider his frailty,
and then judge of my merit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: I will tell her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Do so. Between nine and ten, sayest thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Eight and nine, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Well, be gone: I will not miss her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Peace be with you, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I marvel I hear not of Master Brook; he sent me word
to stay within: I like his money well. O, here he comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Bless you, sir!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Now, master Brook, you come to know what hath passed
between me and Ford's wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: That, indeed, Sir John, is my business.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Master Brook, I will not lie to you: I was at her
house the hour she appointed me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And sped you, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Very ill-favoredly, Master Brook.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: How so, sir? Did she change her determination?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: No, Master Brook; but the peaking Cornuto her
husband, Master Brook, dwelling in a continual
'larum of jealousy, comes me in the instant of our
encounter, after we had embraced, kissed, protested,
and, as it were, spoke the prologue of our comedy;
and at his heels a rabble of his companions, thither
provoked and instigated by his distemper, and,
forsooth, to search his house for his wife's love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: What, while you were there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: While I was there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And did he search for you, and could not find you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: You shall hear. As good luck would have it, comes
in one Mistress Page; gives intelligence of Ford's
approach; and, in her invention and Ford's wife's
distraction, they conveyed me into a buck-basket.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: A buck-basket!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: By the Lord, a buck-basket! rammed me in with foul
shirts and smocks, socks, foul stockings, greasy
napkins; that, Master Brook, there was the rankest
compound of villanous smell that ever offended nostril.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And how long lay you there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, you shall hear, Master Brook, what I have
suffered to bring this woman to evil for your good.
Being thus crammed in the basket, a couple of Ford's
knaves, his hinds, were called forth by their
mistress to carry me in the name of foul clothes to
Datchet-lane: they took me on their shoulders; met
the jealous knave their master in the door, who
asked them once or twice what they had in their
basket: I quaked for fear, lest the lunatic knave
would have searched it; but fate, ordaining he
should be a cuckold, held his hand. Well: on went he
for a search, and away went I for foul clothes. But
mark the sequel, Master Brook: I suffered the pangs
of three several deaths; first, an intolerable
fright, to be detected with a jealous rotten
bell-wether; next, to be compassed, like a good
bilbo, in the circumference of a peck, hilt to
point, heel to head; and then, to be stopped in,
like a strong distillation, with stinking clothes
that fretted in their own grease: think of that,--a
man of my kidney,--think of that,--that am as subject
to heat as butter; a man of continual dissolution
and thaw: it was a miracle to scape suffocation.
And in the height of this bath, when I was more than
half stewed in grease, like a Dutch dish, to be
thrown into the Thames, and cooled, glowing hot,
in that surge, like a horse-shoe; think of
that,--hissing hot,--think of that, Master Brook.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: In good sadness, I am sorry that for my sake you
have sufferd all this. My suit then is desperate;
you'll undertake her no more?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Master Brook, I will be thrown into Etna, as I have
been into Thames, ere I will leave her thus. Her
husband is this morning gone a-birding: I have
received from her another embassy of meeting; 'twixt
eight and nine is the hour, Master Brook.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis past eight already, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Is it? I will then address me to my appointment.
Come to me at your convenient leisure, and you shall
know how I speed; and the conclusion shall be
crowned with your enjoying her. Adieu. You shall
have her, Master Brook; Master Brook, you shall
cuckold Ford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Hum! ha! is this a vision? is this a dream? do I
sleep? Master Ford awake! awake, Master Ford!
there's a hole made in your best coat, Master Ford.
This 'tis to be married! this 'tis to have linen
and buck-baskets! Well, I will proclaim myself
what I am: I will now take the lecher; he is at my
house; he cannot 'scape me; 'tis impossible he
should; he cannot creep into a halfpenny purse,
nor into a pepper-box: but, lest the devil that
guides him should aid him, I will search
impossible places. Though what I am I cannot avoid,
yet to be what I would not shall not make me tame:
if I have horns to make one mad, let the proverb go
with me: I'll be horn-mad.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A street.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS QUICKLY, and WILLIAM PAGE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Is he at Master Ford's already, think'st thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Sure he is by this, or will be presently: but,
truly, he is very courageous mad about his throwing
into the water. Mistress Ford desires you to come suddenly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I'll be with her by and by; I'll but bring my young
man here to school. Look, where his master comes;
'tis a playing-day, I see.
How now, Sir Hugh! no school to-day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: No; Master Slender is let the boys leave to play.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Blessing of his heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Hugh, my husband says my son profits nothing in
the world at his book. I pray you, ask him some
questions in his accidence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, William; hold up your head; come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, sirrah; hold up your head; answer your
master, be not afraid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: William, how many numbers is in nouns?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Two.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, I thought there had been one number more,
because they say, ''Od's nouns.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Peace your tattlings! What is 'fair,' William?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Pulcher.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Polecats! there are fairer things than polecats, sure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: You are a very simplicity 'oman: I pray you peace.
What is 'lapis,' William?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: A stone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: And what is 'a stone,' William?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: A pebble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: No, it is 'lapis:' I pray you, remember in your prain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Lapis.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: That is a good William. What is he, William, that
does lend articles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Articles are borrowed of the pronoun, and be thus
declined, Singulariter, nominativo, hic, haec, hoc.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Nominativo, hig, hag, hog; pray you, mark:
genitivo, hujus. Well, what is your accusative case?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Accusativo, hinc.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, have your remembrance, child,
accusative, hung, hang, hog.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: 'Hang-hog' is Latin for bacon, I warrant you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Leave your prabbles, 'oman. What is the focative
case, William?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: O,--vocativo, O.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Remember, William; focative is caret.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: And that's a good root.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Oman, forbear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: What is your genitive case plural, William?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Genitive case!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Genitive,--horum, harum, horum.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Vengeance of Jenny's case! fie on her! never name
her, child, if she be a whore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: For shame, 'oman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: You do ill to teach the child such words: he
teaches him to hick and to hack, which they'll do
fast enough of themselves, and to call 'horum:' fie upon you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Oman, art thou lunatics? hast thou no
understandings for thy cases and the numbers of the
genders? Thou art as foolish Christian creatures as
I would desires.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, hold thy peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Show me now, William, some declensions of your pronouns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: WILLIAM PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Forsooth, I have forgot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: It is qui, quae, quod: if you forget your 'quies,'
your 'quaes,' and your 'quods,' you must be
preeches. Go your ways, and play; go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: He is a better scholar than I thought he was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: He is a good sprag memory. Farewell, Mistress Page.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Adieu, good Sir Hugh.
Get you home, boy. Come, we stay too long.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A room in FORD'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Ford, your sorrow hath eaten up my
sufferance. I see you are obsequious in your love,
and I profess requital to a hair's breadth; not
only, Mistress Ford, in the simple
office of love, but in all the accoutrement,
complement and ceremony of it. But are you
sure of your husband now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: He's a-birding, sweet Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Within What, ho, gossip Ford! what, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Step into the chamber, Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: How now, sweetheart! who's at home besides yourself?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, none but mine own people.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: No, certainly.
Speak louder.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, I am so glad you have nobody here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, woman, your husband is in his old lunes again:
he so takes on yonder with my husband; so rails
against all married mankind; so curses all Eve's
daughters, of what complexion soever; and so buffets
himself on the forehead, crying, 'Peer out, peer
out!' that any madness I ever yet beheld seemed but
tameness, civility and patience, to this his
distemper he is in now: I am glad the fat knight is not here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, does he talk of him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Of none but him; and swears he was carried out, the
last time he searched for him, in a basket; protests
to my husband he is now here, and hath drawn him and
the rest of their company from their sport, to make
another experiment of his suspicion: but I am glad
the knight is not here; now he shall see his own foolery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: How near is he, Mistress Page?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Hard by; at street end; he will be here anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I am undone! The knight is here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why then you are utterly shamed, and he's but a dead
man. What a woman are you!--Away with him, away
with him! better shame than murder.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Which way should be go? how should I bestow him?
Shall I put him into the basket again?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: No, I'll come no more i' the basket. May I not go
out ere he come?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, three of Master Ford's brothers watch the door
with pistols, that none shall issue out; otherwise
you might slip away ere he came. But what make you here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What shall I do? I'll creep up into the chimney.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: There they always use to discharge their
birding-pieces. Creep into the kiln-hole.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Where is it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: He will seek there, on my word. Neither press,
coffer, chest, trunk, well, vault, but he hath an
abstract for the remembrance of such places, and
goes to them by his note: there is no hiding you in the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I'll go out then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: If you go out in your own semblance, you die, Sir
John. Unless you go out disguised--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: How might we disguise him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas the day, I know not! There is no woman's gown
big enough for him otherwise he might put on a hat,
a muffler and a kerchief, and so escape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Good hearts, devise something: any extremity rather
than a mischief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: My maid's aunt, the fat woman of Brentford, has a
gown above.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: On my word, it will serve him; she's as big as he
is: and there's her thrummed hat and her muffler
too. Run up, Sir John.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Go, go, sweet Sir John: Mistress Page and I will
look some linen for your head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Quick, quick! we'll come dress you straight: put
on the gown the while.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I would my husband would meet him in this shape: he
cannot abide the old woman of Brentford; he swears
she's a witch; forbade her my house and hath
threatened to beat her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Heaven guide him to thy husband's cudgel, and the
devil guide his cudgel afterwards!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: But is my husband coming?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, in good sadness, is he; and talks of the basket
too, howsoever he hath had intelligence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: We'll try that; for I'll appoint my men to carry the
basket again, to meet him at the door with it, as
they did last time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but he'll be here presently: let's go dress him
like the witch of Brentford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I'll first direct my men what they shall do with the
basket. Go up; I'll bring linen for him straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Hang him, dishonest varlet! we cannot misuse him enough.
We'll leave a proof, by that which we will do,
Wives may be merry, and yet honest too:
We do not act that often jest and laugh;
'Tis old, but true, Still swine eat all the draff.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter MISTRESS FORD with two Servants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Go, sirs, take the basket again on your shoulders:
your master is hard at door; if he bid you set it
down, obey him: quickly, dispatch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, take it up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Pray heaven it be not full of knight again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I hope not; I had as lief bear so much lead.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FORD, PAGE, SHALLOW, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but if it prove true, Master Page, have you any
way then to unfool me again? Set down the basket,
villain! Somebody call my wife. Youth in a basket!
O you panderly rascals! there's a knot, a ging, a
pack, a conspiracy against me: now shall the devil
be shamed. What, wife, I say! Come, come forth!
Behold what honest clothes you send forth to bleaching!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this passes, Master Ford; you are not to go
loose any longer; you must be pinioned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this is lunatics! this is mad as a mad dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, Master Ford, this is not well, indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: So say I too, sir.
Come hither, Mistress Ford; Mistress Ford the honest
woman, the modest wife, the virtuous creature, that
hath the jealous fool to her husband! I suspect
without cause, mistress, do I?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Heaven be my witness you do, if you suspect me in
any dishonesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, brazen-face! hold it out. Come forth, sirrah!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Pulling clothes out of the basket

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: This passes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Are you not ashamed? let the clothes alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I shall find you anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis unreasonable! Will you take up your wife's
clothes? Come away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Empty the basket, I say!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Why, man, why?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Master Page, as I am a man, there was one conveyed
out of my house yesterday in this basket: why may
not he be there again? In my house I am sure he is:
my intelligence is true; my jealousy is reasonable.
Pluck me out all the linen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: If you find a man there, he shall die a flea's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Here's no man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: By my fidelity, this is not well, Master Ford; this
wrongs you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Master Ford, you must pray, and not follow the
imaginations of your own heart: this is jealousies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Well, he's not here I seek for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: No, nor nowhere else but in your brain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Help to search my house this one time. If I find
not what I seek, show no colour for my extremity; let
me for ever be your table-sport; let them say of
me, 'As jealous as Ford, Chat searched a hollow
walnut for his wife's leman.' Satisfy me once more;
once more search with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: What, ho, Mistress Page! come you and the old woman
down; my husband will come into the chamber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Old woman! what old woman's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, it is my maid's aunt of Brentford.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: A witch, a quean, an old cozening quean! Have I not
forbid her my house? She comes of errands, does
she? We are simple men; we do not know what's
brought to pass under the profession of
fortune-telling. She works by charms, by spells,
by the figure, and such daubery as this is, beyond
our element we know nothing. Come down, you witch,
you hag, you; come down, I say!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good, sweet husband! Good gentlemen, let him
not strike the old woman.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter FALSTAFF in woman's clothes, and MISTRESS PAGE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Mother Prat; come, give me your hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I'll prat her.
Out of my door, you witch, you hag, you baggage, you
polecat, you runyon! out, out! I'll conjure you,
I'll fortune-tell you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Are you not ashamed? I think you have killed the
poor woman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, he will do it. 'Tis a goodly credit for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Hang her, witch!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: By the yea and no, I think the 'oman is a witch
indeed: I like not when a 'oman has a great peard;
I spy a great peard under his muffler.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Will you follow, gentlemen? I beseech you, follow;
see but the issue of my jealousy: if I cry out thus
upon no trail, never trust me when I open again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Let's obey his humour a little further: come,
gentlemen.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt FORD, PAGE, SHALLOW, DOCTOR CAIUS, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Trust me, he beat him most pitifully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, by the mass, that he did not; he beat him most
unpitifully, methought.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have the cudgel hallowed and hung o'er the
altar; it hath done meritorious service.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: What think you? may we, with the warrant of
womanhood and the witness of a good conscience,
pursue him with any further revenge?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: The spirit of wantonness is, sure, scared out of
him: if the devil have him not in fee-simple, with
fine and recovery, he will never, I think, in the
way of waste, attempt us again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Shall we tell our husbands how we have served him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, by all means; if it be but to scrape the
figures out of your husband's brains. If they can
find in their hearts the poor unvirtuous fat knight
shall be any further afflicted, we two will still be
the ministers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I'll warrant they'll have him publicly shamed: and
methinks there would be no period to the jest,
should he not be publicly shamed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Come, to the forge with it then; shape it: I would
not have things cool.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A room in the Garter Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, the Germans desire to have three of your
horses: the duke himself will be to-morrow at
court, and they are going to meet him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: What duke should that be comes so secretly? I hear
not of him in the court. Let me speak with the
gentlemen: they speak English?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir; I'll call them to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: They shall have my horses; but I'll make them pay;
I'll sauce them: they have had my house a week at
command; I have turned away my other guests: they
must come off; I'll sauce them. Come.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. A room in FORD'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PAGE, FORD, MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis one of the best discretions of a 'oman as ever
I did look upon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: And did he send you both these letters at an instant?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Within a quarter of an hour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, wife. Henceforth do what thou wilt;
I rather will suspect the sun with cold
Than thee with wantonness: now doth thy honour stand
In him that was of late an heretic,
As firm as faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well, 'tis well; no more:
Be not as extreme in submission
As in offence.
But let our plot go forward: let our wives
Yet once again, to make us public sport,
Appoint a meeting with this old fat fellow,
Where we may take him and disgrace him for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: There is no better way than that they spoke of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: How? to send him word they'll meet him in the park
at midnight? Fie, fie! he'll never come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: You say he has been thrown in the rivers and has
been grievously peaten as an old 'oman: methinks
there should be terrors in him that he should not
come; methinks his flesh is punished, he shall have
no desires.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: So think I too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Devise but how you'll use him when he comes,
And let us two devise to bring him thither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: There is an old tale goes that Herne the hunter,
Sometime a keeper here in Windsor forest,
Doth all the winter-time, at still midnight,
Walk round about an oak, with great ragg'd horns;
And there he blasts the tree and takes the cattle
And makes milch-kine yield blood and shakes a chain
In a most hideous and dreadful manner:
You have heard of such a spirit, and well you know
The superstitious idle-headed eld
Received and did deliver to our age
This tale of Herne the hunter for a truth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, yet there want not many that do fear
In deep of night to walk by this Herne's oak:
But what of this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, this is our device;
That Falstaff at that oak shall meet with us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Well, let it not be doubted but he'll come:
And in this shape when you have brought him thither,
What shall be done with him? what is your plot?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: That likewise have we thought upon, and thus:
Nan Page my daughter and my little son
And three or four more of their growth we'll dress
Like urchins, ouphes and fairies, green and white,
With rounds of waxen tapers on their heads,
And rattles in their hands: upon a sudden,
As Falstaff, she and I, are newly met,
Let them from forth a sawpit rush at once
With some diffused song: upon their sight,
We two in great amazedness will fly:
Then let them all encircle him about
And, fairy-like, to-pinch the unclean knight,
And ask him why, that hour of fairy revel,
In their so sacred paths he dares to tread
In shape profane.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And till he tell the truth,
Let the supposed fairies pinch him sound
And burn him with their tapers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: The truth being known,
We'll all present ourselves, dis-horn the spirit,
And mock him home to Windsor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: The children must
Be practised well to this, or they'll ne'er do't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: I will teach the children their behaviors; and I
will be like a jack-an-apes also, to burn the
knight with my taber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: That will be excellent. I'll go and buy them vizards.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: My Nan shall be the queen of all the fairies,
Finely attired in a robe of white.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: That silk will I go buy.
And in that time
Shall Master Slender steal my Nan away
And marry her at Eton. Go send to Falstaff straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Nay I'll to him again in name of Brook
He'll tell me all his purpose: sure, he'll come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Fear not you that. Go get us properties
And tricking for our fairies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Let us about it: it is admirable pleasures and fery
honest knaveries.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt PAGE, FORD, and SIR HUGH EVANS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Go, Mistress Ford,
Send quickly to Sir John, to know his mind.
I'll to the doctor: he hath my good will,
And none but he, to marry with Nan Page.
That Slender, though well landed, is an idiot;
And he my husband best of all affects.
The doctor is well money'd, and his friends
Potent at court: he, none but he, shall have her,
Though twenty thousand worthier come to crave her.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. A room in the Garter Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: What wouldst thou have, boor? what: thick-skin?
speak, breathe, discuss; brief, short, quick, snap.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, I come to speak with Sir John Falstaff
from Master Slender.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: There's his chamber, his house, his castle, his
standing-bed and truckle-bed; 'tis painted about
with the story of the Prodigal, fresh and new. Go
knock and call; hell speak like an Anthropophaginian
unto thee: knock, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: There's an old woman, a fat woman, gone up into his
chamber: I'll be so bold as stay, sir, till she come
down; I come to speak with her, indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! a fat woman! the knight may be robbed: I'll
call. Bully knight! bully Sir John! speak from
thy lungs military: art thou there? it is thine
host, thine Ephesian, calls.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Above How now, mine host!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Here's a Bohemian-Tartar tarries the coming down of
thy fat woman. Let her descend, bully, let her
descend; my chambers are honourable: fie! privacy?
fie!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: There was, mine host, an old fat woman even now with
me; but she's gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, sir, was't not the wise woman of
Brentford?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry, was it, mussel-shell: what would you with her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: My master, sir, Master Slender, sent to her, seeing
her go through the streets, to know, sir, whether
one Nym, sir, that beguiled him of a chain, had the
chain or no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I spake with the old woman about it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: And what says she, I pray, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, she says that the very same man that
beguiled Master Slender of his chain cozened him of
it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: I would I could have spoken with the woman herself;
I had other things to have spoken with her too from
him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What are they? let us know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, come; quick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: I may not conceal them, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Conceal them, or thou diest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, sir, they were nothing but about Mistress Anne
Page; to know if it were my master's fortune to
have her or no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis, 'tis his fortune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: What, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: To have her, or no. Go; say the woman told me so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: May I be bold to say so, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir; like who more bold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIMPLE
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your worship: I shall make my master glad
with these tidings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art clerkly, thou art clerkly, Sir John. Was
there a wise woman with thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that there was, mine host; one that hath taught
me more wit than ever I learned before in my life;
and I paid nothing for it neither, but was paid for
my learning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Out, alas, sir! cozenage, mere cozenage!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Where be my horses? speak well of them, varletto.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BARDOLPH
SPEECH.LINE: Run away with the cozeners; for so soon as I came
beyond Eton, they threw me off from behind one of
them, in a slough of mire; and set spurs and away,
like three German devils, three Doctor Faustuses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: They are gone but to meet the duke, villain: do not
say they be fled; Germans are honest men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Where is mine host?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: What is the matter, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Have a care of your entertainments: there is a
friend of mine come to town tells me there is three
cozen-germans that has cozened all the hosts of
Readins, of Maidenhead, of Colebrook, of horses and
money. I tell you for good will, look you: you
are wise and full of gibes and vlouting-stocks, and
'tis not convenient you should be cozened. Fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Vere is mine host de Jarteer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Here, master doctor, in perplexity and doubtful dilemma.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot tell vat is dat: but it is tell-a me dat
you make grand preparation for a duke de Jamany: by
my trot, dere is no duke dat the court is know to
come. I tell you for good vill: adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Hue and cry, villain, go! Assist me, knight. I am
undone! Fly, run, hue and cry, villain! I am undone!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I would all the world might be cozened; for I have
been cozened and beaten too. If it should come to
the ear of the court, how I have been transformed
and how my transformation hath been washed and
cudgelled, they would melt me out of my fat drop by
drop and liquor fishermen's boots with me; I warrant
they would whip me with their fine wits till I were
as crest-fallen as a dried pear. I never prospered
since I forswore myself at primero. Well, if my
wind were but long enough to say my prayers, I would repent.
Now, whence come you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: From the two parties, forsooth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: The devil take one party and his dam the other! and
so they shall be both bestowed. I have suffered more
for their sakes, more than the villanous inconstancy
of man's disposition is able to bear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: And have not they suffered? Yes, I warrant;
speciously one of them; Mistress Ford, good heart,
is beaten black and blue, that you cannot see a
white spot about her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What tellest thou me of black and blue? I was
beaten myself into all the colours of the rainbow;
and I was like to be apprehended for the witch of
Brentford: but that my admirable dexterity of wit,
my counterfeiting the action of an old woman,
delivered me, the knave constable had set me i' the
stocks, i' the common stocks, for a witch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, let me speak with you in your chamber: you
shall hear how things go; and, I warrant, to your
content. Here is a letter will say somewhat. Good
hearts, what ado here is to bring you together!
Sure, one of you does not serve heaven well, that
you are so crossed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come up into my chamber.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. Another room in the Garter Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Master Fenton, talk not to me; my mind is heavy: I
will give over all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Yet hear me speak. Assist me in my purpose,
And, as I am a gentleman, I'll give thee
A hundred pound in gold more than your loss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: I will hear you, Master Fenton; and I will at the
least keep your counsel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: From time to time I have acquainted you
With the dear love I bear to fair Anne Page;
Who mutually hath answer'd my affection,
So far forth as herself might be her chooser,
Even to my wish: I have a letter from her
Of such contents as you will wonder at;
The mirth whereof so larded with my matter,
That neither singly can be manifested,
Without the show of both; fat Falstaff
Hath a great scene: the image of the jest
I'll show you here at large. Hark, good mine host.
To-night at Herne's oak, just 'twixt twelve and one,
Must my sweet Nan present the Fairy Queen;
The purpose why, is here: in which disguise,
While other jests are something rank on foot,
Her father hath commanded her to slip
Away with Slender and with him at Eton
Immediately to marry: she hath consented: Now, sir,
Her mother, ever strong against that match
And firm for Doctor Caius, hath appointed
That he shall likewise shuffle her away,
While other sports are tasking of their minds,
And at the deanery, where a priest attends,
Straight marry her: to this her mother's plot
She seemingly obedient likewise hath
Made promise to the doctor. Now, thus it rests:
Her father means she shall be all in white,
And in that habit, when Slender sees his time
To take her by the hand and bid her go,
She shall go with him: her mother hath intended,
The better to denote her to the doctor,
For they must all be mask'd and vizarded,
That quaint in green she shall be loose enrobed,
With ribands pendent, flaring 'bout her head;
And when the doctor spies his vantage ripe,
To pinch her by the hand, and, on that token,
The maid hath given consent to go with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Which means she to deceive, father or mother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: Both, my good host, to go along with me:
And here it rests, that you'll procure the vicar
To stay for me at church 'twixt twelve and one,
And, in the lawful name of marrying,
To give our hearts united ceremony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Host
SPEECH.LINE: Well, husband your device; I'll to the vicar:
Bring you the maid, you shall not lack a priest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: So shall I evermore be bound to thee;
Besides, I'll make a present recompense.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A room in the Garter Inn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, no more prattling; go. I'll hold. This is
the third time; I hope good luck lies in odd
numbers. Away I go. They say there is divinity in
odd numbers, either in nativity, chance, or death. Away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: I'll provide you a chain; and I'll do what I can to
get you a pair of horns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Away, I say; time wears: hold up your head, and mince.
How now, Master Brook! Master Brook, the matter
will be known to-night, or never. Be you in the
Park about midnight, at Herne's oak, and you shall
see wonders.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Went you not to her yesterday, sir, as you told me
you had appointed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I went to her, Master Brook, as you see, like a poor
old man: but I came from her, Master Brook, like a
poor old woman. That same knave Ford, her husband,
hath the finest mad devil of jealousy in him,
Master Brook, that ever governed frenzy. I will tell
you: he beat me grievously, in the shape of a
woman; for in the shape of man, Master Brook, I fear
not Goliath with a weaver's beam; because I know
also life is a shuttle. I am in haste; go along
with me: I'll tell you all, Master Brook. Since I
plucked geese, played truant and whipped top, I knew
not what 'twas to be beaten till lately. Follow
me: I'll tell you strange things of this knave
Ford, on whom to-night I will be revenged, and I
will deliver his wife into your hand. Follow.
Strange things in hand, Master Brook! Follow.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Windsor Park.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come; we'll couch i' the castle-ditch till we
see the light of our fairies. Remember, son Slender,
my daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, forsooth; I have spoke with her and we have a
nay-word how to know one another: I come to her in
white, and cry 'mum;' she cries 'budget;' and by
that we know one another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHALLOW
SPEECH.LINE: That's good too: but what needs either your 'mum'
or her 'budget?' the white will decipher her well
enough. It hath struck ten o'clock.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: The night is dark; light and spirits will become it
well. Heaven prosper our sport! No man means evil
but the devil, and we shall know him by his horns.
Let's away; follow me.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A street leading to the Park.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MISTRESS PAGE, MISTRESS FORD, and DOCTOR CAIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Master doctor, my daughter is in green: when you
see your time, take her by the band, away with her
to the deanery, and dispatch it quickly. Go before
into the Park: we two must go together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know vat I have to do. Adieu.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, sir.
My husband will not rejoice so much at the abuse of
Falstaff as he will chafe at the doctor's marrying
my daughter: but 'tis no matter; better a little
chiding than a great deal of heart-break.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Where is Nan now and her troop of fairies, and the
Welsh devil Hugh?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: They are all couched in a pit hard by Herne's oak,
with obscured lights; which, at the very instant of
Falstaff's and our meeting, they will at once
display to the night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: That cannot choose but amaze him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: If he be not amazed, he will be mocked; if he be
amazed, he will every way be mocked.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: We'll betray him finely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Against such lewdsters and their lechery
Those that betray them do no treachery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: The hour draws on. To the oak, to the oak!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Windsor Park.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS, disguised, with others as Fairies

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Trib, trib, fairies; come; and remember your parts:
be pold, I pray you; follow me into the pit; and
when I give the watch-'ords, do as I pid you:
come, come; trib, trib.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another part of the Park.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: The Windsor bell hath struck twelve; the minute
draws on. Now, the hot-blooded gods assist me!
Remember, Jove, thou wast a bull for thy Europa; love
set on thy horns. O powerful love! that, in some
respects, makes a beast a man, in some other, a man
a beast. You were also, Jupiter, a swan for the love
of Leda. O omnipotent Love! how near the god drew
to the complexion of a goose! A fault done first in
the form of a beast. O Jove, a beastly fault! And
then another fault in the semblance of a fowl; think
on 't, Jove; a foul fault! When gods have hot
backs, what shall poor men do? For me, I am here a
Windsor stag; and the fattest, I think, i' the
forest. Send me a cool rut-time, Jove, or who can
blame me to piss my tallow? Who comes here? my
doe?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MISTRESS FORD and MISTRESS PAGE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John! art thou there, my deer? my male deer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: My doe with the black scut! Let the sky rain
potatoes; let it thunder to the tune of Green
Sleeves, hail kissing-comfits and snow eringoes; let
there come a tempest of provocation, I will shelter me here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Page is come with me, sweetheart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Divide me like a bribe buck, each a haunch: I will
keep my sides to myself, my shoulders for the fellow
of this walk, and my horns I bequeath your husbands.
Am I a woodman, ha? Speak I like Herne the hunter?
Why, now is Cupid a child of conscience; he makes
restitution. As I am a true spirit, welcome!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, what noise?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Heaven forgive our sins

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: What should this be?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Away, away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I think the devil will not have me damned, lest the
oil that's in me should set hell on fire; he would
never else cross me thus.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SIR HUGH EVANS, disguised as before; PISTOL, as Hobgoblin; MISTRESS QUICKLY, ANNE PAGE, and others, as Fairies, with tapers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Fairies, black, grey, green, and white,
You moonshine revellers and shades of night,
You orphan heirs of fixed destiny,
Attend your office and your quality.
Crier Hobgoblin, make the fairy oyes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISTOL
SPEECH.LINE: Elves, list your names; silence, you airy toys.
Cricket, to Windsor chimneys shalt thou leap:
Where fires thou find'st unraked and hearths unswept,
There pinch the maids as blue as bilberry:
Our radiant queen hates sluts and sluttery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: They are fairies; he that speaks to them shall die:
I'll wink and couch: no man their works must eye.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Where's Bede? Go you, and where you find a maid
That, ere she sleep, has thrice her prayers said,
Raise up the organs of her fantasy;
Sleep she as sound as careless infancy:
But those as sleep and think not on their sins,
Pinch them, arms, legs, backs, shoulders, sides and shins.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: About, about;
Search Windsor Castle, elves, within and out:
Strew good luck, ouphes, on every sacred room:
That it may stand till the perpetual doom,
In state as wholesome as in state 'tis fit,
Worthy the owner, and the owner it.
The several chairs of order look you scour
With juice of balm and every precious flower:
Each fair instalment, coat, and several crest,
With loyal blazon, evermore be blest!
And nightly, meadow-fairies, look you sing,
Like to the Garter's compass, in a ring:
The expressure that it bears, green let it be,
More fertile-fresh than all the field to see;
And 'Honi soit qui mal y pense' write
In emerald tufts, flowers purple, blue and white;
Let sapphire, pearl and rich embroidery,
Buckled below fair knighthood's bending knee:
Fairies use flowers for their charactery.
Away; disperse: but till 'tis one o'clock,
Our dance of custom round about the oak
Of Herne the hunter, let us not forget.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, lock hand in hand; yourselves in order set
And twenty glow-worms shall our lanterns be,
To guide our measure round about the tree.
But, stay; I smell a man of middle-earth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Heavens defend me from that Welsh fairy, lest he
transform me to a piece of cheese!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISTOL
SPEECH.LINE: Vile worm, thou wast o'erlook'd even in thy birth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: With trial-fire touch me his finger-end:
If he be chaste, the flame will back descend
And turn him to no pain; but if he start,
It is the flesh of a corrupted heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PISTOL
SPEECH.LINE: A trial, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, will this wood take fire?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: They burn him with their tapers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Oh, Oh, Oh!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS QUICKLY
SPEECH.LINE: Corrupt, corrupt, and tainted in desire!
About him, fairies; sing a scornful rhyme;
And, as you trip, still pinch him to your time.
Fie on sinful fantasy!
Fie on lust and luxury!
Lust is but a bloody fire,
Kindled with unchaste desire,
Fed in heart, whose flames aspire
As thoughts do blow them, higher and higher.
Pinch him, fairies, mutually;
Pinch him for his villany;
Pinch him, and burn him, and turn him about,
Till candles and starlight and moonshine be out.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: During this song they pinch FALSTAFF. DOCTOR CAIUS comes one way, and steals away a boy in green; SLENDER another way, and takes off a boy in white; and FENTON comes and steals away ANN PAGE. A noise of hunting is heard within. All the Fairies run away. FALSTAFF pulls off his buck's head, and rises
Enter PAGE, FORD, MISTRESS PAGE, and MISTRESS FORD

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, do not fly; I think we have watch'd you now
Will none but Herne the hunter serve your turn?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, come, hold up the jest no higher
Now, good Sir John, how like you Windsor wives?
See you these, husband? do not these fair yokes
Become the forest better than the town?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Now, sir, who's a cuckold now? Master Brook,
Falstaff's a knave, a cuckoldly knave; here are his
horns, Master Brook: and, Master Brook, he hath
enjoyed nothing of Ford's but his buck-basket, his
cudgel, and twenty pounds of money, which must be
paid to Master Brook; his horses are arrested for
it, Master Brook.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John, we have had ill luck; we could never meet.
I will never take you for my love again; but I will
always count you my deer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I do begin to perceive that I am made an ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and an ox too: both the proofs are extant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: And these are not fairies? I was three or four
times in the thought they were not fairies: and yet
the guiltiness of my mind, the sudden surprise of my
powers, drove the grossness of the foppery into a
received belief, in despite of the teeth of all
rhyme and reason, that they were fairies. See now
how wit may be made a Jack-a-Lent, when 'tis upon
ill employment!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir John Falstaff, serve Got, and leave your
desires, and fairies will not pinse you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, fairy Hugh.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: And leave your jealousies too, I pray you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: I will never mistrust my wife again till thou art
able to woo her in good English.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Have I laid my brain in the sun and dried it, that
it wants matter to prevent so gross o'erreaching as
this? Am I ridden with a Welsh goat too? shall I
have a coxcomb of frize? 'Tis time I were choked
with a piece of toasted cheese.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: Seese is not good to give putter; your belly is all putter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: 'Seese' and 'putter'! have I lived to stand at the
taunt of one that makes fritters of English? This
is enough to be the decay of lust and late-walking
through the realm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why Sir John, do you think, though we would have the
virtue out of our hearts by the head and shoulders
and have given ourselves without scruple to hell,
that ever the devil could have made you our delight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: What, a hodge-pudding? a bag of flax?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: A puffed man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Old, cold, withered and of intolerable entrails?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And one that is as slanderous as Satan?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: And as poor as Job?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: And as wicked as his wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR HUGH EVANS
SPEECH.LINE: And given to fornications, and to taverns and sack
and wine and metheglins, and to drinkings and
swearings and starings, pribbles and prabbles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I am your theme: you have the start of me; I
am dejected; I am not able to answer the Welsh
flannel; ignorance itself is a plummet o'er me: use
me as you will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, we'll bring you to Windsor, to one
Master Brook, that you have cozened of money, to
whom you should have been a pander: over and above
that you have suffered, I think to repay that money
will be a biting affliction.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Yet be cheerful, knight: thou shalt eat a posset
to-night at my house; where I will desire thee to
laugh at my wife, that now laughs at thee: tell her
Master Slender hath married her daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Doctors doubt that: if Anne Page be my
daughter, she is, by this, Doctor Caius' wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Whoa ho! ho, father Page!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Son, how now! how now, son! have you dispatched?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: Dispatched! I'll make the best in Gloucestershire
know on't; would I were hanged, la, else.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Of what, son?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: I came yonder at Eton to marry Mistress Anne Page,
and she's a great lubberly boy. If it had not been
i' the church, I would have swinged him, or he
should have swinged me. If I did not think it had
been Anne Page, would I might never stir!--and 'tis
a postmaster's boy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Upon my life, then, you took the wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: What need you tell me that? I think so, when I took
a boy for a girl. If I had been married to him, for
all he was in woman's apparel, I would not have had
him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this is your own folly. Did not I tell you how
you should know my daughter by her garments?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SLENDER
SPEECH.LINE: I went to her in white, and cried 'mum,' and she
cried 'budget,' as Anne and I had appointed; and yet
it was not Anne, but a postmaster's boy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Good George, be not angry: I knew of your purpose;
turned my daughter into green; and, indeed, she is
now with the doctor at the deanery, and there married.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Vere is Mistress Page? By gar, I am cozened: I ha'
married un garcon, a boy; un paysan, by gar, a boy;
it is not Anne Page: by gar, I am cozened.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, did you take her in green?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOCTOR CAIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, by gar, and 'tis a boy: by gar, I'll raise all Windsor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: This is strange. Who hath got the right Anne?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: My heart misgives me: here comes Master Fenton.
How now, Master Fenton!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANNE PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, good father! good my mother, pardon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Now, mistress, how chance you went not with Master Slender?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Why went you not with master doctor, maid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FENTON
SPEECH.LINE: You do amaze her: hear the truth of it.
You would have married her most shamefully,
Where there was no proportion held in love.
The truth is, she and I, long since contracted,
Are now so sure that nothing can dissolve us.
The offence is holy that she hath committed;
And this deceit loses the name of craft,
Of disobedience, or unduteous title,
Since therein she doth evitate and shun
A thousand irreligious cursed hours,
Which forced marriage would have brought upon her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Stand not amazed; here is no remedy:
In love the heavens themselves do guide the state;
Money buys lands, and wives are sold by fate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad, though you have ta'en a special stand to
strike at me, that your arrow hath glanced.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Well, what remedy? Fenton, heaven give thee joy!
What cannot be eschew'd must be embraced.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FALSTAFF
SPEECH.LINE: When night-dogs run, all sorts of deer are chased.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MISTRESS PAGE
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will muse no further. Master Fenton,
Heaven give you many, many merry days!
Good husband, let us every one go home,
And laugh this sport o'er by a country fire;
Sir John and all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FORD
SPEECH.LINE: Let it be so. Sir John,
To Master Brook you yet shall hold your word
For he tonight shall lie with Mistress Ford.

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: SIWARD, Earl of Northumberland, general of the English forces.
SEYTON, an officer attending on Macbeth.
Lords, Gentlemen, Officers, Soldiers, Murderers, Attendants, and Messengers.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A desert place.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Thunder and lightning. Enter three Witches

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: When shall we three meet again
In thunder, lightning, or in rain?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: When the hurlyburly's done,
When the battle's lost and won.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: That will be ere the set of sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Where the place?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the heath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: There to meet with Macbeth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: I come, Graymalkin!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Paddock calls.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: Fair is foul, and foul is fair:
Hover through the fog and filthy air.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A camp near Forres.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum within. Enter DUNCAN, MALCOLM, DONALBAIN, LENNOX, with Attendants, meeting a bleeding Sergeant

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: What bloody man is that? He can report,
As seemeth by his plight, of the revolt
The newest state.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALCOLM
SPEECH.LINE: This is the sergeant
Who like a good and hardy soldier fought
'Gainst my captivity. Hail, brave friend!
Say to the king the knowledge of the broil
As thou didst leave it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sergeant
SPEECH.LINE: Doubtful it stood;
As two spent swimmers, that do cling together
And choke their art. The merciless Macdonwald--
Worthy to be a rebel, for to that
The multiplying villanies of nature
Do swarm upon him--from the western isles
Of kerns and gallowglasses is supplied;
And fortune, on his damned quarrel smiling,
Show'd like a rebel's whore: but all's too weak:
For brave Macbeth--well he deserves that name--
Disdaining fortune, with his brandish'd steel,
Which smoked with bloody execution,
Like valour's minion carved out his passage
Till he faced the slave;
Which ne'er shook hands, nor bade farewell to him,
Till he unseam'd him from the nave to the chaps,
And fix'd his head upon our battlements.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: O valiant cousin! worthy gentleman!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sergeant
SPEECH.LINE: As whence the sun 'gins his reflection
Shipwrecking storms and direful thunders break,
So from that spring whence comfort seem'd to come
Discomfort swells. Mark, king of Scotland, mark:
No sooner justice had with valour arm'd
Compell'd these skipping kerns to trust their heels,
But the Norweyan lord surveying vantage,
With furbish'd arms and new supplies of men
Began a fresh assault.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: Dismay'd not this
Our captains, Macbeth and Banquo?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sergeant
SPEECH.LINE: Yes;
As sparrows eagles, or the hare the lion.
If I say sooth, I must report they were
As cannons overcharged with double cracks, so they
Doubly redoubled strokes upon the foe:
Except they meant to bathe in reeking wounds,
Or memorise another Golgotha,
I cannot tell.
But I am faint, my gashes cry for help.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: So well thy words become thee as thy wounds;
They smack of honour both. Go get him surgeons.
Who comes here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALCOLM
SPEECH.LINE: The worthy thane of Ross.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LENNOX
SPEECH.LINE: What a haste looks through his eyes! So should he look
That seems to speak things strange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: God save the king!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: Whence camest thou, worthy thane?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: From Fife, great king;
Where the Norweyan banners flout the sky
And fan our people cold. Norway himself,
With terrible numbers,
Assisted by that most disloyal traitor
The thane of Cawdor, began a dismal conflict;
Till that Bellona's bridegroom, lapp'd in proof,
Confronted him with self-comparisons,
Point against point rebellious, arm 'gainst arm.
Curbing his lavish spirit: and, to conclude,
The victory fell on us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: Great happiness!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: That now
Sweno, the Norways' king, craves composition:
Nor would we deign him burial of his men
Till he disbursed at Saint Colme's inch
Ten thousand dollars to our general use.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: No more that thane of Cawdor shall deceive
Our bosom interest: go pronounce his present death,
And with his former title greet Macbeth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll see it done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUNCAN
SPEECH.LINE: What he hath lost noble Macbeth hath won.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A heath near Forres.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Where hast thou been, sister?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Killing swine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Sister, where thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: A sailor's wife had chestnuts in her lap,
And munch'd, and munch'd, and munch'd:--
'Give me,' quoth I:
'Aroint thee, witch!' the rump-fed ronyon cries.
Her husband's to Aleppo gone, master o' the Tiger:
But in a sieve I'll thither sail,
And, like a rat without a tail,
I'll do, I'll do, and I'll do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: I'll give thee a wind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Thou'rt kind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: And I another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: I myself have all the other,
And the very ports they blow,
All the quarters that they know
I' the shipman's card.
I will drain him dry as hay:
Sleep shall neither night nor day
Hang upon his pent-house lid;
He shall live a man forbid:
Weary se'nnights nine times nine
Shall he dwindle, peak and pine:
Though his bark cannot be lost,
Yet it shall be tempest-tost.
Look what I have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Show me, show me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Here I have a pilot's thumb,
Wreck'd as homeward he did come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: A drum, a drum!
Macbeth doth come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: The weird sisters, hand in hand,
Posters of the sea and land,
Thus do go about, about:
Thrice to thine and thrice to mine
And thrice again, to make up nine.
Peace! the charm's wound up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: So foul and fair a day I have not seen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: How far is't call'd to Forres? What are these
So wither'd and so wild in their attire,
That look not like the inhabitants o' the earth,
And yet are on't? Live you? or are you aught
That man may question? You seem to understand me,
By each at once her chappy finger laying
Upon her skinny lips: you should be women,
And yet your beards forbid me to interpret
That you are so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: Speak, if you can: what are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: All hail, Macbeth! hail to thee, thane of Glamis!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: All hail, Macbeth, hail to thee, thane of Cawdor!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: All hail, Macbeth, thou shalt be king hereafter!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: Good sir, why do you start; and seem to fear
Things that do sound so fair? I' the name of truth,
Are ye fantastical, or that indeed
Which outwardly ye show? My noble partner
You greet with present grace and great prediction
Of noble having and of royal hope,
That he seems rapt withal: to me you speak not.
If you can look into the seeds of time,
And say which grain will grow and which will not,
Speak then to me, who neither beg nor fear
Your favours nor your hate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Hail!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Hail!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Hail!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Lesser than Macbeth, and greater.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Not so happy, yet much happier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt get kings, though thou be none:
So all hail, Macbeth and Banquo!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Witch
SPEECH.LINE: Banquo and Macbeth, all hail!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, you imperfect speakers, tell me more:
By Sinel's death I know I am thane of Glamis;
But how of Cawdor? the thane of Cawdor lives,
A prosperous gentleman; and to be king
Stands not within the prospect of belief,
No more than to be Cawdor. Say from whence
You owe this strange intelligence? or why
Upon this blasted heath you stop our way
With such prophetic greeting? Speak, I charge you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: The earth hath bubbles, as the water has,
And these are of them. Whither are they vanish'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: Into the air; and what seem'd corporal melted
As breath into the wind. Would they had stay'd!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: Were such things here as we do speak about?
Or have we eaten on the insane root
That takes the reason prisoner?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: Your children shall be kings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: You shall be king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MACBETH
SPEECH.LINE: And thane of Cawdor too: went it not so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BANQUO
SPEECH.LINE: To the selfsame tune and words. Who's here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: The king hath happily received, Macbeth,
The news of thy success; and when he reads
Thy personal venture in the rebels' fight,
His wonders and his praises do contend
Which should be thine or his: silenced with that,
In viewing o'er the rest o' the selfsame day,
He finds thee in the stout Norweyan ranks,
Nothing afeard of what thyself didst make,
Strange images of death. As thick as hail
Came post with post; and every one did bear
Thy praises in his kingdom's great defence,
And pour'd them down before him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANGUS
SPEECH.LINE: We are sent
To give thee from our royal master thanks;
Only to herald thee into his sight,
Not pay thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROSS
SPEECH.LINE: And, for an earnest of a greater honour,
He bade me, from him, call thee thane of Cawdor:
