Spits in the face of heaven, is no bar
To stop the foreign spirits, but they come,
As o'er a brook, to see fair Portia.
One of these three contains her heavenly picture.
Is't like that lead contains her? 'Twere damnation
To think so base a thought: it were too gross
To rib her cerecloth in the obscure grave.
Or shall I think in silver she's immured,
Being ten times undervalued to tried gold?
O sinful thought! Never so rich a gem
Was set in worse than gold. They have in England
A coin that bears the figure of an angel
Stamped in gold, but that's insculp'd upon;
But here an angel in a golden bed
Lies all within. Deliver me the key:
Here do I choose, and thrive I as I may!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: There, take it, prince; and if my form lie there,
Then I am yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MOROCCO
SPEECH.LINE: O hell! what have we here?
A carrion Death, within whose empty eye
There is a written scroll! I'll read the writing.
All that glitters is not gold;
Often have you heard that told:
Many a man his life hath sold
But my outside to behold:
Gilded tombs do worms enfold.
Had you been as wise as bold,
Young in limbs, in judgment old,
Your answer had not been inscroll'd:
Fare you well; your suit is cold.
Cold, indeed; and labour lost:
Then, farewell, heat, and welcome, frost!
Portia, adieu. I have too grieved a heart
To take a tedious leave: thus losers part.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exit with his train. Flourish of cornets

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: A gentle riddance. Draw the curtains, go.
Let all of his complexion choose me so.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VIII. Venice. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, man, I saw Bassanio under sail:
With him is Gratiano gone along;
And in their ship I am sure Lorenzo is not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: The villain Jew with outcries raised the duke,
Who went with him to search Bassanio's ship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: He came too late, the ship was under sail:
But there the duke was given to understand
That in a gondola were seen together
Lorenzo and his amorous Jessica:
Besides, Antonio certified the duke
They were not with Bassanio in his ship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I never heard a passion so confused,
So strange, outrageous, and so variable,
As the dog Jew did utter in the streets:
'My daughter! O my ducats! O my daughter!
Fled with a Christian! O my Christian ducats!
Justice! the law! my ducats, and my daughter!
A sealed bag, two sealed bags of ducats,
Of double ducats, stolen from me by my daughter!
And jewels, two stones, two rich and precious stones,
Stolen by my daughter! Justice! find the girl;
She hath the stones upon her, and the ducats.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, all the boys in Venice follow him,
Crying, his stones, his daughter, and his ducats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let good Antonio look he keep his day,
Or he shall pay for this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, well remember'd.
I reason'd with a Frenchman yesterday,
Who told me, in the narrow seas that part
The French and English, there miscarried
A vessel of our country richly fraught:
I thought upon Antonio when he told me;
And wish'd in silence that it were not his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: You were best to tell Antonio what you hear;
Yet do not suddenly, for it may grieve him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: A kinder gentleman treads not the earth.
I saw Bassanio and Antonio part:
Bassanio told him he would make some speed
Of his return: he answer'd, 'Do not so;
Slubber not business for my sake, Bassanio
But stay the very riping of the time;
And for the Jew's bond which he hath of me,
Let it not enter in your mind of love:
Be merry, and employ your chiefest thoughts
To courtship and such fair ostents of love
As shall conveniently become you there:'
And even there, his eye being big with tears,
Turning his face, he put his hand behind him,
And with affection wondrous sensible
He wrung Bassanio's hand; and so they parted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I think he only loves the world for him.
I pray thee, let us go and find him out
And quicken his embraced heaviness
With some delight or other.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Do we so.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IX. Belmont. A room in PORTIA'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Quick, quick, I pray thee; draw the curtain straight:
The Prince of Arragon hath ta'en his oath,
And comes to his election presently.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish of cornets. Enter the PRINCE OF ARRAGON, PORTIA, and their trains

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Behold, there stand the caskets, noble prince:
If you choose that wherein I am contain'd,
Straight shall our nuptial rites be solemnized:
But if you fail, without more speech, my lord,
You must be gone from hence immediately.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARRAGON
SPEECH.LINE: I am enjoin'd by oath to observe three things:
First, never to unfold to any one
Which casket 'twas I chose; next, if I fail
Of the right casket, never in my life
To woo a maid in way of marriage: Lastly,
If I do fail in fortune of my choice,
Immediately to leave you and be gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: To these injunctions every one doth swear
That comes to hazard for my worthless self.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARRAGON
SPEECH.LINE: And so have I address'd me. Fortune now
To my heart's hope! Gold; silver; and base lead.
'Who chooseth me must give and hazard all he hath.'
You shall look fairer, ere I give or hazard.
What says the golden chest? ha! let me see:
'Who chooseth me shall gain what many men desire.'
What many men desire! that 'many' may be meant
By the fool multitude, that choose by show,
Not learning more than the fond eye doth teach;
Which pries not to the interior, but, like the martlet,
Builds in the weather on the outward wall,
Even in the force and road of casualty.
I will not choose what many men desire,
Because I will not jump with common spirits
And rank me with the barbarous multitudes.
Why, then to thee, thou silver treasure-house;
Tell me once more what title thou dost bear:
'Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves:'
And well said too; for who shall go about
To cozen fortune and be honourable
Without the stamp of merit? Let none presume
To wear an undeserved dignity.
O, that estates, degrees and offices
Were not derived corruptly, and that clear honour
Were purchased by the merit of the wearer!
How many then should cover that stand bare!
How many be commanded that command!
How much low peasantry would then be glean'd
From the true seed of honour! and how much honour
Pick'd from the chaff and ruin of the times
To be new-varnish'd! Well, but to my choice:
'Who chooseth me shall get as much as he deserves.'
I will assume desert. Give me a key for this,
And instantly unlock my fortunes here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Too long a pause for that which you find there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARRAGON
SPEECH.LINE: What's here? the portrait of a blinking idiot,
Presenting me a schedule! I will read it.
How much unlike art thou to Portia!
How much unlike my hopes and my deservings!
'Who chooseth me shall have as much as he deserves.'
Did I deserve no more than a fool's head?
Is that my prize? are my deserts no better?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: To offend, and judge, are distinct offices
And of opposed natures.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARRAGON
SPEECH.LINE: What is here?
The fire seven times tried this:
Seven times tried that judgment is,
That did never choose amiss.
Some there be that shadows kiss;
Such have but a shadow's bliss:
There be fools alive, I wis,
Silver'd o'er; and so was this.
Take what wife you will to bed,
I will ever be your head:
So be gone: you are sped.
Still more fool I shall appear
By the time I linger here
With one fool's head I came to woo,
But I go away with two.
Sweet, adieu. I'll keep my oath,
Patiently to bear my wroth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thus hath the candle singed the moth.
O, these deliberate fools! when they do choose,
They have the wisdom by their wit to lose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: The ancient saying is no heresy,
Hanging and wiving goes by destiny.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, draw the curtain, Nerissa.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Where is my lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Here: what would my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, there is alighted at your gate
A young Venetian, one that comes before
To signify the approaching of his lord;
From whom he bringeth sensible regreets,
To wit, besides commends and courteous breath,
Gifts of rich value. Yet I have not seen
So likely an ambassador of love:
A day in April never came so sweet,
To show how costly summer was at hand,
As this fore-spurrer comes before his lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: No more, I pray thee: I am half afeard
Thou wilt say anon he is some kin to thee,
Thou spend'st such high-day wit in praising him.
Come, come, Nerissa; for I long to see
Quick Cupid's post that comes so mannerly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Bassanio, lord Love, if thy will it be!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Venice. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, what news on the Rialto?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, yet it lives there uncheck'd that Antonio hath
a ship of rich lading wrecked on the narrow seas;
the Goodwins, I think they call the place; a very
dangerous flat and fatal, where the carcasses of many
a tall ship lie buried, as they say, if my gossip
Report be an honest woman of her word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I would she were as lying a gossip in that as ever
knapped ginger or made her neighbours believe she
wept for the death of a third husband. But it is
true, without any slips of prolixity or crossing the
plain highway of talk, that the good Antonio, the
honest Antonio,--O that I had a title good enough
to keep his name company!--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, the full stop.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! what sayest thou? Why, the end is, he hath
lost a ship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: I would it might prove the end of his losses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let me say 'amen' betimes, lest the devil cross my
prayer, for here he comes in the likeness of a Jew.
How now, Shylock! what news among the merchants?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: You know, none so well, none so well as you, of my
daughter's flight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: That's certain: I, for my part, knew the tailor
that made the wings she flew withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: And Shylock, for his own part, knew the bird was
fledged; and then it is the complexion of them all
to leave the dam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: She is damned for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: That's certain, if the devil may be her judge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: My own flesh and blood to rebel!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Out upon it, old carrion! rebels it at these years?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I say, my daughter is my flesh and blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: There is more difference between thy flesh and hers
than between jet and ivory; more between your bloods
than there is between red wine and rhenish. But
tell us, do you hear whether Antonio have had any
loss at sea or no?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: There I have another bad match: a bankrupt, a
prodigal, who dare scarce show his head on the
Rialto; a beggar, that was used to come so smug upon
the mart; let him look to his bond: he was wont to
call me usurer; let him look to his bond: he was
wont to lend money for a Christian courtesy; let him
look to his bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I am sure, if he forfeit, thou wilt not take
his flesh: what's that good for?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: To bait fish withal: if it will feed nothing else,
it will feed my revenge. He hath disgraced me, and
hindered me half a million; laughed at my losses,
mocked at my gains, scorned my nation, thwarted my
bargains, cooled my friends, heated mine
enemies; and what's his reason? I am a Jew. Hath
not a Jew eyes? hath not a Jew hands, organs,
dimensions, senses, affections, passions? fed with
the same food, hurt with the same weapons, subject
to the same diseases, healed by the same means,
warmed and cooled by the same winter and summer, as
a Christian is? If you prick us, do we not bleed?
if you tickle us, do we not laugh? if you poison
us, do we not die? and if you wrong us, shall we not
revenge? If we are like you in the rest, we will
resemble you in that. If a Jew wrong a Christian,
what is his humility? Revenge. If a Christian
wrong a Jew, what should his sufferance be by
Christian example? Why, revenge. The villany you
teach me, I will execute, and it shall go hard but I
will better the instruction.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Gentlemen, my master Antonio is at his house and
desires to speak with you both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: We have been up and down to seek him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes another of the tribe: a third cannot be
matched, unless the devil himself turn Jew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Tubal! what news from Genoa? hast thou
found my daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: I often came where I did hear of her, but cannot find her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, there, there, there, there! a diamond gone,
cost me two thousand ducats in Frankfort! The curse
never fell upon our nation till now; I never felt it
till now: two thousand ducats in that; and other
precious, precious jewels. I would my daughter
were dead at my foot, and the jewels in her ear!
would she were hearsed at my foot, and the ducats in
her coffin! No news of them? Why, so: and I know
not what's spent in the search: why, thou loss upon
loss! the thief gone with so much, and so much to
find the thief; and no satisfaction, no revenge:
nor no in luck stirring but what lights on my
shoulders; no sighs but of my breathing; no tears
but of my shedding.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, other men have ill luck too: Antonio, as I
heard in Genoa,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: What, what, what? ill luck, ill luck?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: Hath an argosy cast away, coming from Tripolis.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I thank God, I thank God. Is't true, is't true?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: I spoke with some of the sailors that escaped the wreck.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, good Tubal: good news, good news!
ha, ha! where? in Genoa?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: Your daughter spent in Genoa, as I heard, in one
night fourscore ducats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou stickest a dagger in me: I shall never see my
gold again: fourscore ducats at a sitting!
fourscore ducats!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: There came divers of Antonio's creditors in my
company to Venice, that swear he cannot choose but break.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I am very glad of it: I'll plague him; I'll torture
him: I am glad of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: One of them showed me a ring that he had of your
daughter for a monkey.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Out upon her! Thou torturest me, Tubal: it was my
turquoise; I had it of Leah when I was a bachelor:
I would not have given it for a wilderness of monkeys.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TUBAL
SPEECH.LINE: But Antonio is certainly undone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that's true, that's very true. Go, Tubal, fee
me an officer; bespeak him a fortnight before. I
will have the heart of him, if he forfeit; for, were
he out of Venice, I can make what merchandise I
will. Go, go, Tubal, and meet me at our synagogue;
go, good Tubal; at our synagogue, Tubal.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Belmont. A room in PORTIA'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BASSANIO, PORTIA, GRATIANO, NERISSA, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, tarry: pause a day or two
Before you hazard; for, in choosing wrong,
I lose your company: therefore forbear awhile.
There's something tells me, but it is not love,
I would not lose you; and you know yourself,
Hate counsels not in such a quality.
But lest you should not understand me well,--
And yet a maiden hath no tongue but thought,--
I would detain you here some month or two
Before you venture for me. I could teach you
How to choose right, but I am then forsworn;
So will I never be: so may you miss me;
But if you do, you'll make me wish a sin,
That I had been forsworn. Beshrew your eyes,
They have o'erlook'd me and divided me;
One half of me is yours, the other half yours,
Mine own, I would say; but if mine, then yours,
And so all yours. O, these naughty times
Put bars between the owners and their rights!
And so, though yours, not yours. Prove it so,
Let fortune go to hell for it, not I.
I speak too long; but 'tis to peize the time,
To eke it and to draw it out in length,
To stay you from election.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let me choose
For as I am, I live upon the rack.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the rack, Bassanio! then confess
What treason there is mingled with your love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: None but that ugly treason of mistrust,
Which makes me fear the enjoying of my love:
There may as well be amity and life
'Tween snow and fire, as treason and my love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but I fear you speak upon the rack,
Where men enforced do speak anything.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Promise me life, and I'll confess the truth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Well then, confess and live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Confess' and 'love'
Had been the very sum of my confession:
O happy torment, when my torturer
Doth teach me answers for deliverance!
But let me to my fortune and the caskets.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Away, then! I am lock'd in one of them:
If you do love me, you will find me out.
Nerissa and the rest, stand all aloof.
Let music sound while he doth make his choice;
Then, if he lose, he makes a swan-like end,
Fading in music: that the comparison
May stand more proper, my eye shall be the stream
And watery death-bed for him. He may win;
And what is music then? Then music is
Even as the flourish when true subjects bow
To a new-crowned monarch: such it is
As are those dulcet sounds in break of day
That creep into the dreaming bridegroom's ear,
And summon him to marriage. Now he goes,
With no less presence, but with much more love,
Than young Alcides, when he did redeem
The virgin tribute paid by howling Troy
To the sea-monster: I stand for sacrifice
The rest aloof are the Dardanian wives,
With bleared visages, come forth to view
The issue of the exploit. Go, Hercules!
Live thou, I live: with much, much more dismay
I view the fight than thou that makest the fray.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Music, whilst BASSANIO comments on the caskets to himself
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me where is fancy bred,
Or in the heart, or in the head?
How begot, how nourished?
Reply, reply.
It is engender'd in the eyes,
With gazing fed; and fancy dies
In the cradle where it lies.
Let us all ring fancy's knell
I'll begin it,--Ding, dong, bell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: Ding, dong, bell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: So may the outward shows be least themselves:
The world is still deceived with ornament.
In law, what plea so tainted and corrupt,
But, being seasoned with a gracious voice,
Obscures the show of evil? In religion,
What damned error, but some sober brow
Will bless it and approve it with a text,
Hiding the grossness with fair ornament?
There is no vice so simple but assumes
Some mark of virtue on his outward parts:
How many cowards, whose hearts are all as false
As stairs of sand, wear yet upon their chins
The beards of Hercules and frowning Mars;
Who, inward search'd, have livers white as milk;
And these assume but valour's excrement
To render them redoubted! Look on beauty,
And you shall see 'tis purchased by the weight;
Which therein works a miracle in nature,
Making them lightest that wear most of it:
So are those crisped snaky golden locks
Which make such wanton gambols with the wind,
Upon supposed fairness, often known
To be the dowry of a second head,
The skull that bred them in the sepulchre.
Thus ornament is but the guiled shore
To a most dangerous sea; the beauteous scarf
Veiling an Indian beauty; in a word,
The seeming truth which cunning times put on
To entrap the wisest. Therefore, thou gaudy gold,
Hard food for Midas, I will none of thee;
Nor none of thee, thou pale and common drudge
'Tween man and man: but thou, thou meagre lead,
Which rather threatenest than dost promise aught,
Thy paleness moves me more than eloquence;
And here choose I; joy be the consequence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Aside How all the other passions fleet to air,
As doubtful thoughts, and rash-embraced despair,
And shuddering fear, and green-eyed jealousy! O love,
Be moderate; allay thy ecstasy,
In measure rein thy joy; scant this excess.
I feel too much thy blessing: make it less,
For fear I surfeit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: What find I here?
Fair Portia's counterfeit! What demi-god
Hath come so near creation? Move these eyes?
Or whether, riding on the balls of mine,
Seem they in motion? Here are sever'd lips,
Parted with sugar breath: so sweet a bar
Should sunder such sweet friends. Here in her hairs
The painter plays the spider and hath woven
A golden mesh to entrap the hearts of men,
Faster than gnats in cobwebs; but her eyes,--
How could he see to do them? having made one,
Methinks it should have power to steal both his
And leave itself unfurnish'd. Yet look, how far
The substance of my praise doth wrong this shadow
In underprizing it, so far this shadow
Doth limp behind the substance. Here's the scroll,
The continent and summary of my fortune.
You that choose not by the view,
Chance as fair and choose as true!
Since this fortune falls to you,
Be content and seek no new,
If you be well pleased with this
And hold your fortune for your bliss,
Turn you where your lady is
And claim her with a loving kiss.
A gentle scroll. Fair lady, by your leave;
I come by note, to give and to receive.
Like one of two contending in a prize,
That thinks he hath done well in people's eyes,
Hearing applause and universal shout,
Giddy in spirit, still gazing in a doubt
Whether these pearls of praise be his or no;
So, thrice fair lady, stand I, even so;
As doubtful whether what I see be true,
Until confirm'd, sign'd, ratified by you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: You see me, Lord Bassanio, where I stand,
Such as I am: though for myself alone
I would not be ambitious in my wish,
To wish myself much better; yet, for you
I would be trebled twenty times myself;
A thousand times more fair, ten thousand times more rich;
That only to stand high in your account,
I might in virtue, beauties, livings, friends,
Exceed account; but the full sum of me
Is sum of something, which, to term in gross,
Is an unlesson'd girl, unschool'd, unpractised;
Happy in this, she is not yet so old
But she may learn; happier than this,
She is not bred so dull but she can learn;
Happiest of all is that her gentle spirit
Commits itself to yours to be directed,
As from her lord, her governor, her king.
Myself and what is mine to you and yours
Is now converted: but now I was the lord
Of this fair mansion, master of my servants,
Queen o'er myself: and even now, but now,
This house, these servants and this same myself
Are yours, my lord: I give them with this ring;
Which when you part from, lose, or give away,
Let it presage the ruin of your love
And be my vantage to exclaim on you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, you have bereft me of all words,
Only my blood speaks to you in my veins;
And there is such confusion in my powers,
As after some oration fairly spoke
By a beloved prince, there doth appear
Among the buzzing pleased multitude;
Where every something, being blent together,
Turns to a wild of nothing, save of joy,
Express'd and not express'd. But when this ring
Parts from this finger, then parts life from hence:
O, then be bold to say Bassanio's dead!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: My lord and lady, it is now our time,
That have stood by and seen our wishes prosper,
To cry, good joy: good joy, my lord and lady!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord Bassanio and my gentle lady,
I wish you all the joy that you can wish;
For I am sure you can wish none from me:
And when your honours mean to solemnize
The bargain of your faith, I do beseech you,
Even at that time I may be married too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: With all my heart, so thou canst get a wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your lordship, you have got me one.
My eyes, my lord, can look as swift as yours:
You saw the mistress, I beheld the maid;
You loved, I loved for intermission.
No more pertains to me, my lord, than you.
Your fortune stood upon the casket there,
And so did mine too, as the matter falls;
For wooing here until I sweat again,
And sweating until my very roof was dry
With oaths of love, at last, if promise last,
I got a promise of this fair one here
To have her love, provided that your fortune
Achieved her mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is this true, Nerissa?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, it is, so you stand pleased withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: And do you, Gratiano, mean good faith?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, faith, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Our feast shall be much honour'd in your marriage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: We'll play with them the first boy for a thousand ducats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: What, and stake down?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: No; we shall ne'er win at that sport, and stake down.
But who comes here? Lorenzo and his infidel? What,
and my old Venetian friend Salerio?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter LORENZO, JESSICA, and SALERIO, a Messenger from Venice

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Lorenzo and Salerio, welcome hither;
If that the youth of my new interest here
Have power to bid you welcome. By your leave,
I bid my very friends and countrymen,
Sweet Portia, welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: So do I, my lord:
They are entirely welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your honour. For my part, my lord,
My purpose was not to have seen you here;
But meeting with Salerio by the way,
He did entreat me, past all saying nay,
To come with him along.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: I did, my lord;
And I have reason for it. Signior Antonio
Commends him to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ere I ope his letter,
I pray you, tell me how my good friend doth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not sick, my lord, unless it be in mind;
Nor well, unless in mind: his letter there
Will show you his estate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Nerissa, cheer yon stranger; bid her welcome.
Your hand, Salerio: what's the news from Venice?
How doth that royal merchant, good Antonio?
I know he will be glad of our success;
We are the Jasons, we have won the fleece.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: I would you had won the fleece that he hath lost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: There are some shrewd contents in yon same paper,
That steals the colour from Bassanio's cheek:
Some dear friend dead; else nothing in the world
Could turn so much the constitution
Of any constant man. What, worse and worse!
With leave, Bassanio: I am half yourself,
And I must freely have the half of anything
That this same paper brings you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: O sweet Portia,
Here are a few of the unpleasant'st words
That ever blotted paper! Gentle lady,
When I did first impart my love to you,
I freely told you, all the wealth I had
Ran in my veins, I was a gentleman;
And then I told you true: and yet, dear lady,
Rating myself at nothing, you shall see
How much I was a braggart. When I told you
My state was nothing, I should then have told you
That I was worse than nothing; for, indeed,
I have engaged myself to a dear friend,
Engaged my friend to his mere enemy,
To feed my means. Here is a letter, lady;
The paper as the body of my friend,
And every word in it a gaping wound,
Issuing life-blood. But is it true, Salerio?
Have all his ventures fail'd? What, not one hit?
From Tripolis, from Mexico and England,
From Lisbon, Barbary and India?
And not one vessel 'scape the dreadful touch
Of merchant-marring rocks?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not one, my lord.
Besides, it should appear, that if he had
The present money to discharge the Jew,
He would not take it. Never did I know
A creature, that did bear the shape of man,
So keen and greedy to confound a man:
He plies the duke at morning and at night,
And doth impeach the freedom of the state,
If they deny him justice: twenty merchants,
The duke himself, and the magnificoes
Of greatest port, have all persuaded with him;
But none can drive him from the envious plea
Of forfeiture, of justice and his bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: When I was with him I have heard him swear
To Tubal and to Chus, his countrymen,
That he would rather have Antonio's flesh
Than twenty times the value of the sum
That he did owe him: and I know, my lord,
If law, authority and power deny not,
It will go hard with poor Antonio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is it your dear friend that is thus in trouble?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: The dearest friend to me, the kindest man,
The best-condition'd and unwearied spirit
In doing courtesies, and one in whom
The ancient Roman honour more appears
Than any that draws breath in Italy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: What sum owes he the Jew?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: For me three thousand ducats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: What, no more?
Pay him six thousand, and deface the bond;
Double six thousand, and then treble that,
Before a friend of this description
Shall lose a hair through Bassanio's fault.
First go with me to church and call me wife,
And then away to Venice to your friend;
For never shall you lie by Portia's side
With an unquiet soul. You shall have gold
To pay the petty debt twenty times over:
When it is paid, bring your true friend along.
My maid Nerissa and myself meantime
Will live as maids and widows. Come, away!
For you shall hence upon your wedding-day:
Bid your friends welcome, show a merry cheer:
Since you are dear bought, I will love you dear.
But let me hear the letter of your friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Reads Sweet Bassanio, my ships have all
miscarried, my creditors grow cruel, my estate is
very low, my bond to the Jew is forfeit; and since
in paying it, it is impossible I should live, all
debts are cleared between you and I, if I might but
see you at my death. Notwithstanding, use your
pleasure: if your love do not persuade you to come,
let not my letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: O love, dispatch all business, and be gone!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Since I have your good leave to go away,
I will make haste: but, till I come again,
No bed shall e'er be guilty of my stay,
No rest be interposer 'twixt us twain.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Venice. A street.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SHYLOCK, SALARINO, ANTONIO, and Gaoler

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Gaoler, look to him: tell not me of mercy;
This is the fool that lent out money gratis:
Gaoler, look to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me yet, good Shylock.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have my bond; speak not against my bond:
I have sworn an oath that I will have my bond.
Thou call'dst me dog before thou hadst a cause;
But, since I am a dog, beware my fangs:
The duke shall grant me justice. I do wonder,
Thou naughty gaoler, that thou art so fond
To come abroad with him at his request.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have my bond; I will not hear thee speak:
I'll have my bond; and therefore speak no more.
I'll not be made a soft and dull-eyed fool,
To shake the head, relent, and sigh, and yield
To Christian intercessors. Follow not;
I'll have no speaking: I will have my bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: It is the most impenetrable cur
That ever kept with men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let him alone:
I'll follow him no more with bootless prayers.
He seeks my life; his reason well I know:
I oft deliver'd from his forfeitures
Many that have at times made moan to me;
Therefore he hates me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALARINO
SPEECH.LINE: I am sure the duke
Will never grant this forfeiture to hold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: The duke cannot deny the course of law:
For the commodity that strangers have
With us in Venice, if it be denied,
Will much impeach the justice of his state;
Since that the trade and profit of the city
Consisteth of all nations. Therefore, go:
These griefs and losses have so bated me,
That I shall hardly spare a pound of flesh
To-morrow to my bloody creditor.
Well, gaoler, on. Pray God, Bassanio come
To see me pay his debt, and then I care not!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Belmont. A room in PORTIA'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PORTIA, NERISSA, LORENZO, JESSICA, and BALTHASAR

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, although I speak it in your presence,
You have a noble and a true conceit
Of godlike amity; which appears most strongly
In bearing thus the absence of your lord.
But if you knew to whom you show this honour,
How true a gentleman you send relief,
How dear a lover of my lord your husband,
I know you would be prouder of the work
Than customary bounty can enforce you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I never did repent for doing good,
Nor shall not now: for in companions
That do converse and waste the time together,
Whose souls do bear an equal yoke Of love,
There must be needs a like proportion
Of lineaments, of manners and of spirit;
Which makes me think that this Antonio,
Being the bosom lover of my lord,
Must needs be like my lord. If it be so,
How little is the cost I have bestow'd
In purchasing the semblance of my soul
From out the state of hellish misery!
This comes too near the praising of myself;
Therefore no more of it: hear other things.
Lorenzo, I commit into your hands
The husbandry and manage of my house
Until my lord's return: for mine own part,
I have toward heaven breathed a secret vow
To live in prayer and contemplation,
Only attended by Nerissa here,
Until her husband and my lord's return:
There is a monastery two miles off;
And there will we abide. I do desire you
Not to deny this imposition;
The which my love and some necessity
Now lays upon you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, with all my heart;
I shall obey you in all fair commands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: My people do already know my mind,
And will acknowledge you and Jessica
In place of Lord Bassanio and myself.
And so farewell, till we shall meet again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Fair thoughts and happy hours attend on you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: I wish your ladyship all heart's content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you for your wish, and am well pleased
To wish it back on you: fare you well Jessica.
Now, Balthasar,
As I have ever found thee honest-true,
So let me find thee still. Take this same letter,
And use thou all the endeavour of a man
In speed to Padua: see thou render this
Into my cousin's hand, Doctor Bellario;
And, look, what notes and garments he doth give thee,
Bring them, I pray thee, with imagined speed
Unto the tranect, to the common ferry
Which trades to Venice. Waste no time in words,
But get thee gone: I shall be there before thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BALTHASAR
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, I go with all convenient speed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, Nerissa; I have work in hand
That you yet know not of: we'll see our husbands
Before they think of us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Shall they see us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: They shall, Nerissa; but in such a habit,
That they shall think we are accomplished
With that we lack. I'll hold thee any wager,
When we are both accoutred like young men,
I'll prove the prettier fellow of the two,
And wear my dagger with the braver grace,
And speak between the change of man and boy
With a reed voice, and turn two mincing steps
Into a manly stride, and speak of frays
Like a fine bragging youth, and tell quaint lies,
How honourable ladies sought my love,
Which I denying, they fell sick and died;
I could not do withal; then I'll repent,
And wish for all that, that I had not killed them;
And twenty of these puny lies I'll tell,
That men shall swear I have discontinued school
Above a twelvemonth. I have within my mind
A thousand raw tricks of these bragging Jacks,
Which I will practise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, shall we turn to men?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, what a question's that,
If thou wert near a lewd interpreter!
But come, I'll tell thee all my whole device
When I am in my coach, which stays for us
At the park gate; and therefore haste away,
For we must measure twenty miles to-day.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The same. A garden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, truly; for, look you, the sins of the father
are to be laid upon the children: therefore, I
promise ye, I fear you. I was always plain with
you, and so now I speak my agitation of the matter:
therefore be of good cheer, for truly I think you
are damned. There is but one hope in it that can do
you any good; and that is but a kind of bastard
hope neither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: And what hope is that, I pray thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, you may partly hope that your father got you
not, that you are not the Jew's daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: That were a kind of bastard hope, indeed: so the
sins of my mother should be visited upon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Truly then I fear you are damned both by father and
mother: thus when I shun Scylla, your father, I
fall into Charybdis, your mother: well, you are
gone both ways.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: I shall be saved by my husband; he hath made me a
Christian.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, the more to blame he: we were Christians
enow before; e'en as many as could well live, one by
another. This making Christians will raise the
price of hogs: if we grow all to be pork-eaters, we
shall not shortly have a rasher on the coals for money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll tell my husband, Launcelot, what you say: here he comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: I shall grow jealous of you shortly, Launcelot, if
you thus get my wife into corners.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, you need not fear us, Lorenzo: Launcelot and I
are out. He tells me flatly, there is no mercy for
me in heaven, because I am a Jew's daughter: and he
says, you are no good member of the commonwealth,
for in converting Jews to Christians, you raise the
price of pork.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: I shall answer that better to the commonwealth than
you can the getting up of the negro's belly: the
Moor is with child by you, Launcelot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: It is much that the Moor should be more than reason:
but if she be less than an honest woman, she is
indeed more than I took her for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: How every fool can play upon the word! I think the
best grace of wit will shortly turn into silence,
and discourse grow commendable in none only but
parrots. Go in, sirrah; bid them prepare for dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: That is done, sir; they have all stomachs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Goodly Lord, what a wit-snapper are you! then bid
them prepare dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: That is done too, sir; only 'cover' is the word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Will you cover then, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Not so, sir, neither; I know my duty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Yet more quarrelling with occasion! Wilt thou show
the whole wealth of thy wit in an instant? I pray
tree, understand a plain man in his plain meaning:
go to thy fellows; bid them cover the table, serve
in the meat, and we will come in to dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: For the table, sir, it shall be served in; for the
meat, sir, it shall be covered; for your coming in
to dinner, sir, why, let it be as humours and
conceits shall govern.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: O dear discretion, how his words are suited!
The fool hath planted in his memory
An army of good words; and I do know
A many fools, that stand in better place,
Garnish'd like him, that for a tricksy word
Defy the matter. How cheerest thou, Jessica?
And now, good sweet, say thy opinion,
How dost thou like the Lord Bassanio's wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: Past all expressing. It is very meet
The Lord Bassanio live an upright life;
For, having such a blessing in his lady,
He finds the joys of heaven here on earth;
And if on earth he do not mean it, then
In reason he should never come to heaven
Why, if two gods should play some heavenly match
And on the wager lay two earthly women,
And Portia one, there must be something else
Pawn'd with the other, for the poor rude world
Hath not her fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Even such a husband
Hast thou of me as she is for a wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but ask my opinion too of that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: I will anon: first, let us go to dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, let me praise you while I have a stomach.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: No, pray thee, let it serve for table-talk;
' Then, howso'er thou speak'st, 'mong other things
I shall digest it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I'll set you forth.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Venice. A court of justice.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the DUKE, the Magnificoes, ANTONIO, BASSANIO, GRATIANO, SALERIO, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: What, is Antonio here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ready, so please your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry for thee: thou art come to answer
A stony adversary, an inhuman wretch
uncapable of pity, void and empty
From any dram of mercy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: I have heard
Your grace hath ta'en great pains to qualify
His rigorous course; but since he stands obdurate
And that no lawful means can carry me
Out of his envy's reach, I do oppose
My patience to his fury, and am arm'd
To suffer, with a quietness of spirit,
The very tyranny and rage of his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Go one, and call the Jew into the court.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: He is ready at the door: he comes, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Make room, and let him stand before our face.
Shylock, the world thinks, and I think so too,
That thou but lead'st this fashion of thy malice
To the last hour of act; and then 'tis thought
Thou'lt show thy mercy and remorse more strange
Than is thy strange apparent cruelty;
And where thou now exact'st the penalty,
Which is a pound of this poor merchant's flesh,
Thou wilt not only loose the forfeiture,
But, touch'd with human gentleness and love,
Forgive a moiety of the principal;
Glancing an eye of pity on his losses,
That have of late so huddled on his back,
Enow to press a royal merchant down
And pluck commiseration of his state
From brassy bosoms and rough hearts of flint,
From stubborn Turks and Tartars, never train'd
To offices of tender courtesy.
We all expect a gentle answer, Jew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I have possess'd your grace of what I purpose;
And by our holy Sabbath have I sworn
To have the due and forfeit of my bond:
If you deny it, let the danger light
Upon your charter and your city's freedom.
You'll ask me, why I rather choose to have
A weight of carrion flesh than to receive
Three thousand ducats: I'll not answer that:
But, say, it is my humour: is it answer'd?
What if my house be troubled with a rat
And I be pleased to give ten thousand ducats
To have it baned? What, are you answer'd yet?
Some men there are love not a gaping pig;
Some, that are mad if they behold a cat;
And others, when the bagpipe sings i' the nose,
Cannot contain their urine: for affection,
Mistress of passion, sways it to the mood
Of what it likes or loathes. Now, for your answer:
As there is no firm reason to be render'd,
Why he cannot abide a gaping pig;
Why he, a harmless necessary cat;
Why he, a woollen bagpipe; but of force
Must yield to such inevitable shame
As to offend, himself being offended;
So can I give no reason, nor I will not,
More than a lodged hate and a certain loathing
I bear Antonio, that I follow thus
A losing suit against him. Are you answer'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: This is no answer, thou unfeeling man,
To excuse the current of thy cruelty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I am not bound to please thee with my answers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Do all men kill the things they do not love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Hates any man the thing he would not kill?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Every offence is not a hate at first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: What, wouldst thou have a serpent sting thee twice?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, think you question with the Jew:
You may as well go stand upon the beach
And bid the main flood bate his usual height;
You may as well use question with the wolf
Why he hath made the ewe bleat for the lamb;
You may as well forbid the mountain pines
To wag their high tops and to make no noise,
When they are fretten with the gusts of heaven;
You may as well do anything most hard,
As seek to soften that--than which what's harder?--
His Jewish heart: therefore, I do beseech you,
Make no more offers, use no farther means,
But with all brief and plain conveniency
Let me have judgment and the Jew his will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: For thy three thousand ducats here is six.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: What judgment shall I dread, doing
Were in six parts and every part a ducat,
I would not draw them; I would have my bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: How shalt thou hope for mercy, rendering none?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: What judgment shall I dread, doing no wrong?
You have among you many a purchased slave,
Which, like your asses and your dogs and mules,
You use in abject and in slavish parts,
Because you bought them: shall I say to you,
Let them be free, marry them to your heirs?
Why sweat they under burthens? let their beds
Be made as soft as yours and let their palates
Be season'd with such viands? You will answer
'The slaves are ours:' so do I answer you:
The pound of flesh, which I demand of him,
Is dearly bought; 'tis mine and I will have it.
If you deny me, fie upon your law!
There is no force in the decrees of Venice.
I stand for judgment: answer; shall I have it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Upon my power I may dismiss this court,
Unless Bellario, a learned doctor,
Whom I have sent for to determine this,
Come here to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SALERIO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, here stays without
A messenger with letters from the doctor,
New come from Padua.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Bring us the letter; call the messenger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Good cheer, Antonio! What, man, courage yet!
The Jew shall have my flesh, blood, bones and all,
Ere thou shalt lose for me one drop of blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: I am a tainted wether of the flock,
Meetest for death: the weakest kind of fruit
Drops earliest to the ground; and so let me
You cannot better be employ'd, Bassanio,
Than to live still and write mine epitaph.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter NERISSA, dressed like a lawyer's clerk

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Came you from Padua, from Bellario?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: From both, my lord. Bellario greets your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why dost thou whet thy knife so earnestly?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: To cut the forfeiture from that bankrupt there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Not on thy sole, but on thy soul, harsh Jew,
Thou makest thy knife keen; but no metal can,
No, not the hangman's axe, bear half the keenness
Of thy sharp envy. Can no prayers pierce thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: No, none that thou hast wit enough to make.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: O, be thou damn'd, inexecrable dog!
And for thy life let justice be accused.
Thou almost makest me waver in my faith
To hold opinion with Pythagoras,
That souls of animals infuse themselves
Into the trunks of men: thy currish spirit
Govern'd a wolf, who, hang'd for human slaughter,
Even from the gallows did his fell soul fleet,
And, whilst thou lay'st in thy unhallow'd dam,
Infused itself in thee; for thy desires
Are wolvish, bloody, starved and ravenous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Till thou canst rail the seal from off my bond,
Thou but offend'st thy lungs to speak so loud:
Repair thy wit, good youth, or it will fall
To cureless ruin. I stand here for law.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: This letter from Bellario doth commend
A young and learned doctor to our court.
Where is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: He attendeth here hard by,
To know your answer, whether you'll admit him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: With all my heart. Some three or four of you
Go give him courteous conduct to this place.
Meantime the court shall hear Bellario's letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clerk
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace shall understand that at the receipt of
your letter I am very sick: but in the instant that
your messenger came, in loving visitation was with
me a young doctor of Rome; his name is Balthasar. I
acquainted him with the cause in controversy between
the Jew and Antonio the merchant: we turned o'er
many books together: he is furnished with my
opinion; which, bettered with his own learning, the
greatness whereof I cannot enough commend, comes
with him, at my importunity, to fill up your grace's
request in my stead. I beseech you, let his lack of
years be no impediment to let him lack a reverend
estimation; for I never knew so young a body with so
old a head. I leave him to your gracious
acceptance, whose trial shall better publish his
commendation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: You hear the learn'd Bellario, what he writes:
And here, I take it, is the doctor come.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter PORTIA, dressed like a doctor of laws
SPEECH.LINE: Give me your hand. Come you from old Bellario?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I did, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: You are welcome: take your place.
Are you acquainted with the difference
That holds this present question in the court?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I am informed thoroughly of the cause.
Which is the merchant here, and which the Jew?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Antonio and old Shylock, both stand forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is your name Shylock?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Shylock is my name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Of a strange nature is the suit you follow;
Yet in such rule that the Venetian law
Cannot impugn you as you do proceed.
You stand within his danger, do you not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, so he says.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Do you confess the bond?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: I do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Then must the Jew be merciful.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: On what compulsion must I? tell me that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: The quality of mercy is not strain'd,
It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven
Upon the place beneath: it is twice blest;
It blesseth him that gives and him that takes:
'Tis mightiest in the mightiest: it becomes
The throned monarch better than his crown;
His sceptre shows the force of temporal power,
The attribute to awe and majesty,
Wherein doth sit the dread and fear of kings;
But mercy is above this sceptred sway;
It is enthroned in the hearts of kings,
It is an attribute to God himself;
And earthly power doth then show likest God's
When mercy seasons justice. Therefore, Jew,
Though justice be thy plea, consider this,
That, in the course of justice, none of us
Should see salvation: we do pray for mercy;
And that same prayer doth teach us all to render
The deeds of mercy. I have spoke thus much
To mitigate the justice of thy plea;
Which if thou follow, this strict court of Venice
Must needs give sentence 'gainst the merchant there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: My deeds upon my head! I crave the law,
The penalty and forfeit of my bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is he not able to discharge the money?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, here I tender it for him in the court;
Yea, twice the sum: if that will not suffice,
I will be bound to pay it ten times o'er,
On forfeit of my hands, my head, my heart:
If this will not suffice, it must appear
That malice bears down truth. And I beseech you,
Wrest once the law to your authority:
To do a great right, do a little wrong,
And curb this cruel devil of his will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: It must not be; there is no power in Venice
Can alter a decree established:
'Twill be recorded for a precedent,
And many an error by the same example
Will rush into the state: it cannot be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: A Daniel come to judgment! yea, a Daniel!
O wise young judge, how I do honour thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, let me look upon the bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Here 'tis, most reverend doctor, here it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Shylock, there's thrice thy money offer'd thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: An oath, an oath, I have an oath in heaven:
Shall I lay perjury upon my soul?
No, not for Venice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this bond is forfeit;
And lawfully by this the Jew may claim
A pound of flesh, to be by him cut off
Nearest the merchant's heart. Be merciful:
Take thrice thy money; bid me tear the bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: When it is paid according to the tenor.
It doth appear you are a worthy judge;
You know the law, your exposition
Hath been most sound: I charge you by the law,
Whereof you are a well-deserving pillar,
Proceed to judgment: by my soul I swear
There is no power in the tongue of man
To alter me: I stay here on my bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Most heartily I do beseech the court
To give the judgment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why then, thus it is:
You must prepare your bosom for his knife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: O noble judge! O excellent young man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: For the intent and purpose of the law
Hath full relation to the penalty,
Which here appeareth due upon the bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis very true: O wise and upright judge!
How much more elder art thou than thy looks!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore lay bare your bosom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, his breast:
So says the bond: doth it not, noble judge?
'Nearest his heart:' those are the very words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: It is so. Are there balance here to weigh
The flesh?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I have them ready.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Have by some surgeon, Shylock, on your charge,
To stop his wounds, lest he do bleed to death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Is it so nominated in the bond?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: It is not so express'd: but what of that?
'Twere good you do so much for charity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot find it; 'tis not in the bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: You, merchant, have you any thing to say?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: But little: I am arm'd and well prepared.
Give me your hand, Bassanio: fare you well!
Grieve not that I am fallen to this for you;
For herein Fortune shows herself more kind
Than is her custom: it is still her use
To let the wretched man outlive his wealth,
To view with hollow eye and wrinkled brow
An age of poverty; from which lingering penance
Of such misery doth she cut me off.
Commend me to your honourable wife:
Tell her the process of Antonio's end;
Say how I loved you, speak me fair in death;
And, when the tale is told, bid her be judge
Whether Bassanio had not once a love.
Repent but you that you shall lose your friend,
And he repents not that he pays your debt;
For if the Jew do cut but deep enough,
I'll pay it presently with all my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Antonio, I am married to a wife
Which is as dear to me as life itself;
But life itself, my wife, and all the world,
Are not with me esteem'd above thy life:
I would lose all, ay, sacrifice them all
Here to this devil, to deliver you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Your wife would give you little thanks for that,
If she were by, to hear you make the offer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: I have a wife, whom, I protest, I love:
I would she were in heaven, so she could
Entreat some power to change this currish Jew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well you offer it behind her back;
The wish would make else an unquiet house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: These be the Christian husbands. I have a daughter;
Would any of the stock of Barrabas
Had been her husband rather than a Christian!
We trifle time: I pray thee, pursue sentence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: A pound of that same merchant's flesh is thine:
The court awards it, and the law doth give it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Most rightful judge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: And you must cut this flesh from off his breast:
The law allows it, and the court awards it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Most learned judge! A sentence! Come, prepare!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Tarry a little; there is something else.
This bond doth give thee here no jot of blood;
The words expressly are 'a pound of flesh:'
Take then thy bond, take thou thy pound of flesh;
But, in the cutting it, if thou dost shed
One drop of Christian blood, thy lands and goods
Are, by the laws of Venice, confiscate
Unto the state of Venice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: O upright judge! Mark, Jew: O learned judge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Is that the law?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thyself shalt see the act:
For, as thou urgest justice, be assured
Thou shalt have justice, more than thou desirest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: O learned judge! Mark, Jew: a learned judge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I take this offer, then; pay the bond thrice
And let the Christian go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here is the money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Soft!
The Jew shall have all justice; soft! no haste:
He shall have nothing but the penalty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: O Jew! an upright judge, a learned judge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore prepare thee to cut off the flesh.
Shed thou no blood, nor cut thou less nor more
But just a pound of flesh: if thou cut'st more
Or less than a just pound, be it but so much
As makes it light or heavy in the substance,
Or the division of the twentieth part
Of one poor scruple, nay, if the scale do turn
But in the estimation of a hair,
Thou diest and all thy goods are confiscate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: A second Daniel, a Daniel, Jew!
Now, infidel, I have you on the hip.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why doth the Jew pause? take thy forfeiture.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Give me my principal, and let me go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I have it ready for thee; here it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: He hath refused it in the open court:
He shall have merely justice and his bond.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: A Daniel, still say I, a second Daniel!
I thank thee, Jew, for teaching me that word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I not have barely my principal?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt have nothing but the forfeiture,
To be so taken at thy peril, Jew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then the devil give him good of it!
I'll stay no longer question.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Tarry, Jew:
The law hath yet another hold on you.
It is enacted in the laws of Venice,
If it be proved against an alien
That by direct or indirect attempts
He seek the life of any citizen,
The party 'gainst the which he doth contrive
Shall seize one half his goods; the other half
Comes to the privy coffer of the state;
And the offender's life lies in the mercy
Of the duke only, 'gainst all other voice.
In which predicament, I say, thou stand'st;
For it appears, by manifest proceeding,
That indirectly and directly too
Thou hast contrived against the very life
Of the defendant; and thou hast incurr'd
The danger formerly by me rehearsed.
Down therefore and beg mercy of the duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Beg that thou mayst have leave to hang thyself:
And yet, thy wealth being forfeit to the state,
Thou hast not left the value of a cord;
Therefore thou must be hang'd at the state's charge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: That thou shalt see the difference of our spirits,
I pardon thee thy life before thou ask it:
For half thy wealth, it is Antonio's;
The other half comes to the general state,
Which humbleness may drive unto a fine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, for the state, not for Antonio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, take my life and all; pardon not that:
You take my house when you do take the prop
That doth sustain my house; you take my life
When you do take the means whereby I live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: What mercy can you render him, Antonio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: A halter gratis; nothing else, for God's sake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: So please my lord the duke and all the court
To quit the fine for one half of his goods,
I am content; so he will let me have
The other half in use, to render it,
Upon his death, unto the gentleman
That lately stole his daughter:
Two things provided more, that, for this favour,
He presently become a Christian;
The other, that he do record a gift,
Here in the court, of all he dies possess'd,
Unto his son Lorenzo and his daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: He shall do this, or else I do recant
The pardon that I late pronounced here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou contented, Jew? what dost thou say?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I am content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Clerk, draw a deed of gift.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SHYLOCK
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, give me leave to go from hence;
I am not well: send the deed after me,
And I will sign it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Get thee gone, but do it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: In christening shalt thou have two god-fathers:
Had I been judge, thou shouldst have had ten more,
To bring thee to the gallows, not the font.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I entreat you home with me to dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I humbly do desire your grace of pardon:
I must away this night toward Padua,
And it is meet I presently set forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE
SPEECH.LINE: I am sorry that your leisure serves you not.
Antonio, gratify this gentleman,
For, in my mind, you are much bound to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Most worthy gentleman, I and my friend
Have by your wisdom been this day acquitted
Of grievous penalties; in lieu whereof,
Three thousand ducats, due unto the Jew,
We freely cope your courteous pains withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: And stand indebted, over and above,
In love and service to you evermore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: He is well paid that is well satisfied;
And I, delivering you, am satisfied
And therein do account myself well paid:
My mind was never yet more mercenary.
I pray you, know me when we meet again:
I wish you well, and so I take my leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Dear sir, of force I must attempt you further:
Take some remembrance of us, as a tribute,
Not as a fee: grant me two things, I pray you,
Not to deny me, and to pardon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: You press me far, and therefore I will yield.
Give me your gloves, I'll wear them for your sake;
And, for your love, I'll take this ring from you:
Do not draw back your hand; I'll take no more;
And you in love shall not deny me this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: This ring, good sir, alas, it is a trifle!
I will not shame myself to give you this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I will have nothing else but only this;
And now methinks I have a mind to it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: There's more depends on this than on the value.
The dearest ring in Venice will I give you,
And find it out by proclamation:
Only for this, I pray you, pardon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: I see, sir, you are liberal in offers
You taught me first to beg; and now methinks
You teach me how a beggar should be answer'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Good sir, this ring was given me by my wife;
And when she put it on, she made me vow
That I should neither sell nor give nor lose it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: That 'scuse serves many men to save their gifts.
An if your wife be not a mad-woman,
And know how well I have deserved the ring,
She would not hold out enemy for ever,
For giving it to me. Well, peace be with you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Bassanio, let him have the ring:
Let his deservings and my love withal
Be valued against your wife's commandment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Go, Gratiano, run and overtake him;
Give him the ring, and bring him, if thou canst,
Unto Antonio's house: away! make haste.
Come, you and I will thither presently;
And in the morning early will we both
Fly toward Belmont: come, Antonio.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Inquire the Jew's house out, give him this deed
And let him sign it: we'll away to-night
And be a day before our husbands home:
This deed will be well welcome to Lorenzo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Fair sir, you are well o'erta'en
My Lord Bassanio upon more advice
Hath sent you here this ring, and doth entreat
Your company at dinner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: That cannot be:
His ring I do accept most thankfully:
And so, I pray you, tell him: furthermore,
I pray you, show my youth old Shylock's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: That will I do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I would speak with you.
I'll see if I can get my husband's ring,
Which I did make him swear to keep for ever.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to NERISSA Thou mayst, I warrant.
We shall have old swearing
That they did give the rings away to men;
But we'll outface them, and outswear them too.
Away! make haste: thou knowist where I will tarry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, good sir, will you show me to this house?

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Belmont. Avenue to PORTIA'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: The moon shines bright: in such a night as this,
When the sweet wind did gently kiss the trees
And they did make no noise, in such a night
Troilus methinks mounted the Troyan walls
And sigh'd his soul toward the Grecian tents,
Where Cressid lay that night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Did Thisbe fearfully o'ertrip the dew
And saw the lion's shadow ere himself
And ran dismay'd away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Stood Dido with a willow in her hand
Upon the wild sea banks and waft her love
To come again to Carthage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Medea gather'd the enchanted herbs
That did renew old AEson.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Did Jessica steal from the wealthy Jew
And with an unthrift love did run from Venice
As far as Belmont.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Did young Lorenzo swear he loved her well,
Stealing her soul with many vows of faith
And ne'er a true one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: In such a night
Did pretty Jessica, like a little shrew,
Slander her love, and he forgave it her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: I would out-night you, did no body come;
But, hark, I hear the footing of a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Who comes so fast in silence of the night?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: A friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: A friend! what friend? your name, I pray you, friend?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: Stephano is my name; and I bring word
My mistress will before the break of day
Be here at Belmont; she doth stray about
By holy crosses, where she kneels and prays
For happy wedlock hours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Who comes with her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: None but a holy hermit and her maid.
I pray you, is my master yet return'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: He is not, nor we have not heard from him.
But go we in, I pray thee, Jessica,
And ceremoniously let us prepare
Some welcome for the mistress of the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Sola, sola! wo ha, ho! sola, sola!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Who calls?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Sola! did you see Master Lorenzo?
Master Lorenzo, sola, sola!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Leave hollaing, man: here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Sola! where? where?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAUNCELOT
SPEECH.LINE: Tell him there's a post come from my master, with
his horn full of good news: my master will be here
ere morning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet soul, let's in, and there expect their coming.
And yet no matter: why should we go in?
My friend Stephano, signify, I pray you,
Within the house, your mistress is at hand;
And bring your music forth into the air.
How sweet the moonlight sleeps upon this bank!
Here will we sit and let the sounds of music
Creep in our ears: soft stillness and the night
Become the touches of sweet harmony.
Sit, Jessica. Look how the floor of heaven
Is thick inlaid with patines of bright gold:
There's not the smallest orb which thou behold'st
But in his motion like an angel sings,
Still quiring to the young-eyed cherubins;
Such harmony is in immortal souls;
But whilst this muddy vesture of decay
Doth grossly close it in, we cannot hear it.
Come, ho! and wake Diana with a hymn!
With sweetest touches pierce your mistress' ear,
And draw her home with music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JESSICA
SPEECH.LINE: I am never merry when I hear sweet music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: The reason is, your spirits are attentive:
For do but note a wild and wanton herd,
Or race of youthful and unhandled colts,
Fetching mad bounds, bellowing and neighing loud,
Which is the hot condition of their blood;
If they but hear perchance a trumpet sound,
Or any air of music touch their ears,
You shall perceive them make a mutual stand,
Their savage eyes turn'd to a modest gaze
By the sweet power of music: therefore the poet
Did feign that Orpheus drew trees, stones and floods;
Since nought so stockish, hard and full of rage,
But music for the time doth change his nature.
The man that hath no music in himself,
Nor is not moved with concord of sweet sounds,
Is fit for treasons, stratagems and spoils;
The motions of his spirit are dull as night
And his affections dark as Erebus:
Let no such man be trusted. Mark the music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: That light we see is burning in my hall.
How far that little candle throws his beams!
So shines a good deed in a naughty world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: When the moon shone, we did not see the candle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: So doth the greater glory dim the less:
A substitute shines brightly as a king
Unto the king be by, and then his state
Empties itself, as doth an inland brook
Into the main of waters. Music! hark!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: It is your music, madam, of the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing is good, I see, without respect:
Methinks it sounds much sweeter than by day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Silence bestows that virtue on it, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: The crow doth sing as sweetly as the lark,
When neither is attended, and I think
The nightingale, if she should sing by day,
When every goose is cackling, would be thought
No better a musician than the wren.
How many things by season season'd are
To their right praise and true perfection!
Peace, ho! the moon sleeps with Endymion
And would not be awaked.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: That is the voice,
Or I am much deceived, of Portia.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: He knows me as the blind man knows the cuckoo,
By the bad voice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Dear lady, welcome home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: We have been praying for our husbands' healths,
Which speed, we hope, the better for our words.
Are they return'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, they are not yet;
But there is come a messenger before,
To signify their coming.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Go in, Nerissa;
Give order to my servants that they take
No note at all of our being absent hence;
Nor you, Lorenzo; Jessica, nor you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORENZO
SPEECH.LINE: Your husband is at hand; I hear his trumpet:
We are no tell-tales, madam; fear you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: This night methinks is but the daylight sick;
It looks a little paler: 'tis a day,
Such as the day is when the sun is hid.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BASSANIO, ANTONIO, GRATIANO, and their followers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: We should hold day with the Antipodes,
If you would walk in absence of the sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Let me give light, but let me not be light;
For a light wife doth make a heavy husband,
And never be Bassanio so for me:
But God sort all! You are welcome home, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, madam. Give welcome to my friend.
This is the man, this is Antonio,
To whom I am so infinitely bound.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: You should in all sense be much bound to him.
For, as I hear, he was much bound for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: No more than I am well acquitted of.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, you are very welcome to our house:
It must appear in other ways than words,
Therefore I scant this breathing courtesy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: To NERISSA By yonder moon I swear you do me wrong;
In faith, I gave it to the judge's clerk:
Would he were gelt that had it, for my part,
Since you do take it, love, so much at heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: A quarrel, ho, already! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: About a hoop of gold, a paltry ring
That she did give me, whose posy was
For all the world like cutler's poetry
Upon a knife, 'Love me, and leave me not.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: What talk you of the posy or the value?
You swore to me, when I did give it you,
That you would wear it till your hour of death
And that it should lie with you in your grave:
Though not for me, yet for your vehement oaths,
You should have been respective and have kept it.
Gave it a judge's clerk! no, God's my judge,
The clerk will ne'er wear hair on's face that had it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: He will, an if he live to be a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, if a woman live to be a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by this hand, I gave it to a youth,
A kind of boy, a little scrubbed boy,
No higher than thyself; the judge's clerk,
A prating boy, that begg'd it as a fee:
I could not for my heart deny it him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: You were to blame, I must be plain with you,
To part so slightly with your wife's first gift:
A thing stuck on with oaths upon your finger
And so riveted with faith unto your flesh.
I gave my love a ring and made him swear
Never to part with it; and here he stands;
I dare be sworn for him he would not leave it
Nor pluck it from his finger, for the wealth
That the world masters. Now, in faith, Gratiano,
You give your wife too unkind a cause of grief:
An 'twere to me, I should be mad at it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Why, I were best to cut my left hand off
And swear I lost the ring defending it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRATIANO
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Bassanio gave his ring away
Unto the judge that begg'd it and indeed
Deserved it too; and then the boy, his clerk,
That took some pains in writing, he begg'd mine;
And neither man nor master would take aught
But the two rings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: What ring gave you my lord?
Not that, I hope, which you received of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: If I could add a lie unto a fault,
I would deny it; but you see my finger
Hath not the ring upon it; it is gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Even so void is your false heart of truth.
By heaven, I will ne'er come in your bed
Until I see the ring.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NERISSA
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I in yours
Till I again see mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Portia,
If you did know to whom I gave the ring,
If you did know for whom I gave the ring
And would conceive for what I gave the ring
And how unwillingly I left the ring,
When nought would be accepted but the ring,
You would abate the strength of your displeasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: If you had known the virtue of the ring,
Or half her worthiness that gave the ring,
Or your own honour to contain the ring,
You would not then have parted with the ring.
What man is there so much unreasonable,
If you had pleased to have defended it
With any terms of zeal, wanted the modesty
To urge the thing held as a ceremony?
Nerissa teaches me what to believe:
I'll die for't but some woman had the ring.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSANIO
SPEECH.LINE: No, by my honour, madam, by my soul,
No woman had it, but a civil doctor,
Which did refuse three thousand ducats of me
And begg'd the ring; the which I did deny him
And suffer'd him to go displeased away;
Even he that did uphold the very life
Of my dear friend. What should I say, sweet lady?
I was enforced to send it after him;
I was beset with shame and courtesy;
My honour would not let ingratitude
So much besmear it. Pardon me, good lady;
For, by these blessed candles of the night,
Had you been there, I think you would have begg'd
The ring of me to give the worthy doctor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PORTIA
SPEECH.LINE: Let not that doctor e'er come near my house:
Since he hath got the jewel that I loved,
