offend: only, have a care that your bills be not
stolen. Well, you are to call at all the
ale-houses, and bid those that are drunk get them to bed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: How if they will not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, let them alone till they are sober: if
they make you not then the better answer, you may
say they are not the men you took them for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: If you meet a thief, you may suspect him, by virtue
of your office, to be no true man; and, for such
kind of men, the less you meddle or make with them,
why the more is for your honesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: If we know him to be a thief, shall we not lay
hands on him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, by your office, you may; but I think they
that touch pitch will be defiled: the most peaceable
way for you, if you do take a thief, is to let him
show himself what he is and steal out of your company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: You have been always called a merciful man, partner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, I would not hang a dog by my will, much more
a man who hath any honesty in him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: If you hear a child cry in the night, you must call
to the nurse and bid her still it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: How if the nurse be asleep and will not hear us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, depart in peace, and let the child wake
her with crying; for the ewe that will not hear her
lamb when it baes will never answer a calf when he bleats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis very true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: This is the end of the charge:--you, constable, are
to present the prince's own person: if you meet the
prince in the night, you may stay him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, by'r our lady, that I think a' cannot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Five shillings to one on't, with any man that knows
the statutes, he may stay him: marry, not without
the prince be willing; for, indeed, the watch ought
to offend no man; and it is an offence to stay a
man against his will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: By'r lady, I think it be so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha, ha! Well, masters, good night: an there be
any matter of weight chances, call up me: keep your
fellows' counsels and your own; and good night.
Come, neighbour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Well, masters, we hear our charge: let us go sit here
upon the church-bench till two, and then all to bed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: One word more, honest neighbours. I pray you watch
about Signior Leonato's door; for the wedding being
there to-morrow, there is a great coil to-night.
Adieu: be vigitant, I beseech you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: What Conrade!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Peace! stir not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Conrade, I say!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Here, man; I am at thy elbow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mass, and my elbow itched; I thought there would a
scab follow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: I will owe thee an answer for that: and now forward
with thy tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Stand thee close, then, under this pent-house, for
it drizzles rain; and I will, like a true drunkard,
utter all to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Some treason, masters: yet stand close.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore know I have earned of Don John a thousand ducats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Is it possible that any villany should be so dear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shouldst rather ask if it were possible any
villany should be so rich; for when rich villains
have need of poor ones, poor ones may make what
price they will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder at it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: That shows thou art unconfirmed. Thou knowest that
the fashion of a doublet, or a hat, or a cloak, is
nothing to a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, it is apparel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I mean, the fashion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, the fashion is the fashion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Tush! I may as well say the fool's the fool. But
seest thou not what a deformed thief this fashion
is?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I know that Deformed; a' has been a vile
thief this seven year; a' goes up and down like a
gentleman: I remember his name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Didst thou not hear somebody?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: No; 'twas the vane on the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Seest thou not, I say, what a deformed thief this
fashion is? how giddily a' turns about all the hot
bloods between fourteen and five-and-thirty?
sometimes fashioning them like Pharaoh's soldiers
in the reeky painting, sometime like god Bel's
priests in the old church-window, sometime like the
shaven Hercules in the smirched worm-eaten tapestry,
where his codpiece seems as massy as his club?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: All this I see; and I see that the fashion wears
out more apparel than the man. But art not thou
thyself giddy with the fashion too, that thou hast
shifted out of thy tale into telling me of the fashion?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not so, neither: but know that I have to-night
wooed Margaret, the Lady Hero's gentlewoman, by the
name of Hero: she leans me out at her mistress'
chamber-window, bids me a thousand times good
night,--I tell this tale vilely:--I should first
tell thee how the prince, Claudio and my master,
planted and placed and possessed by my master Don
John, saw afar off in the orchard this amiable encounter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: And thought they Margaret was Hero?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Two of them did, the prince and Claudio; but the
devil my master knew she was Margaret; and partly
by his oaths, which first possessed them, partly by
the dark night, which did deceive them, but chiefly
by my villany, which did confirm any slander that
Don John had made, away went Claudio enraged; swore
he would meet her, as he was appointed, next morning
at the temple, and there, before the whole
congregation, shame her with what he saw o'er night
and send her home again without a husband.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: We charge you, in the prince's name, stand!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Call up the right master constable. We have here
recovered the most dangerous piece of lechery that
ever was known in the commonwealth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: And one Deformed is one of them: I know him; a'
wears a lock.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Masters, masters,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: You'll be made bring Deformed forth, I warrant you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Masters,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Never speak: we charge you let us obey you to go with us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: We are like to prove a goodly commodity, being taken
up of these men's bills.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: A commodity in question, I warrant you. Come, we'll obey you.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. HERO's apartment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Good Ursula, wake my cousin Beatrice, and desire
her to rise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: URSULA
SPEECH.LINE: I will, lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: And bid her come hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: URSULA
SPEECH.LINE: Well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Troth, I think your other rabato were better.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: No, pray thee, good Meg, I'll wear this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, 's not so good; and I warrant your
cousin will say so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: My cousin's a fool, and thou art another: I'll wear
none but this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: I like the new tire within excellently, if the hair
were a thought browner; and your gown's a most rare
fashion, i' faith. I saw the Duchess of Milan's
gown that they praise so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: O, that exceeds, they say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, 's but a night-gown in respect of
yours: cloth o' gold, and cuts, and laced with
silver, set with pearls, down sleeves, side sleeves,
and skirts, round underborne with a bluish tinsel:
but for a fine, quaint, graceful and excellent
fashion, yours is worth ten on 't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: God give me joy to wear it! for my heart is
exceeding heavy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twill be heavier soon by the weight of a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Fie upon thee! art not ashamed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Of what, lady? of speaking honourably? Is not
marriage honourable in a beggar? Is not your lord
honourable without marriage? I think you would have
me say, 'saving your reverence, a husband:' and bad
thinking do not wrest true speaking, I'll offend
nobody: is there any harm in 'the heavier for a
husband'? None, I think, and it be the right husband
and the right wife; otherwise 'tis light, and not
heavy: ask my Lady Beatrice else; here she comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, coz.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, sweet Hero.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Why how now? do you speak in the sick tune?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: I am out of all other tune, methinks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Clap's into 'Light o' love;' that goes without a
burden: do you sing it, and I'll dance it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Ye light o' love, with your heels! then, if your
husband have stables enough, you'll see he shall
lack no barns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: O illegitimate construction! I scorn that with my heels.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis almost five o'clock, cousin; tis time you were
ready. By my troth, I am exceeding ill: heigh-ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: For a hawk, a horse, or a husband?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: For the letter that begins them all, H.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Well, and you be not turned Turk, there's no more
sailing by the star.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: What means the fool, trow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing I; but God send every one their heart's desire!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: These gloves the count sent me; they are an
excellent perfume.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: I am stuffed, cousin; I cannot smell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: A maid, and stuffed! there's goodly catching of cold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: O, God help me! God help me! how long have you
professed apprehension?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Even since you left it. Doth not my wit become me rarely?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: It is not seen enough, you should wear it in your
cap. By my troth, I am sick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Get you some of this distilled Carduus Benedictus,
and lay it to your heart: it is the only thing for a qualm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: There thou prickest her with a thistle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Benedictus! why Benedictus? you have some moral in
this Benedictus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Moral! no, by my troth, I have no moral meaning; I
meant, plain holy-thistle. You may think perchance
that I think you are in love: nay, by'r lady, I am
not such a fool to think what I list, nor I list
not to think what I can, nor indeed I cannot think,
if I would think my heart out of thinking, that you
are in love or that you will be in love or that you
can be in love. Yet Benedick was such another, and
now is he become a man: he swore he would never
marry, and yet now, in despite of his heart, he eats
his meat without grudging: and how you may be
converted I know not, but methinks you look with
your eyes as other women do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: What pace is this that thy tongue keeps?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Not a false gallop.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: URSULA
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, withdraw: the prince, the count, Signior
Benedick, Don John, and all the gallants of the
town, are come to fetch you to church.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Help to dress me, good coz, good Meg, good Ursula.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another room in LEONATO'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter LEONATO, with DOGBERRY and VERGES

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: What would you with me, honest neighbour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, I would have some confidence with you
that decerns you nearly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Brief, I pray you; for you see it is a busy time with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, this it is, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, in truth it is, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: What is it, my good friends?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Goodman Verges, sir, speaks a little off the
matter: an old man, sir, and his wits are not so
blunt as, God help, I would desire they were; but,
in faith, honest as the skin between his brows.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, I thank God I am as honest as any man living
that is an old man and no honester than I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Comparisons are odorous: palabras, neighbour Verges.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Neighbours, you are tedious.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: It pleases your worship to say so, but we are the
poor duke's officers; but truly, for mine own part,
if I were as tedious as a king, I could find it in
my heart to bestow it all of your worship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: All thy tediousness on me, ah?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, an 'twere a thousand pound more than 'tis; for
I hear as good exclamation on your worship as of any
man in the city; and though I be but a poor man, I
am glad to hear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: And so am I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I would fain know what you have to say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, our watch to-night, excepting your
worship's presence, ha' ta'en a couple of as arrant
knaves as any in Messina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: A good old man, sir; he will be talking: as they
say, when the age is in, the wit is out: God help
us! it is a world to see. Well said, i' faith,
neighbour Verges: well, God's a good man; an two men
ride of a horse, one must ride behind. An honest
soul, i' faith, sir; by my troth he is, as ever
broke bread; but God is to be worshipped; all men
are not alike; alas, good neighbour!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, neighbour, he comes too short of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Gifts that God gives.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I must leave you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: One word, sir: our watch, sir, have indeed
comprehended two aspicious persons, and we would
have them this morning examined before your worship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Take their examination yourself and bring it me: I
am now in great haste, as it may appear unto you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: It shall be suffigance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Drink some wine ere you go: fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, they stay for you to give your daughter to
her husband.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll wait upon them: I am ready.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Go, good partner, go, get you to Francis Seacole;
bid him bring his pen and inkhorn to the gaol: we
are now to examination these men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: And we must do it wisely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: We will spare for no wit, I warrant you; here's
that shall drive some of them to a non-come: only
get the learned writer to set down our
excommunication and meet me at the gaol.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A church.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DON PEDRO, DON JOHN, LEONATO, FRIAR FRANCIS, CLAUDIO, BENEDICK, HERO, BEATRICE, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Friar Francis, be brief; only to the plain
form of marriage, and you shall recount their
particular duties afterwards.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: You come hither, my lord, to marry this lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: To be married to her: friar, you come to marry her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Lady, you come hither to be married to this count.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: I do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: If either of you know any inward impediment why you
should not be conjoined, charge you, on your souls,
to utter it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Know you any, Hero?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: None, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Know you any, count?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I dare make his answer, none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: O, what men dare do! what men may do! what men daily
do, not knowing what they do!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: How now! interjections? Why, then, some be of
laughing, as, ah, ha, he!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Stand thee by, friar. Father, by your leave:
Will you with free and unconstrained soul
Give me this maid, your daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: As freely, son, as God did give her me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: And what have I to give you back, whose worth
May counterpoise this rich and precious gift?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing, unless you render her again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet prince, you learn me noble thankfulness.
There, Leonato, take her back again:
Give not this rotten orange to your friend;
She's but the sign and semblance of her honour.
Behold how like a maid she blushes here!
O, what authority and show of truth
Can cunning sin cover itself withal!
Comes not that blood as modest evidence
To witness simple virtue? Would you not swear,
All you that see her, that she were a maid,
By these exterior shows? But she is none:
She knows the heat of a luxurious bed;
Her blush is guiltiness, not modesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: What do you mean, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not to be married,
Not to knit my soul to an approved wanton.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Dear my lord, if you, in your own proof,
Have vanquish'd the resistance of her youth,
And made defeat of her virginity,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I know what you would say: if I have known her,
You will say she did embrace me as a husband,
And so extenuate the 'forehand sin:
No, Leonato,
I never tempted her with word too large;
But, as a brother to his sister, show'd
Bashful sincerity and comely love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: And seem'd I ever otherwise to you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Out on thee! Seeming! I will write against it:
You seem to me as Dian in her orb,
As chaste as is the bud ere it be blown;
But you are more intemperate in your blood
Than Venus, or those pamper'd animals
That rage in savage sensuality.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Is my lord well, that he doth speak so wide?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet prince, why speak not you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: What should I speak?
I stand dishonour'd, that have gone about
To link my dear friend to a common stale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Are these things spoken, or do I but dream?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON JOHN
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, they are spoken, and these things are true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: This looks not like a nuptial.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: True! O God!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Leonato, stand I here?
Is this the prince? is this the prince's brother?
Is this face Hero's? are our eyes our own?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: All this is so: but what of this, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let me but move one question to your daughter;
And, by that fatherly and kindly power
That you have in her, bid her answer truly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I charge thee do so, as thou art my child.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: O, God defend me! how am I beset!
What kind of catechising call you this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: To make you answer truly to your name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Is it not Hero? Who can blot that name
With any just reproach?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, that can Hero;
Hero itself can blot out Hero's virtue.
What man was he talk'd with you yesternight
Out at your window betwixt twelve and one?
Now, if you are a maid, answer to this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: I talk'd with no man at that hour, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then are you no maiden. Leonato,
I am sorry you must hear: upon mine honour,
Myself, my brother and this grieved count
Did see her, hear her, at that hour last night
Talk with a ruffian at her chamber-window
Who hath indeed, most like a liberal villain,
Confess'd the vile encounters they have had
A thousand times in secret.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON JOHN
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie! they are not to be named, my lord,
Not to be spoke of;
There is not chastity enough in language
Without offence to utter them. Thus, pretty lady,
I am sorry for thy much misgovernment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: O Hero, what a Hero hadst thou been,
If half thy outward graces had been placed
About thy thoughts and counsels of thy heart!
But fare thee well, most foul, most fair! farewell,
Thou pure impiety and impious purity!
For thee I'll lock up all the gates of love,
And on my eyelids shall conjecture hang,
To turn all beauty into thoughts of harm,
And never shall it more be gracious.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Hath no man's dagger here a point for me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, cousin! wherefore sink you down?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON JOHN
SPEECH.LINE: Come, let us go. These things, come thus to light,
Smother her spirits up.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt DON PEDRO, DON JOHN, and CLAUDIO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: How doth the lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Dead, I think. Help, uncle!
Hero! why, Hero! Uncle! Signior Benedick! Friar!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: O Fate! take not away thy heavy hand.
Death is the fairest cover for her shame
That may be wish'd for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: How now, cousin Hero!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Have comfort, lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou look up?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, wherefore should she not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore! Why, doth not every earthly thing
Cry shame upon her? Could she here deny
The story that is printed in her blood?
Do not live, Hero; do not ope thine eyes:
For, did I think thou wouldst not quickly die,
Thought I thy spirits were stronger than thy shames,
Myself would, on the rearward of reproaches,
Strike at thy life. Grieved I, I had but one?
Chid I for that at frugal nature's frame?
O, one too much by thee! Why had I one?
Why ever wast thou lovely in my eyes?
Why had I not with charitable hand
Took up a beggar's issue at my gates,
Who smirch'd thus and mired with infamy,
I might have said 'No part of it is mine;
This shame derives itself from unknown loins'?
But mine and mine I loved and mine I praised
And mine that I was proud on, mine so much
That I myself was to myself not mine,
Valuing of her,--why, she, O, she is fallen
Into a pit of ink, that the wide sea
Hath drops too few to wash her clean again
And salt too little which may season give
To her foul-tainted flesh!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, sir, be patient.
For my part, I am so attired in wonder,
I know not what to say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: O, on my soul, my cousin is belied!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Lady, were you her bedfellow last night?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: No, truly not; although, until last night,
I have this twelvemonth been her bedfellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Confirm'd, confirm'd! O, that is stronger made
Which was before barr'd up with ribs of iron!
Would the two princes lie, and Claudio lie,
Who loved her so, that, speaking of her foulness,
Wash'd it with tears? Hence from her! let her die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me a little; for I have only been
Silent so long and given way unto
This course of fortune
By noting of the lady. I have mark'd
A thousand blushing apparitions
To start into her face, a thousand innocent shames
In angel whiteness beat away those blushes;
And in her eye there hath appear'd a fire,
To burn the errors that these princes hold
Against her maiden truth. Call me a fool;
Trust not my reading nor my observations,
Which with experimental seal doth warrant
The tenor of my book; trust not my age,
My reverence, calling, nor divinity,
If this sweet lady lie not guiltless here
Under some biting error.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Friar, it cannot be.
Thou seest that all the grace that she hath left
Is that she will not add to her damnation
A sin of perjury; she not denies it:
Why seek'st thou then to cover with excuse
That which appears in proper nakedness?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Lady, what man is he you are accused of?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: They know that do accuse me; I know none:
If I know more of any man alive
Than that which maiden modesty doth warrant,
Let all my sins lack mercy! O my father,
Prove you that any man with me conversed
At hours unmeet, or that I yesternight
Maintain'd the change of words with any creature,
Refuse me, hate me, torture me to death!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: There is some strange misprision in the princes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Two of them have the very bent of honour;
And if their wisdoms be misled in this,
The practise of it lives in John the bastard,
Whose spirits toil in frame of villanies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I know not. If they speak but truth of her,
These hands shall tear her; if they wrong her honour,
The proudest of them shall well hear of it.
Time hath not yet so dried this blood of mine,
Nor age so eat up my invention,
Nor fortune made such havoc of my means,
Nor my bad life reft me so much of friends,
But they shall find, awaked in such a kind,
Both strength of limb and policy of mind,
Ability in means and choice of friends,
To quit me of them throughly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Pause awhile,
And let my counsel sway you in this case.
Your daughter here the princes left for dead:
Let her awhile be secretly kept in,
And publish it that she is dead indeed;
Maintain a mourning ostentation
And on your family's old monument
Hang mournful epitaphs and do all rites
That appertain unto a burial.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: What shall become of this? what will this do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, this well carried shall on her behalf
Change slander to remorse; that is some good:
But not for that dream I on this strange course,
But on this travail look for greater birth.
She dying, as it must so be maintain'd,
Upon the instant that she was accused,
Shall be lamented, pitied and excused
Of every hearer: for it so falls out
That what we have we prize not to the worth
Whiles we enjoy it, but being lack'd and lost,
Why, then we rack the value, then we find
The virtue that possession would not show us
Whiles it was ours. So will it fare with Claudio:
When he shall hear she died upon his words,
The idea of her life shall sweetly creep
Into his study of imagination,
And every lovely organ of her life
Shall come apparell'd in more precious habit,
More moving-delicate and full of life,
Into the eye and prospect of his soul,
Than when she lived indeed; then shall he mourn,
If ever love had interest in his liver,
And wish he had not so accused her,
No, though he thought his accusation true.
Let this be so, and doubt not but success
Will fashion the event in better shape
Than I can lay it down in likelihood.
But if all aim but this be levell'd false,
The supposition of the lady's death
Will quench the wonder of her infamy:
And if it sort not well, you may conceal her,
As best befits her wounded reputation,
In some reclusive and religious life,
Out of all eyes, tongues, minds and injuries.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Signior Leonato, let the friar advise you:
And though you know my inwardness and love
Is very much unto the prince and Claudio,
Yet, by mine honour, I will deal in this
As secretly and justly as your soul
Should with your body.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Being that I flow in grief,
The smallest twine may lead me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well consented: presently away;
For to strange sores strangely they strain the cure.
Come, lady, die to live: this wedding-day
Perhaps is but prolong'd: have patience and endure.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but BENEDICK and BEATRICE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Lady Beatrice, have you wept all this while?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, and I will weep a while longer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: I will not desire that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: You have no reason; I do it freely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Surely I do believe your fair cousin is wronged.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, how much might the man deserve of me that would right her!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Is there any way to show such friendship?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: A very even way, but no such friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: May a man do it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: It is a man's office, but not yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: I do love nothing in the world so well as you: is
not that strange?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: As strange as the thing I know not. It were as
possible for me to say I loved nothing so well as
you: but believe me not; and yet I lie not; I
confess nothing, nor I deny nothing. I am sorry for my cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: By my sword, Beatrice, thou lovest me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Do not swear, and eat it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: I will swear by it that you love me; and I will make
him eat it that says I love not you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Will you not eat your word?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: With no sauce that can be devised to it. I protest
I love thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, God forgive me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: What offence, sweet Beatrice?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: You have stayed me in a happy hour: I was about to
protest I loved you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: And do it with all thy heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: I love you with so much of my heart that none is
left to protest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Come, bid me do any thing for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Kill Claudio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! not for the wide world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: You kill me to deny it. Farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Tarry, sweet Beatrice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: I am gone, though I am here: there is no love in
you: nay, I pray you, let me go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Beatrice,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: In faith, I will go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: We'll be friends first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: You dare easier be friends with me than fight with mine enemy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Is Claudio thine enemy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Is he not approved in the height a villain, that
hath slandered, scorned, dishonoured my kinswoman? O
that I were a man! What, bear her in hand until they
come to take hands; and then, with public
accusation, uncovered slander, unmitigated rancour,
--O God, that I were a man! I would eat his heart
in the market-place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, Beatrice,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Talk with a man out at a window! A proper saying!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but, Beatrice,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Hero! She is wronged, she is slandered, she is undone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Beat--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Princes and counties! Surely, a princely testimony,
a goodly count, Count Comfect; a sweet gallant,
surely! O that I were a man for his sake! or that I
had any friend would be a man for my sake! But
manhood is melted into courtesies, valour into
compliment, and men are only turned into tongue, and
trim ones too: he is now as valiant as Hercules
that only tells a lie and swears it. I cannot be a
man with wishing, therefore I will die a woman with grieving.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Tarry, good Beatrice. By this hand, I love thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Use it for my love some other way than swearing by it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Think you in your soul the Count Claudio hath wronged Hero?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, as sure as I have a thought or a soul.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Enough, I am engaged; I will challenge him. I will
kiss your hand, and so I leave you. By this hand,
Claudio shall render me a dear account. As you
hear of me, so think of me. Go, comfort your
cousin: I must say she is dead: and so, farewell.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A prison.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DOGBERRY, VERGES, and Sexton, in gowns; and the Watch, with CONRADE and BORACHIO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Is our whole dissembly appeared?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: O, a stool and a cushion for the sexton.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: Which be the malefactors?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, that am I and my partner.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that's certain; we have the exhibition to examine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: But which are the offenders that are to be
examined? let them come before master constable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, marry, let them come before me. What is your
name, friend?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Borachio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, write down, Borachio. Yours, sirrah?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: I am a gentleman, sir, and my name is Conrade.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Write down, master gentleman Conrade. Masters, do
you serve God?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, sir, we hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Write down, that they hope they serve God: and
write God first; for God defend but God should go
before such villains! Masters, it is proved already
that you are little better than false knaves; and it
will go near to be thought so shortly. How answer
you for yourselves?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, we say we are none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: A marvellous witty fellow, I assure you: but I
will go about with him. Come you hither, sirrah; a
word in your ear: sir, I say to you, it is thought
you are false knaves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I say to you we are none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Well, stand aside. 'Fore God, they are both in a
tale. Have you writ down, that they are none?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: Master constable, you go not the way to examine:
you must call forth the watch that are their accusers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, marry, that's the eftest way. Let the watch
come forth. Masters, I charge you, in the prince's
name, accuse these men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: This man said, sir, that Don John, the prince's
brother, was a villain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Write down Prince John a villain. Why, this is flat
perjury, to call a prince's brother villain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Master constable,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Pray thee, fellow, peace: I do not like thy look,
I promise thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: What heard you him say else?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, that he had received a thousand ducats of
Don John for accusing the Lady Hero wrongfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Flat burglary as ever was committed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, by mass, that it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: What else, fellow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: And that Count Claudio did mean, upon his words, to
disgrace Hero before the whole assembly. and not marry her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: O villain! thou wilt be condemned into everlasting
redemption for this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: What else?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Watchman
SPEECH.LINE: This is all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Sexton
SPEECH.LINE: And this is more, masters, than you can deny.
Prince John is this morning secretly stolen away;
Hero was in this manner accused, in this very manner
refused, and upon the grief of this suddenly died.
Master constable, let these men be bound, and
brought to Leonato's: I will go before and show
him their examination.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Come, let them be opinioned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Let them be in the hands--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Off, coxcomb!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: God's my life, where's the sexton? let him write
down the prince's officer coxcomb. Come, bind them.
Thou naughty varlet!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CONRADE
SPEECH.LINE: Away! you are an ass, you are an ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou not suspect my place? dost thou not
suspect my years? O that he were here to write me
down an ass! But, masters, remember that I am an
ass; though it be not written down, yet forget not
that I am an ass. No, thou villain, thou art full of
piety, as shall be proved upon thee by good witness.
I am a wise fellow, and, which is more, an officer,
and, which is more, a householder, and, which is
more, as pretty a piece of flesh as any is in
Messina, and one that knows the law, go to; and a
rich fellow enough, go to; and a fellow that hath
had losses, and one that hath two gowns and every
thing handsome about him. Bring him away. O that
I had been writ down an ass!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Before LEONATO'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: If you go on thus, you will kill yourself:
And 'tis not wisdom thus to second grief
Against yourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, cease thy counsel,
Which falls into mine ears as profitless
As water in a sieve: give not me counsel;
Nor let no comforter delight mine ear
But such a one whose wrongs do suit with mine.
Bring me a father that so loved his child,
Whose joy of her is overwhelm'd like mine,
And bid him speak of patience;
Measure his woe the length and breadth of mine
And let it answer every strain for strain,
As thus for thus and such a grief for such,
In every lineament, branch, shape, and form:
If such a one will smile and stroke his beard,
Bid sorrow wag, cry 'hem!' when he should groan,
Patch grief with proverbs, make misfortune drunk
With candle-wasters; bring him yet to me,
And I of him will gather patience.
But there is no such man: for, brother, men
Can counsel and speak comfort to that grief
Which they themselves not feel; but, tasting it,
Their counsel turns to passion, which before
Would give preceptial medicine to rage,
Fetter strong madness in a silken thread,
Charm ache with air and agony with words:
No, no; 'tis all men's office to speak patience
To those that wring under the load of sorrow,
But no man's virtue nor sufficiency
To be so moral when he shall endure
The like himself. Therefore give me no counsel:
My griefs cry louder than advertisement.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Therein do men from children nothing differ.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, peace. I will be flesh and blood;
For there was never yet philosopher
That could endure the toothache patiently,
However they have writ the style of gods
And made a push at chance and sufferance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yet bend not all the harm upon yourself;
Make those that do offend you suffer too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: There thou speak'st reason: nay, I will do so.
My soul doth tell me Hero is belied;
And that shall Claudio know; so shall the prince
And all of them that thus dishonour her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the prince and Claudio hastily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Good den, good den.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Good day to both of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Hear you. my lords,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: We have some haste, Leonato.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Some haste, my lord! well, fare you well, my lord:
Are you so hasty now? well, all is one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, do not quarrel with us, good old man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: If he could right himself with quarreling,
Some of us would lie low.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Who wrongs him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, thou dost wrong me; thou dissembler, thou:--
Nay, never lay thy hand upon thy sword;
I fear thee not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, beshrew my hand,
If it should give your age such cause of fear:
In faith, my hand meant nothing to my sword.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Tush, tush, man; never fleer and jest at me:
I speak not like a dotard nor a fool,
As under privilege of age to brag
What I have done being young, or what would do
Were I not old. Know, Claudio, to thy head,
Thou hast so wrong'd mine innocent child and me
That I am forced to lay my reverence by
And, with grey hairs and bruise of many days,
Do challenge thee to trial of a man.
I say thou hast belied mine innocent child;
Thy slander hath gone through and through her heart,
And she lies buried with her ancestors;
O, in a tomb where never scandal slept,
Save this of hers, framed by thy villany!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: My villany?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Thine, Claudio; thine, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: You say not right, old man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, my lord,
I'll prove it on his body, if he dare,
Despite his nice fence and his active practise,
His May of youth and bloom of lustihood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Away! I will not have to do with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Canst thou so daff me? Thou hast kill'd my child:
If thou kill'st me, boy, thou shalt kill a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: He shall kill two of us, and men indeed:
But that's no matter; let him kill one first;
Win me and wear me; let him answer me.
Come, follow me, boy; come, sir boy, come, follow me:
Sir boy, I'll whip you from your foining fence;
Nay, as I am a gentleman, I will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Brother,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Content yourself. God knows I loved my niece;
And she is dead, slander'd to death by villains,
That dare as well answer a man indeed
As I dare take a serpent by the tongue:
Boys, apes, braggarts, Jacks, milksops!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Brother Antony,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Hold you content. What, man! I know them, yea,
And what they weigh, even to the utmost scruple,--
Scrambling, out-facing, fashion-monging boys,
That lie and cog and flout, deprave and slander,
Go anticly, show outward hideousness,
And speak off half a dozen dangerous words,
How they might hurt their enemies, if they durst;
And this is all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: But, brother Antony,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, 'tis no matter:
Do not you meddle; let me deal in this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Gentlemen both, we will not wake your patience.
My heart is sorry for your daughter's death:
But, on my honour, she was charged with nothing
But what was true and very full of proof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, my lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: I will not hear you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: No? Come, brother; away! I will be heard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: And shall, or some of us will smart for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: See, see; here comes the man we went to seek.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, signior, what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Good day, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, signior: you are almost come to part
almost a fray.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: We had like to have had our two noses snapped off
with two old men without teeth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Leonato and his brother. What thinkest thou? Had
we fought, I doubt we should have been too young for them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: In a false quarrel there is no true valour. I came
to seek you both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: We have been up and down to seek thee; for we are
high-proof melancholy and would fain have it beaten
away. Wilt thou use thy wit?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: It is in my scabbard: shall I draw it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou wear thy wit by thy side?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Never any did so, though very many have been beside
their wit. I will bid thee draw, as we do the
minstrels; draw, to pleasure us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: As I am an honest man, he looks pale. Art thou
sick, or angry?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: What, courage, man! What though care killed a cat,
thou hast mettle enough in thee to kill care.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I shall meet your wit in the career, and you
charge it against me. I pray you choose another subject.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, then, give him another staff: this last was
broke cross.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: By this light, he changes more and more: I think
he be angry indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: If he be, he knows how to turn his girdle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I speak a word in your ear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: God bless me from a challenge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to CLAUDIO You are a villain; I jest not:
I will make it good how you dare, with what you
dare, and when you dare. Do me right, or I will
protest your cowardice. You have killed a sweet
lady, and her death shall fall heavy on you. Let me
hear from you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will meet you, so I may have good cheer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: What, a feast, a feast?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I' faith, I thank him; he hath bid me to a calf's
head and a capon; the which if I do not carve most
curiously, say my knife's naught. Shall I not find
a woodcock too?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, your wit ambles well; it goes easily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll tell thee how Beatrice praised thy wit the
other day. I said, thou hadst a fine wit: 'True,'
said she, 'a fine little one.' 'No,' said I, 'a
great wit:' 'Right,' says she, 'a great gross one.'
'Nay,' said I, 'a good wit:' 'Just,' said she, 'it
hurts nobody.' 'Nay,' said I, 'the gentleman
is wise:' 'Certain,' said she, 'a wise gentleman.'
'Nay,' said I, 'he hath the tongues:' 'That I
believe,' said she, 'for he swore a thing to me on
Monday night, which he forswore on Tuesday morning;
there's a double tongue; there's two tongues.' Thus
did she, an hour together, transshape thy particular
virtues: yet at last she concluded with a sigh, thou
wast the properest man in Italy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: For the which she wept heartily and said she cared
not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, that she did: but yet, for all that, an if she
did not hate him deadly, she would love him dearly:
the old man's daughter told us all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: All, all; and, moreover, God saw him when he was
hid in the garden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: But when shall we set the savage bull's horns on
the sensible Benedick's head?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, and text underneath, 'Here dwells Benedick the
married man'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, boy: you know my mind. I will leave
you now to your gossip-like humour: you break jests
as braggarts do their blades, which God be thanked,
hurt not. My lord, for your many courtesies I thank
you: I must discontinue your company: your brother
the bastard is fled from Messina: you have among
you killed a sweet and innocent lady. For my Lord
Lackbeard there, he and I shall meet: and, till
then, peace be with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: He is in earnest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: In most profound earnest; and, I'll warrant you, for
the love of Beatrice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: And hath challenged thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Most sincerely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: What a pretty thing man is when he goes in his
doublet and hose and leaves off his wit!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: He is then a giant to an ape; but then is an ape a
doctor to such a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: But, soft you, let me be: pluck up, my heart, and
be sad. Did he not say, my brother was fled?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DOGBERRY, VERGES, and the Watch, with CONRADE and BORACHIO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Come you, sir: if justice cannot tame you, she
shall ne'er weigh more reasons in her balance: nay,
an you be a cursing hypocrite once, you must be looked to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: How now? two of my brother's men bound! Borachio
one!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Hearken after their offence, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Officers, what offence have these men done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, they have committed false report;
moreover, they have spoken untruths; secondarily,
they are slanders; sixth and lastly, they have
belied a lady; thirdly, they have verified unjust
things; and, to conclude, they are lying knaves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: First, I ask thee what they have done; thirdly, I
ask thee what's their offence; sixth and lastly, why
they are committed; and, to conclude, what you lay
to their charge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Rightly reasoned, and in his own division: and, by
my troth, there's one meaning well suited.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Who have you offended, masters, that you are thus
bound to your answer? this learned constable is
too cunning to be understood: what's your offence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet prince, let me go no farther to mine answer:
do you hear me, and let this count kill me. I have
deceived even your very eyes: what your wisdoms
could not discover, these shallow fools have brought
to light: who in the night overheard me confessing
to this man how Don John your brother incensed me
to slander the Lady Hero, how you were brought into
the orchard and saw me court Margaret in Hero's
garments, how you disgraced her, when you should
marry her: my villany they have upon record; which
I had rather seal with my death than repeat over
to my shame. The lady is dead upon mine and my
master's false accusation; and, briefly, I desire
nothing but the reward of a villain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Runs not this speech like iron through your blood?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I have drunk poison whiles he utter'd it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: But did my brother set thee on to this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, and paid me richly for the practise of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: He is composed and framed of treachery:
And fled he is upon this villany.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Hero! now thy image doth appear
In the rare semblance that I loved it first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Come, bring away the plaintiffs: by this time our
sexton hath reformed Signior Leonato of the matter:
and, masters, do not forget to specify, when time
and place shall serve, that I am an ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VERGES
SPEECH.LINE: Here, here comes master Signior Leonato, and the
Sexton too.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter LEONATO and ANTONIO, with the Sexton

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Which is the villain? let me see his eyes,
That, when I note another man like him,
I may avoid him: which of these is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: If you would know your wronger, look on me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou the slave that with thy breath hast kill'd
Mine innocent child?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, even I alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: No, not so, villain; thou beliest thyself:
Here stand a pair of honourable men;
A third is fled, that had a hand in it.
I thank you, princes, for my daughter's death:
Record it with your high and worthy deeds:
'Twas bravely done, if you bethink you of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I know not how to pray your patience;
Yet I must speak. Choose your revenge yourself;
Impose me to what penance your invention
Can lay upon my sin: yet sinn'd I not
But in mistaking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: By my soul, nor I:
And yet, to satisfy this good old man,
I would bend under any heavy weight
That he'll enjoin me to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot bid you bid my daughter live;
That were impossible: but, I pray you both,
Possess the people in Messina here
How innocent she died; and if your love
Can labour ought in sad invention,
Hang her an epitaph upon her tomb
And sing it to her bones, sing it to-night:
To-morrow morning come you to my house,
And since you could not be my son-in-law,
Be yet my nephew: my brother hath a daughter,
Almost the copy of my child that's dead,
And she alone is heir to both of us:
Give her the right you should have given her cousin,
And so dies my revenge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: O noble sir,
Your over-kindness doth wring tears from me!
I do embrace your offer; and dispose
For henceforth of poor Claudio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: To-morrow then I will expect your coming;
To-night I take my leave. This naughty man
Shall face to face be brought to Margaret,
Who I believe was pack'd in all this wrong,
Hired to it by your brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BORACHIO
SPEECH.LINE: No, by my soul, she was not,
Nor knew not what she did when she spoke to me,
But always hath been just and virtuous
In any thing that I do know by her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Moreover, sir, which indeed is not under white and
black, this plaintiff here, the offender, did call
me ass: I beseech you, let it be remembered in his
punishment. And also, the watch heard them talk of
one Deformed: they say be wears a key in his ear and
a lock hanging by it, and borrows money in God's
name, the which he hath used so long and never paid
that now men grow hard-hearted and will lend nothing
for God's sake: pray you, examine him upon that point.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee for thy care and honest pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: Your worship speaks like a most thankful and
reverend youth; and I praise God for you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: There's for thy pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: God save the foundation!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Go, I discharge thee of thy prisoner, and I thank thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DOGBERRY
SPEECH.LINE: I leave an arrant knave with your worship; which I
beseech your worship to correct yourself, for the
example of others. God keep your worship! I wish
your worship well; God restore you to health! I
humbly give you leave to depart; and if a merry
meeting may be wished, God prohibit it! Come, neighbour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Until to-morrow morning, lords, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, my lords: we look for you to-morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: We will not fail.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: To-night I'll mourn with Hero.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: To the Watch Bring you these fellows on. We'll
talk with Margaret,
How her acquaintance grew with this lewd fellow.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. LEONATO'S garden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Pray thee, sweet Mistress Margaret, deserve well at
my hands by helping me to the speech of Beatrice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Will you then write me a sonnet in praise of my beauty?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: In so high a style, Margaret, that no man living
shall come over it; for, in most comely truth, thou
deservest it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: To have no man come over me! why, shall I always
keep below stairs?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thy wit is as quick as the greyhound's mouth; it catches.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: And yours as blunt as the fencer's foils, which hit,
but hurt not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: A most manly wit, Margaret; it will not hurt a
woman: and so, I pray thee, call Beatrice: I give
thee the bucklers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Give us the swords; we have bucklers of our own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: If you use them, Margaret, you must put in the
pikes with a vice; and they are dangerous weapons for maids.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will call Beatrice to you, who I think hath legs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: And therefore will come.
The god of love,
That sits above,
And knows me, and knows me,
How pitiful I deserve,--
I mean in singing; but in loving, Leander the good
swimmer, Troilus the first employer of panders, and
a whole bookful of these quondam carpet-mangers,
whose names yet run smoothly in the even road of a
blank verse, why, they were never so truly turned
over and over as my poor self in love. Marry, I
cannot show it in rhyme; I have tried: I can find
out no rhyme to 'lady' but 'baby,' an innocent
rhyme; for 'scorn,' 'horn,' a hard rhyme; for,
'school,' 'fool,' a babbling rhyme; very ominous
endings: no, I was not born under a rhyming planet,
nor I cannot woo in festival terms.
Sweet Beatrice, wouldst thou come when I called thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, signior, and depart when you bid me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: O, stay but till then!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: 'Then' is spoken; fare you well now: and yet, ere
I go, let me go with that I came; which is, with
knowing what hath passed between you and Claudio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Only foul words; and thereupon I will kiss thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Foul words is but foul wind, and foul wind is but
foul breath, and foul breath is noisome; therefore I
will depart unkissed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast frighted the word out of his right sense,
so forcible is thy wit. But I must tell thee
plainly, Claudio undergoes my challenge; and either
I must shortly hear from him, or I will subscribe
him a coward. And, I pray thee now, tell me for
which of my bad parts didst thou first fall in love with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: For them all together; which maintained so politic
a state of evil that they will not admit any good
part to intermingle with them. But for which of my
good parts did you first suffer love for me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Suffer love! a good epithet! I do suffer love
indeed, for I love thee against my will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: In spite of your heart, I think; alas, poor heart!
If you spite it for my sake, I will spite it for
yours; for I will never love that which my friend hates.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Thou and I are too wise to woo peaceably.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: It appears not in this confession: there's not one
wise man among twenty that will praise himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: An old, an old instance, Beatrice, that lived in
the lime of good neighbours. If a man do not erect
in this age his own tomb ere he dies, he shall live
no longer in monument than the bell rings and the
widow weeps.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: And how long is that, think you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Question: why, an hour in clamour and a quarter in
rheum: therefore is it most expedient for the
wise, if Don Worm, his conscience, find no
impediment to the contrary, to be the trumpet of his
own virtues, as I am to myself. So much for
praising myself, who, I myself will bear witness, is
praiseworthy: and now tell me, how doth your cousin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Very ill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: And how do you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Very ill too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Serve God, love me and mend. There will I leave
you too, for here comes one in haste.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: URSULA
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, you must come to your uncle. Yonder's old
coil at home: it is proved my Lady Hero hath been
falsely accused, the prince and Claudio mightily
abused; and Don John is the author of all, who is
fed and gone. Will you come presently?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Will you go hear this news, signior?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: I will live in thy heart, die in thy lap, and be
buried in thy eyes; and moreover I will go with
thee to thy uncle's.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A church.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DON PEDRO, CLAUDIO, and three or four with tapers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is this the monument of Leonato?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord
SPEECH.LINE: It is, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Done to death by slanderous tongues
Was the Hero that here lies:
Death, in guerdon of her wrongs,
Gives her fame which never dies.
So the life that died with shame
Lives in death with glorious fame.
Hang thou there upon the tomb,
Praising her when I am dumb.
Now, music, sound, and sing your solemn hymn.
Pardon, goddess of the night,
Those that slew thy virgin knight;
For the which, with songs of woe,
Round about her tomb they go.
Midnight, assist our moan;
Help us to sigh and groan,
Heavily, heavily:
Graves, yawn and yield your dead,
Till death be uttered,
Heavily, heavily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, unto thy bones good night!
Yearly will I do this rite.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, masters; put your torches out:
The wolves have prey'd; and look, the gentle day,
Before the wheels of Phoebus, round about
Dapples the drowsy east with spots of grey.
Thanks to you all, and leave us: fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, masters: each his several way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, let us hence, and put on other weeds;
And then to Leonato's we will go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: And Hymen now with luckier issue speed's
Than this for whom we render'd up this woe.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. A room in LEONATO'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter LEONATO, ANTONIO, BENEDICK, BEATRICE, MARGARET, URSULA, FRIAR FRANCIS, and HERO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: Did I not tell you she was innocent?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: So are the prince and Claudio, who accused her
Upon the error that you heard debated:
But Margaret was in some fault for this,
Although against her will, as it appears
In the true course of all the question.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I am glad that all things sort so well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: And so am I, being else by faith enforced
To call young Claudio to a reckoning for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, daughter, and you gentle-women all,
Withdraw into a chamber by yourselves,
And when I send for you, come hither mask'd.
The prince and Claudio promised by this hour
To visit me. You know your office, brother:
You must be father to your brother's daughter
And give her to young Claudio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Which I will do with confirm'd countenance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Friar, I must entreat your pains, I think.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: To do what, signior?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: To bind me, or undo me; one of them.
Signior Leonato, truth it is, good signior,
Your niece regards me with an eye of favour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: That eye my daughter lent her: 'tis most true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: And I do with an eye of love requite her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: The sight whereof I think you had from me,
From Claudio and the prince: but what's your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Your answer, sir, is enigmatical:
But, for my will, my will is your good will
May stand with ours, this day to be conjoin'd
In the state of honourable marriage:
In which, good friar, I shall desire your help.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: My heart is with your liking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: And my help.
Here comes the prince and Claudio.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DON PEDRO and CLAUDIO, and two or three others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow to this fair assembly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, prince; good morrow, Claudio:
We here attend you. Are you yet determined
To-day to marry with my brother's daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll hold my mind, were she an Ethiope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Call her forth, brother; here's the friar ready.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, Benedick. Why, what's the matter,
That you have such a February face,
So full of frost, of storm and cloudiness?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I think he thinks upon the savage bull.
Tush, fear not, man; we'll tip thy horns with gold
And all Europa shall rejoice at thee,
As once Europa did at lusty Jove,
When he would play the noble beast in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Bull Jove, sir, had an amiable low;
And some such strange bull leap'd your father's cow,
And got a calf in that same noble feat
Much like to you, for you have just his bleat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: For this I owe you: here comes other reckonings.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Re-enter ANTONIO, with the Ladies masked
SPEECH.LINE: Which is the lady I must seize upon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: This same is she, and I do give you her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then she's mine. Sweet, let me see your face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: No, that you shall not, till you take her hand
Before this friar and swear to marry her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Give me your hand: before this holy friar,
I am your husband, if you like of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: And when I lived, I was your other wife:
And when you loved, you were my other husband.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: Another Hero!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing certainer:
One Hero died defiled, but I do live,
And surely as I live, I am a maid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: The former Hero! Hero that is dead!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: She died, my lord, but whiles her slander lived.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FRIAR FRANCIS
SPEECH.LINE: All this amazement can I qualify:
When after that the holy rites are ended,
I'll tell you largely of fair Hero's death:
Meantime let wonder seem familiar,
And to the chapel let us presently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Soft and fair, friar. Which is Beatrice?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Unmasking I answer to that name. What is your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Do not you love me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, no; no more than reason.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then your uncle and the prince and Claudio
Have been deceived; they swore you did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Do not you love me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Troth, no; no more than reason.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then my cousin Margaret and Ursula
Are much deceived; for they did swear you did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: They swore that you were almost sick for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: They swore that you were well-nigh dead for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis no such matter. Then you do not love me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: No, truly, but in friendly recompense.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, cousin, I am sure you love the gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: And I'll be sworn upon't that he loves her;
For here's a paper written in his hand,
A halting sonnet of his own pure brain,
Fashion'd to Beatrice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HERO
SPEECH.LINE: And here's another
Writ in my cousin's hand, stolen from her pocket,
Containing her affection unto Benedick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: A miracle! here's our own hands against our hearts.
Come, I will have thee; but, by this light, I take
thee for pity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BEATRICE
SPEECH.LINE: I would not deny you; but, by this good day, I yield
upon great persuasion; and partly to save your life,
for I was told you were in a consumption.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Peace! I will stop your mouth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DON PEDRO
SPEECH.LINE: How dost thou, Benedick, the married man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: I'll tell thee what, prince; a college of
wit-crackers cannot flout me out of my humour. Dost
thou think I care for a satire or an epigram? No:
if a man will be beaten with brains, a' shall wear
nothing handsome about him. In brief, since I do
purpose to marry, I will think nothing to any
purpose that the world can say against it; and
therefore never flout at me for what I have said
against it; for man is a giddy thing, and this is my
conclusion. For thy part, Claudio, I did think to
have beaten thee, but in that thou art like to be my
kinsman, live unbruised and love my cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLAUDIO
SPEECH.LINE: I had well hoped thou wouldst have denied Beatrice,
that I might have cudgelled thee out of thy single
life, to make thee a double-dealer; which, out of
question, thou wilt be, if my cousin do not look
exceedingly narrowly to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, we are friends: let's have a dance ere
we are married, that we may lighten our own hearts
and our wives' heels.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONATO
SPEECH.LINE: We'll have dancing afterward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: First, of my word; therefore play, music. Prince,
thou art sad; get thee a wife, get thee a wife:
there is no staff more reverend than one tipped with horn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, your brother John is ta'en in flight,
And brought with armed men back to Messina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENEDICK
SPEECH.LINE: Think not on him till to-morrow:
I'll devise thee brave punishments for him.
Strike up, pipers.

PLAY.TITLE: The Tragedy of Othello, the Moor of Venice

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: OTHELLO, a noble Moor in the service of the Venetian state.
MONTANO, Othello's predecessor in the government of Cyprus.
DESDEMONA, daughter to Brabantio and wife to Othello.
Sailor, Messenger, Herald, Officers, Gentlemen, Musicians, and Attendants.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE Venice: a Sea-port in Cyprus.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Venice. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Tush! never tell me; I take it much unkindly
That thou, Iago, who hast had my purse
As if the strings were thine, shouldst know of this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Sblood, but you will not hear me:
If ever I did dream of such a matter, Abhor me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou told'st me thou didst hold him in thy hate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Despise me, if I do not. Three great ones of the city,
In personal suit to make me his lieutenant,
Off-capp'd to him: and, by the faith of man,
I know my price, I am worth no worse a place:
But he; as loving his own pride and purposes,
Evades them, with a bombast circumstance
Horribly stuff'd with epithets of war;
And, in conclusion,
Nonsuits my mediators; for, 'Certes,' says he,
'I have already chose my officer.'
And what was he?
Forsooth, a great arithmetician,
One Michael Cassio, a Florentine,
A fellow almost damn'd in a fair wife;
That never set a squadron in the field,
Nor the division of a battle knows
More than a spinster; unless the bookish theoric,
Wherein the toged consuls can propose
As masterly as he: mere prattle, without practise,
Is all his soldiership. But he, sir, had the election:
And I, of whom his eyes had seen the proof
At Rhodes, at Cyprus and on other grounds
Christian and heathen, must be be-lee'd and calm'd
By debitor and creditor: this counter-caster,
He, in good time, must his lieutenant be,
And I--God bless the mark!--his Moorship's ancient.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, I rather would have been his hangman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, there's no remedy; 'tis the curse of service,
Preferment goes by letter and affection,
And not by old gradation, where each second
Stood heir to the first. Now, sir, be judge yourself,
Whether I in any just term am affined
To love the Moor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: I would not follow him then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, content you;
I follow him to serve my turn upon him:
We cannot all be masters, nor all masters
Cannot be truly follow'd. You shall mark
Many a duteous and knee-crooking knave,
That, doting on his own obsequious bondage,
Wears out his time, much like his master's ass,
For nought but provender, and when he's old, cashier'd:
Whip me such honest knaves. Others there are
Who, trimm'd in forms and visages of duty,
Keep yet their hearts attending on themselves,
And, throwing but shows of service on their lords,
Do well thrive by them and when they have lined
their coats
Do themselves homage: these fellows have some soul;
And such a one do I profess myself. For, sir,
It is as sure as you are Roderigo,
Were I the Moor, I would not be Iago:
In following him, I follow but myself;
Heaven is my judge, not I for love and duty,
But seeming so, for my peculiar end:
For when my outward action doth demonstrate
The native act and figure of my heart
In compliment extern, 'tis not long after
But I will wear my heart upon my sleeve
For daws to peck at: I am not what I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: What a full fortune does the thicklips owe
If he can carry't thus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Call up her father,
Rouse him: make after him, poison his delight,
Proclaim him in the streets; incense her kinsmen,
And, though he in a fertile climate dwell,
Plague him with flies: though that his joy be joy,
Yet throw such changes of vexation on't,
As it may lose some colour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Here is her father's house; I'll call aloud.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Do, with like timorous accent and dire yell
As when, by night and negligence, the fire
Is spied in populous cities.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: What, ho, Brabantio! Signior Brabantio, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Awake! what, ho, Brabantio! thieves! thieves! thieves!
Look to your house, your daughter and your bags!
Thieves! thieves!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: BRABANTIO appears above, at a window

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What is the reason of this terrible summons?
What is the matter there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Signior, is all your family within?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: Are your doors lock'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, wherefore ask you this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds, sir, you're robb'd; for shame, put on
your gown;
Your heart is burst, you have lost half your soul;
Even now, now, very now, an old black ram
Is topping your white ewe. Arise, arise;
Awake the snorting citizens with the bell,
Or else the devil will make a grandsire of you:
Arise, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What, have you lost your wits?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Most reverend signior, do you know my voice?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not I what are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: My name is Roderigo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: The worser welcome:
I have charged thee not to haunt about my doors:
In honest plainness thou hast heard me say
My daughter is not for thee; and now, in madness,
Being full of supper and distempering draughts,
Upon malicious bravery, dost thou come
To start my quiet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, sir, sir,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: But thou must needs be sure
My spirit and my place have in them power
To make this bitter to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Patience, good sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What tell'st thou me of robbing? this is Venice;
My house is not a grange.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Most grave Brabantio,
In simple and pure soul I come to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds, sir, you are one of those that will not
serve God, if the devil bid you. Because we come to
do you service and you think we are ruffians, you'll
have your daughter covered with a Barbary horse;
you'll have your nephews neigh to you; you'll have
coursers for cousins and gennets for germans.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What profane wretch art thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: I am one, sir, that comes to tell you your daughter
and the Moor are now making the beast with two backs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art a villain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: IAGO
SPEECH.LINE: You are--a senator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRABANTIO
SPEECH.LINE: This thou shalt answer; I know thee, Roderigo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RODERIGO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I will answer any thing. But, I beseech you,
If't be your pleasure and most wise consent,
As partly I find it is, that your fair daughter,
At this odd-even and dull watch o' the night,
Transported, with no worse nor better guard
But with a knave of common hire, a gondolier,
To the gross clasps of a lascivious Moor--
If this be known to you and your allowance,
We then have done you bold and saucy wrongs;
But if you know not this, my manners tell me
We have your wrong rebuke. Do not believe
That, from the sense of all civility,
I thus would play and trifle with your reverence:
Your daughter, if you have not given her leave,
I say again, hath made a gross revolt;
Tying her duty, beauty, wit and fortunes
In an extravagant and wheeling stranger
