SPEECH.LINE: How close 'tis caulk'd and bitumed!
Did the sea cast it up?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I never saw so huge a billow, sir,
As toss'd it upon shore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Wrench it open;
Soft! it smells most sweetly in my sense.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: A delicate odour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: As ever hit my nostril. So, up with it.
O you most potent gods! what's here? a corse!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Most strange!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Shrouded in cloth of state; balm'd and entreasured
With full bags of spices! A passport too!
Apollo, perfect me in the characters!
'Here I give to understand,
If e'er this coffin drive a-land,
I, King Pericles, have lost
This queen, worth all our mundane cost.
Who finds her, give her burying;
She was the daughter of a king:
Besides this treasure for a fee,
The gods requite his charity!'
If thou livest, Pericles, thou hast a heart
That even cracks for woe! This chanced tonight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Most likely, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, certainly to-night;
For look how fresh she looks! They were too rough
That threw her in the sea. Make a fire within:
Fetch hither all my boxes in my closet.
Death may usurp on nature many hours,
And yet the fire of life kindle again
The o'erpress'd spirits. I heard of an Egyptian
That had nine hours lien dead,
Who was by good appliance recovered.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Re-enter a Servant, with boxes, napkins, and fire
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, well said; the fire and cloths.
The rough and woeful music that we have,
Cause it to sound, beseech you.
The viol once more: how thou stirr'st, thou block!
The music there!--I pray you, give her air.
Gentlemen.
This queen will live: nature awakes; a warmth
Breathes out of her: she hath not been entranced
Above five hours: see how she gins to blow
Into life's flower again!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: The heavens,
Through you, increase our wonder and set up
Your fame forever.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: She is alive; behold,
Her eyelids, cases to those heavenly jewels
Which Pericles hath lost,
Begin to part their fringes of bright gold;
The diamonds of a most praised water
Do appear, to make the world twice rich. Live,
And make us weep to hear your fate, fair creature,
Rare as you seem to be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: O dear Diana,
Where am I? Where's my lord? What world is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Is not this strange?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Most rare.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Hush, my gentle neighbours!
Lend me your hands; to the next chamber bear her.
Get linen: now this matter must be look'd to,
For her relapse is mortal. Come, come;
And AEsculapius guide us!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Tarsus. A room in CLEON's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PERICLES, CLEON, DIONYZA, and LYCHORIDA with MARINA in her arms

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Most honour'd Cleon, I must needs be gone;
My twelve months are expired, and Tyrus stands
In a litigious peace. You, and your lady,
Take from my heart all thankfulness! The gods
Make up the rest upon you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: Your shafts of fortune, though they hurt you mortally,
Yet glance full wanderingly on us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: O your sweet queen!
That the strict fates had pleased you had brought her hither,
To have bless'd mine eyes with her!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: We cannot but obey
The powers above us. Could I rage and roar
As doth the sea she lies in, yet the end
Must be as 'tis. My gentle babe Marina, whom,
For she was born at sea, I have named so, here
I charge your charity withal, leaving her
The infant of your care; beseeching you
To give her princely training, that she may be
Manner'd as she is born.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: Fear not, my lord, but think
Your grace, that fed my country with your corn,
For which the people's prayers still fall upon you,
Must in your child be thought on. If neglection
Should therein make me vile, the common body,
By you relieved, would force me to my duty:
But if to that my nature need a spur,
The gods revenge it upon me and mine,
To the end of generation!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I believe you;
Your honour and your goodness teach me to't,
Without your vows. Till she be married, madam,
By bright Diana, whom we honour, all
Unscissor'd shall this hair of mine remain,
Though I show ill in't. So I take my leave.
Good madam, make me blessed in your care
In bringing up my child.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: I have one myself,
Who shall not be more dear to my respect
Than yours, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, my thanks and prayers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: We'll bring your grace e'en to the edge o' the shore,
Then give you up to the mask'd Neptune and
The gentlest winds of heaven.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I will embrace
Your offer. Come, dearest madam. O, no tears,
Lychorida, no tears:
Look to your little mistress, on whose grace
You may depend hereafter. Come, my lord.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Ephesus. A room in CERIMON's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, this letter, and some certain jewels,
Lay with you in your coffer: which are now
At your command. Know you the character?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: It is my lord's.
That I was shipp'd at sea, I well remember,
Even on my eaning time; but whether there
Deliver'd, by the holy gods,
I cannot rightly say. But since King Pericles,
My wedded lord, I ne'er shall see again,
A vestal livery will I take me to,
And never more have joy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, if this you purpose as ye speak,
Diana's temple is not distant far,
Where you may abide till your date expire.
Moreover, if you please, a niece of mine
Shall there attend you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: My recompense is thanks, that's all;
Yet my good will is great, though the gift small.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GOWER
SPEECH.LINE: Imagine Pericles arrived at Tyre,
Welcomed and settled to his own desire.
His woeful queen we leave at Ephesus,
Unto Diana there a votaress.
Now to Marina bend your mind,
Whom our fast-growing scene must find
At Tarsus, and by Cleon train'd
In music, letters; who hath gain'd
Of education all the grace,
Which makes her both the heart and place
Of general wonder. But, alack,
That monster envy, oft the wrack
Of earned praise, Marina's life
Seeks to take off by treason's knife.
And in this kind hath our Cleon
One daughter, and a wench full grown,
Even ripe for marriage-rite; this maid
Hight Philoten: and it is said
For certain in our story, she
Would ever with Marina be:
Be't when she weaved the sleided silk
With fingers long, small, white as milk;
Or when she would with sharp needle wound
The cambric, which she made more sound
By hurting it; or when to the lute
She sung, and made the night-bird mute,
That still records with moan; or when
She would with rich and constant pen
Vail to her mistress Dian; still
This Philoten contends in skill
With absolute Marina: so
With the dove of Paphos might the crow
Vie feathers white. Marina gets
All praises, which are paid as debts,
And not as given. This so darks
In Philoten all graceful marks,
That Cleon's wife, with envy rare,
A present murderer does prepare
For good Marina, that her daughter
Might stand peerless by this slaughter.
The sooner her vile thoughts to stead,
Lychorida, our nurse, is dead:
And cursed Dionyza hath
The pregnant instrument of wrath
Prest for this blow. The unborn event
I do commend to your content:
Only I carry winged time
Post on the lame feet of my rhyme;
Which never could I so convey,
Unless your thoughts went on my way.
Dionyza does appear,
With Leonine, a murderer.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Tarsus. An open place near the sea-shore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Thy oath remember; thou hast sworn to do't:
'Tis but a blow, which never shall be known.
Thou canst not do a thing in the world so soon,
To yield thee so much profit. Let not conscience,
Which is but cold, inflaming love i' thy bosom,
Inflame too nicely; nor let pity, which
Even women have cast off, melt thee, but be
A soldier to thy purpose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: I will do't; but yet she is a goodly creature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: The fitter, then, the gods should have her. Here
she comes weeping for her only mistress' death.
Thou art resolved?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: I am resolved.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MARINA, with a basket of flowers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No, I will rob Tellus of her weed,
To strew thy green with flowers: the yellows, blues,
The purple violets, and marigolds,
Shall as a carpet hang upon thy grave,
While summer-days do last. Ay me! poor maid,
Born in a tempest, when my mother died,
This world to me is like a lasting storm,
Whirring me from my friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Marina! why do you keep alone?
How chance my daughter is not with you? Do not
Consume your blood with sorrowing: you have
A nurse of me. Lord, how your favour's changed
With this unprofitable woe!
Come, give me your flowers, ere the sea mar it.
Walk with Leonine; the air is quick there,
And it pierces and sharpens the stomach. Come,
Leonine, take her by the arm, walk with her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No, I pray you;
I'll not bereave you of your servant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come;
I love the king your father, and yourself,
With more than foreign heart. We every day
Expect him here: when he shall come and find
Our paragon to all reports thus blasted,
He will repent the breadth of his great voyage;
Blame both my lord and me, that we have taken
No care to your best courses. Go, I pray you,
Walk, and be cheerful once again; reserve
That excellent complexion, which did steal
The eyes of young and old. Care not for me
I can go home alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will go;
But yet I have no desire to it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, I know 'tis good for you.
Walk half an hour, Leonine, at the least:
Remember what I have said.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: I warrant you, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll leave you, my sweet lady, for a while:
Pray, walk softly, do not heat your blood:
What! I must have a care of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: My thanks, sweet madam.
Is this wind westerly that blows?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: South-west.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: When I was born, the wind was north.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: Was't so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: My father, as nurse said, did never fear,
But cried 'Good seaman!' to the sailors, galling
His kingly hands, haling ropes;
And, clasping to the mast, endured a sea
That almost burst the deck.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: When was this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: When I was born:
Never was waves nor wind more violent;
And from the ladder-tackle washes off
A canvas-climber. 'Ha!' says one, 'wilt out?'
And with a dropping industry they skip
From stem to stern: the boatswain whistles, and
The master calls, and trebles their confusion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: Come, say your prayers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What mean you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: If you require a little space for prayer,
I grant it: pray; but be not tedious,
For the gods are quick of ear, and I am sworn
To do my work with haste.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Why will you kill me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: To satisfy my lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Why would she have me kill'd?
Now, as I can remember, by my troth,
I never did her hurt in all my life:
I never spake bad word, nor did ill turn
To any living creature: believe me, la,
I never kill'd a mouse, nor hurt a fly:
I trod upon a worm against my will,
But I wept for it. How have I offended,
Wherein my death might yield her any profit,
Or my life imply her any danger?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: My commission
Is not to reason of the deed, but do it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: You will not do't for all the world, I hope.
You are well favour'd, and your looks foreshow
You have a gentle heart. I saw you lately,
When you caught hurt in parting two that fought:
Good sooth, it show'd well in you: do so now:
Your lady seeks my life; come you between,
And save poor me, the weaker.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: I am sworn,
And will dispatch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Pirate
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, villain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Pirate
SPEECH.LINE: A prize! a prize!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Pirate
SPEECH.LINE: Half-part, mates, half-part.
Come, let's have her aboard suddenly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LEONINE
SPEECH.LINE: These roguing thieves serve the great pirate Valdes;
And they have seized Marina. Let her go:
There's no hope she will return. I'll swear
she's dead,
And thrown into the sea. But I'll see further:
Perhaps they will but please themselves upon her,
Not carry her aboard. If she remain,
Whom they have ravish'd must by me be slain.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Mytilene. A room in a brothel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Boult!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Search the market narrowly; Mytilene is full of
gallants. We lost too much money this mart by being
too wenchless.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: We were never so much out of creatures. We have but
poor three, and they can do no more than they can
do; and they with continual action are even as good as rotten.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore let's have fresh ones, whate'er we pay for
them. If there be not a conscience to be used in
every trade, we shall never prosper.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Thou sayest true: 'tis not our bringing up of poor
bastards,--as, I think, I have brought up some eleven--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, to eleven; and brought them down again. But
shall I search the market?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: What else, man? The stuff we have, a strong wind
will blow it to pieces, they are so pitifully sodden.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Thou sayest true; they're too unwholesome, o'
conscience. The poor Transylvanian is dead, that
lay with the little baggage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, she quickly pooped him; she made him roast-meat
for worms. But I'll go search the market.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Three or four thousand chequins were as pretty a
proportion to live quietly, and so give over.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Why to give over, I pray you? is it a shame to get
when we are old?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: O, our credit comes not in like the commodity, nor
the commodity wages not with the danger: therefore,
if in our youths we could pick up some pretty
estate, 'twere not amiss to keep our door hatched.
Besides, the sore terms we stand upon with the gods
will be strong with us for giving over.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Come, other sorts offend as well as we.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: As well as we! ay, and better too; we offend worse.
Neither is our profession any trade; it's no
calling. But here comes Boult.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter BOULT, with the Pirates and MARINA

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: To MARINA Come your ways. My masters, you say
she's a virgin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Pirate
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, we doubt it not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Master, I have gone through for this piece, you see:
if you like her, so; if not, I have lost my earnest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Boult, has she any qualities?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: She has a good face, speaks well, and has excellent
good clothes: there's no further necessity of
qualities can make her be refused.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: What's her price, Boult?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot be bated one doit of a thousand pieces.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Well, follow me, my masters, you shall have your
money presently. Wife, take her in; instruct her
what she has to do, that she may not be raw in her
entertainment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Boult, take you the marks of her, the colour of her
hair, complexion, height, age, with warrant of her
virginity; and cry 'He that will give most shall
have her first.' Such a maidenhead were no cheap
thing, if men were as they have been. Get this done
as I command you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Performance shall follow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Alack that Leonine was so slack, so slow!
He should have struck, not spoke; or that these pirates,
Not enough barbarous, had not o'erboard thrown me
For to seek my mother!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Why lament you, pretty one?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: That I am pretty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Come, the gods have done their part in you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I accuse them not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: You are light into my hands, where you are like to live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The more my fault
To scape his hands where I was like to die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and you shall live in pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, indeed shall you, and taste gentlemen of all
fashions: you shall fare well; you shall have the
difference of all complexions. What! do you stop your ears?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Are you a woman?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: What would you have me be, an I be not a woman?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: An honest woman, or not a woman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, whip thee, gosling: I think I shall have
something to do with you. Come, you're a young
foolish sapling, and must be bowed as I would have
you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The gods defend me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: If it please the gods to defend you by men, then men
must comfort you, men must feed you, men must stir
you up. Boult's returned.
Now, sir, hast thou cried her through the market?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I have cried her almost to the number of her hairs;
I have drawn her picture with my voice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: And I prithee tell me, how dost thou find the
inclination of the people, especially of the younger sort?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, they listened to me as they would have
hearkened to their father's testament. There was a
Spaniard's mouth so watered, that he went to bed to
her very description.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: We shall have him here to-morrow with his best ruff on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: To-night, to-night. But, mistress, do you know the
French knight that cowers i' the hams?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Who, Monsieur Veroles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, he: he offered to cut a caper at the
proclamation; but he made a groan at it, and swore
he would see her to-morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Well, well; as for him, he brought his disease
hither: here he does but repair it. I know he will
come in our shadow, to scatter his crowns in the
sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Well, if we had of every nation a traveller, we
should lodge them with this sign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: To MARINA Pray you, come hither awhile. You
have fortunes coming upon you. Mark me: you must
seem to do that fearfully which you commit
willingly, despise profit where you have most gain.
To weep that you live as ye do makes pity in your
lovers: seldom but that pity begets you a good
opinion, and that opinion a mere profit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I understand you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: O, take her home, mistress, take her home: these
blushes of hers must be quenched with some present practise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Thou sayest true, i' faith, so they must; for your
bride goes to that with shame which is her way to go
with warrant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, some do, and some do not. But, mistress, if
I have bargained for the joint,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Thou mayst cut a morsel off the spit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I may so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Who should deny it? Come, young one, I like the
manner of your garments well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, by my faith, they shall not be changed yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Boult, spend thou that in the town: report what a
sojourner we have; you'll lose nothing by custom.
When nature flamed this piece, she meant thee a good
turn; therefore say what a paragon she is, and thou
hast the harvest out of thine own report.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I warrant you, mistress, thunder shall not so awake
the beds of eels as my giving out her beauty stir up
the lewdly-inclined. I'll bring home some to-night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Come your ways; follow me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: If fires be hot, knives sharp, or waters deep,
Untied I still my virgin knot will keep.
Diana, aid my purpose!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: What have we to do with Diana? Pray you, will you go with us?

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Tarsus. A room in CLEON's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, are you foolish? Can it be undone?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: O Dionyza, such a piece of slaughter
The sun and moon ne'er look'd upon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: I think
You'll turn a child again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: Were I chief lord of all this spacious world,
I'ld give it to undo the deed. O lady,
Much less in blood than virtue, yet a princess
To equal any single crown o' the earth
I' the justice of compare! O villain Leonine!
Whom thou hast poison'd too:
If thou hadst drunk to him, 't had been a kindness
Becoming well thy fact: what canst thou say
When noble Pericles shall demand his child?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: That she is dead. Nurses are not the fates,
To foster it, nor ever to preserve.
She died at night; I'll say so. Who can cross it?
Unless you play the pious innocent,
And for an honest attribute cry out
'She died by foul play.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: O, go to. Well, well,
Of all the faults beneath the heavens, the gods
Do like this worst.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Be one of those that think
The petty wrens of Tarsus will fly hence,
And open this to Pericles. I do shame
To think of what a noble strain you are,
And of how coward a spirit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: To such proceeding
Who ever but his approbation added,
Though not his prime consent, he did not flow
From honourable sources.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so, then:
Yet none does know, but you, how she came dead,
Nor none can know, Leonine being gone.
She did disdain my child, and stood between
Her and her fortunes: none would look on her,
But cast their gazes on Marina's face;
Whilst ours was blurted at and held a malkin
Not worth the time of day. It pierced me through;
And though you call my course unnatural,
You not your child well loving, yet I find
It greets me as an enterprise of kindness
Perform'd to your sole daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: Heavens forgive it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: And as for Pericles,
What should he say? We wept after her hearse,
And yet we mourn: her monument
Is almost finish'd, and her epitaphs
In glittering golden characters express
A general praise to her, and care in us
At whose expense 'tis done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLEON
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art like the harpy,
Which, to betray, dost, with thine angel's face,
Seize with thine eagle's talons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: You are like one that superstitiously
Doth swear to the gods that winter kills the flies:
But yet I know you'll do as I advise.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter GOWER, before the monument of MARINA at Tarsus

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GOWER
SPEECH.LINE: Thus time we waste, and longest leagues make short;
Sail seas in cockles, have an wish but for't;
Making, to take your imagination,
From bourn to bourn, region to region.
By you being pardon'd, we commit no crime
To use one language in each several clime
Where our scenes seem to live. I do beseech you
To learn of me, who stand i' the gaps to teach you,
The stages of our story. Pericles
Is now again thwarting the wayward seas,
Attended on by many a lord and knight.
To see his daughter, all his life's delight.
Old Escanes, whom Helicanus late
Advanced in time to great and high estate,
Is left to govern. Bear you it in mind,
Old Helicanus goes along behind.
Well-sailing ships and bounteous winds have brought
This king to Tarsus,--think his pilot thought;
So with his steerage shall your thoughts grow on,--
To fetch his daughter home, who first is gone.
Like motes and shadows see them move awhile;
Your ears unto your eyes I'll reconcile.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter PERICLES, at one door, with all his train; CLEON and DIONYZA, at the other. CLEON shows PERICLES the tomb; whereat PERICLES makes lamentation, puts on sackcloth, and in a mighty passion departs. Then exeunt CLEON and DIONYZA
SPEECH.LINE: See how belief may suffer by foul show!
This borrow'd passion stands for true old woe;
And Pericles, in sorrow all devour'd,
With sighs shot through, and biggest tears
o'ershower'd,
Leaves Tarsus and again embarks. He swears
Never to wash his face, nor cut his hairs:
He puts on sackcloth, and to sea. He bears
A tempest, which his mortal vessel tears,
And yet he rides it out. Now please you wit.
The epitaph is for Marina writ
By wicked Dionyza.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Reads the inscription on MARINA's monument
SPEECH.LINE: 'The fairest, sweet'st, and best lies here,
Who wither'd in her spring of year.
She was of Tyrus the king's daughter,
On whom foul death hath made this slaughter;
Marina was she call'd; and at her birth,
Thetis, being proud, swallow'd some part o' the earth:
Therefore the earth, fearing to be o'erflow'd,
Hath Thetis' birth-child on the heavens bestow'd:
Wherefore she does, and swears she'll never stint,
Make raging battery upon shores of flint.'
No visor does become black villany
So well as soft and tender flattery.
Let Pericles believe his daughter's dead,
And bear his courses to be ordered
By Lady Fortune; while our scene must play
His daughter's woe and heavy well-a-day
In her unholy service. Patience, then,
And think you now are all in Mytilene.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Mytilene. A street before the brothel.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter, from the brothel, two Gentlemen

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Did you ever hear the like?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: No, nor never shall do in such a place as this, she
being once gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: But to have divinity preached there! did you ever
dream of such a thing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: No, no. Come, I am for no more bawdy-houses:
shall's go hear the vestals sing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: I'll do any thing now that is virtuous; but I
am out of the road of rutting for ever.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. The same. A room in the brothel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I had rather than twice the worth of her she
had ne'er come here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie upon her! she's able to freeze the god
Priapus, and undo a whole generation. We must
either get her ravished, or be rid of her. When she
should do for clients her fitment, and do me the
kindness of our profession, she has me her quirks,
her reasons, her master reasons, her prayers, her
knees; that she would make a puritan of the devil,
if he should cheapen a kiss of her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, I must ravish her, or she'll disfurnish us
of all our cavaliers, and make our swearers priests.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pandar
SPEECH.LINE: Now, the pox upon her green-sickness for me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, there's no way to be rid on't but by the
way to the pox. Here comes the Lord Lysimachus disguised.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: We should have both lord and lown, if the peevish
baggage would but give way to customers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now! How a dozen of virginities?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Now, the gods to-bless your honour!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad to see your honour in good health.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: You may so; 'tis the better for you that your
resorters stand upon sound legs. How now!
wholesome iniquity have you that a man may deal
withal, and defy the surgeon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: We have here one, sir, if she would--but there never
came her like in Mytilene.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: If she'ld do the deed of darkness, thou wouldst say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Your honour knows what 'tis to say well enough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, call forth, call forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: For flesh and blood, sir, white and red, you shall
see a rose; and she were a rose indeed, if she had but--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, prithee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, I can be modest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: That dignifies the renown of a bawd, no less than it
gives a good report to a number to be chaste.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes that which grows to the stalk; never
plucked yet, I can assure you.
Is she not a fair creature?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, she would serve after a long voyage at sea.
Well, there's for you: leave us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech your honour, give me leave: a word, and
I'll have done presently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech you, do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: To MARINA First, I would have you note, this is
an honourable man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I desire to find him so, that I may worthily note him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Next, he's the governor of this country, and a man
whom I am bound to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: If he govern the country, you are bound to him
indeed; but how honourable he is in that, I know not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, without any more virginal fencing, will
you use him kindly? He will line your apron with gold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What he will do graciously, I will thankfully receive.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha' you done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, she's not paced yet: you must take some
pains to work her to your manage. Come, we will
leave his honour and her together. Go thy ways.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, pretty one, how long have you been at this trade?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What trade, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I cannot name't but I shall offend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot be offended with my trade. Please you to name it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: How long have you been of this profession?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: E'er since I can remember.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Did you go to 't so young? Were you a gamester at
five or at seven?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Earlier too, sir, if now I be one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, the house you dwell in proclaims you to be a
creature of sale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Do you know this house to be a place of such resort,
and will come into 't? I hear say you are of
honourable parts, and are the governor of this place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, hath your principal made known unto you who I am?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Who is my principal?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, your herb-woman; she that sets seeds and roots
of shame and iniquity. O, you have heard something
of my power, and so stand aloof for more serious
wooing. But I protest to thee, pretty one, my
authority shall not see thee, or else look friendly
upon thee. Come, bring me to some private place:
come, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: If you were born to honour, show it now;
If put upon you, make the judgment good
That thought you worthy of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: How's this? how's this? Some more; be sage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: For me,
That am a maid, though most ungentle fortune
Have placed me in this sty, where, since I came,
Diseases have been sold dearer than physic,
O, that the gods
Would set me free from this unhallow'd place,
Though they did change me to the meanest bird
That flies i' the purer air!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: I did not think
Thou couldst have spoke so well; ne'er dream'd thou couldst.
Had I brought hither a corrupted mind,
Thy speech had alter'd it. Hold, here's gold for thee:
Persever in that clear way thou goest,
And the gods strengthen thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The good gods preserve you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: For me, be you thoughten
That I came with no ill intent; for to me
The very doors and windows savour vilely.
Fare thee well. Thou art a piece of virtue, and
I doubt not but thy training hath been noble.
Hold, here's more gold for thee.
A curse upon him, die he like a thief,
That robs thee of thy goodness! If thou dost
Hear from me, it shall be for thy good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech your honour, one piece for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Avaunt, thou damned door-keeper!
Your house, but for this virgin that doth prop it,
Would sink and overwhelm you. Away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: How's this? We must take another course with you.
If your peevish chastity, which is not worth a
breakfast in the cheapest country under the cope,
shall undo a whole household, let me be gelded like
a spaniel. Come your ways.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Whither would you have me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: I must have your maidenhead taken off, or the common
hangman shall execute it. Come your ways. We'll
have no more gentlemen driven away. Come your ways, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Worse and worse, mistress; she has here spoken holy
words to the Lord Lysimachus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: O abominable!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: She makes our profession as it were to stink afore
the face of the gods.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, hang her up for ever!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: The nobleman would have dealt with her like a
nobleman, and she sent him away as cold as a
snowball; saying his prayers too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: Boult, take her away; use her at thy pleasure:
crack the glass of her virginity, and make the rest malleable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: An if she were a thornier piece of ground than she
is, she shall be ploughed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Hark, hark, you gods!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Bawd
SPEECH.LINE: She conjures: away with her! Would she had never
come within my doors! Marry, hang you! She's born
to undo us. Will you not go the way of women-kind?
Marry, come up, my dish of chastity with rosemary and bays!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Come, mistress; come your ways with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Whither wilt thou have me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: To take from you the jewel you hold so dear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, tell me one thing first.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Come now, your one thing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What canst thou wish thine enemy to be?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I could wish him to be my master, or rather, my mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Neither of these are so bad as thou art,
Since they do better thee in their command.
Thou hold'st a place, for which the pained'st fiend
Of hell would not in reputation change:
Thou art the damned doorkeeper to every
Coistrel that comes inquiring for his Tib;
To the choleric fisting of every rogue
Thy ear is liable; thy food is such
As hath been belch'd on by infected lungs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: What would you have me do? go to the wars, would
you? where a man may serve seven years for the loss
of a leg, and have not money enough in the end to
buy him a wooden one?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Do any thing but this thou doest. Empty
Old receptacles, or common shores, of filth;
Serve by indenture to the common hangman:
Any of these ways are yet better than this;
For what thou professest, a baboon, could he speak,
Would own a name too dear. O, that the gods
Would safely deliver me from this place!
Here, here's gold for thee.
If that thy master would gain by thee,
Proclaim that I can sing, weave, sew, and dance,
With other virtues, which I'll keep from boast:
And I will undertake all these to teach.
I doubt not but this populous city will
Yield many scholars.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: But can you teach all this you speak of?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Prove that I cannot, take me home again,
And prostitute me to the basest groom
That doth frequent your house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I will see what I can do for thee: if I can
place thee, I will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: But amongst honest women.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BOULT
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, my acquaintance lies little amongst them.
But since my master and mistress have bought you,
there's no going but by their consent: therefore I
will make them acquainted with your purpose, and I
doubt not but I shall find them tractable enough.
Come, I'll do for thee what I can; come your ways.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GOWER
SPEECH.LINE: Marina thus the brothel 'scapes, and chances
Into an honest house, our story says.
She sings like one immortal, and she dances
As goddess-like to her admired lays;
Deep clerks she dumbs; and with her needle composes
Nature's own shape, of bud, bird, branch, or berry,
That even her art sisters the natural roses;
Her inkle, silk, twin with the rubied cherry:
That pupils lacks she none of noble race,
Who pour their bounty on her; and her gain
She gives the cursed bawd. Here we her place;
And to her father turn our thoughts again,
Where we left him, on the sea. We there him lost;
Whence, driven before the winds, he is arrived
Here where his daughter dwells; and on this coast
Suppose him now at anchor. The city strived
God Neptune's annual feast to keep: from whence
Lysimachus our Tyrian ship espies,
His banners sable, trimm'd with rich expense;
And to him in his barge with fervor hies.
In your supposing once more put your sight
Of heavy Pericles; think this his bark:
Where what is done in action, more, if might,
Shall be discover'd; please you, sit and hark.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. On board PERICLES' ship, off Mytilene. A close pavilion on deck, with a curtain before it; PERICLES within it, reclined on a couch. A barge lying beside the Tyrian vessel.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter two Sailors, one belonging to the Tyrian vessel, the other to the barge; to them HELICANUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tyrian Sailor
SPEECH.LINE: To the Sailor of Mytilene Where is lord Helicanus?
he can resolve you.
O, here he is.
Sir, there's a barge put off from Mytilene,
And in it is Lysimachus the governor,
Who craves to come aboard. What is your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: That he have his. Call up some gentlemen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tyrian Sailor
SPEECH.LINE: Ho, gentlemen! my lord calls.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Gentleman
SPEECH.LINE: Doth your lordship call?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Gentlemen, there's some of worth would come aboard;
I pray ye, greet them fairly.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: The Gentlemen and the two Sailors descend, and go on board the barge
Enter, from thence, LYSIMACHUS and Lords; with the Gentlemen and the two Sailors

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tyrian Sailor
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
This is the man that can, in aught you would,
Resolve you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, reverend sir! the gods preserve you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: And you, sir, to outlive the age I am,
And die as I would do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: You wish me well.
Being on shore, honouring of Neptune's triumphs,
Seeing this goodly vessel ride before us,
I made to it, to know of whence you are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: First, what is your place?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am the governor of this place you lie before.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
Our vessel is of Tyre, in it the king;
A man who for this three months hath not spoken
To any one, nor taken sustenance
But to prorogue his grief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon what ground is his distemperature?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twould be too tedious to repeat;
But the main grief springs from the loss
Of a beloved daughter and a wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: May we not see him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: You may;
But bootless is your sight: he will not speak To any.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yet let me obtain my wish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Behold him.
This was a goodly person,
Till the disaster that, one mortal night,
Drove him to this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir king, all hail! the gods preserve you!
Hail, royal sir!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is in vain; he will not speak to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
We have a maid in Mytilene, I durst wager,
Would win some words of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well bethought.
She questionless with her sweet harmony
And other chosen attractions, would allure,
And make a battery through his deafen'd parts,
Which now are midway stopp'd:
She is all happy as the fairest of all,
And, with her fellow maids is now upon
The leafy shelter that abuts against
The island's side.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Whispers a Lord, who goes off in the barge of LYSIMACHUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sure, all's effectless; yet nothing we'll omit
That bears recovery's name. But, since your kindness
We have stretch'd thus far, let us beseech you
That for our gold we may provision have,
Wherein we are not destitute for want,
But weary for the staleness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, a courtesy
Which if we should deny, the most just gods
For every graff would send a caterpillar,
And so afflict our province. Yet once more
Let me entreat to know at large the cause
Of your king's sorrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sit, sir, I will recount it to you:
But, see, I am prevented.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter, from the barge, Lord, with MARINA, and a young Lady

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, here is
The lady that I sent for. Welcome, fair one!
Is't not a goodly presence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: She's a gallant lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: She's such a one, that, were I well assured
Came of a gentle kind and noble stock,
I'ld wish no better choice, and think me rarely wed.
Fair one, all goodness that consists in bounty
Expect even here, where is a kingly patient:
If that thy prosperous and artificial feat
Can draw him but to answer thee in aught,
Thy sacred physic shall receive such pay
As thy desires can wish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I will use
My utmost skill in his recovery, Provided
That none but I and my companion maid
Be suffer'd to come near him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, let us leave her;
And the gods make her prosperous!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mark'd he your music?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No, nor look'd on us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: See, she will speak to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, sir! my lord, lend ear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Hum, ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I am a maid,
My lord, that ne'er before invited eyes,
But have been gazed on like a comet: she speaks,
My lord, that, may be, hath endured a grief
Might equal yours, if both were justly weigh'd.
Though wayward fortune did malign my state,
My derivation was from ancestors
Who stood equivalent with mighty kings:
But time hath rooted out my parentage,
And to the world and awkward casualties
Bound me in servitude.
I will desist;
But there is something glows upon my cheek,
And whispers in mine ear, 'Go not till he speak.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: My fortunes--parentage--good parentage--
To equal mine!--was it not thus? what say you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I said, my lord, if you did know my parentage,
You would not do me violence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I do think so. Pray you, turn your eyes upon me.
You are like something that--What country-woman?
Here of these shores?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No, nor of any shores:
Yet I was mortally brought forth, and am
No other than I appear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I am great with woe, and shall deliver weeping.
My dearest wife was like this maid, and such a one
My daughter might have been: my queen's square brows;
Her stature to an inch; as wand-like straight;
As silver-voiced; her eyes as jewel-like
And cased as richly; in pace another Juno;
Who starves the ears she feeds, and makes them hungry,
The more she gives them speech. Where do you live?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Where I am but a stranger: from the deck
You may discern the place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Where were you bred?
And how achieved you these endowments, which
You make more rich to owe?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: If I should tell my history, it would seem
Like lies disdain'd in the reporting.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, speak:
Falseness cannot come from thee; for thou look'st
Modest as Justice, and thou seem'st a palace
For the crown'd Truth to dwell in: I will
believe thee,
And make my senses credit thy relation
To points that seem impossible; for thou look'st
Like one I loved indeed. What were thy friends?
Didst thou not say, when I did push thee back--
Which was when I perceived thee--that thou camest
From good descending?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: So indeed I did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Report thy parentage. I think thou said'st
Thou hadst been toss'd from wrong to injury,
And that thou thought'st thy griefs might equal mine,
If both were open'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Some such thing
I said, and said no more but what my thoughts
Did warrant me was likely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Tell thy story;
If thine consider'd prove the thousandth part
Of my endurance, thou art a man, and I
Have suffer'd like a girl: yet thou dost look
Like Patience gazing on kings' graves, and smiling
Extremity out of act. What were thy friends?
How lost thou them? Thy name, my most kind virgin?
Recount, I do beseech thee: come, sit by me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: My name is Marina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: O, I am mock'd,
And thou by some incensed god sent hither
To make the world to laugh at me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Patience, good sir,
Or here I'll cease.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I'll be patient.
Thou little know'st how thou dost startle me,
To call thyself Marina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The name
Was given me by one that had some power,
My father, and a king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: How! a king's daughter?
And call'd Marina?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: You said you would believe me;
But, not to be a troubler of your peace,
I will end here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: But are you flesh and blood?
Have you a working pulse? and are no fairy?
Motion! Well; speak on. Where were you born?
And wherefore call'd Marina?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Call'd Marina
For I was born at sea.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: At sea! what mother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: My mother was the daughter of a king;
Who died the minute I was born,
As my good nurse Lychorida hath oft
Deliver'd weeping.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: O, stop there a little!
This is the rarest dream that e'er dull sleep
Did mock sad fools withal: this cannot be:
My daughter's buried. Well: where were you bred?
I'll hear you more, to the bottom of your story,
And never interrupt you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: You scorn: believe me, 'twere best I did give o'er.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I will believe you by the syllable
Of what you shall deliver. Yet, give me leave:
How came you in these parts? where were you bred?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The king my father did in Tarsus leave me;
Till cruel Cleon, with his wicked wife,
Did seek to murder me: and having woo'd
A villain to attempt it, who having drawn to do't,
A crew of pirates came and rescued me;
Brought me to Mytilene. But, good sir,
Whither will you have me? Why do you weep?
It may be,
You think me an impostor: no, good faith;
I am the daughter to King Pericles,
If good King Pericles be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Ho, Helicanus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Calls my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art a grave and noble counsellor,
Most wise in general: tell me, if thou canst,
What this maid is, or what is like to be,
That thus hath made me weep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know not; but
Here is the regent, sir, of Mytilene
Speaks nobly of her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: She would never tell
Her parentage; being demanded that,
She would sit still and weep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: O Helicanus, strike me, honour'd sir;
Give me a gash, put me to present pain;
Lest this great sea of joys rushing upon me
O'erbear the shores of my mortality,
And drown me with their sweetness. O, come hither,
Thou that beget'st him that did thee beget;
Thou that wast born at sea, buried at Tarsus,
And found at sea again! O Helicanus,
Down on thy knees, thank the holy gods as loud
As thunder threatens us: this is Marina.
What was thy mother's name? tell me but that,
For truth can never be confirm'd enough,
Though doubts did ever sleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: First, sir, I pray,
What is your title?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I am Pericles of Tyre: but tell me now
My drown'd queen's name, as in the rest you said
Thou hast been godlike perfect,
The heir of kingdoms and another like
To Pericles thy father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Is it no more to be your daughter than
To say my mother's name was Thaisa?
Thaisa was my mother, who did end
The minute I began.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Now, blessing on thee! rise; thou art my child.
Give me fresh garments. Mine own, Helicanus;
She is not dead at Tarsus, as she should have been,
By savage Cleon: she shall tell thee all;
When thou shalt kneel, and justify in knowledge
She is thy very princess. Who is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, 'tis the governor of Mytilene,
Who, hearing of your melancholy state,
Did come to see you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: I embrace you.
Give me my robes. I am wild in my beholding.
O heavens bless my girl! But, hark, what music?
Tell Helicanus, my Marina, tell him
O'er, point by point, for yet he seems to doubt,
How sure you are my daughter. But, what music?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I hear none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: None!
The music of the spheres! List, my Marina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is not good to cross him; give him way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Rarest sounds! Do ye not hear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I hear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Most heavenly music!
It nips me unto listening, and thick slumber
Hangs upon mine eyes: let me rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: A pillow for his head:
So, leave him all. Well, my companion friends,
If this but answer to my just belief,
I'll well remember you.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: DIANA appears to PERICLES as in a vision

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIANA
SPEECH.LINE: My temple stands in Ephesus: hie thee thither,
And do upon mine altar sacrifice.
There, when my maiden priests are met together,
Before the people all,
Reveal how thou at sea didst lose thy wife:
To mourn thy crosses, with thy daughter's, call
And give them repetition to the life.
Or perform my bidding, or thou livest in woe;
Do it, and happy; by my silver bow!
Awake, and tell thy dream.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Celestial Dian, goddess argentine,
I will obey thee. Helicanus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: My purpose was for Tarsus, there to strike
The inhospitable Cleon; but I am
For other service first: toward Ephesus
Turn our blown sails; eftsoons I'll tell thee why.
Shall we refresh us, sir, upon your shore,
And give you gold for such provision
As our intents will need?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir,
With all my heart; and, when you come ashore,
I have another suit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: You shall prevail,
Were it to woo my daughter; for it seems
You have been noble towards her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LYSIMACHUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, lend me your arm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, my Marina.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter GOWER, before the temple of DIANA at Ephesus

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GOWER
SPEECH.LINE: Now our sands are almost run;
More a little, and then dumb.
This, my last boon, give me,
For such kindness must relieve me,
That you aptly will suppose
What pageantry, what feats, what shows,
What minstrelsy, and pretty din,
The regent made in Mytilene
To greet the king. So he thrived,
That he is promised to be wived
To fair Marina; but in no wise
Till he had done his sacrifice,
As Dian bade: whereto being bound,
The interim, pray you, all confound.
In feather'd briefness sails are fill'd,
And wishes fall out as they're will'd.
At Ephesus, the temple see,
Our king and all his company.
That he can hither come so soon,
Is by your fancy's thankful doom.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The temple of Diana at Ephesus; THAISA standing near the altar, as high priestess; a number of Virgins on each side; CERIMON and other Inhabitants of Ephesus attending.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PERICLES, with his train; LYSIMACHUS, HELICANUS, MARINA, and a Lady

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, Dian! to perform thy just command,
I here confess myself the king of Tyre;
Who, frighted from my country, did wed
At Pentapolis the fair Thaisa.
At sea in childbed died she, but brought forth
A maid-child call'd Marina; who, O goddess,
Wears yet thy silver livery. She at Tarsus
Was nursed with Cleon; who at fourteen years
He sought to murder: but her better stars
Brought her to Mytilene; 'gainst whose shore
Riding, her fortunes brought the maid aboard us,
Where, by her own most clear remembrance, she
Made known herself my daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: Voice and favour!
You are, you are--O royal Pericles!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: What means the nun? she dies! help, gentlemen!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Noble sir,
If you have told Diana's altar true,
This is your wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Reverend appearer, no;
I threw her overboard with these very arms.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Upon this coast, I warrant you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis most certain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Look to the lady; O, she's but o'erjoy'd.
Early in blustering morn this lady was
Thrown upon this shore. I oped the coffin,
Found there rich jewels; recover'd her, and placed her
Here in Diana's temple.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: May we see them?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Great sir, they shall be brought you to my house,
Whither I invite you. Look, Thaisa is recovered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: O, let me look!
If he be none of mine, my sanctity
Will to my sense bend no licentious ear,
But curb it, spite of seeing. O, my lord,
Are you not Pericles? Like him you spake,
Like him you are: did you not name a tempest,
A birth, and death?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: The voice of dead Thaisa!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: That Thaisa am I, supposed dead
And drown'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Immortal Dian!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: Now I know you better.
When we with tears parted Pentapolis,
The king my father gave you such a ring.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: This, this: no more, you gods! your present kindness
Makes my past miseries sports: you shall do well,
That on the touching of her lips I may
Melt and no more be seen. O, come, be buried
A second time within these arms.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARINA
SPEECH.LINE: My heart
Leaps to be gone into my mother's bosom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Look, who kneels here! Flesh of thy flesh, Thaisa;
Thy burden at the sea, and call'd Marina
For she was yielded there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: Blest, and mine own!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELICANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, madam, and my queen!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: I know you not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: You have heard me say, when I did fly from Tyre,
I left behind an ancient substitute:
Can you remember what I call'd the man?
I have named him oft.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas Helicanus then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Still confirmation:
Embrace him, dear Thaisa; this is he.
Now do I long to hear how you were found;
How possibly preserved; and who to thank,
Besides the gods, for this great miracle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Cerimon, my lord; this man,
Through whom the gods have shown their power; that can
From first to last resolve you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Reverend sir,
The gods can have no mortal officer
More like a god than you. Will you deliver
How this dead queen re-lives?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CERIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I will, my lord.
Beseech you, first go with me to my house,
Where shall be shown you all was found with her;
How she came placed here in the temple;
No needful thing omitted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Pure Dian, bless thee for thy vision! I
Will offer night-oblations to thee. Thaisa,
This prince, the fair-betrothed of your daughter,
Shall marry her at Pentapolis. And now,
This ornament
Makes me look dismal will I clip to form;
And what this fourteen years no razor touch'd,
To grace thy marriage-day, I'll beautify.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THAISA
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Cerimon hath letters of good credit, sir,
My father's dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PERICLES
SPEECH.LINE: Heavens make a star of him! Yet there, my queen,
We'll celebrate their nuptials, and ourselves
Will in that kingdom spend our following days:
Our son and daughter shall in Tyrus reign.
Lord Cerimon, we do our longing stay
To hear the rest untold: sir, lead's the way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GOWER
SPEECH.LINE: In Antiochus and his daughter you have heard
Of monstrous lust the due and just reward:
In Pericles, his queen and daughter, seen,
Although assail'd with fortune fierce and keen,
Virtue preserved from fell destruction's blast,
Led on by heaven, and crown'd with joy at last:
In Helicanus may you well descry
A figure of truth, of faith, of loyalty:
In reverend Cerimon there well appears
The worth that learned charity aye wears:
For wicked Cleon and his wife, when fame
Had spread their cursed deed, and honour'd name
Of Pericles, to rage the city turn,
That him and his they in his palace burn;
The gods for murder seemed so content
To punish them; although not done, but meant.
So, on your patience evermore attending,
New joy wait on you! Here our play has ending.

PLAY.TITLE: The Tragedy of Romeo and Juliet

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: PARIS, a young nobleman, kinsman to the prince.

PGROUP.GRPDESCR: heads of two houses at variance with each other.

PERSONAE.PERSONA: An old man, cousin to Capulet.
MERCUTIO, kinsman to the prince, and friend to Romeo.
BENVOLIO, nephew to Montague, and friend to Romeo.
Page to Paris; another Page; an officer.
Citizens of Verona; several Men and Women, relations to both houses; Maskers, Guards, Watchmen, and Attendants.

SPEECH.LINE: Two households, both alike in dignity,
In fair Verona, where we lay our scene,
From ancient grudge break to new mutiny,
Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean.
From forth the fatal loins of these two foes
A pair of star-cross'd lovers take their life;
Whole misadventured piteous overthrows
Do with their death bury their parents' strife.
The fearful passage of their death-mark'd love,
And the continuance of their parents' rage,
Which, but their children's end, nought could remove,
Is now the two hours' traffic of our stage;
The which if you with patient ears attend,
What here shall miss, our toil shall strive to mend.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Verona. A public place.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SAMPSON and GREGORY, of the house of Capulet, armed with swords and bucklers

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Gregory, o' my word, we'll not carry coals.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: No, for then we should be colliers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: I mean, an we be in choler, we'll draw.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, while you live, draw your neck out o' the collar.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: I strike quickly, being moved.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: But thou art not quickly moved to strike.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: A dog of the house of Montague moves me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: To move is to stir; and to be valiant is to stand:
therefore, if thou art moved, thou runn'st away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: A dog of that house shall move me to stand: I will
take the wall of any man or maid of Montague's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: That shows thee a weak slave; for the weakest goes
to the wall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: True; and therefore women, being the weaker vessels,
are ever thrust to the wall: therefore I will push
Montague's men from the wall, and thrust his maids
to the wall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: The quarrel is between our masters and us their men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis all one, I will show myself a tyrant: when I
have fought with the men, I will be cruel with the
maids, and cut off their heads.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: The heads of the maids?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, the heads of the maids, or their maidenheads;
take it in what sense thou wilt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: They must take it in sense that feel it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Me they shall feel while I am able to stand: and
'tis known I am a pretty piece of flesh.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well thou art not fish; if thou hadst, thou
hadst been poor John. Draw thy tool! here comes
two of the house of the Montagues.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: My naked weapon is out: quarrel, I will back thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: How! turn thy back and run?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Fear me not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: No, marry; I fear thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Let us take the law of our sides; let them begin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: I will frown as I pass by, and let them take it as
they list.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, as they dare. I will bite my thumb at them;
which is a disgrace to them, if they bear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABRAHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: I do bite my thumb, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABRAHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Do you bite your thumb at us, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to GREGORY Is the law of our side, if I say
ay?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir, I do not bite my thumb at you, sir, but I
bite my thumb, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: Do you quarrel, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABRAHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Quarrel sir! no, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: If you do, sir, I am for you: I serve as good a man as you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABRAHAM
SPEECH.LINE: No better.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREGORY
SPEECH.LINE: Say 'better:' here comes one of my master's kinsmen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, better, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ABRAHAM
SPEECH.LINE: You lie.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SAMPSON
SPEECH.LINE: Draw, if you be men. Gregory, remember thy swashing blow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Part, fools!
Put up your swords; you know not what you do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TYBALT
SPEECH.LINE: What, art thou drawn among these heartless hinds?
Turn thee, Benvolio, look upon thy death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I do but keep the peace: put up thy sword,
Or manage it to part these men with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TYBALT
SPEECH.LINE: What, drawn, and talk of peace! I hate the word,
As I hate hell, all Montagues, and thee:
Have at thee, coward!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter, several of both houses, who join the fray; then enter Citizens, with clubs

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Clubs, bills, and partisans! strike! beat them down!
Down with the Capulets! down with the Montagues!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CAPULET in his gown, and LADY CAPULET

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: What noise is this? Give me my long sword, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LADY CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: A crutch, a crutch! why call you for a sword?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: My sword, I say! Old Montague is come,
And flourishes his blade in spite of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou villain Capulet,--Hold me not, let me go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LADY MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt not stir a foot to seek a foe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE
SPEECH.LINE: Rebellious subjects, enemies to peace,
Profaners of this neighbour-stained steel,--
Will they not hear? What, ho! you men, you beasts,
That quench the fire of your pernicious rage
With purple fountains issuing from your veins,
On pain of torture, from those bloody hands
Throw your mistemper'd weapons to the ground,
And hear the sentence of your moved prince.
Three civil brawls, bred of an airy word,
By thee, old Capulet, and Montague,
Have thrice disturb'd the quiet of our streets,
And made Verona's ancient citizens
Cast by their grave beseeming ornaments,
To wield old partisans, in hands as old,
Canker'd with peace, to part your canker'd hate:
If ever you disturb our streets again,
Your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.
For this time, all the rest depart away:
You Capulet; shall go along with me:
And, Montague, come you this afternoon,
To know our further pleasure in this case,
To old Free-town, our common judgment-place.
Once more, on pain of death, all men depart.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but MONTAGUE, LADY MONTAGUE, and BENVOLIO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Who set this ancient quarrel new abroach?
Speak, nephew, were you by when it began?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here were the servants of your adversary,
And yours, close fighting ere I did approach:
I drew to part them: in the instant came
The fiery Tybalt, with his sword prepared,
Which, as he breathed defiance to my ears,
He swung about his head and cut the winds,
Who nothing hurt withal hiss'd him in scorn:
While we were interchanging thrusts and blows,
Came more and more and fought on part and part,
Till the prince came, who parted either part.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LADY MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: O, where is Romeo? saw you him to-day?
Right glad I am he was not at this fray.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, an hour before the worshipp'd sun
Peer'd forth the golden window of the east,
A troubled mind drave me to walk abroad;
Where, underneath the grove of sycamore
That westward rooteth from the city's side,
So early walking did I see your son:
Towards him I made, but he was ware of me
And stole into the covert of the wood:
I, measuring his affections by my own,
That most are busied when they're most alone,
Pursued my humour not pursuing his,
And gladly shunn'd who gladly fled from me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Many a morning hath he there been seen,
With tears augmenting the fresh morning dew.
Adding to clouds more clouds with his deep sighs;
But all so soon as the all-cheering sun
Should in the furthest east begin to draw
The shady curtains from Aurora's bed,
Away from the light steals home my heavy son,
And private in his chamber pens himself,
Shuts up his windows, locks far daylight out
And makes himself an artificial night:
Black and portentous must this humour prove,
Unless good counsel may the cause remove.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: My noble uncle, do you know the cause?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: I neither know it nor can learn of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Have you importuned him by any means?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: Both by myself and many other friends:
But he, his own affections' counsellor,
Is to himself--I will not say how true--
But to himself so secret and so close,
So far from sounding and discovery,
As is the bud bit with an envious worm,
Ere he can spread his sweet leaves to the air,
Or dedicate his beauty to the sun.
Could we but learn from whence his sorrows grow.
We would as willingly give cure as know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: See, where he comes: so please you, step aside;
I'll know his grievance, or be much denied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MONTAGUE
SPEECH.LINE: I would thou wert so happy by thy stay,
To hear true shrift. Come, madam, let's away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Good-morrow, cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Is the day so young?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: But new struck nine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay me! sad hours seem long.
Was that my father that went hence so fast?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: It was. What sadness lengthens Romeo's hours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Not having that, which, having, makes them short.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: In love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Out--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Of love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Out of her favour, where I am in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, that love, so gentle in his view,
Should be so tyrannous and rough in proof!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, that love, whose view is muffled still,
Should, without eyes, see pathways to his will!
Where shall we dine? O me! What fray was here?
Yet tell me not, for I have heard it all.
Here's much to do with hate, but more with love.
Why, then, O brawling love! O loving hate!
O any thing, of nothing first create!
O heavy lightness! serious vanity!
Mis-shapen chaos of well-seeming forms!
Feather of lead, bright smoke, cold fire,
sick health!
Still-waking sleep, that is not what it is!
This love feel I, that feel no love in this.
Dost thou not laugh?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: No, coz, I rather weep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Good heart, at what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: At thy good heart's oppression.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, such is love's transgression.
Griefs of mine own lie heavy in my breast,
Which thou wilt propagate, to have it prest
With more of thine: this love that thou hast shown
Doth add more grief to too much of mine own.
Love is a smoke raised with the fume of sighs;
Being purged, a fire sparkling in lovers' eyes;
Being vex'd a sea nourish'd with lovers' tears:
What is it else? a madness most discreet,
A choking gall and a preserving sweet.
Farewell, my coz.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Soft! I will go along;
An if you leave me so, you do me wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Tut, I have lost myself; I am not here;
This is not Romeo, he's some other where.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me in sadness, who is that you love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall I groan and tell thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Groan! why, no.
But sadly tell me who.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Bid a sick man in sadness make his will:
Ah, word ill urged to one that is so ill!
In sadness, cousin, I do love a woman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I aim'd so near, when I supposed you loved.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: A right good mark-man! And she's fair I love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: A right fair mark, fair coz, is soonest hit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, in that hit you miss: she'll not be hit
With Cupid's arrow; she hath Dian's wit;
And, in strong proof of chastity well arm'd,
From love's weak childish bow she lives unharm'd.
She will not stay the siege of loving terms,
Nor bide the encounter of assailing eyes,
Nor ope her lap to saint-seducing gold:
O, she is rich in beauty, only poor,
That when she dies with beauty dies her store.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Then she hath sworn that she will still live chaste?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: She hath, and in that sparing makes huge waste,
For beauty starved with her severity
Cuts beauty off from all posterity.
She is too fair, too wise, wisely too fair,
To merit bliss by making me despair:
She hath forsworn to love, and in that vow
Do I live dead that live to tell it now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Be ruled by me, forget to think of her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: O, teach me how I should forget to think.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: By giving liberty unto thine eyes;
Examine other beauties.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis the way
To call hers exquisite, in question more:
These happy masks that kiss fair ladies' brows
Being black put us in mind they hide the fair;
He that is strucken blind cannot forget
The precious treasure of his eyesight lost:
Show me a mistress that is passing fair,
What doth her beauty serve, but as a note
Where I may read who pass'd that passing fair?
Farewell: thou canst not teach me to forget.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll pay that doctrine, or else die in debt.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: But Montague is bound as well as I,
In penalty alike; and 'tis not hard, I think,
For men so old as we to keep the peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Of honourable reckoning are you both;
And pity 'tis you lived at odds so long.
But now, my lord, what say you to my suit?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: But saying o'er what I have said before:
My child is yet a stranger in the world;
She hath not seen the change of fourteen years,
Let two more summers wither in their pride,
Ere we may think her ripe to be a bride.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Younger than she are happy mothers made.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPULET
SPEECH.LINE: And too soon marr'd are those so early made.
The earth hath swallow'd all my hopes but she,
She is the hopeful lady of my earth:
But woo her, gentle Paris, get her heart,
My will to her consent is but a part;
An she agree, within her scope of choice
Lies my consent and fair according voice.
This night I hold an old accustom'd feast,
Whereto I have invited many a guest,
Such as I love; and you, among the store,
One more, most welcome, makes my number more.
At my poor house look to behold this night
Earth-treading stars that make dark heaven light:
Such comfort as do lusty young men feel
When well-apparell'd April on the heel
Of limping winter treads, even such delight
Among fresh female buds shall you this night
Inherit at my house; hear all, all see,
And like her most whose merit most shall be:
Which on more view, of many mine being one
May stand in number, though in reckoning none,
Come, go with me.
Go, sirrah, trudge about
Through fair Verona; find those persons out
Whose names are written there, and to them say,
My house and welcome on their pleasure stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Find them out whose names are written here! It is
written, that the shoemaker should meddle with his
yard, and the tailor with his last, the fisher with
his pencil, and the painter with his nets; but I am
sent to find those persons whose names are here
writ, and can never find what names the writing
person hath here writ. I must to the learned.--In good time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Tut, man, one fire burns out another's burning,
One pain is lessen'd by another's anguish;
Turn giddy, and be holp by backward turning;
One desperate grief cures with another's languish:
Take thou some new infection to thy eye,
And the rank poison of the old will die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Your plaintain-leaf is excellent for that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: For what, I pray thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: For your broken shin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, Romeo, art thou mad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Not mad, but bound more than a mad-man is;
Shut up in prison, kept without my food,
Whipp'd and tormented and--God-den, good fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: God gi' god-den. I pray, sir, can you read?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, mine own fortune in my misery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Perhaps you have learned it without book: but, I
pray, can you read any thing you see?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, if I know the letters and the language.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ye say honestly: rest you merry!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, fellow; I can read.
'Signior Martino and his wife and daughters;
County Anselme and his beauteous sisters; the lady
widow of Vitravio; Signior Placentio and his lovely
nieces; Mercutio and his brother Valentine; mine
uncle Capulet, his wife and daughters; my fair niece
Rosaline; Livia; Signior Valentio and his cousin
Tybalt, Lucio and the lively Helena.' A fair
assembly: whither should they come?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Whither?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: To supper; to our house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Whose house?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My master's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, I should have ask'd you that before.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Now I'll tell you without asking: my master is the
great rich Capulet; and if you be not of the house
of Montagues, I pray, come and crush a cup of wine.
Rest you merry!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BENVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: At this same ancient feast of Capulet's
Sups the fair Rosaline whom thou so lovest,
With all the admired beauties of Verona:
Go thither; and, with unattainted eye,
Compare her face with some that I shall show,
And I will make thee think thy swan a crow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ROMEO
SPEECH.LINE: When the devout religion of mine eye
Maintains such falsehood, then turn tears to fires;
