'Tis time to speak; my pains are quite forgot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Out, devil! I remember them too well:
Thou slewest my husband Henry in the Tower,
And Edward, my poor son, at Tewksbury.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Ere you were queen, yea, or your husband king,
I was a pack-horse in his great affairs;
A weeder-out of his proud adversaries,
A liberal rewarder of his friends:
To royalize his blood I spilt mine own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, and much better blood than his or thine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: In all which time you and your husband Grey
Were factious for the house of Lancaster;
And, Rivers, so were you. Was not your husband
In Margaret's battle at Saint Alban's slain?
Let me put in your minds, if you forget,
What you have been ere now, and what you are;
Withal, what I have been, and what I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: A murderous villain, and so still thou art.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Poor Clarence did forsake his father, Warwick;
Yea, and forswore himself,--which Jesu pardon!--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Which God revenge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: To fight on Edward's party for the crown;
And for his meed, poor lord, he is mew'd up.
I would to God my heart were flint, like Edward's;
Or Edward's soft and pitiful, like mine
I am too childish-foolish for this world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Hie thee to hell for shame, and leave the world,
Thou cacodemon! there thy kingdom is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord of Gloucester, in those busy days
Which here you urge to prove us enemies,
We follow'd then our lord, our lawful king:
So should we you, if you should be our king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: If I should be! I had rather be a pedlar:
Far be it from my heart, the thought of it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: As little joy, my lord, as you suppose
You should enjoy, were you this country's king,
As little joy may you suppose in me.
That I enjoy, being the queen thereof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: A little joy enjoys the queen thereof;
For I am she, and altogether joyless.
I can no longer hold me patient.
Hear me, you wrangling pirates, that fall out
In sharing that which you have pill'd from me!
Which of you trembles not that looks on me?
If not, that, I being queen, you bow like subjects,
Yet that, by you deposed, you quake like rebels?
O gentle villain, do not turn away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Foul wrinkled witch, what makest thou in my sight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: But repetition of what thou hast marr'd;
That will I make before I let thee go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Wert thou not banished on pain of death?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: I was; but I do find more pain in banishment
Than death can yield me here by my abode.
A husband and a son thou owest to me;
And thou a kingdom; all of you allegiance:
The sorrow that I have, by right is yours,
And all the pleasures you usurp are mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: The curse my noble father laid on thee,
When thou didst crown his warlike brows with paper
And with thy scorns drew'st rivers from his eyes,
And then, to dry them, gavest the duke a clout
Steep'd in the faultless blood of pretty Rutland--
His curses, then from bitterness of soul
Denounced against thee, are all fall'n upon thee;
And God, not we, hath plagued thy bloody deed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: So just is God, to right the innocent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'twas the foulest deed to slay that babe,
And the most merciless that e'er was heard of!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Tyrants themselves wept when it was reported.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: No man but prophesied revenge for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Northumberland, then present, wept to see it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: What were you snarling all before I came,
Ready to catch each other by the throat,
And turn you all your hatred now on me?
Did York's dread curse prevail so much with heaven?
That Henry's death, my lovely Edward's death,
Their kingdom's loss, my woful banishment,
Could all but answer for that peevish brat?
Can curses pierce the clouds and enter heaven?
Why, then, give way, dull clouds, to my quick curses!
If not by war, by surfeit die your king,
As ours by murder, to make him a king!
Edward thy son, which now is Prince of Wales,
For Edward my son, which was Prince of Wales,
Die in his youth by like untimely violence!
Thyself a queen, for me that was a queen,
Outlive thy glory, like my wretched self!
Long mayst thou live to wail thy children's loss;
And see another, as I see thee now,
Deck'd in thy rights, as thou art stall'd in mine!
Long die thy happy days before thy death;
And, after many lengthen'd hours of grief,
Die neither mother, wife, nor England's queen!
Rivers and Dorset, you were standers by,
And so wast thou, Lord Hastings, when my son
Was stabb'd with bloody daggers: God, I pray him,
That none of you may live your natural age,
But by some unlook'd accident cut off!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Have done thy charm, thou hateful wither'd hag!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: And leave out thee? stay, dog, for thou shalt hear me.
If heaven have any grievous plague in store
Exceeding those that I can wish upon thee,
O, let them keep it till thy sins be ripe,
And then hurl down their indignation
On thee, the troubler of the poor world's peace!
The worm of conscience still begnaw thy soul!
Thy friends suspect for traitors while thou livest,
And take deep traitors for thy dearest friends!
No sleep close up that deadly eye of thine,
Unless it be whilst some tormenting dream
Affrights thee with a hell of ugly devils!
Thou elvish-mark'd, abortive, rooting hog!
Thou that wast seal'd in thy nativity
The slave of nature and the son of hell!
Thou slander of thy mother's heavy womb!
Thou loathed issue of thy father's loins!
Thou rag of honour! thou detested--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Margaret.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Richard!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: I call thee not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I cry thee mercy then, for I had thought
That thou hadst call'd me all these bitter names.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so I did; but look'd for no reply.
O, let me make the period to my curse!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis done by me, and ends in 'Margaret.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Thus have you breathed your curse against yourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Poor painted queen, vain flourish of my fortune!
Why strew'st thou sugar on that bottled spider,
Whose deadly web ensnareth thee about?
Fool, fool! thou whet'st a knife to kill thyself.
The time will come when thou shalt wish for me
To help thee curse that poisonous bunchback'd toad.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: False-boding woman, end thy frantic curse,
Lest to thy harm thou move our patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Foul shame upon you! you have all moved mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Were you well served, you would be taught your duty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: To serve me well, you all should do me duty,
Teach me to be your queen, and you my subjects:
O, serve me well, and teach yourselves that duty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: Dispute not with her; she is lunatic.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, master marquess, you are malapert:
Your fire-new stamp of honour is scarce current.
O, that your young nobility could judge
What 'twere to lose it, and be miserable!
They that stand high have many blasts to shake them;
And if they fall, they dash themselves to pieces.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Good counsel, marry: learn it, learn it, marquess.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: It toucheth you, my lord, as much as me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, and much more: but I was born so high,
Our aery buildeth in the cedar's top,
And dallies with the wind and scorns the sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: And turns the sun to shade; alas! alas!
Witness my son, now in the shade of death;
Whose bright out-shining beams thy cloudy wrath
Hath in eternal darkness folded up.
Your aery buildeth in our aery's nest.
O God, that seest it, do not suffer it!
As it was won with blood, lost be it so!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Have done! for shame, if not for charity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: Urge neither charity nor shame to me:
Uncharitably with me have you dealt,
And shamefully by you my hopes are butcher'd.
My charity is outrage, life my shame
And in that shame still live my sorrow's rage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Have done, have done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: O princely Buckingham I'll kiss thy hand,
In sign of league and amity with thee:
Now fair befal thee and thy noble house!
Thy garments are not spotted with our blood,
Nor thou within the compass of my curse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Nor no one here; for curses never pass
The lips of those that breathe them in the air.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: I'll not believe but they ascend the sky,
And there awake God's gentle-sleeping peace.
O Buckingham, take heed of yonder dog!
Look, when he fawns, he bites; and when he bites,
His venom tooth will rankle to the death:
Have not to do with him, beware of him;
Sin, death, and hell have set their marks on him,
And all their ministers attend on him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: What doth she say, my Lord of Buckingham?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing that I respect, my gracious lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN MARGARET
SPEECH.LINE: What, dost thou scorn me for my gentle counsel?
And soothe the devil that I warn thee from?
O, but remember this another day,
When he shall split thy very heart with sorrow,
And say poor Margaret was a prophetess!
Live each of you the subjects to his hate,
And he to yours, and all of you to God's!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: My hair doth stand on end to hear her curses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: And so doth mine: I muse why she's at liberty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot blame her: by God's holy mother,
She hath had too much wrong; and I repent
My part thereof that I have done to her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: I never did her any, to my knowledge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: But you have all the vantage of her wrong.
I was too hot to do somebody good,
That is too cold in thinking of it now.
Marry, as for Clarence, he is well repaid,
He is frank'd up to fatting for his pains
God pardon them that are the cause of it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: A virtuous and a Christian-like conclusion,
To pray for them that have done scathe to us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: So do I ever:
being well-advised.
For had I cursed now, I had cursed myself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, his majesty doth call for you,
And for your grace; and you, my noble lords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Catesby, we come. Lords, will you go with us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, we will attend your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I do the wrong, and first begin to brawl.
The secret mischiefs that I set abroach
I lay unto the grievous charge of others.
Clarence, whom I, indeed, have laid in darkness,
I do beweep to many simple gulls
Namely, to Hastings, Derby, Buckingham;
And say it is the queen and her allies
That stir the king against the duke my brother.
Now, they believe it; and withal whet me
To be revenged on Rivers, Vaughan, Grey:
But then I sigh; and, with a piece of scripture,
Tell them that God bids us do good for evil:
And thus I clothe my naked villany
With old odd ends stolen out of holy writ;
And seem a saint, when most I play the devil.
But, soft! here come my executioners.
How now, my hardy, stout resolved mates!
Are you now going to dispatch this deed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: We are, my lord; and come to have the warrant
That we may be admitted where he is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Well thought upon; I have it here about me.
When you have done, repair to Crosby Place.
But, sirs, be sudden in the execution,
Withal obdurate, do not hear him plead;
For Clarence is well-spoken, and perhaps
May move your hearts to pity if you mark him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Tush!
Fear not, my lord, we will not stand to prate;
Talkers are no good doers: be assured
We come to use our hands and not our tongues.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Your eyes drop millstones, when fools' eyes drop tears:
I like you, lads; about your business straight;
Go, go, dispatch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: We will, my noble lord.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. London. The Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: Why looks your grace so heavily today?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O, I have pass'd a miserable night,
So full of ugly sights, of ghastly dreams,
That, as I am a Christian faithful man,
I would not spend another such a night,
Though 'twere to buy a world of happy days,
So full of dismal terror was the time!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: What was your dream? I long to hear you tell it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Methoughts that I had broken from the Tower,
And was embark'd to cross to Burgundy;
And, in my company, my brother Gloucester;
Who from my cabin tempted me to walk
Upon the hatches: thence we looked toward England,
And cited up a thousand fearful times,
During the wars of York and Lancaster
That had befall'n us. As we paced along
Upon the giddy footing of the hatches,
Methought that Gloucester stumbled; and, in falling,
Struck me, that thought to stay him, overboard,
Into the tumbling billows of the main.
Lord, Lord! methought, what pain it was to drown!
What dreadful noise of waters in mine ears!
What ugly sights of death within mine eyes!
Methought I saw a thousand fearful wrecks;
Ten thousand men that fishes gnaw'd upon;
Wedges of gold, great anchors, heaps of pearl,
Inestimable stones, unvalued jewels,
All scatter'd in the bottom of the sea:
Some lay in dead men's skulls; and, in those holes
Where eyes did once inhabit, there were crept,
As 'twere in scorn of eyes, reflecting gems,
Which woo'd the slimy bottom of the deep,
And mock'd the dead bones that lay scatter'd by.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: Had you such leisure in the time of death
To gaze upon the secrets of the deep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Methought I had; and often did I strive
To yield the ghost: but still the envious flood
Kept in my soul, and would not let it forth
To seek the empty, vast and wandering air;
But smother'd it within my panting bulk,
Which almost burst to belch it in the sea.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: Awaked you not with this sore agony?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O, no, my dream was lengthen'd after life;
O, then began the tempest to my soul,
Who pass'd, methought, the melancholy flood,
With that grim ferryman which poets write of,
Unto the kingdom of perpetual night.
The first that there did greet my stranger soul,
Was my great father-in-law, renowned Warwick;
Who cried aloud, 'What scourge for perjury
Can this dark monarchy afford false Clarence?'
And so he vanish'd: then came wandering by
A shadow like an angel, with bright hair
Dabbled in blood; and he squeak'd out aloud,
'Clarence is come; false, fleeting, perjured Clarence,
That stabb'd me in the field by Tewksbury;
Seize on him, Furies, take him to your torments!'
With that, methoughts, a legion of foul fiends
Environ'd me about, and howled in mine ears
Such hideous cries, that with the very noise
I trembling waked, and for a season after
Could not believe but that I was in hell,
Such terrible impression made the dream.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: No marvel, my lord, though it affrighted you;
I promise, I am afraid to hear you tell it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O Brakenbury, I have done those things,
Which now bear evidence against my soul,
For Edward's sake; and see how he requites me!
O God! if my deep prayers cannot appease thee,
But thou wilt be avenged on my misdeeds,
Yet execute thy wrath in me alone,
O, spare my guiltless wife and my poor children!
I pray thee, gentle keeper, stay by me;
My soul is heavy, and I fain would sleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: I will, my lord: God give your grace good rest!
Sorrow breaks seasons and reposing hours,
Makes the night morning, and the noon-tide night.
Princes have but their tides for their glories,
An outward honour for an inward toil;
And, for unfelt imagination,
They often feel a world of restless cares:
So that, betwixt their tides and low names,
There's nothing differs but the outward fame.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Ho! who's here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: In God's name what are you, and how came you hither?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: I would speak with Clarence, and I came hither on my legs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, are you so brief?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: O sir, it is better to be brief than tedious. Show
him our commission; talk no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BRAKENBURY
SPEECH.LINE: I am, in this, commanded to deliver
The noble Duke of Clarence to your hands:
I will not reason what is meant hereby,
Because I will be guiltless of the meaning.
Here are the keys, there sits the duke asleep:
I'll to the king; and signify to him
That thus I have resign'd my charge to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Do so, it is a point of wisdom: fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall we stab him as he sleeps?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: No; then he will say 'twas done cowardly, when he wakes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: When he wakes! why, fool, he shall never wake till
the judgment-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then he will say we stabbed him sleeping.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: The urging of that word 'judgment' hath bred a kind
of remorse in me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: What, art thou afraid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Not to kill him, having a warrant for it; but to be
damned for killing him, from which no warrant can defend us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: I thought thou hadst been resolute.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: So I am, to let him live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Back to the Duke of Gloucester, tell him so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, stay a while: I hope my holy humour
will change; 'twas wont to hold me but while one
would tell twenty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: How dost thou feel thyself now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, some certain dregs of conscience are yet
within me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Remember our reward, when the deed is done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds, he dies: I had forgot the reward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Where is thy conscience now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: In the Duke of Gloucester's purse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: So when he opens his purse to give us our reward,
thy conscience flies out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Let it go; there's few or none will entertain it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: How if it come to thee again?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: I'll not meddle with it: it is a dangerous thing: it
makes a man a coward: a man cannot steal, but it
accuseth him; he cannot swear, but it cheques him;
he cannot lie with his neighbour's wife, but it
detects him: 'tis a blushing shamefast spirit that
mutinies in a man's bosom; it fills one full of
obstacles: it made me once restore a purse of gold
that I found; it beggars any man that keeps it: it
is turned out of all towns and cities for a
dangerous thing; and every man that means to live
well endeavours to trust to himself and to live
without it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds, it is even now at my elbow, persuading me
not to kill the duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Take the devil in thy mind, and relieve him not: he
would insinuate with thee but to make thee sigh.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Tut, I am strong-framed, he cannot prevail with me,
I warrant thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Spoke like a tail fellow that respects his
reputation. Come, shall we to this gear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Take him over the costard with the hilts of thy
sword, and then we will chop him in the malmsey-butt
in the next room.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: O excellent devise! make a sop of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Hark! he stirs: shall I strike?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: No, first let's reason with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Where art thou, keeper? give me a cup of wine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second murderer
SPEECH.LINE: You shall have wine enough, my lord, anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: In God's name, what art thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: A man, as you are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: But not, as I am, royal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Nor you, as we are, loyal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Thy voice is thunder, but thy looks are humble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: My voice is now the king's, my looks mine own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: How darkly and how deadly dost thou speak!
Your eyes do menace me: why look you pale?
Who sent you hither? Wherefore do you come?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both
SPEECH.LINE: To, to, to--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: To murder me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: You scarcely have the hearts to tell me so,
And therefore cannot have the hearts to do it.
Wherein, my friends, have I offended you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Offended us you have not, but the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: I shall be reconciled to him again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Never, my lord; therefore prepare to die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Are you call'd forth from out a world of men
To slay the innocent? What is my offence?
Where are the evidence that do accuse me?
What lawful quest have given their verdict up
Unto the frowning judge? or who pronounced
The bitter sentence of poor Clarence' death?
Before I be convict by course of law,
To threaten me with death is most unlawful.
I charge you, as you hope to have redemption
By Christ's dear blood shed for our grievous sins,
That you depart and lay no hands on me
The deed you undertake is damnable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: What we will do, we do upon command.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: And he that hath commanded is the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Erroneous vassal! the great King of kings
Hath in the tables of his law commanded
That thou shalt do no murder: and wilt thou, then,
Spurn at his edict and fulfil a man's?
Take heed; for he holds vengeance in his hands,
To hurl upon their heads that break his law.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: And that same vengeance doth he hurl on thee,
For false forswearing and for murder too:
Thou didst receive the holy sacrament,
To fight in quarrel of the house of Lancaster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: And, like a traitor to the name of God,
Didst break that vow; and with thy treacherous blade
Unrip'dst the bowels of thy sovereign's son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Whom thou wert sworn to cherish and defend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: How canst thou urge God's dreadful law to us,
When thou hast broke it in so dear degree?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Alas! for whose sake did I that ill deed?
For Edward, for my brother, for his sake: Why, sirs,
He sends ye not to murder me for this
For in this sin he is as deep as I.
If God will be revenged for this deed.
O, know you yet, he doth it publicly,
Take not the quarrel from his powerful arm;
He needs no indirect nor lawless course
To cut off those that have offended him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Who made thee, then, a bloody minister,
When gallant-springing brave Plantagenet,
That princely novice, was struck dead by thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: My brother's love, the devil, and my rage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Thy brother's love, our duty, and thy fault,
Provoke us hither now to slaughter thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Oh, if you love my brother, hate not me;
I am his brother, and I love him well.
If you be hired for meed, go back again,
And I will send you to my brother Gloucester,
Who shall reward you better for my life
Than Edward will for tidings of my death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: You are deceived, your brother Gloucester hates you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O, no, he loves me, and he holds me dear:
Go you to him from me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, so we will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Tell him, when that our princely father York
Bless'd his three sons with his victorious arm,
And charged us from his soul to love each other,
He little thought of this divided friendship:
Bid Gloucester think of this, and he will weep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, millstones; as be lesson'd us to weep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: O, do not slander him, for he is kind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Right,
As snow in harvest. Thou deceivest thyself:
'Tis he that sent us hither now to slaughter thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: It cannot be; for when I parted with him,
He hugg'd me in his arms, and swore, with sobs,
That he would labour my delivery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so he doth, now he delivers thee
From this world's thraldom to the joys of heaven.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Make peace with God, for you must die, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Hast thou that holy feeling in thy soul,
To counsel me to make my peace with God,
And art thou yet to thy own soul so blind,
That thou wilt war with God by murdering me?
Ah, sirs, consider, he that set you on
To do this deed will hate you for the deed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: What shall we do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Relent, and save your souls.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Relent! 'tis cowardly and womanish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CLARENCE
SPEECH.LINE: Not to relent is beastly, savage, devilish.
Which of you, if you were a prince's son,
Being pent from liberty, as I am now,
if two such murderers as yourselves came to you,
Would not entreat for life?
My friend, I spy some pity in thy looks:
O, if thine eye be not a flatterer,
Come thou on my side, and entreat for me,
As you would beg, were you in my distress
A begging prince what beggar pities not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Look behind you, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: Take that, and that: if all this will not do,
I'll drown you in the malmsey-butt within.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: A bloody deed, and desperately dispatch'd!
How fain, like Pilate, would I wash my hands
Of this most grievous guilty murder done!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what mean'st thou, that thou help'st me not?
By heavens, the duke shall know how slack thou art!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: I would he knew that I had saved his brother!
Take thou the fee, and tell him what I say;
For I repent me that the duke is slain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Murderer
SPEECH.LINE: So do not I: go, coward as thou art.
Now must I hide his body in some hole,
Until the duke take order for his burial:
And when I have my meed, I must away;
For this will out, and here I must not stay.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. London. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Enter KING EDWARD IV sick, QUEEN ELIZABETH, DORSET, RIVERS, HASTINGS, BUCKINGHAM, GREY, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so: now have I done a good day's work:
You peers, continue this united league:
I every day expect an embassage
From my Redeemer to redeem me hence;
And now in peace my soul shall part to heaven,
Since I have set my friends at peace on earth.
Rivers and Hastings, take each other's hand;
Dissemble not your hatred, swear your love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, my heart is purged from grudging hate:
And with my hand I seal my true heart's love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: So thrive I, as I truly swear the like!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Take heed you dally not before your king;
Lest he that is the supreme King of kings
Confound your hidden falsehood, and award
Either of you to be the other's end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: So prosper I, as I swear perfect love!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: And I, as I love Hastings with my heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, yourself are not exempt in this,
Nor your son Dorset, Buckingham, nor you;
You have been factious one against the other,
Wife, love Lord Hastings, let him kiss your hand;
And what you do, do it unfeignedly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Here, Hastings; I will never more remember
Our former hatred, so thrive I and mine!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Dorset, embrace him; Hastings, love lord marquess.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: This interchange of love, I here protest,
Upon my part shall be unviolable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: And so swear I, my lord

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Now, princely Buckingham, seal thou this league
With thy embracements to my wife's allies,
And make me happy in your unity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Whenever Buckingham doth turn his hate
On you or yours,
but with all duteous love
Doth cherish you and yours, God punish me
With hate in those where I expect most love!
When I have most need to employ a friend,
And most assured that he is a friend
Deep, hollow, treacherous, and full of guile,
Be he unto me! this do I beg of God,
When I am cold in zeal to yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: A pleasing cordial, princely Buckingham,
is this thy vow unto my sickly heart.
There wanteth now our brother Gloucester here,
To make the perfect period of this peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: And, in good time, here comes the noble duke.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow to my sovereign king and queen:
And, princely peers, a happy time of day!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Happy, indeed, as we have spent the day.
Brother, we done deeds of charity;
Made peace enmity, fair love of hate,
Between these swelling wrong-incensed peers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: A blessed labour, my most sovereign liege:
Amongst this princely heap, if any here,
By false intelligence, or wrong surmise,
Hold me a foe;
If I unwittingly, or in my rage,
Have aught committed that is hardly borne
By any in this presence, I desire
To reconcile me to his friendly peace:
'Tis death to me to be at enmity;
I hate it, and desire all good men's love.
First, madam, I entreat true peace of you,
Which I will purchase with my duteous service;
Of you, my noble cousin Buckingham,
If ever any grudge were lodged between us;
Of you, Lord Rivers, and, Lord Grey, of you;
That without desert have frown'd on me;
Dukes, earls, lords, gentlemen; indeed, of all.
I do not know that Englishman alive
With whom my soul is any jot at odds
More than the infant that is born to-night
I thank my God for my humility.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: A holy day shall this be kept hereafter:
I would to God all strifes were well compounded.
My sovereign liege, I do beseech your majesty
To take our brother Clarence to your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Why, madam, have I offer'd love for this
To be so bouted in this royal presence?
Who knows not that the noble duke is dead?
You do him injury to scorn his corse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Who knows not he is dead! who knows he is?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: All seeing heaven, what a world is this!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Look I so pale, Lord Dorset, as the rest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord; and no one in this presence
But his red colour hath forsook his cheeks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Is Clarence dead? the order was reversed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: But he, poor soul, by your first order died,
And that a winged Mercury did bear:
Some tardy cripple bore the countermand,
That came too lag to see him buried.
God grant that some, less noble and less loyal,
Nearer in bloody thoughts, but not in blood,
Deserve not worse than wretched Clarence did,
And yet go current from suspicion!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: A boon, my sovereign, for my service done!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, peace: my soul is full of sorrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: I will not rise, unless your highness grant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Then speak at once what is it thou demand'st.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: The forfeit, sovereign, of my servant's life;
Who slew to-day a righteous gentleman
Lately attendant on the Duke of Norfolk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING EDWARD IV
SPEECH.LINE: Have a tongue to doom my brother's death,
And shall the same give pardon to a slave?
My brother slew no man; his fault was thought,
And yet his punishment was cruel death.
Who sued to me for him? who, in my rage,
Kneel'd at my feet, and bade me be advised
Who spake of brotherhood? who spake of love?
Who told me how the poor soul did forsake
The mighty Warwick, and did fight for me?
Who told me, in the field by Tewksbury
When Oxford had me down, he rescued me,
And said, 'Dear brother, live, and be a king'?
Who told me, when we both lay in the field
Frozen almost to death, how he did lap me
Even in his own garments, and gave himself,
All thin and naked, to the numb cold night?
All this from my remembrance brutish wrath
Sinfully pluck'd, and not a man of you
Had so much grace to put it in my mind.
But when your carters or your waiting-vassals
Have done a drunken slaughter, and defaced
The precious image of our dear Redeemer,
You straight are on your knees for pardon, pardon;
And I unjustly too, must grant it you
But for my brother not a man would speak,
Nor I, ungracious, speak unto myself
For him, poor soul. The proudest of you all
Have been beholding to him in his life;
Yet none of you would once plead for his life.
O God, I fear thy justice will take hold
On me, and you, and mine, and yours for this!
Come, Hastings, help me to my closet.
Oh, poor Clarence!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt some with KING EDWARD IV and QUEEN MARGARET

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: This is the fruit of rashness! Mark'd you not
How that the guilty kindred of the queen
Look'd pale when they did hear of Clarence' death?
O, they did urge it still unto the king!
God will revenge it. But come, let us in,
To comfort Edward with our company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: We wait upon your grace.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the DUCHESS OF YORK, with the two children of CLARENCE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me, good grandam, is our father dead?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: No, boy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Why do you wring your hands, and beat your breast,
And cry 'O Clarence, my unhappy son!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Girl
SPEECH.LINE: Why do you look on us, and shake your head,
And call us wretches, orphans, castaways
If that our noble father be alive?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: My pretty cousins, you mistake me much;
I do lament the sickness of the king.
As loath to lose him, not your father's death;
It were lost sorrow to wail one that's lost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Then, grandam, you conclude that he is dead.
The king my uncle is to blame for this:
God will revenge it; whom I will importune
With daily prayers all to that effect.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Girl
SPEECH.LINE: And so will I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, children, peace! the king doth love you well:
Incapable and shallow innocents,
You cannot guess who caused your father's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Grandam, we can; for my good uncle Gloucester
Told me, the king, provoked by the queen,
Devised impeachments to imprison him :
And when my uncle told me so, he wept,
And hugg'd me in his arm, and kindly kiss'd my cheek;
Bade me rely on him as on my father,
And he would love me dearly as his child.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Oh, that deceit should steal such gentle shapes,
And with a virtuous vizard hide foul guile!
He is my son; yea, and therein my shame;
Yet from my dugs he drew not this deceit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Think you my uncle did dissemble, grandam?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, boy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot think it. Hark! what noise is this?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter QUEEN ELIZABETH, with her hair about her ears; RIVERS, and DORSET after her

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Oh, who shall hinder me to wail and weep,
To chide my fortune, and torment myself?
I'll join with black despair against my soul,
And to myself become an enemy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What means this scene of rude impatience?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: To make an act of tragic violence:
Edward, my lord, your son, our king, is dead.
Why grow the branches now the root is wither'd?
Why wither not the leaves the sap being gone?
If you will live, lament; if die, be brief,
That our swift-winged souls may catch the king's;
Or, like obedient subjects, follow him
To his new kingdom of perpetual rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, so much interest have I in thy sorrow
As I had title in thy noble husband!
I have bewept a worthy husband's death,
And lived by looking on his images:
But now two mirrors of his princely semblance
Are crack'd in pieces by malignant death,
And I for comfort have but one false glass,
Which grieves me when I see my shame in him.
Thou art a widow; yet thou art a mother,
And hast the comfort of thy children left thee:
But death hath snatch'd my husband from mine arms,
And pluck'd two crutches from my feeble limbs,
Edward and Clarence. O, what cause have I,
Thine being but a moiety of my grief,
To overgo thy plaints and drown thy cries!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: Good aunt, you wept not for our father's death;
How can we aid you with our kindred tears?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Girl
SPEECH.LINE: Our fatherless distress was left unmoan'd;
Your widow-dolour likewise be unwept!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Give me no help in lamentation;
I am not barren to bring forth complaints
All springs reduce their currents to mine eyes,
That I, being govern'd by the watery moon,
May send forth plenteous tears to drown the world!
Oh for my husband, for my dear lord Edward!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Children
SPEECH.LINE: Oh for our father, for our dear lord Clarence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Alas for both, both mine, Edward and Clarence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: What stay had I but Edward? and he's gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Children
SPEECH.LINE: What stay had we but Clarence? and he's gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What stays had I but they? and they are gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Was never widow had so dear a loss!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Children
SPEECH.LINE: Were never orphans had so dear a loss!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Was never mother had so dear a loss!
Alas, I am the mother of these moans!
Their woes are parcell'd, mine are general.
She for an Edward weeps, and so do I;
I for a Clarence weep, so doth not she:
These babes for Clarence weep and so do I;
I for an Edward weep, so do not they:
Alas, you three, on me, threefold distress'd,
Pour all your tears! I am your sorrow's nurse,
And I will pamper it with lamentations.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DORSET
SPEECH.LINE: Comfort, dear mother: God is much displeased
That you take with unthankfulness, his doing:
In common worldly things, 'tis call'd ungrateful,
With dull unwilligness to repay a debt
Which with a bounteous hand was kindly lent;
Much more to be thus opposite with heaven,
For it requires the royal debt it lent you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, bethink you, like a careful mother,
Of the young prince your son: send straight for him
Let him be crown'd; in him your comfort lives:
Drown desperate sorrow in dead Edward's grave,
And plant your joys in living Edward's throne.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter GLOUCESTER, BUCKINGHAM, DERBY, HASTINGS, and RATCLIFF

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, have comfort: all of us have cause
To wail the dimming of our shining star;
But none can cure their harms by wailing them.
Madam, my mother, I do cry you mercy;
I did not see your grace: humbly on my knee
I crave your blessing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: God bless thee; and put meekness in thy mind,
Love, charity, obedience, and true duty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Amen; and make me die a good old man!
That is the butt-end of a mother's blessing:
I marvel why her grace did leave it out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: You cloudy princes and heart-sorrowing peers,
That bear this mutual heavy load of moan,
Now cheer each other in each other's love
Though we have spent our harvest of this king,
We are to reap the harvest of his son.
The broken rancour of your high-swoln hearts,
But lately splinter'd, knit, and join'd together,
Must gently be preserved, cherish'd, and kept:
Me seemeth good, that, with some little train,
Forthwith from Ludlow the young prince be fetch'd
Hither to London, to be crown'd our king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Why with some little train, my Lord of Buckingham?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, my lord, lest, by a multitude,
The new-heal'd wound of malice should break out,
Which would be so much the more dangerous
By how much the estate is green and yet ungovern'd:
Where every horse bears his commanding rein,
And may direct his course as please himself,
As well the fear of harm, as harm apparent,
In my opinion, ought to be prevented.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I hope the king made peace with all of us
And the compact is firm and true in me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: And so in me; and so, I think, in all:
Yet, since it is but green, it should be put
To no apparent likelihood of breach,
Which haply by much company might be urged:
Therefore I say with noble Buckingham,
That it is meet so few should fetch the prince.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: And so say I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Then be it so; and go we to determine
Who they shall be that straight shall post to Ludlow.
Madam, and you, my mother, will you go
To give your censures in this weighty business?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: With all our harts.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but BUCKINGHAM and GLOUCESTER

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, whoever journeys to the Prince,
For God's sake, let not us two be behind;
For, by the way, I'll sort occasion,
As index to the story we late talk'd of,
To part the queen's proud kindred from the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My other self, my counsel's consistory,
My oracle, my prophet! My dear cousin,
I, like a child, will go by thy direction.
Towards Ludlow then, for we'll not stay behind.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. London. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Neighbour, well met: whither away so fast?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: I promise you, I scarcely know myself:
Hear you the news abroad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that the king is dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Bad news, by'r lady; seldom comes the better:
I fear, I fear 'twill prove a troublous world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Neighbours, God speed!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Give you good morrow, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Doth this news hold of good King Edward's death?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, it is too true; God help the while!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Then, masters, look to see a troublous world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: No, no; by God's good grace his son shall reign.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Woe to the land that's govern'd by a child!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: In him there is a hope of government,
That in his nonage council under him,
And in his full and ripen'd years himself,
No doubt, shall then and till then govern well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: So stood the state when Henry the Sixth
Was crown'd in Paris but at nine months old.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Stood the state so? No, no, good friends, God wot;
For then this land was famously enrich'd
With politic grave counsel; then the king
Had virtuous uncles to protect his grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so hath this, both by the father and mother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Better it were they all came by the father,
Or by the father there were none at all;
For emulation now, who shall be nearest,
Will touch us all too near, if God prevent not.
O, full of danger is the Duke of Gloucester!
And the queen's sons and brothers haught and proud:
And were they to be ruled, and not to rule,
This sickly land might solace as before.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, we fear the worst; all shall be well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: When clouds appear, wise men put on their cloaks;
When great leaves fall, the winter is at hand;
When the sun sets, who doth not look for night?
Untimely storms make men expect a dearth.
All may be well; but, if God sort it so,
'Tis more than we deserve, or I expect.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, the souls of men are full of dread:
Ye cannot reason almost with a man
That looks not heavily and full of fear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Before the times of change, still is it so:
By a divine instinct men's minds mistrust
Ensuing dangers; as by proof, we see
The waters swell before a boisterous storm.
But leave it all to God. whither away?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, we were sent for to the justices.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Citizen
SPEECH.LINE: And so was I: I'll bear you company.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. London. The palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the ARCHBISHOP OF YORK, young YORK, QUEEN ELIZABETH, and the DUCHESS OF YORK

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Last night, I hear, they lay at Northampton;
At Stony-Stratford will they be to-night:
To-morrow, or next day, they will be here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I long with all my heart to see the prince:
I hope he is much grown since last I saw him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: But I hear, no; they say my son of York
Hath almost overta'en him in his growth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, mother; but I would not have it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, my young cousin, it is good to grow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Grandam, one night, as we did sit at supper,
My uncle Rivers talk'd how I did grow
More than my brother: 'Ay,' quoth my uncle
Gloucester,
'Small herbs have grace, great weeds do grow apace:'
And since, methinks, I would not grow so fast,
Because sweet flowers are slow and weeds make haste.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Good faith, good faith, the saying did not hold
In him that did object the same to thee;
He was the wretched'st thing when he was young,
So long a-growing and so leisurely,
That, if this rule were true, he should be gracious.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Why, madam, so, no doubt, he is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I hope he is; but yet let mothers doubt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my troth, if I had been remember'd,
I could have given my uncle's grace a flout,
To touch his growth nearer than he touch'd mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: How, my pretty York? I pray thee, let me hear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, they say my uncle grew so fast
That he could gnaw a crust at two hours old
'Twas full two years ere I could get a tooth.
Grandam, this would have been a biting jest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, pretty York, who told thee this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Grandam, his nurse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: His nurse! why, she was dead ere thou wert born.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: If 'twere not she, I cannot tell who told me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: A parlous boy: go to, you are too shrewd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Good madam, be not angry with the child.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Pitchers have ears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes a messenger. What news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Such news, my lord, as grieves me to unfold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: How fares the prince?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Well, madam, and in health.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What is thy news then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Rivers and Lord Grey are sent to Pomfret,
With them Sir Thomas Vaughan, prisoners.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Who hath committed them?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: The mighty dukes
Gloucester and Buckingham.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: For what offence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: The sum of all I can, I have disclosed;
Why or for what these nobles were committed
Is all unknown to me, my gracious lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Ay me, I see the downfall of our house!
The tiger now hath seized the gentle hind;
Insulting tyranny begins to jet
Upon the innocent and aweless throne:
Welcome, destruction, death, and massacre!
I see, as in a map, the end of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Accursed and unquiet wrangling days,
How many of you have mine eyes beheld!
My husband lost his life to get the crown;
And often up and down my sons were toss'd,
For me to joy and weep their gain and loss:
And being seated, and domestic broils
Clean over-blown, themselves, the conquerors.
Make war upon themselves; blood against blood,
Self against self: O, preposterous
And frantic outrage, end thy damned spleen;
Or let me die, to look on death no more!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, my boy; we will to sanctuary.
Madam, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUCHESS OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I'll go along with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUEEN ELIZABETH
SPEECH.LINE: You have no cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARCHBISHOP OF YORK
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious lady, go;
And thither bear your treasure and your goods.
For my part, I'll resign unto your grace
The seal I keep: and so betide to me
As well I tender you and all of yours!
Come, I'll conduct you to the sanctuary.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. London. A street.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: The trumpets sound. Enter the young PRINCE EDWARD, GLOUCESTER, BUCKINGHAM, CARDINAL, CATESBY, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, sweet prince, to London, to your chamber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, dear cousin, my thoughts' sovereign
The weary way hath made you melancholy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: No, uncle; but our crosses on the way
Have made it tedious, wearisome, and heavy
I want more uncles here to welcome me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet prince, the untainted virtue of your years
Hath not yet dived into the world's deceit
Nor more can you distinguish of a man
Than of his outward show; which, God he knows,
Seldom or never jumpeth with the heart.
Those uncles which you want were dangerous;
Your grace attended to their sugar'd words,
But look'd not on the poison of their hearts :
God keep you from them, and from such false friends!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: God keep me from false friends! but they were none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, the mayor of London comes to greet you.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the Lord Mayor and his train

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lord Mayor
SPEECH.LINE: God bless your grace with health and happy days!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, good my lord; and thank you all.
I thought my mother, and my brother York,
Would long ere this have met us on the way
Fie, what a slug is Hastings, that he comes not
To tell us whether they will come or no!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: And, in good time, here comes the sweating lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, my lord: what, will our mother come?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: On what occasion, God he knows, not I,
The queen your mother, and your brother York,
Have taken sanctuary: the tender prince
Would fain have come with me to meet your grace,
But by his mother was perforce withheld.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, what an indirect and peevish course
Is this of hers! Lord cardinal, will your grace
Persuade the queen to send the Duke of York
Unto his princely brother presently?
If she deny, Lord Hastings, go with him,
And from her jealous arms pluck him perforce.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord of Buckingham, if my weak oratory
Can from his mother win the Duke of York,
Anon expect him here; but if she be obdurate
To mild entreaties, God in heaven forbid
We should infringe the holy privilege
Of blessed sanctuary! not for all this land
Would I be guilty of so deep a sin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: You are too senseless--obstinate, my lord,
Too ceremonious and traditional
Weigh it but with the grossness of this age,
You break not sanctuary in seizing him.
The benefit thereof is always granted
To those whose dealings have deserved the place,
And those who have the wit to claim the place:
This prince hath neither claim'd it nor deserved it;
And therefore, in mine opinion, cannot have it:
Then, taking him from thence that is not there,
You break no privilege nor charter there.
Oft have I heard of sanctuary men;
But sanctuary children ne'er till now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CARDINAL
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, you shall o'er-rule my mind for once.
Come on, Lord Hastings, will you go with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I go, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Good lords, make all the speedy haste you may.
Say, uncle Gloucester, if our brother come,
Where shall we sojourn till our coronation?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Where it seems best unto your royal self.
If I may counsel you, some day or two
Your highness shall repose you at the Tower:
Then where you please, and shall be thought most fit
For your best health and recreation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I do not like the Tower, of any place.
Did Julius Caesar build that place, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: He did, my gracious lord, begin that place;
Which, since, succeeding ages have re-edified.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Is it upon record, or else reported
Successively from age to age, he built it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Upon record, my gracious lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: But say, my lord, it were not register'd,
Methinks the truth should live from age to age,
As 'twere retail'd to all posterity,
Even to the general all-ending day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Aside So wise so young, they say, do never
live long.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: What say you, uncle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I say, without characters, fame lives long.
Thus, like the formal vice, Iniquity,
I moralize two meanings in one word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: That Julius Caesar was a famous man;
With what his valour did enrich his wit,
His wit set down to make his valour live
Death makes no conquest of this conqueror;
For now he lives in fame, though not in life.
I'll tell you what, my cousin Buckingham,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: What, my gracious lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: An if I live until I be a man,
I'll win our ancient right in France again,
Or die a soldier, as I lived a king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Short summers lightly have a forward spring.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter young YORK, HASTINGS, and the CARDINAL

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Now, in good time, here comes the Duke of York.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Richard of York! how fares our loving brother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Well, my dread lord; so must I call you now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, brother, to our grief, as it is yours:
Too late he died that might have kept that title,
Which by his death hath lost much majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: How fares our cousin, noble Lord of York?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, gentle uncle. O, my lord,
You said that idle weeds are fast in growth
The prince my brother hath outgrown me far.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: He hath, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: And therefore is he idle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: O, my fair cousin, I must not say so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Then is he more beholding to you than I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: He may command me as my sovereign;
But you have power in me as in a kinsman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, uncle, give me this dagger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My dagger, little cousin? with all my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: A beggar, brother?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Of my kind uncle, that I know will give;
And being but a toy, which is no grief to give.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: A greater gift than that I'll give my cousin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: A greater gift! O, that's the sword to it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: A gentle cousin, were it light enough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: O, then, I see, you will part but with light gifts;
In weightier things you'll say a beggar nay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: It is too heavy for your grace to wear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I weigh it lightly, were it heavier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: What, would you have my weapon, little lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I would, that I might thank you as you call me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: How?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Little.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord of York will still be cross in talk:
Uncle, your grace knows how to bear with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: You mean, to bear me, not to bear with me:
Uncle, my brother mocks both you and me;
Because that I am little, like an ape,
He thinks that you should bear me on your shoulders.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: With what a sharp-provided wit he reasons!
To mitigate the scorn he gives his uncle,
He prettily and aptly taunts himself:
So cunning and so young is wonderful.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, will't please you pass along?
Myself and my good cousin Buckingham
Will to your mother, to entreat of her
To meet you at the Tower and welcome you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: What, will you go unto the Tower, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: My lord protector needs will have it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: I shall not sleep in quiet at the Tower.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what should you fear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: YORK
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, my uncle Clarence' angry ghost:
My grandam told me he was murdered there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: I fear no uncles dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Nor none that live, I hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRINCE EDWARD
SPEECH.LINE: An if they live, I hope I need not fear.
But come, my lord; and with a heavy heart,
Thinking on them, go I unto the Tower.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: A Sennet. Exeunt all but GLOUCESTER, BUCKINGHAM and CATESBY

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Think you, my lord, this little prating York
Was not incensed by his subtle mother
To taunt and scorn you thus opprobriously?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: No doubt, no doubt; O, 'tis a parlous boy;
Bold, quick, ingenious, forward, capable
He is all the mother's, from the top to toe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Well, let them rest. Come hither, Catesby.
Thou art sworn as deeply to effect what we intend
As closely to conceal what we impart:
Thou know'st our reasons urged upon the way;
What think'st thou? is it not an easy matter
To make William Lord Hastings of our mind,
For the instalment of this noble duke
In the seat royal of this famous isle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: He for his father's sake so loves the prince,
That he will not be won to aught against him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: What think'st thou, then, of Stanley? what will he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: He will do all in all as Hastings doth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Well, then, no more but this: go, gentle Catesby,
And, as it were far off sound thou Lord Hastings,
How doth he stand affected to our purpose;
And summon him to-morrow to the Tower,
To sit about the coronation.
If thou dost find him tractable to us,
Encourage him, and show him all our reasons:
If he be leaden, icy-cold, unwilling,
Be thou so too; and so break off your talk,
And give us notice of his inclination:
For we to-morrow hold divided councils,
Wherein thyself shalt highly be employ'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Commend me to Lord William: tell him, Catesby,
His ancient knot of dangerous adversaries
To-morrow are let blood at Pomfret-castle;
And bid my friend, for joy of this good news,
Give mistress Shore one gentle kiss the more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Good Catesby, go, effect this business soundly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: My good lords both, with all the heed I may.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Shall we hear from you, Catesby, ere we sleep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: You shall, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: At Crosby Place, there shall you find us both.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Now, my lord, what shall we do, if we perceive
Lord Hastings will not yield to our complots?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Chop off his head, man; somewhat we will do:
And, look, when I am king, claim thou of me
The earldom of Hereford, and the moveables
Whereof the king my brother stood possess'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I'll claim that promise at your grace's hands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: And look to have it yielded with all willingness.
Come, let us sup betimes, that afterwards
We may digest our complots in some form.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Before Lord Hastings' house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: What, ho! my lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Within Who knocks at the door?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: A messenger from the Lord Stanley.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: What is't o'clock?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the stroke of four.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Cannot thy master sleep these tedious nights?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: So it should seem by that I have to say.
First, he commends him to your noble lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: And then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: And then he sends you word
He dreamt to-night the boar had razed his helm:
Besides, he says there are two councils held;
And that may be determined at the one
which may make you and him to rue at the other.
Therefore he sends to know your lordship's pleasure,
If presently you will take horse with him,
And with all speed post with him toward the north,
To shun the danger that his soul divines.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Go, fellow, go, return unto thy lord;
Bid him not fear the separated councils
His honour and myself are at the one,
And at the other is my servant Catesby
Where nothing can proceed that toucheth us
Whereof I shall not have intelligence.
Tell him his fears are shallow, wanting instance:
And for his dreams, I wonder he is so fond
To trust the mockery of unquiet slumbers
To fly the boar before the boar pursues,
Were to incense the boar to follow us
And make pursuit where he did mean no chase.
Go, bid thy master rise and come to me
And we will both together to the Tower,
Where, he shall see, the boar will use us kindly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious lord, I'll tell him what you say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Many good morrows to my noble lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, Catesby; you are early stirring
What news, what news, in this our tottering state?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: It is a reeling world, indeed, my lord;
And I believe twill never stand upright
Tim Richard wear the garland of the realm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: How! wear the garland! dost thou mean the crown?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have this crown of mine cut from my shoulders
Ere I will see the crown so foul misplaced.
But canst thou guess that he doth aim at it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, on my life; and hopes to find forward
Upon his party for the gain thereof:
And thereupon he sends you this good news,
That this same very day your enemies,
The kindred of the queen, must die at Pomfret.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, I am no mourner for that news,
Because they have been still mine enemies:
But, that I'll give my voice on Richard's side,
To bar my master's heirs in true descent,
God knows I will not do it, to the death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: God keep your lordship in that gracious mind!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: But I shall laugh at this a twelve-month hence,
That they who brought me in my master's hate
I live to look upon their tragedy.
I tell thee, Catesby--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: What, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Ere a fortnight make me elder,
I'll send some packing that yet think not on it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a vile thing to die, my gracious lord,
When men are unprepared and look not for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: O monstrous, monstrous! and so falls it out
With Rivers, Vaughan, Grey: and so 'twill do
With some men else, who think themselves as safe
As thou and I; who, as thou know'st, are dear
To princely Richard and to Buckingham.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: The princes both make high account of you;
For they account his head upon the bridge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I know they do; and I have well deserved it.
Come on, come on; where is your boar-spear, man?
Fear you the boar, and go so unprovided?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STANLEY
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, good morrow; good morrow, Catesby:
You may jest on, but, by the holy rood,
I do not like these several councils, I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,
I hold my life as dear as you do yours;
And never in my life, I do protest,
Was it more precious to me than 'tis now:
Think you, but that I know our state secure,
I would be so triumphant as I am?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STANLEY
SPEECH.LINE: The lords at Pomfret, when they rode from London,
Were jocund, and supposed their state was sure,
And they indeed had no cause to mistrust;
But yet, you see how soon the day o'ercast.
This sudden stag of rancour I misdoubt:
Pray God, I say, I prove a needless coward!
What, shall we toward the Tower? the day is spent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, have with you. Wot you what, my lord?
To-day the lords you talk of are beheaded.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORD STANLEY
SPEECH.LINE: They, for their truth, might better wear their heads
Than some that have accused them wear their hats.
But come, my lord, let us away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Go on before; I'll talk with this good fellow.
How now, sirrah! how goes the world with thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pursuivant
SPEECH.LINE: The better that your lordship please to ask.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I tell thee, man, 'tis better with me now
Than when I met thee last where now we meet:
Then was I going prisoner to the Tower,
By the suggestion of the queen's allies;
But now, I tell thee--keep it to thyself--
This day those enemies are put to death,
And I in better state than e'er I was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pursuivant
SPEECH.LINE: God hold it, to your honour's good content!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Gramercy, fellow: there, drink that for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pursuivant
SPEECH.LINE: God save your lordship!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Priest
SPEECH.LINE: Well met, my lord; I am glad to see your honour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, good Sir John, with all my heart.
I am in your debt for your last exercise;
Come the next Sabbath, and I will content you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: What, talking with a priest, lord chamberlain?
Your friends at Pomfret, they do need the priest;
Your honour hath no shriving work in hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Good faith, and when I met this holy man,
Those men you talk of came into my mind.
What, go you toward the Tower?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: I do, my lord; but long I shall not stay
I shall return before your lordship thence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis like enough, for I stay dinner there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Aside And supper too, although thou know'st it not.
Come, will you go?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll wait upon your lordship.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Pomfret Castle.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter RATCLIFF, with halberds, carrying RIVERS, GREY, and VAUGHAN to death

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Come, bring forth the prisoners.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Richard Ratcliff, let me tell thee this:
To-day shalt thou behold a subject die
For truth, for duty, and for loyalty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREY
SPEECH.LINE: God keep the prince from all the pack of you!
A knot you are of damned blood-suckers!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VAUGHAN
SPEECH.LINE: You live that shall cry woe for this after.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Dispatch; the limit of your lives is out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: O Pomfret, Pomfret! O thou bloody prison,
Fatal and ominous to noble peers!
Within the guilty closure of thy walls
Richard the second here was hack'd to death;
And, for more slander to thy dismal seat,
We give thee up our guiltless blood to drink.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREY
SPEECH.LINE: Now Margaret's curse is fall'n upon our heads,
For standing by when Richard stabb'd her son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Then cursed she Hastings, then cursed she Buckingham,
Then cursed she Richard. O, remember, God
To hear her prayers for them, as now for us
And for my sister and her princely sons,
Be satisfied, dear God, with our true blood,
Which, as thou know'st, unjustly must be spilt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Make haste; the hour of death is expiate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RIVERS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Grey, come, Vaughan, let us all embrace:
And take our leave, until we meet in heaven.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. The Tower of London.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BUCKINGHAM, DERBY, HASTINGS, the BISHOP OF ELY, RATCLIFF, LOVEL, with others, and take their seats at a table

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: My lords, at once: the cause why we are met
Is, to determine of the coronation.
In God's name, speak: when is the royal day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Are all things fitting for that royal time?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: It is, and wants but nomination.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: To-morrow, then, I judge a happy day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Who knows the lord protector's mind herein?
Who is most inward with the royal duke?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: Your grace, we think, should soonest know his mind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Who, I, my lord I we know each other's faces,
But for our hearts, he knows no more of mine,
Than I of yours;
Nor I no more of his, than you of mine.
Lord Hastings, you and he are near in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank his grace, I know he loves me well;
But, for his purpose in the coronation.
I have not sounded him, nor he deliver'd
His gracious pleasure any way therein:
But you, my noble lords, may name the time;
And in the duke's behalf I'll give my voice,
Which, I presume, he'll take in gentle part.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: Now in good time, here comes the duke himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My noble lords and cousins all, good morrow.
I have been long a sleeper; but, I hope,
My absence doth neglect no great designs,
Which by my presence might have been concluded.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Had not you come upon your cue, my lord
William Lord Hastings had pronounced your part,--
I mean, your voice,--for crowning of the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Than my Lord Hastings no man might be bolder;
His lordship knows me well, and loves me well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: My lord of Ely!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: When I was last in Holborn,
I saw good strawberries in your garden there
I do beseech you send for some of them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, and will, my lord, with all my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Cousin of Buckingham, a word with you.
Catesby hath sounded Hastings in our business,
And finds the testy gentleman so hot,
As he will lose his head ere give consent
His master's son, as worshipful as he terms it,
Shall lose the royalty of England's throne.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: Withdraw you hence, my lord, I'll follow you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: We have not yet set down this day of triumph.
To-morrow, in mine opinion, is too sudden;
For I myself am not so well provided
As else I would be, were the day prolong'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BISHOP OF ELY
SPEECH.LINE: Where is my lord protector? I have sent for these
strawberries.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: His grace looks cheerfully and smooth to-day;
There's some conceit or other likes him well,
When he doth bid good morrow with such a spirit.
I think there's never a man in Christendom
That can less hide his love or hate than he;
For by his face straight shall you know his heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: What of his heart perceive you in his face
By any likelihood he show'd to-day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, that with no man here he is offended;
For, were he, he had shown it in his looks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: I pray God he be not, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you all, tell me what they deserve
That do conspire my death with devilish plots
Of damned witchcraft, and that have prevail'd
Upon my body with their hellish charms?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: The tender love I bear your grace, my lord,
Makes me most forward in this noble presence
To doom the offenders, whatsoever they be
I say, my lord, they have deserved death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: Then be your eyes the witness of this ill:
See how I am bewitch'd; behold mine arm
Is, like a blasted sapling, wither'd up:
And this is Edward's wife, that monstrous witch,
Consorted with that harlot strumpet Shore,
That by their witchcraft thus have marked me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: If they have done this thing, my gracious lord--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
SPEECH.LINE: If I thou protector of this damned strumpet--
Tellest thou me of 'ifs'? Thou art a traitor:
Off with his head! Now, by Saint Paul I swear,
I will not dine until I see the same.
Lovel and Ratcliff, look that it be done:
The rest, that love me, rise and follow me.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but HASTINGS, RATCLIFF, and LOVEL

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: Woe, woe for England! not a whit for me;
For I, too fond, might have prevented this.
Stanley did dream the boar did raze his helm;
But I disdain'd it, and did scorn to fly:
Three times to-day my foot-cloth horse did stumble,
And startled, when he look'd upon the Tower,
As loath to bear me to the slaughter-house.
O, now I want the priest that spake to me:
I now repent I told the pursuivant
As 'twere triumphing at mine enemies,
How they at Pomfret bloodily were butcher'd,
And I myself secure in grace and favour.
O Margaret, Margaret, now thy heavy curse
Is lighted on poor Hastings' wretched head!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Dispatch, my lord; the duke would be at dinner:
Make a short shrift; he longs to see your head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: O momentary grace of mortal men,
Which we more hunt for than the grace of God!
Who builds his hopes in air of your good looks,
Lives like a drunken sailor on a mast,
Ready, with every nod, to tumble down
Into the fatal bowels of the deep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LOVEL
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, dispatch; 'tis bootless to exclaim.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HASTINGS
SPEECH.LINE: O bloody Richard! miserable England!
I prophesy the fearful'st time to thee
That ever wretched age hath look'd upon.
Come, lead me to the block; bear him my head.
They smile at me that shortly shall be dead.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The Tower-walls.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter GLOUCESTER and BUCKINGHAM, in rotten armour, marvellous ill-favoured

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GLOUCESTER
