Thy nephews' souls bid thee despair and die!
Sleep, Richmond, sleep in peace, and wake in joy;
Good angels guard thee from the boar's annoy!
Live, and beget a happy race of kings!
Edward's unhappy sons do bid thee flourish.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the Ghost of LADY ANNE

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Ghost of LADY ANNE
SPEECH.LINE: Richard, thy wife, that wretched Anne thy wife,
That never slept a quiet hour with thee,
Now fills thy sleep with perturbations
To-morrow in the battle think on me,
And fall thy edgeless sword: despair, and die!
Thou quiet soul, sleep thou a quiet sleep
Dream of success and happy victory!
Thy adversary's wife doth pray for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Ghost of BUCKINGHAM
SPEECH.LINE: The last was I that helped thee to the crown;
The last was I that felt thy tyranny:
O, in the battle think on Buckingham,
And die in terror of thy guiltiness!
Dream on, dream on, of bloody deeds and death:
Fainting, despair; despairing, yield thy breath!
I died for hope ere I could lend thee aid:
But cheer thy heart, and be thou not dismay'd:
God and good angel fight on Richmond's side;
And Richard falls in height of all his pride.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: KING RICHARD III starts out of his dream

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: Give me another horse: bind up my wounds.
Have mercy, Jesu!--Soft! I did but dream.
O coward conscience, how dost thou afflict me!
The lights burn blue. It is now dead midnight.
Cold fearful drops stand on my trembling flesh.
What do I fear? myself? there's none else by:
Richard loves Richard; that is, I am I.
Is there a murderer here? No. Yes, I am:
Then fly. What, from myself? Great reason why:
Lest I revenge. What, myself upon myself?
Alack. I love myself. Wherefore? for any good
That I myself have done unto myself?
O, no! alas, I rather hate myself
For hateful deeds committed by myself!
I am a villain: yet I lie. I am not.
Fool, of thyself speak well: fool, do not flatter.
My conscience hath a thousand several tongues,
And every tongue brings in a several tale,
And every tale condemns me for a villain.
Perjury, perjury, in the high'st degree
Murder, stem murder, in the direst degree;
All several sins, all used in each degree,
Throng to the bar, crying all, Guilty! guilty!
I shall despair. There is no creature loves me;
And if I die, no soul shall pity me:
Nay, wherefore should they, since that I myself
Find in myself no pity to myself?
Methought the souls of all that I had murder'd
Came to my tent; and every one did threat
To-morrow's vengeance on the head of Richard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: My lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds! who is there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Ratcliff, my lord; 'tis I. The early village-cock
Hath twice done salutation to the morn;
Your friends are up, and buckle on their armour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: O Ratcliff, I have dream'd a fearful dream!
What thinkest thou, will our friends prove all true?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: No doubt, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: O Ratcliff, I fear, I fear,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good my lord, be not afraid of shadows.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: By the apostle Paul, shadows to-night
Have struck more terror to the soul of Richard
Than can the substance of ten thousand soldiers
Armed in proof, and led by shallow Richmond.
It is not yet near day. Come, go with me;
Under our tents I'll play the eaves-dropper,
To see if any mean to shrink from me.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter the Lords to RICHMOND, sitting in his tent

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORDS
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, Richmond!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: Cry mercy, lords and watchful gentlemen,
That you have ta'en a tardy sluggard here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORDS
SPEECH.LINE: How have you slept, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: The sweetest sleep, and fairest-boding dreams
That ever enter'd in a drowsy head,
Have I since your departure had, my lords.
Methought their souls, whose bodies Richard murder'd,
Came to my tent, and cried on victory:
I promise you, my soul is very jocund
In the remembrance of so fair a dream.
How far into the morning is it, lords?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LORDS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the stroke of four.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then 'tis time to arm and give direction.
More than I have said, loving countrymen,
The leisure and enforcement of the time
Forbids to dwell upon: yet remember this,
God and our good cause fight upon our side;
The prayers of holy saints and wronged souls,
Like high-rear'd bulwarks, stand before our faces;
Richard except, those whom we fight against
Had rather have us win than him they follow:
For what is he they follow? truly, gentlemen,
A bloody tyrant and a homicide;
One raised in blood, and one in blood establish'd;
One that made means to come by what he hath,
And slaughter'd those that were the means to help him;
Abase foul stone, made precious by the foil
Of England's chair, where he is falsely set;
One that hath ever been God's enemy:
Then, if you fight against God's enemy,
God will in justice ward you as his soldiers;
If you do sweat to put a tyrant down,
You sleep in peace, the tyrant being slain;
If you do fight against your country's foes,
Your country's fat shall pay your pains the hire;
If you do fight in safeguard of your wives,
Your wives shall welcome home the conquerors;
If you do free your children from the sword,
Your children's children quit it in your age.
Then, in the name of God and all these rights,
Advance your standards, draw your willing swords.
For me, the ransom of my bold attempt
Shall be this cold corpse on the earth's cold face;
But if I thrive, the gain of my attempt
The least of you shall share his part thereof.
Sound drums and trumpets boldly and cheerfully;
God and Saint George! Richmond and victory!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter KING RICHARD, RATCLIFF, Attendants and Forces

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: What said Northumberland as touching Richmond?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: That he was never trained up in arms.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: He said the truth: and what said Surrey then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: He smiled and said 'The better for our purpose.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: He was in the right; and so indeed it is.
Ten the clock there. Give me a calendar.
Who saw the sun to-day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: Not I, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: Then he disdains to shine; for by the book
He should have braved the east an hour ago
A black day will it be to somebody. Ratcliff!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RATCLIFF
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: The sun will not be seen to-day;
The sky doth frown and lour upon our army.
I would these dewy tears were from the ground.
Not shine to-day! Why, what is that to me
More than to Richmond? for the selfsame heaven
That frowns on me looks sadly upon him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: Arm, arm, my lord; the foe vaunts in the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: Come, bustle, bustle; caparison my horse.
Call up Lord Stanley, bid him bring his power:
I will lead forth my soldiers to the plain,
And thus my battle shall be ordered:
My foreward shall be drawn out all in length,
Consisting equally of horse and foot;
Our archers shall be placed in the midst
John Duke of Norfolk, Thomas Earl of Surrey,
Shall have the leading of this foot and horse.
They thus directed, we will follow
In the main battle, whose puissance on either side
Shall be well winged with our chiefest horse.
This, and Saint George to boot! What think'st thou, Norfolk?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: A good direction, warlike sovereign.
This found I on my tent this morning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: 'Jockey of Norfolk, be not too bold,
For Dickon thy master is bought and sold.'
A thing devised by the enemy.
Go, gentleman, every man unto his charge
Let not our babbling dreams affright our souls:
Conscience is but a word that cowards use,
Devised at first to keep the strong in awe:
Our strong arms be our conscience, swords our law.
March on, join bravely, let us to't pell-mell
If not to heaven, then hand in hand to hell.
What shall I say more than I have inferr'd?
Remember whom you are to cope withal;
A sort of vagabonds, rascals, and runaways,
A scum of Bretons, and base lackey peasants,
Whom their o'er-cloyed country vomits forth
To desperate ventures and assured destruction.
You sleeping safe, they bring to you unrest;
You having lands, and blest with beauteous wives,
They would restrain the one, distain the other.
And who doth lead them but a paltry fellow,
Long kept in Bretagne at our mother's cost?
A milk-sop, one that never in his life
Felt so much cold as over shoes in snow?
Let's whip these stragglers o'er the seas again;
Lash hence these overweening rags of France,
These famish'd beggars, weary of their lives;
Who, but for dreaming on this fond exploit,
For want of means, poor rats, had hang'd themselves:
If we be conquer'd, let men conquer us,
And not these bastard Bretons; whom our fathers
Have in their own land beaten, bobb'd, and thump'd,
And in record, left them the heirs of shame.
Shall these enjoy our lands? lie with our wives?
Ravish our daughters?
Hark! I hear their drum.
Fight, gentlemen of England! fight, bold yoemen!
Draw, archers, draw your arrows to the head!
Spur your proud horses hard, and ride in blood;
Amaze the welkin with your broken staves!
What says Lord Stanley? will he bring his power?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, he doth deny to come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: Off with his son George's head!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NORFOLK
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, the enemy is past the marsh
After the battle let George Stanley die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: A thousand hearts are great within my bosom:
Advance our standards, set upon our foes
Our ancient word of courage, fair Saint George,
Inspire us with the spleen of fiery dragons!
Upon them! victory sits on our helms.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Another part of the field.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum: excursions. Enter NORFOLK and forces fighting; to him CATESBY

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Rescue, my Lord of Norfolk, rescue, rescue!
The king enacts more wonders than a man,
Daring an opposite to every danger:
His horse is slain, and all on foot he fights,
Seeking for Richmond in the throat of death.
Rescue, fair lord, or else the day is lost!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: A horse! a horse! my kingdom for a horse!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CATESBY
SPEECH.LINE: Withdraw, my lord; I'll help you to a horse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KING RICHARD III
SPEECH.LINE: Slave, I have set my life upon a cast,
And I will stand the hazard of the die:
I think there be six Richmonds in the field;
Five have I slain to-day instead of him.
A horse! a horse! my kingdom for a horse!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another part of the field.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Alarum. Enter KING RICHARD III and RICHMOND; they fight. KING RICHARD III is slain. Retreat and flourish. Re-enter RICHMOND, DERBY bearing the crown, with divers other Lords

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: God and your arms be praised, victorious friends,
The day is ours, the bloody dog is dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: Courageous Richmond, well hast thou acquit thee.
Lo, here, this long-usurped royalty
From the dead temples of this bloody wretch
Have I pluck'd off, to grace thy brows withal:
Wear it, enjoy it, and make much of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: Great God of heaven, say Amen to all!
But, tell me, is young George Stanley living?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: He is, my lord, and safe in Leicester town;
Whither, if it please you, we may now withdraw us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: What men of name are slain on either side?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DERBY
SPEECH.LINE: John Duke of Norfolk, Walter Lord Ferrers,
Sir Robert Brakenbury, and Sir William Brandon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: RICHMOND
SPEECH.LINE: Inter their bodies as becomes their births:
Proclaim a pardon to the soldiers fled
That in submission will return to us:
And then, as we have ta'en the sacrament,
We will unite the white rose and the red:
Smile heaven upon this fair conjunction,
That long have frown'd upon their enmity!
What traitor hears me, and says not amen?
England hath long been mad, and scarr'd herself;
The brother blindly shed the brother's blood,
The father rashly slaughter'd his own son,
The son, compell'd, been butcher to the sire:
All this divided York and Lancaster,
Divided in their dire division,
O, now, let Richmond and Elizabeth,
The true succeeders of each royal house,
By God's fair ordinance conjoin together!
And let their heirs, God, if thy will be so.
Enrich the time to come with smooth-faced peace,
With smiling plenty and fair prosperous days!
Abate the edge of traitors, gracious Lord,
That would reduce these bloody days again,
And make poor England weep in streams of blood!
Let them not live to taste this land's increase
That would with treason wound this fair land's peace!
Now civil wounds are stopp'd, peace lives again:
That she may long live here, God say amen!

PLAY.TITLE: Twelfth Night, or What You Will

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: ANTONIO, a sea captain, friend to Sebastian.
A Sea Captain, friend to Viola.
SIR TOBY BELCH, uncle to Olivia.
Lords, Priests, Sailors, Officers, Musicians, and other Attendants.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE A city in Illyria, and the sea-coast near it.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. DUKE ORSINO's palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DUKE ORSINO, CURIO, and other Lords; Musicians attending

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: If music be the food of love, play on;
Give me excess of it, that, surfeiting,
The appetite may sicken, and so die.
That strain again! it had a dying fall:
O, it came o'er my ear like the sweet sound,
That breathes upon a bank of violets,
Stealing and giving odour! Enough; no more:
'Tis not so sweet now as it was before.
O spirit of love! how quick and fresh art thou,
That, notwithstanding thy capacity
Receiveth as the sea, nought enters there,
Of what validity and pitch soe'er,
But falls into abatement and low price,
Even in a minute: so full of shapes is fancy
That it alone is high fantastical.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURIO
SPEECH.LINE: Will you go hunt, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: What, Curio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURIO
SPEECH.LINE: The hart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so I do, the noblest that I have:
O, when mine eyes did see Olivia first,
Methought she purged the air of pestilence!
That instant was I turn'd into a hart;
And my desires, like fell and cruel hounds,
E'er since pursue me.
How now! what news from her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: So please my lord, I might not be admitted;
But from her handmaid do return this answer:
The element itself, till seven years' heat,
Shall not behold her face at ample view;
But, like a cloistress, she will veiled walk
And water once a day her chamber round
With eye-offending brine: all this to season
A brother's dead love, which she would keep fresh
And lasting in her sad remembrance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: O, she that hath a heart of that fine frame
To pay this debt of love but to a brother,
How will she love, when the rich golden shaft
Hath kill'd the flock of all affections else
That live in her; when liver, brain and heart,
These sovereign thrones, are all supplied, and fill'd
Her sweet perfections with one self king!
Away before me to sweet beds of flowers:
Love-thoughts lie rich when canopied with bowers.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The sea-coast.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter VIOLA, a Captain, and Sailors

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: What country, friends, is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: This is Illyria, lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: And what should I do in Illyria?
My brother he is in Elysium.
Perchance he is not drown'd: what think you, sailors?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: It is perchance that you yourself were saved.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: O my poor brother! and so perchance may he be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: True, madam: and, to comfort you with chance,
Assure yourself, after our ship did split,
When you and those poor number saved with you
Hung on our driving boat, I saw your brother,
Most provident in peril, bind himself,
Courage and hope both teaching him the practise,
To a strong mast that lived upon the sea;
Where, like Arion on the dolphin's back,
I saw him hold acquaintance with the waves
So long as I could see.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: For saying so, there's gold:
Mine own escape unfoldeth to my hope,
Whereto thy speech serves for authority,
The like of him. Know'st thou this country?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, madam, well; for I was bred and born
Not three hours' travel from this very place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Who governs here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: A noble duke, in nature as in name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: What is the name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: Orsino.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Orsino! I have heard my father name him:
He was a bachelor then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: And so is now, or was so very late;
For but a month ago I went from hence,
And then 'twas fresh in murmur,--as, you know,
What great ones do the less will prattle of,--
That he did seek the love of fair Olivia.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: What's she?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: A virtuous maid, the daughter of a count
That died some twelvemonth since, then leaving her
In the protection of his son, her brother,
Who shortly also died: for whose dear love,
They say, she hath abjured the company
And sight of men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: O that I served that lady
And might not be delivered to the world,
Till I had made mine own occasion mellow,
What my estate is!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: That were hard to compass;
Because she will admit no kind of suit,
No, not the duke's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: There is a fair behavior in thee, captain;
And though that nature with a beauteous wall
Doth oft close in pollution, yet of thee
I will believe thou hast a mind that suits
With this thy fair and outward character.
I prithee, and I'll pay thee bounteously,
Conceal me what I am, and be my aid
For such disguise as haply shall become
The form of my intent. I'll serve this duke:
Thou shall present me as an eunuch to him:
It may be worth thy pains; for I can sing
And speak to him in many sorts of music
That will allow me very worth his service.
What else may hap to time I will commit;
Only shape thou thy silence to my wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Captain
SPEECH.LINE: Be you his eunuch, and your mute I'll be:
When my tongue blabs, then let mine eyes not see.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee: lead me on.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. OLIVIA'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SIR TOBY BELCH and MARIA

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What a plague means my niece, to take the death of
her brother thus? I am sure care's an enemy to life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, Sir Toby, you must come in earlier o'
nights: your cousin, my lady, takes great
exceptions to your ill hours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Why, let her except, before excepted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but you must confine yourself within the modest
limits of order.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Confine! I'll confine myself no finer than I am:
these clothes are good enough to drink in; and so be
these boots too: an they be not, let them hang
themselves in their own straps.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: That quaffing and drinking will undo you: I heard
my lady talk of it yesterday; and of a foolish
knight that you brought in one night here to be her wooer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Who, Sir Andrew Aguecheek?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: He's as tall a man as any's in Illyria.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: What's that to the purpose?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Why, he has three thousand ducats a year.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but he'll have but a year in all these ducats:
he's a very fool and a prodigal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, that you'll say so! he plays o' the
viol-de-gamboys, and speaks three or four languages
word for word without book, and hath all the good
gifts of nature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: He hath indeed, almost natural: for besides that
he's a fool, he's a great quarreller: and but that
he hath the gift of a coward to allay the gust he
hath in quarrelling, 'tis thought among the prudent
he would quickly have the gift of a grave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: By this hand, they are scoundrels and subtractors
that say so of him. Who are they?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: They that add, moreover, he's drunk nightly in your company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: With drinking healths to my niece: I'll drink to
her as long as there is a passage in my throat and
drink in Illyria: he's a coward and a coystrill
that will not drink to my niece till his brains turn
o' the toe like a parish-top. What, wench!
Castiliano vulgo! for here comes Sir Andrew Agueface.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Toby Belch! how now, Sir Toby Belch!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Sir Andrew!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Bless you, fair shrew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: And you too, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Accost, Sir Andrew, accost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: What's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: My niece's chambermaid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Good Mistress Accost, I desire better acquaintance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: My name is Mary, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Good Mistress Mary Accost,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: You mistake, knight; 'accost' is front her, board
her, woo her, assail her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, I would not undertake her in this
company. Is that the meaning of 'accost'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, gentlemen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: An thou let part so, Sir Andrew, would thou mightst
never draw sword again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: An you part so, mistress, I would I might never
draw sword again. Fair lady, do you think you have
fools in hand?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I have not you by the hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, but you shall have; and here's my hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, sir, 'thought is free:' I pray you, bring
your hand to the buttery-bar and let it drink.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore, sweet-heart? what's your metaphor?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: It's dry, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I think so: I am not such an ass but I can
keep my hand dry. But what's your jest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: A dry jest, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Are you full of them?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, I have them at my fingers' ends: marry,
now I let go your hand, I am barren.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: O knight thou lackest a cup of canary: when did I
see thee so put down?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Never in your life, I think; unless you see canary
put me down. Methinks sometimes I have no more wit
than a Christian or an ordinary man has: but I am a
great eater of beef and I believe that does harm to my wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: No question.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: An I thought that, I'ld forswear it. I'll ride home
to-morrow, Sir Toby.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Pourquoi, my dear knight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: What is 'Pourquoi'? do or not do? I would I had
bestowed that time in the tongues that I have in
fencing, dancing and bear-baiting: O, had I but
followed the arts!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Then hadst thou had an excellent head of hair.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Why, would that have mended my hair?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Past question; for thou seest it will not curl by nature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: But it becomes me well enough, does't not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent; it hangs like flax on a distaff; and I
hope to see a housewife take thee between her legs
and spin it off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, I'll home to-morrow, Sir Toby: your niece
will not be seen; or if she be, it's four to one
she'll none of me: the count himself here hard by woos her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: She'll none o' the count: she'll not match above
her degree, neither in estate, years, nor wit; I
have heard her swear't. Tut, there's life in't,
man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I'll stay a month longer. I am a fellow o' the
strangest mind i' the world; I delight in masques
and revels sometimes altogether.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou good at these kickshawses, knight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: As any man in Illyria, whatsoever he be, under the
degree of my betters; and yet I will not compare
with an old man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What is thy excellence in a galliard, knight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, I can cut a caper.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: And I can cut the mutton to't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: And I think I have the back-trick simply as strong
as any man in Illyria.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore are these things hid? wherefore have
these gifts a curtain before 'em? are they like to
take dust, like Mistress Mall's picture? why dost
thou not go to church in a galliard and come home in
a coranto? My very walk should be a jig; I would not
so much as make water but in a sink-a-pace. What
dost thou mean? Is it a world to hide virtues in?
I did think, by the excellent constitution of thy
leg, it was formed under the star of a galliard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, 'tis strong, and it does indifferent well in a
flame-coloured stock. Shall we set about some revels?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What shall we do else? were we not born under Taurus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Taurus! That's sides and heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir; it is legs and thighs. Let me see the
caper; ha! higher: ha, ha! excellent!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. DUKE ORSINO's palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter VALENTINE and VIOLA in man's attire

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: If the duke continue these favours towards you,
Cesario, you are like to be much advanced: he hath
known you but three days, and already you are no stranger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: You either fear his humour or my negligence, that
you call in question the continuance of his love:
is he inconstant, sir, in his favours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: No, believe me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you. Here comes the count.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DUKE ORSINO, CURIO, and Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Who saw Cesario, ho?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: On your attendance, my lord; here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Stand you a while aloof, Cesario,
Thou know'st no less but all; I have unclasp'd
To thee the book even of my secret soul:
Therefore, good youth, address thy gait unto her;
Be not denied access, stand at her doors,
And tell them, there thy fixed foot shall grow
Till thou have audience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Sure, my noble lord,
If she be so abandon'd to her sorrow
As it is spoke, she never will admit me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Be clamorous and leap all civil bounds
Rather than make unprofited return.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Say I do speak with her, my lord, what then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: O, then unfold the passion of my love,
Surprise her with discourse of my dear faith:
It shall become thee well to act my woes;
She will attend it better in thy youth
Than in a nuncio's of more grave aspect.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I think not so, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Dear lad, believe it;
For they shall yet belie thy happy years,
That say thou art a man: Diana's lip
Is not more smooth and rubious; thy small pipe
Is as the maiden's organ, shrill and sound,
And all is semblative a woman's part.
I know thy constellation is right apt
For this affair. Some four or five attend him;
All, if you will; for I myself am best
When least in company. Prosper well in this,
And thou shalt live as freely as thy lord,
To call his fortunes thine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll do my best
To woo your lady:
yet, a barful strife!
Whoe'er I woo, myself would be his wife.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. OLIVIA'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, either tell me where thou hast been, or I will
not open my lips so wide as a bristle may enter in
way of thy excuse: my lady will hang thee for thy absence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Let her hang me: he that is well hanged in this
world needs to fear no colours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Make that good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: He shall see none to fear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: A good lenten answer: I can tell thee where that
saying was born, of 'I fear no colours.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Where, good Mistress Mary?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: In the wars; and that may you be bold to say in your foolery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Well, God give them wisdom that have it; and those
that are fools, let them use their talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Yet you will be hanged for being so long absent; or,
to be turned away, is not that as good as a hanging to you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Many a good hanging prevents a bad marriage; and,
for turning away, let summer bear it out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: You are resolute, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Not so, neither; but I am resolved on two points.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: That if one break, the other will hold; or, if both
break, your gaskins fall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Apt, in good faith; very apt. Well, go thy way; if
Sir Toby would leave drinking, thou wert as witty a
piece of Eve's flesh as any in Illyria.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, you rogue, no more o' that. Here comes my
lady: make your excuse wisely, you were best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Wit, an't be thy will, put me into good fooling!
Those wits, that think they have thee, do very oft
prove fools; and I, that am sure I lack thee, may
pass for a wise man: for what says Quinapalus?
'Better a witty fool, than a foolish wit.'
God bless thee, lady!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Take the fool away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Do you not hear, fellows? Take away the lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Go to, you're a dry fool; I'll no more of you:
besides, you grow dishonest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Two faults, madonna, that drink and good counsel
will amend: for give the dry fool drink, then is
the fool not dry: bid the dishonest man mend
himself; if he mend, he is no longer dishonest; if
he cannot, let the botcher mend him. Any thing
that's mended is but patched: virtue that
transgresses is but patched with sin; and sin that
amends is but patched with virtue. If that this
simple syllogism will serve, so; if it will not,
what remedy? As there is no true cuckold but
calamity, so beauty's a flower. The lady bade take
away the fool; therefore, I say again, take her away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I bade them take away you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Misprision in the highest degree! Lady, cucullus non
facit monachum; that's as much to say as I wear not
motley in my brain. Good madonna, give me leave to
prove you a fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Can you do it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Dexterously, good madonna.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Make your proof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: I must catechise you for it, madonna: good my mouse
of virtue, answer me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, for want of other idleness, I'll bide your proof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Good madonna, why mournest thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Good fool, for my brother's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: I think his soul is in hell, madonna.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: I know his soul is in heaven, fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: The more fool, madonna, to mourn for your brother's
soul being in heaven. Take away the fool, gentlemen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: What think you of this fool, Malvolio? doth he not mend?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, and shall do till the pangs of death shake him:
infirmity, that decays the wise, doth ever make the
better fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: God send you, sir, a speedy infirmity, for the
better increasing your folly! Sir Toby will be
sworn that I am no fox; but he will not pass his
word for two pence that you are no fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: How say you to that, Malvolio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I marvel your ladyship takes delight in such a
barren rascal: I saw him put down the other day
with an ordinary fool that has no more brain
than a stone. Look you now, he's out of his guard
already; unless you laugh and minister occasion to
him, he is gagged. I protest, I take these wise men,
that crow so at these set kind of fools, no better
than the fools' zanies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Oh, you are sick of self-love, Malvolio, and taste
with a distempered appetite. To be generous,
guiltless and of free disposition, is to take those
things for bird-bolts that you deem cannon-bullets:
there is no slander in an allowed fool, though he do
nothing but rail; nor no railing in a known discreet
man, though he do nothing but reprove.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Now Mercury endue thee with leasing, for thou
speakest well of fools!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, there is at the gate a young gentleman much
desires to speak with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: From the Count Orsino, is it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: I know not, madam: 'tis a fair young man, and well attended.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Who of my people hold him in delay?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Toby, madam, your kinsman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Fetch him off, I pray you; he speaks nothing but
madman: fie on him!
Go you, Malvolio: if it be a suit from the count, I
am sick, or not at home; what you will, to dismiss it.
Now you see, sir, how your fooling grows old, and
people dislike it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast spoke for us, madonna, as if thy eldest
son should be a fool; whose skull Jove cram with
brains! for,--here he comes,--one of thy kin has a
most weak pia mater.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: By mine honour, half drunk. What is he at the gate, cousin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: A gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: A gentleman! what gentleman?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a gentle man here--a plague o' these
pickle-herring! How now, sot!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Good Sir Toby!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Cousin, cousin, how have you come so early by this lethargy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Lechery! I defy lechery. There's one at the gate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry, what is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Let him be the devil, an he will, I care not: give
me faith, say I. Well, it's all one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: What's a drunken man like, fool?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Like a drowned man, a fool and a mad man: one
draught above heat makes him a fool; the second mads
him; and a third drowns him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Go thou and seek the crowner, and let him sit o' my
coz; for he's in the third degree of drink, he's
drowned: go, look after him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: He is but mad yet, madonna; and the fool shall look
to the madman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, yond young fellow swears he will speak with
you. I told him you were sick; he takes on him to
understand so much, and therefore comes to speak
with you. I told him you were asleep; he seems to
have a foreknowledge of that too, and therefore
comes to speak with you. What is to be said to him,
lady? he's fortified against any denial.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Tell him he shall not speak with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Has been told so; and he says, he'll stand at your
door like a sheriff's post, and be the supporter to
a bench, but he'll speak with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: What kind o' man is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, of mankind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: What manner of man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Of very ill manner; he'll speak with you, will you or no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Of what personage and years is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Not yet old enough for a man, nor young enough for
a boy; as a squash is before 'tis a peascod, or a
cooling when 'tis almost an apple: 'tis with him
in standing water, between boy and man. He is very
well-favoured and he speaks very shrewishly; one
would think his mother's milk were scarce out of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Let him approach: call in my gentlewoman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Gentlewoman, my lady calls.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Give me my veil: come, throw it o'er my face.
We'll once more hear Orsino's embassy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: The honourable lady of the house, which is she?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Speak to me; I shall answer for her.
Your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Most radiant, exquisite and unmatchable beauty,--I
pray you, tell me if this be the lady of the house,
for I never saw her: I would be loath to cast away
my speech, for besides that it is excellently well
penned, I have taken great pains to con it. Good
beauties, let me sustain no scorn; I am very
comptible, even to the least sinister usage.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Whence came you, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I can say little more than I have studied, and that
question's out of my part. Good gentle one, give me
modest assurance if you be the lady of the house,
that I may proceed in my speech.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Are you a comedian?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: No, my profound heart: and yet, by the very fangs
of malice I swear, I am not that I play. Are you
the lady of the house?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: If I do not usurp myself, I am.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Most certain, if you are she, you do usurp
yourself; for what is yours to bestow is not yours
to reserve. But this is from my commission: I will
on with my speech in your praise, and then show you
the heart of my message.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Come to what is important in't: I forgive you the praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, I took great pains to study it, and 'tis poetical.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: It is the more like to be feigned: I pray you,
keep it in. I heard you were saucy at my gates,
and allowed your approach rather to wonder at you
than to hear you. If you be not mad, be gone; if
you have reason, be brief: 'tis not that time of
moon with me to make one in so skipping a dialogue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Will you hoist sail, sir? here lies your way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: No, good swabber; I am to hull here a little
longer. Some mollification for your giant, sweet
lady. Tell me your mind: I am a messenger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sure, you have some hideous matter to deliver, when
the courtesy of it is so fearful. Speak your office.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: It alone concerns your ear. I bring no overture of
war, no taxation of homage: I hold the olive in my
hand; my words are as fun of peace as matter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Yet you began rudely. What are you? what would you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: The rudeness that hath appeared in me have I
learned from my entertainment. What I am, and what I
would, are as secret as maidenhead; to your ears,
divinity, to any other's, profanation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Give us the place alone: we will hear this divinity.
Now, sir, what is your text?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Most sweet lady,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: A comfortable doctrine, and much may be said of it.
Where lies your text?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: In Orsino's bosom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: In his bosom! In what chapter of his bosom?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: To answer by the method, in the first of his heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, I have read it: it is heresy. Have you no more to say?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Good madam, let me see your face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Have you any commission from your lord to negotiate
with my face? You are now out of your text: but
we will draw the curtain and show you the picture.
Look you, sir, such a one I was this present: is't
not well done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Excellently done, if God did all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis in grain, sir; 'twill endure wind and weather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis beauty truly blent, whose red and white
Nature's own sweet and cunning hand laid on:
Lady, you are the cruell'st she alive,
If you will lead these graces to the grave
And leave the world no copy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, I will not be so hard-hearted; I will give
out divers schedules of my beauty: it shall be
inventoried, and every particle and utensil
labelled to my will: as, item, two lips,
indifferent red; item, two grey eyes, with lids to
them; item, one neck, one chin, and so forth. Were
you sent hither to praise me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I see you what you are, you are too proud;
But, if you were the devil, you are fair.
My lord and master loves you: O, such love
Could be but recompensed, though you were crown'd
The nonpareil of beauty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: How does he love me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: With adorations, fertile tears,
With groans that thunder love, with sighs of fire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Your lord does know my mind; I cannot love him:
Yet I suppose him virtuous, know him noble,
Of great estate, of fresh and stainless youth;
In voices well divulged, free, learn'd and valiant;
And in dimension and the shape of nature
A gracious person: but yet I cannot love him;
He might have took his answer long ago.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: If I did love you in my master's flame,
With such a suffering, such a deadly life,
In your denial I would find no sense;
I would not understand it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what would you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Make me a willow cabin at your gate,
And call upon my soul within the house;
Write loyal cantons of contemned love
And sing them loud even in the dead of night;
Halloo your name to the reverberate hills
And make the babbling gossip of the air
Cry out 'Olivia!' O, You should not rest
Between the elements of air and earth,
But you should pity me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: You might do much.
What is your parentage?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Above my fortunes, yet my state is well:
I am a gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Get you to your lord;
I cannot love him: let him send no more;
Unless, perchance, you come to me again,
To tell me how he takes it. Fare you well:
I thank you for your pains: spend this for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I am no fee'd post, lady; keep your purse:
My master, not myself, lacks recompense.
Love make his heart of flint that you shall love;
And let your fervor, like my master's, be
Placed in contempt! Farewell, fair cruelty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'What is your parentage?'
'Above my fortunes, yet my state is well:
I am a gentleman.' I'll be sworn thou art;
Thy tongue, thy face, thy limbs, actions and spirit,
Do give thee five-fold blazon: not too fast:
soft, soft!
Unless the master were the man. How now!
Even so quickly may one catch the plague?
Methinks I feel this youth's perfections
With an invisible and subtle stealth
To creep in at mine eyes. Well, let it be.
What ho, Malvolio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here, madam, at your service.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: Run after that same peevish messenger,
The county's man: he left this ring behind him,
Would I or not: tell him I'll none of it.
Desire him not to flatter with his lord,
Nor hold him up with hopes; I am not for him:
If that the youth will come this way to-morrow,
I'll give him reasons for't: hie thee, Malvolio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, I will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: OLIVIA
SPEECH.LINE: I do I know not what, and fear to find
Mine eye too great a flatterer for my mind.
Fate, show thy force: ourselves we do not owe;
What is decreed must be, and be this so.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The sea-coast.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Will you stay no longer? nor will you not that I go with you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: By your patience, no. My stars shine darkly over
me: the malignancy of my fate might perhaps
distemper yours; therefore I shall crave of you your
leave that I may bear my evils alone: it were a bad
recompense for your love, to lay any of them on you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let me yet know of you whither you are bound.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: No, sooth, sir: my determinate voyage is mere
extravagancy. But I perceive in you so excellent a
touch of modesty, that you will not extort from me
what I am willing to keep in; therefore it charges
me in manners the rather to express myself. You
must know of me then, Antonio, my name is Sebastian,
which I called Roderigo. My father was that
Sebastian of Messaline, whom I know you have heard
of. He left behind him myself and a sister, both
born in an hour: if the heavens had been pleased,
would we had so ended! but you, sir, altered that;
for some hour before you took me from the breach of
the sea was my sister drowned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Alas the day!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: A lady, sir, though it was said she much resembled
me, was yet of many accounted beautiful: but,
though I could not with such estimable wonder
overfar believe that, yet thus far I will boldly
publish her; she bore a mind that envy could not but
call fair. She is drowned already, sir, with salt
water, though I seem to drown her remembrance again with more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, sir, your bad entertainment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: O good Antonio, forgive me your trouble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: If you will not murder me for my love, let me be
your servant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: If you will not undo what you have done, that is,
kill him whom you have recovered, desire it not.
Fare ye well at once: my bosom is full of kindness,
and I am yet so near the manners of my mother, that
upon the least occasion more mine eyes will tell
tales of me. I am bound to the Count Orsino's court: farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: The gentleness of all the gods go with thee!
I have many enemies in Orsino's court,
Else would I very shortly see thee there.
But, come what may, I do adore thee so,
That danger shall seem sport, and I will go.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A street.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Were not you even now with the Countess Olivia?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Even now, sir; on a moderate pace I have since
arrived but hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: She returns this ring to you, sir: you might have
saved me my pains, to have taken it away yourself.
She adds, moreover, that you should put your lord
into a desperate assurance she will none of him:
and one thing more, that you be never so hardy to
come again in his affairs, unless it be to report
your lord's taking of this. Receive it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: She took the ring of me: I'll none of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, sir, you peevishly threw it to her; and her
will is, it should be so returned: if it be worth
stooping for, there it lies in your eye; if not, be
it his that finds it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I left no ring with her: what means this lady?
Fortune forbid my outside have not charm'd her!
She made good view of me; indeed, so much,
That sure methought her eyes had lost her tongue,
For she did speak in starts distractedly.
She loves me, sure; the cunning of her passion
Invites me in this churlish messenger.
None of my lord's ring! why, he sent her none.
I am the man: if it be so, as 'tis,
Poor lady, she were better love a dream.
Disguise, I see, thou art a wickedness,
Wherein the pregnant enemy does much.
How easy is it for the proper-false
In women's waxen hearts to set their forms!
Alas, our frailty is the cause, not we!
For such as we are made of, such we be.
How will this fadge? my master loves her dearly;
And I, poor monster, fond as much on him;
And she, mistaken, seems to dote on me.
What will become of this? As I am man,
My state is desperate for my master's love;
As I am woman,--now alas the day!--
What thriftless sighs shall poor Olivia breathe!
O time! thou must untangle this, not I;
It is too hard a knot for me to untie!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. OLIVIA's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SIR TOBY BELCH and SIR ANDREW

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Approach, Sir Andrew: not to be abed after
midnight is to be up betimes; and 'diluculo
surgere,' thou know'st,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, my troth, I know not: but I know, to be up
late is to be up late.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: A false conclusion: I hate it as an unfilled can.
To be up after midnight and to go to bed then, is
early: so that to go to bed after midnight is to go
to bed betimes. Does not our life consist of the
four elements?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, so they say; but I think it rather consists
of eating and drinking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Thou'rt a scholar; let us therefore eat and drink.
Marian, I say! a stoup of wine!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the fool, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: How now, my hearts! did you never see the picture
of 'we three'?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, ass. Now let's have a catch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: By my troth, the fool has an excellent breast. I
had rather than forty shillings I had such a leg,
and so sweet a breath to sing, as the fool has. In
sooth, thou wast in very gracious fooling last
night, when thou spokest of Pigrogromitus, of the
Vapians passing the equinoctial of Queubus: 'twas
very good, i' faith. I sent thee sixpence for thy
leman: hadst it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: I did impeticos thy gratillity; for Malvolio's nose
is no whipstock: my lady has a white hand, and the
Myrmidons are no bottle-ale houses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent! why, this is the best fooling, when all
is done. Now, a song.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Come on; there is sixpence for you: let's have a song.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: There's a testril of me too: if one knight give a--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Would you have a love-song, or a song of good life?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: A love-song, a love-song.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay: I care not for good life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: O mistress mine, where are you roaming?
O, stay and hear; your true love's coming,
That can sing both high and low:
Trip no further, pretty sweeting;
Journeys end in lovers meeting,
Every wise man's son doth know.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent good, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Good, good.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: What is love? 'tis not hereafter;
Present mirth hath present laughter;
What's to come is still unsure:
In delay there lies no plenty;
Then come kiss me, sweet and twenty,
Youth's a stuff will not endure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: A mellifluous voice, as I am true knight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: A contagious breath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Very sweet and contagious, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: To hear by the nose, it is dulcet in contagion.
But shall we make the welkin dance indeed? shall we
rouse the night-owl in a catch that will draw three
souls out of one weaver? shall we do that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: An you love me, let's do't: I am dog at a catch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: By'r lady, sir, and some dogs will catch well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Most certain. Let our catch be, 'Thou knave.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: 'Hold thy peace, thou knave,' knight? I shall be
constrained in't to call thee knave, knight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis not the first time I have constrained one to
call me knave. Begin, fool: it begins 'Hold thy peace.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: I shall never begin if I hold my peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Good, i' faith. Come, begin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: What a caterwauling do you keep here! If my lady
have not called up her steward Malvolio and bid him
turn you out of doors, never trust me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: My lady's a Cataian, we are politicians, Malvolio's
a Peg-a-Ramsey, and 'Three merry men be we.' Am not
I consanguineous? am I not of her blood?
Tillyvally. Lady!
'There dwelt a man in Babylon, lady, lady!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Beshrew me, the knight's in admirable fooling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, he does well enough if he be disposed, and so do
I too: he does it with a better grace, but I do it
more natural.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Sings 'O, the twelfth day of December,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: For the love o' God, peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: My masters, are you mad? or what are you? Have ye
no wit, manners, nor honesty, but to gabble like
tinkers at this time of night? Do ye make an
alehouse of my lady's house, that ye squeak out your
coziers' catches without any mitigation or remorse
of voice? Is there no respect of place, persons, nor
time in you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: We did keep time, sir, in our catches. Sneck up!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Toby, I must be round with you. My lady bade me
tell you, that, though she harbours you as her
kinsman, she's nothing allied to your disorders. If
you can separate yourself and your misdemeanors, you
are welcome to the house; if not, an it would please
you to take leave of her, she is very willing to bid
you farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: 'Farewell, dear heart, since I must needs be gone.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good Sir Toby.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: 'His eyes do show his days are almost done.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is't even so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: 'But I will never die.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Toby, there you lie.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: This is much credit to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: 'Shall I bid him go?'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: 'What an if you do?'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: 'Shall I bid him go, and spare not?'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: 'O no, no, no, no, you dare not.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Out o' tune, sir: ye lie. Art any more than a
steward? Dost thou think, because thou art
virtuous, there shall be no more cakes and ale?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, by Saint Anne, and ginger shall be hot i' the
mouth too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Thou'rt i' the right. Go, sir, rub your chain with
crumbs. A stoup of wine, Maria!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Mary, if you prized my lady's favour at any
thing more than contempt, you would not give means
for this uncivil rule: she shall know of it, by this hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Go shake your ears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twere as good a deed as to drink when a man's
a-hungry, to challenge him the field, and then to
break promise with him and make a fool of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Do't, knight: I'll write thee a challenge: or I'll
deliver thy indignation to him by word of mouth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Sir Toby, be patient for tonight: since the
youth of the count's was today with thy lady, she is
much out of quiet. For Monsieur Malvolio, let me
alone with him: if I do not gull him into a
nayword, and make him a common recreation, do not
think I have wit enough to lie straight in my bed:
I know I can do it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Possess us, possess us; tell us something of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, sometimes he is a kind of puritan.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: O, if I thought that I'ld beat him like a dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What, for being a puritan? thy exquisite reason,
dear knight?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I have no exquisite reason for't, but I have reason
good enough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: The devil a puritan that he is, or any thing
constantly, but a time-pleaser; an affectioned ass,
that cons state without book and utters it by great
swarths: the best persuaded of himself, so
crammed, as he thinks, with excellencies, that it is
his grounds of faith that all that look on him love
him; and on that vice in him will my revenge find
notable cause to work.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What wilt thou do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: I will drop in his way some obscure epistles of
love; wherein, by the colour of his beard, the shape
of his leg, the manner of his gait, the expressure
of his eye, forehead, and complexion, he shall find
himself most feelingly personated. I can write very
like my lady your niece: on a forgotten matter we
can hardly make distinction of our hands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent! I smell a device.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I have't in my nose too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: He shall think, by the letters that thou wilt drop,
that they come from my niece, and that she's in
love with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: My purpose is, indeed, a horse of that colour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: And your horse now would make him an ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ass, I doubt not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'twill be admirable!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sport royal, I warrant you: I know my physic will
work with him. I will plant you two, and let the
fool make a third, where he shall find the letter:
observe his construction of it. For this night, to
bed, and dream on the event. Farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, Penthesilea.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Before me, she's a good wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: She's a beagle, true-bred, and one that adores me:
what o' that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I was adored once too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Let's to bed, knight. Thou hadst need send for
more money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: If I cannot recover your niece, I am a foul way out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Send for money, knight: if thou hast her not i'
the end, call me cut.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: If I do not, never trust me, take it how you will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, I'll go burn some sack; 'tis too late
to go to bed now: come, knight; come, knight.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. DUKE ORSINO's palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DUKE ORSINO, VIOLA, CURIO, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Give me some music. Now, good morrow, friends.
Now, good Cesario, but that piece of song,
That old and antique song we heard last night:
Methought it did relieve my passion much,
More than light airs and recollected terms
Of these most brisk and giddy-paced times:
Come, but one verse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURIO
SPEECH.LINE: He is not here, so please your lordship that should sing it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Who was it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURIO
SPEECH.LINE: Feste, the jester, my lord; a fool that the lady
Olivia's father took much delight in. He is about the house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Seek him out, and play the tune the while.
Come hither, boy: if ever thou shalt love,
In the sweet pangs of it remember me;
For such as I am all true lovers are,
Unstaid and skittish in all motions else,
Save in the constant image of the creature
That is beloved. How dost thou like this tune?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: It gives a very echo to the seat
Where Love is throned.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou dost speak masterly:
My life upon't, young though thou art, thine eye
Hath stay'd upon some favour that it loves:
Hath it not, boy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: A little, by your favour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: What kind of woman is't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Of your complexion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: She is not worth thee, then. What years, i' faith?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: About your years, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Too old by heaven: let still the woman take
An elder than herself: so wears she to him,
So sways she level in her husband's heart:
For, boy, however we do praise ourselves,
Our fancies are more giddy and unfirm,
More longing, wavering, sooner lost and worn,
Than women's are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I think it well, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Then let thy love be younger than thyself,
Or thy affection cannot hold the bent;
For women are as roses, whose fair flower
Being once display'd, doth fall that very hour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: And so they are: alas, that they are so;
To die, even when they to perfection grow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: O, fellow, come, the song we had last night.
Mark it, Cesario, it is old and plain;
The spinsters and the knitters in the sun
And the free maids that weave their thread with bones
Do use to chant it: it is silly sooth,
And dallies with the innocence of love,
Like the old age.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Are you ready, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; prithee, sing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Come away, come away, death,
And in sad cypress let me be laid;
Fly away, fly away breath;
I am slain by a fair cruel maid.
My shroud of white, stuck all with yew,
O, prepare it!
My part of death, no one so true
Did share it.
Not a flower, not a flower sweet
On my black coffin let there be strown;
Not a friend, not a friend greet
My poor corpse, where my bones shall be thrown:
A thousand thousand sighs to save,
Lay me, O, where
Sad true lover never find my grave,
To weep there!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: There's for thy pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: No pains, sir: I take pleasure in singing, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll pay thy pleasure then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, sir, and pleasure will be paid, one time or another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Give me now leave to leave thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: Now, the melancholy god protect thee; and the
tailor make thy doublet of changeable taffeta, for
thy mind is a very opal. I would have men of such
constancy put to sea, that their business might be
every thing and their intent every where; for that's
it that always makes a good voyage of nothing. Farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Let all the rest give place.
Once more, Cesario,
Get thee to yond same sovereign cruelty:
Tell her, my love, more noble than the world,
Prizes not quantity of dirty lands;
The parts that fortune hath bestow'd upon her,
Tell her, I hold as giddily as fortune;
But 'tis that miracle and queen of gems
That nature pranks her in attracts my soul.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: But if she cannot love you, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot be so answer'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Sooth, but you must.
Say that some lady, as perhaps there is,
Hath for your love a great a pang of heart
As you have for Olivia: you cannot love her;
You tell her so; must she not then be answer'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: There is no woman's sides
Can bide the beating of so strong a passion
As love doth give my heart; no woman's heart
So big, to hold so much; they lack retention
Alas, their love may be call'd appetite,
No motion of the liver, but the palate,
That suffer surfeit, cloyment and revolt;
But mine is all as hungry as the sea,
And can digest as much: make no compare
Between that love a woman can bear me
And that I owe Olivia.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but I know--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: What dost thou know?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Too well what love women to men may owe:
In faith, they are as true of heart as we.
My father had a daughter loved a man,
As it might be, perhaps, were I a woman,
I should your lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: And what's her history?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: A blank, my lord. She never told her love,
But let concealment, like a worm i' the bud,
Feed on her damask cheek: she pined in thought,
And with a green and yellow melancholy
She sat like patience on a monument,
Smiling at grief. Was not this love indeed?
We men may say more, swear more: but indeed
Our shows are more than will; for still we prove
Much in our vows, but little in our love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: But died thy sister of her love, my boy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: I am all the daughters of my father's house,
And all the brothers too: and yet I know not.
Sir, shall I to this lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DUKE ORSINO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that's the theme.
To her in haste; give her this jewel; say,
My love can give no place, bide no denay.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. OLIVIA's garden.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SIR TOBY BELCH, SIR ANDREW, and FABIAN

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Come thy ways, Signior Fabian.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I'll come: if I lose a scruple of this sport,
let me be boiled to death with melancholy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Wouldst thou not be glad to have the niggardly
rascally sheep-biter come by some notable shame?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: I would exult, man: you know, he brought me out o'
favour with my lady about a bear-baiting here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: To anger him we'll have the bear again; and we will
fool him black and blue: shall we not, Sir Andrew?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: An we do not, it is pity of our lives.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the little villain.
How now, my metal of India!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Get ye all three into the box-tree: Malvolio's
coming down this walk: he has been yonder i' the
sun practising behavior to his own shadow this half
hour: observe him, for the love of mockery; for I
know this letter will make a contemplative idiot of
him. Close, in the name of jesting! Lie thou there,
for here comes the trout that must be caught with tickling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis but fortune; all is fortune. Maria once told
me she did affect me: and I have heard herself come
thus near, that, should she fancy, it should be one
of my complexion. Besides, she uses me with a more
exalted respect than any one else that follows her.
What should I think on't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Here's an overweening rogue!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: O, peace! Contemplation makes a rare turkey-cock
of him: how he jets under his advanced plumes!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: 'Slight, I could so beat the rogue!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: To be Count Malvolio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, rogue!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Pistol him, pistol him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: There is example for't; the lady of the Strachy
married the yeoman of the wardrobe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Fie on him, Jezebel!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: O, peace! now he's deeply in: look how
imagination blows him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Having been three months married to her, sitting in
my state,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: O, for a stone-bow, to hit him in the eye!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Calling my officers about me, in my branched velvet
gown; having come from a day-bed, where I have left
Olivia sleeping,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Fire and brimstone!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: O, peace, peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: And then to have the humour of state; and after a
demure travel of regard, telling them I know my
place as I would they should do theirs, to for my
kinsman Toby,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Bolts and shackles!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: O peace, peace, peace! now, now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Seven of my people, with an obedient start, make
out for him: I frown the while; and perchance wind
up watch, or play with my--some rich jewel. Toby
approaches; courtesies there to me,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Shall this fellow live?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Though our silence be drawn from us with cars, yet peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I extend my hand to him thus, quenching my familiar
smile with an austere regard of control,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: And does not Toby take you a blow o' the lips then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Saying, 'Cousin Toby, my fortunes having cast me on
your niece give me this prerogative of speech,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: What, what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'You must amend your drunkenness.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Out, scab!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, patience, or we break the sinews of our plot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Besides, you waste the treasure of your time with
a foolish knight,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: That's me, I warrant you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'One Sir Andrew,'--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I knew 'twas I; for many do call me fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: What employment have we here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Now is the woodcock near the gin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: O, peace! and the spirit of humour intimate reading
aloud to him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: By my life, this is my lady's hand these be her
very C's, her U's and her T's and thus makes she her
great P's. It is, in contempt of question, her hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Her C's, her U's and her T's: why that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'To the unknown beloved, this, and my good
wishes:'--her very phrases! By your leave, wax.
Soft! and the impressure her Lucrece, with which she
uses to seal: 'tis my lady. To whom should this be?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: This wins him, liver and all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: Jove knows I love: But who?
Lips, do not move;
No man must know.
'No man must know.' What follows? the numbers
altered! 'No man must know:' if this should be
thee, Malvolio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, hang thee, brock!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: I may command where I adore;
But silence, like a Lucrece knife,
With bloodless stroke my heart doth gore:
M, O, A, I, doth sway my life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: A fustian riddle!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent wench, say I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'M, O, A, I, doth sway my life.' Nay, but first, let
me see, let me see, let me see.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: What dish o' poison has she dressed him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: And with what wing the staniel cheques at it!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'I may command where I adore.' Why, she may command
me: I serve her; she is my lady. Why, this is
evident to any formal capacity; there is no
obstruction in this: and the end,--what should
that alphabetical position portend? If I could make
that resemble something in me,--Softly! M, O, A,

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: O, ay, make up that: he is now at a cold scent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Sowter will cry upon't for all this, though it be as
rank as a fox.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: M,--Malvolio; M,--why, that begins my name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Did not I say he would work it out? the cur is
excellent at faults.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: M,--but then there is no consonancy in the sequel;
that suffers under probation A should follow but O does.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: And O shall end, I hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, or I'll cudgel him, and make him cry O!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: And then I comes behind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, an you had any eye behind you, you might see
more detraction at your heels than fortunes before
you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MALVOLIO
SPEECH.LINE: M, O, A, I; this simulation is not as the former: and
yet, to crush this a little, it would bow to me, for
every one of these letters are in my name. Soft!
here follows prose.
'If this fall into thy hand, revolve. In my stars I
am above thee; but be not afraid of greatness: some
are born great, some achieve greatness, and some
have greatness thrust upon 'em. Thy Fates open
their hands; let thy blood and spirit embrace them;
and, to inure thyself to what thou art like to be,
cast thy humble slough and appear fresh. Be
opposite with a kinsman, surly with servants; let
thy tongue tang arguments of state; put thyself into
the trick of singularity: she thus advises thee
that sighs for thee. Remember who commended thy
yellow stockings, and wished to see thee ever
cross-gartered: I say, remember. Go to, thou art
made, if thou desirest to be so; if not, let me see
thee a steward still, the fellow of servants, and
not worthy to touch Fortune's fingers. Farewell.
She that would alter services with thee,
THE FORTUNATE-UNHAPPY.'
Daylight and champaign discovers not more: this is
open. I will be proud, I will read politic authors,
I will baffle Sir Toby, I will wash off gross
acquaintance, I will be point-devise the very man.
I do not now fool myself, to let imagination jade
me; for every reason excites to this, that my lady
loves me. She did commend my yellow stockings of
late, she did praise my leg being cross-gartered;
and in this she manifests herself to my love, and
with a kind of injunction drives me to these habits
of her liking. I thank my stars I am happy. I will
be strange, stout, in yellow stockings, and
cross-gartered, even with the swiftness of putting
on. Jove and my stars be praised! Here is yet a
postscript.
'Thou canst not choose but know who I am. If thou
entertainest my love, let it appear in thy smiling;
thy smiles become thee well; therefore in my
presence still smile, dear my sweet, I prithee.'
Jove, I thank thee: I will smile; I will do
everything that thou wilt have me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: I will not give my part of this sport for a pension
of thousands to be paid from the Sophy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: I could marry this wench for this device.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: So could I too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: And ask no other dowry with her but such another jest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I neither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FABIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes my noble gull-catcher.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Wilt thou set thy foot o' my neck?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: Or o' mine either?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I play my freedom at traytrip, and become thy
bond-slave?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I' faith, or I either?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Why, thou hast put him in such a dream, that when
the image of it leaves him he must run mad.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but say true; does it work upon him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: Like aqua-vitae with a midwife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARIA
SPEECH.LINE: If you will then see the fruits of the sport, mark
his first approach before my lady: he will come to
her in yellow stockings, and 'tis a colour she
abhors, and cross-gartered, a fashion she detests;
and he will smile upon her, which will now be so
unsuitable to her disposition, being addicted to a
melancholy as she is, that it cannot but turn him
into a notable contempt. If you will see it, follow
me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR TOBY BELCH
SPEECH.LINE: To the gates of Tartar, thou most excellent devil of wit!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SIR ANDREW
SPEECH.LINE: I'll make one too.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. OLIVIA's garden.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter VIOLA, and Clown with a tabour

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Save thee, friend, and thy music: dost thou live by
thy tabour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Clown
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir, I live by the church.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VIOLA
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou a churchman?
