SPEECH.LINE: Why, 'Jack, boy! ho! boy!' and as much news as
will thaw.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, you are so full of cony-catching!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, therefore fire; for I have caught extreme cold.
Where's the cook? is supper ready, the house
trimmed, rushes strewed, cobwebs swept; the
serving-men in their new fustian, their white
stockings, and every officer his wedding-garment on?
Be the jacks fair within, the jills fair without,
the carpets laid, and every thing in order?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: All ready; and therefore, I pray thee, news.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: First, know, my horse is tired; my master and
mistress fallen out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: How?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Out of their saddles into the dirt; and thereby
hangs a tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Let's ha't, good Grumio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Lend thine ear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: There.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: This is to feel a tale, not to hear a tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: And therefore 'tis called a sensible tale: and this
cuff was but to knock at your ear, and beseech
listening. Now I begin: Imprimis, we came down a
foul hill, my master riding behind my mistress,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Both of one horse?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: What's that to thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, a horse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Tell thou the tale: but hadst thou not crossed me,
thou shouldst have heard how her horse fell and she
under her horse; thou shouldst have heard in how
miry a place, how she was bemoiled, how he left her
with the horse upon her, how he beat me because
her horse stumbled, how she waded through the dirt
to pluck him off me, how he swore, how she prayed,
that never prayed before, how I cried, how the
horses ran away, how her bridle was burst, how I
lost my crupper, with many things of worthy memory,
which now shall die in oblivion and thou return
unexperienced to thy grave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: By this reckoning he is more shrew than she.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; and that thou and the proudest of you all shall
find when he comes home. But what talk I of this?
Call forth Nathaniel, Joseph, Nicholas, Philip,
Walter, Sugarsop and the rest: let their heads be
sleekly combed their blue coats brushed and their
garters of an indifferent knit: let them curtsy
with their left legs and not presume to touch a hair
of my master's horse-tail till they kiss their
hands. Are they all ready?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: They are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Call them forth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear, ho? you must meet my master to
countenance my mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, she hath a face of her own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: Who knows not that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou, it seems, that calls for company to
countenance her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: I call them forth to credit her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, she comes to borrow nothing of them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome home, Grumio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILIP
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Grumio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JOSEPH
SPEECH.LINE: What, Grumio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NICHOLAS
SPEECH.LINE: Fellow Grumio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: How now, old lad?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, you;--how now, you;-- what, you;--fellow,
you;--and thus much for greeting. Now, my spruce
companions, is all ready, and all things neat?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: All things is ready. How near is our master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: E'en at hand, alighted by this; and therefore be
not--Cock's passion, silence! I hear my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Where be these knaves? What, no man at door
To hold my stirrup nor to take my horse!
Where is Nathaniel, Gregory, Philip?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL SERVING-MEN
SPEECH.LINE: Here, here, sir; here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir! here, sir! here, sir! here, sir!
You logger-headed and unpolish'd grooms!
What, no attendance? no regard? no duty?
Where is the foolish knave I sent before?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir; as foolish as I was before.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: You peasant swain! you whoreson malt-horse drudge!
Did I not bid thee meet me in the park,
And bring along these rascal knaves with thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nathaniel's coat, sir, was not fully made,
And Gabriel's pumps were all unpink'd i' the heel;
There was no link to colour Peter's hat,
And Walter's dagger was not come from sheathing:
There were none fine but Adam, Ralph, and Gregory;
The rest were ragged, old, and beggarly;
Yet, as they are, here are they come to meet you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Go, rascals, go, and fetch my supper in.
Where is the life that late I led--
Where are those--Sit down, Kate, and welcome.--
Sound, sound, sound, sound!
Why, when, I say? Nay, good sweet Kate, be merry.
Off with my boots, you rogues! you villains, when?
It was the friar of orders grey,
As he forth walked on his way:--
Out, you rogue! you pluck my foot awry:
Take that, and mend the plucking off the other.
Be merry, Kate. Some water, here; what, ho!
Where's my spaniel Troilus? Sirrah, get you hence,
And bid my cousin Ferdinand come hither:
One, Kate, that you must kiss, and be acquainted with.
Where are my slippers? Shall I have some water?
Come, Kate, and wash, and welcome heartily.
You whoreson villain! will you let it fall?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Patience, I pray you; 'twas a fault unwilling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: A whoreson beetle-headed, flap-ear'd knave!
Come, Kate, sit down; I know you have a stomach.
Will you give thanks, sweet Kate; or else shall I?
What's this? mutton?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Who brought it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETER
SPEECH.LINE: I.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis burnt; and so is all the meat.
What dogs are these! Where is the rascal cook?
How durst you, villains, bring it from the dresser,
And serve it thus to me that love it not?
Theretake it to you, trenchers, cups, and all;
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Throws the meat, &c. about the stage
SPEECH.LINE: You heedless joltheads and unmanner'd slaves!
What, do you grumble? I'll be with you straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, husband, be not so disquiet:
The meat was well, if you were so contented.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I tell thee, Kate, 'twas burnt and dried away;
And I expressly am forbid to touch it,
For it engenders choler, planteth anger;
And better 'twere that both of us did fast,
Since, of ourselves, ourselves are choleric,
Than feed it with such over-roasted flesh.
Be patient; to-morrow 't shall be mended,
And, for this night, we'll fast for company:
Come, I will bring thee to thy bridal chamber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NATHANIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Peter, didst ever see the like?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETER
SPEECH.LINE: He kills her in her own humour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Where is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CURTIS
SPEECH.LINE: In her chamber, making a sermon of continency to her;
And rails, and swears, and rates, that she, poor soul,
Knows not which way to stand, to look, to speak,
And sits as one new-risen from a dream.
Away, away! for he is coming hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thus have I politicly begun my reign,
And 'tis my hope to end successfully.
My falcon now is sharp and passing empty;
And till she stoop she must not be full-gorged,
For then she never looks upon her lure.
Another way I have to man my haggard,
To make her come and know her keeper's call,
That is, to watch her, as we watch these kites
That bate and beat and will not be obedient.
She eat no meat to-day, nor none shall eat;
Last night she slept not, nor to-night she shall not;
As with the meat, some undeserved fault
I'll find about the making of the bed;
And here I'll fling the pillow, there the bolster,
This way the coverlet, another way the sheets:
Ay, and amid this hurly I intend
That all is done in reverend care of her;
And in conclusion she shall watch all night:
And if she chance to nod I'll rail and brawl
And with the clamour keep her still awake.
This is a way to kill a wife with kindness;
And thus I'll curb her mad and headstrong humour.
He that knows better how to tame a shrew,
Now let him speak: 'tis charity to show.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Padua. Before BAPTISTA'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible, friend Licio, that Mistress Bianca
Doth fancy any other but Lucentio?
I tell you, sir, she bears me fair in hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, to satisfy you in what I have said,
Stand by and mark the manner of his teaching.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, mistress, profit you in what you read?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: What, master, read you? first resolve me that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I read that I profess, the Art to Love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: And may you prove, sir, master of your art!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: While you, sweet dear, prove mistress of my heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Quick proceeders, marry! Now, tell me, I pray,
You that durst swear at your mistress Bianca
Loved none in the world so well as Lucentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: O despiteful love! unconstant womankind!
I tell thee, Licio, this is wonderful.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mistake no more: I am not Licio,
Nor a musician, as I seem to be;
But one that scorn to live in this disguise,
For such a one as leaves a gentleman,
And makes a god of such a cullion:
Know, sir, that I am call'd Hortensio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Signior Hortensio, I have often heard
Of your entire affection to Bianca;
And since mine eyes are witness of her lightness,
I will with you, if you be so contented,
Forswear Bianca and her love for ever.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: See, how they kiss and court! Signior Lucentio,
Here is my hand, and here I firmly vow
Never to woo her no more, but do forswear her,
As one unworthy all the former favours
That I have fondly flatter'd her withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: And here I take the unfeigned oath,
Never to marry with her though she would entreat:
Fie on her! see, how beastly she doth court him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Would all the world but he had quite forsworn!
For me, that I may surely keep mine oath,
I will be married to a wealthy widow,
Ere three days pass, which hath as long loved me
As I have loved this proud disdainful haggard.
And so farewell, Signior Lucentio.
Kindness in women, not their beauteous looks,
Shall win my love: and so I take my leave,
In resolution as I swore before.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Bianca, bless you with such grace
As 'longeth to a lover's blessed case!
Nay, I have ta'en you napping, gentle love,
And have forsworn you with Hortensio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Tranio, you jest: but have you both forsworn me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress, we have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Then we are rid of Licio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I' faith, he'll have a lusty widow now,
That shall be wood and wedded in a day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: God give him joy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and he'll tame her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: He says so, Tranio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, he is gone unto the taming-school.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: The taming-school! what, is there such a place?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, mistress, and Petruchio is the master;
That teacheth tricks eleven and twenty long,
To tame a shrew and charm her chattering tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: O master, master, I have watch'd so long
That I am dog-weary: but at last I spied
An ancient angel coming down the hill,
Will serve the turn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: What is he, Biondello?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Master, a mercatante, or a pedant,
I know not what; but format in apparel,
In gait and countenance surely like a father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: And what of him, Tranio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: If he be credulous and trust my tale,
I'll make him glad to seem Vincentio,
And give assurance to Baptista Minola,
As if he were the right Vincentio
Take in your love, and then let me alone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: God save you, sir!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: And you, sir! you are welcome.
Travel you far on, or are you at the farthest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, at the farthest for a week or two:
But then up farther, and as for as Rome;
And so to Tripoli, if God lend me life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: What countryman, I pray?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Of Mantua.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Of Mantua, sir? marry, God forbid!
And come to Padua, careless of your life?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: My life, sir! how, I pray? for that goes hard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis death for any one in Mantua
To come to Padua. Know you not the cause?
Your ships are stay'd at Venice, and the duke,
For private quarrel 'twixt your duke and him,
Hath publish'd and proclaim'd it openly:
'Tis, marvel, but that you are but newly come,
You might have heard it else proclaim'd about.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Alas! sir, it is worse for me than so;
For I have bills for money by exchange
From Florence and must here deliver them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, to do you courtesy,
This will I do, and this I will advise you:
First, tell me, have you ever been at Pisa?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, in Pisa have I often been,
Pisa renowned for grave citizens.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Among them know you one Vincentio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: I know him not, but I have heard of him;
A merchant of incomparable wealth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: He is my father, sir; and, sooth to say,
In countenance somewhat doth resemble you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside As much as an apple doth an oyster,
and all one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: To save your life in this extremity,
This favour will I do you for his sake;
And think it not the worst of an your fortunes
That you are like to Sir Vincentio.
His name and credit shall you undertake,
And in my house you shall be friendly lodged:
Look that you take upon you as you should;
You understand me, sir: so shall you stay
Till you have done your business in the city:
If this be courtesy, sir, accept of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: O sir, I do; and will repute you ever
The patron of my life and liberty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Then go with me to make the matter good.
This, by the way, I let you understand;
my father is here look'd for every day,
To pass assurance of a dower in marriage
'Twixt me and one Baptista's daughter here:
In all these circumstances I'll instruct you:
Go with me to clothe you as becomes you.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A room in PETRUCHIO'S house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, forsooth; I dare not for my life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The more my wrong, the more his spite appears:
What, did he marry me to famish me?
Beggars, that come unto my father's door,
Upon entreaty have a present aims;
If not, elsewhere they meet with charity:
But I, who never knew how to entreat,
Nor never needed that I should entreat,
Am starved for meat, giddy for lack of sleep,
With oath kept waking and with brawling fed:
And that which spites me more than all these wants,
He does it under name of perfect love;
As who should say, if I should sleep or eat,
'Twere deadly sickness or else present death.
I prithee go and get me some repast;
I care not what, so it be wholesome food.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: What say you to a neat's foot?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis passing good: I prithee let me have it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I fear it is too choleric a meat.
How say you to a fat tripe finely broil'd?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I like it well: good Grumio, fetch it me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot tell; I fear 'tis choleric.
What say you to a piece of beef and mustard?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: A dish that I do love to feed upon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but the mustard is too hot a little.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Why then, the beef, and let the mustard rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay then, I will not: you shall have the mustard,
Or else you get no beef of Grumio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Then both, or one, or any thing thou wilt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why then, the mustard without the beef.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Go, get thee gone, thou false deluding slave,
That feed'st me with the very name of meat:
Sorrow on thee and all the pack of you,
That triumph thus upon my misery!
Go, get thee gone, I say.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PETRUCHIO and HORTENSIO with meat

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: How fares my Kate? What, sweeting, all amort?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress, what cheer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, as cold as can be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Pluck up thy spirits; look cheerfully upon me.
Here love; thou see'st how diligent I am
To dress thy meat myself and bring it thee:
I am sure, sweet Kate, this kindness merits thanks.
What, not a word? Nay, then thou lovest it not;
And all my pains is sorted to no proof.
Here, take away this dish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, let it stand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: The poorest service is repaid with thanks;
And so shall mine, before you touch the meat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Signior Petruchio, fie! you are to blame.
Come, mistress Kate, I'll bear you company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Eat it up all, Hortensio, if thou lovest me.
Much good do it unto thy gentle heart!
Kate, eat apace: and now, my honey love,
Will we return unto thy father's house
And revel it as bravely as the best,
With silken coats and caps and golden rings,
With ruffs and cuffs and fardingales and things;
With scarfs and fans and double change of bravery,
With amber bracelets, beads and all this knavery.
What, hast thou dined? The tailor stays thy leisure,
To deck thy body with his ruffling treasure.
Come, tailor, let us see these ornaments;
Lay forth the gown.
What news with you, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Haberdasher
SPEECH.LINE: Here is the cap your worship did bespeak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this was moulded on a porringer;
A velvet dish: fie, fie! 'tis lewd and filthy:
Why, 'tis a cockle or a walnut-shell,
A knack, a toy, a trick, a baby's cap:
Away with it! come, let me have a bigger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have no bigger: this doth fit the time,
And gentlewomen wear such caps as these

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: When you are gentle, you shall have one too,
And not till then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside That will not be in haste.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, sir, I trust I may have leave to speak;
And speak I will; I am no child, no babe:
Your betters have endured me say my mind,
And if you cannot, best you stop your ears.
My tongue will tell the anger of my heart,
Or else my heart concealing it will break,
And rather than it shall, I will be free
Even to the uttermost, as I please, in words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, thou say'st true; it is a paltry cap,
A custard-coffin, a bauble, a silken pie:
I love thee well, in that thou likest it not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Love me or love me not, I like the cap;
And it I will have, or I will have none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thy gown? why, ay: come, tailor, let us see't.
O mercy, God! what masquing stuff is here?
What's this? a sleeve? 'tis like a demi-cannon:
What, up and down, carved like an apple-tart?
Here's snip and nip and cut and slish and slash,
Like to a censer in a barber's shop:
Why, what, i' devil's name, tailor, call'st thou this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I see she's like to have neither cap nor gown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: You bid me make it orderly and well,
According to the fashion and the time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, and did; but if you be remember'd,
I did not bid you mar it to the time.
Go, hop me over every kennel home,
For you shall hop without my custom, sir:
I'll none of it: hence! make your best of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I never saw a better-fashion'd gown,
More quaint, more pleasing, nor more commendable:
Belike you mean to make a puppet of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, true; he means to make a puppet of thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: She says your worship means to make
a puppet of her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: O monstrous arrogance! Thou liest, thou thread,
thou thimble,
Thou yard, three-quarters, half-yard, quarter, nail!
Thou flea, thou nit, thou winter-cricket thou!
Braved in mine own house with a skein of thread?
Away, thou rag, thou quantity, thou remnant;
Or I shall so be-mete thee with thy yard
As thou shalt think on prating whilst thou livest!
I tell thee, I, that thou hast marr'd her gown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Your worship is deceived; the gown is made
Just as my master had direction:
Grumio gave order how it should be done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I gave him no order; I gave him the stuff.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: But how did you desire it should be made?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, with needle and thread.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: But did you not request to have it cut?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast faced many things.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: I have.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Face not me: thou hast braved many men; brave not
me; I will neither be faced nor braved. I say unto
thee, I bid thy master cut out the gown; but I did
not bid him cut it to pieces: ergo, thou liest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Why, here is the note of the fashion to testify

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Read it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: The note lies in's throat, if he say I said so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'Imprimis, a loose-bodied gown:'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Master, if ever I said loose-bodied gown, sew me in
the skirts of it, and beat me to death with a bottom
of brown thread: I said a gown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Proceed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'With a small compassed cape:'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I confess the cape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'With a trunk sleeve:'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I confess two sleeves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'The sleeves curiously cut.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, there's the villany.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Error i' the bill, sir; error i' the bill.
I commanded the sleeves should be cut out and
sewed up again; and that I'll prove upon thee,
though thy little finger be armed in a thimble.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Tailor
SPEECH.LINE: This is true that I say: an I had thee
in place where, thou shouldst know it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I am for thee straight: take thou the
bill, give me thy mete-yard, and spare not me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: God-a-mercy, Grumio! then he shall have no odds.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, in brief, the gown is not for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: You are i' the right, sir: 'tis for my mistress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Go, take it up unto thy master's use.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Villain, not for thy life: take up my mistress'
gown for thy master's use!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, sir, what's your conceit in that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GRUMIO
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, the conceit is deeper than you think for:
Take up my mistress' gown to his master's use!
O, fie, fie, fie!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Hortensio, say thou wilt see the tailor paid.
Go take it hence; be gone, and say no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Tailor, I'll pay thee for thy gown tomorrow:
Take no unkindness of his hasty words:
Away! I say; commend me to thy master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, come, my Kate; we will unto your father's
Even in these honest mean habiliments:
Our purses shall be proud, our garments poor;
For 'tis the mind that makes the body rich;
And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds,
So honour peereth in the meanest habit.
What is the jay more precious than the lark,
Because his fathers are more beautiful?
Or is the adder better than the eel,
Because his painted skin contents the eye?
O, no, good Kate; neither art thou the worse
For this poor furniture and mean array.
if thou account'st it shame. lay it on me;
And therefore frolic: we will hence forthwith,
To feast and sport us at thy father's house.
Go, call my men, and let us straight to him;
And bring our horses unto Long-lane end;
There will we mount, and thither walk on foot
Let's see; I think 'tis now some seven o'clock,
And well we may come there by dinner-time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I dare assure you, sir, 'tis almost two;
And 'twill be supper-time ere you come there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: It shall be seven ere I go to horse:
Look, what I speak, or do, or think to do,
You are still crossing it. Sirs, let't alone:
I will not go to-day; and ere I do,
It shall be what o'clock I say it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Why, so this gallant will command the sun.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Padua. Before BAPTISTA'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TRANIO, and the Pedant dressed like VINCENTIO

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, this is the house: please it you that I call?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, what else? and but I be deceived
Signior Baptista may remember me,
Near twenty years ago, in Genoa,
Where we were lodgers at the Pegasus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well; and hold your own, in any case,
With such austerity as 'longeth to a father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: I warrant you.
But, sir, here comes your boy;
'Twere good he were school'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Fear you not him. Sirrah Biondello,
Now do your duty throughly, I advise you:
Imagine 'twere the right Vincentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Tut, fear not me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: But hast thou done thy errand to Baptista?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I told him that your father was at Venice,
And that you look'd for him this day in Padua.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou'rt a tall fellow: hold thee that to drink.
Here comes Baptista: set your countenance, sir.
Signior Baptista, you are happily met.
Sir, this is the gentleman I told you of:
I pray you stand good father to me now,
Give me Bianca for my patrimony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Soft son!
Sir, by your leave: having come to Padua
To gather in some debts, my son Lucentio
Made me acquainted with a weighty cause
Of love between your daughter and himself:
And, for the good report I hear of you
And for the love he beareth to your daughter
And she to him, to stay him not too long,
I am content, in a good father's care,
To have him match'd; and if you please to like
No worse than I, upon some agreement
Me shall you find ready and willing
With one consent to have her so bestow'd;
For curious I cannot be with you,
Signior Baptista, of whom I hear so well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, pardon me in what I have to say:
Your plainness and your shortness please me well.
Right true it is, your son Lucentio here
Doth love my daughter and she loveth him,
Or both dissemble deeply their affections:
And therefore, if you say no more than this,
That like a father you will deal with him
And pass my daughter a sufficient dower,
The match is made, and all is done:
Your son shall have my daughter with consent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, sir. Where then do you know best
We be affied and such assurance ta'en
As shall with either part's agreement stand?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Not in my house, Lucentio; for, you know,
Pitchers have ears, and I have many servants:
Besides, old Gremio is hearkening still;
And happily we might be interrupted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Then at my lodging, an it like you:
There doth my father lie; and there, this night,
We'll pass the business privately and well.
Send for your daughter by your servant here:
My boy shall fetch the scrivener presently.
The worst is this, that, at so slender warning,
You are like to have a thin and slender pittance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: It likes me well. Biondello, hie you home,
And bid Bianca make her ready straight;
And, if you will, tell what hath happened,
Lucentio's father is arrived in Padua,
And how she's like to be Lucentio's wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray the gods she may with all my heart!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Dally not with the gods, but get thee gone.
Signior Baptista, shall I lead the way?
Welcome! one mess is like to be your cheer:
Come, sir; we will better it in Pisa.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: I follow you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Cambio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What sayest thou, Biondello?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: You saw my master wink and laugh upon you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Biondello, what of that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, nothing; but has left me here behind, to
expound the meaning or moral of his signs and tokens.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, moralize them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Then thus. Baptista is safe, talking with the
deceiving father of a deceitful son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: And what of him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: His daughter is to be brought by you to the supper.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: And then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: The old priest of Saint Luke's church is at your
command at all hours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: And what of all this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot tell; expect they are busied about a
counterfeit assurance: take you assurance of her,
'cum privilegio ad imprimendum solum:' to the
church; take the priest, clerk, and some sufficient
honest witnesses: If this be not that you look for,
I have no more to say, But bid Bianca farewell for
ever and a day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Hearest thou, Biondello?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot tarry: I knew a wench married in an
afternoon as she went to the garden for parsley to
stuff a rabbit; and so may you, sir: and so, adieu,
sir. My master hath appointed me to go to Saint
Luke's, to bid the priest be ready to come against
you come with your appendix.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I may, and will, if she be so contented:
She will be pleased; then wherefore should I doubt?
Hap what hap may, I'll roundly go about her:
It shall go hard if Cambio go without her.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. A public road.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PETRUCHIO, KATHARINA, HORTENSIO, and Servants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, i' God's name; once more toward our father's.
Good Lord, how bright and goodly shines the moon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: The moon! the sun: it is not moonlight now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I say it is the moon that shines so bright.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I know it is the sun that shines so bright.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my mother's son, and that's myself,
It shall be moon, or star, or what I list,
Or ere I journey to your father's house.
Go on, and fetch our horses back again.
Evermore cross'd and cross'd; nothing but cross'd!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Say as he says, or we shall never go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Forward, I pray, since we have come so far,
And be it moon, or sun, or what you please:
An if you please to call it a rush-candle,
Henceforth I vow it shall be so for me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I say it is the moon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: I know it is the moon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, then you lie: it is the blessed sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Then, God be bless'd, it is the blessed sun:
But sun it is not, when you say it is not;
And the moon changes even as your mind.
What you will have it named, even that it is;
And so it shall be so for Katharina.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Petruchio, go thy ways; the field is won.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, forward, forward! thus the bowl should run,
And not unluckily against the bias.
But, soft! company is coming here.
Good morrow, gentle mistress: where away?
Tell me, sweet Kate, and tell me truly too,
Hast thou beheld a fresher gentlewoman?
Such war of white and red within her cheeks!
What stars do spangle heaven with such beauty,
As those two eyes become that heavenly face?
Fair lovely maid, once more good day to thee.
Sweet Kate, embrace her for her beauty's sake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: A' will make the man mad, to make a woman of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Young budding virgin, fair and fresh and sweet,
Whither away, or where is thy abode?
Happy the parents of so fair a child;
Happier the man, whom favourable stars
Allot thee for his lovely bed-fellow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, Kate! I hope thou art not mad:
This is a man, old, wrinkled, faded, wither'd,
And not a maiden, as thou say'st he is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, old father, my mistaking eyes,
That have been so bedazzled with the sun
That everything I look on seemeth green:
Now I perceive thou art a reverend father;
Pardon, I pray thee, for my mad mistaking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Do, good old grandsire; and withal make known
Which way thou travellest: if along with us,
We shall be joyful of thy company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Fair sir, and you my merry mistress,
That with your strange encounter much amazed me,
My name is call'd Vincentio; my dwelling Pisa;
And bound I am to Padua; there to visit
A son of mine, which long I have not seen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: What is his name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Lucentio, gentle sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Happily we met; the happier for thy son.
And now by law, as well as reverend age,
I may entitle thee my loving father:
The sister to my wife, this gentlewoman,
Thy son by this hath married. Wonder not,
Nor be grieved: she is of good esteem,
Her dowery wealthy, and of worthy birth;
Beside, so qualified as may beseem
The spouse of any noble gentleman.
Let me embrace with old Vincentio,
And wander we to see thy honest son,
Who will of thy arrival be full joyous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: But is it true? or else is it your pleasure,
Like pleasant travellers, to break a jest
Upon the company you overtake?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: I do assure thee, father, so it is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, go along, and see the truth hereof;
For our first merriment hath made thee jealous.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, Petruchio, this has put me in heart.
Have to my widow! and if she be froward,
Then hast thou taught Hortensio to be untoward.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Padua. Before LUCENTIO'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: GREMIO discovered. Enter behind BIONDELLO, LUCENTIO, and BIANCA

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Softly and swiftly, sir; for the priest is ready.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I fly, Biondello: but they may chance to need thee
at home; therefore leave us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, faith, I'll see the church o' your back; and
then come back to my master's as soon as I can.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: I marvel Cambio comes not all this while.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PETRUCHIO, KATHARINA, VINCENTIO, GRUMIO, with Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, here's the door, this is Lucentio's house:
My father's bears more toward the market-place;
Thither must I, and here I leave you, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: You shall not choose but drink before you go:
I think I shall command your welcome here,
And, by all likelihood, some cheer is toward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: They're busy within; you were best knock louder.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Pedant looks out of the window

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: What's he that knocks as he would beat down the gate?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is Signior Lucentio within, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: He's within, sir, but not to be spoken withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What if a man bring him a hundred pound or two, to
make merry withal?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Keep your hundred pounds to yourself: he shall
need none, so long as I live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I told you your son was well beloved in Padua.
Do you hear, sir? To leave frivolous circumstances,
I pray you, tell Signior Lucentio that his father is
come from Pisa, and is here at the door to speak with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Thou liest: his father is come from Padua and here
looking out at the window.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Art thou his father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir; so his mother says, if I may believe her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: To VINCENTIO Why, how now, gentleman! why, this
is flat knavery, to take upon you another man's name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Lay hands on the villain: I believe a' means to
cozen somebody in this city under my countenance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I have seen them in the church together: God send
'em good shipping! But who is here? mine old
master Vincentio! now we are undone and brought to nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, crack-hemp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Hope I may choose, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, you rogue. What, have you forgot me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Forgot you! no, sir: I could not forget you, for I
never saw you before in all my life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What, you notorious villain, didst thou never see
thy master's father, Vincentio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: What, my old worshipful old master? yes, marry, sir:
see where he looks out of the window.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is't so, indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Help, help, help! here's a madman will murder me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Help, son! help, Signior Baptista!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, Kate, let's stand aside and see the end of
this controversy.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter Pedant below; TRANIO, BAPTISTA, and Servants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, what are you that offer to beat my servant?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: What am I, sir! nay, what are you, sir? O immortal
gods! O fine villain! A silken doublet! a velvet
hose! a scarlet cloak! and a copatain hat! O, I
am undone! I am undone! while I play the good
husband at home, my son and my servant spend all at
the university.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: What, is the man lunatic?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, you seem a sober ancient gentleman by your
habit, but your words show you a madman. Why, sir,
what 'cerns it you if I wear pearl and gold? I
thank my good father, I am able to maintain it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thy father! O villain! he is a sailmaker in Bergamo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: You mistake, sir, you mistake, sir. Pray, what do
you think is his name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: His name! as if I knew not his name: I have brought
him up ever since he was three years old, and his
name is Tranio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Away, away, mad ass! his name is Lucentio and he is
mine only son, and heir to the lands of me, Signior Vincentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Lucentio! O, he hath murdered his master! Lay hold
on him, I charge you, in the duke's name. O, my
son, my son! Tell me, thou villain, where is my son Lucentio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Call forth an officer.
Carry this mad knave to the gaol. Father Baptista,
I charge you see that he be forthcoming.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Carry me to the gaol!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, officer: he shall not go to prison.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Talk not, Signior Gremio: I say he shall go to prison.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Take heed, Signior Baptista, lest you be
cony-catched in this business: I dare swear this
is the right Vincentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Pedant
SPEECH.LINE: Swear, if thou darest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I dare not swear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: Then thou wert best say that I am not Lucentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, I know thee to be Signior Lucentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Away with the dotard! to the gaol with him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Thus strangers may be hailed and abused: O
monstrous villain!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter BIONDELLO, with LUCENTIO and BIANCA

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: O! we are spoiled and--yonder he is: deny him,
forswear him, or else we are all undone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Kneeling Pardon, sweet father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Lives my sweet son?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt BIONDELLO, TRANIO, and Pedant, as fast as may be

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, dear father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: How hast thou offended?
Where is Lucentio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here's Lucentio,
Right son to the right Vincentio;
That have by marriage made thy daughter mine,
While counterfeit supposes bleared thine eyne.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here's packing, with a witness to deceive us all!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Where is that damned villain Tranio,
That faced and braved me in this matter so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, tell me, is not this my Cambio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Cambio is changed into Lucentio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Love wrought these miracles. Bianca's love
Made me exchange my state with Tranio,
While he did bear my countenance in the town;
And happily I have arrived at the last
Unto the wished haven of my bliss.
What Tranio did, myself enforced him to;
Then pardon him, sweet father, for my sake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll slit the villain's nose, that would have sent
me to the gaol.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: But do you hear, sir? have you married my daughter
without asking my good will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Fear not, Baptista; we will content you, go to: but
I will in, to be revenged for this villany.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: And I, to sound the depth of this knavery.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Look not pale, Bianca; thy father will not frown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: My cake is dough; but I'll in among the rest,
Out of hope of all, but my share of the feast.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Husband, let's follow, to see the end of this ado.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: First kiss me, Kate, and we will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What, in the midst of the street?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: What, art thou ashamed of me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir, God forbid; but ashamed to kiss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then let's home again. Come, sirrah, let's away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I will give thee a kiss: now pray thee, love, stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Is not this well? Come, my sweet Kate:
Better once than never, for never too late.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Padua. LUCENTIO'S house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter BAPTISTA, VINCENTIO, GREMIO, the Pedant, LUCENTIO, BIANCA, PETRUCHIO, KATHARINA, HORTENSIO, and Widow, TRANIO, BIONDELLO, and GRUMIO the Serving-men with Tranio bringing in a banquet

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: At last, though long, our jarring notes agree:
And time it is, when raging war is done,
To smile at scapes and perils overblown.
My fair Bianca, bid my father welcome,
While I with self-same kindness welcome thine.
Brother Petruchio, sister Katharina,
And thou, Hortensio, with thy loving widow,
Feast with the best, and welcome to my house:
My banquet is to close our stomachs up,
After our great good cheer. Pray you, sit down;
For now we sit to chat as well as eat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing but sit and sit, and eat and eat!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Padua affords this kindness, son Petruchio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Padua affords nothing but what is kind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: For both our sakes, I would that word were true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, for my life, Hortensio fears his widow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Then never trust me, if I be afeard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: You are very sensible, and yet you miss my sense:
I mean, Hortensio is afeard of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: He that is giddy thinks the world turns round.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Roundly replied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress, how mean you that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Thus I conceive by him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Conceives by me! How likes Hortensio that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: My widow says, thus she conceives her tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Very well mended. Kiss him for that, good widow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: 'He that is giddy thinks the world turns round:'
I pray you, tell me what you meant by that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Your husband, being troubled with a shrew,
Measures my husband's sorrow by his woe:
And now you know my meaning,

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: A very mean meaning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Right, I mean you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: And I am mean indeed, respecting you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: To her, Kate!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: To her, widow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: A hundred marks, my Kate does put her down.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: That's my office.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Spoke like an officer; ha' to thee, lad!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: How likes Gremio these quick-witted folks?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Believe me, sir, they butt together well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Head, and butt! an hasty-witted body
Would say your head and butt were head and horn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, mistress bride, hath that awaken'd you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but not frighted me; therefore I'll sleep again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that you shall not: since you have begun,
Have at you for a bitter jest or two!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Am I your bird? I mean to shift my bush;
And then pursue me as you draw your bow.
You are welcome all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: She hath prevented me. Here, Signior Tranio.
This bird you aim'd at, though you hit her not;
Therefore a health to all that shot and miss'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, Lucentio slipp'd me like his greyhound,
Which runs himself and catches for his master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: A good swift simile, but something currish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRANIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis well, sir, that you hunted for yourself:
'Tis thought your deer does hold you at a bay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: O ho, Petruchio! Tranio hits you now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee for that gird, good Tranio.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Confess, confess, hath he not hit you here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: A' has a little gall'd me, I confess;
And, as the jest did glance away from me,
'Tis ten to one it maim'd you two outright.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, in good sadness, son Petruchio,
I think thou hast the veriest shrew of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I say no: and therefore for assurance
Let's each one send unto his wife;
And he whose wife is most obedient
To come at first when he doth send for her,
Shall win the wager which we will propose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Content. What is the wager?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Twenty crowns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Twenty crowns!
I'll venture so much of my hawk or hound,
But twenty times so much upon my wife.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: A hundred then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: A match! 'tis done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Who shall begin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: That will I.
Go, Biondello, bid your mistress come to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: I go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Son, I'll be your half, Bianca comes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have no halves; I'll bear it all myself.
How now! what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, my mistress sends you word
That she is busy and she cannot come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: How! she is busy and she cannot come!
Is that an answer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GREMIO
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and a kind one too:
Pray God, sir, your wife send you not a worse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I hope better.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah Biondello, go and entreat my wife
To come to me forthwith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: O, ho! entreat her!
Nay, then she must needs come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: I am afraid, sir,
Do what you can, yours will not be entreated.
Now, where's my wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIONDELLO
SPEECH.LINE: She says you have some goodly jest in hand:
She will not come: she bids you come to her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Worse and worse; she will not come! O vile,
Intolerable, not to be endured!
Sirrah Grumio, go to your mistress;
Say, I command her to come to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: I know her answer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: What?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: She will not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: The fouler fortune mine, and there an end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my holidame, here comes Katharina!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: What is your will, sir, that you send for me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Where is your sister, and Hortensio's wife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: They sit conferring by the parlor fire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Go fetch them hither: if they deny to come.
Swinge me them soundly forth unto their husbands:
Away, I say, and bring them hither straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Here is a wonder, if you talk of a wonder.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: And so it is: I wonder what it bodes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, peace it bodes, and love and quiet life,
And awful rule and right supremacy;
And, to be short, what not, that's sweet and happy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BAPTISTA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, fair befal thee, good Petruchio!
The wager thou hast won; and I will add
Unto their losses twenty thousand crowns;
Another dowry to another daughter,
For she is changed, as she had never been.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I will win my wager better yet
And show more sign of her obedience,
Her new-built virtue and obedience.
See where she comes and brings your froward wives
As prisoners to her womanly persuasion.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Re-enter KATHARINA, with BIANCA and Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Katharina, that cap of yours becomes you not:
Off with that bauble, throw it under-foot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Lord, let me never have a cause to sigh,
Till I be brought to such a silly pass!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: Fie! what a foolish duty call you this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: I would your duty were as foolish too:
The wisdom of your duty, fair Bianca,
Hath cost me an hundred crowns since supper-time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BIANCA
SPEECH.LINE: The more fool you, for laying on my duty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Katharina, I charge thee, tell these headstrong women
What duty they do owe their lords and husbands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, you're mocking: we will have no telling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, I say; and first begin with her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Widow
SPEECH.LINE: She shall not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: I say she shall: and first begin with her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: KATHARINA
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie! unknit that threatening unkind brow,
And dart not scornful glances from those eyes,
To wound thy lord, thy king, thy governor:
It blots thy beauty as frosts do bite the meads,
Confounds thy fame as whirlwinds shake fair buds,
And in no sense is meet or amiable.
A woman moved is like a fountain troubled,
Muddy, ill-seeming, thick, bereft of beauty;
And while it is so, none so dry or thirsty
Will deign to sip or touch one drop of it.
Thy husband is thy lord, thy life, thy keeper,
Thy head, thy sovereign; one that cares for thee,
And for thy maintenance commits his body
To painful labour both by sea and land,
To watch the night in storms, the day in cold,
Whilst thou liest warm at home, secure and safe;
And craves no other tribute at thy hands
But love, fair looks and true obedience;
Too little payment for so great a debt.
Such duty as the subject owes the prince
Even such a woman oweth to her husband;
And when she is froward, peevish, sullen, sour,
And not obedient to his honest will,
What is she but a foul contending rebel
And graceless traitor to her loving lord?
I am ashamed that women are so simple
To offer war where they should kneel for peace;
Or seek for rule, supremacy and sway,
When they are bound to serve, love and obey.
Why are our bodies soft and weak and smooth,
Unapt to toil and trouble in the world,
But that our soft conditions and our hearts
Should well agree with our external parts?
Come, come, you froward and unable worms!
My mind hath been as big as one of yours,
My heart as great, my reason haply more,
To bandy word for word and frown for frown;
But now I see our lances are but straws,
Our strength as weak, our weakness past compare,
That seeming to be most which we indeed least are.
Then vail your stomachs, for it is no boot,
And place your hands below your husband's foot:
In token of which duty, if he please,
My hand is ready; may it do him ease.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Why, there's a wench! Come on, and kiss me, Kate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: Well, go thy ways, old lad; for thou shalt ha't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VINCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a good hearing when children are toward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: But a harsh hearing when women are froward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PETRUCHIO
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Kate, we'll to bed.
We three are married, but you two are sped.
'Twas I won the wager, though you hit the white;
And, being a winner, God give you good night!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIO
SPEECH.LINE: Now, go thy ways; thou hast tamed a curst shrew.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCENTIO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a wonder, by your leave, she will be tamed so.

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: PROSPERO, the right Duke of Milan.
ANTONIO, his brother, the usurping Duke of Milan.
FERDINAND, son to the King of Naples.
CALIBAN, a savage and deformed Slave.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE A ship at Sea: an island.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. On a ship at sea: a tempestuous noise of thunder and lightning heard.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter a Master and a Boatswain

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Master
SPEECH.LINE: Boatswain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Here, master: what cheer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Master
SPEECH.LINE: Good, speak to the mariners: fall to't, yarely,
or we run ourselves aground: bestir, bestir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Heigh, my hearts! cheerly, cheerly, my hearts!
yare, yare! Take in the topsail. Tend to the
master's whistle. Blow, till thou burst thy wind,
if room enough!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter ALONSO, SEBASTIAN, ANTONIO, FERDINAND, GONZALO, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: Good boatswain, have care. Where's the master?
Play the men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: I pray now, keep below.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Where is the master, boatswain?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Do you not hear him? You mar our labour: keep your
cabins: you do assist the storm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good, be patient.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: When the sea is. Hence! What cares these roarers
for the name of king? To cabin: silence! trouble us not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: Good, yet remember whom thou hast aboard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: None that I more love than myself. You are a
counsellor; if you can command these elements to
silence, and work the peace of the present, we will
not hand a rope more; use your authority: if you
cannot, give thanks you have lived so long, and make
yourself ready in your cabin for the mischance of
the hour, if it so hap. Cheerly, good hearts! Out
of our way, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: I have great comfort from this fellow: methinks he
hath no drowning mark upon him; his complexion is
perfect gallows. Stand fast, good Fate, to his
hanging: make the rope of his destiny our cable,
for our own doth little advantage. If he be not
born to be hanged, our case is miserable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Down with the topmast! yare! lower, lower! Bring
her to try with main-course.
A plague upon this howling! they are louder than
the weather or our office.
Yet again! what do you here? Shall we give o'er
and drown? Have you a mind to sink?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: A pox o' your throat, you bawling, blasphemous,
incharitable dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Work you then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Hang, cur! hang, you whoreson, insolent noisemaker!
We are less afraid to be drowned than thou art.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll warrant him for drowning; though the ship were
no stronger than a nutshell and as leaky as an
unstanched wench.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: Lay her a-hold, a-hold! set her two courses off to
sea again; lay her off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Mariners
SPEECH.LINE: All lost! to prayers, to prayers! all lost!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: What, must our mouths be cold?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: The king and prince at prayers! let's assist them,
For our case is as theirs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: I'm out of patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: We are merely cheated of our lives by drunkards:
This wide-chapp'd rascal--would thou mightst lie drowning
The washing of ten tides!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: He'll be hang'd yet,
Though every drop of water swear against it
And gape at widest to glut him.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: A confused noise within: 'Mercy on us!'-- 'We split, we split!'--'Farewell, my wife and children!'-- 'Farewell, brother!'--'We split, we split, we split!'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Let's all sink with the king.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Let's take leave of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: Now would I give a thousand furlongs of sea for an
acre of barren ground, long heath, brown furze, any
thing. The wills above be done! but I would fain
die a dry death.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The island. Before PROSPERO'S cell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: If by your art, my dearest father, you have
Put the wild waters in this roar, allay them.
The sky, it seems, would pour down stinking pitch,
But that the sea, mounting to the welkin's cheek,
Dashes the fire out. O, I have suffered
With those that I saw suffer: a brave vessel,
Who had, no doubt, some noble creature in her,
Dash'd all to pieces. O, the cry did knock
Against my very heart. Poor souls, they perish'd.
Had I been any god of power, I would
Have sunk the sea within the earth or ere
It should the good ship so have swallow'd and
The fraughting souls within her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Be collected:
No more amazement: tell your piteous heart
There's no harm done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, woe the day!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: No harm.
I have done nothing but in care of thee,
Of thee, my dear one, thee, my daughter, who
Art ignorant of what thou art, nought knowing
Of whence I am, nor that I am more better
Than Prospero, master of a full poor cell,
And thy no greater father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: More to know
Did never meddle with my thoughts.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis time
I should inform thee farther. Lend thy hand,
And pluck my magic garment from me. So:
Lie there, my art. Wipe thou thine eyes; have comfort.
The direful spectacle of the wreck, which touch'd
The very virtue of compassion in thee,
I have with such provision in mine art
So safely ordered that there is no soul--
No, not so much perdition as an hair
Betid to any creature in the vessel
Which thou heard'st cry, which thou saw'st sink. Sit down;
For thou must now know farther.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: You have often
Begun to tell me what I am, but stopp'd
And left me to a bootless inquisition,
Concluding 'Stay: not yet.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: The hour's now come;
The very minute bids thee ope thine ear;
Obey and be attentive. Canst thou remember
A time before we came unto this cell?
I do not think thou canst, for then thou wast not
Out three years old.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Certainly, sir, I can.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: By what? by any other house or person?
Of any thing the image tell me that
Hath kept with thy remembrance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis far off
And rather like a dream than an assurance
That my remembrance warrants. Had I not
Four or five women once that tended me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hadst, and more, Miranda. But how is it
That this lives in thy mind? What seest thou else
In the dark backward and abysm of time?
If thou remember'st aught ere thou camest here,
How thou camest here thou mayst.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: But that I do not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Twelve year since, Miranda, twelve year since,
Thy father was the Duke of Milan and
A prince of power.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, are not you my father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thy mother was a piece of virtue, and
She said thou wast my daughter; and thy father
Was Duke of Milan; and thou his only heir
And princess no worse issued.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O the heavens!
What foul play had we, that we came from thence?
Or blessed was't we did?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Both, both, my girl:
By foul play, as thou say'st, were we heaved thence,
But blessedly holp hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, my heart bleeds
To think o' the teen that I have turn'd you to,
Which is from my remembrance! Please you, farther.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: My brother and thy uncle, call'd Antonio--
I pray thee, mark me--that a brother should
Be so perfidious!--he whom next thyself
Of all the world I loved and to him put
The manage of my state; as at that time
Through all the signories it was the first
And Prospero the prime duke, being so reputed
In dignity, and for the liberal arts
Without a parallel; those being all my study,
The government I cast upon my brother
And to my state grew stranger, being transported
And rapt in secret studies. Thy false uncle--
Dost thou attend me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, most heedfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Being once perfected how to grant suits,
How to deny them, who to advance and who
To trash for over-topping, new created
The creatures that were mine, I say, or changed 'em,
Or else new form'd 'em; having both the key
Of officer and office, set all hearts i' the state
To what tune pleased his ear; that now he was
The ivy which had hid my princely trunk,
And suck'd my verdure out on't. Thou attend'st not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, good sir, I do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, mark me.
I, thus neglecting worldly ends, all dedicated
To closeness and the bettering of my mind
With that which, but by being so retired,
O'er-prized all popular rate, in my false brother
Awaked an evil nature; and my trust,
Like a good parent, did beget of him
A falsehood in its contrary as great
As my trust was; which had indeed no limit,
A confidence sans bound. He being thus lorded,
Not only with what my revenue yielded,
But what my power might else exact, like one
Who having into truth, by telling of it,
Made such a sinner of his memory,
To credit his own lie, he did believe
He was indeed the duke; out o' the substitution
And executing the outward face of royalty,
With all prerogative: hence his ambition growing--
Dost thou hear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Your tale, sir, would cure deafness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: To have no screen between this part he play'd
And him he play'd it for, he needs will be
Absolute Milan. Me, poor man, my library
Was dukedom large enough: of temporal royalties
He thinks me now incapable; confederates--
So dry he was for sway--wi' the King of Naples
To give him annual tribute, do him homage,
Subject his coronet to his crown and bend
The dukedom yet unbow'd--alas, poor Milan!--
To most ignoble stooping.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O the heavens!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Mark his condition and the event; then tell me
If this might be a brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: I should sin
To think but nobly of my grandmother:
Good wombs have borne bad sons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Now the condition.
The King of Naples, being an enemy
To me inveterate, hearkens my brother's suit;
Which was, that he, in lieu o' the premises
Of homage and I know not how much tribute,
Should presently extirpate me and mine
Out of the dukedom and confer fair Milan
With all the honours on my brother: whereon,
A treacherous army levied, one midnight
Fated to the purpose did Antonio open
The gates of Milan, and, i' the dead of darkness,
The ministers for the purpose hurried thence
Me and thy crying self.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Alack, for pity!
I, not remembering how I cried out then,
Will cry it o'er again: it is a hint
That wrings mine eyes to't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Hear a little further
And then I'll bring thee to the present business
Which now's upon's; without the which this story
Were most impertinent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore did they not
That hour destroy us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Well demanded, wench:
My tale provokes that question. Dear, they durst not,
So dear the love my people bore me, nor set
A mark so bloody on the business, but
With colours fairer painted their foul ends.
In few, they hurried us aboard a bark,
Bore us some leagues to sea; where they prepared
A rotten carcass of a boat, not rigg'd,
Nor tackle, sail, nor mast; the very rats
Instinctively had quit it: there they hoist us,
To cry to the sea that roar'd to us, to sigh
To the winds whose pity, sighing back again,
Did us but loving wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Alack, what trouble
Was I then to you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: O, a cherubim
Thou wast that did preserve me. Thou didst smile.
Infused with a fortitude from heaven,
When I have deck'd the sea with drops full salt,
Under my burthen groan'd; which raised in me
An undergoing stomach, to bear up
Against what should ensue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: How came we ashore?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: By Providence divine.
Some food we had and some fresh water that
A noble Neapolitan, Gonzalo,
Out of his charity, being then appointed
Master of this design, did give us, with
Rich garments, linens, stuffs and necessaries,
Which since have steaded much; so, of his gentleness,
Knowing I loved my books, he furnish'd me
From mine own library with volumes that
I prize above my dukedom.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Would I might
But ever see that man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Now I arise:
Sit still, and hear the last of our sea-sorrow.
Here in this island we arrived; and here
Have I, thy schoolmaster, made thee more profit
Than other princesses can that have more time
For vainer hours and tutors not so careful.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Heavens thank you for't! And now, I pray you, sir,
For still 'tis beating in my mind, your reason
For raising this sea-storm?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Know thus far forth.
By accident most strange, bountiful Fortune,
Now my dear lady, hath mine enemies
Brought to this shore; and by my prescience
I find my zenith doth depend upon
A most auspicious star, whose influence
If now I court not but omit, my fortunes
Will ever after droop. Here cease more questions:
Thou art inclined to sleep; 'tis a good dulness,
And give it way: I know thou canst not choose.
Come away, servant, come. I am ready now.
Approach, my Ariel, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: All hail, great master! grave sir, hail! I come
To answer thy best pleasure; be't to fly,
To swim, to dive into the fire, to ride
On the curl'd clouds, to thy strong bidding task
Ariel and all his quality.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Hast thou, spirit,
Perform'd to point the tempest that I bade thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: To every article.
I boarded the king's ship; now on the beak,
Now in the waist, the deck, in every cabin,
I flamed amazement: sometime I'ld divide,
And burn in many places; on the topmast,
The yards and bowsprit, would I flame distinctly,
Then meet and join. Jove's lightnings, the precursors
O' the dreadful thunder-claps, more momentary
And sight-outrunning were not; the fire and cracks
Of sulphurous roaring the most mighty Neptune
Seem to besiege and make his bold waves tremble,
Yea, his dread trident shake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: My brave spirit!
Who was so firm, so constant, that this coil
Would not infect his reason?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Not a soul
But felt a fever of the mad and play'd
Some tricks of desperation. All but mariners
Plunged in the foaming brine and quit the vessel,
Then all afire with me: the king's son, Ferdinand,
With hair up-staring,--then like reeds, not hair,--
Was the first man that leap'd; cried, 'Hell is empty
And all the devils are here.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Why that's my spirit!
But was not this nigh shore?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Close by, my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: But are they, Ariel, safe?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Not a hair perish'd;
On their sustaining garments not a blemish,
But fresher than before: and, as thou badest me,
In troops I have dispersed them 'bout the isle.
The king's son have I landed by himself;
Whom I left cooling of the air with sighs
In an odd angle of the isle and sitting,
His arms in this sad knot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Of the king's ship
The mariners say how thou hast disposed
And all the rest o' the fleet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Safely in harbour
Is the king's ship; in the deep nook, where once
Thou call'dst me up at midnight to fetch dew
From the still-vex'd Bermoothes, there she's hid:
The mariners all under hatches stow'd;
Who, with a charm join'd to their suffer'd labour,
I have left asleep; and for the rest o' the fleet
Which I dispersed, they all have met again
And are upon the Mediterranean flote,
Bound sadly home for Naples,
Supposing that they saw the king's ship wreck'd
And his great person perish.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Ariel, thy charge
Exactly is perform'd: but there's more work.
What is the time o' the day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Past the mid season.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: At least two glasses. The time 'twixt six and now
Must by us both be spent most preciously.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Is there more toil? Since thou dost give me pains,
Let me remember thee what thou hast promised,
Which is not yet perform'd me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: How now? moody?
What is't thou canst demand?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: My liberty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Before the time be out? no more!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee,
Remember I have done thee worthy service;
Told thee no lies, made thee no mistakings, served
Without or grudge or grumblings: thou didst promise
To bate me a full year.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou forget
From what a torment I did free thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou dost, and think'st it much to tread the ooze
Of the salt deep,
To run upon the sharp wind of the north,
To do me business in the veins o' the earth
When it is baked with frost.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: I do not, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou liest, malignant thing! Hast thou forgot
The foul witch Sycorax, who with age and envy
Was grown into a hoop? hast thou forgot her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast. Where was she born? speak; tell me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, in Argier.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: O, was she so? I must
Once in a month recount what thou hast been,
Which thou forget'st. This damn'd witch Sycorax,
For mischiefs manifold and sorceries terrible
To enter human hearing, from Argier,
Thou know'st, was banish'd: for one thing she did
They would not take her life. Is not this true?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: This blue-eyed hag was hither brought with child
And here was left by the sailors. Thou, my slave,
As thou report'st thyself, wast then her servant;
And, for thou wast a spirit too delicate
To act her earthy and abhorr'd commands,
Refusing her grand hests, she did confine thee,
By help of her more potent ministers
And in her most unmitigable rage,
Into a cloven pine; within which rift
Imprison'd thou didst painfully remain
A dozen years; within which space she died
And left thee there; where thou didst vent thy groans
As fast as mill-wheels strike. Then was this island--
Save for the son that she did litter here,
A freckled whelp hag-born--not honour'd with
A human shape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, Caliban her son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Dull thing, I say so; he, that Caliban
Whom now I keep in service. Thou best know'st
What torment I did find thee in; thy groans
Did make wolves howl and penetrate the breasts
Of ever angry bears: it was a torment
To lay upon the damn'd, which Sycorax
Could not again undo: it was mine art,
When I arrived and heard thee, that made gape
The pine and let thee out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: If thou more murmur'st, I will rend an oak
And peg thee in his knotty entrails till
Thou hast howl'd away twelve winters.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, master;
I will be correspondent to command
And do my spiriting gently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Do so, and after two days
I will discharge thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: That's my noble master!
What shall I do? say what; what shall I do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Go make thyself like a nymph o' the sea: be subject
To no sight but thine and mine, invisible
To every eyeball else. Go take this shape
And hither come in't: go, hence with diligence!
Awake, dear heart, awake! thou hast slept well; Awake!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: The strangeness of your story put
Heaviness in me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Shake it off. Come on;
We'll visit Caliban my slave, who never
Yields us kind answer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a villain, sir,
I do not love to look on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: But, as 'tis,
We cannot miss him: he does make our fire,
Fetch in our wood and serves in offices
That profit us. What, ho! slave! Caliban!
Thou earth, thou! speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: Within There's wood enough within.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Come forth, I say! there's other business for thee:
Come, thou tortoise! when?
Fine apparition! My quaint Ariel,
Hark in thine ear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: My lord it shall be done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Thou poisonous slave, got by the devil himself
Upon thy wicked dam, come forth!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: As wicked dew as e'er my mother brush'd
With raven's feather from unwholesome fen
Drop on you both! a south-west blow on ye
And blister you all o'er!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: For this, be sure, to-night thou shalt have cramps,
Side-stitches that shall pen thy breath up; urchins
Shall, for that vast of night that they may work,
All exercise on thee; thou shalt be pinch'd
As thick as honeycomb, each pinch more stinging
Than bees that made 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: I must eat my dinner.
This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother,
Which thou takest from me. When thou camest first,
Thou strokedst me and madest much of me, wouldst give me
Water with berries in't, and teach me how
To name the bigger light, and how the less,
That burn by day and night: and then I loved thee
