My dukedom of thee, which perforce, I know,
Thou must restore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: If thou be'st Prospero,
Give us particulars of thy preservation;
How thou hast met us here, who three hours since
Were wreck'd upon this shore; where I have lost--
How sharp the point of this remembrance is!--
My dear son Ferdinand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: I am woe for't, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: Irreparable is the loss, and patience
Says it is past her cure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: I rather think
You have not sought her help, of whose soft grace
For the like loss I have her sovereign aid
And rest myself content.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: You the like loss!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: As great to me as late; and, supportable
To make the dear loss, have I means much weaker
Than you may call to comfort you, for I
Have lost my daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: A daughter?
O heavens, that they were living both in Naples,
The king and queen there! that they were, I wish
Myself were mudded in that oozy bed
Where my son lies. When did you lose your daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: In this last tempest. I perceive these lords
At this encounter do so much admire
That they devour their reason and scarce think
Their eyes do offices of truth, their words
Are natural breath: but, howsoe'er you have
Been justled from your senses, know for certain
That I am Prospero and that very duke
Which was thrust forth of Milan, who most strangely
Upon this shore, where you were wreck'd, was landed,
To be the lord on't. No more yet of this;
For 'tis a chronicle of day by day,
Not a relation for a breakfast nor
Befitting this first meeting. Welcome, sir;
This cell's my court: here have I few attendants
And subjects none abroad: pray you, look in.
My dukedom since you have given me again,
I will requite you with as good a thing;
At least bring forth a wonder, to content ye
As much as me my dukedom.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Here PROSPERO discovers FERDINAND and MIRANDA playing at chess

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet lord, you play me false.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: No, my dear'st love,
I would not for the world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, for a score of kingdoms you should wrangle,
And I would call it, fair play.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: If this prove
A vision of the Island, one dear son
Shall I twice lose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: A most high miracle!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Though the seas threaten, they are merciful;
I have cursed them without cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: Now all the blessings
Of a glad father compass thee about!
Arise, and say how thou camest here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MIRANDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, wonder!
How many goodly creatures are there here!
How beauteous mankind is! O brave new world,
That has such people in't!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis new to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: What is this maid with whom thou wast at play?
Your eld'st acquaintance cannot be three hours:
Is she the goddess that hath sever'd us,
And brought us thus together?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FERDINAND
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, she is mortal;
But by immortal Providence she's mine:
I chose her when I could not ask my father
For his advice, nor thought I had one. She
Is daughter to this famous Duke of Milan,
Of whom so often I have heard renown,
But never saw before; of whom I have
Received a second life; and second father
This lady makes him to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: I am hers:
But, O, how oddly will it sound that I
Must ask my child forgiveness!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: There, sir, stop:
Let us not burthen our remembrance with
A heaviness that's gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: I have inly wept,
Or should have spoke ere this. Look down, you god,
And on this couple drop a blessed crown!
For it is you that have chalk'd forth the way
Which brought us hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: I say, Amen, Gonzalo!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: Was Milan thrust from Milan, that his issue
Should become kings of Naples? O, rejoice
Beyond a common joy, and set it down
With gold on lasting pillars: In one voyage
Did Claribel her husband find at Tunis,
And Ferdinand, her brother, found a wife
Where he himself was lost, Prospero his dukedom
In a poor isle and all of us ourselves
When no man was his own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: To FERDINAND and MIRANDA Give me your hands:
Let grief and sorrow still embrace his heart
That doth not wish you joy!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: GONZALO
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so! Amen!
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Re-enter ARIEL, with the Master and Boatswain amazedly following
SPEECH.LINE: O, look, sir, look, sir! here is more of us:
I prophesied, if a gallows were on land,
This fellow could not drown. Now, blasphemy,
That swear'st grace o'erboard, not an oath on shore?
Hast thou no mouth by land? What is the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: The best news is, that we have safely found
Our king and company; the next, our ship--
Which, but three glasses since, we gave out split--
Is tight and yare and bravely rigg'd as when
We first put out to sea.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to PROSPERO Sir, all this service
Have I done since I went.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to ARIEL My tricksy spirit!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: These are not natural events; they strengthen
From strange to stranger. Say, how came you hither?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boatswain
SPEECH.LINE: If I did think, sir, I were well awake,
I'ld strive to tell you. We were dead of sleep,
And--how we know not--all clapp'd under hatches;
Where but even now with strange and several noises
Of roaring, shrieking, howling, jingling chains,
And more diversity of sounds, all horrible,
We were awaked; straightway, at liberty;
Where we, in all her trim, freshly beheld
Our royal, good and gallant ship, our master
Capering to eye her: on a trice, so please you,
Even in a dream, were we divided from them
And were brought moping hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ARIEL
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to PROSPERO Was't well done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to ARIEL Bravely, my diligence. Thou shalt be free.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: This is as strange a maze as e'er men trod
And there is in this business more than nature
Was ever conduct of: some oracle
Must rectify our knowledge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, my liege,
Do not infest your mind with beating on
The strangeness of this business; at pick'd leisure
Which shall be shortly, single I'll resolve you,
Which to you shall seem probable, of every
These happen'd accidents; till when, be cheerful
And think of each thing well.
Come hither, spirit:
Set Caliban and his companions free;
Untie the spell.
How fares my gracious sir?
There are yet missing of your company
Some few odd lads that you remember not.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter ARIEL, driving in CALIBAN, STEPHANO and TRINCULO, in their stolen apparel

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: Every man shift for all the rest, and
let no man take care for himself; for all is
but fortune. Coragio, bully-monster, coragio!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRINCULO
SPEECH.LINE: If these be true spies which I wear in my head,
here's a goodly sight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: O Setebos, these be brave spirits indeed!
How fine my master is! I am afraid
He will chastise me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha!
What things are these, my lord Antonio?
Will money buy 'em?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANTONIO
SPEECH.LINE: Very like; one of them
Is a plain fish, and, no doubt, marketable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Mark but the badges of these men, my lords,
Then say if they be true. This mis-shapen knave,
His mother was a witch, and one so strong
That could control the moon, make flows and ebbs,
And deal in her command without her power.
These three have robb'd me; and this demi-devil--
For he's a bastard one--had plotted with them
To take my life. Two of these fellows you
Must know and own; this thing of darkness!
Acknowledge mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: I shall be pinch'd to death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: Is not this Stephano, my drunken butler?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: He is drunk now: where had he wine?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: And Trinculo is reeling ripe: where should they
Find this grand liquor that hath gilded 'em?
How camest thou in this pickle?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TRINCULO
SPEECH.LINE: I have been in such a pickle since I
saw you last that, I fear me, will never out of
my bones: I shall not fear fly-blowing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, Stephano!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: O, touch me not; I am not Stephano, but a cramp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: You'ld be king o' the isle, sirrah?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: STEPHANO
SPEECH.LINE: I should have been a sore one then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: This is a strange thing as e'er I look'd on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: He is as disproportion'd in his manners
As in his shape. Go, sirrah, to my cell;
Take with you your companions; as you look
To have my pardon, trim it handsomely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALIBAN
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that I will; and I'll be wise hereafter
And seek for grace. What a thrice-double ass
Was I, to take this drunkard for a god
And worship this dull fool!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Go to; away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: Hence, and bestow your luggage where you found it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEBASTIAN
SPEECH.LINE: Or stole it, rather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I invite your highness and your train
To my poor cell, where you shall take your rest
For this one night; which, part of it, I'll waste
With such discourse as, I not doubt, shall make it
Go quick away; the story of my life
And the particular accidents gone by
Since I came to this isle: and in the morn
I'll bring you to your ship and so to Naples,
Where I have hope to see the nuptial
Of these our dear-beloved solemnized;
And thence retire me to my Milan, where
Every third thought shall be my grave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALONSO
SPEECH.LINE: I long
To hear the story of your life, which must
Take the ear strangely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROSPERO
SPEECH.LINE: I'll deliver all;
And promise you calm seas, auspicious gales
And sail so expeditious that shall catch
Your royal fleet far off.
My Ariel, chick,
That is thy charge: then to the elements
Be free, and fare thou well! Please you, draw near.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: [PROSPERO]
SPEECH.LINE: Now my charms are all o'erthrown,
And what strength I have's mine own,
Which is most faint: now, 'tis true,
I must be here confined by you,
Or sent to Naples. Let me not,
Since I have my dukedom got
And pardon'd the deceiver, dwell
In this bare island by your spell;
But release me from my bands
With the help of your good hands:
Gentle breath of yours my sails
Must fill, or else my project fails,
Which was to please. Now I want
Spirits to enforce, art to enchant,
And my ending is despair,
Unless I be relieved by prayer,
Which pierces so that it assaults
Mercy itself and frees all faults.
As you from crimes would pardon'd be,
Let your indulgence set me free.

PLAY.TITLE: The Life of Timon of Athens

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: VENTIDIUS, one of Timon's false friends.
Cupid and Amazons in the mask.
Other Lords, Senators, Officers, Soldiers, Banditti, and Attendants.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE Athens, and the neighbouring woods.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Athens. A hall in Timon's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter Poet, Painter, Jeweller, Merchant, and others, at several doors

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Good day, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: I am glad you're well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: I have not seen you long: how goes the world?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: It wears, sir, as it grows.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that's well known:
But what particular rarity? what strange,
Which manifold record not matches? See,
Magic of bounty! all these spirits thy power
Hath conjured to attend. I know the merchant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: I know them both; th' other's a jeweller.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'tis a worthy lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that's most fix'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: A most incomparable man, breathed, as it were,
To an untirable and continuate goodness:
He passes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller:
SPEECH.LINE: I have a jewel here--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: O, pray, let's see't: for the Lord Timon, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller:
SPEECH.LINE: If he will touch the estimate: but, for that--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Reciting to himself 'When we for recompense have
praised the vile,
It stains the glory in that happy verse
Which aptly sings the good.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a good form.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: And rich: here is a water, look ye.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: You are rapt, sir, in some work, some dedication
To the great lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: A thing slipp'd idly from me.
Our poesy is as a gum, which oozes
From whence 'tis nourish'd: the fire i' the flint
Shows not till it be struck; our gentle flame
Provokes itself and like the current flies
Each bound it chafes. What have you there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: A picture, sir. When comes your book forth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Upon the heels of my presentment, sir.
Let's see your piece.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis a good piece.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: So 'tis: this comes off well and excellent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: Indifferent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Admirable: how this grace
Speaks his own standing! what a mental power
This eye shoots forth! how big imagination
Moves in this lip! to the dumbness of the gesture
One might interpret.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: It is a pretty mocking of the life.
Here is a touch; is't good?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: I will say of it,
It tutors nature: artificial strife
Lives in these touches, livelier than life.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter certain Senators, and pass over

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: How this lord is follow'd!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: The senators of Athens: happy man!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: Look, more!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: You see this confluence, this great flood
of visitors.
I have, in this rough work, shaped out a man,
Whom this beneath world doth embrace and hug
With amplest entertainment: my free drift
Halts not particularly, but moves itself
In a wide sea of wax: no levell'd malice
Infects one comma in the course I hold;
But flies an eagle flight, bold and forth on,
Leaving no tract behind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: How shall I understand you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: I will unbolt to you.
You see how all conditions, how all minds,
As well of glib and slippery creatures as
Of grave and austere quality, tender down
Their services to Lord Timon: his large fortune
Upon his good and gracious nature hanging
Subdues and properties to his love and tendance
All sorts of hearts; yea, from the glass-faced flatterer
To Apemantus, that few things loves better
Than to abhor himself: even he drops down
The knee before him, and returns in peace
Most rich in Timon's nod.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: I saw them speak together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I have upon a high and pleasant hill
Feign'd Fortune to be throned: the base o' the mount
Is rank'd with all deserts, all kind of natures,
That labour on the bosom of this sphere
To propagate their states: amongst them all,
Whose eyes are on this sovereign lady fix'd,
One do I personate of Lord Timon's frame,
Whom Fortune with her ivory hand wafts to her;
Whose present grace to present slaves and servants
Translates his rivals.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis conceived to scope.
This throne, this Fortune, and this hill, methinks,
With one man beckon'd from the rest below,
Bowing his head against the sleepy mount
To climb his happiness, would be well express'd
In our condition.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, sir, but hear me on.
All those which were his fellows but of late,
Some better than his value, on the moment
Follow his strides, his lobbies fill with tendance,
Rain sacrificial whisperings in his ear,
Make sacred even his stirrup, and through him
Drink the free air.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, marry, what of these?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: When Fortune in her shift and change of mood
Spurns down her late beloved, all his dependants
Which labour'd after him to the mountain's top
Even on their knees and hands, let him slip down,
Not one accompanying his declining foot.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis common:
A thousand moral paintings I can show
That shall demonstrate these quick blows of Fortune's
More pregnantly than words. Yet you do well
To show Lord Timon that mean eyes have seen
The foot above the head.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Trumpets sound. Enter TIMON, addressing himself courteously to every suitor; a Messenger from VENTIDIUS talking with him; LUCILIUS and other servants following

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Imprison'd is he, say you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord: five talents is his debt,
His means most short, his creditors most strait:
Your honourable letter he desires
To those have shut him up; which failing,
Periods his comfort.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Noble Ventidius! Well;
I am not of that feather to shake off
My friend when he must need me. I do know him
A gentleman that well deserves a help:
Which he shall have: I'll pay the debt,
and free him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Your lordship ever binds him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Commend me to him: I will send his ransom;
And being enfranchised, bid him come to me.
'Tis not enough to help the feeble up,
But to support him after. Fare you well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: All happiness to your honour!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Timon, hear me speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Freely, good father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast a servant named Lucilius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I have so: what of him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Most noble Timon, call the man before thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Attends he here, or no? Lucilius!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here, at your lordship's service.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: This fellow here, Lord Timon, this thy creature,
By night frequents my house. I am a man
That from my first have been inclined to thrift;
And my estate deserves an heir more raised
Than one which holds a trencher.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Well; what further?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: One only daughter have I, no kin else,
On whom I may confer what I have got:
The maid is fair, o' the youngest for a bride,
And I have bred her at my dearest cost
In qualities of the best. This man of thine
Attempts her love: I prithee, noble lord,
Join with me to forbid him her resort;
Myself have spoke in vain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: The man is honest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore he will be, Timon:
His honesty rewards him in itself;
It must not bear my daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Does she love him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: She is young and apt:
Our own precedent passions do instruct us
What levity's in youth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: To LUCILIUS Love you the maid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good lord, and she accepts of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: If in her marriage my consent be missing,
I call the gods to witness, I will choose
Mine heir from forth the beggars of the world,
And dispossess her all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: How shall she be endow'd,
if she be mated with an equal husband?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Three talents on the present; in future, all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: This gentleman of mine hath served me long:
To build his fortune I will strain a little,
For 'tis a bond in men. Give him thy daughter:
What you bestow, in him I'll counterpoise,
And make him weigh with her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Old Athenian
SPEECH.LINE: Most noble lord,
Pawn me to this your honour, she is his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: My hand to thee; mine honour on my promise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Humbly I thank your lordship: never may
The state or fortune fall into my keeping,
Which is not owed to you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Vouchsafe my labour, and long live your lordship!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you; you shall hear from me anon:
Go not away. What have you there, my friend?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: A piece of painting, which I do beseech
Your lordship to accept.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Painting is welcome.
The painting is almost the natural man;
or since dishonour traffics with man's nature,
He is but outside: these pencill'd figures are
Even such as they give out. I like your work;
And you shall find I like it: wait attendance
Till you hear further from me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: The gods preserve ye!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Well fare you, gentleman: give me your hand;
We must needs dine together. Sir, your jewel
Hath suffer'd under praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: What, my lord! dispraise?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: A more satiety of commendations.
If I should pay you for't as 'tis extoll'd,
It would unclew me quite.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, 'tis rated
As those which sell would give: but you well know,
Things of like value differing in the owners
Are prized by their masters: believe't, dear lord,
You mend the jewel by the wearing it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Well mock'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord; he speaks the common tongue,
Which all men speak with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Look, who comes here: will you be chid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: We'll bear, with your lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: He'll spare none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow to thee, gentle Apemantus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Till I be gentle, stay thou for thy good morrow;
When thou art Timon's dog, and these knaves honest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Why dost thou call them knaves? thou know'st them not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Are they not Athenians?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Yes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then I repent not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Jeweller
SPEECH.LINE: You know me, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou know'st I do: I call'd thee by thy name.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art proud, Apemantus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Of nothing so much as that I am not like Timon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Whither art going?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: To knock out an honest Athenian's brains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: That's a deed thou'lt die for.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Right, if doing nothing be death by the law.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: How likest thou this picture, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: The best, for the innocence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Wrought he not well that painted it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He wrought better that made the painter; and yet
he's but a filthy piece of work.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Painter
SPEECH.LINE: You're a dog.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thy mother's of my generation: what's she, if I be a dog?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Wilt dine with me, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No; I eat not lords.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: An thou shouldst, thou 'ldst anger ladies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, they eat lords; so they come by great bellies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: That's a lascivious apprehension.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: So thou apprehendest it: take it for thy labour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: How dost thou like this jewel, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not so well as plain-dealing, which will not cost a
man a doit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What dost thou think 'tis worth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not worth my thinking. How now, poet!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: How now, philosopher!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou liest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Art not one?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Then I lie not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Art not a poet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: Yes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then thou liest: look in thy last work, where thou
hast feigned him a worthy fellow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Poet
SPEECH.LINE: That's not feigned; he is so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, he is worthy of thee, and to pay thee for thy
labour: he that loves to be flattered is worthy o'
the flatterer. Heavens, that I were a lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What wouldst do then, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: E'en as Apemantus does now; hate a lord with my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What, thyself?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: That I had no angry wit to be a lord.
Art not thou a merchant?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Apemantus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Traffic confound thee, if the gods will not!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Merchant
SPEECH.LINE: If traffic do it, the gods do it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Traffic's thy god; and thy god confound thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What trumpet's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis Alcibiades, and some twenty horse,
All of companionship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, entertain them; give them guide to us.
You must needs dine with me: go not you hence
Till I have thank'd you: when dinner's done,
Show me this piece. I am joyful of your sights.
Most welcome, sir!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: So, so, there!
Aches contract and starve your supple joints!
That there should be small love 'mongst these
sweet knaves,
And all this courtesy! The strain of man's bred out
Into baboon and monkey.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, you have saved my longing, and I feed
Most hungerly on your sight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Right welcome, sir!
Ere we depart, we'll share a bounteous time
In different pleasures. Pray you, let us in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: What time o' day is't, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Time to be honest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: That time serves still.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: The more accursed thou, that still omitt'st it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art going to Lord Timon's feast?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, to see meat fill knaves and wine heat fools.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Fare thee well, fare thee well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art a fool to bid me farewell twice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Why, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Shouldst have kept one to thyself, for I mean to
give thee none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Hang thyself!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, I will do nothing at thy bidding: make thy
requests to thy friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Away, unpeaceable dog, or I'll spurn thee hence!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I will fly, like a dog, the heels o' the ass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: He's opposite to humanity. Come, shall we in,
And taste Lord Timon's bounty? he outgoes
The very heart of kindness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: He pours it out; Plutus, the god of gold,
Is but his steward: no meed, but he repays
Sevenfold above itself; no gift to him,
But breeds the giver a return exceeding
All use of quittance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: The noblest mind he carries
That ever govern'd man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Long may he live in fortunes! Shall we in?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I'll keep you company.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A banqueting-room in Timon's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Hautboys playing loud music. A great banquet served in; FLAVIUS and others attending; then enter TIMON, ALCIBIADES, Lords, Senators, and VENTIDIUS. Then comes, dropping, after all, APEMANTUS, discontentedly, like himself

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VENTIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Most honour'd Timon,
It hath pleased the gods to remember my father's age,
And call him to long peace.
He is gone happy, and has left me rich:
Then, as in grateful virtue I am bound
To your free heart, I do return those talents,
Doubled with thanks and service, from whose help
I derived liberty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: O, by no means,
Honest Ventidius; you mistake my love:
I gave it freely ever; and there's none
Can truly say he gives, if he receives:
If our betters play at that game, we must not dare
To imitate them; faults that are rich are fair.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VENTIDIUS
SPEECH.LINE: A noble spirit!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, my lords,
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: They all stand ceremoniously looking on TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Ceremony was but devised at first
To set a gloss on faint deeds, hollow welcomes,
Recanting goodness, sorry ere 'tis shown;
But where there is true friendship, there needs none.
Pray, sit; more welcome are ye to my fortunes
Than my fortunes to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, we always have confess'd it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ho, ho, confess'd it! hang'd it, have you not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: O, Apemantus, you are welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No;
You shall not make me welcome:
I come to have thee thrust me out of doors.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, thou'rt a churl; ye've got a humour there
Does not become a man: 'tis much to blame.
They say, my lords, 'ira furor brevis est;' but yond
man is ever angry. Go, let him have a table by
himself, for he does neither affect company, nor is
he fit for't, indeed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let me stay at thine apperil, Timon: I come to
observe; I give thee warning on't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I take no heed of thee; thou'rt an Athenian,
therefore welcome: I myself would have no power;
prithee, let my meat make thee silent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I scorn thy meat; 'twould choke me, for I should
ne'er flatter thee. O you gods, what a number of
men eat Timon, and he sees 'em not! It grieves me
to see so many dip their meat in one man's blood;
and all the madness is, he cheers them up too.
I wonder men dare trust themselves with men:
Methinks they should invite them without knives;
Good for their meat, and safer for their lives.
There's much example for't; the fellow that sits
next him now, parts bread with him, pledges the
breath of him in a divided draught, is the readiest
man to kill him: 't has been proved. If I were a
huge man, I should fear to drink at meals;
Lest they should spy my windpipe's dangerous notes:
Great men should drink with harness on their throats.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, in heart; and let the health go round.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Let it flow this way, my good lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Flow this way! A brave fellow! he keeps his tides
well. Those healths will make thee and thy state
look ill, Timon. Here's that which is too weak to
be a sinner, honest water, which ne'er left man i' the mire:
This and my food are equals; there's no odds:
Feasts are too proud to give thanks to the gods.
Apemantus' grace.
Immortal gods, I crave no pelf;
I pray for no man but myself:
Grant I may never prove so fond,
To trust man on his oath or bond;
Or a harlot, for her weeping;
Or a dog, that seems a-sleeping:
Or a keeper with my freedom;
Or my friends, if I should need 'em.
Amen. So fall to't:
Rich men sin, and I eat root.
Much good dich thy good heart, Apemantus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Captain Alcibiades, your heart's in the field now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: My heart is ever at your service, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You had rather be at a breakfast of enemies than a
dinner of friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: So the were bleeding-new, my lord, there's no meat
like 'em: I could wish my best friend at such a feast.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Would all those fatterers were thine enemies then,
that then thou mightst kill 'em and bid me to 'em!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Might we but have that happiness, my lord, that you
would once use our hearts, whereby we might express
some part of our zeals, we should think ourselves
for ever perfect.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: O, no doubt, my good friends, but the gods
themselves have provided that I shall have much help
from you: how had you been my friends else? why
have you that charitable title from thousands, did
not you chiefly belong to my heart? I have told
more of you to myself than you can with modesty
speak in your own behalf; and thus far I confirm
you. O you gods, think I, what need we have any
friends, if we should ne'er have need of 'em? they
were the most needless creatures living, should we
ne'er have use for 'em, and would most resemble
sweet instruments hung up in cases that keep their
sounds to themselves. Why, I have often wished
myself poorer, that I might come nearer to you. We
are born to do benefits: and what better or
properer can we can our own than the riches of our
friends? O, what a precious comfort 'tis, to have
so many, like brothers, commanding one another's
fortunes! O joy, e'en made away ere 't can be born!
Mine eyes cannot hold out water, methinks: to
forget their faults, I drink to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou weepest to make them drink, Timon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Joy had the like conception in our eyes
And at that instant like a babe sprung up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ho, ho! I laugh to think that babe a bastard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I promise you, my lord, you moved me much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Much!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What means that trump?
How now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Please you, my lord, there are certain
ladies most desirous of admittance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Ladies! what are their wills?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: There comes with them a forerunner, my lord, which
bears that office, to signify their pleasures.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I pray, let them be admitted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Cupid
SPEECH.LINE: Hail to thee, worthy Timon, and to all
That of his bounties taste! The five best senses
Acknowledge thee their patron; and come freely
To gratulate thy plenteous bosom: th' ear,
Taste, touch and smell, pleased from thy tale rise;
They only now come but to feast thine eyes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: They're welcome all; let 'em have kind admittance:
Music, make their welcome!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: You see, my lord, how ample you're beloved.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Music. Re-enter Cupid with a mask of Ladies as Amazons, with lutes in their hands, dancing and playing

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hoy-day, what a sweep of vanity comes this way!
They dance! they are mad women.
Like madness is the glory of this life.
As this pomp shows to a little oil and root.
We make ourselves fools, to disport ourselves;
And spend our flatteries, to drink those men
Upon whose age we void it up again,
With poisonous spite and envy.
Who lives that's not depraved or depraves?
Who dies, that bears not one spurn to their graves
Of their friends' gift?
I should fear those that dance before me now
Would one day stamp upon me: 't has been done;
Men shut their doors against a setting sun.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: The Lords rise from table, with much adoring of TIMON; and to show their loves, each singles out an Amazon, and all dance, men with women, a lofty strain or two to the hautboys, and cease

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You have done our pleasures much grace, fair ladies,
Set a fair fashion on our entertainment,
Which was not half so beautiful and kind;
You have added worth unto 't and lustre,
And entertain'd me with mine own device;
I am to thank you for 't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lady
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, you take us even at the best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, for the worst is filthy; and would not hold
taking, I doubt me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Ladies, there is an idle banquet attends you:
Please you to dispose yourselves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Ladies
SPEECH.LINE: Most thankfully, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Flavius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: The little casket bring me hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, my lord. More jewels yet!
There is no crossing him in 's humour;
Else I should tell him,--well, i' faith I should,
When all's spent, he 'ld be cross'd then, an he could.
'Tis pity bounty had not eyes behind,
That man might ne'er be wretched for his mind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Where be our men?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Here, my lord, in readiness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: Our horses!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: O my friends,
I have one word to say to you: look you, my good lord,
I must entreat you, honour me so much
As to advance this jewel; accept it and wear it,
Kind my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: I am so far already in your gifts,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: So are we all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, there are certain nobles of the senate
Newly alighted, and come to visit you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: They are fairly welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I beseech your honour,
Vouchsafe me a word; it does concern you near.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Near! why then, another time I'll hear thee:
I prithee, let's be provided to show them
entertainment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside I scarce know how.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Servant
SPEECH.LINE: May it please your honour, Lord Lucius,
Out of his free love, hath presented to you
Four milk-white horses, trapp'd in silver.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I shall accept them fairly; let the presents
Be worthily entertain'd.
How now! what news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Please you, my lord, that honourable
gentleman, Lord Lucullus, entreats your company
to-morrow to hunt with him, and has sent your honour
two brace of greyhounds.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I'll hunt with him; and let them be received,
Not without fair reward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside What will this come to?
He commands us to provide, and give great gifts,
And all out of an empty coffer:
Nor will he know his purse, or yield me this,
To show him what a beggar his heart is,
Being of no power to make his wishes good:
His promises fly so beyond his state
That what he speaks is all in debt; he owes
For every word: he is so kind that he now
Pays interest for 't; his land's put to their books.
Well, would I were gently put out of office
Before I were forced out!
Happier is he that has no friend to feed
Than such that do e'en enemies exceed.
I bleed inwardly for my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You do yourselves
Much wrong, you bate too much of your own merits:
Here, my lord, a trifle of our love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: With more than common thanks I will receive it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Lord
SPEECH.LINE: O, he's the very soul of bounty!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: And now I remember, my lord, you gave
Good words the other day of a bay courser
I rode on: it is yours, because you liked it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: O, I beseech you, pardon me, my lord, in that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You may take my word, my lord; I know, no man
Can justly praise but what he does affect:
I weigh my friend's affection with mine own;
I'll tell you true. I'll call to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Lords
SPEECH.LINE: O, none so welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I take all and your several visitations
So kind to heart, 'tis not enough to give;
Methinks, I could deal kingdoms to my friends,
And ne'er be weary. Alcibiades,
Thou art a soldier, therefore seldom rich;
It comes in charity to thee: for all thy living
Is 'mongst the dead, and all the lands thou hast
Lie in a pitch'd field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, defiled land, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: We are so virtuously bound--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: And so
Am I to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Lord
SPEECH.LINE: So infinitely endear'd--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: All to you. Lights, more lights!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Lord
SPEECH.LINE: The best of happiness,
Honour and fortunes, keep with you, Lord Timon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Ready for his friends.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all but APEMANTUS and TIMON

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What a coil's here!
Serving of becks and jutting-out of bums!
I doubt whether their legs be worth the sums
That are given for 'em. Friendship's full of dregs:
Methinks, false hearts should never have sound legs,
Thus honest fools lay out their wealth on court'sies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Apemantus, if thou wert not sullen, I would be
good to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, I'll nothing: for if I should be bribed too,
there would be none left to rail upon thee, and then
thou wouldst sin the faster. Thou givest so long,
Timon, I fear me thou wilt give away thyself in
paper shortly: what need these feasts, pomps and
vain-glories?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, an you begin to rail on society once, I am
sworn not to give regard to you. Farewell; and come
with better music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: So:
Thou wilt not hear me now; thou shalt not then:
I'll lock thy heaven from thee.
O, that men's ears should be
To counsel deaf, but not to flattery!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A Senator's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter Senator, with papers in his hand

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Senator
SPEECH.LINE: And late, five thousand: to Varro and to Isidore
He owes nine thousand; besides my former sum,
Which makes it five and twenty. Still in motion
Of raging waste? It cannot hold; it will not.
If I want gold, steal but a beggar's dog,
And give it Timon, why, the dog coins gold.
If I would sell my horse, and buy twenty more
Better than he, why, give my horse to Timon,
Ask nothing, give it him, it foals me, straight,
And able horses. No porter at his gate,
But rather one that smiles and still invites
All that pass by. It cannot hold: no reason
Can found his state in safety. Caphis, ho!
Caphis, I say!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sir; what is your pleasure?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Get on your cloak, and haste you to Lord Timon;
Importune him for my moneys; be not ceased
With slight denial, nor then silenced when--
'Commend me to your master'--and the cap
Plays in the right hand, thus: but tell him,
My uses cry to me, I must serve my turn
Out of mine own; his days and times are past
And my reliances on his fracted dates
Have smit my credit: I love and honour him,
But must not break my back to heal his finger;
Immediate are my needs, and my relief
Must not be toss'd and turn'd to me in words,
But find supply immediate. Get you gone:
Put on a most importunate aspect,
A visage of demand; for, I do fear,
When every feather sticks in his own wing,
Lord Timon will be left a naked gull,
Which flashes now a phoenix. Get you gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: I go, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Senator
SPEECH.LINE: 'I go, sir!'--Take the bonds along with you,
And have the dates in contempt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: I will, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Go.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. A hall in Timon's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FLAVIUS, with many bills in his hand

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No care, no stop! so senseless of expense,
That he will neither know how to maintain it,
Nor cease his flow of riot: takes no account
How things go from him, nor resumes no care
Of what is to continue: never mind
Was to be so unwise, to be so kind.
What shall be done? he will not hear, till feel:
I must be round with him, now he comes from hunting.
Fie, fie, fie, fie!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter CAPHIS, and the Servants of Isidore and Varro

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Good even, Varro: what,
You come for money?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Is't not your business too?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: It is: and yours too, Isidore?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Isidore's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: It is so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Would we were all discharged!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I fear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes the lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: So soon as dinner's done, we'll forth again,
My Alcibiades. With me? what is your will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, here is a note of certain dues.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Dues! Whence are you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Of Athens here, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Go to my steward.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Please it your lordship, he hath put me off
To the succession of new days this month:
My master is awaked by great occasion
To call upon his own, and humbly prays you
That with your other noble parts you'll suit
In giving him his right.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Mine honest friend,
I prithee, but repair to me next morning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good my lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Contain thyself, good friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: One Varro's servant, my good lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Isidore's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: From Isidore;
He humbly prays your speedy payment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: If you did know, my lord, my master's wants--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas due on forfeiture, my lord, six weeks And past.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Isidore's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Your steward puts me off, my lord;
And I am sent expressly to your lordship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Give me breath.
I do beseech you, good my lords, keep on;
I'll wait upon you instantly.
Come hither: pray you,
How goes the world, that I am thus encounter'd
With clamourous demands of date-broke bonds,
And the detention of long-since-due debts,
Against my honour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Please you, gentlemen,
The time is unagreeable to this business:
Your importunacy cease till after dinner,
That I may make his lordship understand
Wherefore you are not paid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Do so, my friends. See them well entertain'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray, draw near.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, stay, here comes the fool with Apemantus:
let's ha' some sport with 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Hang him, he'll abuse us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Isidore's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: A plague upon him, dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: How dost, fool?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Dost dialogue with thy shadow?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I speak not to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No,'tis to thyself.
Come away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Isidore's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: There's the fool hangs on your back already.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, thou stand'st single, thou'rt not on him yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CAPHIS
SPEECH.LINE: Where's the fool now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He last asked the question. Poor rogues, and
usurers' men! bawds between gold and want!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: What are we, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Asses.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: Why?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: That you ask me what you are, and do not know
yourselves. Speak to 'em, fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: How do you, gentlemen?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: Gramercies, good fool: how does your mistress?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: She's e'en setting on water to scald such chickens
as you are. Would we could see you at Corinth!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good! gramercy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: Look you, here comes my mistress' page.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Page
SPEECH.LINE: To the Fool Why, how now, captain! what do you
in this wise company? How dost thou, Apemantus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Would I had a rod in my mouth, that I might answer
thee profitably.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Page
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, Apemantus, read me the superscription of
these letters: I know not which is which.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Canst not read?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Page
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: There will little learning die then, that day thou
art hanged. This is to Lord Timon; this to
Alcibiades. Go; thou wast born a bastard, and thou't
die a bawd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Page
SPEECH.LINE: Thou wast whelped a dog, and thou shalt famish a
dog's death. Answer not; I am gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: E'en so thou outrunnest grace. Fool, I will go with
you to Lord Timon's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: Will you leave me there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: If Timon stay at home. You three serve three usurers?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; would they served us!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: So would I,--as good a trick as ever hangman served thief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: Are you three usurers' men?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: I think no usurer but has a fool to his servant: my
mistress is one, and I am her fool. When men come
to borrow of your masters, they approach sadly, and
go away merry; but they enter my mistress' house
merrily, and go away sadly: the reason of this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I could render one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do it then, that we may account thee a whoremaster
and a knave; which not-withstanding, thou shalt be
no less esteemed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: What is a whoremaster, fool?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: A fool in good clothes, and something like thee.
'Tis a spirit: sometime't appears like a lord;
sometime like a lawyer; sometime like a philosopher,
with two stones moe than's artificial one: he is
very often like a knight; and, generally, in all
shapes that man goes up and down in from fourscore
to thirteen, this spirit walks in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art not altogether a fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: Nor thou altogether a wise man: as much foolery as
I have, so much wit thou lackest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: That answer might have become Apemantus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All Servants
SPEECH.LINE: Aside, aside; here comes Lord Timon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: APEMANTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come with me, fool, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Fool
SPEECH.LINE: I do not always follow lover, elder brother and
woman; sometime the philosopher.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, walk near: I'll speak with you anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You make me marvel: wherefore ere this time
Had you not fully laid my state before me,
That I might so have rated my expense,
As I had leave of means?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: You would not hear me,
At many leisures I proposed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Go to:
Perchance some single vantages you took.
When my indisposition put you back:
And that unaptness made your minister,
Thus to excuse yourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O my good lord,
At many times I brought in my accounts,
Laid them before you; you would throw them off,
And say, you found them in mine honesty.
When, for some trifling present, you have bid me
Return so much, I have shook my head and wept;
Yea, 'gainst the authority of manners, pray'd you
To hold your hand more close: I did endure
Not seldom, nor no slight cheques, when I have
Prompted you in the ebb of your estate
And your great flow of debts. My loved lord,
Though you hear now, too late--yet now's a time--
The greatest of your having lacks a half
To pay your present debts.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Let all my land be sold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis all engaged, some forfeited and gone;
And what remains will hardly stop the mouth
Of present dues: the future comes apace:
What shall defend the interim? and at length
How goes our reckoning?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: To Lacedaemon did my land extend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O my good lord, the world is but a word:
Were it all yours to give it in a breath,
How quickly were it gone!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You tell me true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If you suspect my husbandry or falsehood,
Call me before the exactest auditors
And set me on the proof. So the gods bless me,
When all our offices have been oppress'd
With riotous feeders, when our vaults have wept
With drunken spilth of wine, when every room
Hath blazed with lights and bray'd with minstrelsy,
I have retired me to a wasteful cock,
And set mine eyes at flow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Heavens, have I said, the bounty of this lord!
How many prodigal bits have slaves and peasants
This night englutted! Who is not Timon's?
What heart, head, sword, force, means, but is
Lord Timon's?
Great Timon, noble, worthy, royal Timon!
Ah, when the means are gone that buy this praise,
The breath is gone whereof this praise is made:
Feast-won, fast-lost; one cloud of winter showers,
These flies are couch'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Come, sermon me no further:
No villanous bounty yet hath pass'd my heart;
Unwisely, not ignobly, have I given.
Why dost thou weep? Canst thou the conscience lack,
To think I shall lack friends? Secure thy heart;
If I would broach the vessels of my love,
And try the argument of hearts by borrowing,
Men and men's fortunes could I frankly use
As I can bid thee speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Assurance bless your thoughts!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: And, in some sort, these wants of mine are crown'd,
That I account them blessings; for by these
Shall I try friends: you shall perceive how you
Mistake my fortunes; I am wealthy in my friends.
Within there! Flaminius! Servilius!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FLAMINIUS, SERVILIUS, and other Servants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servants
SPEECH.LINE: My lord? my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I will dispatch you severally; you to Lord Lucius;
to Lord Lucullus you: I hunted with his honour
to-day: you, to Sempronius: commend me to their
loves, and, I am proud, say, that my occasions have
found time to use 'em toward a supply of money: let
the request be fifty talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: As you have said, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Lord Lucius and Lucullus? hum!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Go you, sir, to the senators--
Of whom, even to the state's best health, I have
Deserved this hearing--bid 'em send o' the instant
A thousand talents to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have been bold--
For that I knew it the most general way--
To them to use your signet and your name;
But they do shake their heads, and I am here
No richer in return.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Is't true? can't be?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: They answer, in a joint and corporate voice,
That now they are at fall, want treasure, cannot
Do what they would; are sorry--you are honourable,--
But yet they could have wish'd--they know not--
Something hath been amiss--a noble nature
May catch a wrench--would all were well--'tis pity;--
And so, intending other serious matters,
After distasteful looks and these hard fractions,
With certain half-caps and cold-moving nods
They froze me into silence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: You gods, reward them!
Prithee, man, look cheerly. These old fellows
Have their ingratitude in them hereditary:
Their blood is caked, 'tis cold, it seldom flows;
'Tis lack of kindly warmth they are not kind;
And nature, as it grows again toward earth,
Is fashion'd for the journey, dull and heavy.
Go to Ventidius.
Prithee, be not sad,
Thou art true and honest; ingeniously I speak.
No blame belongs to thee.
Ventidius lately
Buried his father; by whose death he's stepp'd
Into a great estate: when he was poor,
Imprison'd and in scarcity of friends,
I clear'd him with five talents: greet him from me;
Bid him suppose some good necessity
Touches his friend, which craves to be remember'd
With those five talents.
That had, give't these fellows
To whom 'tis instant due. Ne'er speak, or think,
That Timon's fortunes 'mong his friends can sink.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I would I could not think it: that thought is
bounty's foe;
Being free itself, it thinks all others so.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A room in Lucullus' house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: FLAMINIUS waiting. Enter a Servant to him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I have told my lord of you; he is coming down to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Here's my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside One of Lord Timon's men? a gift, I
warrant. Why, this hits right; I dreamt of a silver
basin and ewer to-night. Flaminius, honest
Flaminius; you are very respectively welcome, sir.
Fill me some wine.
And how does that honourable, complete, free-hearted
gentleman of Athens, thy very bountiful good lord
and master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: His health is well sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am right glad that his health is well, sir: and
what hast thou there under thy cloak, pretty Flaminius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, nothing but an empty box, sir; which, in my
lord's behalf, I come to entreat your honour to
supply; who, having great and instant occasion to
use fifty talents, hath sent to your lordship to
furnish him, nothing doubting your present
assistance therein.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: La, la, la, la! 'nothing doubting,' says he? Alas,
good lord! a noble gentleman 'tis, if he would not
keep so good a house. Many a time and often I ha'
dined with him, and told him on't, and come again to
supper to him, of purpose to have him spend less,
and yet he would embrace no counsel, take no warning
by my coming. Every man has his fault, and honesty
is his: I ha' told him on't, but I could ne'er get
him from't.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Please your lordship, here is the wine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Flaminius, I have noted thee always wise. Here's to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your lordship speaks your pleasure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have observed thee always for a towardly prompt
spirit--give thee thy due--and one that knows what
belongs to reason; and canst use the time well, if
the time use thee well: good parts in thee.
Get you gone, sirrah.
Draw nearer, honest Flaminius. Thy lord's a
bountiful gentleman: but thou art wise; and thou
knowest well enough, although thou comest to me,
that this is no time to lend money, especially upon
bare friendship, without security. Here's three
solidares for thee: good boy, wink at me, and say
thou sawest me not. Fare thee well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible the world should so much differ,
And we alive that lived? Fly, damned baseness,
To him that worships thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCULLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! now I see thou art a fool, and fit for thy master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: May these add to the number that may scald thee!
Let moulten coin be thy damnation,
Thou disease of a friend, and not himself!
Has friendship such a faint and milky heart,
It turns in less than two nights? O you gods,
I feel master's passion! this slave,
Unto his honour, has my lord's meat in him:
Why should it thrive and turn to nutriment,
When he is turn'd to poison?
O, may diseases only work upon't!
And, when he's sick to death, let not that part of nature
Which my lord paid for, be of any power
To expel sickness, but prolong his hour!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A public place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who, the Lord Timon? he is my very good friend, and
an honourable gentleman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: We know him for no less, though we are but strangers
to him. But I can tell you one thing, my lord, and
which I hear from common rumours: now Lord Timon's
happy hours are done and past, and his estate
shrinks from him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, no, do not believe it; he cannot want for money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: But believe you this, my lord, that, not long ago,
one of his men was with the Lord Lucullus to borrow
so many talents, nay, urged extremely for't and
showed what necessity belonged to't, and yet was denied.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: I tell you, denied, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What a strange case was that! now, before the gods,
I am ashamed on't. Denied that honourable man!
there was very little honour showed in't. For my own
part, I must needs confess, I have received some
small kindnesses from him, as money, plate, jewels
and such-like trifles, nothing comparing to his;
yet, had he mistook him and sent to me, I should
ne'er have denied his occasion so many talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: See, by good hap, yonder's my lord;
I have sweat to see his honour. My honoured lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Servilius! you are kindly met, sir. Fare thee well:
commend me to thy honourable virtuous lord, my very
exquisite friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: May it please your honour, my lord hath sent--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! what has he sent? I am so much endeared to
that lord; he's ever sending: how shall I thank
him, thinkest thou? And what has he sent now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Has only sent his present occasion now, my lord;
requesting your lordship to supply his instant use
with so many talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know his lordship is but merry with me;
He cannot want fifty five hundred talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: But in the mean time he wants less, my lord.
If his occasion were not virtuous,
I should not urge it half so faithfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou speak seriously, Servilius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon my soul,'tis true, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What a wicked beast was I to disfurnish myself
against such a good time, when I might ha' shown
myself honourable! how unluckily it happened, that I
should purchase the day before for a little part,
and undo a great deal of honoured! Servilius, now,
before the gods, I am not able to do,--the more
beast, I say:--I was sending to use Lord Timon
myself, these gentlemen can witness! but I would
not, for the wealth of Athens, I had done't now.
Commend me bountifully to his good lordship; and I
hope his honour will conceive the fairest of me,
because I have no power to be kind: and tell him
this from me, I count it one of my greatest
afflictions, say, that I cannot pleasure such an
honourable gentleman. Good Servilius, will you
befriend me so far, as to use mine own words to him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, sir, I shall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll look you out a good turn, Servilius.
True as you said, Timon is shrunk indeed;
And he that's once denied will hardly speed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: Do you observe this, Hostilius?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, too well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this is the world's soul; and just of the
same piece
Is every flatterer's spirit. Who can call him
His friend that dips in the same dish? for, in
My knowing, Timon has been this lord's father,
And kept his credit with his purse,
Supported his estate; nay, Timon's money
Has paid his men their wages: he ne'er drinks,
But Timon's silver treads upon his lip;
And yet--O, see the monstrousness of man
When he looks out in an ungrateful shape!--
He does deny him, in respect of his,
What charitable men afford to beggars.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Third Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: Religion groans at it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Stranger
SPEECH.LINE: For mine own part,
I never tasted Timon in my life,
Nor came any of his bounties over me,
To mark me for his friend; yet, I protest,
For his right noble mind, illustrious virtue
And honourable carriage,
Had his necessity made use of me,
I would have put my wealth into donation,
And the best half should have return'd to him,
So much I love his heart: but, I perceive,
Men must learn now with pity to dispense;
For policy sits above conscience.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A room in Sempronius' house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter SEMPRONIUS, and a Servant of TIMON's

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEMPRONIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Must he needs trouble me in 't,--hum!--'bove
all others?
He might have tried Lord Lucius or Lucullus;
And now Ventidius is wealthy too,
Whom he redeem'd from prison: all these
Owe their estates unto him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,
They have all been touch'd and found base metal, for
They have au denied him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SEMPRONIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How! have they denied him?
Has Ventidius and Lucullus denied him?
And does he send to me? Three? hum!
It shows but little love or judgment in him:
Must I be his last refuge! His friends, like
physicians,
Thrive, give him over: must I take the cure upon me?
Has much disgraced me in't; I'm angry at him,
That might have known my place: I see no sense for't,
But his occasion might have woo'd me first;
For, in my conscience, I was the first man
That e'er received gift from him:
And does he think so backwardly of me now,
That I'll requite its last? No:
So it may prove an argument of laughter
To the rest, and 'mongst lords I be thought a fool.
I'ld rather than the worth of thrice the sum,
Had sent to me first, but for my mind's sake;
I'd such a courage to do him good. But now return,
And with their faint reply this answer join;
Who bates mine honour shall not know my coin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Excellent! Your lordship's a goodly villain. The
devil knew not what he did when he made man
politic; he crossed himself by 't: and I cannot
think but, in the end, the villainies of man will
set him clear. How fairly this lord strives to
appear foul! takes virtuous copies to be wicked,
like those that under hot ardent zeal would set
whole realms on fire: Of such a nature is his
politic love.
This was my lord's best hope; now all are fled,
Save only the gods: now his friends are dead,
Doors, that were ne'er acquainted with their wards
Many a bounteous year must be employ'd
Now to guard sure their master.
And this is all a liberal course allows;
Who cannot keep his wealth must keep his house.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. The same. A hall in Timon's house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter two Servants of Varro, and the Servant of LUCIUS, meeting TITUS, HORTENSIUS, and other Servants of TIMON's creditors, waiting his coming out

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Well met; good morrow, Titus and Hortensius.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: The like to you kind Varro.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucius!
What, do we meet together?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and I think
One business does command us all; for mine Is money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: So is theirs and ours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: And Sir Philotus too!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good day at once.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, good brother.
What do you think the hour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Labouring for nine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: So much?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is not my lord seen yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Not yet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder on't; he was wont to shine at seven.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but the days are wax'd shorter with him:
You must consider that a prodigal course
Is like the sun's; but not, like his, recoverable.
I fear 'tis deepest winter in Lord Timon's purse;
That is one may reach deep enough, and yet
Find little.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am of your fear for that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll show you how to observe a strange event.
Your lord sends now for money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Most true, he does.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: And he wears jewels now of Timon's gift,
For which I wait for money.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is against my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Mark, how strange it shows,
Timon in this should pay more than he owes:
And e'en as if your lord should wear rich jewels,
And send for money for 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'm weary of this charge, the gods can witness:
I know my lord hath spent of Timon's wealth,
And now ingratitude makes it worse than stealth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, mine's three thousand crowns: what's yours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Five thousand mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis much deep: and it should seem by the sun,
Your master's confidence was above mine;
Else, surely, his had equall'd.
Enter FLAMINIUS.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: One of Lord Timon's men.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Flaminius! Sir, a word: pray, is my lord ready to
come forth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, indeed, he is not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: We attend his lordship; pray, signify so much.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I need not tell him that; he knows you are too diligent.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter FLAVIUS in a cloak, muffled

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! is not that his steward muffled so?
He goes away in a cloud: call him, call him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Second Servant
SPEECH.LINE: By your leave, sir,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What do ye ask of me, my friend?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: We wait for certain money here, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay,
If money were as certain as your waiting,
'Twere sure enough.
Why then preferr'd you not your sums and bills,
When your false masters eat of my lord's meat?
Then they could smile and fawn upon his debts
And take down the interest into their
gluttonous maws.
You do yourselves but wrong to stir me up;
Let me pass quietly:
Believe 't, my lord and I have made an end;
I have no more to reckon, he to spend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but this answer will not serve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If 'twill not serve,'tis not so base as you;
For you serve knaves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: How! what does his cashiered worship mutter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Second Servant
SPEECH.LINE: No matter what; he's poor, and that's revenge
enough. Who can speak broader than he that has no
house to put his head in? such may rail against
great buildings.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, here's Servilius; now we shall know some answer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If I might beseech you, gentlemen, to repair some
other hour, I should derive much from't; for,
take't of my soul, my lord leans wondrously to
discontent: his comfortable temper has forsook him;
he's much out of health, and keeps his chamber.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Many do keep their chambers are not sick:
And, if it be so far beyond his health,
Methinks he should the sooner pay his debts,
And make a clear way to the gods.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SERVILIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good gods!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: We cannot take this for answer, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAMINIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Within Servilius, help! My lord! my lord!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TIMON, in a rage, FLAMINIUS following

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What, are my doors opposed against my passage?
Have I been ever free, and must my house
Be my retentive enemy, my gaol?
The place which I have feasted, does it now,
Like all mankind, show me an iron heart?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Put in now, Titus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, here is my bill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Here's mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And mine, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Both Varro's Servants
SPEECH.LINE: And ours, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PHILOTUS
SPEECH.LINE: All our bills.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Knock me down with 'em: cleave me to the girdle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, my lord,-

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Cut my heart in sums.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mine, fifty talents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Tell out my blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Lucilius' Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Five thousand crowns, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Five thousand drops pays that.
What yours?--and yours?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's First Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Varro's Second Servant
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Tear me, take me, and the gods fall upon you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HORTENSIUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Faith, I perceive our masters may throw their caps
at their money: these debts may well be called
desperate ones, for a madman owes 'em.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: They have e'en put my breath from me, the slaves.
Creditors? devils!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My dear lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: What if it should be so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have it so. My steward!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: So fitly? Go, bid all my friends again,
Lucius, Lucullus, and Sempronius:
All, sirrah, all:
I'll once more feast the rascals.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: FLAVIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O my lord,
You only speak from your distracted soul;
There is not so much left, to furnish out
A moderate table.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TIMON
SPEECH.LINE: Be't not in thy care; go,
I charge thee, invite them all: let in the tide
Of knaves once more; my cook and I'll provide.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The same. The senate-house. The Senate sitting.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, you have my voice to it; the fault's
Bloody; 'tis necessary he should die:
Nothing emboldens sin so much as mercy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Most true; the law shall bruise him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: Honour, health, and compassion to the senate!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: Now, captain?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: I am an humble suitor to your virtues;
For pity is the virtue of the law,
And none but tyrants use it cruelly.
It pleases time and fortune to lie heavy
Upon a friend of mine, who, in hot blood,
Hath stepp'd into the law, which is past depth
To those that, without heed, do plunge into 't.
He is a man, setting his fate aside,
Of comely virtues:
Nor did he soil the fact with cowardice--
An honour in him which buys out his fault--
But with a noble fury and fair spirit,
Seeing his reputation touch'd to death,
He did oppose his foe:
And with such sober and unnoted passion
He did behave his anger, ere 'twas spent,
As if he had but proved an argument.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You undergo too strict a paradox,
Striving to make an ugly deed look fair:
Your words have took such pains as if they labour'd
To bring manslaughter into form and set quarrelling
Upon the head of valour; which indeed
Is valour misbegot and came into the world
When sects and factions were newly born:
He's truly valiant that can wisely suffer
The worst that man can breathe, and make his wrongs
His outsides, to wear them like his raiment,
carelessly,
And ne'er prefer his injuries to his heart,
To bring it into danger.
If wrongs be evils and enforce us kill,
What folly 'tis to hazard life for ill!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You cannot make gross sins look clear:
To revenge is no valour, but to bear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: My lords, then, under favour, pardon me,
If I speak like a captain.
Why do fond men expose themselves to battle,
And not endure all threats? sleep upon't,
And let the foes quietly cut their throats,
Without repugnancy? If there be
Such valour in the bearing, what make we
Abroad? why then, women are more valiant
That stay at home, if bearing carry it,
And the ass more captain than the lion, the felon
Loaden with irons wiser than the judge,
If wisdom be in suffering. O my lords,
As you are great, be pitifully good:
Who cannot condemn rashness in cold blood?
To kill, I grant, is sin's extremest gust;
But, in defence, by mercy, 'tis most just.
To be in anger is impiety;
But who is man that is not angry?
Weigh but the crime with this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: You breathe in vain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: In vain! his service done
At Lacedaemon and Byzantium
Were a sufficient briber for his life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: First Senator
SPEECH.LINE: What's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALCIBIADES
SPEECH.LINE: I say, my lords, he has done fair service,
And slain in fight many of your enemies:
How full of valour did he bear himself
In the last conflict, and made plenteous wounds!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Second Senator
SPEECH.LINE: He has made too much plenty with 'em;
He's a sworn rioter: he has a sin that often
Drowns him, and takes his valour prisoner:
If there were no foes, that were enough
To overcome him: in that beastly fury
