SPEECH.LINE: O monstrous! what reproachful words are these?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: But go thy ways; go, give that changing piece
To him that flourish'd for her with his sword
A valiant son-in-law thou shalt enjoy;
One fit to bandy with thy lawless sons,
To ruffle in the commonwealth of Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: These words are razors to my wounded heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: And therefore, lovely Tamora, queen of Goths,
That like the stately Phoebe 'mongst her nymphs
Dost overshine the gallant'st dames of Rome,
If thou be pleased with this my sudden choice,
Behold, I choose thee, Tamora, for my bride,
And will create thee empress of Rome,
Speak, Queen of Goths, dost thou applaud my choice?
And here I swear by all the Roman gods,
Sith priest and holy water are so near
And tapers burn so bright and every thing
In readiness for Hymenaeus stand,
I will not re-salute the streets of Rome,
Or climb my palace, till from forth this place
I lead espoused my bride along with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: And here, in sight of heaven, to Rome I swear,
If Saturnine advance the Queen of Goths,
She will a handmaid be to his desires,
A loving nurse, a mother to his youth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ascend, fair queen, Pantheon. Lords, accompany
Your noble emperor and his lovely bride,
Sent by the heavens for Prince Saturnine,
Whose wisdom hath her fortune conquered:
There shall we consummate our spousal rites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am not bid to wait upon this bride.
Titus, when wert thou wont to walk alone,
Dishonour'd thus, and challenged of wrongs?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter MARCUS, LUCIUS, QUINTUS, and MARTIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Titus, see, O, see what thou hast done!
In a bad quarrel slain a virtuous son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, foolish tribune, no; no son of mine,
Nor thou, nor these, confederates in the deed
That hath dishonour'd all our family;
Unworthy brother, and unworthy sons!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: But let us give him burial, as becomes;
Give Mutius burial with our brethren.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Traitors, away! he rests not in this tomb:
This monument five hundred years hath stood,
Which I have sumptuously re-edified:
Here none but soldiers and Rome's servitors
Repose in fame; none basely slain in brawls:
Bury him where you can; he comes not here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, this is impiety in you:
My nephew Mutius' deeds do plead for him
He must be buried with his brethren.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And shall, or him we will accompany.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'And shall!' what villain was it that spake
that word?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: He that would vouch it in any place but here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, would you bury him in my despite?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, noble Titus, but entreat of thee
To pardon Mutius and to bury him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Marcus, even thou hast struck upon my crest,
And, with these boys, mine honour thou hast wounded:
My foes I do repute you every one;
So, trouble me no more, but get you gone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: He is not with himself; let us withdraw.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not I, till Mutius' bones be buried.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: MARCUS and the Sons of TITUS kneel

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Brother, for in that name doth nature plead,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Father, and in that name doth nature speak,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Speak thou no more, if all the rest will speed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Renowned Titus, more than half my soul,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Dear father, soul and substance of us all,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Suffer thy brother Marcus to inter
His noble nephew here in virtue's nest,
That died in honour and Lavinia's cause.
Thou art a Roman; be not barbarous:
The Greeks upon advice did bury Ajax
That slew himself; and wise Laertes' son
Did graciously plead for his funerals:
Let not young Mutius, then, that was thy joy
Be barr'd his entrance here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Rise, Marcus, rise.
The dismall'st day is this that e'er I saw,
To be dishonour'd by my sons in Rome!
Well, bury him, and bury me the next.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: MUTIUS is put into the tomb

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: There lie thy bones, sweet Mutius, with thy friends,
Till we with trophies do adorn thy tomb.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: All
SPEECH.LINE: Kneeling No man shed tears for noble Mutius;
He lives in fame that died in virtue's cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, to step out of these dreary dumps,
How comes it that the subtle Queen of Goths
Is of a sudden thus advanced in Rome?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I know not, Marcus; but I know it is,
Whether by device or no, the heavens can tell:
Is she not then beholding to the man
That brought her for this high good turn so far?
Yes, and will nobly him remunerate.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Flourish. Re-enter, from one side, SATURNINUS attended, TAMORA, DEMETRIUS, CHIRON and AARON; from the other, BASSIANUS, LAVINIA, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: So, Bassianus, you have play'd your prize:
God give you joy, sir, of your gallant bride!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: And you of yours, my lord! I say no more,
Nor wish no less; and so, I take my leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Traitor, if Rome have law or we have power,
Thou and thy faction shall repent this rape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Rape, call you it, my lord, to seize my own,
My truth-betrothed love and now my wife?
But let the laws of Rome determine all;
Meanwhile I am possess'd of that is mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis good, sir: you are very short with us;
But, if we live, we'll be as sharp with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, what I have done, as best I may,
Answer I must and shall do with my life.
Only thus much I give your grace to know:
By all the duties that I owe to Rome,
This noble gentleman, Lord Titus here,
Is in opinion and in honour wrong'd;
That in the rescue of Lavinia
With his own hand did slay his youngest son,
In zeal to you and highly moved to wrath
To be controll'd in that he frankly gave:
Receive him, then, to favor, Saturnine,
That hath express'd himself in all his deeds
A father and a friend to thee and Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prince Bassianus, leave to plead my deeds:
'Tis thou and those that have dishonour'd me.
Rome and the righteous heavens be my judge,
How I have loved and honour'd Saturnine!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: My worthy lord, if ever Tamora
Were gracious in those princely eyes of thine,
Then hear me speak in indifferently for all;
And at my suit, sweet, pardon what is past.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, madam! be dishonour'd openly,
And basely put it up without revenge?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Not so, my lord; the gods of Rome forfend
I should be author to dishonour you!
But on mine honour dare I undertake
For good Lord Titus' innocence in all;
Whose fury not dissembled speaks his griefs:
Then, at my suit, look graciously on him;
Lose not so noble a friend on vain suppose,
Nor with sour looks afflict his gentle heart.
Aside to SATURNINUS My lord, be ruled by me,
be won at last;
Dissemble all your griefs and discontents:
You are but newly planted in your throne;
Lest, then, the people, and patricians too,
Upon a just survey, take Titus' part,
And so supplant you for ingratitude,
Which Rome reputes to be a heinous sin,
Yield at entreats; and then let me alone:
I'll find a day to massacre them all
And raze their faction and their family,
The cruel father and his traitorous sons,
To whom I sued for my dear son's life,
And make them know what 'tis to let a queen
Kneel in the streets and beg for grace in vain.
Come, come, sweet emperor; come, Andronicus;
Take up this good old man, and cheer the heart
That dies in tempest of thy angry frown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Rise, Titus, rise; my empress hath prevail'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank your majesty, and her, my lord:
These words, these looks, infuse new life in me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Titus, I am incorporate in Rome,
A Roman now adopted happily,
And must advise the emperor for his good.
This day all quarrels die, Andronicus;
And let it be mine honour, good my lord,
That I have reconciled your friends and you.
For you, Prince Bassianus, I have pass'd
My word and promise to the emperor,
That you will be more mild and tractable.
And fear not lords, and you, Lavinia;
By my advice, all humbled on your knees,
You shall ask pardon of his majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We do, and vow to heaven and to his highness,
That what we did was mildly as we might,
Tendering our sister's honour and our own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: That, on mine honour, here I do protest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away, and talk not; trouble us no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, nay, sweet emperor, we must all be friends:
The tribune and his nephews kneel for grace;
I will not be denied: sweet heart, look back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Marcus, for thy sake and thy brother's here,
And at my lovely Tamora's entreats,
I do remit these young men's heinous faults: Stand up.
Lavinia, though you left me like a churl,
I found a friend, and sure as death I swore
I would not part a bachelor from the priest.
Come, if the emperor's court can feast two brides,
You are my guest, Lavinia, and your friends.
This day shall be a love-day, Tamora.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: To-morrow, an it please your majesty
To hunt the panther and the hart with me,
With horn and hound we'll give your grace bonjour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Be it so, Titus, and gramercy too.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Rome. Before the Palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Now climbeth Tamora Olympus' top,
Safe out of fortune's shot; and sits aloft,
Secure of thunder's crack or lightning flash;
Advanced above pale envy's threatening reach.
As when the golden sun salutes the morn,
And, having gilt the ocean with his beams,
Gallops the zodiac in his glistering coach,
And overlooks the highest-peering hills;
So Tamora:
Upon her wit doth earthly honour wait,
And virtue stoops and trembles at her frown.
Then, Aaron, arm thy heart, and fit thy thoughts,
To mount aloft with thy imperial mistress,
And mount her pitch, whom thou in triumph long
Hast prisoner held, fetter'd in amorous chains
And faster bound to Aaron's charming eyes
Than is Prometheus tied to Caucasus.
Away with slavish weeds and servile thoughts!
I will be bright, and shine in pearl and gold,
To wait upon this new-made empress.
To wait, said I? to wanton with this queen,
This goddess, this Semiramis, this nymph,
This siren, that will charm Rome's Saturnine,
And see his shipwreck and his commonweal's.
Holloa! what storm is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Chiron, thy years want wit, thy wit wants edge,
And manners, to intrude where I am graced;
And may, for aught thou know'st, affected be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Demetrius, thou dost over-ween in all;
And so in this, to bear me down with braves.
'Tis not the difference of a year or two
Makes me less gracious or thee more fortunate:
I am as able and as fit as thou
To serve, and to deserve my mistress' grace;
And that my sword upon thee shall approve,
And plead my passions for Lavinia's love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Clubs, clubs! these lovers will not keep
the peace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, boy, although our mother, unadvised,
Gave you a dancing-rapier by your side,
Are you so desperate grown, to threat your friends?
Go to; have your lath glued within your sheath
Till you know better how to handle it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Meanwhile, sir, with the little skill I have,
Full well shalt thou perceive how much I dare.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, boy, grow ye so brave?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Coming forward Why, how now, lords!
So near the emperor's palace dare you draw,
And maintain such a quarrel openly?
Full well I wot the ground of all this grudge:
I would not for a million of gold
The cause were known to them it most concerns;
Nor would your noble mother for much more
Be so dishonour'd in the court of Rome.
For shame, put up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not I, till I have sheathed
My rapier in his bosom and withal
Thrust these reproachful speeches down his throat
That he hath breathed in my dishonour here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: For that I am prepared and full resolved.
Foul-spoken coward, that thunder'st with thy tongue,
And with thy weapon nothing darest perform!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Away, I say!
Now, by the gods that warlike Goths adore,
This petty brabble will undo us all.
Why, lords, and think you not how dangerous
It is to jet upon a prince's right?
What, is Lavinia then become so loose,
Or Bassianus so degenerate,
That for her love such quarrels may be broach'd
Without controlment, justice, or revenge?
Young lords, beware! and should the empress know
This discord's ground, the music would not please.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I care not, I, knew she and all the world:
I love Lavinia more than all the world.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Youngling, learn thou to make some meaner choice:
Lavinia is thine elder brother's hope.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, are ye mad? or know ye not, in Rome
How furious and impatient they be,
And cannot brook competitors in love?
I tell you, lords, you do but plot your deaths
By this device.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron, a thousand deaths
Would I propose to achieve her whom I love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: To achieve her! how?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why makest thou it so strange?
She is a woman, therefore may be woo'd;
She is a woman, therefore may be won;
She is Lavinia, therefore must be loved.
What, man! more water glideth by the mill
Than wots the miller of; and easy it is
Of a cut loaf to steal a shive, we know:
Though Bassianus be the emperor's brother.
Better than he have worn Vulcan's badge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Ay, and as good as Saturninus may.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then why should he despair that knows to court it
With words, fair looks and liberality?
What, hast not thou full often struck a doe,
And borne her cleanly by the keeper's nose?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, it seems, some certain snatch or so
Would serve your turns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, so the turn were served.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron, thou hast hit it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Would you had hit it too!
Then should not we be tired with this ado.
Why, hark ye, hark ye! and are you such fools
To square for this? would it offend you, then
That both should speed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, not me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nor me, so I were one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: For shame, be friends, and join for that you jar:
'Tis policy and stratagem must do
That you affect; and so must you resolve,
That what you cannot as you would achieve,
You must perforce accomplish as you may.
Take this of me: Lucrece was not more chaste
Than this Lavinia, Bassianus' love.
A speedier course than lingering languishment
Must we pursue, and I have found the path.
My lords, a solemn hunting is in hand;
There will the lovely Roman ladies troop:
The forest walks are wide and spacious;
And many unfrequented plots there are
Fitted by kind for rape and villany:
Single you thither then this dainty doe,
And strike her home by force, if not by words:
This way, or not at all, stand you in hope.
Come, come, our empress, with her sacred wit
To villany and vengeance consecrate,
Will we acquaint with all that we intend;
And she shall file our engines with advice,
That will not suffer you to square yourselves,
But to your wishes' height advance you both.
The emperor's court is like the house of Fame,
The palace full of tongues, of eyes, and ears:
The woods are ruthless, dreadful, deaf, and dull;
There speak, and strike, brave boys, and take
your turns;
There serve your lusts, shadow'd from heaven's eye,
And revel in Lavinia's treasury.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Thy counsel, lad, smells of no cowardice,

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sit fas aut nefas, till I find the stream
To cool this heat, a charm to calm these fits.
Per Styga, per manes vehor.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A forest near Rome. Horns and cry of hounds heard.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TITUS ANDRONICUS, with Hunters, &c., MARCUS, LUCIUS, QUINTUS, and MARTIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: The hunt is up, the morn is bright and grey,
The fields are fragrant and the woods are green:
Uncouple here and let us make a bay
And wake the emperor and his lovely bride
And rouse the prince and ring a hunter's peal,
That all the court may echo with the noise.
Sons, let it be your charge, as it is ours,
To attend the emperor's person carefully:
I have been troubled in my sleep this night,
But dawning day new comfort hath inspired.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: A cry of hounds and horns, winded in a peal. Enter SATURNINUS, TAMORA, BASSIANUS, LAVINIA, DEMETRIUS, CHIRON, and Attendants
SPEECH.LINE: Many good morrows to your majesty;
Madam, to you as many and as good:
I promised your grace a hunter's peal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: And you have rung it lustily, my lord;
Somewhat too early for new-married ladies.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lavinia, how say you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: I say, no;
I have been broad awake two hours and more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, then; horse and chariots let us have,
And to our sport.
Madam, now shall ye see
Our Roman hunting.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have dogs, my lord,
Will rouse the proudest panther in the chase,
And climb the highest promontory top.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: And I have horse will follow where the game
Makes way, and run like swallows o'er the plain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Chiron, we hunt not, we, with horse nor hound,
But hope to pluck a dainty doe to ground.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. A lonely part of the forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter AARON, with a bag of gold

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: He that had wit would think that I had none,
To bury so much gold under a tree,
And never after to inherit it.
Let him that thinks of me so abjectly
Know that this gold must coin a stratagem,
Which, cunningly effected, will beget
A very excellent piece of villany:
And so repose, sweet gold, for their unrest
That have their alms out of the empress' chest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: My lovely Aaron, wherefore look'st thou sad,
When every thing doth make a gleeful boast?
The birds chant melody on every bush,
The snake lies rolled in the cheerful sun,
The green leaves quiver with the cooling wind
And make a chequer'd shadow on the ground:
Under their sweet shade, Aaron, let us sit,
And, whilst the babbling echo mocks the hounds,
Replying shrilly to the well-tuned horns,
As if a double hunt were heard at once,
Let us sit down and mark their yelping noise;
And, after conflict such as was supposed
The wandering prince and Dido once enjoy'd,
When with a happy storm they were surprised
And curtain'd with a counsel-keeping cave,
We may, each wreathed in the other's arms,
Our pastimes done, possess a golden slumber;
Whiles hounds and horns and sweet melodious birds
Be unto us as is a nurse's song
Of lullaby to bring her babe asleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, though Venus govern your desires,
Saturn is dominator over mine:
What signifies my deadly-standing eye,
My silence and my cloudy melancholy,
My fleece of woolly hair that now uncurls
Even as an adder when she doth unroll
To do some fatal execution?
No, madam, these are no venereal signs:
Vengeance is in my heart, death in my hand,
Blood and revenge are hammering in my head.
Hark Tamora, the empress of my soul,
Which never hopes more heaven than rests in thee,
This is the day of doom for Bassianus:
His Philomel must lose her tongue to-day,
Thy sons make pillage of her chastity
And wash their hands in Bassianus' blood.
Seest thou this letter? take it up, I pray thee,
And give the king this fatal plotted scroll.
Now question me no more; we are espied;
Here comes a parcel of our hopeful booty,
Which dreads not yet their lives' destruction.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, my sweet Moor, sweeter to me than life!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: No more, great empress; Bassianus comes:
Be cross with him; and I'll go fetch thy sons
To back thy quarrels, whatsoe'er they be.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who have we here? Rome's royal empress,
Unfurnish'd of her well-beseeming troop?
Or is it Dian, habited like her,
Who hath abandoned her holy groves
To see the general hunting in this forest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Saucy controller of our private steps!
Had I the power that some say Dian had,
Thy temples should be planted presently
With horns, as was Actaeon's; and the hounds
Should drive upon thy new-transformed limbs,
Unmannerly intruder as thou art!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: Under your patience, gentle empress,
'Tis thought you have a goodly gift in horning;
And to be doubted that your Moor and you
Are singled forth to try experiments:
Jove shield your husband from his hounds to-day!
'Tis pity they should take him for a stag.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: Believe me, queen, your swarth Cimmerian
Doth make your honour of his body's hue,
Spotted, detested, and abominable.
Why are you sequester'd from all your train,
Dismounted from your snow-white goodly steed.
And wander'd hither to an obscure plot,
Accompanied but with a barbarous Moor,
If foul desire had not conducted you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: And, being intercepted in your sport,
Great reason that my noble lord be rated
For sauciness. I pray you, let us hence,
And let her joy her raven-colour'd love;
This valley fits the purpose passing well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: BASSIANUS
SPEECH.LINE: The king my brother shall have note of this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, for these slips have made him noted long:
Good king, to be so mightily abused!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Why have I patience to endure all this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now, dear sovereign, and our gracious mother!
Why doth your highness look so pale and wan?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Have I not reason, think you, to look pale?
These two have 'ticed me hither to this place:
A barren detested vale, you see it is;
The trees, though summer, yet forlorn and lean,
O'ercome with moss and baleful mistletoe:
Here never shines the sun; here nothing breeds,
Unless the nightly owl or fatal raven:
And when they show'd me this abhorred pit,
They told me, here, at dead time of the night,
A thousand fiends, a thousand hissing snakes,
Ten thousand swelling toads, as many urchins,
Would make such fearful and confused cries
As any mortal body hearing it
Should straight fall mad, or else die suddenly.
No sooner had they told this hellish tale,
But straight they told me they would bind me here
Unto the body of a dismal yew,
And leave me to this miserable death:
And then they call'd me foul adulteress,
Lascivious Goth, and all the bitterest terms
That ever ear did hear to such effect:
And, had you not by wondrous fortune come,
This vengeance on me had they executed.
Revenge it, as you love your mother's life,
Or be ye not henceforth call'd my children.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: This is a witness that I am thy son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: And this for me, struck home to show my strength.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, come, Semiramis, nay, barbarous Tamora,
For no name fits thy nature but thy own!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Give me thy poniard; you shall know, my boys
Your mother's hand shall right your mother's wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, madam; here is more belongs to her;
First thrash the corn, then after burn the straw:
This minion stood upon her chastity,
Upon her nuptial vow, her loyalty,
And with that painted hope braves your mightiness:
And shall she carry this unto her grave?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: An if she do, I would I were an eunuch.
Drag hence her husband to some secret hole,
And make his dead trunk pillow to our lust.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: But when ye have the honey ye desire,
Let not this wasp outlive, us both to sting.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I warrant you, madam, we will make that sure.
Come, mistress, now perforce we will enjoy
That nice-preserved honesty of yours.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: O Tamora! thou bear'st a woman's face,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: I will not hear her speak; away with her!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet lords, entreat her hear me but a word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Listen, fair madam: let it be your glory
To see her tears; but be your heart to them
As unrelenting flint to drops of rain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: When did the tiger's young ones teach the dam?
O, do not learn her wrath; she taught it thee;
The milk thou suck'dst from her did turn to marble;
Even at thy teat thou hadst thy tyranny.
Yet every mother breeds not sons alike:
Do thou entreat her show a woman pity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: What, wouldst thou have me prove myself a bastard?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true; the raven doth not hatch a lark:
Yet have I heard,--O, could I find it now!--
The lion moved with pity did endure
To have his princely paws pared all away:
Some say that ravens foster forlorn children,
The whilst their own birds famish in their nests:
O, be to me, though thy hard heart say no,
Nothing so kind, but something pitiful!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: I know not what it means; away with her!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: O, let me teach thee! for my father's sake,
That gave thee life, when well he might have
slain thee,
Be not obdurate, open thy deaf ears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Hadst thou in person ne'er offended me,
Even for his sake am I pitiless.
Remember, boys, I pour'd forth tears in vain,
To save your brother from the sacrifice;
But fierce Andronicus would not relent;
Therefore, away with her, and use her as you will,
The worse to her, the better loved of me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: O Tamora, be call'd a gentle queen,
And with thine own hands kill me in this place!
For 'tis not life that I have begg'd so long;
Poor I was slain when Bassianus died.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: What begg'st thou, then? fond woman, let me go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis present death I beg; and one thing more
That womanhood denies my tongue to tell:
O, keep me from their worse than killing lust,
And tumble me into some loathsome pit,
Where never man's eye may behold my body:
Do this, and be a charitable murderer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: So should I rob my sweet sons of their fee:
No, let them satisfy their lust on thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away! for thou hast stay'd us here too long.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LAVINIA
SPEECH.LINE: No grace? no womanhood? Ah, beastly creature!
The blot and enemy to our general name!
Confusion fall--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, then I'll stop your mouth. Bring thou her husband:
This is the hole where Aaron bid us hide him.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: DEMETRIUS throws the body of BASSIANUS into the pit; then exeunt DEMETRIUS and CHIRON, dragging off LAVINIA

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, my sons: see that you make her sure.
Ne'er let my heart know merry cheer indeed,
Till all the Andronici be made away.
Now will I hence to seek my lovely Moor,
And let my spleenful sons this trull deflow'r.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter AARON, with QUINTUS and MARTIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Come on, my lords, the better foot before:
Straight will I bring you to the loathsome pit
Where I espied the panther fast asleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: My sight is very dull, whate'er it bodes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And mine, I promise you; were't not for shame,
Well could I leave our sport to sleep awhile.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: What art thou fall'n? What subtle hole is this,
Whose mouth is cover'd with rude-growing briers,
Upon whose leaves are drops of new-shed blood
As fresh as morning dew distill'd on flowers?
A very fatal place it seems to me.
Speak, brother, hast thou hurt thee with the fall?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O brother, with the dismall'st object hurt
That ever eye with sight made heart lament!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Now will I fetch the king to find them here,
That he thereby may give a likely guess
How these were they that made away his brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why dost not comfort me, and help me out
From this unhallowed and blood-stained hole?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am surprised with an uncouth fear;
A chilling sweat o'er-runs my trembling joints:
My heart suspects more than mine eye can see.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: To prove thou hast a true-divining heart,
Aaron and thou look down into this den,
And see a fearful sight of blood and death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron is gone; and my compassionate heart
Will not permit mine eyes once to behold
The thing whereat it trembles by surmise;
O, tell me how it is; for ne'er till now
Was I a child to fear I know not what.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lord Bassianus lies embrewed here,
All on a heap, like to a slaughter'd lamb,
In this detested, dark, blood-drinking pit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: If it be dark, how dost thou know 'tis he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon his bloody finger he doth wear
A precious ring, that lightens all the hole,
Which, like a taper in some monument,
Doth shine upon the dead man's earthy cheeks,
And shows the ragged entrails of the pit:
So pale did shine the moon on Pyramus
When he by night lay bathed in maiden blood.
O brother, help me with thy fainting hand--
If fear hath made thee faint, as me it hath--
Out of this fell devouring receptacle,
As hateful as Cocytus' misty mouth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Reach me thy hand, that I may help thee out;
Or, wanting strength to do thee so much good,
I may be pluck'd into the swallowing womb
Of this deep pit, poor Bassianus' grave.
I have no strength to pluck thee to the brink.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I no strength to climb without thy help.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: QUINTUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thy hand once more; I will not loose again,
Till thou art here aloft, or I below:
Thou canst not come to me: I come to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Along with me: I'll see what hole is here,
And what he is that now is leap'd into it.
Say who art thou that lately didst descend
Into this gaping hollow of the earth?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: The unhappy son of old Andronicus:
Brought hither in a most unlucky hour,
To find thy brother Bassianus dead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: My brother dead! I know thou dost but jest:
He and his lady both are at the lodge
Upon the north side of this pleasant chase;
'Tis not an hour since I left him there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARTIUS
SPEECH.LINE: We know not where you left him all alive;
But, out, alas! here have we found him dead.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Re-enter TAMORA, with Attendants; TITUS ANDRONICUS, and Lucius

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Where is my lord the king?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here, Tamora, though grieved with killing grief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Where is thy brother Bassianus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now to the bottom dost thou search my wound:
Poor Bassianus here lies murdered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Then all too late I bring this fatal writ,
The complot of this timeless tragedy;
And wonder greatly that man's face can fold
In pleasing smiles such murderous tyranny.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Reads 'An if we miss to meet him handsomely--
Sweet huntsman, Bassianus 'tis we mean--
Do thou so much as dig the grave for him:
Thou know'st our meaning. Look for thy reward
Among the nettles at the elder-tree
Which overshades the mouth of that same pit
Where we decreed to bury Bassianus.
Do this, and purchase us thy lasting friends.'
O Tamora! was ever heard the like?
This is the pit, and this the elder-tree.
Look, sirs, if you can find the huntsman out
That should have murdered Bassianus here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious lord, here is the bag of gold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: To TITUS Two of thy whelps, fell curs of
bloody kind,
Have here bereft my brother of his life.
Sirs, drag them from the pit unto the prison:
There let them bide until we have devised
Some never-heard-of torturing pain for them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: What, are they in this pit? O wondrous thing!
How easily murder is discovered!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: High emperor, upon my feeble knee
I beg this boon, with tears not lightly shed,
That this fell fault of my accursed sons,
Accursed if the fault be proved in them,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: If it be proved! you see it is apparent.
Who found this letter? Tamora, was it you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Andronicus himself did take it up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I did, my lord: yet let me be their bail;
For, by my father's reverend tomb, I vow
They shall be ready at your highness' will
To answer their suspicion with their lives.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SATURNINUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shalt not bail them: see thou follow me.
Some bring the murder'd body, some the murderers:
Let them not speak a word; the guilt is plain;
For, by my soul, were there worse end than death,
That end upon them should be executed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TAMORA
SPEECH.LINE: Andronicus, I will entreat the king;
Fear not thy sons; they shall do well enough.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Lucius, come; stay not to talk with them.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Another part of the forest.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter DEMETRIUS and CHIRON with LAVINIA, ravished; her hands cut off, and her tongue cut out

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: So, now go tell, an if thy tongue can speak,
Who 'twas that cut thy tongue and ravish'd thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Write down thy mind, bewray thy meaning so,
An if thy stumps will let thee play the scribe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: See, how with signs and tokens she can scrowl.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Go home, call for sweet water, wash thy hands.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: She hath no tongue to call, nor hands to wash;
And so let's leave her to her silent walks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: An 'twere my case, I should go hang myself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: If thou hadst hands to help thee knit the cord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who is this? my niece, that flies away so fast!
Cousin, a word; where is your husband?
If I do dream, would all my wealth would wake me!
If I do wake, some planet strike me down,
That I may slumber in eternal sleep!
Speak, gentle niece, what stern ungentle hands
Have lopp'd and hew'd and made thy body bare
Of her two branches, those sweet ornaments,
Whose circling shadows kings have sought to sleep in,
And might not gain so great a happiness
As have thy love? Why dost not speak to me?
Alas, a crimson river of warm blood,
Like to a bubbling fountain stirr'd with wind,
Doth rise and fall between thy rosed lips,
Coming and going with thy honey breath.
But, sure, some Tereus hath deflowered thee,
And, lest thou shouldst detect him, cut thy tongue.
Ah, now thou turn'st away thy face for shame!
And, notwithstanding all this loss of blood,
As from a conduit with three issuing spouts,
Yet do thy cheeks look red as Titan's face
Blushing to be encountered with a cloud.
Shall I speak for thee? shall I say 'tis so?
O, that I knew thy heart; and knew the beast,
That I might rail at him, to ease my mind!
Sorrow concealed, like an oven stopp'd,
Doth burn the heart to cinders where it is.
Fair Philomela, she but lost her tongue,
And in a tedious sampler sew'd her mind:
But, lovely niece, that mean is cut from thee;
A craftier Tereus, cousin, hast thou met,
And he hath cut those pretty fingers off,
That could have better sew'd than Philomel.
O, had the monster seen those lily hands
Tremble, like aspen-leaves, upon a lute,
And make the silken strings delight to kiss them,
He would not then have touch'd them for his life!
Or, had he heard the heavenly harmony
Which that sweet tongue hath made,
He would have dropp'd his knife, and fell asleep
As Cerberus at the Thracian poet's feet.
Come, let us go, and make thy father blind;
For such a sight will blind a father's eye:
One hour's storm will drown the fragrant meads;
What will whole months of tears thy father's eyes?
Do not draw back, for we will mourn with thee
O, could our mourning ease thy misery!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Rome. A street.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter Judges, Senators and Tribunes, with MARTIUS and QUINTUS, bound, passing on to the place of execution; TITUS going before, pleading

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, grave fathers! noble tribunes, stay!
For pity of mine age, whose youth was spent
In dangerous wars, whilst you securely slept;
For all my blood in Rome's great quarrel shed;
For all the frosty nights that I have watch'd;
And for these bitter tears, which now you see
Filling the aged wrinkles in my cheeks;
Be pitiful to my condemned sons,
Whose souls are not corrupted as 'tis thought.
For two and twenty sons I never wept,
Because they died in honour's lofty bed.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Lieth down; the Judges, &c., pass by him, and Exeunt
SPEECH.LINE: For these, these, tribunes, in the dust I write
My heart's deep languor and my soul's sad tears:
Let my tears stanch the earth's dry appetite;
My sons' sweet blood will make it shame and blush.
O earth, I will befriend thee more with rain,
That shall distil from these two ancient urns,
Than youthful April shall with all his showers:
In summer's drought I'll drop upon thee still;
In winter with warm tears I'll melt the snow
And keep eternal spring-time on thy face,
So thou refuse to drink my dear sons' blood.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter LUCIUS, with his sword drawn
SPEECH.LINE: O reverend tribunes! O gentle, aged men!
Unbind my sons, reverse the doom of death;
And let me say, that never wept before,
My tears are now prevailing orators.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O noble father, you lament in vain:
The tribunes hear you not; no man is by;
And you recount your sorrows to a stone.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Lucius, for thy brothers let me plead.
Grave tribunes, once more I entreat of you,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My gracious lord, no tribune hears you speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, tis no matter, man; if they did hear,
They would not mark me, or if they did mark,
They would not pity me, yet plead I must;
And bootless unto them.
Therefore I tell my sorrows to the stones;
Who, though they cannot answer my distress,
Yet in some sort they are better than the tribunes,
For that they will not intercept my tale:
When I do weep, they humbly at my feet
Receive my tears and seem to weep with me;
And, were they but attired in grave weeds,
Rome could afford no tribune like to these.
A stone is soft as wax,--tribunes more hard than stones;
A stone is silent, and offendeth not,
And tribunes with their tongues doom men to death.
But wherefore stand'st thou with thy weapon drawn?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: To rescue my two brothers from their death:
For which attempt the judges have pronounced
My everlasting doom of banishment.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O happy man! they have befriended thee.
Why, foolish Lucius, dost thou not perceive
That Rome is but a wilderness of tigers?
Tigers must prey, and Rome affords no prey
But me and mine: how happy art thou, then,
From these devourers to be banished!
But who comes with our brother Marcus here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Titus, prepare thy aged eyes to weep;
Or, if not so, thy noble heart to break:
I bring consuming sorrow to thine age.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Will it consume me? let me see it, then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: This was thy daughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, Marcus, so she is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay me, this object kills me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Faint-hearted boy, arise, and look upon her.
Speak, Lavinia, what accursed hand
Hath made thee handless in thy father's sight?
What fool hath added water to the sea,
Or brought a faggot to bright-burning Troy?
My grief was at the height before thou camest,
And now like Nilus, it disdaineth bounds.
Give me a sword, I'll chop off my hands too;
For they have fought for Rome, and all in vain;
And they have nursed this woe, in feeding life;
In bootless prayer have they been held up,
And they have served me to effectless use:
Now all the service I require of them
Is that the one will help to cut the other.
'Tis well, Lavinia, that thou hast no hands;
For hands, to do Rome service, are but vain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Speak, gentle sister, who hath martyr'd thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, that delightful engine of her thoughts
That blabb'd them with such pleasing eloquence,
Is torn from forth that pretty hollow cage,
Where, like a sweet melodious bird, it sung
Sweet varied notes, enchanting every ear!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, say thou for her, who hath done this deed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, thus I found her, straying in the park,
Seeking to hide herself, as doth the deer
That hath received some unrecuring wound.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: It was my deer; and he that wounded her
Hath hurt me more than had he killed me dead:
For now I stand as one upon a rock
Environed with a wilderness of sea,
Who marks the waxing tide grow wave by wave,
Expecting ever when some envious surge
Will in his brinish bowels swallow him.
This way to death my wretched sons are gone;
Here stands my other son, a banished man,
And here my brother, weeping at my woes.
But that which gives my soul the greatest spurn,
Is dear Lavinia, dearer than my soul.
Had I but seen thy picture in this plight,
It would have madded me: what shall I do
Now I behold thy lively body so?
Thou hast no hands, to wipe away thy tears:
Nor tongue, to tell me who hath martyr'd thee:
Thy husband he is dead: and for his death
Thy brothers are condemn'd, and dead by this.
Look, Marcus! ah, son Lucius, look on her!
When I did name her brothers, then fresh tears
Stood on her cheeks, as doth the honey-dew
Upon a gather'd lily almost wither'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Perchance she weeps because they kill'd her husband;
Perchance because she knows them innocent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: If they did kill thy husband, then be joyful
Because the law hath ta'en revenge on them.
No, no, they would not do so foul a deed;
Witness the sorrow that their sister makes.
Gentle Lavinia, let me kiss thy lips.
Or make some sign how I may do thee ease:
Shall thy good uncle, and thy brother Lucius,
And thou, and I, sit round about some fountain,
Looking all downwards to behold our cheeks
How they are stain'd, as meadows, yet not dry,
With miry slime left on them by a flood?
And in the fountain shall we gaze so long
Till the fresh taste be taken from that clearness,
And made a brine-pit with our bitter tears?
Or shall we cut away our hands, like thine?
Or shall we bite our tongues, and in dumb shows
Pass the remainder of our hateful days?
What shall we do? let us, that have our tongues,
Plot some deuce of further misery,
To make us wonder'd at in time to come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet father, cease your tears; for, at your grief,
See how my wretched sister sobs and weeps.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Patience, dear niece. Good Titus, dry thine eyes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, Marcus, Marcus! brother, well I wot
Thy napkin cannot drink a tear of mine,
For thou, poor man, hast drown'd it with thine own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, my Lavinia, I will wipe thy cheeks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Mark, Marcus, mark! I understand her signs:
Had she a tongue to speak, now would she say
That to her brother which I said to thee:
His napkin, with his true tears all bewet,
Can do no service on her sorrowful cheeks.
O, what a sympathy of woe is this,
As far from help as Limbo is from bliss!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Titus Andronicus, my lord the emperor
Sends thee this word,--that, if thou love thy sons,
Let Marcus, Lucius, or thyself, old Titus,
Or any one of you, chop off your hand,
And send it to the king: he for the same
Will send thee hither both thy sons alive;
And that shall be the ransom for their fault.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O gracious emperor! O gentle Aaron!
Did ever raven sing so like a lark,
That gives sweet tidings of the sun's uprise?
With all my heart, I'll send the emperor My hand:
Good Aaron, wilt thou help to chop it off?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, father! for that noble hand of thine,
That hath thrown down so many enemies,
Shall not be sent: my hand will serve the turn:
My youth can better spare my blood than you;
And therefore mine shall save my brothers' lives.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Which of your hands hath not defended Rome,
And rear'd aloft the bloody battle-axe,
Writing destruction on the enemy's castle?
O, none of both but are of high desert:
My hand hath been but idle; let it serve
To ransom my two nephews from their death;
Then have I kept it to a worthy end.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, come, agree whose hand shall go along,
For fear they die before their pardon come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: My hand shall go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By heaven, it shall not go!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sirs, strive no more: such wither'd herbs as these
Are meet for plucking up, and therefore mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet father, if I shall be thought thy son,
Let me redeem my brothers both from death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: And, for our father's sake and mother's care,
Now let me show a brother's love to thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Agree between you; I will spare my hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Then I'll go fetch an axe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: But I will use the axe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come hither, Aaron; I'll deceive them both:
Lend me thy hand, and I will give thee mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside If that be call'd deceit, I will be honest,
And never, whilst I live, deceive men so:
But I'll deceive you in another sort,
And that you'll say, ere half an hour pass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now stay your strife: what shall be is dispatch'd.
Good Aaron, give his majesty my hand:
Tell him it was a hand that warded him
From thousand dangers; bid him bury it
More hath it merited; that let it have.
As for my sons, say I account of them
As jewels purchased at an easy price;
And yet dear too, because I bought mine own.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: I go, Andronicus: and for thy hand
Look by and by to have thy sons with thee.
Their heads, I mean. O, how this villany
Doth fat me with the very thoughts of it!
Let fools do good, and fair men call for grace.
Aaron will have his soul black like his face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, here I lift this one hand up to heaven,
And bow this feeble ruin to the earth:
If any power pities wretched tears,
To that I call!
What, wilt thou kneel with me?
Do, then, dear heart; for heaven shall hear our prayers;
Or with our sighs we'll breathe the welkin dim,
And stain the sun with fog, as sometime clouds
When they do hug him in their melting bosoms.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O brother, speak with possibilities,
And do not break into these deep extremes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is not my sorrow deep, having no bottom?
Then be my passions bottomless with them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: But yet let reason govern thy lament.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: If there were reason for these miseries,
Then into limits could I bind my woes:
When heaven doth weep, doth not the earth o'erflow?
If the winds rage, doth not the sea wax mad,
Threatening the welkin with his big-swoln face?
And wilt thou have a reason for this coil?
I am the sea; hark, how her sighs do blow!
She is the weeping welkin, I the earth:
Then must my sea be moved with her sighs;
Then must my earth with her continual tears
Become a deluge, overflow'd and drown'd;
For why my bowels cannot hide her woes,
But like a drunkard must I vomit them.
Then give me leave, for losers will have leave
To ease their stomachs with their bitter tongues.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter a Messenger, with two heads and a hand

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Messenger
SPEECH.LINE: Worthy Andronicus, ill art thou repaid
For that good hand thou sent'st the emperor.
Here are the heads of thy two noble sons;
And here's thy hand, in scorn to thee sent back;
Thy griefs their sports, thy resolution mock'd;
That woe is me to think upon thy woes
More than remembrance of my father's death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now let hot AEtna cool in Sicily,
And be my heart an ever-burning hell!
These miseries are more than may be borne.
To weep with them that weep doth ease some deal;
But sorrow flouted at is double death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, that this sight should make so deep a wound,
And yet detested life not shrink thereat!
That ever death should let life bear his name,
Where life hath no more interest but to breathe!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, poor heart, that kiss is comfortless
As frozen water to a starved snake.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: When will this fearful slumber have an end?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, farewell, flattery: die, Andronicus;
Thou dost not slumber: see, thy two sons' heads,
Thy warlike hand, thy mangled daughter here:
Thy other banish'd son, with this dear sight
Struck pale and bloodless; and thy brother, I,
Even like a stony image, cold and numb.
Ah, now no more will I control thy griefs:
Rend off thy silver hair, thy other hand
Gnawing with thy teeth; and be this dismal sight
The closing up of our most wretched eyes;
Now is a time to storm; why art thou still?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha, ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why dost thou laugh? it fits not with this hour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, I have not another tear to shed:
Besides, this sorrow is an enemy,
And would usurp upon my watery eyes
And make them blind with tributary tears:
Then which way shall I find Revenge's cave?
For these two heads do seem to speak to me,
And threat me I shall never come to bliss
Till all these mischiefs be return'd again
Even in their throats that have committed them.
Come, let me see what task I have to do.
You heavy people, circle me about,
That I may turn me to each one of you,
And swear unto my soul to right your wrongs.
The vow is made. Come, brother, take a head;
And in this hand the other I will bear.
Lavinia, thou shalt be employ'd: these arms!
Bear thou my hand, sweet wench, between thy teeth.
As for thee, boy, go get thee from my sight;
Thou art an exile, and thou must not stay:
Hie to the Goths, and raise an army there:
And, if you love me, as I think you do,
Let's kiss and part, for we have much to do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell Andronicus, my noble father,
The wofull'st man that ever lived in Rome:
Farewell, proud Rome; till Lucius come again,
He leaves his pledges dearer than his life:
Farewell, Lavinia, my noble sister;
O, would thou wert as thou tofore hast been!
But now nor Lucius nor Lavinia lives
But in oblivion and hateful griefs.
If Lucius live, he will requite your wrongs;
And make proud Saturnine and his empress
Beg at the gates, like Tarquin and his queen.
Now will I to the Goths, and raise a power,
To be revenged on Rome and Saturnine.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. A room in Titus's house. A banquet set out.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TITUS, MARCUS, LAVINIA and Young LUCIUS, a boy

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: So, so; now sit: and look you eat no more
Than will preserve just so much strength in us
As will revenge these bitter woes of ours.
Marcus, unknit that sorrow-wreathen knot:
Thy niece and I, poor creatures, want our hands,
And cannot passionate our tenfold grief
With folded arms. This poor right hand of mine
Is left to tyrannize upon my breast;
Who, when my heart, all mad with misery,
Beats in this hollow prison of my flesh,
Then thus I thump it down.
Thou map of woe, that thus dost talk in signs!
When thy poor heart beats with outrageous beating,
Thou canst not strike it thus to make it still.
Wound it with sighing, girl, kill it with groans;
Or get some little knife between thy teeth,
And just against thy heart make thou a hole;
That all the tears that thy poor eyes let fall
May run into that sink, and soaking in
Drown the lamenting fool in sea-salt tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, brother, fie! teach her not thus to lay
Such violent hands upon her tender life.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now! has sorrow made thee dote already?
Why, Marcus, no man should be mad but I.
What violent hands can she lay on her life?
Ah, wherefore dost thou urge the name of hands;
To bid AEneas tell the tale twice o'er,
How Troy was burnt and he made miserable?
O, handle not the theme, to talk of hands,
Lest we remember still that we have none.
Fie, fie, how franticly I square my talk,
As if we should forget we had no hands,
If Marcus did not name the word of hands!
Come, let's fall to; and, gentle girl, eat this:
Here is no drink! Hark, Marcus, what she says;
I can interpret all her martyr'd signs;
She says she drinks no other drink but tears,
Brew'd with her sorrow, mesh'd upon her cheeks:
Speechless complainer, I will learn thy thought;
In thy dumb action will I be as perfect
As begging hermits in their holy prayers:
Thou shalt not sigh, nor hold thy stumps to heaven,
Nor wink, nor nod, nor kneel, nor make a sign,
But I of these will wrest an alphabet
And by still practise learn to know thy meaning.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good grandsire, leave these bitter deep laments:
Make my aunt merry with some pleasing tale.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, the tender boy, in passion moved,
Doth weep to see his grandsire's heaviness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, tender sapling; thou art made of tears,
And tears will quickly melt thy life away.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: MARCUS strikes the dish with a knife
SPEECH.LINE: What dost thou strike at, Marcus, with thy knife?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: At that that I have kill'd, my lord; a fly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Out on thee, murderer! thou kill'st my heart;
Mine eyes are cloy'd with view of tyranny:
A deed of death done on the innocent
Becomes not Titus' brother: get thee gone:
I see thou art not for my company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, my lord, I have but kill'd a fly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: But how, if that fly had a father and mother?
How would he hang his slender gilded wings,
And buzz lamenting doings in the air!
Poor harmless fly,
That, with his pretty buzzing melody,
Came here to make us merry! and thou hast
kill'd him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon me, sir; it was a black ill-favor'd fly,
Like to the empress' Moor; therefore I kill'd him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, O, O,
Then pardon me for reprehending thee,
For thou hast done a charitable deed.
Give me thy knife, I will insult on him;
Flattering myself, as if it were the Moor
Come hither purposely to poison me.--
There's for thyself, and that's for Tamora.
Ah, sirrah!
Yet, I think, we are not brought so low,
But that between us we can kill a fly
That comes in likeness of a coal-black Moor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Alas, poor man! grief has so wrought on him,
He takes false shadows for true substances.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, take away. Lavinia, go with me:
I'll to thy closet; and go read with thee
Sad stories chanced in the times of old.
Come, boy, and go with me: thy sight is young,
And thou shalt read when mine begin to dazzle.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Rome. Titus's garden.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter young LUCIUS, and LAVINIA running after him, and the boy flies from her, with books under his arm. Then enter TITUS and MARCUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Help, grandsire, help! my aunt Lavinia
Follows me every where, I know not why:
Good uncle Marcus, see how swift she comes.
Alas, sweet aunt, I know not what you mean.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand by me, Lucius; do not fear thine aunt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: She loves thee, boy, too well to do thee harm.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, when my father was in Rome she did.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: What means my niece Lavinia by these signs?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fear her not, Lucius: somewhat doth she mean:
See, Lucius, see how much she makes of thee:
Somewhither would she have thee go with her.
Ah, boy, Cornelia never with more care
Read to her sons than she hath read to thee
Sweet poetry and Tully's Orator.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Canst thou not guess wherefore she plies thee thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I know not, I, nor can I guess,
Unless some fit or frenzy do possess her:
For I have heard my grandsire say full oft,
Extremity of griefs would make men mad;
And I have read that Hecuba of Troy
Ran mad through sorrow: that made me to fear;
Although, my lord, I know my noble aunt
Loves me as dear as e'er my mother did,
And would not, but in fury, fright my youth:
Which made me down to throw my books, and fly--
Causeless, perhaps. But pardon me, sweet aunt:
And, madam, if my uncle Marcus go,
I will most willingly attend your ladyship.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucius, I will.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: LAVINIA turns over with her stumps the books which LUCIUS has let fall

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Lavinia! Marcus, what means this?
Some book there is that she desires to see.
Which is it, girl, of these? Open them, boy.
But thou art deeper read, and better skill'd
Come, and take choice of all my library,
And so beguile thy sorrow, till the heavens
Reveal the damn'd contriver of this deed.
Why lifts she up her arms in sequence thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: I think she means that there was more than one
Confederate in the fact: ay, more there was;
Or else to heaven she heaves them for revenge.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lucius, what book is that she tosseth so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Grandsire, 'tis Ovid's Metamorphoses;
My mother gave it me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: For love of her that's gone,
Perhaps she cull'd it from among the rest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Soft! see how busily she turns the leaves!
What would she find? Lavinia, shall I read?
This is the tragic tale of Philomel,
And treats of Tereus' treason and his rape:
And rape, I fear, was root of thine annoy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: See, brother, see; note how she quotes the leaves.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Lavinia, wert thou thus surprised, sweet girl,
Ravish'd and wrong'd, as Philomela was,
Forced in the ruthless, vast, and gloomy woods? See, see!
Ay, such a place there is, where we did hunt--
O, had we never, never hunted there!--
Pattern'd by that the poet here describes,
By nature made for murders and for rapes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, why should nature build so foul a den,
Unless the gods delight in tragedies?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Give signs, sweet girl, for here are none
but friends,
What Roman lord it was durst do the deed:
Or slunk not Saturnine, as Tarquin erst,
That left the camp to sin in Lucrece' bed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sit down, sweet niece: brother, sit down by me.
Apollo, Pallas, Jove, or Mercury,
Inspire me, that I may this treason find!
My lord, look here: look here, Lavinia:
This sandy plot is plain; guide, if thou canst
This after me, when I have writ my name
Without the help of any hand at all.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: He writes his name with his staff, and guides it with feet and mouth
SPEECH.LINE: Cursed be that heart that forced us to this shift!
Write thou good niece; and here display, at last,
What God will have discover'd for revenge;
Heaven guide thy pen to print thy sorrows plain,
That we may know the traitors and the truth!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: She takes the staff in her mouth, and guides it with her stumps, and writes

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, do ye read, my lord, what she hath writ?
'Stuprum. Chiron. Demetrius.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, what! the lustful sons of Tamora
Performers of this heinous, bloody deed?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Magni Dominator poli,
Tam lentus audis scelera? tam lentus vides?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, calm thee, gentle lord; although I know
There is enough written upon this earth
To stir a mutiny in the mildest thoughts
And arm the minds of infants to exclaims.
My lord, kneel down with me; Lavinia, kneel;
And kneel, sweet boy, the Roman Hector's hope;
And swear with me, as, with the woful fere
And father of that chaste dishonour'd dame,
Lord Junius Brutus sware for Lucrece' rape,
That we will prosecute by good advice
Mortal revenge upon these traitorous Goths,
And see their blood, or die with this reproach.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis sure enough, an you knew how.
But if you hunt these bear-whelps, then beware:
The dam will wake; and, if she wind you once,
She's with the lion deeply still in league,
And lulls him whilst she playeth on her back,
And when he sleeps will she do what she list.
You are a young huntsman, Marcus; let it alone;
And, come, I will go get a leaf of brass,
And with a gad of steel will write these words,
And lay it by: the angry northern wind
Will blow these sands, like Sibyl's leaves, abroad,
And where's your lesson, then? Boy, what say you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I say, my lord, that if I were a man,
Their mother's bed-chamber should not be safe
For these bad bondmen to the yoke of Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that's my boy! thy father hath full oft
For his ungrateful country done the like.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And, uncle, so will I, an if I live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, go with me into mine armoury;
Lucius, I'll fit thee; and withal, my boy,
Shalt carry from me to the empress' sons
Presents that I intend to send them both:
Come, come; thou'lt do thy message, wilt thou not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, with my dagger in their bosoms, grandsire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, boy, not so; I'll teach thee another course.
Lavinia, come. Marcus, look to my house:
Lucius and I'll go brave it at the court:
Ay, marry, will we, sir; and we'll be waited on.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt TITUS, LAVINIA, and Young LUCIUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O heavens, can you hear a good man groan,
And not relent, or not compassion him?
Marcus, attend him in his ecstasy,
That hath more scars of sorrow in his heart
Than foemen's marks upon his batter'd shield;
But yet so just that he will not revenge.
Revenge, ye heavens, for old Andronicus!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. A room in the palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter, from one side, AARON, DEMETRIUS, and CHIRON; from the other side, Young LUCIUS, and an Attendant, with a bundle of weapons, and verses writ upon them

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Demetrius, here's the son of Lucius;
He hath some message to deliver us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, some mad message from his mad grandfather.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lords, with all the humbleness I may,
I greet your honours from Andronicus.
And pray the Roman gods confound you both!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Gramercy, lovely Lucius: what's the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Young LUCIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Aside That you are both decipher'd, that's the news,
For villains mark'd with rape.--May it please you,
My grandsire, well advised, hath sent by me
The goodliest weapons of his armoury
To gratify your honourable youth,
The hope of Rome; for so he bade me say;
And so I do, and with his gifts present
Your lordships, that, whenever you have need,
You may be armed and appointed well:
And so I leave you both:
like bloody villains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What's here? A scroll; and written round about?
Let's see;
'Integer vitae, scelerisque purus,
Non eget Mauri jaculis, nec arcu.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'tis a verse in Horace; I know it well:
I read it in the grammar long ago.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, just; a verse in Horace; right, you have it.
Now, what a thing it is to be an ass!
Here's no sound jest! the old man hath found their guilt;
And sends them weapons wrapped about with lines,
That wound, beyond their feeling, to the quick.
But were our witty empress well afoot,
She would applaud Andronicus' conceit:
But let her rest in her unrest awhile.
And now, young lords, was't not a happy star
Led us to Rome, strangers, and more than so,
Captives, to be advanced to this height?
It did me good, before the palace gate
To brave the tribune in his brother's hearing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: But me more good, to see so great a lord
Basely insinuate and send us gifts.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Had he not reason, Lord Demetrius?
Did you not use his daughter very friendly?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I would we had a thousand Roman dames
At such a bay, by turn to serve our lust.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: A charitable wish and full of love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Here lacks but your mother for to say amen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: And that would she for twenty thousand more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, let us go; and pray to all the gods
For our beloved mother in her pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Aside Pray to the devils; the gods have given us over.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why do the emperor's trumpets flourish thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Belike, for joy the emperor hath a son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Soft! who comes here?

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter a Nurse, with a blackamoor Child in her arms

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, lords:
O, tell me, did you see Aaron the Moor?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Well, more or less, or ne'er a whit at all,
Here Aaron is; and what with Aaron now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: O gentle Aaron, we are all undone!
Now help, or woe betide thee evermore!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, what a caterwauling dost thou keep!
What dost thou wrap and fumble in thine arms?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: O, that which I would hide from heaven's eye,
Our empress' shame, and stately Rome's disgrace!
She is deliver'd, lords; she is deliver'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: To whom?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: I mean, she is brought a-bed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Well, God give her good rest! What hath he sent her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: A devil.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then she is the devil's dam; a joyful issue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: A joyless, dismal, black, and sorrowful issue:
Here is the babe, as loathsome as a toad
Amongst the fairest breeders of our clime:
The empress sends it thee, thy stamp, thy seal,
And bids thee christen it with thy dagger's point.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: 'Zounds, ye whore! is black so base a hue?
Sweet blowse, you are a beauteous blossom, sure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Villain, what hast thou done?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: That which thou canst not undo.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Thou hast undone our mother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Villain, I have done thy mother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: And therein, hellish dog, thou hast undone.
Woe to her chance, and damn'd her loathed choice!
Accursed the offspring of so foul a fiend!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: It shall not live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: It shall not die.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron, it must; the mother wills it so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: What, must it, nurse? then let no man but I
Do execution on my flesh and blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll broach the tadpole on my rapier's point:
Nurse, give it me; my sword shall soon dispatch it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Sooner this sword shall plough thy bowels up.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Takes the Child from the Nurse, and draws
SPEECH.LINE: Stay, murderous villains! will you kill your brother?
Now, by the burning tapers of the sky,
That shone so brightly when this boy was got,
He dies upon my scimitar's sharp point
That touches this my first-born son and heir!
I tell you, younglings, not Enceladus,
With all his threatening band of Typhon's brood,
Nor great Alcides, nor the god of war,
Shall seize this prey out of his father's hands.
What, what, ye sanguine, shallow-hearted boys!
Ye white-limed walls! ye alehouse painted signs!
Coal-black is better than another hue,
In that it scorns to bear another hue;
For all the water in the ocean
Can never turn the swan's black legs to white,
Although she lave them hourly in the flood.
Tell the empress from me, I am of age
To keep mine own, excuse it how she can.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Wilt thou betray thy noble mistress thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: My mistress is my mistress; this myself,
The vigour and the picture of my youth:
This before all the world do I prefer;
This maugre all the world will I keep safe,
Or some of you shall smoke for it in Rome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: By this our mother is forever shamed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Rome will despise her for this foul escape.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: The emperor, in his rage, will doom her death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: I blush to think upon this ignomy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, there's the privilege your beauty bears:
Fie, treacherous hue, that will betray with blushing
The close enacts and counsels of the heart!
Here's a young lad framed of another leer:
Look, how the black slave smiles upon the father,
As who should say 'Old lad, I am thine own.'
He is your brother, lords, sensibly fed
Of that self-blood that first gave life to you,
And from that womb where you imprison'd were
He is enfranchised and come to light:
Nay, he is your brother by the surer side,
Although my seal be stamped in his face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron, what shall I say unto the empress?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Advise thee, Aaron, what is to be done,
And we will all subscribe to thy advice:
Save thou the child, so we may all be safe.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Then sit we down, and let us all consult.
My son and I will have the wind of you:
Keep there: now talk at pleasure of your safety.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: How many women saw this child of his?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Why, so, brave lords! when we join in league,
I am a lamb: but if you brave the Moor,
The chafed boar, the mountain lioness,
The ocean swells not so as Aaron storms.
But say, again; how many saw the child?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Nurse
SPEECH.LINE: Cornelia the midwife and myself;
And no one else but the deliver'd empress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: The empress, the midwife, and yourself:
Two may keep counsel when the third's away:
Go to the empress, tell her this I said.
Weke, weke! so cries a pig prepared to the spit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: What mean'st thou, Aaron? wherefore didst thou this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: O Lord, sir, 'tis a deed of policy:
Shall she live to betray this guilt of ours,
A long-tongued babbling gossip? no, lords, no:
And now be it known to you my full intent.
Not far, one Muli lives, my countryman;
His wife but yesternight was brought to bed;
His child is like to her, fair as you are:
Go pack with him, and give the mother gold,
And tell them both the circumstance of all;
And how by this their child shall be advanced,
And be received for the emperor's heir,
And substituted in the place of mine,
To calm this tempest whirling in the court;
And let the emperor dandle him for his own.
Hark ye, lords; ye see I have given her physic,
And you must needs bestow her funeral;
The fields are near, and you are gallant grooms:
This done, see that you take no longer days,
But send the midwife presently to me.
The midwife and the nurse well made away,
Then let the ladies tattle what they please.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CHIRON
SPEECH.LINE: Aaron, I see thou wilt not trust the air
With secrets.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEMETRIUS
SPEECH.LINE: For this care of Tamora,
Herself and hers are highly bound to thee.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt DEMETRIUS and CHIRON bearing off the Nurse's body

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AARON
SPEECH.LINE: Now to the Goths, as swift as swallow flies;
There to dispose this treasure in mine arms,
And secretly to greet the empress' friends.
Come on, you thick lipp'd slave, I'll bear you hence;
For it is you that puts us to our shifts:
I'll make you feed on berries and on roots,
And feed on curds and whey, and suck the goat,
And cabin in a cave, and bring you up
To be a warrior, and command a camp.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The same. A public place.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TITUS, bearing arrows with letters at the ends of them; with him, MARCUS, Young LUCIUS, PUBLIUS, SEMPRONIUS, CAIUS, and other Gentlemen, with bows

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Marcus; come, kinsmen; this is the way.
Sir boy, now let me see your archery;
Look ye draw home enough, and 'tis there straight.
Terras Astraea reliquit:
Be you remember'd, Marcus, she's gone, she's fled.
Sirs, take you to your tools. You, cousins, shall
Go sound the ocean, and cast your nets;
Happily you may catch her in the sea;
Yet there's as little justice as at land:
No; Publius and Sempronius, you must do it;
'Tis you must dig with mattock and with spade,
And pierce the inmost centre of the earth:
Then, when you come to Pluto's region,
I pray you, deliver him this petition;
Tell him, it is for justice and for aid,
And that it comes from old Andronicus,
Shaken with sorrows in ungrateful Rome.
Ah, Rome! Well, well; I made thee miserable
What time I threw the people's suffrages
On him that thus doth tyrannize o'er me.
Go, get you gone; and pray be careful all,
And leave you not a man-of-war unsearch'd:
This wicked emperor may have shipp'd her hence;
And, kinsmen, then we may go pipe for justice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Publius, is not this a heavy case,
To see thy noble uncle thus distract?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PUBLIUS
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore, my lord, it highly us concerns
By day and night to attend him carefully,
And feed his humour kindly as we may,
Till time beget some careful remedy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Kinsmen, his sorrows are past remedy.
Join with the Goths; and with revengeful war
Take wreak on Rome for this ingratitude,
And vengeance on the traitor Saturnine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Publius, how now! how now, my masters!
What, have you met with her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PUBLIUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, my good lord; but Pluto sends you word,
If you will have Revenge from hell, you shall:
Marry, for Justice, she is so employ'd,
He thinks, with Jove in heaven, or somewhere else,
So that perforce you must needs stay a time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: He doth me wrong to feed me with delays.
I'll dive into the burning lake below,
And pull her out of Acheron by the heels.
Marcus, we are but shrubs, no cedars we
No big-boned men framed of the Cyclops' size;
But metal, Marcus, steel to the very back,
Yet wrung with wrongs more than our backs can bear:
And, sith there's no justice in earth nor hell,
We will solicit heaven and move the gods
To send down Justice for to wreak our wrongs.
Come, to this gear. You are a good archer, Marcus;
'Ad Jovem,' that's for you: here, 'Ad Apollinem:'
'Ad Martem,' that's for myself:
Here, boy, to Pallas: here, to Mercury:
To Saturn, Caius, not to Saturnine;
You were as good to shoot against the wind.
To it, boy! Marcus, loose when I bid.
Of my word, I have written to effect;
There's not a god left unsolicited.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Kinsmen, shoot all your shafts into the court:
We will afflict the emperor in his pride.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, masters, draw.
O, well said, Lucius!
Good boy, in Virgo's lap; give it Pallas.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I aim a mile beyond the moon;
Your letter is with Jupiter by this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TITUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha!
Publius, Publius, what hast thou done?
See, see, thou hast shot off one of Taurus' horns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARCUS ANDRONICUS
SPEECH.LINE: This was the sport, my lord: when Publius shot,
The Bull, being gall'd, gave Aries such a knock
