To their subsequent volumes, there is seen
The baby figure of the giant mass
Of things to come at large. It is supposed
He that meets Hector issues from our choice
And choice, being mutual act of all our souls,
Makes merit her election, and doth boil,
As 'twere from us all, a man distill'd
Out of our virtues; who miscarrying,
What heart receives from hence the conquering part,
To steel a strong opinion to themselves?
Which entertain'd, limbs are his instruments,
In no less working than are swords and bows
Directive by the limbs.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Give pardon to my speech:
Therefore 'tis meet Achilles meet not Hector.
Let us, like merchants, show our foulest wares,
And think, perchance, they'll sell; if not,
The lustre of the better yet to show,
Shall show the better. Do not consent
That ever Hector and Achilles meet;
For both our honour and our shame in this
Are dogg'd with two strange followers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I see them not with my old eyes: what are they?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: What glory our Achilles shares from Hector,
Were he not proud, we all should share with him:
But he already is too insolent;
And we were better parch in Afric sun
Than in the pride and salt scorn of his eyes,
Should he 'scape Hector fair: if he were foil'd,
Why then, we did our main opinion crush
In taint of our best man. No, make a lottery;
And, by device, let blockish Ajax draw
The sort to fight with Hector: among ourselves
Give him allowance for the better man;
For that will physic the great Myrmidon
Who broils in loud applause, and make him fall
His crest that prouder than blue Iris bends.
If the dull brainless Ajax come safe off,
We'll dress him up in voices: if he fail,
Yet go we under our opinion still
That we have better men. But, hit or miss,
Our project's life this shape of sense assumes:
Ajax employ'd plucks down Achilles' plumes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Ulysses,
Now I begin to relish thy advice;
And I will give a taste of it forthwith
To Agamemnon: go we to him straight.
Two curs shall tame each other: pride alone
Must tarre the mastiffs on, as 'twere their bone.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. A part of the Grecian camp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Thersites!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Agamemnon, how if he had boils? full, all over,
generally?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Thersites!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: And those boils did run? say so: did not the
general run then? were not that a botchy core?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Then would come some matter from him; I see none now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Thou bitch-wolf's son, canst thou not hear?
Feel, then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: The plague of Greece upon thee, thou mongrel
beef-witted lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Speak then, thou vinewedst leaven, speak: I will
beat thee into handsomeness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I shall sooner rail thee into wit and holiness: but,
I think, thy horse will sooner con an oration than
thou learn a prayer without book. Thou canst strike,
canst thou? a red murrain o' thy jade's tricks!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Toadstool, learn me the proclamation.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou think I have no sense, thou strikest me thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: The proclamation!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art proclaimed a fool, I think.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Do not, porpentine, do not: my fingers itch.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I would thou didst itch from head to foot and I had
the scratching of thee; I would make thee the
loathsomest scab in Greece. When thou art forth in
the incursions, thou strikest as slow as another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I say, the proclamation!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou grumblest and railest every hour on Achilles,
and thou art as full of envy at his greatness as
Cerberus is at Proserpine's beauty, ay, that thou
barkest at him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Mistress Thersites!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou shouldest strike him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Cobloaf!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: He would pun thee into shivers with his fist, as a
sailor breaks a biscuit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Beating him You whoreson cur!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Do, do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Thou stool for a witch!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, do, do; thou sodden-witted lord! thou hast no
more brain than I have in mine elbows; an assinego
may tutor thee: thou scurvy-valiant ass! thou art
here but to thrash Trojans; and thou art bought and
sold among those of any wit, like a barbarian slave.
If thou use to beat me, I will begin at thy heel, and
tell what thou art by inches, thou thing of no
bowels, thou!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: You dog!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: You scurvy lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Beating him You cur!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Mars his idiot! do, rudeness; do, camel; do, do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, Ajax! wherefore do you thus? How now,
Thersites! what's the matter, man?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: You see him there, do you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay; what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, look upon him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: So I do: what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but regard him well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Well!' why, I do so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: But yet you look not well upon him; for whosoever you
take him to be, he is Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I know that, fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but that fool knows not himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore I beat thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Lo, lo, lo, lo, what modicums of wit he utters! his
evasions have ears thus long. I have bobbed his
brain more than he has beat my bones: I will buy
nine sparrows for a penny, and his pia mater is not
worth the nineth part of a sparrow. This lord,
Achilles, Ajax, who wears his wit in his belly and
his guts in his head, I'll tell you what I say of
him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I say, this Ajax--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Has not so much wit--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I must hold you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: As will stop the eye of Helen's needle, for whom he
comes to fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, fool!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I would have peace and quietness, but the fool will
not: he there: that he: look you there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: O thou damned cur! I shall--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Will you set your wit to a fool's?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: No, I warrant you; for a fools will shame it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good words, Thersites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What's the quarrel?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I bade the vile owl go learn me the tenor of the
proclamation, and he rails upon me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I serve thee not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Well, go to, go to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I serve here voluntarily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Your last service was sufferance, 'twas not
voluntary: no man is beaten voluntary: Ajax was
here the voluntary, and you as under an impress.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: E'en so; a great deal of your wit, too, lies in your
sinews, or else there be liars. Hector have a great
catch, if he knock out either of your brains: a'
were as good crack a fusty nut with no kernel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What, with me too, Thersites?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: There's Ulysses and old Nestor, whose wit was mouldy
ere your grandsires had nails on their toes, yoke you
like draught-oxen and make you plough up the wars.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What, what?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, good sooth: to, Achilles! to, Ajax! to!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I shall cut out your tongue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis no matter! I shall speak as much as thou
afterwards.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: No more words, Thersites; peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I will hold my peace when Achilles' brach bids me, shall I?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: There's for you, Patroclus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I will see you hanged, like clotpoles, ere I come
any more to your tents: I will keep where there is
wit stirring and leave the faction of fools.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: A good riddance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, this, sir, is proclaim'd through all our host:
That Hector, by the fifth hour of the sun,
Will with a trumpet 'twixt our tents and Troy
To-morrow morning call some knight to arms
That hath a stomach; and such a one that dare
Maintain--I know not what: 'tis trash. Farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell. Who shall answer him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I know not: 'tis put to lottery; otherwise
He knew his man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: O, meaning you. I will go learn more of it.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. Troy. A room in Priam's palace.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PRIAM, HECTOR, TROILUS, PARIS, and HELENUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: After so many hours, lives, speeches spent,
Thus once again says Nestor from the Greeks:
'Deliver Helen, and all damage else--
As honour, loss of time, travail, expense,
Wounds, friends, and what else dear that is consumed
In hot digestion of this cormorant war--
Shall be struck off.' Hector, what say you to't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Though no man lesser fears the Greeks than I
As far as toucheth my particular,
Yet, dread Priam,
There is no lady of more softer bowels,
More spongy to suck in the sense of fear,
More ready to cry out 'Who knows what follows?'
Than Hector is: the wound of peace is surety,
Surety secure; but modest doubt is call'd
The beacon of the wise, the tent that searches
To the bottom of the worst. Let Helen go:
Since the first sword was drawn about this question,
Every tithe soul, 'mongst many thousand dismes,
Hath been as dear as Helen; I mean, of ours:
If we have lost so many tenths of ours,
To guard a thing not ours nor worth to us,
Had it our name, the value of one ten,
What merit's in that reason which denies
The yielding of her up?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie, my brother!
Weigh you the worth and honour of a king
So great as our dread father in a scale
Of common ounces? will you with counters sum
The past proportion of his infinite?
And buckle in a waist most fathomless
With spans and inches so diminutive
As fears and reasons? fie, for godly shame!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELENUS
SPEECH.LINE: No marvel, though you bite so sharp at reasons,
You are so empty of them. Should not our father
Bear the great sway of his affairs with reasons,
Because your speech hath none that tells him so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: You are for dreams and slumbers, brother priest;
You fur your gloves with reason. Here are
your reasons:
You know an enemy intends you harm;
You know a sword employ'd is perilous,
And reason flies the object of all harm:
Who marvels then, when Helenus beholds
A Grecian and his sword, if he do set
The very wings of reason to his heels
And fly like chidden Mercury from Jove,
Or like a star disorb'd? Nay, if we talk of reason,
Let's shut our gates and sleep: manhood and honour
Should have hare-hearts, would they but fat
their thoughts
With this cramm'd reason: reason and respect
Make livers pale and lustihood deject.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Brother, she is not worth what she doth cost
The holding.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: What is aught, but as 'tis valued?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: But value dwells not in particular will;
It holds his estimate and dignity
As well wherein 'tis precious of itself
As in the prizer: 'tis mad idolatry
To make the service greater than the god
And the will dotes that is attributive
To what infectiously itself affects,
Without some image of the affected merit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I take to-day a wife, and my election
Is led on in the conduct of my will;
My will enkindled by mine eyes and ears,
Two traded pilots 'twixt the dangerous shores
Of will and judgment: how may I avoid,
Although my will distaste what it elected,
The wife I chose? there can be no evasion
To blench from this and to stand firm by honour:
We turn not back the silks upon the merchant,
When we have soil'd them, nor the remainder viands
We do not throw in unrespective sieve,
Because we now are full. It was thought meet
Paris should do some vengeance on the Greeks:
Your breath of full consent bellied his sails;
The seas and winds, old wranglers, took a truce
And did him service: he touch'd the ports desired,
And for an old aunt whom the Greeks held captive,
He brought a Grecian queen, whose youth and freshness
Wrinkles Apollo's, and makes stale the morning.
Why keep we her? the Grecians keep our aunt:
Is she worth keeping? why, she is a pearl,
Whose price hath launch'd above a thousand ships,
And turn'd crown'd kings to merchants.
If you'll avouch 'twas wisdom Paris went--
As you must needs, for you all cried 'Go, go,'--
If you'll confess he brought home noble prize--
As you must needs, for you all clapp'd your hands
And cried 'Inestimable!'--why do you now
The issue of your proper wisdoms rate,
And do a deed that fortune never did,
Beggar the estimation which you prized
Richer than sea and land? O, theft most base,
That we have stol'n what we do fear to keep!
But, thieves, unworthy of a thing so stol'n,
That in their country did them that disgrace,
We fear to warrant in our native place!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Within Cry, Trojans, cry!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: What noise? what shriek is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis our mad sister, I do know her voice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Within Cry, Trojans!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: It is Cassandra.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Cry, Trojans, cry! lend me ten thousand eyes,
And I will fill them with prophetic tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, sister, peace!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Virgins and boys, mid-age and wrinkled eld,
Soft infancy, that nothing canst but cry,
Add to my clamours! let us pay betimes
A moiety of that mass of moan to come.
Cry, Trojans, cry! practise your eyes with tears!
Troy must not be, nor goodly Ilion stand;
Our firebrand brother, Paris, burns us all.
Cry, Trojans, cry! a Helen and a woe:
Cry, cry! Troy burns, or else let Helen go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Now, youthful Troilus, do not these high strains
Of divination in our sister work
Some touches of remorse? or is your blood
So madly hot that no discourse of reason,
Nor fear of bad success in a bad cause,
Can qualify the same?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, brother Hector,
We may not think the justness of each act
Such and no other than event doth form it,
Nor once deject the courage of our minds,
Because Cassandra's mad: her brain-sick raptures
Cannot distaste the goodness of a quarrel
Which hath our several honours all engaged
To make it gracious. For my private part,
I am no more touch'd than all Priam's sons:
And Jove forbid there should be done amongst us
Such things as might offend the weakest spleen
To fight for and maintain!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Else might the world convince of levity
As well my undertakings as your counsels:
But I attest the gods, your full consent
Gave wings to my propension and cut off
All fears attending on so dire a project.
For what, alas, can these my single arms?
What Propugnation is in one man's valour,
To stand the push and enmity of those
This quarrel would excite? Yet, I protest,
Were I alone to pass the difficulties
And had as ample power as I have will,
Paris should ne'er retract what he hath done,
Nor faint in the pursuit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: Paris, you speak
Like one besotted on your sweet delights:
You have the honey still, but these the gall;
So to be valiant is no praise at all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I propose not merely to myself
The pleasures such a beauty brings with it;
But I would have the soil of her fair rape
Wiped off, in honourable keeping her.
What treason were it to the ransack'd queen,
Disgrace to your great worths and shame to me,
Now to deliver her possession up
On terms of base compulsion! Can it be
That so degenerate a strain as this
Should once set footing in your generous bosoms?
There's not the meanest spirit on our party
Without a heart to dare or sword to draw
When Helen is defended, nor none so noble
Whose life were ill bestow'd or death unfamed
Where Helen is the subject; then, I say,
Well may we fight for her whom, we know well,
The world's large spaces cannot parallel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Paris and Troilus, you have both said well,
And on the cause and question now in hand
Have glozed, but superficially: not much
Unlike young men, whom Aristotle thought
Unfit to hear moral philosophy:
The reasons you allege do more conduce
To the hot passion of distemper'd blood
Than to make up a free determination
'Twixt right and wrong, for pleasure and revenge
Have ears more deaf than adders to the voice
Of any true decision. Nature craves
All dues be render'd to their owners: now,
What nearer debt in all humanity
Than wife is to the husband? If this law
Of nature be corrupted through affection,
And that great minds, of partial indulgence
To their benumbed wills, resist the same,
There is a law in each well-order'd nation
To curb those raging appetites that are
Most disobedient and refractory.
If Helen then be wife to Sparta's king,
As it is known she is, these moral laws
Of nature and of nations speak aloud
To have her back return'd: thus to persist
In doing wrong extenuates not wrong,
But makes it much more heavy. Hector's opinion
Is this in way of truth; yet ne'ertheless,
My spritely brethren, I propend to you
In resolution to keep Helen still,
For 'tis a cause that hath no mean dependance
Upon our joint and several dignities.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, there you touch'd the life of our design:
Were it not glory that we more affected
Than the performance of our heaving spleens,
I would not wish a drop of Trojan blood
Spent more in her defence. But, worthy Hector,
She is a theme of honour and renown,
A spur to valiant and magnanimous deeds,
Whose present courage may beat down our foes,
And fame in time to come canonize us;
For, I presume, brave Hector would not lose
So rich advantage of a promised glory
As smiles upon the forehead of this action
For the wide world's revenue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I am yours,
You valiant offspring of great Priamus.
I have a roisting challenge sent amongst
The dun and factious nobles of the Greeks
Will strike amazement to their drowsy spirits:
I was advertised their great general slept,
Whilst emulation in the army crept:
This, I presume, will wake him.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The Grecian camp. Before Achilles' tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Thersites! what lost in the labyrinth of
thy fury! Shall the elephant Ajax carry it thus? He
beats me, and I rail at him: O, worthy satisfaction!
would it were otherwise; that I could beat him,
whilst he railed at me. 'Sfoot, I'll learn to
conjure and raise devils, but I'll see some issue of
my spiteful execrations. Then there's Achilles, a
rare enginer! If Troy be not taken till these two
undermine it, the walls will stand till they fall of
themselves. O thou great thunder-darter of Olympus,
forget that thou art Jove, the king of gods and,
Mercury, lose all the serpentine craft of thy
caduceus, if ye take not that little, little less
than little wit from them that they have! which
short-armed ignorance itself knows is so abundant
scarce, it will not in circumvention deliver a fly
from a spider, without drawing their massy irons and
cutting the web. After this, the vengeance on the
whole camp! or rather, the bone-ache! for that,
methinks, is the curse dependent on those that war
for a placket. I have said my prayers and devil Envy
say Amen. What ho! my Lord Achilles!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who's there? Thersites! Good Thersites, come in and rail.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: If I could have remembered a gilt counterfeit, thou
wouldst not have slipped out of my contemplation: but
it is no matter; thyself upon thyself! The common
curse of mankind, folly and ignorance, be thine in
great revenue! heaven bless thee from a tutor, and
discipline come not near thee! Let thy blood be thy
direction till thy death! then if she that lays thee
out says thou art a fair corse, I'll be sworn and
sworn upon't she never shrouded any but lazars.
Amen. Where's Achilles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, art thou devout? wast thou in prayer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay: the heavens hear me!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Who's there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thersites, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Where, where? Art thou come? why, my cheese, my
digestion, why hast thou not served thyself in to
my table so many meals? Come, what's Agamemnon?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Thy commander, Achilles. Then tell me, Patroclus,
what's Achilles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thy lord, Thersites: then tell me, I pray thee,
what's thyself?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Thy knower, Patroclus: then tell me, Patroclus,
what art thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou mayst tell that knowest.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: O, tell, tell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I'll decline the whole question. Agamemnon commands
Achilles; Achilles is my lord; I am Patroclus'
knower, and Patroclus is a fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: You rascal!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, fool! I have not done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: He is a privileged man. Proceed, Thersites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Agamemnon is a fool; Achilles is a fool; Thersites
is a fool, and, as aforesaid, Patroclus is a fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Derive this; come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Agamemnon is a fool to offer to command Achilles;
Achilles is a fool to be commanded of Agamemnon;
Thersites is a fool to serve such a fool, and
Patroclus is a fool positive.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why am I a fool?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Make that demand of the prover. It suffices me thou
art. Look you, who comes here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Patroclus, I'll speak with nobody.
Come in with me, Thersites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Here is such patchery, such juggling and such
knavery! all the argument is a cuckold and a
whore; a good quarrel to draw emulous factions
and bleed to death upon. Now, the dry serpigo on
the subject! and war and lechery confound all!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter AGAMEMNON, ULYSSES, NESTOR, DIOMEDES, and AJAX

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Where is Achilles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Within his tent; but ill disposed, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Let it be known to him that we are here.
He shent our messengers; and we lay by
Our appertainments, visiting of him:
Let him be told so; lest perchance he think
We dare not move the question of our place,
Or know not what we are.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: I shall say so to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: We saw him at the opening of his tent:
He is not sick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Yes, lion-sick, sick of proud heart: you may call it
melancholy, if you will favour the man; but, by my
head, 'tis pride: but why, why? let him show us the
cause. A word, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: What moves Ajax thus to bay at him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Achilles hath inveigled his fool from him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Who, Thersites?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: He.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Then will Ajax lack matter, if he have lost his argument.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: No, you see, he is his argument that has his
argument, Achilles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: All the better; their fraction is more our wish than
their faction: but it was a strong composure a fool
could disunite.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: The amity that wisdom knits not, folly may easily
untie. Here comes Patroclus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: No Achilles with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: The elephant hath joints, but none for courtesy:
his legs are legs for necessity, not for flexure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Achilles bids me say, he is much sorry,
If any thing more than your sport and pleasure
Did move your greatness and this noble state
To call upon him; he hopes it is no other
But for your health and your digestion sake,
And after-dinner's breath.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Hear you, Patroclus:
We are too well acquainted with these answers:
But his evasion, wing'd thus swift with scorn,
Cannot outfly our apprehensions.
Much attribute he hath, and much the reason
Why we ascribe it to him; yet all his virtues,
Not virtuously on his own part beheld,
Do in our eyes begin to lose their gloss,
Yea, like fair fruit in an unwholesome dish,
Are like to rot untasted. Go and tell him,
We come to speak with him; and you shall not sin,
If you do say we think him over-proud
And under-honest, in self-assumption greater
Than in the note of judgment; and worthier
than himself
Here tend the savage strangeness he puts on,
Disguise the holy strength of their command,
And underwrite in an observing kind
His humorous predominance; yea, watch
His pettish lunes, his ebbs, his flows, as if
The passage and whole carriage of this action
Rode on his tide. Go tell him this, and add,
That if he overhold his price so much,
We'll none of him; but let him, like an engine
Not portable, lie under this report:
'Bring action hither, this cannot go to war:
A stirring dwarf we do allowance give
Before a sleeping giant.' Tell him so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: I shall; and bring his answer presently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: In second voice we'll not be satisfied;
We come to speak with him. Ulysses, enter you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: What is he more than another?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: No more than what he thinks he is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Is he so much? Do you not think he thinks himself a
better man than I am?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: No question.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Will you subscribe his thought, and say he is?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: No, noble Ajax; you are as strong, as valiant, as
wise, no less noble, much more gentle, and altogether
more tractable.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Why should a man be proud? How doth pride grow? I
know not what pride is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Your mind is the clearer, Ajax, and your virtues the
fairer. He that is proud eats up himself: pride is
his own glass, his own trumpet, his own chronicle;
and whatever praises itself but in the deed, devours
the deed in the praise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I do hate a proud man, as I hate the engendering of toads.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Yet he loves himself: is't not strange?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Achilles will not to the field to-morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: What's his excuse?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: He doth rely on none,
But carries on the stream of his dispose
Without observance or respect of any,
In will peculiar and in self-admission.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Why will he not upon our fair request
Untent his person and share the air with us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Things small as nothing, for request's sake only,
He makes important: possess'd he is with greatness,
And speaks not to himself but with a pride
That quarrels at self-breath: imagined worth
Holds in his blood such swoln and hot discourse
That 'twixt his mental and his active parts
Kingdom'd Achilles in commotion rages
And batters down himself: what should I say?
He is so plaguy proud that the death-tokens of it
Cry 'No recovery.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Let Ajax go to him.
Dear lord, go you and greet him in his tent:
'Tis said he holds you well, and will be led
At your request a little from himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: O Agamemnon, let it not be so!
We'll consecrate the steps that Ajax makes
When they go from Achilles: shall the proud lord
That bastes his arrogance with his own seam
And never suffers matter of the world
Enter his thoughts, save such as do revolve
And ruminate himself, shall he be worshipp'd
Of that we hold an idol more than he?
No, this thrice worthy and right valiant lord
Must not so stale his palm, nobly acquired;
Nor, by my will, assubjugate his merit,
As amply titled as Achilles is,
By going to Achilles:
That were to enlard his fat already pride
And add more coals to Cancer when he burns
With entertaining great Hyperion.
This lord go to him! Jupiter forbid,
And say in thunder 'Achilles go to him.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to DIOMEDES O, this is well; he rubs the
vein of him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to NESTOR And how his silence drinks up
this applause!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: If I go to him, with my armed fist I'll pash him o'er the face.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: O, no, you shall not go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: An a' be proud with me, I'll pheeze his pride:
Let me go to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Not for the worth that hangs upon our quarrel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: A paltry, insolent fellow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: How he describes himself!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Can he not be sociable?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: The raven chides blackness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I'll let his humours blood.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: He will be the physician that should be the patient.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: An all men were o' my mind,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Wit would be out of fashion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: A' should not bear it so, a' should eat swords first:
shall pride carry it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: An 'twould, you'ld carry half.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: A' would have ten shares.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I will knead him; I'll make him supple.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: He's not yet through warm: force him with praises:
pour in, pour in; his ambition is dry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: To AGAMEMNON My lord, you feed too much on this dislike.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Our noble general, do not do so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: You must prepare to fight without Achilles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, 'tis this naming of him does him harm.
Here is a man--but 'tis before his face;
I will be silent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Wherefore should you so?
He is not emulous, as Achilles is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Know the whole world, he is as valiant.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: A whoreson dog, that shall pelter thus with us!
Would he were a Trojan!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: What a vice were it in Ajax now,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: If he were proud,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Or covetous of praise,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, or surly borne,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Or strange, or self-affected!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Thank the heavens, lord, thou art of sweet composure;
Praise him that got thee, she that gave thee suck:
Famed be thy tutor, and thy parts of nature
Thrice famed, beyond all erudition:
But he that disciplined thy arms to fight,
Let Mars divide eternity in twain,
And give him half: and, for thy vigour,
Bull-bearing Milo his addition yield
To sinewy Ajax. I will not praise thy wisdom,
Which, like a bourn, a pale, a shore, confines
Thy spacious and dilated parts: here's Nestor;
Instructed by the antiquary times,
He must, he is, he cannot but be wise:
Put pardon, father Nestor, were your days
As green as Ajax' and your brain so temper'd,
You should not have the eminence of him,
But be as Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Shall I call you father?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my good son.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Be ruled by him, Lord Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: There is no tarrying here; the hart Achilles
Keeps thicket. Please it our great general
To call together all his state of war;
Fresh kings are come to Troy: to-morrow
We must with all our main of power stand fast:
And here's a lord,--come knights from east to west,
And cull their flower, Ajax shall cope the best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Go we to council. Let Achilles sleep:
Light boats sail swift, though greater hulks draw deep.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Troy. Priam's palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Friend, you! pray you, a word: do not you follow
the young Lord Paris?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, sir, when he goes before me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: You depend upon him, I mean?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I do depend upon the lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: You depend upon a noble gentleman; I must needs
praise him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: The lord be praised!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: You know me, do you not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Faith, sir, superficially.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Friend, know me better; I am the Lord Pandarus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I hope I shall know your honour better.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do desire it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: You are in the state of grace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Grace! not so, friend: honour and lordship are my titles.
What music is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I do but partly know, sir: it is music in parts.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Know you the musicians?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Wholly, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who play they to?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: To the hearers, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: At whose pleasure, friend

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: At mine, sir, and theirs that love music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Command, I mean, friend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Who shall I command, sir?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Friend, we understand not one another: I am too
courtly and thou art too cunning. At whose request
do these men play?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: That's to 't indeed, sir: marry, sir, at the request
of Paris my lord, who's there in person; with him,
the mortal Venus, the heart-blood of beauty, love's
invisible soul,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who, my cousin Cressida?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir, Helen: could you not find out that by her
attributes?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: It should seem, fellow, that thou hast not seen the
Lady Cressida. I come to speak with Paris from the
Prince Troilus: I will make a complimental assault
upon him, for my business seethes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: Sodden business! there's a stewed phrase indeed!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fair be to you, my lord, and to all this fair
company! fair desires, in all fair measure,
fairly guide them! especially to you, fair queen!
fair thoughts be your fair pillow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Dear lord, you are full of fair words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: You speak your fair pleasure, sweet queen. Fair
prince, here is good broken music.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: You have broke it, cousin: and, by my life, you
shall make it whole again; you shall piece it out
with a piece of your performance. Nell, he is full
of harmony.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, lady, no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Rude, in sooth; in good sooth, very rude.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, my lord! well, you say so in fits.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: I have business to my lord, dear queen. My lord,
will you vouchsafe me a word?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, this shall not hedge us out: we'll hear you
sing, certainly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sweet queen. you are pleasant with me. But,
marry, thus, my lord: my dear lord and most esteemed
friend, your brother Troilus,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Pandarus; honey-sweet lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go to, sweet queen, to go:--commends himself most
affectionately to you,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: You shall not bob us out of our melody: if you do,
our melancholy upon your head!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet queen, sweet queen! that's a sweet queen, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: And to make a sweet lady sad is a sour offence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that shall not serve your turn; that shall not,
in truth, la. Nay, I care not for such words; no,
no. And, my lord, he desires you, that if the king
call for him at supper, you will make his excuse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Pandarus,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: What says my sweet queen, my very very sweet queen?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: What exploit's in hand? where sups he to-night?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but, my lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: What says my sweet queen? My cousin will fall out
with you. You must not know where he sups.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll lay my life, with my disposer Cressida.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, no such matter; you are wide: come, your
disposer is sick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I'll make excuse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, good my lord. Why should you say Cressida? no,
your poor disposer's sick.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: I spy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: You spy! what do you spy? Come, give me an
instrument. Now, sweet queen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Why, this is kindly done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: My niece is horribly in love with a thing you have,
sweet queen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: She shall have it, my lord, if it be not my lord Paris.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: He! no, she'll none of him; they two are twain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Falling in, after falling out, may make them three.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, I'll hear no more of this; I'll sing
you a song now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay, prithee now. By my troth, sweet lord, thou
hast a fine forehead.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, you may, you may.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Let thy song be love: this love will undo us all.
O Cupid, Cupid, Cupid!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Love! ay, that it shall, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, good now, love, love, nothing but love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: In good troth, it begins so.
Love, love, nothing but love, still more!
For, O, love's bow
Shoots buck and doe:
The shaft confounds,
Not that it wounds,
But tickles still the sore.
These lovers cry Oh! oh! they die!
Yet that which seems the wound to kill,
Doth turn oh! oh! to ha! ha! he!
So dying love lives still:
Oh! oh! a while, but ha! ha! ha!
Oh! oh! groans out for ha! ha! ha!
Heigh-ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: In love, i' faith, to the very tip of the nose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: He eats nothing but doves, love, and that breeds hot
blood, and hot blood begets hot thoughts, and hot
thoughts beget hot deeds, and hot deeds is love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is this the generation of love? hot blood, hot
thoughts, and hot deeds? Why, they are vipers:
is love a generation of vipers? Sweet lord, who's
a-field to-day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Hector, Deiphobus, Helenus, Antenor, and all the
gallantry of Troy: I would fain have armed to-day,
but my Nell would not have it so. How chance my
brother Troilus went not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: He hangs the lip at something: you know all, Lord Pandarus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Not I, honey-sweet queen. I long to hear how they
sped to-day. You'll remember your brother's excuse?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: To a hair.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell, sweet queen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: Commend me to your niece.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: I will, sweet queen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: They're come from field: let us to Priam's hall,
To greet the warriors. Sweet Helen, I must woo you
To help unarm our Hector: his stubborn buckles,
With these your white enchanting fingers touch'd,
Shall more obey than to the edge of steel
Or force of Greekish sinews; you shall do more
Than all the island kings,--disarm great Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HELEN
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twill make us proud to be his servant, Paris;
Yea, what he shall receive of us in duty
Gives us more palm in beauty than we have,
Yea, overshines ourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet, above thought I love thee.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. Pandarus' orchard.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PANDARUS and Troilus's Boy, meeting

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now! where's thy master? at my cousin
Cressida's?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Boy
SPEECH.LINE: No, sir; he stays for you to conduct him thither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, here he comes.
How now, how now!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sirrah, walk off.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Have you seen my cousin?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, Pandarus: I stalk about her door,
Like a strange soul upon the Stygian banks
Staying for waftage. O, be thou my Charon,
And give me swift transportance to those fields
Where I may wallow in the lily-beds
Proposed for the deserver! O gentle Pandarus,
From Cupid's shoulder pluck his painted wings
And fly with me to Cressid!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Walk here i' the orchard, I'll bring her straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I am giddy; expectation whirls me round.
The imaginary relish is so sweet
That it enchants my sense: what will it be,
When that the watery palate tastes indeed
Love's thrice repured nectar? death, I fear me,
Swooning destruction, or some joy too fine,
Too subtle-potent, tuned too sharp in sweetness,
For the capacity of my ruder powers:
I fear it much; and I do fear besides,
That I shall lose distinction in my joys;
As doth a battle, when they charge on heaps
The enemy flying.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: She's making her ready, she'll come straight: you
must be witty now. She does so blush, and fetches
her wind so short, as if she were frayed with a
sprite: I'll fetch her. It is the prettiest
villain: she fetches her breath as short as a
new-ta'en sparrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Even such a passion doth embrace my bosom:
My heart beats thicker than a feverous pulse;
And all my powers do their bestowing lose,
Like vassalage at unawares encountering
The eye of majesty.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, what need you blush? shame's a baby.
Here she is now: swear the oaths now to her that
you have sworn to me. What, are you gone again?
you must be watched ere you be made tame, must you?
Come your ways, come your ways; an you draw backward,
we'll put you i' the fills. Why do you not speak to
her? Come, draw this curtain, and let's see your
picture. Alas the day, how loath you are to offend
daylight! an 'twere dark, you'ld close sooner.
So, so; rub on, and kiss the mistress. How now!
a kiss in fee-farm! build there, carpenter; the air
is sweet. Nay, you shall fight your hearts out ere
I part you. The falcon as the tercel, for all the
ducks i' the river: go to, go to.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: You have bereft me of all words, lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Words pay no debts, give her deeds: but she'll
bereave you o' the deeds too, if she call your
activity in question. What, billing again? Here's
'In witness whereof the parties interchangeably'--
Come in, come in: I'll go get a fire.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Will you walk in, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Cressida, how often have I wished me thus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Wished, my lord! The gods grant,--O my lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: What should they grant? what makes this pretty
abruption? What too curious dreg espies my sweet
lady in the fountain of our love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: More dregs than water, if my fears have eyes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fears make devils of cherubims; they never see truly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Blind fear, that seeing reason leads, finds safer
footing than blind reason stumbling without fear: to
fear the worst oft cures the worse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, let my lady apprehend no fear: in all Cupid's
pageant there is presented no monster.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Nor nothing monstrous neither?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing, but our undertakings; when we vow to weep
seas, live in fire, eat rocks, tame tigers; thinking
it harder for our mistress to devise imposition
enough than for us to undergo any difficulty imposed.
This is the monstruosity in love, lady, that the will
is infinite and the execution confined, that the
desire is boundless and the act a slave to limit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: They say all lovers swear more performance than they
are able and yet reserve an ability that they never
perform, vowing more than the perfection of ten and
discharging less than the tenth part of one. They
that have the voice of lions and the act of hares,
are they not monsters?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Are there such? such are not we: praise us as we
are tasted, allow us as we prove; our head shall go
bare till merit crown it: no perfection in reversion
shall have a praise in present: we will not name
desert before his birth, and, being born, his addition
shall be humble. Few words to fair faith: Troilus
shall be such to Cressid as what envy can say worst
shall be a mock for his truth, and what truth can
speak truest not truer than Troilus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Will you walk in, my lord?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: What, blushing still? have you not done talking yet?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, uncle, what folly I commit, I dedicate to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: I thank you for that: if my lord get a boy of you,
you'll give him me. Be true to my lord: if he
flinch, chide me for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: You know now your hostages; your uncle's word and my
firm faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I'll give my word for her too: our kindred,
though they be long ere they are wooed, they are
constant being won: they are burs, I can tell you;
they'll stick where they are thrown.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Boldness comes to me now, and brings me heart.
Prince Troilus, I have loved you night and day
For many weary months.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why was my Cressid then so hard to win?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Hard to seem won: but I was won, my lord,
With the first glance that ever--pardon me--
If I confess much, you will play the tyrant.
I love you now; but not, till now, so much
But I might master it: in faith, I lie;
My thoughts were like unbridled children, grown
Too headstrong for their mother. See, we fools!
Why have I blabb'd? who shall be true to us,
When we are so unsecret to ourselves?
But, though I loved you well, I woo'd you not;
And yet, good faith, I wish'd myself a man,
Or that we women had men's privilege
Of speaking first. Sweet, bid me hold my tongue,
For in this rapture I shall surely speak
The thing I shall repent. See, see, your silence,
Cunning in dumbness, from my weakness draws
My very soul of counsel! stop my mouth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: And shall, albeit sweet music issues thence.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Pretty, i' faith.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I do beseech you, pardon me;
'Twas not my purpose, thus to beg a kiss:
I am ashamed. O heavens! what have I done?
For this time will I take my leave, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your leave, sweet Cressid!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Leave! an you take leave till to-morrow morning,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Pray you, content you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: What offends you, lady?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, mine own company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: You cannot shun Yourself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Let me go and try:
I have a kind of self resides with you;
But an unkind self, that itself will leave,
To be another's fool. I would be gone:
Where is my wit? I know not what I speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well know they what they speak that speak so wisely.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Perchance, my lord, I show more craft than love;
And fell so roundly to a large confession,
To angle for your thoughts: but you are wise,
Or else you love not, for to be wise and love
Exceeds man's might; that dwells with gods above.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O that I thought it could be in a woman--
As, if it can, I will presume in you--
To feed for aye her ramp and flames of love;
To keep her constancy in plight and youth,
Outliving beauty's outward, with a mind
That doth renew swifter than blood decays!
Or that persuasion could but thus convince me,
That my integrity and truth to you
Might be affronted with the match and weight
Of such a winnow'd purity in love;
How were I then uplifted! but, alas!
I am as true as truth's simplicity
And simpler than the infancy of truth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: In that I'll war with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O virtuous fight,
When right with right wars who shall be most right!
True swains in love shall in the world to come
Approve their truths by Troilus: when their rhymes,
Full of protest, of oath and big compare,
Want similes, truth tired with iteration,
As true as steel, as plantage to the moon,
As sun to day, as turtle to her mate,
As iron to adamant, as earth to the centre,
Yet, after all comparisons of truth,
As truth's authentic author to be cited,
'As true as Troilus' shall crown up the verse,
And sanctify the numbers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Prophet may you be!
If I be false, or swerve a hair from truth,
When time is old and hath forgot itself,
When waterdrops have worn the stones of Troy,
And blind oblivion swallow'd cities up,
And mighty states characterless are grated
To dusty nothing, yet let memory,
From false to false, among false maids in love,
Upbraid my falsehood! when they've said 'as false
As air, as water, wind, or sandy earth,
As fox to lamb, as wolf to heifer's calf,
Pard to the hind, or stepdame to her son,'
'Yea,' let them say, to stick the heart of falsehood,
'As false as Cressid.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go to, a bargain made: seal it, seal it; I'll be the
witness. Here I hold your hand, here my cousin's.
If ever you prove false one to another, since I have
taken such pains to bring you together, let all
pitiful goers-between be called to the world's end
after my name; call them all Pandars; let all
constant men be Troiluses, all false women Cressids,
and all brokers-between Pandars! say, amen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Amen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Amen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Amen. Whereupon I will show you a chamber with a
bed; which bed, because it shall not speak of your
pretty encounters, press it to death: away!
And Cupid grant all tongue-tied maidens here
Bed, chamber, Pandar to provide this gear!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The Grecian camp. Before Achilles' tent.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter AGAMEMNON, ULYSSES, DIOMEDES, NESTOR, AJAX, MENELAUS, and CALCHAS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALCHAS
SPEECH.LINE: Now, princes, for the service I have done you,
The advantage of the time prompts me aloud
To call for recompense. Appear it to your mind
That, through the sight I bear in things to love,
I have abandon'd Troy, left my possession,
Incurr'd a traitor's name; exposed myself,
From certain and possess'd conveniences,
To doubtful fortunes; sequestering from me all
That time, acquaintance, custom and condition
Made tame and most familiar to my nature,
And here, to do you service, am become
As new into the world, strange, unacquainted:
I do beseech you, as in way of taste,
To give me now a little benefit,
Out of those many register'd in promise,
Which, you say, live to come in my behalf.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: What wouldst thou of us, Trojan? make demand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALCHAS
SPEECH.LINE: You have a Trojan prisoner, call'd Antenor,
Yesterday took: Troy holds him very dear.
Oft have you--often have you thanks therefore--
Desired my Cressid in right great exchange,
Whom Troy hath still denied: but this Antenor,
I know, is such a wrest in their affairs
That their negotiations all must slack,
Wanting his manage; and they will almost
Give us a prince of blood, a son of Priam,
In change of him: let him be sent, great princes,
And he shall buy my daughter; and her presence
Shall quite strike off all service I have done,
In most accepted pain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Let Diomedes bear him,
And bring us Cressid hither: Calchas shall have
What he requests of us. Good Diomed,
Furnish you fairly for this interchange:
Withal bring word if Hector will to-morrow
Be answer'd in his challenge: Ajax is ready.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: This shall I undertake; and 'tis a burden
Which I am proud to bear.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter ACHILLES and PATROCLUS, before their tent

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Achilles stands i' the entrance of his tent:
Please it our general to pass strangely by him,
As if he were forgot; and, princes all,
Lay negligent and loose regard upon him:
I will come last. 'Tis like he'll question me
Why such unplausive eyes are bent on him:
If so, I have derision medicinable,
To use between your strangeness and his pride,
Which his own will shall have desire to drink:
It may be good: pride hath no other glass
To show itself but pride, for supple knees
Feed arrogance and are the proud man's fees.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: We'll execute your purpose, and put on
A form of strangeness as we pass along:
So do each lord, and either greet him not,
Or else disdainfully, which shall shake him more
Than if not look'd on. I will lead the way.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What, comes the general to speak with me?
You know my mind, I'll fight no more 'gainst Troy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: What says Achilles? would he aught with us?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Would you, my lord, aught with the general?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: No.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: The better.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Good day, good day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: How do you? how do you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What, does the cuckold scorn me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Patroclus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Ha?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and good next day too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What mean these fellows? Know they not Achilles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: They pass by strangely: they were used to bend
To send their smiles before them to Achilles;
To come as humbly as they used to creep
To holy altars.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What, am I poor of late?
'Tis certain, greatness, once fall'n out with fortune,
Must fall out with men too: what the declined is
He shall as soon read in the eyes of others
As feel in his own fall; for men, like butterflies,
Show not their mealy wings but to the summer,
And not a man, for being simply man,
Hath any honour, but honour for those honours
That are without him, as place, riches, favour,
Prizes of accident as oft as merit:
Which when they fall, as being slippery standers,
The love that lean'd on them as slippery too,
Do one pluck down another and together
Die in the fall. But 'tis not so with me:
Fortune and I are friends: I do enjoy
At ample point all that I did possess,
Save these men's looks; who do, methinks, find out
Something not worth in me such rich beholding
As they have often given. Here is Ulysses;
I'll interrupt his reading.
How now Ulysses!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Now, great Thetis' son!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What are you reading?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: A strange fellow here
Writes me: 'That man, how dearly ever parted,
How much in having, or without or in,
Cannot make boast to have that which he hath,
Nor feels not what he owes, but by reflection;
As when his virtues shining upon others
Heat them and they retort that heat again
To the first giver.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: This is not strange, Ulysses.
The beauty that is borne here in the face
The bearer knows not, but commends itself
To others' eyes; nor doth the eye itself,
That most pure spirit of sense, behold itself,
Not going from itself; but eye to eye opposed
Salutes each other with each other's form;
For speculation turns not to itself,
Till it hath travell'd and is mirror'd there
Where it may see itself. This is not strange at all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: I do not strain at the position,--
It is familiar,--but at the author's drift;
Who, in his circumstance, expressly proves
That no man is the lord of any thing,
Though in and of him there be much consisting,
Till he communicate his parts to others:
Nor doth he of himself know them for aught
Till he behold them form'd in the applause
Where they're extended; who, like an arch,
reverberates
The voice again, or, like a gate of steel
Fronting the sun, receives and renders back
His figure and his heat. I was much wrapt in this;
And apprehended here immediately
The unknown Ajax.
Heavens, what a man is there! a very horse,
That has he knows not what. Nature, what things there are
Most abject in regard and dear in use!
What things again most dear in the esteem
And poor in worth! Now shall we see to-morrow--
An act that very chance doth throw upon him--
Ajax renown'd. O heavens, what some men do,
While some men leave to do!
How some men creep in skittish fortune's hall,
Whiles others play the idiots in her eyes!
How one man eats into another's pride,
While pride is fasting in his wantonness!
To see these Grecian lords!--why, even already
They clap the lubber Ajax on the shoulder,
As if his foot were on brave Hector's breast
And great Troy shrieking.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I do believe it; for they pass'd by me
As misers do by beggars, neither gave to me
Good word nor look: what, are my deeds forgot?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Time hath, my lord, a wallet at his back,
Wherein he puts alms for oblivion,
A great-sized monster of ingratitudes:
Those scraps are good deeds past; which are devour'd
As fast as they are made, forgot as soon
As done: perseverance, dear my lord,
Keeps honour bright: to have done is to hang
Quite out of fashion, like a rusty mail
In monumental mockery. Take the instant way;
For honour travels in a strait so narrow,
Where one but goes abreast: keep then the path;
For emulation hath a thousand sons
That one by one pursue: if you give way,
Or hedge aside from the direct forthright,
Like to an enter'd tide, they all rush by
And leave you hindmost;
Or like a gallant horse fall'n in first rank,
Lie there for pavement to the abject rear,
O'er-run and trampled on: then what they do in present,
Though less than yours in past, must o'ertop yours;
For time is like a fashionable host
That slightly shakes his parting guest by the hand,
And with his arms outstretch'd, as he would fly,
Grasps in the comer: welcome ever smiles,
And farewell goes out sighing. O, let not
virtue seek
Remuneration for the thing it was;
For beauty, wit,
High birth, vigour of bone, desert in service,
Love, friendship, charity, are subjects all
To envious and calumniating time.
One touch of nature makes the whole world kin,
That all with one consent praise new-born gawds,
Though they are made and moulded of things past,
And give to dust that is a little gilt
More laud than gilt o'er-dusted.
The present eye praises the present object.
Then marvel not, thou great and complete man,
That all the Greeks begin to worship Ajax;
Since things in motion sooner catch the eye
Than what not stirs. The cry went once on thee,
And still it might, and yet it may again,
If thou wouldst not entomb thyself alive
And case thy reputation in thy tent;
Whose glorious deeds, but in these fields of late,
Made emulous missions 'mongst the gods themselves
And drave great Mars to faction.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Of this my privacy
I have strong reasons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: But 'gainst your privacy
The reasons are more potent and heroical:
'Tis known, Achilles, that you are in love
With one of Priam's daughters.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! known!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Is that a wonder?
The providence that's in a watchful state
Knows almost every grain of Plutus' gold,
Finds bottom in the uncomprehensive deeps,
Keeps place with thought and almost, like the gods,
Does thoughts unveil in their dumb cradles.
There is a mystery--with whom relation
Durst never meddle--in the soul of state;
Which hath an operation more divine
Than breath or pen can give expressure to:
All the commerce that you have had with Troy
As perfectly is ours as yours, my lord;
And better would it fit Achilles much
To throw down Hector than Polyxena:
But it must grieve young Pyrrhus now at home,
When fame shall in our islands sound her trump,
And all the Greekish girls shall tripping sing,
'Great Hector's sister did Achilles win,
But our great Ajax bravely beat down him.'
Farewell, my lord: I as your lover speak;
The fool slides o'er the ice that you should break.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: To this effect, Achilles, have I moved you:
A woman impudent and mannish grown
Is not more loathed than an effeminate man
In time of action. I stand condemn'd for this;
They think my little stomach to the war
And your great love to me restrains you thus:
Sweet, rouse yourself; and the weak wanton Cupid
Shall from your neck unloose his amorous fold,
And, like a dew-drop from the lion's mane,
Be shook to air.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Shall Ajax fight with Hector?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and perhaps receive much honour by him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I see my reputation is at stake
My fame is shrewdly gored.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, then, beware;
Those wounds heal ill that men do give themselves:
Omission to do what is necessary
Seals a commission to a blank of danger;
And danger, like an ague, subtly taints
Even then when we sit idly in the sun.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Go call Thersites hither, sweet Patroclus:
I'll send the fool to Ajax and desire him
To invite the Trojan lords after the combat
To see us here unarm'd: I have a woman's longing,
An appetite that I am sick withal,
To see great Hector in his weeds of peace,
To talk with him and to behold his visage,
Even to my full of view.
A labour saved!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: A wonder!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: What?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ajax goes up and down the field, asking for himself.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: How so?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: He must fight singly to-morrow with Hector, and is so
prophetically proud of an heroical cudgelling that he
raves in saying nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: How can that be?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, he stalks up and down like a peacock,--a stride
and a stand: ruminates like an hostess that hath no
arithmetic but her brain to set down her reckoning:
bites his lip with a politic regard, as who should
say 'There were wit in this head, an 'twould out;'
and so there is, but it lies as coldly in him as fire
in a flint, which will not show without knocking.
The man's undone forever; for if Hector break not his
neck i' the combat, he'll break 't himself in
vain-glory. He knows not me: I said 'Good morrow,
Ajax;' and he replies 'Thanks, Agamemnon.' What think
you of this man that takes me for the general? He's
grown a very land-fish, language-less, a monster.
A plague of opinion! a man may wear it on both
sides, like a leather jerkin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou must be my ambassador to him, Thersites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Who, I? why, he'll answer nobody; he professes not
answering: speaking is for beggars; he wears his
tongue in's arms. I will put on his presence: let
Patroclus make demands to me, you shall see the
pageant of Ajax.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: To him, Patroclus; tell him I humbly desire the
valiant Ajax to invite the most valorous Hector
to come unarmed to my tent, and to procure
safe-conduct for his person of the magnanimous
and most illustrious six-or-seven-times-honoured
captain-general of the Grecian army, Agamemnon,
et cetera. Do this.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Jove bless great Ajax!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Hum!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: I come from the worthy Achilles,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who most humbly desires you to invite Hector to his tent,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Hum!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: And to procure safe-conduct from Agamemnon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Agamemnon!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: What say you to't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: God b' wi' you, with all my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your answer, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: If to-morrow be a fair day, by eleven o'clock it will
go one way or other: howsoever, he shall pay for me
ere he has me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Your answer, sir.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Fare you well, with all my heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, but he is not in this tune, is he?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: No, but he's out o' tune thus. What music will be in
him when Hector has knocked out his brains, I know
not; but, I am sure, none, unless the fiddler Apollo
get his sinews to make catlings on.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, thou shalt bear a letter to him straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Let me bear another to his horse; for that's the more
capable creature.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: My mind is troubled, like a fountain stirr'd;
And I myself see not the bottom of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Would the fountain of your mind were clear again,
that I might water an ass at it! I had rather be a
tick in a sheep than such a valiant ignorance.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Troy. A street.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter, from one side, AENEAS, and Servant with a torch; from the other, PARIS, DEIPHOBUS, ANTENOR, DIOMEDES, and others, with torches

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: See, ho! who is that there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEIPHOBUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is the Lord AEneas.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Is the prince there in person?
Had I so good occasion to lie long
As you, prince Paris, nothing but heavenly business
Should rob my bed-mate of my company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: That's my mind too. Good morrow, Lord AEneas.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: A valiant Greek, AEneas,--take his hand,--
Witness the process of your speech, wherein
You told how Diomed, a whole week by days,
Did haunt you in the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Health to you, valiant sir,
During all question of the gentle truce;
But when I meet you arm'd, as black defiance
As heart can think or courage execute.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: The one and other Diomed embraces.
Our bloods are now in calm; and, so long, health!
But when contention and occasion meet,
By Jove, I'll play the hunter for thy life
With all my force, pursuit and policy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: And thou shalt hunt a lion, that will fly
With his face backward. In humane gentleness,
Welcome to Troy! now, by Anchises' life,
Welcome, indeed! By Venus' hand I swear,
No man alive can love in such a sort
The thing he means to kill more excellently.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: We sympathize: Jove, let AEneas live,
If to my sword his fate be not the glory,
A thousand complete courses of the sun!
But, in mine emulous honour, let him die,
With every joint a wound, and that to-morrow!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: We know each other well.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: We do; and long to know each other worse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: This is the most despiteful gentle greeting,
The noblest hateful love, that e'er I heard of.
What business, lord, so early?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: I was sent for to the king; but why, I know not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: His purpose meets you: 'twas to bring this Greek
To Calchas' house, and there to render him,
For the enfreed Antenor, the fair Cressid:
Let's have your company, or, if you please,
Haste there before us: I constantly do think--
Or rather, call my thought a certain knowledge--
My brother Troilus lodges there to-night:
Rouse him and give him note of our approach.
With the whole quality wherefore: I fear
We shall be much unwelcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: That I assure you:
Troilus had rather Troy were borne to Greece
Than Cressid borne from Troy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: There is no help;
The bitter disposition of the time
Will have it so. On, lord; we'll follow you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: And tell me, noble Diomed, faith, tell me true,
Even in the soul of sound good-fellowship,
Who, in your thoughts, merits fair Helen best,
Myself or Menelaus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Both alike:
He merits well to have her, that doth seek her,
Not making any scruple of her soilure,
With such a hell of pain and world of charge,
And you as well to keep her, that defend her,
Not palating the taste of her dishonour,
With such a costly loss of wealth and friends:
He, like a puling cuckold, would drink up
The lees and dregs of a flat tamed piece;
You, like a lecher, out of whorish loins
Are pleased to breed out your inheritors:
Both merits poised, each weighs nor less nor more;
But he as he, the heavier for a whore.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: You are too bitter to your countrywoman.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: She's bitter to her country: hear me, Paris:
For every false drop in her bawdy veins
A Grecian's life hath sunk; for every scruple
Of her contaminated carrion weight,
A Trojan hath been slain: since she could speak,
She hath not given so many good words breath
As for her Greeks and Trojans suffer'd death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Fair Diomed, you do as chapmen do,
Dispraise the thing that you desire to buy:
But we in silence hold this virtue well,
We'll but commend what we intend to sell.
Here lies our way.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. Court of Pandarus' house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Dear, trouble not yourself: the morn is cold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Then, sweet my lord, I'll call mine uncle down;
He shall unbolt the gates.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Trouble him not;
To bed, to bed: sleep kill those pretty eyes,
And give as soft attachment to thy senses
As infants' empty of all thought!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee now, to bed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Are you a-weary of me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Cressida! but that the busy day,
Waked by the lark, hath roused the ribald crows,
And dreaming night will hide our joys no longer,
I would not from thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Night hath been too brief.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Beshrew the witch! with venomous wights she stays
As tediously as hell, but flies the grasps of love
With wings more momentary-swift than thought.
You will catch cold, and curse me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, tarry:
You men will never tarry.
O foolish Cressid! I might have still held off,
And then you would have tarried. Hark!
there's one up.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Within What, 's all the doors open here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is your uncle.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: A pestilence on him! now will he be mocking:
I shall have such a life!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now, how now! how go maidenheads? Here, you
maid! where's my cousin Cressid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Go hang yourself, you naughty mocking uncle!
You bring me to do, and then you flout me too.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: To do what? to do what? let her say
what: what have I brought you to do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, beshrew your heart! you'll ne'er be good,
Nor suffer others.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha! ha! Alas, poor wretch! ah, poor capocchia!
hast not slept to-night? would he not, a naughty
man, let it sleep? a bugbear take him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Did not I tell you? Would he were knock'd i' the head!
Who's that at door? good uncle, go and see.
My lord, come you again into my chamber:
You smile and mock me, as if I meant naughtily.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, ha!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Come, you are deceived, I think of no such thing.
How earnestly they knock! Pray you, come in:
I would not for half Troy have you seen here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who's there? what's the matter? will you beat
down the door? How now! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Good morrow, lord, good morrow.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who's there? my Lord AEneas! By my troth,
I knew you not: what news with you so early?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Is not Prince Troilus here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here! what should he do here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, he is here, my lord; do not deny him:
It doth import him much to speak with me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is he here, say you? 'tis more than I know, I'll
be sworn: for my own part, I came in late. What
should he do here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Who!--nay, then: come, come, you'll do him wrong
ere you're ware: you'll be so true to him, to be
false to him: do not you know of him, but yet go
fetch him hither; go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, I scarce have leisure to salute you,
My matter is so rash: there is at hand
Paris your brother, and Deiphobus,
The Grecian Diomed, and our Antenor
Deliver'd to us; and for him forthwith,
Ere the first sacrifice, within this hour,
We must give up to Diomedes' hand
The Lady Cressida.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is it so concluded?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: By Priam and the general state of Troy:
They are at hand and ready to effect it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: How my achievements mock me!
I will go meet them: and, my Lord AEneas,
We met by chance; you did not find me here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Good, good, my lord; the secrets of nature
Have not more gift in taciturnity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Is't possible? no sooner got but lost? The devil
take Antenor! the young prince will go mad: a
plague upon Antenor! I would they had broke 's neck!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what's the matter? who was here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ah, ah!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Why sigh you so profoundly? where's my lord? gone!
Tell me, sweet uncle, what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Would I were as deep under the earth as I am above!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O the gods! what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, get thee in: would thou hadst ne'er been
born! I knew thou wouldst be his death. O, poor
gentleman! A plague upon Antenor!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Good uncle, I beseech you, on my knees! beseech you,
what's the matter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou must be gone, wench, thou must be gone; thou
art changed for Antenor: thou must to thy father,
and be gone from Troilus: 'twill be his death;
'twill be his bane; he cannot bear it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O you immortal gods! I will not go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thou must.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I will not, uncle: I have forgot my father;
I know no touch of consanguinity;
No kin no love, no blood, no soul so near me
As the sweet Troilus. O you gods divine!
Make Cressid's name the very crown of falsehood,
If ever she leave Troilus! Time, force, and death,
Do to this body what extremes you can;
But the strong base and building of my love
Is as the very centre of the earth,
Drawing all things to it. I'll go in and weep,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do, do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Tear my bright hair and scratch my praised cheeks,
