Crack my clear voice with sobs and break my heart
With sounding Troilus. I will not go from Troy.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. The same. Street before Pandarus' house.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter PARIS, TROILUS, AENEAS, DEIPHOBUS, ANTENOR, and DIOMEDES

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: It is great morning, and the hour prefix'd
Of her delivery to this valiant Greek
Comes fast upon. Good my brother Troilus,
Tell you the lady what she is to do,
And haste her to the purpose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Walk into her house;
I'll bring her to the Grecian presently:
And to his hand when I deliver her,
Think it an altar, and thy brother Troilus
A priest there offering to it his own heart.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: I know what 'tis to love;
And would, as I shall pity, I could help!
Please you walk in, my lords.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. The same. Pandarus' house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Be moderate, be moderate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Why tell you me of moderation?
The grief is fine, full, perfect, that I taste,
And violenteth in a sense as strong
As that which causeth it: how can I moderate it?
If I could temporize with my affection,
Or brew it to a weak and colder palate,
The like allayment could I give my grief.
My love admits no qualifying dross;
No more my grief, in such a precious loss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here, here, here he comes.
Ah, sweet ducks!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O Troilus! Troilus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: What a pair of spectacles is here!
Let me embrace too. 'O heart,' as the goodly saying is,
'--O heart, heavy heart,
Why sigh'st thou without breaking?
where he answers again,
'Because thou canst not ease thy smart
By friendship nor by speaking.'
There was never a truer rhyme. Let us cast away
nothing, for we may live to have need of such a
verse: we see it, we see it. How now, lambs?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cressid, I love thee in so strain'd a purity,
That the bless'd gods, as angry with my fancy,
More bright in zeal than the devotion which
Cold lips blow to their deities, take thee from me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Have the gods envy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, ay, ay, ay; 'tis too plain a case.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: And is it true that I must go from Troy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: A hateful truth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: What, and from Troilus too?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: From Troy and Troilus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Is it possible?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: And suddenly; where injury of chance
Puts back leave-taking, justles roughly by
All time of pause, rudely beguiles our lips
Of all rejoindure, forcibly prevents
Our lock'd embrasures, strangles our dear vows
Even in the birth of our own labouring breath:
We two, that with so many thousand sighs
Did buy each other, must poorly sell ourselves
With the rude brevity and discharge of one.
Injurious time now with a robber's haste
Crams his rich thievery up, he knows not how:
As many farewells as be stars in heaven,
With distinct breath and consign'd kisses to them,
He fumbles up into a lose adieu,
And scants us with a single famish'd kiss,
Distasted with the salt of broken tears.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Within My lord, is the lady ready?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hark! you are call'd: some say the Genius so
Cries 'come' to him that instantly must die.
Bid them have patience; she shall come anon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Where are my tears? rain, to lay this wind, or
my heart will be blown up by the root.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I must then to the Grecians?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: No remedy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: A woful Cressid 'mongst the merry Greeks!
When shall we see again?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear me, my love: be thou but true of heart,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I true! how now! what wicked deem is this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, we must use expostulation kindly,
For it is parting from us:
I speak not 'be thou true,' as fearing thee,
For I will throw my glove to Death himself,
That there's no maculation in thy heart:
But 'be thou true,' say I, to fashion in
My sequent protestation; be thou true,
And I will see thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, you shall be exposed, my lord, to dangers
As infinite as imminent! but I'll be true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: And I'll grow friend with danger. Wear this sleeve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: And you this glove. When shall I see you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I will corrupt the Grecian sentinels,
To give thee nightly visitation.
But yet be true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O heavens! 'be true' again!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hear while I speak it, love:
The Grecian youths are full of quality;
They're loving, well composed with gifts of nature,
Flowing and swelling o'er with arts and exercise:
How novelty may move, and parts with person,
Alas, a kind of godly jealousy--
Which, I beseech you, call a virtuous sin--
Makes me afeard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O heavens! you love me not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Die I a villain, then!
In this I do not call your faith in question
So mainly as my merit: I cannot sing,
Nor heel the high lavolt, nor sweeten talk,
Nor play at subtle games; fair virtues all,
To which the Grecians are most prompt and pregnant:
But I can tell that in each grace of these
There lurks a still and dumb-discoursive devil
That tempts most cunningly: but be not tempted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Do you think I will?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: No.
But something may be done that we will not:
And sometimes we are devils to ourselves,
When we will tempt the frailty of our powers,
Presuming on their changeful potency.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Within Nay, good my lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, kiss; and let us part.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Within Brother Troilus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good brother, come you hither;
And bring AEneas and the Grecian with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, will you be true?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who, I? alas, it is my vice, my fault:
Whiles others fish with craft for great opinion,
I with great truth catch mere simplicity;
Whilst some with cunning gild their copper crowns,
With truth and plainness I do wear mine bare.
Fear not my truth: the moral of my wit
Is 'plain and true;' there's all the reach of it.
SPEECH.STAGEDIR: Enter AENEAS, PARIS, ANTENOR, DEIPHOBUS, and DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, Sir Diomed! here is the lady
Which for Antenor we deliver you:
At the port, lord, I'll give her to thy hand,
And by the way possess thee what she is.
Entreat her fair; and, by my soul, fair Greek,
If e'er thou stand at mercy of my sword,
Name Cressida and thy life shall be as safe
As Priam is in Ilion.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Fair Lady Cressid,
So please you, save the thanks this prince expects:
The lustre in your eye, heaven in your cheek,
Pleads your fair usage; and to Diomed
You shall be mistress, and command him wholly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Grecian, thou dost not use me courteously,
To shame the zeal of my petition to thee
In praising her: I tell thee, lord of Greece,
She is as far high-soaring o'er thy praises
As thou unworthy to be call'd her servant.
I charge thee use her well, even for my charge;
For, by the dreadful Pluto, if thou dost not,
Though the great bulk Achilles be thy guard,
I'll cut thy throat.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: O, be not moved, Prince Troilus:
Let me be privileged by my place and message,
To be a speaker free; when I am hence
I'll answer to my lust: and know you, lord,
I'll nothing do on charge: to her own worth
She shall be prized; but that you say 'be't so,'
I'll speak it in my spirit and honour, 'no.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, to the port. I'll tell thee, Diomed,
This brave shall oft make thee to hide thy head.
Lady, give me your hand, and, as we walk,
To our own selves bend we our needful talk.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: Hark! Hector's trumpet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: How have we spent this morning!
The prince must think me tardy and remiss,
That sore to ride before him to the field.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PARIS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis Troilus' fault: come, come, to field with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DEIPHOBUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let us make ready straight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, with a bridegroom's fresh alacrity,
Let us address to tend on Hector's heels:
The glory of our Troy doth this day lie
On his fair worth and single chivalry.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. The Grecian camp. Lists set out.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter AJAX, armed; AGAMEMNON, ACHILLES, PATROCLUS, MENELAUS, ULYSSES, NESTOR, and others

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Here art thou in appointment fresh and fair,
Anticipating time with starting courage.
Give with thy trumpet a loud note to Troy,
Thou dreadful Ajax; that the appalled air
May pierce the head of the great combatant
And hale him hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Thou, trumpet, there's my purse.
Now crack thy lungs, and split thy brazen pipe:
Blow, villain, till thy sphered bias cheek
Outswell the colic of puff'd Aquilon:
Come, stretch thy chest and let thy eyes spout blood;
Thou blow'st for Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: No trumpet answers.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis but early days.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Is not yond Diomed, with Calchas' daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis he, I ken the manner of his gait;
He rises on the toe: that spirit of his
In aspiration lifts him from the earth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Is this the Lady Cressid?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Even she.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Most dearly welcome to the Greeks, sweet lady.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Our general doth salute you with a kiss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Yet is the kindness but particular;
'Twere better she were kiss'd in general.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: And very courtly counsel: I'll begin.
So much for Nestor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I'll take what winter from your lips, fair lady:
Achilles bids you welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: I had good argument for kissing once.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: But that's no argument for kissing now;
For this popp'd Paris in his hardiment,
And parted thus you and your argument.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: O deadly gall, and theme of all our scorns!
For which we lose our heads to gild his horns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: The first was Menelaus' kiss; this, mine:
Patroclus kisses you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, this is trim!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Paris and I kiss evermore for him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll have my kiss, sir. Lady, by your leave.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: In kissing, do you render or receive?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Both take and give.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll make my match to live,
The kiss you take is better than you give;
Therefore no kiss.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: I'll give you boot, I'll give you three for one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: You're an odd man; give even or give none.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: An odd man, lady! every man is odd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: No, Paris is not; for you know 'tis true,
That you are odd, and he is even with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: You fillip me o' the head.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: No, I'll be sworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: It were no match, your nail against his horn.
May I, sweet lady, beg a kiss of you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: You may.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: I do desire it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Why, beg, then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Why then for Venus' sake, give me a kiss,
When Helen is a maid again, and his.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I am your debtor, claim it when 'tis due.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Never's my day, and then a kiss of you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Lady, a word: I'll bring you to your father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: A woman of quick sense.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, fie upon her!
There's language in her eye, her cheek, her lip,
Nay, her foot speaks; her wanton spirits look out
At every joint and motive of her body.
O, these encounterers, so glib of tongue,
That give accosting welcome ere it comes,
And wide unclasp the tables of their thoughts
To every ticklish reader! set them down
For sluttish spoils of opportunity
And daughters of the game.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: The Trojans' trumpet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Yonder comes the troop.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter HECTOR, armed; AENEAS, TROILUS, and other Trojans, with Attendants

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Hail, all you state of Greece! what shall be done
To him that victory commands? or do you purpose
A victor shall be known? will you the knights
Shall to the edge of all extremity
Pursue each other, or shall be divided
By any voice or order of the field?
Hector bade ask.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Which way would Hector have it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: He cares not; he'll obey conditions.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis done like Hector; but securely done,
A little proudly, and great deal misprizing
The knight opposed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: If not Achilles, sir,
What is your name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: If not Achilles, nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Therefore Achilles: but, whate'er, know this:
In the extremity of great and little,
Valour and pride excel themselves in Hector;
The one almost as infinite as all,
The other blank as nothing. Weigh him well,
And that which looks like pride is courtesy.
This Ajax is half made of Hector's blood:
In love whereof, half Hector stays at home;
Half heart, half hand, half Hector comes to seek
This blended knight, half Trojan and half Greek.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: A maiden battle, then? O, I perceive you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Here is Sir Diomed. Go, gentle knight,
Stand by our Ajax: as you and Lord AEneas
Consent upon the order of their fight,
So be it; either to the uttermost,
Or else a breath: the combatants being kin
Half stints their strife before their strokes begin.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: AJAX and HECTOR enter the lists

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: They are opposed already.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: What Trojan is that same that looks so heavy?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: The youngest son of Priam, a true knight,
Not yet mature, yet matchless, firm of word,
Speaking in deeds and deedless in his tongue;
Not soon provoked nor being provoked soon calm'd:
His heart and hand both open and both free;
For what he has he gives, what thinks he shows;
Yet gives he not till judgment guide his bounty,
Nor dignifies an impure thought with breath;
Manly as Hector, but more dangerous;
For Hector in his blaze of wrath subscribes
To tender objects, but he in heat of action
Is more vindicative than jealous love:
They call him Troilus, and on him erect
A second hope, as fairly built as Hector.
Thus says AEneas; one that knows the youth
Even to his inches, and with private soul
Did in great Ilion thus translate him to me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: They are in action.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Now, Ajax, hold thine own!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hector, thou sleep'st;
Awake thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: His blows are well disposed: there, Ajax!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: You must no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Princes, enough, so please you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I am not warm yet; let us fight again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: As Hector pleases.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then will I no more:
Thou art, great lord, my father's sister's son,
A cousin-german to great Priam's seed;
The obligation of our blood forbids
A gory emulation 'twixt us twain:
Were thy commixtion Greek and Trojan so
That thou couldst say 'This hand is Grecian all,
And this is Trojan; the sinews of this leg
All Greek, and this all Troy; my mother's blood
Runs on the dexter cheek, and this sinister
Bounds in my father's;' by Jove multipotent,
Thou shouldst not bear from me a Greekish member
Wherein my sword had not impressure made
Of our rank feud: but the just gods gainsay
That any drop thou borrow'dst from thy mother,
My sacred aunt, should by my mortal sword
Be drain'd! Let me embrace thee, Ajax:
By him that thunders, thou hast lusty arms;
Hector would have them fall upon him thus:
Cousin, all honour to thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, Hector
Thou art too gentle and too free a man:
I came to kill thee, cousin, and bear hence
A great addition earned in thy death.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Not Neoptolemus so mirable,
On whose bright crest Fame with her loud'st Oyes
Cries 'This is he,' could promise to himself
A thought of added honour torn from Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: There is expectance here from both the sides,
What further you will do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: We'll answer it;
The issue is embracement: Ajax, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: If I might in entreaties find success--
As seld I have the chance--I would desire
My famous cousin to our Grecian tents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis Agamemnon's wish, and great Achilles
Doth long to see unarm'd the valiant Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: AEneas, call my brother Troilus to me,
And signify this loving interview
To the expecters of our Trojan part;
Desire them home. Give me thy hand, my cousin;
I will go eat with thee and see your knights.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Great Agamemnon comes to meet us here.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: The worthiest of them tell me name by name;
But for Achilles, mine own searching eyes
Shall find him by his large and portly size.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Worthy of arms! as welcome as to one
That would be rid of such an enemy;
But that's no welcome: understand more clear,
What's past and what's to come is strew'd with husks
And formless ruin of oblivion;
But in this extant moment, faith and troth,
Strain'd purely from all hollow bias-drawing,
Bids thee, with most divine integrity,
From heart of very heart, great Hector, welcome.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I thank thee, most imperious Agamemnon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: To TROILUS My well-famed lord of Troy, no
less to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let me confirm my princely brother's greeting:
You brace of warlike brothers, welcome hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Who must we answer?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: The noble Menelaus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: O, you, my lord? by Mars his gauntlet, thanks!
Mock not, that I affect the untraded oath;
Your quondam wife swears still by Venus' glove:
She's well, but bade me not commend her to you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: Name her not now, sir; she's a deadly theme.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: O, pardon; I offend.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I have, thou gallant Trojan, seen thee oft
Labouring for destiny make cruel way
Through ranks of Greekish youth, and I have seen thee,
As hot as Perseus, spur thy Phrygian steed,
Despising many forfeits and subduements,
When thou hast hung thy advanced sword i' the air,
Not letting it decline on the declined,
That I have said to some my standers by
'Lo, Jupiter is yonder, dealing life!'
And I have seen thee pause and take thy breath,
When that a ring of Greeks have hemm'd thee in,
Like an Olympian wrestling: this have I seen;
But this thy countenance, still lock'd in steel,
I never saw till now. I knew thy grandsire,
And once fought with him: he was a soldier good;
But, by great Mars, the captain of us all,
Never saw like thee. Let an old man embrace thee;
And, worthy warrior, welcome to our tents.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis the old Nestor.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Let me embrace thee, good old chronicle,
That hast so long walk'd hand in hand with time:
Most reverend Nestor, I am glad to clasp thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I would my arms could match thee in contention,
As they contend with thee in courtesy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I would they could.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Ha!
By this white beard, I'ld fight with thee to-morrow.
Well, welcome, welcome! I have seen the time.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: I wonder now how yonder city stands
When we have here her base and pillar by us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I know your favour, Lord Ulysses, well.
Ah, sir, there's many a Greek and Trojan dead,
Since first I saw yourself and Diomed
In Ilion, on your Greekish embassy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I foretold you then what would ensue:
My prophecy is but half his journey yet;
For yonder walls, that pertly front your town,
Yond towers, whose wanton tops do buss the clouds,
Must kiss their own feet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I must not believe you:
There they stand yet, and modestly I think,
The fall of every Phrygian stone will cost
A drop of Grecian blood: the end crowns all,
And that old common arbitrator, Time,
Will one day end it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: So to him we leave it.
Most gentle and most valiant Hector, welcome:
After the general, I beseech you next
To feast with me and see me at my tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I shall forestall thee, Lord Ulysses, thou!
Now, Hector, I have fed mine eyes on thee;
I have with exact view perused thee, Hector,
And quoted joint by joint.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Is this Achilles?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I am Achilles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Stand fair, I pray thee: let me look on thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Behold thy fill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, I have done already.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou art too brief: I will the second time,
As I would buy thee, view thee limb by limb.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: O, like a book of sport thou'lt read me o'er;
But there's more in me than thou understand'st.
Why dost thou so oppress me with thine eye?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Tell me, you heavens, in which part of his body
Shall I destroy him? whether there, or there, or there?
That I may give the local wound a name
And make distinct the very breach whereout
Hector's great spirit flew: answer me, heavens!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: It would discredit the blest gods, proud man,
To answer such a question: stand again:
Think'st thou to catch my life so pleasantly
As to prenominate in nice conjecture
Where thou wilt hit me dead?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I tell thee, yea.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Wert thou an oracle to tell me so,
I'd not believe thee. Henceforth guard thee well;
For I'll not kill thee there, nor there, nor there;
But, by the forge that stithied Mars his helm,
I'll kill thee every where, yea, o'er and o'er.
You wisest Grecians, pardon me this brag;
His insolence draws folly from my lips;
But I'll endeavour deeds to match these words,
Or may I never--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Do not chafe thee, cousin:
And you, Achilles, let these threats alone,
Till accident or purpose bring you to't:
You may have every day enough of Hector
If you have stomach; the general state, I fear,
Can scarce entreat you to be odd with him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, let us see you in the field:
We have had pelting wars, since you refused
The Grecians' cause.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Dost thou entreat me, Hector?
To-morrow do I meet thee, fell as death;
To-night all friends.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Thy hand upon that match.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: First, all you peers of Greece, go to my tent;
There in the full convive we: afterwards,
As Hector's leisure and your bounties shall
Concur together, severally entreat him.
Beat loud the tabourines, let the trumpets blow,
That this great soldier may his welcome know.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt all except TROILUS and ULYSSES

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: My Lord Ulysses, tell me, I beseech you,
In what place of the field doth Calchas keep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: At Menelaus' tent, most princely Troilus:
There Diomed doth feast with him to-night;
Who neither looks upon the heaven nor earth,
But gives all gaze and bent of amorous view
On the fair Cressid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Shall sweet lord, be bound to you so much,
After we part from Agamemnon's tent,
To bring me thither?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: You shall command me, sir.
As gentle tell me, of what honour was
This Cressida in Troy? Had she no lover there
That wails her absence?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O, sir, to such as boasting show their scars
A mock is due. Will you walk on, my lord?
She was beloved, she loved; she is, and doth:
But still sweet love is food for fortune's tooth.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. The Grecian camp. Before Achilles' tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I'll heat his blood with Greekish wine to-night,
Which with my scimitar I'll cool to-morrow.
Patroclus, let us feast him to the height.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes Thersites.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: How now, thou core of envy!
Thou crusty batch of nature, what's the news?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, thou picture of what thou seemest, and idol
of idiot worshippers, here's a letter for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: From whence, fragment?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, thou full dish of fool, from Troy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who keeps the tent now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: The surgeon's box, or the patient's wound.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well said, adversity! and what need these tricks?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Prithee, be silent, boy; I profit not by thy talk:
thou art thought to be Achilles' male varlet.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Male varlet, you rogue! what's that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, his masculine whore. Now, the rotten diseases
of the south, the guts-griping, ruptures, catarrhs,
loads o' gravel i' the back, lethargies, cold
palsies, raw eyes, dirt-rotten livers, wheezing
lungs, bladders full of imposthume, sciaticas,
limekilns i' the palm, incurable bone-ache, and the
rivelled fee-simple of the tetter, take and take
again such preposterous discoveries!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why thou damnable box of envy, thou, what meanest
thou to curse thus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Do I curse thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why no, you ruinous butt, you whoreson
indistinguishable cur, no.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: No! why art thou then exasperate, thou idle
immaterial skein of sleave-silk, thou green sarcenet
flap for a sore eye, thou tassel of a prodigal's
purse, thou? Ah, how the poor world is pestered
with such waterflies, diminutives of nature!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PATROCLUS
SPEECH.LINE: Out, gall!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Finch-egg!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: My sweet Patroclus, I am thwarted quite
From my great purpose in to-morrow's battle.
Here is a letter from Queen Hecuba,
A token from her daughter, my fair love,
Both taxing me and gaging me to keep
An oath that I have sworn. I will not break it:
Fall Greeks; fail fame; honour or go or stay;
My major vow lies here, this I'll obey.
Come, come, Thersites, help to trim my tent:
This night in banqueting must all be spent.
Away, Patroclus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: With too much blood and too little brain, these two
may run mad; but, if with too much brain and too
little blood they do, I'll be a curer of madmen.
Here's Agamemnon, an honest fellow enough and one
that loves quails; but he has not so much brain as
earwax: and the goodly transformation of Jupiter
there, his brother, the bull,--the primitive statue,
and oblique memorial of cuckolds; a thrifty
shoeing-horn in a chain, hanging at his brother's
leg,--to what form but that he is, should wit larded
with malice and malice forced with wit turn him to?
To an ass, were nothing; he is both ass and ox: to
an ox, were nothing; he is both ox and ass. To be a
dog, a mule, a cat, a fitchew, a toad, a lizard, an
owl, a puttock, or a herring without a roe, I would
not care; but to be Menelaus, I would conspire
against destiny. Ask me not, what I would be, if I
were not Thersites; for I care not to be the louse
of a lazar, so I were not Menelaus! Hey-day!
spirits and fires!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter HECTOR, TROILUS, AJAX, AGAMEMNON, ULYSSES, NESTOR, MENELAUS, and DIOMEDES, with lights

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: We go wrong, we go wrong.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: No, yonder 'tis;
There, where we see the lights.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I trouble you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: No, not a whit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Here comes himself to guide you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Welcome, brave Hector; welcome, princes all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: So now, fair prince of Troy, I bid good night.
Ajax commands the guard to tend on you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Thanks and good night to the Greeks' general.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MENELAUS
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Good night, sweet lord Menelaus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet draught: 'sweet' quoth 'a! sweet sink,
sweet sewer.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Good night and welcome, both at once, to those
That go or tarry.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Good night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Old Nestor tarries; and you too, Diomed,
Keep Hector company an hour or two.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot, lord; I have important business,
The tide whereof is now. Good night, great Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Give me your hand.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Aside to TROILUS Follow his torch; he goes to
Calchas' tent:
I'll keep you company.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet sir, you honour me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: And so, good night.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exit DIOMEDES; ULYSSES and TROILUS following

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come, enter my tent.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt ACHILLES, HECTOR, AJAX, and NESTOR

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: That same Diomed's a false-hearted rogue, a most
unjust knave; I will no more trust him when he leers
than I will a serpent when he hisses: he will spend
his mouth, and promise, like Brabbler the hound:
but when he performs, astronomers foretell it; it
is prodigious, there will come some change; the sun
borrows of the moon, when Diomed keeps his
word. I will rather leave to see Hector, than
not to dog him: they say he keeps a Trojan
drab, and uses the traitor Calchas' tent: I'll
after. Nothing but lechery! all incontinent varlets!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. Before Calchas' tent.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: What, are you up here, ho? speak.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALCHAS
SPEECH.LINE: Within Who calls?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Calchas, I think. Where's your daughter?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CALCHAS
SPEECH.LINE: Within She comes to you.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter TROILUS and ULYSSES, at a distance; after them, THERSITES

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Stand where the torch may not discover us.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Cressid comes forth to him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: How now, my charge!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, my sweet guardian! Hark, a word with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, so familiar!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: She will sing any man at first sight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: And any man may sing her, if he can take her cliff;
she's noted.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Will you remember?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Remember! yes.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but do, then;
And let your mind be coupled with your words.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: What should she remember?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: List.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet honey Greek, tempt me no more to folly.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Roguery!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, then,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll tell you what,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Foh, foh! come, tell a pin: you are forsworn.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: In faith, I cannot: what would you have me do?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: A juggling trick,--to be secretly open.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: What did you swear you would bestow on me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I prithee, do not hold me to mine oath;
Bid me do any thing but that, sweet Greek.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Good night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hold, patience!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: How now, Trojan!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Diomed,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, good night: I'll be your fool no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Thy better must.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Hark, one word in your ear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O plague and madness!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: You are moved, prince; let us depart, I pray you,
Lest your displeasure should enlarge itself
To wrathful terms: this place is dangerous;
The time right deadly; I beseech you, go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Behold, I pray you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, good my lord, go off:
You flow to great distraction; come, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I pray thee, stay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: You have not patience; come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I pray you, stay; by hell and all hell's torments
I will not speak a word!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: And so, good night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, but you part in anger.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Doth that grieve thee?
O wither'd truth!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, how now, lord!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: By Jove,
I will be patient.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Guardian!--why, Greek!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Foh, foh! adieu; you palter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: In faith, I do not: come hither once again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: You shake, my lord, at something: will you go?
You will break out.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: She strokes his cheek!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, come.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, stay; by Jove, I will not speak a word:
There is between my will and all offences
A guard of patience: stay a little while.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: How the devil Luxury, with his fat rump and
potato-finger, tickles these together! Fry, lechery, fry!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: But will you, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: In faith, I will, la; never trust me else.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Give me some token for the surety of it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: I'll fetch you one.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: You have sworn patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fear me not, sweet lord;
I will not be myself, nor have cognition
Of what I feel: I am all patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Now the pledge; now, now, now!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Here, Diomed, keep this sleeve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O beauty! where is thy faith?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: My lord,--

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I will be patient; outwardly I will.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: You look upon that sleeve; behold it well.
He loved me--O false wench!--Give't me again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Whose was't?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: It is no matter, now I have't again.
I will not meet with you to-morrow night:
I prithee, Diomed, visit me no more.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Now she sharpens: well said, whetstone!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I shall have it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: What, this?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, that.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: O, all you gods! O pretty, pretty pledge!
Thy master now lies thinking in his bed
Of thee and me, and sighs, and takes my glove,
And gives memorial dainty kisses to it,
As I kiss thee. Nay, do not snatch it from me;
He that takes that doth take my heart withal.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I had your heart before, this follows it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: I did swear patience.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: You shall not have it, Diomed; faith, you shall not;
I'll give you something else.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I will have this: whose was it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: It is no matter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Come, tell me whose it was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: 'Twas one's that loved me better than you will.
But, now you have it, take it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Whose was it?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: By all Diana's waiting-women yond,
And by herself, I will not tell you whose.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: To-morrow will I wear it on my helm,
And grieve his spirit that dares not challenge it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Wert thou the devil, and worest it on thy horn,
It should be challenged.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Well, well, 'tis done, 'tis past: and yet it is not;
I will not keep my word.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Why, then, farewell;
Thou never shalt mock Diomed again.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: You shall not go: one cannot speak a word,
But it straight starts you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I do not like this fooling.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Nor I, by Pluto: but that that likes not you pleases me best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: What, shall I come? the hour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, come:--O Jove!--do come:--I shall be plagued.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell till then.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CRESSIDA
SPEECH.LINE: Good night: I prithee, come.
Troilus, farewell! one eye yet looks on thee
But with my heart the other eye doth see.
Ah, poor our sex! this fault in us I find,
The error of our eye directs our mind:
What error leads must err; O, then conclude
Minds sway'd by eyes are full of turpitude.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: A proof of strength she could not publish more,
Unless she said ' My mind is now turn'd whore.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: All's done, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: It is.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Why stay we, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: To make a recordation to my soul
Of every syllable that here was spoke.
But if I tell how these two did co-act,
Shall I not lie in publishing a truth?
Sith yet there is a credence in my heart,
An esperance so obstinately strong,
That doth invert the attest of eyes and ears,
As if those organs had deceptious functions,
Created only to calumniate.
Was Cressid here?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot conjure, Trojan.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: She was not, sure.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Most sure she was.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, my negation hath no taste of madness.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: Nor mine, my lord: Cressid was here but now.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let it not be believed for womanhood!
Think, we had mothers; do not give advantage
To stubborn critics, apt, without a theme,
For depravation, to square the general sex
By Cressid's rule: rather think this not Cressid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: What hath she done, prince, that can soil our mothers?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing at all, unless that this were she.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Will he swagger himself out on's own eyes?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: This she? no, this is Diomed's Cressida:
If beauty have a soul, this is not she;
If souls guide vows, if vows be sanctimonies,
If sanctimony be the gods' delight,
If there be rule in unity itself,
This is not she. O madness of discourse,
That cause sets up with and against itself!
Bi-fold authority! where reason can revolt
Without perdition, and loss assume all reason
Without revolt: this is, and is not, Cressid.
Within my soul there doth conduce a fight
Of this strange nature that a thing inseparate
Divides more wider than the sky and earth,
And yet the spacious breadth of this division
Admits no orifex for a point as subtle
As Ariachne's broken woof to enter.
Instance, O instance! strong as Pluto's gates;
Cressid is mine, tied with the bonds of heaven:
Instance, O instance! strong as heaven itself;
The bonds of heaven are slipp'd, dissolved, and loosed;
And with another knot, five-finger-tied,
The fractions of her faith, orts of her love,
The fragments, scraps, the bits and greasy relics
Of her o'er-eaten faith, are bound to Diomed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: May worthy Troilus be half attach'd
With that which here his passion doth express?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, Greek; and that shall be divulged well
In characters as red as Mars his heart
Inflamed with Venus: never did young man fancy
With so eternal and so fix'd a soul.
Hark, Greek: as much as I do Cressid love,
So much by weight hate I her Diomed:
That sleeve is mine that he'll bear on his helm;
Were it a casque composed by Vulcan's skill,
My sword should bite it: not the dreadful spout
Which shipmen do the hurricano call,
Constringed in mass by the almighty sun,
Shall dizzy with more clamour Neptune's ear
In his descent than shall my prompted sword
Falling on Diomed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: He'll tickle it for his concupy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O Cressid! O false Cressid! false, false, false!
Let all untruths stand by thy stained name,
And they'll seem glorious.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: O, contain yourself
Your passion draws ears hither.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: I have been seeking you this hour, my lord:
Hector, by this, is arming him in Troy;
Ajax, your guard, stays to conduct you home.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Have with you, prince. My courteous lord, adieu.
Farewell, revolted fair! and, Diomed,
Stand fast, and wear a castle on thy head!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: I'll bring you to the gates.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Accept distracted thanks.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Would I could meet that rogue Diomed! I would
croak like a raven; I would bode, I would bode.
Patroclus will give me any thing for the
intelligence of this whore: the parrot will not
do more for an almond than he for a commodious drab.
Lechery, lechery; still, wars and lechery; nothing
else holds fashion: a burning devil take them!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE III. Troy. Before Priam's palace.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: When was my lord so much ungently temper'd,
To stop his ears against admonishment?
Unarm, unarm, and do not fight to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: You train me to offend you; get you in:
By all the everlasting gods, I'll go!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: My dreams will, sure, prove ominous to the day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: No more, I say.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Where is my brother Hector?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: Here, sister; arm'd, and bloody in intent.
Consort with me in loud and dear petition,
Pursue we him on knees; for I have dream'd
Of bloody turbulence, and this whole night
Hath nothing been but shapes and forms of slaughter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: O, 'tis true.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Ho! bid my trumpet sound!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: No notes of sally, for the heavens, sweet brother.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Be gone, I say: the gods have heard me swear.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: The gods are deaf to hot and peevish vows:
They are polluted offerings, more abhorr'd
Than spotted livers in the sacrifice.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: O, be persuaded! do not count it holy
To hurt by being just: it is as lawful,
For we would give much, to use violent thefts,
And rob in the behalf of charity.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: It is the purpose that makes strong the vow;
But vows to every purpose must not hold:
Unarm, sweet Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Hold you still, I say;
Mine honour keeps the weather of my fate:
Lie every man holds dear; but the brave man
Holds honour far more precious-dear than life.
How now, young man! mean'st thou to fight to-day?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: Cassandra, call my father to persuade.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: No, faith, young Troilus; doff thy harness, youth;
I am to-day i' the vein of chivalry:
Let grow thy sinews till their knots be strong,
And tempt not yet the brushes of the war.
Unarm thee, go, and doubt thou not, brave boy,
I'll stand to-day for thee and me and Troy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Brother, you have a vice of mercy in you,
Which better fits a lion than a man.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: What vice is that, good Troilus? chide me for it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: When many times the captive Grecian falls,
Even in the fan and wind of your fair sword,
You bid them rise, and live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: O,'tis fair play.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fool's play, by heaven, Hector.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: How now! how now!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: For the love of all the gods,
Let's leave the hermit pity with our mothers,
And when we have our armours buckled on,
The venom'd vengeance ride upon our swords,
Spur them to ruthful work, rein them from ruth.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Fie, savage, fie!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hector, then 'tis wars.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Troilus, I would not have you fight to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Who should withhold me?
Not fate, obedience, nor the hand of Mars
Beckoning with fiery truncheon my retire;
Not Priamus and Hecuba on knees,
Their eyes o'ergalled with recourse of tears;
Not you, my brother, with your true sword drawn,
Opposed to hinder me, should stop my way,
But by my ruin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Lay hold upon him, Priam, hold him fast:
He is thy crutch; now if thou lose thy stay,
Thou on him leaning, and all Troy on thee,
Fall all together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: Come, Hector, come, go back:
Thy wife hath dream'd; thy mother hath had visions;
Cassandra doth foresee; and I myself
Am like a prophet suddenly enrapt
To tell thee that this day is ominous:
Therefore, come back.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: AEneas is a-field;
And I do stand engaged to many Greeks,
Even in the faith of valour, to appear
This morning to them.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, but thou shalt not go.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I must not break my faith.
You know me dutiful; therefore, dear sir,
Let me not shame respect; but give me leave
To take that course by your consent and voice,
Which you do here forbid me, royal Priam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: O Priam, yield not to him!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ANDROMACHE
SPEECH.LINE: Do not, dear father.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Andromache, I am offended with you:
Upon the love you bear me, get you in.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: This foolish, dreaming, superstitious girl
Makes all these bodements.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: O, farewell, dear Hector!
Look, how thou diest! look, how thy eye turns pale!
Look, how thy wounds do bleed at many vents!
Hark, how Troy roars! how Hecuba cries out!
How poor Andromache shrills her dolours forth!
Behold, distraction, frenzy and amazement,
Like witless antics, one another meet,
And all cry, Hector! Hector's dead! O Hector!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Away! away!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: CASSANDRA
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell: yet, soft! Hector! take my leave:
Thou dost thyself and all our Troy deceive.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: You are amazed, my liege, at her exclaim:
Go in and cheer the town: we'll forth and fight,
Do deeds worth praise and tell you them at night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PRIAM
SPEECH.LINE: Farewell: the gods with safety stand about thee!

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Exeunt severally PRIAM and HECTOR. Alarums

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: They are at it, hark! Proud Diomed, believe,
I come to lose my arm, or win my sleeve.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Do you hear, my lord? do you hear?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: What now?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here's a letter come from yond poor girl.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Let me read.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: A whoreson tisick, a whoreson rascally tisick so
troubles me, and the foolish fortune of this girl;
and what one thing, what another, that I shall
leave you one o' these days: and I have a rheum
in mine eyes too, and such an ache in my bones
that, unless a man were cursed, I cannot tell what
to think on't. What says she there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Words, words, mere words, no matter from the heart:
The effect doth operate another way.
Go, wind, to wind, there turn and change together.
My love with words and errors still she feeds;
But edifies another with her deeds.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IV. Plains between Troy and the Grecian camp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Now they are clapper-clawing one another; I'll go
look on. That dissembling abominable varlets Diomed,
has got that same scurvy doting foolish young knave's
sleeve of Troy there in his helm: I would fain see
them meet; that that same young Trojan ass, that
loves the whore there, might send that Greekish
whore-masterly villain, with the sleeve, back to the
dissembling luxurious drab, of a sleeveless errand.
O' the t'other side, the policy of those crafty
swearing rascals, that stale old mouse-eaten dry
cheese, Nestor, and that same dog-fox, Ulysses, is
not proved worthy a blackberry: they set me up, in
policy, that mongrel cur, Ajax, against that dog of
as bad a kind, Achilles: and now is the cur Ajax
prouder than the cur Achilles, and will not arm
to-day; whereupon the Grecians begin to proclaim
barbarism, and policy grows into an ill opinion.
Soft! here comes sleeve, and t'other.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Fly not; for shouldst thou take the river Styx,
I would swim after.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Thou dost miscall retire:
I do not fly, but advantageous care
Withdrew me from the odds of multitude:
Have at thee!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: Hold thy whore, Grecian!--now for thy whore,
Trojan!--now the sleeve, now the sleeve!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: What art thou, Greek? art thou for Hector's match?
Art thou of blood and honour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: No, no, I am a rascal; a scurvy railing knave:
a very filthy rogue.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I do believe thee: live.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: God-a-mercy, that thou wilt believe me; but a
plague break thy neck for frightening me! What's
become of the wenching rogues? I think they have
swallowed one another: I would laugh at that
miracle: yet, in a sort, lechery eats itself.
I'll seek them.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE V. Another part of the plains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Go, go, my servant, take thou Troilus' horse;
Present the fair steed to my lady Cressid:
Fellow, commend my service to her beauty;
Tell her I have chastised the amorous Trojan,
And am her knight by proof.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: Servant
SPEECH.LINE: I go, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Renew, renew! The fierce Polydamas
Hath beat down Menon: bastard Margarelon
Hath Doreus prisoner,
And stands colossus-wise, waving his beam,
Upon the pashed corses of the kings
Epistrophus and Cedius: Polyxenes is slain,
Amphimachus and Thoas deadly hurt,
Patroclus ta'en or slain, and Palamedes
Sore hurt and bruised: the dreadful Sagittary
Appals our numbers: haste we, Diomed,
To reinforcement, or we perish all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Go, bear Patroclus' body to Achilles;
And bid the snail-paced Ajax arm for shame.
There is a thousand Hectors in the field:
Now here he fights on Galathe his horse,
And there lacks work; anon he's there afoot,
And there they fly or die, like scaled sculls
Before the belching whale; then is he yonder,
And there the strawy Greeks, ripe for his edge,
Fall down before him, like the mower's swath:
Here, there, and every where, he leaves and takes,
Dexterity so obeying appetite
That what he will he does, and does so much
That proof is call'd impossibility.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ULYSSES
SPEECH.LINE: O, courage, courage, princes! great Achilles
Is arming, weeping, cursing, vowing vengeance:
Patroclus' wounds have roused his drowsy blood,
Together with his mangled Myrmidons,
That noseless, handless, hack'd and chipp'd, come to him,
Crying on Hector. Ajax hath lost a friend
And foams at mouth, and he is arm'd and at it,
Roaring for Troilus, who hath done to-day
Mad and fantastic execution,
Engaging and redeeming of himself
With such a careless force and forceless care
As if that luck, in very spite of cunning,
Bade him win all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Troilus! thou coward Troilus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, there, there.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: So, so, we draw together.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Where is this Hector?
Come, come, thou boy-queller, show thy face;
Know what it is to meet Achilles angry:
Hector? where's Hector? I will none but Hector.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VI. Another part of the plains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Troilus, thou coward Troilus, show thy head!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Troilus, I say! where's Troilus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: What wouldst thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: I would correct him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: Were I the general, thou shouldst have my office
Ere that correction. Troilus, I say! what, Troilus!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: O traitor Diomed! turn thy false face, thou traitor,
And pay thy life thou owest me for my horse!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: Ha, art thou there?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: I'll fight with him alone: stand, Diomed.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: He is my prize; I will not look upon.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come, both you cogging Greeks; have at you both!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Yea, Troilus? O, well fought, my youngest brother!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Now do I see thee, ha! have at thee, Hector!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Pause, if thou wilt.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: I do disdain thy courtesy, proud Trojan:
Be happy that my arms are out of use:
My rest and negligence befriends thee now,
But thou anon shalt hear of me again;
Till when, go seek thy fortune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Fare thee well:
I would have been much more a fresher man,
Had I expected thee. How now, my brother!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Ajax hath ta'en AEneas: shall it be?
No, by the flame of yonder glorious heaven,
He shall not carry him: I'll be ta'en too,
Or bring him off: fate, hear me what I say!
I reck not though I end my life to-day.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, stand, thou Greek; thou art a goodly mark:
No? wilt thou not? I like thy armour well;
I'll frush it and unlock the rivets all,
But I'll be master of it: wilt thou not,
beast, abide?
Why, then fly on, I'll hunt thee for thy hide.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VII. Another part of the plains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Come here about me, you my Myrmidons;
Mark what I say. Attend me where I wheel:
Strike not a stroke, but keep yourselves in breath:
And when I have the bloody Hector found,
Empale him with your weapons round about;
In fellest manner execute your aims.
Follow me, sirs, and my proceedings eye:
It is decreed Hector the great must die.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter MENELAUS and PARIS, fighting: then THERSITES

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: The cuckold and the cuckold-maker are at it. Now,
bull! now, dog! 'Loo, Paris, 'loo! now my double-
henned sparrow! 'loo, Paris, 'loo! The bull has the
game: ware horns, ho!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARELON
SPEECH.LINE: Turn, slave, and fight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: What art thou?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARELON
SPEECH.LINE: A bastard son of Priam's.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: THERSITES
SPEECH.LINE: I am a bastard too; I love bastards: I am a bastard
begot, bastard instructed, bastard in mind, bastard
in valour, in every thing illegitimate. One bear will
not bite another, and wherefore should one bastard?
Take heed, the quarrel's most ominous to us: if the
son of a whore fight for a whore, he tempts judgment:
farewell, bastard.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MARGARELON
SPEECH.LINE: The devil take thee, coward!

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE VIII. Another part of the plains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Most putrefied core, so fair without,
Thy goodly armour thus hath cost thy life.
Now is my day's work done; I'll take good breath:
Rest, sword; thou hast thy fill of blood and death.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: Puts off his helmet and hangs his shield behind him

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Look, Hector, how the sun begins to set;
How ugly night comes breathing at his heels:
Even with the vail and darking of the sun,
To close the day up, Hector's life is done.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: HECTOR
SPEECH.LINE: I am unarm'd; forego this vantage, Greek.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: Strike, fellows, strike; this is the man I seek.
So, Ilion, fall thou next! now, Troy, sink down!
Here lies thy heart, thy sinews, and thy bone.
On, Myrmidons, and cry you all amain,
'Achilles hath the mighty Hector slain.'
Hark! a retire upon our Grecian part.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: MYRMIDONS
SPEECH.LINE: The Trojan trumpets sound the like, my lord.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ACHILLES
SPEECH.LINE: The dragon wing of night o'erspreads the earth,
And, stickler-like, the armies separates.
My half-supp'd sword, that frankly would have fed,
Pleased with this dainty bait, thus goes to bed.
Come, tie his body to my horse's tail;
Along the field I will the Trojan trail.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE IX. Another part of the plains.
SCENE.STAGEDIR: Enter AGAMEMNON, AJAX, MENELAUS, NESTOR, DIOMEDES, and others, marching. Shouts within

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: Hark! hark! what shout is that?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: NESTOR
SPEECH.LINE: Peace, drums!
Achilles! Achilles! Hector's slain! Achilles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: DIOMEDES
SPEECH.LINE: The bruit is, Hector's slain, and by Achilles.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AJAX
SPEECH.LINE: If it be so, yet bragless let it be;
Great Hector was a man as good as he.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AGAMEMNON
SPEECH.LINE: March patiently along: let one be sent
To pray Achilles see us at our tent.
If in his death the gods have us befriended,
Great Troy is ours, and our sharp wars are ended.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE X. Another part of the plains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: Stand, ho! yet are we masters of the field:
Never go home; here starve we out the night.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hector is slain.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: ALL
SPEECH.LINE: Hector! the gods forbid!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: He's dead; and at the murderer's horse's tail,
In beastly sort, dragg'd through the shameful field.
Frown on, you heavens, effect your rage with speed!
Sit, gods, upon your thrones, and smile at Troy!
I say, at once let your brief plagues be mercy,
And linger not our sure destructions on!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: AENEAS
SPEECH.LINE: My lord, you do discomfort all the host!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: You understand me not that tell me so:
I do not speak of flight, of fear, of death,
But dare all imminence that gods and men
Address their dangers in. Hector is gone:
Who shall tell Priam so, or Hecuba?
Let him that will a screech-owl aye be call'd,
Go in to Troy, and say there, Hector's dead:
There is a word will Priam turn to stone;
Make wells and Niobes of the maids and wives,
Cold statues of the youth, and, in a word,
Scare Troy out of itself. But, march away:
Hector is dead; there is no more to say.
Stay yet. You vile abominable tents,
Thus proudly pight upon our Phrygian plains,
Let Titan rise as early as he dare,
I'll through and through you! and, thou great-sized coward,
No space of earth shall sunder our two hates:
I'll haunt thee like a wicked conscience still,
That mouldeth goblins swift as frenzy's thoughts.
Strike a free march to Troy! with comfort go:
Hope of revenge shall hide our inward woe.

SCENE.STAGEDIR: As TROILUS is going out, enter, from the other side, PANDARUS

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: But hear you, hear you!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: TROILUS
SPEECH.LINE: Hence, broker-lackey! ignomy and shame
Pursue thy life, and live aye with thy name!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PANDARUS
SPEECH.LINE: A goodly medicine for my aching bones! O world!
world! world! thus is the poor agent despised!
O traitors and bawds, how earnestly are you set
a-work, and how ill requited! why should our
endeavour be so loved and the performance so loathed?
what verse for it? what instance for it? Let me see:
Full merrily the humble-bee doth sing,
Till he hath lost his honey and his sting;
And being once subdued in armed tail,
Sweet honey and sweet notes together fail.
Good traders in the flesh, set this in your
painted cloths.
As many as be here of pander's hall,
Your eyes, half out, weep out at Pandar's fall;
Or if you cannot weep, yet give some groans,
Though not for me, yet for your aching bones.
Brethren and sisters of the hold-door trade,
Some two months hence my will shall here be made:
It should be now, but that my fear is this,
Some galled goose of Winchester would hiss:
Till then I'll sweat and seek about for eases,
And at that time bequeathe you my diseases.

PLAY.TITLE: The Two Gentlemen of Verona

PERSONAE.TITLE: Dramatis Personae
PERSONAE.PERSONA: DUKE OF MILAN, Father to Silvia.
THURIO, a foolish rival to Valentine.
EGLAMOUR, Agent for Silvia in her escape.
SPEED, a clownish servant to Valentine.

PLAY.SCNDESCR: SCENE Verona; Milan; the frontiers of Mantua.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE I. Verona. An open place.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus:
Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.
Were't not affection chains thy tender days
To the sweet glances of thy honour'd love,
I rather would entreat thy company
To see the wonders of the world abroad,
Than, living dully sluggardized at home,
Wear out thy youth with shapeless idleness.
But since thou lovest, love still and thrive therein,
Even as I would when I to love begin.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Wilt thou be gone? Sweet Valentine, adieu!
Think on thy Proteus, when thou haply seest
Some rare note-worthy object in thy travel:
Wish me partaker in thy happiness
When thou dost meet good hap; and in thy danger,
If ever danger do environ thee,
Commend thy grievance to my holy prayers,
For I will be thy beadsman, Valentine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: And on a love-book pray for my success?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Upon some book I love I'll pray for thee.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: That's on some shallow story of deep love:
How young Leander cross'd the Hellespont.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: That's a deep story of a deeper love:
For he was more than over shoes in love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis true; for you are over boots in love,
And yet you never swum the Hellespont.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Over the boots? nay, give me not the boots.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: No, I will not, for it boots thee not.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: What?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: To be in love, where scorn is bought with groans;
Coy looks with heart-sore sighs; one fading moment's mirth
With twenty watchful, weary, tedious nights:
If haply won, perhaps a hapless gain;
If lost, why then a grievous labour won;
However, but a folly bought with wit,
Or else a wit by folly vanquished.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: So, by your circumstance, you call me fool.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: So, by your circumstance, I fear you'll prove.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: 'Tis love you cavil at: I am not Love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: Love is your master, for he masters you:
And he that is so yoked by a fool,
Methinks, should not be chronicled for wise.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Yet writers say, as in the sweetest bud
The eating canker dwells, so eating love
Inhabits in the finest wits of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: And writers say, as the most forward bud
Is eaten by the canker ere it blow,
Even so by love the young and tender wit
Is turn'd to folly, blasting in the bud,
Losing his verdure even in the prime
And all the fair effects of future hopes.
But wherefore waste I time to counsel thee,
That art a votary to fond desire?
Once more adieu! my father at the road
Expects my coming, there to see me shipp'd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: And thither will I bring thee, Valentine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: Sweet Proteus, no; now let us take our leave.
To Milan let me hear from thee by letters
Of thy success in love, and what news else
Betideth here in absence of thy friend;
And likewise will visit thee with mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: All happiness bechance to thee in Milan!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: VALENTINE
SPEECH.LINE: As much to you at home! and so, farewell.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: He after honour hunts, I after love:
He leaves his friends to dignify them more,
I leave myself, my friends and all, for love.
Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,
Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,
War with good counsel, set the world at nought;
Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Sir Proteus, save you! Saw you my master?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: But now he parted hence, to embark for Milan.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Twenty to one then he is shipp'd already,
And I have play'd the sheep in losing him.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, a sheep doth very often stray,
An if the shepherd be a while away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: You conclude that my master is a shepherd, then,
and I a sheep?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: I do.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Why then, my horns are his horns, whether I wake or sleep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: A silly answer and fitting well a sheep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: This proves me still a sheep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: True; and thy master a shepherd.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, that I can deny by a circumstance.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: It shall go hard but I'll prove it by another.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: The shepherd seeks the sheep, and not the sheep the
shepherd; but I seek my master, and my master seeks
not me: therefore I am no sheep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: The sheep for fodder follow the shepherd; the
shepherd for food follows not the sheep: thou for
wages followest thy master; thy master for wages
follows not thee: therefore thou art a sheep.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Such another proof will make me cry 'baa.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: But, dost thou hear? gavest thou my letter to Julia?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Ay sir: I, a lost mutton, gave your letter to her,
a laced mutton, and she, a laced mutton, gave me, a
lost mutton, nothing for my labour.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Here's too small a pasture for such store of muttons.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: If the ground be overcharged, you were best stick her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nay: in that you are astray, 'twere best pound you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, sir, less than a pound shall serve me for
carrying your letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: You mistake; I mean the pound,--a pinfold.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: From a pound to a pin? fold it over and over,
'Tis threefold too little for carrying a letter to
your lover.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: But what said she?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: First nodding Ay.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Nod--Ay--why, that's noddy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: You mistook, sir; I say, she did nod: and you ask
me if she did nod; and I say, 'Ay.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: And that set together is noddy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Now you have taken the pains to set it together,
take it for your pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: No, no; you shall have it for bearing the letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Well, I perceive I must be fain to bear with you.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why sir, how do you bear with me?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Marry, sir, the letter, very orderly; having nothing
but the word 'noddy' for my pains.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Beshrew me, but you have a quick wit.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: And yet it cannot overtake your slow purse.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Come come, open the matter in brief: what said she?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Open your purse, that the money and the matter may
be both at once delivered.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Well, sir, here is for your pains. What said she?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Truly, sir, I think you'll hardly win her.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Why, couldst thou perceive so much from her?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: Sir, I could perceive nothing at all from her; no,
not so much as a ducat for delivering your letter:
and being so hard to me that brought your mind, I
fear she'll prove as hard to you in telling your
mind. Give her no token but stones; for she's as
hard as steel.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: What said she? nothing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: SPEED
SPEECH.LINE: No, not so much as 'Take this for thy pains.' To
testify your bounty, I thank you, you have testerned
me; in requital whereof, henceforth carry your
letters yourself: and so, sir, I'll commend you to my master.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: PROTEUS
SPEECH.LINE: Go, go, be gone, to save your ship from wreck,
Which cannot perish having thee aboard,
Being destined to a drier death on shore.
I must go send some better messenger:
I fear my Julia would not deign my lines,
Receiving them from such a worthless post.

SCENE.TITLE: SCENE II. The same. Garden of JULIA's house.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: But say, Lucetta, now we are alone,
Wouldst thou then counsel me to fall in love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, madam, so you stumble not unheedfully.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Of all the fair resort of gentlemen
That every day with parle encounter me,
In thy opinion which is worthiest love?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Please you repeat their names, I'll show my mind
According to my shallow simple skill.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: What think'st thou of the fair Sir Eglamour?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: As of a knight well-spoken, neat and fine;
But, were I you, he never should be mine.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: What think'st thou of the rich Mercatio?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Well of his wealth; but of himself, so so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: What think'st thou of the gentle Proteus?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Lord, Lord! to see what folly reigns in us!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: How now! what means this passion at his name?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Pardon, dear madam: 'tis a passing shame
That I, unworthy body as I am,
Should censure thus on lovely gentlemen.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why not on Proteus, as of all the rest?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Then thus: of many good I think him best.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Your reason?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: I have no other, but a woman's reason;
I think him so because I think him so.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: And wouldst thou have me cast my love on him?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, if you thought your love not cast away.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why he, of all the rest, hath never moved me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Yet he, of all the rest, I think, best loves ye.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: His little speaking shows his love but small.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Fire that's closest kept burns most of all.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: They do not love that do not show their love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: O, they love least that let men know their love.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: I would I knew his mind.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Peruse this paper, madam.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: 'To Julia.' Say, from whom?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: That the contents will show.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Say, say, who gave it thee?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Valentine's page; and sent, I think, from Proteus.
He would have given it you; but I, being in the way,
Did in your name receive it: pardon the
fault I pray.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Now, by my modesty, a goodly broker!
Dare you presume to harbour wanton lines?
To whisper and conspire against my youth?
Now, trust me, 'tis an office of great worth
And you an officer fit for the place.
Or else return no more into my sight.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: To plead for love deserves more fee than hate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Will ye be gone?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: That you may ruminate.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: And yet I would I had o'erlooked the letter:
It were a shame to call her back again
And pray her to a fault for which I chid her.
What a fool is she, that knows I am a maid,
And would not force the letter to my view!
Since maids, in modesty, say 'no' to that
Which they would have the profferer construe 'ay.'
Fie, fie, how wayward is this foolish love
That, like a testy babe, will scratch the nurse
And presently all humbled kiss the rod!
How churlishly I chid Lucetta hence,
When willingly I would have had her here!
How angerly I taught my brow to frown,
When inward joy enforced my heart to smile!
My penance is to call Lucetta back
And ask remission for my folly past.
What ho! Lucetta!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: What would your ladyship?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Is't near dinner-time?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: I would it were,
That you might kill your stomach on your meat
And not upon your maid.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: What is't that you took up so gingerly?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Why didst thou stoop, then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: To take a paper up that I let fall.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: And is that paper nothing?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Nothing concerning me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Then let it lie for those that it concerns.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Madam, it will not lie where it concerns
Unless it have a false interpeter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Some love of yours hath writ to you in rhyme.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: That I might sing it, madam, to a tune.
Give me a note: your ladyship can set.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: As little by such toys as may be possible.
Best sing it to the tune of 'Light o' love.'

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: It is too heavy for so light a tune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Heavy! belike it hath some burden then?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Ay, and melodious were it, would you sing it.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: And why not you?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: I cannot reach so high.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Let's see your song. How now, minion!

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Keep tune there still, so you will sing it out:
And yet methinks I do not like this tune.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: You do not?

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: No, madam; it is too sharp.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: You, minion, are too saucy.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, now you are too flat
And mar the concord with too harsh a descant:
There wanteth but a mean to fill your song.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: The mean is drown'd with your unruly bass.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: Indeed, I bid the base for Proteus.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: This babble shall not henceforth trouble me.
Here is a coil with protestation!
Go get you gone, and let the papers lie:
You would be fingering them, to anger me.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: LUCETTA
SPEECH.LINE: She makes it strange; but she would be best pleased
To be so anger'd with another letter.

SPEECH.SPEAKER: JULIA
SPEECH.LINE: Nay, would I were so anger'd with the same!
O hateful hands, to tear such loving words!
Injurious wasps, to feed on such sweet honey
And kill the bees that yield it with your stings!
I'll kiss each several paper for amends.
Look, here is writ 'kind Julia.' Unkind Julia!
As in revenge of thy ingratitude,
I throw thy name against the bruising stones,
Trampling contemptuously on thy disdain.
And here is writ 'love-wounded Proteus.'
Poor wounded name! my bosom as a bed
Shall lodge thee till thy wound be thoroughly heal'd;
And thus I search it with a sovereign kiss.
But twice or thrice was 'Proteus' written down.
Be calm, good wind, blow not a word away
Till I have found each letter in the letter,
Except mine own name: that some whirlwind bear
Unto a ragged fearful-hanging rock
And throw it thence into the raging sea!
